entries.zh: 又詔曰：「伯固隨同巨逆，自絕于天，俾無遺育，抑有恆典。
entries.en: Another edict said, "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.

entries.zh: 但童孺靡識，兼預葭莩，寘之甸人，良以惻憫，及伯固所生王氏，[4]可並特宥為庶人。」
entries.en: Yet the children know nothing and share the family tie; to set them among common folk is true compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, [4] may both be specially pardoned as commoners."
entries.literal: Yet children know nothing and also share the reed-and-rush tie; to place them among field folk is truly from compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, may both be specially pardoned as commoners."

entries.zh: 國除。
entries.en: The fief was abolished.
entries.literal: The state was abolished.

entries.zh: 新安王伯固字牢之，世祖之第五子也。
entries.en: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, styled Laozhi, was Emperor Wen's fifth son.
entries.literal: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, styled Laozhi, was the fifth son of Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 生而龜胸，目通精揚白，形狀眇小，而俊辯善言論。
entries.en: He was born with a pigeon chest and eyes whose whites showed bright; though slight in stature he was handsome in debate and fluent in speech.
entries.literal: From birth he had a pigeon chest; his eyes were clear with the whites showing; his form was slight and small, yet he was handsome in debate and skilled in discourse.

entries.zh: 天嘉六年，立為新安郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 6 he was made Prince of Xin'an with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjia, he was established as Prince of Xin'an with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 廢帝嗣立，為使持節、都督南琅邪彭城東海三郡諸軍事、雲麾將軍、彭城琅邪二郡太守。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he received the credential staff, command of southern Langye, Pengcheng, and Donghai, the rank of cloud-banner general, and the Pengcheng and Langye administratorates.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he was made credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in southern Langye, Pengcheng, and Donghai, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Pengcheng and Langye.

entries.zh: 尋入為丹陽尹，將軍如故。
entries.en: Soon he entered court as governor of Danyang, keeping his general's rank.
entries.literal: Soon he entered court as governor of Danyang; his general's rank was unchanged.

entries.zh: 陳書卷三十六
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 36
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 36

entries.zh: 高祖，沛豐邑中陽里人也，姓劉氏。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was born in Zhongyang Village in the town of Fengyi, Pei County. His surname was Liu.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was a person of Zhongyang Village, Fengyi Town, Pei County, and his surname was Liu.

entries.zh: 母媼嘗息大澤之陂，夢與神遇。
entries.en: Once, while resting by the dike of a vast marsh, his mother dreamed that she encountered a divine being.
entries.literal: His mother the old woman once rested by the dike of the great marsh, and dreamed of encountering a god.

entries.zh: 是時雷電晦冥，父太公往視，則見交龍於上。
entries.en: At that moment, thunder crashed and darkness fell. His father, Taigong, went to investigate and saw two dragons entwined in the sky above.
entries.literal: At this time thunder and lightning were dark and obscure, father Taigong went to look, then saw two dragons entwining above.

entries.zh: 已而有娠，遂產高祖。
entries.en: Soon after, she became pregnant and gave birth to Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: Soon after she became pregnant, and then gave birth to the Supreme Ancestor.

entries.zh: 單父人呂公善沛令，辟仇，從之客，因家焉。
entries.en: Lü Gong from Shanfu was on good terms with the magistrate of Pei. To avoid his enemies, he became the magistrate's guest and settled his family there.
entries.literal: Shanfu person Lü Gong was friendly with the Pei magistrate, avoided enmity by becoming his guest, and thus settled his household there.

entries.zh: 沛中豪傑吏聞令有重客，皆往賀。
entries.en: When the influential officials and clerks of Pei heard that the magistrate had an important guest, they all came to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: The Pei middle powerful officials and clerks heard the magistrate had an important guest, all went to congratulate.

entries.zh: 蕭何為主吏，主進，令諸大夫曰：「進不滿千錢，坐之堂下。」
entries.en: Xiao He served as chief clerk and was in charge of receiving guests. He instructed the other officials: "Those who present less than one thousand cash should be seated below the hall."
entries.literal: Xiao He was the chief clerk, took charge of receiving, commanded the various officials saying: "Those who advance less than one thousand cash, seat them below the hall."

entries.zh: 高祖為亭長，素易諸吏，乃紿為謁曰「賀錢萬」，實不持一錢。
entries.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu had always treated the officials lightly. He deceived them by having the announcement read "Congratulatory gift: ten thousand cash," though in fact he did not bring a single coin.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was pavilion chief, usually casual with the officials, then deceived to make the announcement saying "Congratulatory money ten thousand," in reality he did not bring a single cash.

entries.zh: 謁入，呂公大驚，起，迎之門。
entries.en: When the announcement was read, Lü Gong was greatly startled. He rose and went out to welcome him at the gate.
entries.literal: The announcement entered, Lü Gong was greatly startled, rose, welcomed him outside the gate.

entries.zh: 呂公者，好相人，見高祖狀貌，因重敬之，引入坐上坐。
entries.en: Lü Gong was skilled in reading faces. When he saw Emperor Gaozu's appearance, he was greatly impressed and led him inside to be seated in the place of honor.
entries.literal: Lü Gong was good at physiognomy, saw the Supreme Ancestor's appearance, because of this greatly respected him, led him in to sit in the seat of honor.

entries.zh: 蕭何曰：「劉季固多大言，少成事。」
entries.en: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji certainly talks big but accomplishes little."
entries.literal: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji indeed makes many big claims, accomplishes few matters."

entries.zh: 高祖因狎侮諸客，遂坐上坐，無所詘。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu took advantage of this to treat all the guests with casual familiarity and even insult them. He sat in the place of honor without showing any humility.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor because of this treated the various guests with familiarity and insult, then sat in the seat of honor, was not humble in any way.

entries.zh: 酒闌，呂公因目固留高祖。
entries.en: As the banquet ended, Lü Gong signaled insistently to keep Emperor Gaozu there.
entries.literal: The wine came to an end, Lü Gong because of this gave meaningful looks and firmly kept the Supreme Ancestor.

entries.zh: 竟酒，後。
entries.en: When the wine was finished, Gaozu stayed behind.
entries.literal: The wine banquet ended, afterwards.

entries.zh: 呂公曰：「臣少好相人，相人多矣，無如季相，願季自愛。
entries.en: Lü Gong said: "Since I was young, I've enjoyed reading faces. I've read many people's faces, but none compare to Ji's. I hope Ji takes good care of himself.
entries.literal: Lü Gong said: "I from youth favored physiognomy, have read many people's faces, none like Ji's appearance, wish Ji to take care of himself.

entries.zh: 臣有息女，願為箕帚妾。」
entries.en: I have a young daughter and wish to make her Ji's humble servant."
entries.literal: I have a young daughter, wish to make her Ji's broom and dustpan servant."

entries.zh: 酒罷，呂媼怒呂公曰：「公始常欲奇此女，與貴人。
entries.en: After the wine ended, Lü Po angrily confronted Lü Gong: "You always said this daughter was exceptional and should marry someone noble.
entries.literal: The wine ended, Lü Po became angry at Lü Gong and said: "You at first constantly wished to treat this daughter as exceptional, to match her with a noble person.

entries.zh: 沛令善公，求之不與，何自妄許與劉季？」
entries.en: The magistrate of Pei was your friend and asked for her, but you wouldn't give her. Why are you now rashly promising her to Liu Ji?"
entries.literal: The Pei magistrate was friendly with you, requested her and you did not give, why now rashly promise her to Liu Ji?"

entries.zh: 呂公曰：「此非兒女子所知。」
entries.en: Lü Gong replied: "This is not something that mere children and women can understand."
entries.literal: Lü Gong said: "This is not something that children and women understand."

entries.zh: 卒與高祖。
entries.en: In the end, she married Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: In the end he married with the Supreme Ancestor.

entries.zh: 呂公女即呂后也，生孝惠帝、魯元公主。
entries.en: This daughter of Lü Gong would become Empress Lü. She gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
entries.literal: Lü Gong's daughter was namely Empress Lü, gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

entries.zh: 秦二年十月，沛公攻胡陵、方與，還守豐。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the second year of Qin, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, then returned to defend Feng.
entries.literal: Qin second year tenth month, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, returned to defend Feng.

entries.zh: 秦泗川監平將兵圍豐。
entries.en: The Qin governor of Si River Ping led troops to besiege Feng.
entries.literal: Qin Sishui inspector Ping led troops to surround Feng.

entries.zh: 二日，出與戰，破之。
entries.en: For two days they came out to battle and defeated him.
entries.literal: Two days, went out and fought with them, defeated them.

entries.zh: 令雍齒守豐。
entries.en: He ordered Yong Chi to defend Feng.
entries.literal: Ordered Yong Chi to defend Feng.

entries.zh: 十一月，沛公引兵之薛。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xue.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xi.

entries.zh: 秦泗川守壯兵敗於薛，走至戚，沛公左司馬得殺之。
entries.en: The Qin governor of Si River Zhuang was defeated at Xue and fled to Qi, where Pei Gong's left commander Sima De killed him.
entries.literal: Qin Sishui defender Zhuang's troops defeated at Xue, fled to Qi, Pei Gong's left marshal captured and killed him.

entries.zh: 沛公還軍亢父，至方與。
entries.en: Pei Gong returned his army to Kangfu and arrived at Fang Yu.
entries.literal: Pei Gong returned his army to Kang Fu, arrived at Fang Yu.

entries.zh: 趙王武臣為其將所殺。
entries.en: King Wu of Zhao was killed by his own general.
entries.literal: Zhao King wuchen day was killed by his general.

entries.zh: 十二月，楚王陳涉為其御莊賈所殺。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, King Chen She of Chu was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Chu King Chen Sheng was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.

entries.zh: 魏人周市略地豐沛，使人謂雍齒曰：「豐，故梁徙也，今魏地已定者數十城。
entries.en: The Wei man Zhou Shi seized territory in Feng and Pei, and sent someone to tell Yong Chi: "Feng was originally Liang territory, now Wei has already pacified dozens of cities.
entries.literal: Wei person Zhou Shi conquered territory Feng Pei, sent person to tell Yong Chi: 'Feng was originally Liang migrants, now Wei territory already settled dozens of cities.

entries.zh: 齒今下魏，魏以齒為侯守豐；
entries.en: If Chi now submits to Wei, Wei will make Chi a marquess to guard Feng;
entries.literal: Chi now submit to Wei, Wei will make Chi marquis to guard Feng;

entries.zh: 不下，且屠豐。」
entries.en: if he doesn't submit, Wei will massacre Feng."
entries.literal: if not submit, then will slaughter Feng.'

entries.zh: 雍齒雅不欲屬沛公，及魏招之，即反為魏守豐。
entries.en: Yong Chi had long not wanted to serve Pei Gong, and when Wei summoned him, he immediately rebelled and defended Feng for Wei.
entries.literal: Yong Chi usually did not wish to belong to Pei Gong, when Wei summoned him, immediately rebelled to guard Feng for Wei.

entries.zh: 沛公攻豐，不能取。
entries.en: Pei Gong attacked Feng but could not capture it.
entries.literal: Pei Gong attacked Feng, could not capture it.

entries.zh: 沛公還之沛，怨雍齒與豐子弟畔之。
entries.en: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resentful that Yong Chi and the young men of Feng had rebelled against him.
entries.literal: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resented Yong Chi and the Feng youths rebelling against him.

entries.zh: 秦始皇帝嘗曰「東南有天子氣」，於是東游以猒當之。
entries.en: Qin Shihuang once said: "There is imperial aura in the southeast." So he traveled east to suppress it.
entries.literal: Qin Shi Huang often said 'there is emperor aura in the southeast', therefore traveled east to suppress it.

entries.zh: 高祖隱於芒、碭山澤間，呂后與人俱求，常得之。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang. Empress Lü and others searched for him together and always found him.
entries.literal: Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang, Empress Lu and others together sought him, constantly found him.

entries.zh: 高祖怪問之。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was surprised and asked how.
entries.literal: Gaozu strangely questioned her.

entries.zh: 呂后曰：「季所居上常有雲氣，故從往常得季。」
entries.en: Empress Lü said: "There are always clouds above where you stay. That's why we can always find you by following them."
entries.literal: Empress Lu said: 'Where Ji resides above constantly has cloud aura, therefore following it constantly finds Ji.'

entries.zh: 高祖又喜。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was delighted once more.
entries.literal: Gaozu again was happy.

entries.zh: 沛中子弟或聞之，多欲附者矣。
entries.en: Some young men from Pei heard about this and many wished to join him.
entries.literal: Some of the youths in Pei heard of it, many wished to attach themselves.

entries.zh: 於是樊噲從高祖來。
entries.en: So Fan Kuai came to follow Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and came.

entries.zh: 沛令後悔，恐其有變，乃閉城城守，欲誅蕭、曹。
entries.en: The magistrate of Pei later regretted it and feared there would be trouble, so he closed the city gates and defended, wanting to execute Xiao and Cao.
entries.literal: The Pei magistrate afterward regretted, feared there would be change, then closed the city gates and defended, wished to execute Xiao and Cao.

entries.zh: 蕭、曹恐，踰城保高祖。
entries.en: Xiao and Cao were afraid, so they climbed over the wall to join Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: Xiao and Cao feared, climbed over the wall to protect Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖乃書帛射城上，與沛父老曰：「天下同苦秦久矣。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, saying to the elders of Pei: "All under heaven have suffered under Qin for a long time.
entries.literal: Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, telling the Pei elders: 'The world together has suffered under Qin for a long time.

entries.zh: 今父老雖為沛令守，諸侯並起，今屠沛。
entries.en: Now although you elders are defending for the magistrate of Pei, the feudal lords are all rising up, and Pei will be massacred.
entries.literal: Now although elders defend for the Pei magistrate, the feudal lords all rise, now will slaughter Pei.

entries.zh: 沛今共誅令，擇可立立之，以應諸侯，即室家完。
entries.en: If Pei now joins together to execute the magistrate and chooses someone worthy to establish as leader to respond to the feudal lords, then your families will be safe.
entries.literal: Pei now together execute the magistrate, choose suitable one and establish him, to respond to the feudal lords, then families complete.

entries.zh: 不然，父子俱屠，無為也。」
entries.en: Otherwise, fathers and sons will all be massacred together. There will be no benefit."
entries.literal: If not, fathers and sons together slaughtered, useless.'

entries.zh: 父老乃帥子弟共殺沛令，開城門迎高祖，欲以為沛令。
entries.en: The elders then led the young men together to kill the magistrate of Pei, opened the city gates to welcome Emperor Gaozu, and wanted to make him magistrate of Pei.
entries.literal: The elders then led the young men together to kill the Pei magistrate, opened the city gates to welcome Gaozu, wished to make him Pei magistrate.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「天下方擾，諸侯並起，令置將不善，一敗塗地。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu said: "The world is in chaos right now, with feudal lords rising up everywhere. If you appoint a commander who is not capable, one defeat will ruin everything.
entries.literal: Gaozu said: 'The world is currently in chaos, feudal lords all rise, if the magistrate appoints generals poorly, one defeat and all lost.

entries.zh: 吾非敢自愛，恐能薄，不能完父兄子弟。
entries.en: I'm not trying to protect myself. I'm afraid my abilities are weak and I cannot protect the fathers, brothers, and children.
entries.literal: I do not dare cherish myself, fear my abilities are meager, cannot protect fathers, elder brothers, younger brothers.

entries.zh: 此大事，願吏擇可者。」
entries.en: This is a major matter. I hope the officials will choose someone suitable."
entries.literal: This is a great matter, wish officials choose suitable one.'

entries.zh: 蕭、曹等皆文吏，自愛，恐事不就，後秦種族其家，盡讓高祖。
entries.en: Xiao, Cao, and the others were all civil officials who cherished themselves. They feared that if things didn't succeed, Qin would exterminate their families, so they all yielded to Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: Xiao, Cao and others all were civil officials, cherished themselves, feared the matter would not succeed, afterward Qin would exterminate their families, all yielded to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 諸父老皆曰：「平生所聞劉季奇怪，當貴，且卜筮之，莫如劉季最吉。」
entries.en: All the elders said: "In our lifetimes we have heard that Liu Ji is strange and marked for nobility. Moreover, when we divined on it, none was more auspicious than Liu Ji."
entries.literal: All the elders said: 'In our lives we have heard Liu Ji is strange and extraordinary, should be noble, moreover divining it, none is more auspicious than Liu Ji.'

entries.zh: 高祖數讓。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu declined repeatedly.
entries.literal: Gaozu repeatedly declined.

entries.zh: 眾莫肯為，高祖乃立為沛公。
entries.en: No one else was willing to take it, so Emperor Gaozu was established as Lord of Pei.
entries.literal: The crowd none would do it, Gaozu then was established as Pei Gong.

entries.zh: 祠黃帝，祭蚩尤於沛廷，而釁鼓旗。
entries.en: He sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor and made offerings to Chiyou in the Pei court, and smeared blood on the drums and flags.
entries.literal: Sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor, offered sacrifice to Chi You in the Pei court, and smeared blood on drums and flags.

entries.zh: 幟皆赤，由所殺蛇白帝子，所殺者赤帝子故也。
entries.en: All the banners were red, because the snake he killed was the son of the White Emperor, and the one who killed it was the son of the Red Emperor.
entries.literal: The banners all red, because the killed snake was White Emperor's son, the one who killed was Red Emperor's son therefore.

entries.zh: 於是少年豪吏如蕭、曹、樊噲等皆為收沛子弟，得三千人。
entries.en: So the young brave officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai, and others all recruited young men from Pei and gathered three thousand.
entries.literal: Therefore young heroic officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai and others all recruited Pei youths, got three thousand.

entries.zh: 高祖為人，隆準而龍顏，美須髯，左股有七十二黑子。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu had a prominent nose, a face like a dragon, beautiful whiskers and beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor as a person had a high nose and dragon face, beautiful beard and whiskers, and on his left thigh there were seventy-two black moles.

entries.zh: 寬仁愛人，意豁如也。
entries.en: He was generous, benevolent, and loved people. His mind was open and magnanimous.
entries.literal: Broadly benevolent and loving people, his intentions were magnanimous and open.

entries.zh: 常有大度，不事家人生產作業。
entries.en: He always showed great magnanimity and never concerned himself with the family's farming and business.
entries.literal: Constantly having great breadth of mind, he did not engage in the family's production and work.

entries.zh: 及壯，試吏，為泗上亭長，廷中吏無所不狎侮。
entries.en: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official and became pavilion chief of Sishang. Among the officials at court there was none he did not treat with familiar disrespect.
entries.literal: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official, became the pavilion chief of Sishang, and among the officials in the court there was none he did not treat with familiarity and insult.

entries.zh: 好酒及色。
entries.en: He loved wine and women.
entries.literal: He favored wine and sex.

entries.zh: 常從王媼、武負貰酒，時飲醉臥，武負、王媼見其上常有怪。
entries.en: He often bought wine on credit from Wang Po and Wu Fu. Sometimes he drank until he lay down drunk. Wu Fu and Wang Po saw that strange things constantly appeared above him.
entries.literal: He constantly obtained wine on credit from Wang Po and Wu Fu, sometimes drank until drunk and lay down; Wu Fu and Wang Po saw that above him there was constantly something strange.

entries.zh: 高祖每酤留飲，酒讎數倍。
entries.en: Whenever Emperor Gaozu bought wine, he stayed to drink, and the bill was several times higher.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor each time he bought wine would stay and drink, the wine price several times.

entries.zh: 及見怪，歲竟，此兩家常折券棄責。
entries.en: When they saw the strange omens, at the end of the year the two households would always tear up the wine tabs and forgive what he owed.
entries.literal: When they saw the strange signs, at year's end these two households would always tear up the IOUs and abandon the debts.

entries.zh: 高祖常繇咸陽，縱觀秦皇帝，喟然大息，曰：「嗟乎，大丈夫當如此矣！」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu often passed through Xianyang and gazed upon the Qin emperor. He would sigh deeply and say: "Ah, this is how a true man should live!"
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor often performed corvée service at Xianyang and was allowed to observe the Qin emperor; he sighed deeply and said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"

entries.zh: 高祖嘗告歸之田。
entries.en: Once, Emperor Gaozu requested leave to return to his fields.
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor once requested leave to return to the fields.

entries.zh: 呂后與兩子居田中，有一老父過請飲，呂后因餔之。
entries.en: Empress Lü lived in the countryside with their two children. An old man passed by and asked for a drink. Empress Lü fed him.
entries.literal: Empress Lü and the two children resided in the fields, there was an old father who passed by requesting drink, Empress Lü because of this fed him.

entries.zh: 老父相后曰：「夫人天下貴人也。」
entries.en: The old man read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame, you are a noble person of the world."
entries.literal: The old father read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame is a noble person of the world."

entries.zh: 令相兩子，見孝惠帝，曰：「夫人所以貴者，乃此男也。」
entries.en: He had him read the faces of the two children. When he saw Emperor Xiaohui, he said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."
entries.literal: She had him read the faces of the two children; when he saw Emperor Xiaohui, he said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."

entries.zh: 相魯元公主，亦皆貴。
entries.en: He read Princess Lu Yuan's face as well - all were noble.
entries.literal: He read Princess Lu Yuan's face, all were noble.

entries.zh: 老父已去，高祖適從旁舍來，呂后具言客有過，相我子母皆大貴。
entries.en: The old man had already left. Emperor Gaozu had just returned from a neighboring house. Empress Lü told him everything: a guest had passed by and read the faces of her, the children, and her mother—they were all greatly noble.
entries.literal: The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and her children—all were greatly noble.

entries.zh: 高祖問，曰：「未遠。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu asked where the old man had gone. She said, "Not far."
entries.literal: Gaozu asked, said: 'Not far.'

entries.zh: 乃追及，問老父。
entries.en: So he pursued and caught up with him, asking the old man.
entries.literal: Then pursued and caught up, questioned the old father.

entries.zh: 老父曰：「鄉者夫人兒子皆以君，君相貴不可言。」
entries.en: The old man said: "Just now, Madame and the children all take after you. Your appearance shows nobility beyond words."
entries.literal: The old father said: 'Just now, madam and the children were all judged noble because of you; your features show nobility beyond words.'

entries.zh: 高祖乃謝曰：「誠如父言，不敢忘德。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu then thanked him and said: "If what you say is true, I won't forget your kindness."
entries.literal: Gaozu then thanked saying: 'Truly as father says, do not dare forget the kindness.'

entries.zh: 及高祖貴，遂不知老父處。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu rose to power, he could no longer find the old man.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became noble, then did not know the old father's whereabouts.

entries.zh: 高祖為亭長，乃鲈竹皮為冠，令求盜之薛治，時時冠之，及貴常冠，所謂「劉氏冠」也。
entries.en: While he was pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu made a cap of bamboo sheathing. When he was sent to pursue bandits in the Xue district he wore it from time to time, and after he rose high he still wore it constantly. This is what was called the "Liu family cap."
entries.literal: While Gaozu was pavilion chief, he made a cap of bamboo sheathing; he was ordered to pursue bandits in the Xue district and wore it from time to time; after he rose high he still wore it constantly—this is what is called the "Liu family cap."

entries.zh: 高祖以亭長為縣送徒驪山，徒多道亡。
entries.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu was assigned by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li. Many of the convicts fled along the road.
entries.literal: Gaozu as pavilion chief was ordered by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li, the convicts many fled on the road.

entries.zh: 自度比至皆亡之，到豐西澤中亭，止飲，夜皆解縱所送徒。
entries.en: He reckoned that by the time they arrived all would have fled anyway. When they reached the pavilion in the western marsh at Feng, he stopped to drink. At night he released all the convicts he was escorting.
entries.literal: He estimated that by the time he arrived all would have fled, arrived at the pavilion in the western marshes of Feng, stopped to drink, at night all released the convicts he was escorting.

entries.en: He said, “
entries.literal: He said, “

entries.zh: 公等皆去，吾亦從此逝矣！」
entries.en: You all go ahead. I'll take my leave from here too!"
entries.literal: You gentlemen all go, I also from here depart!'

entries.zh: 徒中壯士願從諸十餘人。
entries.en: Over ten strong men among the convicts wished to follow him.
entries.literal: Among the convicts the strong men who wished to follow were more than ten people.

entries.zh: 高祖被酒，夜徑澤中，令一人行前。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and at night went directly through the marsh, ordering one man to go ahead.
entries.literal: Gaozu was drunk, at night went straight through the marshes, ordered one person to go ahead.

entries.zh: 行前者還報曰：「
entries.en: The man sent ahead came back and reported, “
entries.literal: The one who went ahead returned and reported, “

entries.zh: 前有大蛇當徑，願還。」
entries.en: There is a large snake blocking the path ahead. We should turn back."
entries.literal: Ahead there is a large snake blocking the path, wish to turn back.'

entries.zh: 高祖醉，曰：「壯士行，何畏！」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "A brave man walks on. What is there to fear!"
entries.literal: Gaozu was drunk, said: 'A brave man walks forward, what is there to fear!'

entries.zh: 乃前，拔劍斬蛇。
entries.en: So he went forward and drew his sword to cut the snake.
entries.literal: Then went forward, drew sword and cut the snake.

entries.zh: 蛇分為兩，道開。
entries.en: The snake split into two, and the path opened.
entries.literal: The snake divided into two, the path opened.

entries.zh: 行數里，醉困臥。
entries.en: He walked several li, then lay down drunk and exhausted.
entries.literal: Walked several li, drunk and weary lay down.

entries.zh: 後人來至蛇所，有一老嫗夜哭。
entries.en: Later people came to the place where the snake was, and there was an old woman crying at night.
entries.literal: Later people came to the snake's location, there was an old woman crying at night.

entries.zh: 人問嫗何哭，嫗曰：「人殺吾子。」
entries.en: People asked the old woman why she was crying. The old woman said: "Someone killed my son."
entries.literal: People asked the old woman why she cried, the old woman said: 'A person killed my son.'

entries.zh: 人曰：「嫗子何為見殺？」
entries.en: People said: "Why was your son killed?"
entries.literal: People said: 'Old woman's son why was he killed?'

entries.zh: 嫗曰：「吾子，白帝子也，化為蛇，當道，今者赤帝子斬之，故哭。」
entries.en: The old woman said: "My son was the son of the White Emperor. He transformed into a snake and blocked the road. Just now, the son of the Red Emperor cut him down. That's why I'm crying."
entries.literal: Old woman said: 'My son was the son of the White Emperor, transformed into a snake, blocked the path, now the son of the Red Emperor cut him, therefore cry.'

entries.zh: 人乃以嫗為不誠，欲苦之，嫗因忽不見。
entries.en: The men thought the old woman was lying and wanted to punish her, but she suddenly disappeared.
entries.literal: People then considered the old woman not sincere, wished to harm her, the old woman thus suddenly disappeared.

entries.zh: 後人至，高祖覺。
entries.en: Later people arrived, and Emperor Gaozu woke up.
entries.literal: Later people arrived, Gaozu awoke.

entries.zh: 告高祖，高祖乃心獨喜，自負。
entries.en: They told Emperor Gaozu, who was secretly delighted and grew confident in himself.
entries.literal: Told Gaozu, Gaozu then in his heart alone rejoiced, considered himself superior.

entries.zh: 諸從者日益畏之。
entries.en: His followers grew increasingly fearful of him.
entries.literal: The various followers increasingly feared him.

entries.zh: 秦二世元年秋七月，陳涉起蘄，至陳，自立為楚王，遣武臣、張耳、陳餘略趙地。
entries.en: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi. He reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi, reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.

entries.zh: 八月，武臣自立為趙王。
entries.en: In the eighth month, Wu Chen set himself up as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Wu Chen set himself up as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 郡縣多殺長吏以應涉。
entries.en: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in response to Chen She.
entries.literal: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in order to respond to Chen She.

entries.zh: 九月，沛令欲以沛應之。
entries.en: In the ninth month, the magistrate of Pei wanted Pei to join the uprising in response to him.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, the magistrate of Pei wanted to respond to him with Pei.

entries.zh: 掾、主吏蕭何、曹參曰：「君為秦吏，今欲背之，帥沛子弟，恐不聽。
entries.en: The assistants and chief clerks Xiao He and Cao Shen said, "You are an official of Qin. If you now turn against it and try to lead the young men of Pei, we fear they will not obey.
entries.literal: The assistants and chief clerks Xiao He and Cao Shen said, "You are an official of Qin. If you now wish to turn your back on it and lead the young men of Pei, we fear they will not obey.

entries.zh: 願君召諸亡在外者，可得數百人，因以劫眾，眾不敢不聽。」
entries.en: We hope you will summon those fugitives who are outside. You can get several hundred men, and by using them to overawe the people, the people will not dare disobey."
entries.literal: We hope that you will summon those fugitives who are outside; you can get several hundred men, and by using them to overawe the people, the people will not dare not to obey."

entries.zh: 乃令樊噲召高祖。
entries.en: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.
entries.literal: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖之眾已數百人矣。
entries.en: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.
entries.literal: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.

entries.zh: 正月，張耳等立趙後趙歇為趙王。
entries.en: In the first month, Zhang Er and others established Zhao's former king Zhao Xie as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: First month, Zhang Er and others established Zhao descendant Zhao Xie as Zhao King.

entries.zh: 東陽甯君、秦嘉立景駒為楚王，在留。
entries.en: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Qin Jia established Jing Ju as King of Chu, stationed at Liu.
entries.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Qin Jia established Jing Ju as Chu King, at Liu.

entries.zh: 沛公往從之，道得張良，遂與俱見景駒，請兵以攻豐。
entries.en: Pei Gong went to join him, met Zhang Liang along the way, and together they went to see Jing Ju, requesting troops to attack Feng.
entries.literal: Pei Gong went to follow them, on the road obtained Zhang Liang, then together went to see Jing Ju, requested troops to attack Feng.

entries.zh: 時章邯從陳，別將司馬镛將兵北定楚地，屠相，至碭。
entries.en: At this time, Zhang Han was pursuing Chen, while his deputy general Sima Yiou led troops north to pacify Chu territory, massacring Xiang and reaching Dang.
entries.literal: At this time Zhang Han came from Chen, separate general Sima Ni led troops north to pacify Chu territory, massacred Xiang, arrived at Dang.

entries.zh: 東陽甯君、沛公引兵西，與戰蕭西，不利，還收兵聚留。
entries.en: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Pei Gong led troops west and battled west of Xiao, but were unsuccessful, so they retreated and gathered troops at Liu.
entries.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Pei Gong led troops west, fought battle at Xiao west, unfavorable, returned gathered troops at Liu.

entries.zh: 二月，攻碭，三日拔之。
entries.en: In the second month, they attacked Dang and captured it after three days.
entries.literal: Second month, attacked Dang, three days captured it.

entries.zh: 收碭兵，得六千人，與故合九千人。
entries.en: They recruited troops from Dang, getting six thousand men, and together with the previous troops made nine thousand.
entries.literal: Recruited Dang troops, got six thousand, combined with original made nine thousand.

entries.zh: 三月，攻下邑，拔之。
entries.en: In the third month, they attacked Xiayi and captured it.
entries.literal: Third month, attacked Xiayi, captured it.

entries.zh: 還擊豐，不下。
entries.en: They returned to attack Feng, but could not capture it.
entries.literal: Returned to attack Feng, could not capture.

entries.zh: 四月，項梁擊殺景駒、秦嘉，止薛，沛公往見之。
entries.en: In the fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju and Qin Jia, then stopped at Xue. Pei Gong went to see him.
entries.literal: Fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju, Qin Jia, stopped at Xue, Pei Gong went to see him.

entries.zh: 項梁益沛公卒五千人，五大夫將十人。
entries.en: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops by five thousand men and ten generals of the rank of Grand Master.
entries.literal: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops five thousand, Grand Master generals ten people.

entries.zh: 沛公還，引兵攻豐，拔之。
entries.en: Pei Gong returned and led troops to attack Feng, capturing it.
entries.literal: Pei Gong returned, led troops to attack Feng, captured it.

entries.zh: 雍齒奔魏。
entries.en: Yong Chi fled to the state of Wei.
entries.literal: Yong Chi fled to Wei.

entries.zh: 五月，項羽拔襄城還。
entries.en: In the fifth month, Xiang Yu captured Xiangcheng and returned.
entries.literal: Fifth month, Xiang Yu captured Xiangcheng and returned.

entries.zh: 項梁盡召別將。
entries.en: Xiang Liang summoned all his deputy generals.
entries.literal: Xiang Liang completely summoned the separate generals.

entries.zh: 六月，沛公如薛，與項梁共立楚懷王孫心為楚懷王。
entries.en: In the sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue and together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as King Huai of Chu.
entries.literal: Sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue, together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as Chu King Huai.

entries.zh: 章邯破殺魏王咎、齊王田儋於臨濟。
entries.en: Zhang Han defeated and killed King Jiu of Wei and King Tian Dan of Qi at Linji.
entries.literal: Zhang Han defeated and killed Wei King Jiu, Qi King Tian Dan at Linji.

entries.zh: 七月，大霖雨。
entries.en: In the seventh month, there was heavy continuous rain.
entries.literal: Seventh month, great continuous rain.

entries.zh: 沛公攻亢父。
entries.en: Pei Gong attacked Kangfu.
entries.literal: Pei Gong attacked Kang Fu.

entries.zh: 章邯圍田榮於東阿。
entries.en: Zhang Han besieged Tian Rong at Dong'e.
entries.literal: Zhang Han besieged Tian Rong at Dong'a.

entries.zh: 沛公與項梁共救田榮，大破章邯東阿。
entries.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Liang together went to rescue Tian Rong and greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'e.
entries.literal: Pei Gong together with Xiang Liang rescued Tian Rong, greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'a.

entries.zh: 田榮歸，沛公、項羽追北，至城陽，攻屠其城。
entries.en: Tian Rong returned. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu pursued the defeated enemy north to Chengyang and attacked, massacring the population of the city.
entries.literal: Tian Rong returned, Pei Gong, Xiang Yu pursued north, arrived at Chengyang, attacked and slaughtered its city.

entries.zh: 軍濮陽東，復與章邯戰，又破之。
entries.en: The army encamped east of Puyang and again battled Zhang Han, defeating him once more.
entries.literal: Camped east of Puyang, again fought with Zhang Han, again defeated him.

entries.zh: 章邯復振，守濮陽，環水。
entries.en: Zhang Han recovered his strength and defended Puyang, surrounding it with water.
entries.literal: Zhang Han again recovered, defended Puyang, surrounded by water.

entries.zh: 沛公、項羽去攻定陶。
entries.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.
entries.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.

entries.zh: 八月，田榮立田儋子市為齊王。
entries.en: In the eighth month, Tian Rong established Tian Dan's son Shi as King of Qi.
entries.literal: Eighth month, Tian Rong established Tian Dan's son Shi as Qi King.

entries.zh: 定陶未下，沛公與項羽西略地至雍丘，與秦軍戰，大敗之，斬三川守李由。
entries.en: Dingtao had not yet fallen. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu marched west to seize territory as far as Yongqiu, where they battled Qin troops and greatly defeated them, beheading the governor of Sanchuan, Li You.
entries.literal: Dingtao not yet fallen, Pei Gong together with Xiang Yu west conquered territory to Yongqiu, fought with Qin army, greatly defeated them, beheaded Sanchuan defender Li You.

entries.zh: 還攻外黃，外黃未下。
entries.en: They returned to attack Waihuang, but Waihuang did not fall.
entries.literal: Returned to attack Waihuang, Waihuang did not fall.

entries.zh: 項梁再破秦軍，有驕色。
entries.en: Xiang Liang defeated the Qin army again and showed arrogant bearing.
entries.literal: Xiang Liang again defeated Qin army, had arrogant appearance.

entries.zh: 宋義諫，不聽。
entries.en: Song Yi advised against it, but Xiang Liang did not listen.
entries.literal: Song Yi advised, did not listen.

entries.zh: 秦益章邯兵。
entries.en: Qin reinforced Zhang Han's army.
entries.literal: Qin increased Zhang Han's troops.

entries.zh: 九月，章邯夜銜枚擊項梁定陶，大破之，殺項梁。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Zhang Han bit on wooden sticks and attacked Xiang Liang at Dingtao by night, greatly defeating him and killing Xiang Liang.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Zhang Han night held wooden gag attacked Xiang Liang at Dingtao, greatly defeated him, killed Xiang Liang.

entries.zh: 時連雨自七月至九月。
entries.en: At this time there was continuous rain from the seventh month until the ninth month.
entries.literal: At this time continuous rain from seventh month to ninth month.

entries.zh: 沛公、項羽方攻陳留，聞梁死，士卒恐，乃與將軍呂臣引兵而東，徙懷王自盱台都彭城。
entries.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu were attacking Chenliu when they heard of Liang's death. The soldiers were terrified, so they joined with General Lü Chen and led troops east, moving King Huai from Xutai to Pengcheng as the capital.
entries.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu just attacking Chenliu, heard Liang died, soldiers afraid, then together with general Lu Chen led troops east, moved King Huai from Xutai capital to Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 呂臣軍彭城東，項羽軍彭城西，沛公軍碭。
entries.en: Lü Chen's army was stationed east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, and Pei Gong's army at Dang.
entries.literal: Lu Chen's army east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, Pei Gong's army at Dang.

entries.zh: 魏咎弟豹自立為魏王。
entries.en: Wei Jiu's younger brother Bao established himself as King of Wei.
entries.literal: Wei Jiu's younger brother Bao self-established as Wei King.

entries.zh: 後九月，懷王并呂臣、項羽軍自將之。
entries.en: In the ninth month afterward, King Huai combined Lü Chen and Xiang Yu's armies and personally took command.
entries.literal: After ninth month, King Huai merged Lu Chen, Xiang Yu's armies and personally led them.

entries.zh: 以沛公為碭郡長，封武安侯，將碭郡兵。
entries.en: He appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuan, and put him in command of Dang commandery troops.
entries.literal: Made Pei Gong Dang commandery chief, sealed as Marquis of Wuan, led Dang commandery troops.

entries.zh: 以羽為魯公，封長安侯，呂臣為司徒，其父呂青為令尹。
entries.en: He appointed Yu as Duke of Lu and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chang'an. Lü Chen became Minister of Works, and his father Lü Qing became Prime Minister.
entries.literal: Made Yu Duke of Lu, sealed as Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Chen as Minister of the Masses, his father Lu Qing as Prime Minister.

entries.zh: 初，懷王與諸將約，先入定關中者王之。
entries.en: Initially, King Huai had made an agreement with the generals that whoever first entered and pacified Guanzhong would be made king of it.
entries.literal: Originally, King Huai made agreement with various generals, the first to enter and pacify Guanzhong would be made king there.

entries.zh: 當是時，秦兵彊，常乘勝逐北，諸將莫利先入關。
entries.en: At this time, Qin troops were strong and often took advantage of victories to pursue defeated enemies. None of the generals saw benefit in being the first to enter the pass.
entries.literal: At this time, Qin troops strong, constantly took advantage of victory pursued retreating enemy, various generals none saw benefit in entering pass first.

entries.zh: 獨羽怨秦破項梁，奮勢，願與沛公西入關。
entries.en: Only Xiang Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang and was eager to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.
entries.literal: Only Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang, exerted his influence, wished to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.

entries.zh: 懷王諸老將皆曰：「項羽為人慓悍禍賊，嘗攻襄城，襄城無唣類，所過無不殘滅。
entries.en: King Huai's veteran generals all said: "Xiang Yu is fierce and violent, a man of disaster. He once attacked Xiangcheng, leaving no survivors in Xiangcheng. Wherever he passes, nothing is left undestroyed.
entries.literal: King Huai's various old generals all said: 'Xiang Yu as a person is fierce and violent, a calamitous bandit, once attacked Xiangcheng, Xiangcheng had no survivors, wherever he passed nothing was not completely destroyed.

entries.zh: 且楚數進取，前陳王、項梁皆敗，不如更遣長者扶義而西，告諭秦父兄。
entries.en: Moreover, Chu has repeatedly advanced but the former King Chen and Xiang Liang both failed. It would be better to send an elder who upholds righteousness to go west and inform the fathers and brothers of Qin.
entries.literal: Moreover Chu repeatedly advanced and took, previously King Chen, Xiang Liang all defeated, not as good as again send elder who upholds righteousness west, inform and persuade Qin fathers and elder brothers.

entries.zh: 秦父兄苦其主久矣，今誠得長者往，毋侵暴，宜可下。
entries.en: The fathers and brothers of Qin have suffered under their ruler for a long time. Now if we truly send an elder, without invasion or violence, the region should submit.
entries.literal: Qin fathers and elder brothers have suffered under their ruler for a long time, now truly if elder goes, do not invade violently, should be able to surrender.

entries.zh: 項羽不可遣，獨沛公素寬大長者。」
entries.en: Xiang Yu should not be sent. Only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and an elder."
entries.literal: Xiang Yu cannot be sent, only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and elder.'

entries.zh: 卒不許羽，而遣沛公西收陳王、項梁散卒。
entries.en: In the end they did not permit Xiang Yu, but sent Pei Gong west to gather the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang.
entries.literal: In the end did not permit Yu, instead sent Pei Gong west to gather King Chen, Xiang Liang's scattered troops.

entries.zh: 乃道碭至陽城與杠里，攻秦軍壁，破其二軍。
entries.en: So he went by way of Dang to Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin army fortifications, and broke two of their armies.
entries.literal: Then took the Dang road to Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin army fortifications, broke their two armies.

entries.zh: 秦三年十月，齊將田都畔田榮，將兵助項羽救趙。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the third year of Qin, Qi general Tian Du rebelled against Tian Rong and led troops to help Xiang Yu rescue Zhao.
entries.literal: Qin third year tenth month, Qi general Tian Du rebelled against Tian Rong, led troops to assist Xiang Yu rescue Zhao.

entries.zh: 沛公攻破東郡尉於成武。
entries.en: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dong commandery commandant at Chengwu.
entries.literal: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dongjun prefect at Chengwu.

entries.zh: 十一月，項羽殺宋義，并其兵渡河，自立為上將軍，諸將黥布等皆屬。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Xiang Yu killed Song Yi and took his troops, crossed the river, and established himself as supreme commander. Generals like Ying Bu and others all came under his command.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, Xiang Yu killed Song Yi, merged his troops crossed the river, self-established as supreme general, various generals Ying Bu and others all belonged to him.

entries.zh: 十二月，沛公引兵至栗，遇剛武侯，奪其軍四千餘人，并之，與魏將皇欣、武滿軍合，攻秦軍，破之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li and encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized over four thousand of his men, and combined them. He joined with Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man's army and attacked Qin troops, defeating them.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li, encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized his army more than four thousand people, merged them, combined with Wei generals Huang Xin, Wu Man armies, attacked Qin army, defeated it.

entries.zh: 故齊王建孫田安下濟北，從項羽救趙。
entries.en: Former Qi King Jian's grandson Tian An captured Jibei and followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao.
entries.literal: Former Qi King Jian's grandson Tian An went down north of Ji, followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao.

entries.zh: 羽大破秦軍鉅鹿下，虜王離，走章邯。
entries.en: Xiang Yu greatly defeated the Qin army at Julu, captured Wang Li, and drove away Zhang Han.
entries.literal: Yu greatly defeated Qin army below Julu, captured Wang Li, routed Zhang Han.

entries.zh: 二月，沛公從碭北攻昌邑，遇彭越。
entries.en: In the second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi and encountered Peng Yue.
entries.literal: Second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi, encountered Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 越助攻昌邑，未下。
entries.en: Yue helped attack Changyi, but it did not fall.
entries.literal: Yue helped attack Changyi, did not fall.

entries.zh: 沛公西過高陽，酈食其為里監門，曰：「諸將過此者多，吾視沛公大度。」
entries.en: Pei Gong passed west through Gaoyang. Li Yiji was the village gatekeeper and said: "Many generals have passed through here. I can see that Pei Gong has great magnanimity."
entries.literal: Pei Gong west passed Gaoyang, Li Yiji was village gatekeeper, said: 'Various generals who passed this place many, I observe Pei Gong has great magnanimity.'

entries.zh: 乃求見沛公。
entries.en: So he sought to see Pei Gong.
entries.literal: Then requested to see Pei Gong.

entries.zh: 沛公方踞床，使兩女子洗。
entries.en: Pei Gong was sitting cross-legged on a bed, having two women wash his feet.
entries.literal: Pei Gong just then squatting on bed, made two women wash.

entries.zh: 酈生不拜，長揖曰：「足下必欲誅無道秦，不宜踞見長者。」
entries.en: Li Sheng did not bow but gave a deep bow and said: "If you truly wish to execute the tyrannical Qin, you should not sit cross-legged when receiving elders."
entries.literal: Li Sheng did not bow, gave long bow said: 'Your excellency certainly wishes to execute unrighteous Qin, should not lounge to see elders.'

entries.zh: 於是沛公起，攝衣謝之，延上坐。
entries.en: So Pei Gong rose, straightened his clothes, and apologized. He invited him to sit in the honored position.
entries.literal: Thereupon Pei Gong rose, gathered clothes thanked him, invited to upper seat.

entries.zh: 食其說沛公襲陳留。
entries.en: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.
entries.literal: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.

entries.zh: 沛公以為廣野君，以其弟商為將，將陳留兵。
entries.en: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.
entries.literal: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.

entries.zh: 三月，攻開封，未拔。
entries.en: In the third month, they attacked Kaifeng but failed to capture it.
entries.literal: In the third month, they attacked Kaifeng but failed to capture it.

entries.zh: 西與秦將楊熊會戰白馬，又戰曲遇東，大破之。
entries.en: They met Qin general Yang Xiong in battle at Baima to the west, and again at Quyu to the east, greatly defeating him.
entries.literal: They met Qin general Yang Xiong in battle at Baima to the west, and again at Quyu to the east, greatly defeating him.

entries.zh: 楊熊走之滎陽，二世使使斬之以徇。
entries.en: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang. The Second Emperor sent an envoy to execute him as a warning to others.
entries.literal: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang. The Second Emperor sent an envoy to execute him as a warning to others.

entries.zh: 四月，南攻潁川，屠之。
entries.en: In the fourth month, they attacked Yingchuan to the south and massacred the population.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, they attacked Yingchuan to the south and massacred the population.

entries.zh: 因張良遂略韓地。
entries.en: Through Zhang Liang, they then seized the lands of Han.
entries.literal: Through Zhang Liang, they then seized the lands of Han.

entries.zh: 時趙別將司馬卬方欲渡河入關，沛公乃北攻平陰，絕河津。
entries.en: At this time, Sima Ang, a separate Zhao general, was about to cross the Yellow River and enter the passes. Pei Gong therefore attacked Pingyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.
entries.literal: At this time, the Zhao general Sima Ang was about to cross the river into the passes. Pei Gong attacked Beiyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.

entries.zh: 南，戰雒陽東，軍不利，從轘轅至陽城，收軍中馬騎。
entries.en: To the south, they fought east of Luoyang, but the army fared badly. They withdrew from Huanyuan to Yangcheng and gathered the cavalry from the army.
entries.literal: To the south, they fought east of Luoyang. The battle went badly. They retreated from Huan Pass to Yangcheng and gathered cavalry from among the troops.

entries.zh: 六月，與南陽守齮戰犨東，大破之。
entries.en: In the sixth month, they fought Nanyang governor Yin east of Chu, greatly defeating him.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, they fought Nanyang governor Yin east of Chu, greatly defeating him.

entries.zh: 略南陽郡，南陽守走，保城守宛。
entries.en: They seized Nanyang commandery. The Nanyang governor fled and defended the city of Wan.
entries.literal: They seized Nanyang commandery. The Nanyang governor fled and defended the city of Wan.

entries.zh: 沛公引兵過宛西。
entries.en: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.
entries.literal: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.

entries.zh: 張良諫曰：「沛公雖欲急入關，秦兵尚眾，距險。
entries.en: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.
entries.literal: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.

entries.zh: 今不下宛，宛從後擊，彊秦在前，此危道也。」
entries.en: If we do not take Wan now, Wan will attack from behind while the strong Qin face us ahead. This is a dangerous path."
entries.literal: If we do not take Wan now, Wan will attack from behind while the strong Qin face us ahead. This is a dangerous path."

entries.zh: 於是沛公乃夜引軍從他道還，偃旗幟，遲明，圍宛城三匝。
entries.en: So Pei Gong led his army back by another route at night, hid his banners, and at dawn surrounded Wan city three times.
entries.literal: So Pei Gong led his army back by another route at night, hid his banners, and at dawn surrounded Wan city three times.

entries.zh: 南陽守欲自剄，其舍人陳恢曰：「死未晚也。」
entries.en: The Nanyang governor was about to commit suicide, but his aide Chen Hei said: "It is not yet time to die."
entries.literal: The Nanyang governor was about to commit suicide, but his aide Chen Hei said: "It is not yet time to die."

entries.zh: 乃踰城見沛公，曰：「臣聞足下約先入咸陽者王之，今足下留守宛。
entries.en: He therefore climbed over the wall to meet Pei Gong and said, "I have heard that you agreed that whoever first entered Xianyang would be made king there. Now you are staying here to besiege Wan.
entries.literal: So he climbed over the wall to see Pei Gong and said: "I have heard that you promised to enfeoff as king whoever first entered Xianyang. Now you remain besieging Wan.

entries.zh: 宛郡縣連城數十，其吏民自以為降必死，故皆堅守乘城。
entries.en: Wan Commandery has dozens of linked walled cities. Its officials and people believe that if they surrender they will certainly die, so they are all firmly defending the walls.
entries.literal: Wan commandery has dozens of walled cities connected together. Its officials and people believe they will certainly die if they surrender, so they all defend their walls firmly.

entries.zh: 今足下盡日止攻，士死傷者必多；
entries.en: If you continue attacking all day, your soldiers who die and are wounded will certainly be many;
entries.literal: If you continue attacking all day, your soldiers who die and are wounded will certainly be many;

entries.zh: 引兵去宛，宛必隨足下。
entries.en: Lead your troops away from Wan, and Wan will certainly follow you.
entries.literal: Lead your troops away from Wan, and Wan will certainly follow you.

entries.zh: 足下前則失咸陽之約，後有彊宛之患。
entries.en: Ahead you lose the agreement about Xianyang, behind you have the danger of strong Wan.
entries.literal: Ahead you lose the agreement about Xianyang, behind you have the danger of strong Wan.

entries.zh: 為足下計，莫若約降，封其守，因使止守，引其甲卒與之西。
entries.en: In planning for you, nothing would be better than agreeing on his surrender, enfeoffing its governor, and then ordering him to remain in charge while leading his armored troops west with you.
entries.literal: For your sake, it would be better to make a treaty for surrender, enfeoff the governor, and then order him to remain as governor, leading his armored troops west with you.

entries.zh: 諸城未下者，聞聲爭開門而待足下，足下通行無所累。」
entries.en: The cities not yet taken will hear of this and compete to open their gates to await you. You will pass through without obstruction."
entries.literal: The cities that have not yet surrendered will hear of this and compete to open their gates waiting for you. You will pass through without hindrance."

entries.zh: 沛公曰：「善。」
entries.en: Pei Gong said: "Excellent."
entries.literal: Pei Gong said: "Excellent."

entries.zh: 七月，南陽守齮降，封為殷侯，封陳恢千戶。
entries.en: In the seventh month, Nanyang governor Yin surrendered. He was enfeoffed as Lord Yin, and Chen Hei was enfeoffed with a thousand households.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, Nanyang governor Yin surrendered. He was enfeoffed as Lord Yin, and Chen Hei was enfeoffed with a thousand households.

entries.zh: 引兵西，無不下者。
entries.en: He led troops west, and there was no city that did not surrender.
entries.literal: He led troops west, and there was no city that did not surrender.

entries.zh: 至丹水，高武侯鰓、襄侯王陵降。
entries.en: He reached Danshui. Lord Gaowu Gai and Lord Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.
entries.literal: He reached Danshui. Lord Gaowu Gai and Lord Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.

entries.zh: 還攻胡陽，遇番君別將梅鋗，與偕攻析、酈，皆降。
entries.en: Returning to attack Huyang, he encountered Fan Jun's separate general Mei Zhu, and together they attacked Xi and Li, all of which surrendered.
entries.literal: Returning to attack Huyang, he encountered Fan Jun's separate general Mei Zhu, and together they attacked Xi and Li, all of which surrendered.

entries.zh: 所過毋得鹵掠，秦民喜。
entries.en: Wherever they passed, they did not plunder. The Qin people rejoiced.
entries.literal: Wherever they passed, they did not plunder. The Qin people rejoiced.

entries.zh: 遣魏人甯昌使秦。
entries.en: He sent the Wei man Ning Chang as envoy to Qin.
entries.literal: He sent the Wei man Ning Chang as envoy to Qin.

entries.zh: 是月章邯舉軍降項羽，羽以為雍王。
entries.en: In this month, Zhang Han led his entire army to surrender to Xiang Yu, who enfeoffed him as King of Yong.
entries.literal: In this month, Zhang Han led his entire army to surrender to Xiang Yu, who enfeoffed him as King of Yong.

entries.zh: 瑕丘申陽下河南。
entries.en: Xiaqiu Shen Yang took Henan.
entries.literal: Xiaqiu Shen Yang took Henan.

entries.zh: 元年冬十月，五星聚于東井。
entries.en: In the first year, in winter, in the tenth month, the five planets gathered at Eastern Well.
entries.literal: In the first year, in winter, in the tenth month, the five planets gathered at Eastern Well.

entries.zh: 沛公至霸上。
entries.en: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.
entries.literal: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.

entries.zh: 秦王子嬰素車白馬，係頸以組，封皇帝璽符節，降枳道旁。
entries.en: Ziying, King of Qin, came with a plain carriage and white horses, bound his neck with a cord, sealed up the emperor's seals, tallies, and credentials, and surrendered beside Zhidao.
entries.literal: Ziying, King of Qin, with a plain carriage and white horses, bound his neck with a cord, sealed up the emperor's seals, tallies, and credentials, and surrendered beside Zhidao.

entries.zh: 諸將或言誅秦王，沛公曰：「始懷王遣我，固以能寬容，且人已服降，殺之不祥。」
entries.en: Some of the generals said that the King of Qin should be executed. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient. Moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered; to kill him would be inauspicious."
entries.literal: Some of the generals said to execute the King of Qin. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient; moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered, and to kill him would be inauspicious."

entries.zh: 乃以屬吏。
entries.en: He then handed him over to the officials.
entries.literal: He then handed him over to the officials.

entries.zh: 遂西入咸陽，欲止宮休舍。
entries.en: He then went west into Xianyang and wanted to stop and rest in the palace.
entries.literal: Then he entered Xianyang in the west and wanted to stop and rest in the palace.

entries.zh: 樊噲、張良諫，乃封秦重寶財物府庫，還軍霸上。
entries.en: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.
entries.literal: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.

entries.zh: 蕭何盡收秦丞相府圖籍文書。
entries.en: Xiao He collected all the maps, registers, documents, and writings from the office of the Qin chancellor.
entries.literal: Xiao He collected all the maps, registers, documents, and writings from the office of the Qin chancellor.

entries.zh: 十一月，召諸縣豪桀曰：「父老苦秦苛法久矣，誹謗者族，耦語者棄市。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, he summoned the leading men of the counties and said, "The elders have long suffered from Qin's harsh laws: those who criticized the government were exterminated by clan, and those who spoke together were executed in the marketplace.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, he summoned the leading men of the counties and said, "The elders have long suffered from Qin's harsh laws: those who criticized were exterminated by clan, and those who spoke together were executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。
entries.en: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.
entries.literal: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 與父老約，法三章耳：殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。
entries.en: I make this agreement with the elders: there will be only three articles of law. Those who kill shall die; those who wound others and those who steal shall answer for their crimes.
entries.literal: I make an agreement with the elders: there are only three articles of law. Those who kill shall die; those who wound others and those who steal shall answer for their crimes.

entries.zh: 餘悉除去秦法。
entries.en: All the rest of the Qin laws are abolished.
entries.literal: All the rest of the Qin laws are removed.

entries.zh: 吏民皆按堵如故。
entries.en: Officials and people should all remain settled as before.
entries.literal: Officials and people should all remain settled as before.

entries.zh: 凡吾所以來，為父兄除害，非有所侵暴，毋恐！
entries.en: The whole reason I have come is to remove harm for my fathers and elder brothers; I have not come to invade or oppress you, so do not be afraid!
entries.literal: In general, the reason I have come is to remove harm for my fathers and elder brothers; it is not that there is any invasion or violence, so do not be afraid!

entries.zh: 且吾所以軍霸上，待諸侯至而定要束耳。」
entries.en: Moreover, the reason I have stationed the army at Bashang is only to wait for the feudal lords to arrive and settle the agreements."
entries.literal: Moreover, the reason I have stationed the army at Bashang is only to wait for the feudal lords to arrive and settle the agreements."

entries.zh: 乃使人與秦吏行至縣鄉邑告諭之。
entries.en: He then sent people together with Qin officials to go to the counties, townships, and settlements and proclaim this to them.
entries.literal: He then sent people together with Qin officials to go to the counties, townships, and settlements and proclaim this to them.

entries.zh: 秦民大喜，爭持牛羊酒食獻享軍士。
entries.en: The people of Qin were greatly delighted, and they vied with one another to bring cattle, sheep, wine, and food to present to the soldiers.
entries.literal: The people of Qin were greatly delighted and vied in bringing cattle, sheep, wine, and food to present to and feast the soldiers.

entries.zh: 沛公讓不受，曰：「倉粟多，不欲費民。」
entries.en: The Duke of Pei declined and would not accept them, saying, "There is abundant grain in the granaries, and I do not want to burden the people."
entries.literal: The Duke of Pei declined and would not accept them, saying, "There is much grain in the granaries, and I do not wish to burden the people."

entries.zh: 民又益喜，唯恐沛公不為秦王。
entries.en: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.
entries.literal: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.

entries.zh: 三月，漢王自臨晉渡河，魏王豹降，將兵從。
entries.en: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.
entries.literal: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.

entries.zh: 下河內，虜殷王卬，置河內郡。
entries.en: He reduced Henei, captured King Yin Ang, and established Henei Commandery.
entries.literal: He took Henan and captured King Yin Ang, establishing Henan commandery.

entries.zh: 至脩武，陳平亡楚來降。
entries.en: He reached Xiuwu. Chen Ping deserted Chu and came to surrender.
entries.literal: He reached Xiuwu. Chen Ping deserted Chu and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 漢王與語，說之，使參乘，監諸將。
entries.en: King Han spoke with him and was pleased. He had him ride in the chariot and oversee the various generals.
entries.literal: King Han spoke with him and was pleased. He had him ride in the chariot and oversee the various generals.

entries.zh: 南渡平陰津，至洛陽，新城三老董公遮說漢王曰：「臣聞『順德者昌，逆德者亡』，『兵出無名，事故不成』。
entries.en: He crossed south at Pingyin Ford and reached Luoyang. Dong Gong, the elder of Xincheng, stopped the King of Han and advised him: "I have heard, 'Those who follow virtue prosper; those who oppose virtue perish,' and, 'When troops are sent out without a proper name, the enterprise will not succeed.'
entries.literal: He crossed south at Pingyin ford and reached Luoyang. The elder of Xincheng, Dong Gong, blocked and advised King Han: "I have heard that 'those who follow virtue prosper, those who oppose virtue perish,' and 'when troops are sent out without just cause, affairs will not succeed.'

entries.zh: 故曰：『明其為賊，敵乃可服。』
entries.en: Therefore it is said: 'Make clear that he is the traitor, and the enemy can then be subdued.'
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: 'Make clear that he is the traitor, and the enemy can then be subdued.'

entries.zh: 項羽為無道，放殺其主，天下之賊也。
entries.en: Xiang Yu acts without righteousness, having deposed and killed his lord. He is the traitor of the world.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu acts without righteousness, having deposed and killed his lord. He is the traitor of the world.

entries.zh: 夫仁不以勇，義不以力，三軍之眾為之素服，以告之諸侯，為此東伐，四海之內莫不仰德。
entries.en: Benevolence does not rely on bravery, righteousness does not rely on force. Have the armies dress in mourning and proclaim this to the feudal lords, then march east—all within the four seas will look up to your virtue.
entries.literal: Benevolence does not rely on bravery, righteousness does not rely on strength. The multitudes of the three armies will sincerely submit to you. Proclaim this to the feudal lords and then advance east. All within the four seas will look up to your virtue.

entries.zh: 此三王之舉也。」
entries.en: This is the course of action of the Three Kings."
entries.literal: This is the undertaking of the Three Kings."

entries.zh: 漢王曰：「善，非夫子無所聞。」
entries.en: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."
entries.literal: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."

entries.zh: 於是漢王為義帝發喪，袒而大哭，哀臨三日。
entries.en: So King Han held mourning rites for the Righteous Emperor, bared his shoulder and wept loudly, conducting the mourning rites for three days.
entries.literal: So King Han held mourning rites for the Righteous Emperor, bared his shoulder and wept loudly, conducting the mourning rites for three days.

entries.zh: 發使告諸侯曰：「
entries.en: He sent envoys to proclaim to the lords, “
entries.literal: He sent envoys to proclaim to the feudal lords, “

entries.zh: 五月，將軍紀信曰：「事急矣！
entries.en: In the fifth month, General Ji Xin said: "The situation is urgent!
entries.literal: In the fifth month, General Ji Xin said: "The situation is urgent!

entries.zh: 臣請誑楚，可以間出。」
entries.en: I request to deceive Chu so we can break out."
entries.literal: I request to deceive Chu so we can break out."

entries.zh: 於是陳平夜出女子東門二千餘人，楚因四面擊之。
entries.en: So Chen Ping at night sent out over 2,000 women through the east gate. Chu then attacked from all four sides.
entries.literal: So Chen Ping at night sent out over 2,000 women through the east gate. Chu then attacked from all four sides.

entries.zh: 紀信乃乘王車，黃屋左纛，曰：「食盡，漢王降楚。」
entries.en: Ji Xin then rode in the king's chariot with yellow canopy and left banner, saying: "Food is exhausted. King Han surrenders to Chu."
entries.literal: Ji Xin then rode in the king's chariot with yellow canopy and left banner, saying: "Food is exhausted. King Han surrenders to Chu."

entries.zh: 楚皆呼萬歲，之城東觀，以故漢王得與數十騎出西門遁。
entries.en: All the Chu troops shouted, "Ten thousand years!" and went to the eastern side of the city to watch. Because of this, the King of Han escaped through the west gate with several dozen riders.
entries.literal: All the Chu troops shouted ten thousand years. They went to the east wall to watch, so King Han was able to escape with several dozen cavalry through the west gate.

entries.zh: 令御史大夫周苛、魏豹、樅公守滎陽。
entries.en: He ordered Imperial Secretary Zhou Ke, Wei Bao, and Lord Song to defend Xingyang.
entries.literal: He ordered Imperial Secretary Zhou Ke, Wei Bao, and Lord Song to defend Xingyang.

entries.zh: 羽見紀信，問：「漢王安在？」
entries.en: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"
entries.literal: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"

entries.zh: 曰：「已出去矣。」
entries.en: Ji Xin said: "He has already left."
entries.literal: He said: "He has already left."

entries.zh: 羽燒殺信。
entries.en: Xiang Yu burned and killed Xin.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu burned and killed Xin.

entries.zh: 而周苛、樅公相謂曰：「反國之王，難與守城。」
entries.en: Zhou Ke and Lord Song said to each other: "He is a rebel king—we cannot hold the city with him."
entries.literal: Zhou Ke and Lord Song said to each other: "The king of a rebellious kingdom is difficult to defend the city with."

entries.zh: 因殺魏豹。
entries.en: So they killed Wei Bao.
entries.literal: So they killed Wei Bao.

entries.zh: 項羽自知少助食盡，韓信又進兵擊楚，羽患之。
entries.en: Xiang Yu knew that he had few allies and that his food was exhausted. Han Xin was again advancing troops to attack Chu, and Xiang Yu was troubled by this.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu knew he had few helpers and food was exhausted. Han Xin again advanced troops to attack Chu. Xiang Yu was troubled by this.

entries.zh: 漢遣陸賈說羽，請太公，羽弗聽。
entries.en: Han sent Lu Jia to persuade Xiang Yu to return the Duke of Tai. Xiang Yu did not listen.
entries.literal: Han sent Lu Jia to persuade Xiang Yu to return the Duke of Tai. Xiang Yu did not listen.

entries.zh: 漢復使侯公說羽，羽乃與漢約，中分天下，割鴻溝以西為漢，以東為楚。
entries.en: Han again sent Hou Gong to persuade Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu then made an agreement with Han to divide the realm in two, assigning the lands west of Honggou to Han and those east of it to Chu.
entries.literal: Han again sent Hou Gong to persuade Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu then made a treaty with Han to divide the world in half, giving Honggou west to Han and east to Chu.

entries.zh: 九月，歸太公、呂后，軍皆稱萬歲。
entries.en: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.

entries.zh: 乃封侯公為平國君。
entries.en: He then enfeoffed Hou Gong as Lord of Pingguo.
entries.literal: He then enfeoffed Hou Gong as Lord of Pingguo.

entries.zh: 羽解而東歸。
entries.en: Xiang Yu withdrew and returned east.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu withdrew and returned east.

entries.zh: 漢王欲西歸，張良、陳平諫曰：「今漢有天下太半，而諸侯皆附，楚兵罷食盡，此天亡之時，不因其幾而遂取之，所謂養虎自遺患也。」
entries.en: The King of Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised him: "Han now possesses more than half the realm, and all the feudal lords have attached themselves to it. Chu's troops are exhausted and its food is gone. This is the moment when Heaven is destroying Chu. If we do not seize this opportunity and take it, that is what is called raising a tiger and leaving disaster for oneself."
entries.literal: King Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised: "Now Han possesses more than half the world, and all the feudal lords are attached. Chu troops are exhausted and food is finished. This is the time Heaven has doomed them. If we do not take advantage of this opportunity to destroy them, this is called raising a tiger that brings disaster to oneself."

entries.zh: 漢王從之。
entries.en: King Han followed their advice.
entries.literal: King Han followed their advice.

entries.zh: 二月，羽自立為西楚霸王，王梁、楚地九郡，都彭城。
entries.en: In the second month, Xiang Yu established himself as Hegemon-King of Western Chu, ruling the nine commanderies of Liang and Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng.
entries.literal: In the second month, Xiang Yu established himself as Hegemon King of Western Chu, ruling the lands of Liang and Chu, nine commanderies, with capital at Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 背約，更立沛公為漢王，王巴、蜀、漢中四十一縣，都南鄭。
entries.en: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.
entries.literal: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.

entries.zh: 三分關中，立秦三將：章邯為雍王，都廢丘；
entries.en: He divided Guanzhong into three parts, establishing the three Qin generals: Zhang Han as King of Yong, capital at Feiqiu;
entries.literal: He divided Guanzhong into three parts, establishing the three Qin generals: Zhang Han as King of Yong, capital at Feiqiu;

entries.zh: 司馬欣為塞王，都櫟陽；
entries.en: Sima Xin as King of Sai, capital at Queyang;
entries.literal: Sima Xin as King of Sai, capital at Queyang;

entries.zh: 董翳為翟王，都高奴。
entries.en: Dong Yi as King of Di, capital at Gaonu.
entries.literal: Dong Yi as King of Di, capital at Gaonu.

entries.zh: 楚將瑕丘申陽為河南王，都洛陽。
entries.en: Chu general Xiaqiu Shen Yang as King of Henan, capital at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Chu general Xiaqiu Shen Yang as King of Henan, capital at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 趙將司馬卬為殷王，都朝歌。
entries.en: Zhao general Sima Ang as King of Yin, capital at Zhaoge.
entries.literal: Zhao general Sima Ang as King of Yin, capital at Zhaoge.

entries.zh: 當陽君英布為九江王，都六。
entries.en: Dangyang Lord Ying Bu as King of Jiujiang, capital at Liu.
entries.literal: Dangyang Lord Ying Bu as King of Jiujiang, capital at Liu.

entries.zh: 懷王柱國共敖為臨江王，都江陵。
entries.en: King Huai's Pillar of State Gong Ao as King of Linjiang, capital at Jiangling.
entries.literal: King Huai's Pillar of State Gong Ao as King of Linjiang, capital at Jiangling.

entries.zh: 番君吳芮為衡山王，都邾。
entries.en: Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Hengshan, capital at Zhu.
entries.literal: Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Hengshan, capital at Zhu.

entries.zh: 故齊王建孫田安為濟北王。
entries.en: The former King of Qi Jian's grandson Tian An as King of Jibei.
entries.literal: The former King of Qi Jian's grandson Tian An as King of Jibei.

entries.zh: 徙魏王豹為西魏王，都平陽。
entries.en: Moved King of Wei Bao to King of Western Wei, capital at Pingyang.
entries.literal: Moved King of Wei Bao to King of Western Wei, capital at Pingyang.

entries.zh: 徙燕王韓廣為遼東王。
entries.en: Moved King of Yan Han Guang to King of Liaodong.
entries.literal: Moved King of Yan Han Guang to King of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 燕將臧荼為燕王，都薊。
entries.en: Yan general Zang Tu as King of Yan, capital at Ji.
entries.literal: Yan general Zang Tu as King of Yan, capital at Ji.

entries.zh: 徙齊王田市為膠東王。
entries.en: Moved King of Qi Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: Moved King of Qi Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 齊將田都為齊王，都臨菑。
entries.en: Qi general Tian Du as King of Qi, capital at Linzi.
entries.literal: Qi general Tian Du as King of Qi, capital at Linzi.

entries.zh: 徙趙王歇為代王。
entries.en: Moved King of Zhao Xie to King of Dai.
entries.literal: Moved King of Zhao Xie to King of Dai.

entries.zh: 趙相張耳為常山王。
entries.en: Zhao chancellor Zhang Er as King of Changshan.
entries.literal: Zhao chancellor Zhang Er as King of Changshan.

entries.zh: 漢王怨羽之背約，欲攻之，丞相蕭何諫，乃止。
entries.en: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.
entries.literal: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.

entries.zh: 或說沛公曰：「秦富十倍天下，地形彊。
entries.en: Someone advised Pei Gong: "Qin is ten times as wealthy as all the rest of the realm, and its terrain is strong.
entries.literal: Someone advised Pei Gong: "Qin is ten times richer than the world, and its terrain is strong.

entries.zh: 今聞章邯降項羽，羽號曰雍王，王關中。
entries.en: Now we hear that Zhang Han has surrendered to Xiang Yu, who is titled King of Yong and rules Guanzhong.
entries.literal: Now we hear that Zhang Han has surrendered to Xiang Yu, who is titled King of Yong and rules Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 即來，沛公恐不得有此。
entries.en: If he comes, you may not be able to keep this.
entries.literal: If he comes, Pei Gong fears he may not be able to hold this.

entries.zh: 可急使守函谷關，毋內諸侯軍，稍徵關中兵以自益，距之。」
entries.en: We should quickly send men to defend Hangu Pass, keep the armies of the feudal lords from entering, gradually call up Guanzhong troops to strengthen ourselves, and resist them."
entries.literal: We can urgently send people to defend Hangu Pass and not let the feudal lords' armies enter, gradually conscript Guanzhong troops to strengthen ourselves, and resist them."

entries.zh: 沛公然其計，從之。
entries.en: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.
entries.literal: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.

entries.zh: 十二月，項羽果帥諸侯兵欲西入關，關門閉。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Xiang Yu did indeed lead the troops of the feudal lords westward to enter the passes, but the pass gates were closed.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiang Yu indeed led the feudal lords' troops wanting to enter the passes to the west, but the pass gates were closed.

entries.zh: 聞沛公已定關中，羽大怒，使黥布等攻破函谷關，遂至戲下。
entries.en: When he heard that Pei Gong had already pacified Guanzhong, Xiang Yu was furious and sent Ying Bu and others to break through Hangu Pass, then advanced to Xi.
entries.literal: He heard that Pei Gong had already pacified Guanzhong. Xiang Yu was greatly angered and sent Ying Bu and others to break through Hangu Pass, then reached Xixia.

entries.zh: 沛公左司馬曹毋傷聞羽怒，欲攻沛公，使人言羽曰：「沛公欲王關中，令子嬰相，珍寶盡有之。」
entries.en: Cao Wushang, Pei Gong's Left Marshal, heard that Xiang Yu was angry and wanted to attack Pei Gong. He sent someone to tell Xiang Yu, "Pei Gong wants to become king of Guanzhong, make Zi Ying his chancellor, and keep all the precious treasures."
entries.literal: Pei Gong's left marshal Cao Wushang heard of Xiang Yu's anger and wanted to attack Pei Gong. He sent someone to tell Xiang Yu: "Pei Gong wants to become king of Guanzhong and has Zi Ying as chancellor, possessing all the precious treasures."

entries.zh: 欲以求封。
entries.en: He wanted to seek enfeoffment through this.
entries.literal: He wanted to seek enfeoffment through this.

entries.zh: 亞父范增說羽曰：「沛公居山東時，貪財好色，今聞其入關，珍物無所取，婦女無所幸，此其志不小。
entries.en: Fan Zeng, the Second Father, advised Xiang Yu: "When Pei Gong was east of the mountains, he was greedy for wealth and fond of women. Now we hear that after entering the passes, he has taken no precious objects and favored no women. His ambitions are not small.
entries.literal: Prime Minister Fan Zeng advised Xiang Yu: "When Pei Gong was in Shandong, he was greedy for wealth and fond of women. Now we hear that upon entering the passes, he has taken none of the precious objects and favored none of the women. His ambitions are not small.

entries.zh: 吾使人望其氣，皆為龍，成五色，此天子氣。
entries.en: I sent people to observe his aura, and it was all dragon-shaped, forming five colors. This is the aura of a Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: I sent people to observe his aura, and it was all dragon-shaped, forming five colors. This is the aura of a Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 急擊之，勿失。」
entries.en: Attack him urgently. Do not miss the opportunity."
entries.literal: Attack him urgently. Do not miss the opportunity."

entries.zh: 於是饗士，旦日合戰。
entries.en: So he feasted his troops and the next day engaged in battle.
entries.literal: So he feasted his troops and the next day engaged in battle.

entries.zh: 是時，羽兵四十萬，號百萬。
entries.en: At this time, Xiang Yu's troops numbered 400,000, claiming 1,000,000.
entries.literal: At this time, Xiang Yu's troops numbered 400,000, claiming 1,000,000.

entries.zh: 沛公兵十萬，號二十萬，力不敵。
entries.en: Pei Gong's troops numbered 100,000, claiming 200,000. Their strength was no match.
entries.literal: Pei Gong's troops numbered 100,000, claiming 200,000. Their strength was no match.

entries.zh: 會羽季父左尹項伯素善張良，夜馳見張良，具告其實，欲與俱去，毋特俱死。
entries.en: Xiang Yu's uncle, Left Yin Xiang Bo, had long been on good terms with Zhang Liang. He galloped at night to see Zhang Liang, told him everything in detail, and wanted Zhang Liang to leave with him rather than perish together for nothing.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu's uncle Xiang Bo had long been on good terms with Zhang Liang. He galloped at night to see Zhang Liang and told him everything in detail. He wanted to leave with him and not die together.

entries.zh: 良曰：「臣為韓王送沛公，不可不告，亡去不義。」
entries.en: Liang said, "The King of Han sent me to escort Pei Gong. I cannot fail to inform him; to flee would be unrighteous."
entries.literal: Liang said: "I was sent by the King of Han to escort Pei Gong. I cannot fail to inform him. To flee would be unrighteous."

entries.zh: 乃與項伯俱見沛公。
entries.en: So he went with Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong.
entries.literal: So he went with Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong.

entries.zh: 沛公與伯約為婚姻，曰：「吾入關，秋豪無所敢取，籍吏民，封府庫，待將軍。
entries.en: Pei Gong formed a marriage alliance with Xiang Bo and said: "When I entered the passes, I dared not take even the smallest thing. I registered the officials and people, sealed the storehouses and treasuries, and waited for the general.
entries.literal: Pei Gong made a marriage alliance with Xiang Bo and said: "When I entered the passes, I dared not take even the smallest thing. I registered the officials and people, sealed the treasuries, and waited for the general.

entries.zh: 所以守關者，備他盜也。
entries.en: The reason I guarded the passes was to prepare against other bandits.
entries.literal: The reason I guarded the passes was to prepare against other bandits.

entries.zh: 日夜望將軍到，豈敢反邪！
entries.en: Day and night I hoped for the general's arrival. How could I dare rebel!
entries.literal: Day and night I hoped for the general's arrival. How could I dare rebel!

entries.zh: 願伯明言不敢背德。」
