entries.zh: 異日秦民爵公大夫以上，令丞與 亢禮。
entries.en: In former days Qin people with ranks of public official and Grand Master and above, the county magistrate and assistant treated them with equal ceremony.
entries.literal: In former days Qin people with ranks of public official and grand master and above, the county magistrate and assistant treated them with equal ceremony.

entries.zh: 今吾於爵非輕也，吏獨安取此！
entries.en: Now I do not treat ranks lightly. How can officials arbitrarily take this!
entries.literal: Now I do not treat ranks lightly. How can officials arbitrarily take this!

entries.zh: 且法以有功勞行田宅，今小吏未嘗從軍者多滿，而有功者顧不得，背公立私，守尉長吏教訓甚不善。
entries.en: Moreover, the law assigns fields and homes according to merit and service. Now many minor officials who never served in the army have received their full share, while those with merit instead receive nothing. This turns away from the public and establishes private interest, and the instruction given by commandery and county officials is very improper.
entries.literal: Moreover, the law is that fields and homes are given based on merit and service. Now minor officials who have never served in the army have many who are satisfied, while those with merit instead do not get them. This abandons the public for private, and the commandery and county officials' teaching is very improper.

entries.zh: 其令諸吏善遇高爵，稱吾 意。
entries.en: Command all officials to treat high ranks well, according with my intention.
entries.literal: Command all officials to treat high ranks well, according with my intention.

entries.zh: 且廉問，有不如吾詔者，以重論之。」
entries.en: Moreover, inquire strictly. Those who do not follow my edict, judge them severely."
entries.literal: Moreover, inquire strictly. Those who do not follow my edict, judge them severely."

entries.zh: 十一年冬，上在邯鄲。
entries.en: In the eleventh year winter, the emperor was at Handan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year winter, the emperor was at Handan.

entries.zh: 豨將侯敞將萬餘人游行，王黃將騎千餘軍曲逆，張春將卒萬餘人度河攻聊城。
entries.en: Xi's general Hou Chang led more than ten thousand men in roaming operations, Wang Huang led more than a thousand cavalry to camp at Quni, and Zhang Chun led more than ten thousand soldiers across the river to attack Liaocheng.
entries.literal: Xi's general Hou Chang led over ten thousand men to roam, Wang Huang led over a thousand cavalry to camp at Qu Ni, Zhang Chun led over ten thousand troops to cross the river and attack Liaocheng.

entries.zh: 漢將 軍郭蒙與齊將擊，大破之。
entries.en: Han general Guo Meng together with Qi generals attacked and greatly defeated them.
entries.literal: Han general Guo Meng together with Qi generals attacked and greatly defeated them.

entries.zh: 太尉周勃道太原入定代地，至馬邑，馬邑不下，攻殘之。
entries.en: Grand marshal Zhou Bo took the Taiyuan route to pacify Dai territory, reaching Mayi. Mayi did not submit, so he attacked and devastated it.
entries.literal: Grand marshal Zhou Bo took the Taiyuan route to pacify Dai territory, reaching Mayi. Mayi did not submit, so he attacked and devastated it.

entries.zh: 豨將趙利守東垣，高祖攻之不下。
entries.en: Xi's general Zhao Li defended Dongyuan. Gaozu attacked but could not take it.
entries.literal: Xi's general Zhao Li defended Dongyuan. Gaozu attacked but could not take it.

entries.zh: 卒罵，上怒。
entries.en: The soldiers cursed. The emperor was angry.
entries.literal: The soldiers cursed. The emperor was angry.

entries.zh: 城降，卒罵者斬之。
entries.en: The city surrendered. The cursing soldiers were executed.
entries.literal: The city surrendered. The cursing soldiers were executed.

entries.zh: 諸縣堅守不 降反寇者，復租賦三歲。
entries.en: The various counties that firmly defended and did not surrender to the rebel bandits had their taxes and levies exempted for three years.
entries.literal: The various counties that firmly defended and did not surrender to the rebel bandits had their taxes and levies exempted for three years.

entries.zh: 初，高祖不脩文學，而性明達，好謀，能聽，自監門戍卒，見之如舊。
entries.en: Initially, Gaozu did not cultivate letters and learning, but by nature he was clear and perceptive, fond of strategy, and able to listen. From gatekeepers to garrison soldiers, when he met people he treated them like old acquaintances.
entries.literal: Initially, Gaozu did not study literature, but his nature was clear and understanding, fond of planning, able to listen. From gate guard to soldier, he treated people as old friends.

entries.zh: 初順民心作三章之約。
entries.en: Initially he followed the people's hearts and made the three chapter covenant.
entries.literal: Initially he followed the people's hearts and made the three chapter covenant.

entries.zh: 天下既定，命蕭何次律令，韓信申軍法，張蒼定章程，叔孫通制禮儀，陸賈造新語。
entries.en: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shusun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.
entries.literal: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shu Sun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.

entries.zh: 又與功臣剖符作誓，丹書鐵契，金匱石室，藏之宗廟。
entries.en: He also divided tallies with the meritorious ministers and made oaths, writing in red on iron contracts, placing them in gold caskets and stone chambers, and storing them in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: He also with the meritorious ministers divided tallies and made oaths, red writing on iron contracts, gold caskets and stone chambers, stored in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 雖日不暇給，規摹弘遠矣。
entries.en: Though days were not sufficient, his plans were broad and far-reaching.
entries.literal: Though days were not sufficient, his plans were broad and far-reaching.

entries.zh: 贊曰：春秋晉史蔡墨有言，陶唐氏既衰，其後有劉累，學擾龍，事孔甲，范氏其後也。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Cai Mo, the Jin historian of the Spring and Autumn period, once said that after the House of Taotang declined, there was Liu Lei, who studied dragon-taming and served Kong Jia, and that the House of Fan descended from him.
entries.literal: Appraisal: Cai Mo, the Jin historian of the Spring and Autumn period, once said that when the House of Taotang declined, afterward there was Liu Lei, who studied dragon-taming, served Kong Jia, and the House of Fan was his descendant.

entries.zh: 而大夫范宣子亦曰：「祖自虞以上為陶唐氏，在夏為御龍氏，在商為豕韋氏，在周為唐杜氏，晉主夏盟為范氏。」
entries.en: Grandee Fan Xuanzi also said: "From the time of Yu and earlier, our ancestors were the House of Taotang; in Xia they were the Dragon-Taming clan; in Shang they were the Shiwei clan; in Zhou they were the Tangdu clan; and in Jin, when they presided over the Xia covenant, they were the Fan clan."
entries.literal: Grandee Fan Xuanzi also said: "From the time of Yu and above we were the House of Taotang; in Xia we were the Dragon-Taming clan; in Shang we were the Shiwei clan; in Zhou we were the Tangdu clan; in Jin, leading the Xia covenant, we were the Fan clan."

entries.zh: 范氏為晉士師，魯文公世奔秦。
entries.en: The Fan clan served as judicial minister of Jin; in the era of Duke Wen of Lu they fled to Qin.
entries.literal: The Fan clan served as judicial minister of Jin; in the era of Duke Wen of Lu they fled to Qin.

entries.zh: 後歸于晉，其處者為劉氏。
entries.en: Later they returned to Jin, and those who remained there became the Liu clan.
entries.literal: Later they returned to Jin, and those who remained there became the Liu clan.

entries.zh: 劉向云戰國時劉氏自秦獲於魏。
entries.en: Liu Xiang said that in the Warring States period the Liu clan was captured from Qin by Wei.
entries.literal: Liu Xiang said that in the Warring States period the Liu clan was captured from Qin by Wei.

entries.zh: 秦滅魏，遷大梁，都于豐，故周巿說雍齒曰「豐，故梁徙也」。
entries.en: When Qin destroyed Wei, it transferred the people of Daliang and made their capital at Feng; therefore Zhou Shi said to Yong Chi: "Feng is where Liang moved its seat."
entries.literal: When Qin destroyed Wei, it moved to Daliang and made its capital at Feng; therefore Zhou Shi said to Yong Chi: "Feng is where Liang moved its seat."

entries.zh: 是以頌高祖云：「漢帝本系，出自唐帝。
entries.en: Hence in praising Gaozu it is said: "The imperial lineage of Han issues from the Emperor of Tang.
entries.literal: Hence in praising Gaozu it is said: "The imperial lineage of Han issues from the Emperor of Tang.

entries.zh: 降及于周，在秦作劉。
entries.en: Descending to Zhou, in Qin they became Liu.
entries.literal: Descending to Zhou, in Qin they became Liu.

entries.zh: 涉魏而東，遂為豐公。」
entries.en: Crossing Wei and going east, they thus became Lord of Feng."
entries.literal: Crossing Wei and going east, they thus became Lord of Feng."

entries.zh: 豐公，蓋太上皇父。
entries.en: Lord of Feng — that is, the father of the Grand Emperor Father.
entries.literal: Lord of Feng — that is, the father of the Grand Emperor Father.

entries.zh: 其遷日淺，墳墓在豐鮮焉。
entries.en: Since the move had been recent, his tomb was still fresh at Feng.
entries.literal: Since the move had been recent, his tomb was still fresh at Feng.

entries.zh: 及高祖即位，置祠祀官，則有秦、晉、梁、荊之巫，世祠天地，綴之以祀，豈不信哉！
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, he established sacrificial officials; there were shamans of Qin, Jin, Liang, and Jing who had sacrificed to Heaven and Earth for generations, and these were joined to the rites. Is this not credible!
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he established sacrificial officials; there were wizards of Qin, Jin, Liang, and Jing who for generations sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, which were linked in the rites — is this not credible!

entries.zh: 由是推之，漢承堯運，德祚已盛，斷蛇著符，旗幟上赤，協于火德，自然之應，得天統矣。
entries.en: From this it follows that Han inherited Yao's cycle; its virtue and fortune were already flourishing. The severed serpent displayed the sign, the banners above were red, and in accord with the virtue of Fire, as a natural response, Han obtained Heaven's lineal succession.
entries.literal: From this it follows that Han received Yao's mandate; its virtue and fortune were already flourishing. The severed serpent left its mark, banners bore red above — in accord with the virtue of Fire, a natural portent, it obtained Heaven's lineal succession.

entries.zh: 五月丙寅，葬長陵。
entries.en: In the fifth month on the day bingyin, buried at Changling.
entries.literal: In the fifth month on the day bingyin, buried at Changling.

entries.zh: 已下，皇太子群臣皆反至太上皇廟。
entries.en: After descending, the imperial crown prince and ministers all returned to the Taishang Huang temple.
entries.literal: After descending, the imperial crown prince and ministers all returned to the Taishang Huang temple.

entries.zh: 群臣曰：「帝起細微，撥亂世反之正，平定天下，為漢太祖，功最高。」
entries.en: The ministers said: "The emperor rose from humble origins, set the chaotic age back on the right path, pacified the world, and became the Grand Progenitor of Han. His merit is the highest."
entries.literal: The ministers said: "The emperor rose from humble origins, corrected the chaotic world to righteousness, pacified the world, became Han Taizu. His merit is highest."

entries.zh: 上尊號曰高皇帝。
entries.en: They honored him with the title Gao Huangdi.
entries.literal: They honored him with the title Gao Huangdi.

entries.zh: 上歸櫟陽，五日一朝太公。
entries.en: The emperor returned to Queyang. He visited the Duke of Tai every five days.
entries.literal: The emperor returned to Queyang. He visited the Duke of Tai every five days.

entries.zh: 太公家令說太公曰：「天亡二日，土亡二王。
entries.en: The Duke of Tai's household steward advised the Duke of Tai: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings.
entries.literal: The Duke of Tai's household steward advised the Duke of Tai: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings.

entries.zh: 皇帝雖子，人主也；
entries.en: The emperor is son, but is the ruler.
entries.literal: The emperor is son, but is the ruler.

entries.zh: 太公雖父， 人臣也。
entries.en: The Duke of Tai is father, but is a subject.
entries.literal: The Duke of Tai is father, but is a subject.

entries.zh: 奈何令人主拜人臣！
entries.en: How can you make the ruler bow to a subject!
entries.literal: How can you make the ruler bow to a subject!

entries.zh: 如此，則威重不行。」
entries.en: If you do this, then imperial authority will not be carried out."
entries.literal: If you do this, then imperial authority will not be carried out."

entries.zh: 後上朝，太公擁彗，迎門卻行。
entries.en: Later when the emperor came to court, the Duke of Tai held a broom and went backwards to meet him at the gate.
entries.literal: Later when the emperor came to court, the Duke of Tai held a broom and went backwards to meet him at the gate.

entries.zh: 上大驚，下扶太公。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly shocked and got down to support the Duke of Tai.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly shocked and got down to support the Duke of Tai.

entries.zh: 太公曰：「帝，人主，奈何以我亂天下法！」
entries.en: The Duke of Tai said: "The emperor is the ruler of men. How can you disorder the world's laws for my sake!"
entries.literal: The Duke of Tai said: "The emperor is the ruler of men. How can you disorder the world's laws for my sake!"

entries.zh: 於是上心善家 令言，賜黃金五百斤。
entries.en: So the emperor in his heart approved of the household steward's words and granted five hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: So the emperor in his heart approved of the household steward's words and granted five hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 夏五月丙午，詔曰：「人之至親，莫親於父子，故父有天下傳歸於子，子有天下尊歸於父，此人道之極也。
entries.en: In the fifth month, summer, on the bingwu day, the edict said: "Among human relations, none is closer than father and son. Therefore, when the father has the world, he transmits it to the son; when the son has the world, honor returns to the father. This is the highest point of the human way.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer on the day bingwu, the edict said: "Of human relations, none is closer than father and son. Therefore when father has the world it is transmitted to son, when son has the world honor returns to father. This is the extreme of human righteousness.

entries.zh: 前日天下大亂，兵革並起，萬民苦 殃，朕親被堅執銳，自帥士卒，犯危難，平暴亂，立諸侯，偃兵息民，天下大安，此皆太公之教訓也。
entries.en: Previously the world was in great disorder, weapons and armor rose together, and the people suffered calamity. I personally wore armor and grasped sharp weapons, personally led the officers and soldiers, faced danger and difficulty, pacified violent disorder, established the feudal lords, laid down arms and gave the people rest, and brought great peace to the world. This is all due to the teaching and instruction of the Taigong.
entries.literal: Previously the world was in great disorder, weapons and armor rose together, the ten thousand people suffered calamity. I personally wore armor and grasped sharp weapons, personally led the officers and soldiers, faced danger and difficulty, pacified violent disorder, established the feudal lords, laid down arms and rested the people, the world is greatly peaceful. This is all due to the Duke of Tai's teaching and instruction.

entries.zh: 諸王、通侯、將軍、群卿、大夫已尊朕為皇帝，而太公未有 號。
entries.en: The various kings, noble marquises, generals, ministers, and grandees have honored me as emperor, but the Duke of Tai has no title.
entries.literal: The various kings, noble marquises, generals, ministers, and grandees have honored me as emperor, but the Duke of Tai has no title.

entries.zh: 今上尊太公曰太上皇。」
entries.en: Now I honor the Duke of Tai as Taishang Huang."
entries.literal: Now I honor the Duke of Tai as Taishang Huang."

entries.zh: 盧綰與數千人居塞下候伺，幸上疾愈，自入謝。
entries.en: Lu Wan with several thousand men dwelt below the frontier watching and waiting, hoping the emperor's illness would improve, personally entering to apologize.
entries.literal: Lu Wan with several thousand men dwelt below the frontier watching and waiting, hoping the emperor's illness would improve, personally entering to apologize.

entries.zh: 夏四月甲辰，帝崩于長樂宮。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer on the day jiachen, the emperor passed away in Changlegong Palace.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer on the day jiachen, the emperor passed away in Changlegong Palace.

entries.zh: 盧綰聞之，遂亡入匈奴。
entries.en: Lu Wan heard of it and fled into the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Lu Wan heard of it and fled into the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 甲申，始剖符封功臣曹參等為通侯。
entries.en: On the day jiashen, he first divided tallies and enfeoffed meritorious ministers Cao Shen and others as noble marquises.
entries.literal: On the day jiashen, he first divided tallies and enfeoffed meritorious ministers Cao Shen and others as noble marquises.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「齊，古之建國也，今為郡縣，其復以為諸侯。
entries.en: The edict said: "Qi is an ancient established state. Now it is commanderies and counties. Restore it as feudal lords.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Qi is an ancient established state. Now it is commanderies and counties. Restore it as feudal lords.

entries.zh: 將軍劉賈數有 大功，及擇寬惠脩絜者，王齊、荊地。」
entries.en: General Liu Jia has repeatedly had great merit. Choose one who is lenient, benevolent, and pure to be king of Qi and Jing territories."
entries.literal: General Liu Jia has repeatedly had great merit. Choose one who is lenient, benevolent, and pure to be king of Qi and Jing territories."

entries.zh: 春正月丙午，韓王信等奏請以故東陽郡、鄣郡、吳郡五十三縣立劉賈為荊王，以碭郡、薛郡、郯郡三十六縣立弟文信君交為 楚王。
entries.en: In the first month, spring, on the bingwu day, King Xin of Han and others petitioned to establish Liu Jia as King of Jing with the former Dongyang, Zhang, and Wu commanderies, fifty-three counties in all, and to establish the emperor's younger brother Jiao, Lord Wenxin, as King of Chu with Dang, Xue, and Tan commanderies, thirty-six counties in all.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring on the day bingwu, King Han Xin and others petitioned to establish Liu Jia as King of Jing with the former Dongyang commandery, Zhang commandery, Wu commandery, fifty-three counties; and to establish younger brother Lord Wenxin Jiao as King of Chu with Dang commandery, Xue commandery, Tan commandery, thirty-six counties.

entries.zh: 壬子，以雲中、鴈門、代郡五十三縣立兄宜信侯喜為代王，以膠東、膠西、臨淄、濟北、博陽、城陽郡七十三縣立子肥為齊王，以太原郡三十一縣為韓國，徙 韓王信都晉陽。
entries.en: On the renzi day, he established his elder brother Xi, Marquis of Yixin, as King of Dai with Yunzhong, Yanmen, and Dai commanderies, fifty-three counties in all; established his son Fei as King of Qi with Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Linzi, Jibei, Boyang, and Chengyang commanderies, seventy-three counties in all; made the thirty-one counties of Taiyuan commandery into the Han kingdom; and moved King Xin of Han to set his capital at Jinyang.
entries.literal: On the day renzi, he established elder brother Lord Yixin Xi as King of Dai with Yunzhong, Yanmen, Dai commanderies, fifty-three counties; established son Fei as King of Qi with Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Linzi, Jibei, Boyang, Chengyang commanderies, seventy-three counties; made Taiyuan commandery thirty-one counties into Han kingdom, moved King Han Xin to establish capital at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 十二月，上還過趙，不禮趙王。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, the emperor returned passing through Zhao and did not show courtesy to King Zhao.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor returned passing through Zhao and did not show courtesy to King Zhao.

entries.zh: 是月，匈奴攻代，代王喜棄國，自歸雒陽，赦為合陽侯。
entries.en: This month, the Xiongnu attacked Dai. Xi, King of Dai, abandoned the kingdom and returned on his own to Luoyang. He was pardoned and made Marquis of Heyang.
entries.literal: This month, the Xiongnu attacked Dai. King Dai Xi abandoned the kingdom and personally returned to Luoyang. He was pardoned and made Marquis of Heyang.

entries.zh: 辛卯，立子如意為代王。
entries.en: On the day xinmao, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.
entries.literal: On the day xinmao, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.

entries.zh: 上還雒陽。
entries.en: The emperor returned to Luoyang.
entries.literal: The emperor returned to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「代地居常山之北，與夷狄邊，趙乃從山南有之，遠，數有胡寇，難以為國。
entries.en: The edict said: "Dai territory lies north of Changshan, bordering the Yi and Di barbarians. Zhao controls it from south of the mountains, which is distant. There are frequent Hu incursions, making it difficult to maintain as a kingdom.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Dai territory lies north of Changshan, bordering the Yi and Di barbarians. Zhao then controls it from south of the mountains, which is distant. There are frequently Hu bandits, making it difficult to establish as a kingdom.

entries.zh: 頗取山南 太原之地益屬代，代之雲中以西為雲中郡，則代受邊寇益少矣。
entries.en: Take a portion of Taiyuan territory south of the mountains and add it to Dai. Make Dai's territory from Yunzhong westward into Yunzhong commandery, and Dai will suffer fewer border raids.
entries.literal: Take much of the Taiyuan territory south of the mountains and add it to Dai. Make Dai's Yunzhong and west into Yunzhong commandery, then Dai will receive fewer border bandits.

entries.zh: 王、相國、通侯、吏二千石擇可立為代王者。」
entries.en: Kings, prime ministers, noble marquises, officials of two thousand piculs, select who can be established as King of Dai."
entries.literal: Kings, prime ministers, noble marquises, officials of two thousand piculs, select who can be established as King of Dai."

entries.zh: 燕王綰、相國何等三十三人皆曰：「子恆賢知溫良， 請立以為代王，都晉陽。」
entries.en: King Wan of Yan, Chancellor Xiao He, and thirty-three others all said: "The son Heng is worthy, wise, gentle, and kind. Please establish him as King of Dai, with his capital at Jinyang."
entries.literal: King Yan Wan, prime minister He and thirty-three others all said: "The son Heng is worthy, wise, gentle, and kind. Please establish him as King of Dai, capital at Jinyang."

entries.zh: 大赦天下。
entries.en: There was a great amnesty for the world.
entries.literal: There was a great amnesty for the world.

entries.zh: 三月，梁王彭越謀反，夷三族。
entries.en: In the third month, King Liang Peng Yue plotted rebellion and his three clans were exterminated.
entries.literal: In the third month, King Liang Peng Yue plotted rebellion and his three clans were exterminated.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「擇可以為梁王、淮陽王者。」
entries.en: The edict said: "Select who can be King of Liang, King of Huaiyang."
entries.literal: The edict said: "Select who can be King of Liang, King of Huaiyang."

entries.zh: 燕王綰、相國何等請立子恢為梁王，子友為淮陽王。
entries.en: King Yan Wan, prime minister He and others requested establishing son Hui as King of Liang, son You as King of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: King Yan Wan, prime minister He and others requested establishing son Hui as King of Liang, son You as King of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 罷東郡，頗益梁；
entries.en: Abolished Dong commandery, added much to Liang.
entries.literal: Abolished Dong commandery, added much to Liang.

entries.zh: 罷潁川郡，頗益淮陽。
entries.en: Abolished Yingchuan commandery, added much to Huaiyang.
entries.literal: Abolished Yingchuan commandery, added much to Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 秋七月，淮南王布反。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, King Huainan Ying Bu rebelled.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, King Huainan Ying Bu rebelled.

entries.zh: 上問諸將，滕公言故楚令尹薛公有籌策。
entries.en: The emperor asked the generals. Teng Gong spoke of the former Chu prime minister Xue Gong who had strategy.
entries.literal: The emperor asked the generals. Teng Gong spoke of the former Chu prime minister Xue Gong who had strategy.

entries.zh: 上見公，薛公言布形勢，上善之，封薛公 千戶。
entries.en: The emperor saw Xue Gong. Xue Gong spoke of Ying Bu's situation. The emperor approved it and enfeoffed Xue Gong with a thousand households.
entries.literal: The emperor saw Xue Gong. Xue Gong spoke of Ying Bu's situation. The emperor approved it and enfeoffed Xue Gong with a thousand households.

entries.zh: 詔王、相國擇可立為淮南王者，群臣請立子長為王。
entries.en: He commanded the kings and chancellors to select someone who could be established as King of Huainan. The ministers requested that his son Chang be established as king.
entries.literal: He commanded the kings and prime ministers to select who could be established as King of Huainan. The ministers requested establishing son Chang as king.

entries.zh: 上乃發上郡、北地、隴西車騎，巴蜀材官及中尉卒三萬人為皇太子衛，軍霸上。
entries.en: The emperor then dispatched chariots and cavalry from Shang commandery, Beidi, and Longxi, along with trained soldiers from Ba and Shu and soldiers of the Commandant, 30,000 men in all, to serve as guard for the imperial crown prince, encamping at Bashang.
entries.literal: The emperor then dispatched Shang commandery, Beidi, Longxi chariots and cavalry, Bashu foresters and imperial guards 30,000 men as imperial crown prince guard, encamping at Bashang.

entries.zh: 布果如薛公言，東擊殺荊 王劉賈，劫其兵，度淮擊楚，楚王交走入薛。
entries.en: Ying Bu indeed did as Xue Gong had said: he attacked eastward and killed Liu Jia, King of Jing, seized his troops, and crossed the Huai to attack Chu. Jiao, King of Chu, fled into Xue.
entries.literal: Ying Bu indeed as Xue Gong said, attacked east and killed King Jing Liu Jia, seized his troops, crossed the Huai to attack Chu. King Chu Jiao fled into Xue.

entries.zh: 上赦天下死罪以下，皆令從軍；
entries.en: The emperor pardoned all death sentences and below, all commanded to follow the army.
entries.literal: The emperor pardoned all death sentences and below, all commanded to follow the army.

entries.zh: 徵諸侯兵，上自將以擊布。
entries.en: He summoned the feudal lords' troops. The emperor personally led them to attack Ying Bu.
entries.literal: He summoned the feudal lords' troops. The emperor personally led them to attack Ying Bu.

entries.zh: 十二月，詔曰：「秦皇帝、楚隱王、魏安釐王、齊愍王、趙悼襄王皆絕亡後。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, the edict said: "The First Emperor of Qin, King Yin of Chu, King Anli of Wei, King Min of Qi, and King Daoxiang of Zhao all have lineages without descendants.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the edict said: "The Qin First Emperor, Chu Yin King, Wei Anli King, Qi Min King, Zhao Dao Xiang King all have extinct lineages.

entries.zh: 其與秦始皇帝守冢二十家，楚、魏、齊各十家，趙及魏公子亡忌各五家，令視其冢，復亡與它事。」
entries.en: Assign twenty households to the tomb of the First Emperor of Qin, ten households each to Chu, Wei, and Qi, and five households each to Zhao and Prince Wuji of Wei, to oversee their tombs and be exempt from other service."
entries.literal: Give to the Qin First Emperor's tomb twenty households, Chu, Wei, Qi each ten households, Zhao and Wei prince Wu Ji each five households, to oversee their tombs, exempt from other service."

entries.zh: 陳豨降將言豨反時燕王盧綰使人之豨所陰謀。
entries.en: Chen Xi's surrendering generals said that when Xi rebelled, King Yan Lu Wan sent people to Xi's place with secret plots.
entries.literal: Chen Xi's surrendering generals said that when Xi rebelled, King Yan Lu Wan sent people to Xi's place with secret plots.

entries.zh: 上使辟陽侯審食其迎綰，綰稱疾。
entries.en: The emperor sent Marquis Piyang Shen Shiqi to welcome Lu Wan. Lu Wan claimed illness.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Marquis Piyang Shen Shiqi to welcome Lu Wan. Lu Wan claimed illness.

entries.zh: 食其言綰反有端。
entries.en: Shiqi said Lu Wan had signs of rebellion.
entries.literal: Shiqi said Lu Wan had signs of rebellion.

entries.zh: 春二 月，使樊噲、周勃將兵擊綰。
entries.en: In the second month of spring, he sent Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo to lead troops to attack Lu Wan.
entries.literal: In the second month of spring, he sent Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo to lead troops to attack Lu Wan.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「燕王綰與吾有故，愛之如子，聞與陳豨有謀，吾以為亡有，故使人迎綰。
entries.en: The edict said: "King Lu Wan of Yan has old ties with me. I loved him like a son. When I heard that he had plotted with Chen Xi, I thought there was nothing to it, and so I sent people to welcome Lu Wan.
entries.literal: The edict said: "King Yan Lu Wan has old relations with me. I love him like a son. Hearing he had plots with Chen Xi, I thought there was nothing to it, so I sent people to welcome Lu Wan.

entries.zh: 綰稱疾不來，謀反明矣。
entries.en: Lu Wan claimed illness and did not come. His rebellion is clear.
entries.literal: Lu Wan claimed illness and did not come. His rebellion is clear.

entries.zh: 燕吏民非有罪也，賜其吏六 百石以上爵各一級。
entries.en: Yan officials and people have no crime. Grant officials of 600 piculs and above each one rank.
entries.literal: Yan officials and people have no crime. Grant officials of 600 piculs and above each one rank.

entries.zh: 與綰居，去來歸者，赦之，加爵亦一級。」
entries.en: Those who lived with Lu Wan and come and go returning, pardon them, add one rank also."
entries.literal: Those who lived with Lu Wan and come and go returning, pardon them, add one rank also."

entries.zh: 詔諸侯王議可立為燕王者，長沙王臣等請立子建為燕王。
entries.en: He commanded the feudal kings to discuss who could be established as King of Yan. The King of Changsha and others requested that his son Jian be established as King of Yan.
entries.literal: He commanded the feudal lords to discuss who could be established as King of Yan. King Changsha and others requested establishing son Jian as King of Yan.

entries.zh: 春正月，追尊兄伯號曰武哀侯。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.

entries.zh: 下令曰：「楚地已定，義帝亡後，欲存恤楚眾，以定其主。
entries.en: He issued an order: "Chu territory is already pacified. Since the Righteous Emperor has left no heir, I wish to preserve and care for the Chu multitudes by establishing their ruler.
entries.literal: He issued an order: "Chu territory is already pacified. After the Righteous Emperor's death, I wish to care for the Chu multitudes and establish their ruler.

entries.zh: 齊王信習楚風 俗，更立為楚王，王淮北，都下邳。
entries.en: King Qi Xin was accustomed to Chu customs, so he re-established him as King of Chu, ruling north of the Huai, capital at Xiapi.
entries.literal: King Qi Xin was accustomed to Chu customs, so he re-established him as King of Chu, ruling north of the Huai, capital at Xiapi.

entries.zh: 魏相國建城侯彭越勤勞魏民，卑下士卒，常以少擊眾，數破楚軍，其以魏故地王之，號曰梁王，都定陶。」
entries.en: Peng Yue, Chancellor of Wei and Marquis of Jiancheng, labored diligently for the people of Wei, humbled himself before officers and soldiers, often attacked many with few, and repeatedly broke Chu armies. Let him be made king over the former Wei territory, titled King of Liang, with his capital at Dingtao."
entries.literal: Wei prime minister Lord Jiancheng Peng Yue worked hard for the Wei people, treated officers and soldiers humbly, often attacked many with few, repeatedly broke Chu armies. For this he was enfeoffed with the former Wei territory as king, titled King of Liang, capital at Dingtao."

entries.zh: 又曰：「兵不得休八 年，萬民與苦甚，今天下事畢，其赦天下殊死以下。」
entries.en: He also said: "The troops have had no rest for eight years, and the people have suffered terribly with them. Now the affairs of the realm are complete. Pardon all those sentenced to death or below."
entries.literal: He also said: "The troops have not rested for eight years. The ten thousand people have suffered greatly. Now the world's affairs are finished. Pardon all those sentenced to death or below."

entries.zh: 九年冬十月，淮南王、梁王、趙王、楚王朝未央宮，置酒前殿。
entries.en: In the tenth month, winter, of the ninth year, the King of Huainan, the King of Liang, the King of Zhao, and the King of Chu paid court at Weiyang Palace. A banquet was held in the front hall.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the ninth year, the King of Huainan, King of Liang, King of Zhao, King of Chu paid court at the Weiyang Palace. A banquet was held in the front hall.

entries.zh: 上奉玉卮為太上皇壽，曰：「始大人常以臣亡賴，不能治產業，不如仲力。
entries.en: The emperor raised a jade goblet to toast the Taishang Huang, saying: "At first, Father often said that I was worthless and could not manage property, unlike my elder brother Zhong in ability.
entries.literal: The emperor held a jade goblet to toast the Taishang Huang, saying: "At first, father often said that I was worthless and could not manage property, unlike brother Zhong in strength.

entries.zh: 今某之業所就孰與仲多？」
entries.en: Now whose achievement that I have accomplished is greater, mine or brother Zhong's?"
entries.literal: Now whose achievement that I have accomplished is greater, mine or brother Zhong's?"

entries.zh: 殿上群臣皆稱萬歲，大笑為樂。
entries.en: The ministers in the hall all shouted ten thousand years and laughed with great joy.
entries.literal: The ministers in the hall all shouted ten thousand years and laughed with great joy.

entries.zh: 秋七月，燕王臧荼反，上自將征之。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, King Yan Zang Tu rebelled. The emperor personally led troops to campaign against him.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, King Yan Zang Tu rebelled. The emperor personally led troops to campaign against him.

entries.zh: 九月，虜荼。
entries.en: In the ninth month, he captured Tu.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, he captured Tu.

entries.zh: 詔諸侯王視有功者立以為燕王。
entries.en: He commanded the feudal lords to examine those with merit and establish one as King of Yan.
entries.literal: He commanded the feudal lords to examine those with merit and establish one as King of Yan.

entries.zh: 荊王臣信等十人皆曰：「太尉長安侯盧綰功最多，請立以為燕王。」
entries.en: The King of Jing, Xin, and ten others all said: "Grand Marshal Lu Wan, Marquis of Chang'an, has the most merit. Please establish him as King of Yan."
entries.literal: King Jing Chen Xin and ten others all said: "Grand Marshal Lord Chang'an Lu Wan has the most merit. Please establish him as King of Yan."

entries.zh: 使丞相噲將兵平代地。
entries.en: He sent Chancellor Kuai to lead troops and pacify Dai territory.
entries.literal: He sent Chancellor Kuai to lead troops and pacify Dai territory.

entries.zh: 七年冬十月，上自將擊韓王信於銅鞮，斬其將。
entries.en: In the tenth month, winter, of the seventh year, the emperor personally led troops to attack King Xin of Han at Tongdi, beheading his generals.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the seventh year, the emperor personally led troops to attack King Han Xin at Tongdi, beheading his generals.

entries.zh: 信亡走匈奴，與其將曼丘臣、王黃共立故趙後趙利為王，收信散兵，與匈奴共距漢。
entries.en: Xin fled to the Xiongnu, and together with his generals Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang established Zhao Li, a descendant of the former Zhao, as king. They gathered Xin's scattered troops and, together with the Xiongnu, resisted Han.
entries.literal: Xin fled to the Xiongnu, and together with his generals Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang established the former Zhao descendant Zhao Li as king. They gathered Xin's scattered troops and together with the Xiongnu resisted Han.

entries.zh: 上從晉陽連戰，乘勝逐北，至樓煩，會大寒，士卒墮指者什二三。
entries.en: From Jinyang the emperor fought consecutive battles, pursued the defeated enemy on the strength of his victories, and reached Loufan. Encountering extreme cold, two or three soldiers in ten lost fingers to frostbite.
entries.literal: The emperor from Jinyang fought continuous battles, riding victory to pursue the enemy, reaching Loufan. Encountering great cold, soldiers with frostbitten fingers were two or three in ten.

entries.zh: 遂至平城，為匈奴所圍，七日，用陳平祕計得出。
entries.en: He arrived at Pingcheng and was surrounded by the Xiongnu for seven days. Using Chen Ping's secret plan, he got out.
entries.literal: He arrived at Pingcheng and was surrounded by the Xiongnu for seven days. Using Chen Ping's secret plan, he got out.

entries.zh: 使樊噲留定代地。
entries.en: He sent Fan Kuai to remain and pacify Dai territory.
entries.literal: He sent Fan Kuai to remain and pacify Dai territory.

entries.zh: 二月，至長安。
entries.en: In the second month, he arrived at Chang'an.
entries.literal: In the second month, he arrived at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 蕭何治未央宮，立東闕、北闕、前殿、武庫、大倉。
entries.en: Xiao He had constructed the Weiyang Palace, establishing the eastern gate, northern gate, front hall, armory, and great granary.
entries.literal: Xiao He had constructed the Weiyang Palace, establishing the eastern gate, northern gate, front hall, armory, and great granary.

entries.zh: 上見其壯麗，甚怒，謂何曰：「天下 匈匈，勞苦數歲，成敗未可知，是何治宮室過度也！」
entries.en: The emperor saw its grandeur and was greatly angered. He said to Xiao He: "The world is in turmoil, we have labored bitterly for several years, and success or failure is not yet known. Why have you constructed palace buildings to such excess!"
entries.literal: The emperor saw its grandeur and was greatly angry. He said to He: "The world is in turmoil, we have labored bitterly for several years, success or failure is not yet known. Why have you constructed palace rooms excessively!"

entries.zh: 何曰：「天下方未定，故可因以就宮室。
entries.en: He said: "The world is not yet settled, so it is suitable to take advantage of this to complete the palace rooms.
entries.literal: He said: "The world is not yet settled, so it is suitable to take advantage of this to complete the palace rooms.

entries.zh: 且夫天子以四海為家，非令壯麗亡以重威，且亡令後世有以加也。」
entries.en: Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home. If it is not grand, there is no way to give weight to authority; and if it is not grand, future generations will have nothing to add."
entries.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as home. If not grand, there is no way to increase authority. And if not grand, future generations will have nothing to add."

entries.zh: 上說。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased.

entries.zh: 自櫟陽徙都長安。
entries.en: He moved the capital from Queyang to Chang'an.
entries.literal: He moved the capital from Queyang to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 置宗正宮以序九族。
entries.en: He established the Palace of Imperial Clan Affairs to order the nine clans.
entries.literal: He established the Palace of Imperial Clan Affairs to order the nine clans.

entries.zh: 夏四月，行如雒陽。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, he traveled to Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, he traveled to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 八年冬，上東擊韓信餘寇於東垣。
entries.en: In the winter of the eighth year, the emperor went east to attack the remaining bandits of Han Xin at Dongyuan.
entries.literal: In the winter of the eighth year, the emperor went east to attack the remaining bandits of Han Xin at Dongyuan.

entries.zh: 還過趙，趙相貫高等恥上不禮其王，陰謀欲弒上。
entries.en: On the return, as the emperor passed through Zhao, Zhao Chancellor Guan Gao and the others were ashamed that he had shown no courtesy to their king, and secretly plotted to assassinate him.
entries.literal: On the return passing through Zhao, Zhao chancellor Guan Gao and others were ashamed that the emperor did not show courtesy to their king, and secretly plotted to assassinate the emperor.

entries.zh: 上欲宿，心動，問「縣名何？」
entries.en: The emperor wanted to stay overnight. His heart was moved. He asked "What is the county name?"
entries.literal: The emperor wanted to stay overnight. His heart was moved. He asked "What is the county name?"

entries.zh: 曰：「柏人。」
entries.en: They said: "Boren."
entries.literal: They said: "Boren."

entries.zh: 上曰：「柏人者，迫於人也。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Boren means 'pressed by people.'"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Boren means 'pressed by people.'"

entries.zh: 去弗宿。
entries.en: He left and did not stay.
entries.literal: He left and did not stay.

entries.zh: 十二年冬十月，上破布軍于會缶，布走，令別將追之。
entries.en: In the tenth month, winter, of the twelfth year, the emperor broke Ying Bu's army at Huifu. Ying Bu fled, and the emperor ordered separate generals to pursue him.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the twelfth year, the emperor broke Ying Bu's army at Huifu. Ying Bu fled. He commanded separate generals to pursue him.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「南武侯織亦粵之世也，立以為南海王。」
entries.en: The edict said: "Marquis Nanwu Zhi is also of Yue lineage. Establish him as King of Nanhai."
entries.literal: The edict said: "Marquis Nanwu Zhao Zhi is also of Yue lineage. Establish him as King of Nanhai."

entries.zh: 三月，詔曰：「吾立為天子，帝有天下，十二年于今矣。
entries.en: In the third month, the edict said: "I was established as Son of Heaven and have ruled the world as emperor for twelve years now.
entries.literal: In the third month, the edict said: "I have established myself as Son of Heaven and emperor of the world. It has been twelve years to now.

entries.zh: 與天下之豪士賢大夫共定天下，同安輯之。
entries.en: Together with the world's heroic scholars and worthy grandees I pacified the world and jointly settled it.
entries.literal: Together with the world's heroic scholars and worthy grandees I pacified the world and jointly settled it.

entries.zh: 其有 功者上致之王，次為列侯，下乃食邑。
entries.en: Those who have merit, the highest become kings, next become marquises, lowest receive fiefs.
entries.literal: Those who have merit, the highest become kings, next become marquises, lowest receive fiefs.

entries.zh: 而重臣之親，或為列侯，皆令自置吏，得賦斂，女子公主。
entries.en: While the close relatives of heavy ministers, some become marquises, all are commanded to appoint their own officials, able to collect taxes, marry princesses.
entries.literal: While the close relatives of heavy ministers, some become marquises, all are commanded to appoint their own officials, able to collect taxes, marry princesses.

entries.zh: 為列侯食邑者，皆佩之印，賜大第室。
entries.en: Those who are marquises with fiefs, all wear the seal, granted great mansions.
entries.literal: Those who are marquises with fiefs, all wear the seal, granted great mansions.

entries.zh: 吏二千石，徙之長安，受小 第室。
entries.en: Officials of two thousand piculs, move them to Chang'an, receive small mansions.
entries.literal: Officials of two thousand piculs, move them to Chang'an, receive small mansions.

entries.zh: 入蜀漢定三秦者，皆世世復。
entries.en: Those who entered Shu and Han and pacified the three Qins, all have hereditary exemptions.
entries.literal: Those who entered Shu and Han and pacified the three Qins, all have hereditary exemptions.

entries.zh: 吾於天下賢士功臣，可謂亡負矣。
entries.en: I can say I have not failed the world's worthy scholars and meritorious ministers.
entries.literal: I can say I have not failed the world's worthy scholars and meritorious ministers.

entries.zh: 其有不義背天子擅起兵者，與天下共伐誅之。
entries.en: If any unrighteous person turns his back on the Son of Heaven and presumptuously raises troops, the world shall join together to attack and execute him.
entries.literal: Those who are unrighteous and turn their backs on the Son of Heaven by presumptuously raising troops, the world together shall attack and execute them.

entries.zh: 布告天下，使明知朕意。」
entries.en: Proclaim to the world, so they clearly know my intention."
entries.literal: Proclaim to the world, so they clearly know my intention."

entries.zh: 上擊布時，為流矢所中，行道疾。
entries.en: When the emperor attacked Ying Bu, he was struck by a stray arrow, and traveling the road he became ill.
entries.literal: When the emperor attacked Ying Bu, he was struck by a stray arrow, and traveling the road he became ill.

entries.zh: 疾甚，呂后迎良醫。
entries.en: The illness was severe. Empress Lü welcomed good physicians.
entries.literal: The illness was severe. Empress Lü welcomed good physicians.

entries.zh: 醫入見，上問醫。
entries.en: The physician entered to see him. The emperor questioned the physician.
entries.literal: The physician entered to see him. The emperor questioned the physician.

entries.zh: 曰：「疾可治。」
entries.en: He said: "The illness can be cured."
entries.literal: He said: "The illness can be cured."

entries.zh: 於 是上嫚罵之，曰：「吾以布衣提三尺取天下，此非天命乎？
entries.en: So the emperor insulted him, saying: "I from commoner status, wielding a three-foot sword took the world. Is this not Heaven's mandate?
entries.literal: So the emperor insulted him, saying: "I from commoner status, wielding a three-foot sword took the world. Is this not Heaven's mandate?

entries.zh: 命乃在天，雖扁鵲何益！」
entries.en: The mandate is in Heaven. Though Bian Que came, what benefit!"
entries.literal: The mandate is in Heaven. Though Bian Que came, what benefit!"

entries.zh: 遂不使治疾，賜黃金五十斤，罷之。
entries.en: So he did not have him treat the illness, granted fifty jin of gold, and dismissed him.
entries.literal: So he did not have him treat the illness, granted fifty jin of gold, and dismissed him.

entries.zh: 呂后問曰：「陛下百歲後，蕭相國既死， 誰令代之？」
entries.en: Empress Lü asked: "After Your Majesty reaches a hundred years, when Chancellor Xiao dies, who should replace him?"
entries.literal: Empress Lü asked: "After Your Majesty reaches a hundred years, when Chancellor Xiao dies, who should replace him?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「曹參可。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Cao Shen is suitable."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Cao Shen is suitable."

entries.zh: 問其次，曰：「
entries.en: Asked about the next, he said: "
entries.literal: Asked about the next, he said: "

entries.zh: 十二月，圍羽垓下。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, they surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, they surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia.

entries.zh: 羽夜聞漢軍四面皆楚歌，知盡得楚地，羽與數百騎走，是以兵大敗。
entries.en: At night Xiang Yu heard Han troops on all four sides singing Chu songs and knew that they had taken all Chu territory. He fled with several hundred cavalry, and so his army suffered a great defeat.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu at night heard that Han troops on all four sides were singing Chu songs, knew they had taken all Chu territory, and Xiang Yu fled with several hundred cavalry, which is why his army suffered a great defeat.

entries.zh: 灌嬰追斬羽東 城。
entries.en: Guan Ying pursued and beheaded Xiang Yu at Dongcheng.
entries.literal: Guan Ying pursued and beheaded Xiang Yu at Dongcheng.

entries.zh: 楚地悉定，獨魯不下。
entries.en: Chu territory was completely pacified, only Lu did not submit.
entries.literal: Chu territory was completely pacified, only Lu did not submit.

entries.zh: 漢王引天下兵欲屠之，為其守節禮義之國，乃持羽頭示其父兄，魯乃降。
entries.en: The King of Han led the troops of the world and intended to massacre them, but because Lu was a state that upheld fidelity, ritual, and righteousness, he held up Xiang Yu's head and showed it to their fathers and elder brothers. Lu then surrendered.
entries.literal: King Han led the troops of the world wanting to massacre them, but since it was a state that upheld propriety and righteousness, he held Xiang Yu's head to show their fathers and brothers. Lu then surrendered.

entries.zh: 初，懷王封羽為魯公，及死，魯又為之堅守，故以魯公葬羽於穀 城。
entries.en: Initially, King Huai had enfeoffed Xiang Yu as Duke of Lu, and after his death Lu again defended firmly on his behalf. Therefore Xiang Yu was buried at Gucheng as Duke of Lu.
entries.literal: Initially, King Huai had enfeoffed Xiang Yu as Lord of Lu, and after his death, Lu again defended firmly for him. Therefore they buried Xiang Yu as Lord of Lu at Gucheng.

entries.zh: 漢王為發葬，哭臨而去。
entries.en: King Han conducted the funeral rites and wept at the grave before leaving.
entries.literal: King Han conducted the funeral rites and wept at the grave before leaving.

entries.zh: 封項伯等四人為列侯，賜姓劉氏。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Xiang Bo and three others as marquises and granted them the surname Liu.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Xiang Bo and three others as marquises and granted them the surname Liu.

entries.zh: 諸民略在楚者皆歸之。
entries.en: All the people who had been seized in Chu were returned.
entries.literal: All the people who had been seized in Chu were returned.

entries.zh: 漢王還至定陶，馳入齊王信壁，奪其軍。
entries.en: King Han returned to Dingtao and galloped into King Qi Xin's encampment, seizing his army.
entries.literal: King Han returned to Dingtao and galloped into King Qi Xin's encampment, seizing his army.

entries.zh: 初項羽所立臨江王共敖前死，子尉嗣 立為王，不降。
entries.en: Initially, the Linjiang King Gong Ao whom Xiang Yu had established had died earlier. His son Wei succeeded as king and did not surrender.
entries.literal: Initially, the Linjiang King Gong Ao whom Xiang Yu had established had died earlier. His son Wei succeeded as king and did not surrender.

entries.zh: 遣盧綰、劉賈擊虜尉。
entries.en: He sent Lu Wan and Liu Jia to attack and capture Wei.
entries.literal: He sent Lu Wan and Liu Jia to attack and capture Wei.

entries.zh: 帝置酒雒陽南宮。
entries.en: The emperor held a banquet in Luoyang's southern palace.
entries.literal: The emperor held a banquet in Luoyang's southern palace.

entries.zh: 上曰：「通侯諸將毋敢隱朕，皆言其情。
entries.en: The emperor said: "Noble marquises and generals, do not dare conceal from me. All speak your true feelings.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Noble marquises and generals, do not dare conceal from me. All speak your true feelings.

entries.zh: 吾所以有天下者何？
entries.en: Why did I obtain the world?
entries.literal: Why did I obtain the world?

entries.zh: 項氏之所以失天下者 何？」
entries.en: Why did the Xiang clan lose the world?"
entries.literal: Why did the Xiang clan lose the world?"

entries.zh: 高起、王陵對曰：「陛下嫚而侮人，項羽仁而敬人。
entries.en: Gao Qi and Wang Ling replied: "Your Majesty is casual and insults people. Xiang Yu is benevolent and respects people.
entries.literal: Gao Qi and Wang Ling replied: "Your Majesty is casual and insults people. Xiang Yu is benevolent and respects people.

entries.zh: 然陛下使人攻城略地，所降下者，因以與之，與天下同利也。
entries.en: However, when Your Majesty sends people to attack cities and seize territory, those who surrender are given it, sharing the world's benefits with them.
entries.literal: However, when Your Majesty sends people to attack cities and seize territory, those who surrender are given it, sharing the world's benefits with them.

entries.zh: 項羽妒賢嫉能，有功者害之，賢者疑之，戰 勝而不與人功，得地而不與人利，此其所以失天下也。」
entries.en: Xiang Yu was jealous of the worthy and envious of the able. He harmed those with merit and doubted the worthy. He won battles but did not share credit with others; he obtained land but did not share its benefits. This is why he lost the world."
entries.literal: Xiang Yu was jealous of the worthy and envious of the able. He harmed those with merit, doubted the worthy. He won battles but did not give credit to others, obtained land but did not share benefits with others. This is why he lost the world."

entries.zh: 上曰：「公知其一，未知其二。
entries.en: The emperor said: "You know one aspect, but not the other.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "You know one aspect, but not the other.

entries.zh: 夫運籌帷幄之中，決勝千里之外，吾不如子房；
entries.en: Planning strategy within the command tent, deciding victory a thousand miles away - I am not equal to Zifang.
entries.literal: Planning strategy within the command tent, deciding victory a thousand miles away - I am not equal to Zifang.

entries.zh: 填國家，撫百姓，給餉餽， 不絕糧道，吾不如蕭何；
entries.en: Filling the state treasury, comforting the people, providing supplies without interruption, maintaining the grain routes - I am not equal to Xiao He.
entries.literal: Filling the state treasury, comforting the people, providing supplies without interruption, maintaining the grain routes - I am not equal to Xiao He.

entries.zh: 連百萬之眾，戰必勝，攻必取，吾不如韓信。
entries.en: Commanding a million troops, fighting must win, attacking must take - I am not equal to Han Xin.
entries.literal: Commanding a million troops, fighting must win, attacking must take - I am not equal to Han Xin.

entries.zh: 三者皆人傑，吾能用之，此吾所以取天下者也。
entries.en: These three are all outstanding men. I can employ them. This is why I obtained the world.
entries.literal: These three are all outstanding men. I can employ them. This is why I obtained the world.

entries.zh: 項羽有一范增而不能用，此所以為我禽也。」
entries.en: Xiang Yu had one Fan Zeng but could not employ him. This is why he was captured by me."
entries.literal: Xiang Yu had one Fan Zeng but could not employ him. This is why he was captured by me."

entries.zh: 群臣說服。
entries.en: The ministers were all convinced.
entries.literal: The ministers were all convinced.

entries.zh: 初，田橫歸彭越。
entries.en: Initially, Tian Heng had gone to Peng Yue.
entries.literal: Initially, Tian Heng had gone to Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 項羽已滅，橫懼誅，與賓客亡入海。
entries.en: Xiang Yu had already been destroyed. Heng feared execution and fled to the sea with his retainers.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu had already been destroyed. Heng feared execution and fled to the sea with his retainers.

entries.zh: 上恐其久為亂，遣使者赦橫，曰：「橫來，大者王，小者侯；
entries.en: The emperor feared that he would cause disorder for a long time, so he sent an envoy to pardon Heng, saying: "If Heng comes, at the highest he will be king, at the lowest marquis.
entries.literal: The emperor feared he would long cause disorder, so he sent an envoy to pardon Heng, saying: "If Heng comes, the great one will be king, the small one will be marquis.

entries.zh: 不來，且發兵加誅。」
entries.en: If he does not come, I will send troops to execute him."
entries.literal: If he does not come, I will send troops to execute him."

entries.zh: 橫懼，乘傳詣雒陽，未至三十里，自殺。
entries.en: Heng was afraid and rode the imperial relay to Luoyang. Thirty li from arriving, he committed suicide.
entries.literal: Heng was afraid and rode the imperial relay to Luoyang. Thirty li from arriving, he committed suicide.

entries.zh: 上壯其節，為流涕，發卒二千人，以王禮葬焉。
entries.en: The emperor admired his integrity and shed tears. He sent 2,000 troops and buried him with kingly rites.
entries.literal: The emperor admired his integrity and shed tears. He sent 2,000 troops and buried him with kingly rites.

entries.zh: 戍卒婁敬求見，說上曰：「陛下取天下與周異，而都雒陽，不便，不如入關，據秦之固。」
entries.en: The garrison soldier Lou Jing sought an audience and advised the emperor: "Your Majesty obtained the world differently from Zhou, and establishing the capital at Luoyang is unsuitable. It would be better to enter the passes and occupy Qin's strongholds."
entries.literal: Guard commander Lou Jing sought an audience and advised the emperor: "Your Majesty obtained the world differently from the Zhou, but establishing the capital at Luoyang is inconvenient. It would be better to enter the passes and occupy Qin's strongholds."

entries.zh: 上以問張良，良因勸上。
entries.en: The emperor asked Zhang Liang, who then advised the emperor.
entries.literal: The emperor asked Zhang Liang, who then advised the emperor.

entries.zh: 是日，車駕西都長安。
entries.en: That day, the imperial chariot went west to establish the capital at Chang'an.
entries.literal: That day, the imperial chariot went west to establish the capital at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 拜婁敬為奉春君，賜姓劉氏。
entries.en: He appointed Lou Jing as Lord Fengchun and granted him the surname Liu.
entries.literal: He appointed Lou Jing as Lord Fengchun and granted him the surname Liu.

entries.zh: 六月壬辰，大赦天下。
entries.en: In the sixth month on the day renchen, there was a great amnesty for the world.
entries.literal: In the sixth month on the day renchen, there was a great amnesty for the world.

entries.zh: 利幾反，上自擊破之。
entries.en: Li Ji rebelled. The emperor personally attacked and defeated him.
entries.literal: Li Ji rebelled. The emperor personally attacked and defeated him.

entries.zh: 利幾者，項羽將。
entries.en: Li Ji was Xiang Yu's general.
entries.literal: Li Ji was Xiang Yu's general.

entries.zh: 羽敗，利幾為陳令，降，上侯之潁川。
entries.en: Yu was defeated. Li Ji became magistrate of Chen and surrendered. The emperor enfeoffed him in Yingchuan.
entries.literal: Yu was defeated. Li Ji became magistrate of Chen and surrendered. The emperor enfeoffed him in Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 上至雒陽，舉通侯籍召之，而利幾恐，反。
entries.en: The emperor reached Luoyang and examined the noble marquises' registers to summon him, but Li Ji feared and rebelled.
entries.literal: The emperor reached Luoyang and examined the noble marquises' registers to summon him, but Li Ji feared and rebelled.

entries.zh: 人告楚王信謀反，上問左右，左右爭欲擊之。
entries.en: Someone informed that King Chu Han Xin was plotting rebellion. The emperor asked his attendants. The attendants all wished to attack him.
entries.literal: Someone informed that King Chu Han Xin was plotting rebellion. The emperor asked his attendants. The attendants all wished to attack him.

entries.zh: 用陳平計，乃偽游雲夢。
entries.en: Using Chen Ping's plan, he pretended to tour Yunmeng.
entries.literal: Using Chen Ping's plan, he pretended to tour Yunmeng.

entries.zh: 十二月，會諸侯于陳，楚王信迎謁，因執之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, he assembled the feudal lords at Chen. King Chu Xin came to greet him, and he arrested him.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, he assembled the feudal lords at Chen. King Chu Xin came to greet him, and he arrested him.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「
entries.en: The edict said, “
entries.literal: The edict said, “

entries.zh: 天下既安，豪桀有功者封侯，新立，未能盡圖其功。
entries.en: The world is now pacified. The heroic and outstanding men with merit have been enfeoffed as marquises, but since the dynasty is newly established, I have not yet been able to account fully for their merit.
entries.literal: The world is now pacified. The heroic and outstanding with merit have been enfeoffed as marquises. Newly established, I have not yet been able to fully reward their merit.

entries.zh: 身居軍九年，或未習法令，或以其故犯法，大者死 刑，吾甚憐之。
entries.en: They have spent nine years in the army. Some are not yet accustomed to the laws and commands, or because of old habits violate the law. In serious cases they receive death penalties. I pity them greatly.
entries.literal: They have been in the army nine years. Some are not yet accustomed to the laws, or because of their past violate the law. The great ones receive death penalties. I pity them greatly.

entries.zh: 其赦天下。」
entries.en: Pardon the world."
entries.literal: Pardon the world."

entries.zh: 田肯賀上曰：「甚善，陛下得韓信，又治秦中。
entries.en: Tian Ken congratulated the emperor: "Very good. Your Majesty has obtained Han Xin and also governs Qinzhong.
entries.literal: Tian Ken congratulated the emperor: "Very good. Your Majesty has obtained Han Xin and also governs Qinzhong.

entries.zh: 秦，形勝之國也，帶河阻山，縣隔千里，持戟百萬，秦得百二焉。
entries.en: Qin is a state of advantageous terrain. It is girded by the river and protected by mountains, suspended apart for a thousand li, and could hold off a million halberds with only two men against a hundred.
entries.literal: Qin is a country of advantageous terrain. It girds the river and is blocked by mountains, spanning a thousand li, holding a million halberds. Qin obtained one hundred and twenty percent of them.

entries.zh: 地勢便利，其以下兵 於諸侯，譬猶居高屋之上建瓴水也。
entries.en: The terrain is advantageous. Sending troops from there down upon the feudal lords is like pouring water from a jar while standing on a high roof.
entries.literal: The terrain is convenient. Sending troops from here against the feudal lords is like living on a high roof and pouring water from the eaves.

entries.zh: 夫齊，東有琅邪、即墨之饒，南有泰山之固，西有濁河之限，北有勃海之利，地方二千里，持戟百萬，縣隔千里之外，齊得十二 焉。
entries.en: Qi to the east has the riches of Langya and Jimo, to the south the strength of Mount Tai, to the west the barrier of the Zhuo River, and to the north the advantage of the Bohai Sea. Its territory is two thousand li square and could hold off a million halberds; set apart for a thousand li, Qi obtains the advantage of twelve against a hundred.
entries.literal: Qi to the east has the richness of Langya and Jimo, to the south has the strength of Mount Tai, to the west has the barrier of the Zhu River, to the north has the advantage of the Bohai Sea. Its territory is two thousand li square, holding a million halberds. Spanning a thousand li away, Qi obtains twelve of them.

entries.zh: 此東西秦也。
entries.en: This is the eastern Qin.
entries.literal: This is the eastern Qin.

entries.zh: 非親子弟，莫可使王齊者。」
entries.en: If not a close relative, no one can be made king of Qi."
entries.literal: If not a close relative, no one can be made king of Qi."

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Good."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Good."

entries.zh: 賜金五百斤。
entries.en: He granted five hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: He granted five hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 上還至雒陽，赦韓信，封為淮陰侯。
entries.en: The emperor returned to Luoyang, pardoned Han Xin, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huaiyin.
entries.literal: The emperor returned to Luoyang, pardoned Han Xin, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huaiyin.

entries.zh: 上已封大功臣三十餘人，其餘爭功，未得行封。
entries.en: The emperor had already enfeoffed over thirty great meritorious ministers. The rest contended for merit and had not yet received enfeoffment.
entries.literal: The emperor had already enfeoffed over thirty great meritorious ministers. The rest contended for merit and had not yet received enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 上居南宮，從復道上見諸將往往耦語，以問張良。
entries.en: The emperor resided in the Southern Palace. From the raised passageway above, he saw the generals often talking in pairs and asked Zhang Liang about it.
entries.literal: The emperor resided in the southern palace. From the covered walkway above he saw the generals often talking in pairs. He asked Zhang Liang about it.

entries.zh: 良曰： 「陛下與此屬共取天下，今已為天子，而所封皆故人所愛，所誅皆平生仇怨。
entries.en: Zhang Liang said: "Your Majesty took the world together with these men. Now you are emperor, but those you enfeoff are all old friends you love, and those you execute are all lifelong enemies.
entries.literal: Liang said: "Your Majesty took the world together with these people. Now you are emperor, but those you enfeoff are all old friends you love, those you execute are all lifelong enemies.

entries.zh: 今軍吏計功，以天下為不足用遍封，而恐以過失及誅，故相聚謀反耳。」
entries.en: Now the army officers are calculating merit, considering even the whole world insufficient to enfeoff everyone, and fear that their faults will lead to execution, so they gather to plot rebellion."
entries.literal: Now the army officers calculate merit, considering the world insufficient to universally enfeoff, and fear that faults will lead to execution, so they gather to plot rebellion."

entries.zh: 上曰：「為之 奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "What should be done?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "What should be done?"

entries.zh: 良曰：「取上素所不快，計群臣所共知最甚者一人，先封以示群臣。」
entries.en: Zhang Liang said: "Take someone whom Your Majesty has always disliked, and whom the ministers all know offended you most severely, and enfeoff him first to show the ministers."
entries.literal: Liang said: "Take one whom the emperor has always disliked, whom the ministers all know had the greatest faults, and enfeoff him first to show the ministers."

entries.zh: 三月，上置酒，封雍齒，因趣丞相急定功行封。
entries.en: In the third month, the emperor held a banquet and enfeoffed Yong Chi. He then urged the Chancellor to determine merit quickly and carry out the enfeoffments.
entries.literal: In the third month, the emperor held a banquet and enfeoffed Yong Chi. He then urged the chancellor to quickly determine merit and carry out enfeoffments.

entries.zh: 罷酒，群臣皆喜，曰：「雍齒且侯， 吾屬亡患矣！」
entries.en: The banquet ended. All the ministers were happy, saying: "Even Yong Chi is made marquis. We have no worries!"
entries.literal: The banquet ended. All the ministers were happy, saying: "Even Yong Chi is made marquis. We have no worries!"

entries.zh: 二月，行自雒陽至。
entries.en: In the second month, he traveled from Luoyang to arrive.
entries.literal: In the second month, he traveled from Luoyang to arrive.

entries.zh: 賢趙臣田叔、孟舒等十人，召見與語，漢廷臣無能出其右者。
entries.en: He regarded the worthy Zhao ministers Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and ten others highly, summoned them to audience, and spoke with them. Among the Han court ministers, none could surpass them.
entries.literal: He considered the worthy Zhao ministers Tian Shu, Meng Shu and ten others excellent. He summoned them for audience and spoke with them. Among the Han court ministers, none could surpass them.

entries.zh: 上說，盡拜為郡守、諸侯相。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and appointed them all as commandery governors and feudal lord prime ministers.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed them all as commandery governors and feudal lord prime ministers.

entries.zh: 九月，代相國陳豨反。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Dai prime minister Chen Xi rebelled.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Dai prime minister Chen Xi rebelled.

entries.zh: 上曰：「豨嘗為吾使，甚有信。
entries.en: The emperor said: "Xi once served as my envoy and was very trustworthy.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Xi once served as my envoy and was very trustworthy.

entries.zh: 代地吾所急，故封豨為列侯，以相國守代，今乃與 王黃等劫掠代地！
entries.en: Dai territory is what concerns me urgently, so I enfeoffed Xi as a ranked marquis and had him guard Dai as Chancellor. Now he has joined Wang Huang and others in plundering Dai territory!
entries.literal: Dai territory is what I consider urgent, so I enfeoffed Xi as a marquis to guard Dai as prime minister. Now he joins with Wang Huang and others to plunder Dai territory!

entries.zh: 吏民非有罪也，能去豨、黃來歸者，皆赦之。」
entries.en: Officials and people have no crime. Those who can leave Xi and Huang and return will all be pardoned."
entries.literal: Officials and people have no crime. Those who can leave Xi and Huang and return will all be pardoned."

entries.zh: 上自東，至邯鄲。
entries.en: The emperor went east himself and arrived at Handan.
entries.literal: The emperor went east himself and arrived at Handan.

entries.zh: 上喜曰：「豨不南據邯鄲而阻漳水，吾知其亡能為矣。」
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and said: "Xi has not gone south to occupy Handan and block the Zhang River. I know he is incapable of doing anything."
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "Xi does not occupy Handan to the south and block the Zhang River. I know he has no ability."

entries.zh: 趙相周昌奏常山二十五 城亡其二十城，請誅守尉。
entries.en: Zhao prime minister Zhou Chang memorialized that of Changshan's twenty-five cities, twenty cities were lost, requesting execution of the guards and commandants.
entries.literal: Zhao prime minister Zhou Chang memorialized that of Changshan's twenty-five cities, twenty cities were lost, requesting execution of the guards and commandants.

entries.zh: 上曰：「守尉反乎？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Did the guards and commandants rebel?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Did the guards and commandants rebel?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「不。」
entries.en: He replied: "No."
entries.literal: He replied: "No."

entries.zh: 上曰：「是力不足，亡罪。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Then their strength was insufficient. No crime."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Then their strength was insufficient. No crime."

entries.zh: 上令周昌選趙壯士可令將者，白見四人。
entries.en: The emperor commanded Zhou Chang to select Zhao warriors who could be made generals. He presented four men.
entries.literal: The emperor commanded Zhou Chang to select Zhao warriors who could be made generals. He presented four men.

entries.zh: 上嫚罵曰：「豎子能為將 乎！」
entries.en: The emperor insulted them saying: "You bastards can be generals?"
entries.literal: The emperor insulted them saying: "You bastards can be generals?"

entries.zh: 四人慚，皆伏地。
entries.en: The four were ashamed and all prostrated themselves.
entries.literal: The four were ashamed and all prostrated themselves.

entries.zh: 上封各千戶，以為將。
entries.en: The emperor enfeoffed each with a thousand households and made them generals.
entries.literal: The emperor enfeoffed each with a thousand households and made them generals.

entries.zh: 左右諫曰：「從入蜀漢，伐楚，賞未遍行，今封此，何功？」
entries.en: His attendants advised: "From entering Shu and Han, attacking Chu, rewards have not been universally distributed. Now enfeoffing these, what merit do they have?"
entries.literal: His attendants advised: "From entering Shu and Han, attacking Chu, rewards have not been universally distributed. Now enfeoffing these, what merit do they have?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「非汝所知。
entries.en: The emperor said: "This is not what you know.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "This is not what you know.

entries.zh: 陳豨反，趙代地皆豨有。
entries.en: Chen Xi has rebelled. Zhao and Dai territories are all Xi's.
entries.literal: Chen Xi has rebelled. Zhao and Dai territories are all Xi's.

entries.zh: 吾以羽檄 徵天下兵，未有至者，今計唯獨邯鄲中兵耳。
entries.en: I have summoned troops from the world with urgent dispatches, but none have arrived yet. Now my only hope is the troops in Handan.
entries.literal: I have summoned troops from the world with urgent dispatches, but none have arrived yet. Now my only hope is the troops in Handan.

entries.zh: 吾何愛四千戶，不以慰趙子弟！」
entries.en: Why should I begrudge four thousand households? I will not use them to console the Zhao youths!"
entries.literal: Why should I begrudge four thousand households? I will not use them to console the Zhao youths!"

entries.zh: 皆曰：「善。」
entries.en: They all said: "Good."
entries.literal: They all said: "Good."

entries.zh: 又求「樂毅有後乎？」
entries.en: He also asked: "Does Yue Yi have descendants?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "Does Yue Yi have descendants?"

entries.zh: 得其孫叔，封之樂鄉，號華成君。
entries.en: He obtained his grandson Shu and enfeoffed him at Yuexiang, titled Lord Huacheng.
entries.literal: He obtained his grandson Shu and enfeoffed him at Yuexiang, titled Lord Huacheng.

entries.zh: 問豨將，皆 故賈人。
entries.en: He questioned Xi's generals. They were all former merchants.
entries.literal: He questioned Xi's generals. They were all former merchants.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾知與之矣。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "I know how to deal with them."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I know how to deal with them."

entries.zh: 乃多以金購豨將，豨將多降。
entries.en: So he used much gold to buy Xi's generals. Xi's generals mostly surrendered.
entries.literal: So he used much gold to buy Xi's generals. Xi's generals mostly surrendered.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「吳，古之建國也，日者荊王兼有其地，今死亡後。
entries.en: The edict said: "Wu is an ancient established state. Previously King Jing combined and had its territory. Now after his death.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Wu is an ancient established state. Previously King Jing combined and had its territory. Now after his death.

entries.zh: 朕欲復立吳王，其議可者。」
entries.en: I wish to re-establish the King of Wu. Discuss who is suitable."
entries.literal: I wish to re-establish the King of Wu. Discuss who is suitable."

entries.zh: 長沙王臣等言：「沛侯濞重厚，請立為吳王。」
entries.en: King Changsha and others said: "Marquis of Pei Liu Bi is substantial and sincere. Please establish him as King of Wu."
entries.literal: King Changsha and others said: "Marquis of Pei Liu Bi is substantial and sincere. Please establish him as King of Wu."

entries.zh: 已拜，上召謂濞曰：「汝狀有反相。」
entries.en: Already enfeoffed, the emperor summoned and said to Liu Bi: "Your appearance has the look of rebellion."
entries.literal: Already enfeoffed, the emperor summoned and said to Liu Bi: "Your appearance has the look of rebellion."

entries.zh: 因拊其背，曰：「漢後五十年東南有亂，豈汝邪？
entries.en: So he patted his back and said: "Fifty years after Han, there will be disorder in the southeast. Will it be you?
entries.literal: So he patted his back and said: "Fifty years after Han, there will be disorder in the southeast. Will it be you?

entries.zh: 然天下同姓一家，汝慎毋反。」
entries.en: However, the world of the same surname is one family. You be careful not to rebel."
entries.literal: However, the world of the same surname is one family. You be careful not to rebel."

entries.zh: 濞頓首曰：「不敢。」
entries.en: Liu Bi bowed his head and said: "I dare not."
entries.literal: Liu Bi bowed his head and said: "I dare not."

entries.zh: 王陵可，然少戇，陳平可以助之。
entries.en: Wang Ling is suitable, but he is somewhat blunt; Chen Ping can assist him.
entries.literal: Wang Ling is suitable, but he is somewhat blunt; Chen Ping can assist him.

entries.zh: 陳平知有餘，然難獨任。
entries.en: Chen Ping has more than enough wisdom, but it is difficult to entrust him alone.
entries.literal: Chen Ping has more than enough wisdom, but it is difficult to entrust him alone.

entries.zh: 周勃重厚少文，然安劉氏者必勃也，可令為太尉。」
entries.en: Zhou Bo is steady and substantial but short on refinement. Yet the man who will secure the Liu clan must be Bo. He can be made Grand Marshal."
entries.literal: Zhou Bo is solid and sincere but lacks refinement. However, the one who will secure the Liu clan must be Bo. Can make him grand marshal."

entries.zh: 呂后復問其次，上曰：「此後亦非乃所知也。」
entries.en: Empress Lü asked about the next. The emperor said: "This after is also not what you know."
entries.literal: Empress Lü asked about the next. The emperor said: "This after is also not what you know."

entries.zh: 呂后與審食其謀曰：「諸將故與帝為編戶民，北面為臣，心常鞅鞅，今乃事少主，非盡族是，天下不 安。」
entries.en: Empress Lü plotted with Shen Yiji: "The generals were formerly registered commoners together with the emperor; they faced north and became subjects, but their hearts have always been resentful. Now they are to serve a young ruler. Unless their clans are exterminated, the world will not be at peace."
entries.literal: Empress Lü plotted with Shen Shiqi: "The generals formerly were commoners with the emperor, facing north as subjects, their hearts often dissatisfied. Now they serve a young ruler. If not exterminate their clans, the world will not be peaceful."

entries.zh: 以故不發喪。
entries.en: Therefore they did not announce the death.
entries.literal: Therefore they did not announce the death.

entries.zh: 人或聞，以語酈商。
entries.en: Someone heard and told Li Shang.
entries.literal: Someone heard and told Ji Shang.

entries.zh: 酈商見審食其曰：「聞帝已崩，四日不發喪，欲誅諸將。
entries.en: Li Shang saw Shen Shiqi and said: "Heard the emperor has passed away. Four days without announcing death, wanting to execute the generals.
entries.literal: Ji Shang saw Shen Shiqi and said: "Heard the emperor has passed away. Four days without announcing death, wanting to execute the generals.

entries.zh: 誠如此，天下危矣。
entries.en: If truly so, the world is in danger.
entries.literal: If truly so, the world is in danger.

entries.zh: 陳平、灌嬰將十萬守滎陽，樊噲、周勃將二十 萬定燕代，此聞帝崩，諸將皆誅，必連兵還鄉，以攻關中。
entries.en: Chen Ping and Guan Ying are leading 100,000 men guarding Xingyang, and Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo are leading 200,000 pacifying Yan and Dai. If they hear that the emperor has died and that the generals are all being executed, they will surely join forces and return home to attack Guanzhong.
entries.literal: Chen Ping and Guan Ying lead 100,000 guarding Xingyang, Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo lead 200,000 pacifying Yan and Dai. If they hear the emperor has died and the generals are all executed, they will surely join forces and return home to attack Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 大臣內畔，諸將外反，亡可蹻足待也。」
entries.en: Ministers rebel internally, generals revolt externally. There will be no time to even stamp one's foot."
entries.literal: Ministers rebel internally, generals revolt externally. There will be no time to even stamp one's foot."

entries.zh: 審食其入言之，乃以丁未發喪，大赦天下。
entries.en: Shen Shiqi entered and spoke of it. So on the day dingwei they announced the death and granted a great amnesty to the world.
entries.literal: Shen Shiqi entered and spoke of it. So on the day dingwei they announced the death and granted a great amnesty to the world.

entries.zh: 孝惠皇帝，高祖太子也，母曰呂皇后。
entries.en: Emperor Hui was Gaozu's crown prince. His mother was Empress Lü.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui was Gaozu's crown prince. His mother was Empress Lü.

entries.zh: 帝年五歲，高祖初為漢王。
entries.en: The emperor was five years old when Gaozu first became King of Han.
entries.literal: The emperor was five years old when Gaozu first became King of Han.

entries.zh: 二年，立為太子。
entries.en: In the second year, he was established as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 十二年四月，高祖 崩。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, fourth month, Gaozu passed away.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, fourth month, Gaozu passed away.

entries.zh: 五月丙寅，太子即皇帝位，尊皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: In the fifth month on the day bingyin, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne. He honored the empress as empress dowager.
entries.literal: In the fifth month on the day bingyin, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne. He honored the empress as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 賜民爵一級。
entries.en: He granted the people one rank each.
entries.literal: He granted the people one rank each.

entries.zh: 中郎、郎中滿六歲爵三級，四歲二級。
entries.en: Attendants-in-ordinary and palace gentlemen who completed six years received three ranks, four years received two ranks.
entries.literal: Attendants-in-ordinary and palace gentlemen who completed six years received three ranks, four years received two ranks.

entries.zh: 外郎滿六歲二級。
entries.en: Outer gentlemen who completed six years received two ranks.
entries.literal: Outer gentlemen who completed six years received two ranks.

entries.zh: 中郎不滿一歲一級。
entries.en: Attendants-in-ordinary who did not complete one year received one rank.
entries.literal: Attendants-in-ordinary who did not complete one year received one rank.

entries.zh: 外郎不滿二歲賜錢萬。
entries.en: Outer gentlemen who did not complete two years were granted ten thousand cash.
entries.literal: Outer gentlemen who did not complete two years were granted ten thousand cash.

entries.zh: 宦官尚食比郎中。
entries.en: Eunuchs and food officials ranked equal to palace gentlemen.
entries.literal: Eunuchs and food officials ranked equal to palace gentlemen.

entries.zh: 謁者、執楯、執戟、武士、騶比外郎。
entries.en: Usher attendants, shield bearers, halberd bearers, warriors, and grooms ranked equal to outer gentlemen.
entries.literal: Usher attendants, shield bearers, halberd bearers, warriors, and grooms ranked equal to outer gentlemen.

entries.zh: 太子御驂乘賜爵五大夫，舍人滿五歲二級。
entries.en: The crown prince's carriage attendants were granted the rank of Grand Master, retainers who completed five years received two ranks.
entries.literal: The crown prince's carriage attendants were granted the rank of grand master, retainers who completed five years received two ranks.

entries.zh: 賜給喪事者，二千石錢二萬，六百石以上萬，五百石、二百石以 下至佐史五千。
entries.en: Those assigned to provide for the funeral rites were granted cash by rank: officials at two thousand bushels received twenty thousand coins, those at six hundred bushels or above received ten thousand, and those from five hundred or two hundred bushels down to assistant clerks received five thousand.
entries.literal: Those who provided for funeral affairs: officials of two thousand piculs received twenty thousand cash, six hundred piculs and above received ten thousand, five hundred piculs and two hundred piculs and below down to assistant clerks received five thousand.

entries.zh: 視作斥上者，將軍四十金，二千石二十金，六百石以上六金，五百石以下至佐史二金。
entries.en: For those who supervised the construction work and reported upward, generals received forty units of gold, two-thousand-bushel officials received twenty, those at six hundred bushels or above received six, and those from five hundred bushels down to assistant clerks received two.
entries.literal: For those who oversaw construction and reported upwards: generals received forty jin of gold, officials of two thousand piculs received twenty jin, six hundred piculs and above received six jin, five hundred piculs and below down to assistant clerks received two jin.

entries.zh: 減田租，復十五稅一。
entries.en: He reduced land taxes, restoring the one-in-fifteen tax rate.
entries.literal: He reduced land taxes, restoring the one-in-fifteen tax rate.

entries.zh: 爵五大夫、吏六百石以上及宦皇帝而知 名者有罪當盜械者，皆頌繫。
entries.en: Holders of the noble rank of Fifth Grandee, officials at six hundred bushels or above, and named palace attendants who served the emperor, if guilty of crimes that would ordinarily require fettered custody, were all to be held under privileged restraint instead.
entries.literal: Holders of the noble rank of Fifth Grandee, officials at six hundred bushels or above, and named palace attendants who served the emperor, if guilty of crimes that would ordinarily require fettered custody, were all to be held under privileged restraint instead.

entries.zh: 上造以上及內外公孫耳孫有罪當刑及當為城旦舂者，皆耐為鬼薪白粲。
entries.en: Those ranked Upper Maker or above, together with imperial grandsons and more distant descendants of both inner and outer branches, if guilty of crimes calling for corporal punishment or labor as wall-builders and grain-pounders, were all to have their sentences commuted to the shaved-head labor penalties of ghost-firewood gatherer or white-grain pounder.
entries.literal: Those ranked Upper Maker or above, together with imperial grandsons and more distant descendants of both inner and outer branches, if guilty of crimes calling for corporal punishment or labor as wall-builders and grain-pounders, were all to have their sentences commuted to the shaved-head labor penalties of ghost-firewood gatherer or white-grain pounder.

entries.zh: 民年七十以上若不滿十歲有罪當刑者，皆完之。
entries.en: People aged seventy and above or below ten who had crimes deserving punishment were all spared.
entries.literal: People aged seventy and above or below ten who had crimes deserving punishment were all spared.

entries.zh: 又曰：「吏所以 治民也，能盡其治則民賴之，故重其祿，所以為民也。
