entries.en: He also said, "Officials are appointed to govern the people. If they perform that work fully, the people depend on them; therefore their stipends are made generous, and this too is for the people's sake.
entries.literal: He also said: "Officials are what govern the people. If they can fully carry out their governance then the people rely on them, so their salaries are made heavy, because it is for the people.

entries.zh: 今吏六百石以上父母妻子與同居，及故吏嘗佩將軍都尉印將兵及佩二千石官印者，家唯給軍賦，他無有所與。
entries.en: Now, for officials of six hundred bushels or above whose parents, wives, and children live with them, and for former officials who once bore the seals of generals or commandants and led troops, or bore the seals of two-thousand-bushel offices, their households shall provide only the military levy and shall not be charged with anything else.
entries.literal: Now officials of six hundred piculs and above have their parents, wives, and children living with them, and former officials who once wore general or commandery commander seals and led troops and wore seals of two thousand piculs, their families only provide military levies, otherwise have no other levies.

entries.zh: 贊曰：孝惠內修親親，外禮宰相，優寵齊悼、趙隱，恩敬篤矣。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Emperor Hui cultivated affection for his kin at home and showed ritual respect to the chancellor abroad. His favor toward King Dao of Qi and King Yin of Zhao was generous, and his kindness and respect were deeply sincere.
entries.literal: Appraisal: Emperor Hui internally cultivated closeness to relatives, externally showed courtesy to the chancellor. He favored and honored King Dao of Qi and King Yin of Zhao. His kindness and respect were sincere.

entries.zh: 聞叔孫通之諫則懼然，納曹相國之對而心說，可謂寬仁之主。
entries.en: When he heard Shusun Tong's admonition he was fearful, when he accepted Chancellor Cao's response his heart was pleased. He can be called a lenient and benevolent ruler.
entries.literal: When he heard Shu Sun Tong's admonition he was fearful, when he accepted Chancellor Cao's response his heart was pleased. He can be called a lenient and benevolent ruler.

entries.zh: 遭呂太后虧損至德，悲夫！」
entries.en: He encountered Empress Lü who damaged his perfect virtue. How sad!”
entries.literal: He encountered Empress Lü who damaged his perfect virtue. How sad!”

entries.zh: 三月甲子，皇帝冠，赦天下。
entries.en: In the third month on the day jiazi, the emperor was capped. He pardoned the world.
entries.literal: In the third month on the day jiazi, the emperor was capped. He pardoned the world.

entries.zh: 省法令妨吏民者；
entries.en: He reduced laws and commands that hindered officials and people.
entries.literal: He reduced laws and commands that hindered officials and people.

entries.zh: 除挾書律。
entries.en: He abolished the law against possessing books.
entries.literal: He abolished the law against possessing books.

entries.zh: 長樂宮鴻臺災。
entries.en: The Hong Terrace of Changle Palace suffered a fire.
entries.literal: Changlegong's Hongtai suffered disaster.

entries.zh: 宜陽雨血。
entries.en: Yiyang rained blood.
entries.literal: Yiyang rained blood.

entries.zh: 秋八月戊寅，帝崩于未央宮。
entries.en: In autumn, eighth month, on the day wuyin, the emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: In autumn, eighth month, on the day wuyin, the emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 九月辛丑，葬安陵。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the day xinchou, he was buried at Anling.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinchou, he was buried at Anling.

entries.zh: 四年冬十月壬寅，立皇后張氏。
entries.en: In the fourth year, winter, tenth month, on the day renyin, he established Empress Zhang.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, winter, tenth month, on the day renyin, he established Empress Zhang.

entries.zh: 令郡諸侯王立高廟。
entries.en: He commanded the commanderies and feudal kings to establish temples to Gaozu.
entries.literal: He commanded the commanderies and feudal kings to establish temples to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 春正月，城長安。
entries.en: In spring, first month, he walled Chang'an.
entries.literal: In spring, first month, he walled Chang'an.

entries.zh: 三年春，發長安六百里內男女十四萬六千人城長安，三十日罷。
entries.en: In the third year, in spring, he mobilized 146,000 men and women from within six hundred li of Chang'an to build the city walls. The work was halted after thirty days.
entries.literal: In the third year, spring, he mobilized 146,000 men and women within six hundred li of Chang'an to wall Chang'an. After thirty days they stopped.

entries.zh: 以宗室女為公主，嫁匈奴單于。
entries.en: He made a princess from the imperial clan and married her to the Xiongnu Chanyu.
entries.literal: He made a princess from the imperial clan and married her to the Xiongnu Chanyu.

entries.zh: 夏五月，立閩越君搖為東海王。
entries.en: In summer, fifth month, he established Lord Yao of Minyue as King of Donghai.
entries.literal: In summer, fifth month, he established Lord Yao of Minyue as King of Donghai.

entries.zh: 六月，發諸侯王、列侯徒隸二萬人城長安。
entries.en: In the sixth month, he mobilized 20,000 convict laborers from the feudal lords and marquises to wall Chang'an.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, he mobilized 20,000 convict laborers from the feudal lords and marquises to wall Chang'an.

entries.zh: 春正月，復發長安六百里內男女十四萬五千人城長安，三十日罷。
entries.en: In spring, in the first month, he again mobilized 145,000 men and women from within six hundred li of Chang'an to build the city walls. The work was halted after thirty days.
entries.literal: In spring, first month, he again mobilized 145,000 men and women within six hundred li of Chang'an to wall Chang'an. After thirty days they stopped.

entries.zh: 九月，長安城成。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Chang'an's city walls were completed.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Chang'an's city walls were completed.

entries.zh: 賜民爵，戶一級。
entries.en: He granted the people ranks, one rank per household.
entries.literal: He granted the people ranks, one rank per household.

entries.zh: 起長安西巿，修敖倉。
entries.en: He built Chang'an's western market and repaired the Ao granary.
entries.literal: He built Chang'an's western market and repaired the Ao granary.

entries.zh: 七年冬十月，發車騎、材官詣滎陽，太尉灌嬰將。
entries.en: In the seventh year, winter, tenth month, he dispatched chariots, cavalry, and foresters to Xingyang. Grand marshal Guan Ying led them.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, winter, tenth month, he dispatched chariots, cavalry, and foresters to Xingyang. Grand marshal Guan Ying led them.

entries.zh: 元年冬十二月，趙隱王如意薨。
entries.en: In the first year, winter, twelfth month, King Yin of Zhao Ruyi passed away.
entries.literal: In the first year, winter, twelfth month, King Yin of Zhao Ruyi passed away.

entries.zh: 民有罪，得買爵三十級以免死罪。
entries.en: People who had crimes could purchase thirty ranks to be exempted from death penalty.
entries.literal: People who had crimes could purchase thirty ranks to be exempted from death penalty.

entries.zh: 賜民爵，戶一級。
entries.en: He granted the people ranks, one rank per household.
entries.literal: He granted the people ranks, one rank per household.

entries.zh: 二年冬十月，齊悼惠王來朝，獻城陽郡以益魯元公主邑，尊公主為太后。
entries.en: In the second year, in winter, in the tenth month, King Daohui of Qi came to court and presented Chengyang Commandery to enlarge the fief of Princess Yuan of Lu, honoring the princess as queen dowager.
entries.literal: In the second year, winter, tenth month, King Daohui of Qi came to court and presented Chengyang Commandery to enlarge the fief of Princess Yuan of Lu, honoring the princess as queen dowager.

entries.zh: 夏旱。
entries.en: Summer drought.
entries.literal: Summer drought.

entries.zh: 郃陽侯仲薨。
entries.en: Marquis Zhong of Heyang passed away.
entries.literal: Marquis Zhong of Heyang passed away.

entries.zh: 秋七月辛未，相國何薨。
entries.en: In autumn, seventh month, on the day xinwei, Chancellor He passed away.
entries.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on the day xinwei, Chancellor He passed away.

entries.zh: 高皇后呂氏，生惠帝。
entries.en: Empress Gao, née Lü, bore Emperor Hui.
entries.literal: Empress Gao, née Lü, bore Emperor Hui.

entries.zh: 佐高祖定天下，父兄及高祖而侯者三人。
entries.en: She assisted Emperor Gao in settling the realm; three men among her father and brothers were enfeoffed as marquises under Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: She assisted Emperor Gao in settling the realm; three men among her father and brothers were enfeoffed as marquises under Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 惠帝即位，尊呂后為太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, Empress Lü was honored as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, Empress Lü was honored as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 太后立帝姊魯元公主女為皇后，無子，取後宮美人子名之以為太子。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager made the daughter of the emperor's elder sister, Princess Luyuan, the empress. Since the empress had no son, the Empress Dowager took a son born to one of the palace beauties, gave him a name, and made him crown prince.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager installed the daughter of the emperor's elder sister, Princess Luyuan, as empress. Having no son, she took a son of a palace beauty, named him, and made him crown prince.

entries.zh: 惠帝崩，太子立為皇帝，年幼，太后臨朝稱制，大赦天下。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui died, the crown prince was installed as emperor. Because he was young, the Empress Dowager presided over court and issued edicts on his behalf, granting a general amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui passed away, the crown prince was established as emperor. He was young, and the Empress Dowager presided over court and held the regalia of rule, granting a great amnesty throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 乃立兄子呂台、產、祿、台子通四人為王，封諸呂六人為列侯。
entries.en: She then made four Lü clansmen kings: her elder brother's sons Lü Tai, Lü Chan, and Lü Lu, together with Lü Tai's son Lü Tong. She also enfeoffed six other Lü relatives as ranked marquises.
entries.literal: She then established her elder brother's sons Lü Tai, Chan, Lu, and Tai's son Tong—four men—as kings, and enfeoffed six members of the Lü clan as marquises.

entries.zh: 語在《外戚傳》。
entries.en: The account is given in the "Biographies of the Consort Families."
entries.literal: The account is given in the "Biographies of the Consort Families."

entries.zh: 元年春正月，詔曰：「前日孝惠皇帝言欲除三族罪、妖言令，議未決而崩，今除之。」
entries.en: In the first year, during the first month of spring, an imperial edict declared: 'Previously, Emperor Xiaohui had expressed a desire to abolish the punishment of the three clans and the ordinance against demonic speech, but the discussion remained unresolved when he passed away. We now abolish them.'
entries.literal: In the first year, spring, first month, the edict said: 'Previously Emperor Xiaohui spoke of wanting to abolish the three clans punishment and the demonic speech ordinance, but the discussion was not decided when he passed away, now we abolish them.'

entries.zh: 二月，賜民爵，戶一級。
entries.en: In the second month, noble ranks were granted to the people, one level per household.
entries.literal: Second month, granted the people noble ranks, one level per household.

entries.zh: 初置孝弟力田二千石者一人。
entries.en: For the first time, one person who exemplifies filial piety, fraternal duty, and dedication to farming was appointed at the rank of 2000 shi.
entries.literal: First established one person at 2000 shi who is filial, fraternal, and works the fields.

entries.zh: 夏五月丙申，趙王宮叢臺災。
entries.en: On the bing-shen day of the fifth month in summer, the Cong Terrace in the Zhao king's palace caught fire.
entries.literal: Summer, fifth month, bing-shen day: fire struck the Cong Terrace at the Zhao king's palace.

entries.zh: 立孝惠後宮子強為淮陽王，不疑為恆山王，弘為襄城侯，朝為軹侯，武為壺關侯。
entries.en: The sons of Emperor Xiaohui's harem were enfeoffed: Qiang as King of Huaiyang, Buyi as King of Hengshan, Hong as Marquis of Xiangcheng, Chao as Marquis of Zhi, and Wu as Marquis of Huguan.
entries.literal: Established Emperor Xiaohui's harem son Qiang as Huaiyang king, Buyi as Hengshan king, Hong as Xiangcheng marquis, Chao as Zhi marquis, Wu as Huguan marquis.

entries.zh: 秋，桃李華。
entries.en: In autumn, peach and plum trees came into bloom.
entries.literal: Autumn, peach and plum blossomed.

entries.zh: 贊曰：孝惠、高后之時，海內得離戰國之苦，君臣俱欲無為，故惠帝拱己，高后女主制政，不出房闥，而天下晏然，刑罰罕用，民務稼穡，衣食滋殖。
entries.en: The commentator says: During the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lü, the realm obtained release from the sufferings of the Warring States period. Ruler and ministers alike wished for non-action; therefore Emperor Hui held to a hands-off posture, while Empress Lü, as female ruler, held power without leaving her chambers—yet the realm remained peaceful, punishments were rarely used, the people devoted themselves to farming, and clothing and food grew ever more abundant.
entries.literal: The commentator says: In the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lü, the realm within the seas obtained release from the sufferings of the Warring States. Ruler and ministers alike wished for non-action; therefore Emperor Hui held to a hands-off posture, while Empress Lü, as female ruler, held power without leaving her chambers—yet the realm was tranquil, punishments were rarely used, the people devoted themselves to farming, and clothing and food grew ever more abundant.

entries.zh: 大臣相與陰謀，以為少帝及三弟為王者皆非孝惠子，復共誅之，尊立文帝。
entries.en: The ministers secretly plotted together, determining that the young emperor and his three younger brothers who were kings were all not sons of Emperor Xiaohui. They executed them as well and honored Emperor Wen by establishing him on the throne.
entries.literal: Ministers mutually secretly plotted, considered the young emperor and three younger brothers who were kings all not Xiaohui's sons, again together executed them, honored and established Wen emperor.

entries.zh: 語在周勃、高五王傳。
entries.en: The account is given in the biographies of Zhou Bo and the Five Sons of Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: The account is given in the biographies of Zhou Bo and the Five Sons of Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 二年春，詔曰：「高皇帝匡飭天下，諸有功者皆受分地為列侯，萬民大安，莫不受休德。
entries.en: In spring of the second year, an imperial edict declared: 'Emperor Gao brought order and discipline to the realm. All who had achieved merit received divided territories as marquises, and the people lived in great peace, all benefiting from his benevolent virtue.
entries.literal: Second year spring, edict said: 'Emperor Gao rectified and ordered the realm, all who had merit received divided land as liehou, the myriad people greatly at peace, none did not receive benevolent virtue.

entries.zh: 朕思念至於久遠 而功名不著，亡以尊大誼，施後世。
entries.en: I have reflected on this extending far into the future, yet their merits and achievements remain unrecorded, leaving nothing to honor the great righteousness and pass on to future generations.
entries.literal: I think of this to the distant future but merit and fame are not manifest, there is nothing to honor great righteousness, extend to later generations.

entries.zh: 今欲差次列侯功以定朝位，臧于高廟，世世勿絕，嗣子各襲其功位。
entries.en: Now I wish to differentiate and rank the merits of the marquises to establish their positions at court. These rankings shall be preserved in the Gao Temple, maintained generation after generation without interruption, with each heir inheriting his father's meritorious position.
entries.literal: Now wish to differentiate and order the liehou merits to establish court positions, store in the Gao Temple, generation after generation never cease, heir sons each inherit their merit positions.

entries.zh: 其與列侯議定奏之。」
entries.en: Discuss and determine this with the marquises, then submit a memorial.'
entries.literal: Discuss and decide with the liehou and memorialize it.'

entries.zh: 丞相臣平言：「謹與絳侯臣勃、曲周 侯臣商、潁陰侯臣嬰、安國侯臣陵等議，列侯幸得賜餐錢奉邑，陛下加惠，以功次定朝位，臣請臧高廟。」
entries.en: Chancellor Chen Ping memorialized: 'I have respectfully deliberated with Bo, Marquis of Jiang; Shang, Marquis of Quzhou; Ying, Marquis of Yingyin; Ling, Marquis of Anguo; and others. The marquises have fortunately received bestowed meal allowances and fief incomes. Your Majesty adds further favor by establishing court positions according to the order of their merits. I request that these rankings be preserved in the Gao Temple.'
entries.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping said: 'I have respectfully deliberated with Bo, Marquis of Jiang; Shang, Marquis of Quzhou; Ying, Marquis of Yingyin; Ling, Marquis of Anguo; and others. The marquises have fortunately received bestowed meal allowances and fief incomes. Your Majesty adds further favor by establishing court positions according to the order of their merits. Your subject requests that they be stored in the Gao Temple.'

entries.zh: 奏可。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: Memorial approved.

entries.zh: 春正月乙卯，地震，羌道、武都道山崩。
entries.en: On the yi-mao day of the first month in spring, an earthquake struck, and mountains collapsed at Qiangdao and Wudao.
entries.literal: Spring, first month, yi-mao day: an earthquake; mountains collapsed at Qiangdao and Wudao.

entries.zh: 夏六月丙 戌晦，日有蝕之。
entries.en: On the last day of the sixth month in summer, a bing-xu day, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: Summer sixth month bing-xu last day, the sun was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 秋七月，恆山王不疑薨。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, King Buyi of Hengshan passed away.
entries.literal: Autumn seventh month, Hengshan king Buyi passed away.

entries.zh: 行八銖錢。
entries.en: Eight-zhu coins were put into circulation.
entries.literal: Circulated eight zhu coins.

entries.zh: 上將軍祿、相國產顓兵秉政，自知背高皇帝約，恐為大臣諸侯王所誅，因謀作亂。
entries.en: Senior General Lü Lu and Chancellor of State Lü Chan had seized control of the armies and the government. Aware that they had broken Emperor Gaozu's covenant, they feared being put to death by the great ministers and the regional kings, and so they plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: Senior General Lü Lu and Chancellor of State Lü Chan monopolized the army and held power. Knowing they had violated Emperor Gaozu's covenant, they feared execution by the ministers and regional kings, and therefore plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 時齊悼惠王子朱虛侯章 在京師，以祿女為婦，知其謀，乃使人告兄齊王，令發兵西。
entries.en: At this time, Zhu Xu Marquis Zhang, son of King Daohui of Qi, was in the capital. Married to Lü Lu's daughter, he knew of their plot and sent messengers to inform his elder brother, the King of Qi, ordering him to dispatch troops westward.
entries.literal: At the time, Zhu Xu Marquis Zhang, son of King Daohui of Qi, was in the capital. He had taken Lü Lu's daughter as his wife, knew of their plot, and sent men to inform his elder brother the King of Qi, ordering him to dispatch troops west.

entries.zh: 章欲與太尉勃、丞相平為內應，以誅諸呂。
entries.en: Zhang wished to coordinate internally with Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and Chancellor Chen Ping to execute the various members of the Lü clan.
entries.literal: Zhang wished to act as an inside responder with Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and Chancellor Chen Ping to execute the various Lü.

entries.zh: 齊王遂發兵，又詐琅邪王澤發其國兵，并將而西。
entries.en: The King of Qi then dispatched troops, and moreover deceived King Ze of Langye into dispatching his country's forces. They combined their armies and marched westward.
entries.literal: Qi king then dispatched troops, moreover deceived Langye king Ze to dispatch his country's troops, combined led and went west.

entries.zh: 產、祿等 遣大將軍灌嬰將兵擊之。
entries.en: Lü Chan and Lü Lu dispatched Grand General Guan Ying to lead troops against them.
entries.literal: Lü Chan, Lü Lu, and the others dispatched Grand General Guan Ying to lead troops against them.

entries.zh: 嬰至滎陽，使人諭齊王與連和，待呂氏變而共誅之。
entries.en: When Ying reached Xingyang, he sent messengers to persuade the King of Qi to form an alliance, waiting for a turn among the Lü before jointly executing them.
entries.literal: Ying reached Xingyang and sent men to persuade the King of Qi to ally with him, waiting for a change among the Lü before jointly executing them.

entries.zh: 七年冬十二月，匈奴寇狄道，略二千餘人。
entries.en: In the seventh year, winter, twelfth month, the Xiongnu raided Di Dao and captured more than two thousand people.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, winter, twelfth month: the Xiongnu raided Di Dao and captured more than two thousand people.

entries.zh: 春正月丁丑，趙王友幽死于邸。
entries.en: In spring, on the ding-chou day of the first month, King You of Zhao died in confinement at the residence.
entries.literal: In spring, first month, ding-chou day: King You of Zhao died in confinement at the residence.

entries.zh: 己丑晦，日有蝕之既，以梁王呂產為相國，趙王祿為上將軍，立營陵侯劉澤為琅邪王。
entries.en: On jichou, the last day of the month, there was a total solar eclipse. Lü Chan, King of Liang, was made Chancellor of State; Lü Lu, King of Zhao, was made Senior General; and Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, was established as King of Langye.
entries.literal: On the last day of the month, ji-chou, there was a total eclipse of the sun. Lü Chan, King of Liang, was made Chancellor of State; Lü Lu, King of Zhao, was made Senior General; and Yingling Marquis Liu Ze was established as King of Langye.

entries.zh: 夏五月辛未，詔曰：「昭靈夫人，太上皇妃也；
entries.en: In summer, on the xin-wei day of the fifth month, an edict declared: "Lady Zhaoling was consort of the Supreme Emperor;
entries.literal: In summer, fifth month, xin-wei day, an edict said: "Lady Zhaoling was consort of the Supreme Emperor;

entries.zh: 武哀侯、宣夫人，高皇帝兄姊也。
entries.en: Marquis Wu'ai and Lady Xuan were the elder brother and elder sister of Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: Marquis Wu'ai and Lady Xuan were the elder brother and elder sister of Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 號諡不稱，其議尊號。」
entries.en: Their titles and posthumous names are not fitting; deliberate on honoring them with proper designations."
entries.literal: Their titles and posthumous names are not fitting; deliberate on honoring them with proper designations."

entries.zh: 丞相臣平等請尊昭靈夫人曰昭靈后，武哀侯曰武哀王，宣夫人曰昭哀后。
entries.en: Chancellor Chen Ping and the others requested new honors: Lady Zhaoling should become Empress Zhaoling, Marquis Wu'ai should become King Wu'ai, and Lady Xuan should become Empress Zhao'ai.
entries.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping and others requested that Lady Zhaoling be honored as Empress Zhaoling, Marquis Wu'ai as King Wu'ai, and Lady Xuan as Empress Zhao'ai.

entries.zh: 六月，趙王恢自殺。
entries.en: In the sixth month, King Hui of Zhao killed himself.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, King Hui of Zhao killed himself.

entries.zh: 秋九月，燕王建薨。
entries.en: In autumn, in the ninth month, King Jian of Yan passed away.
entries.literal: In autumn, ninth month, King Jian of Yan passed away.

entries.zh: 南越侵盜長沙，遣隆慮侯灶將兵擊之。
entries.en: Nanyue invaded and plundered Changsha; Longlu Marquis Zao was dispatched to lead troops against them.
entries.literal: Nanyue invaded and plundered Changsha; Longlu Marquis Zao was dispatched to lead troops against them.

entries.zh: 太尉勃與丞相平謀，以曲周侯酈商子寄與祿善，使人劫商令寄紿說祿曰：「高帝與呂后共定天下，劉氏所 立九王，呂氏所立三王，皆大臣之議。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and Chancellor Chen Ping plotted together. Since Marquis of Quzhou Li Shang's son Ji was on good terms with Lü Lu, they sent men to seize Shang and have Ji deceive and persuade Lü Lu, saying: 'Emperor Gaozu and Empress Lü together settled the realm. The Liu clan established nine kings and the Lü clan established three kings—all were matters deliberated by the ministers.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and Chancellor Chen Ping plotted. Since Marquis of Quzhou Li Shang's son Ji was on good terms with Lü Lu, they sent men to seize Shang and have Ji deceive and persuade Lü Lu, saying: 'Emperor Gaozu and Empress Lü together settled the realm. The Liu clan established nine kings and the Lü clan established three kings—all were matters deliberated by the ministers.

entries.zh: 事以布告諸侯王，諸侯王以為宜。
entries.en: These matters were proclaimed by announcement to the various regional kings, who all considered them appropriate.
entries.literal: Matters with announcements proclaim to the various regional kings, the various regional kings considered it appropriate.

entries.zh: 今太后崩，帝少，足下不急之國守藩，乃為上將將兵留此，為大臣諸侯所疑。
entries.en: Now the Empress Dowager has passed away and the emperor is young. You do not urgently return to your state to guard your border, but instead as senior general you lead troops and remain here, causing ministers and regional kings to suspect you.
entries.literal: Now the Empress Dowager has passed away and the emperor is young. You do not urgently return to your state to guard your border, but instead as senior general lead troops and remain here, causing ministers and regional kings to suspect you.

entries.zh: 何不速歸將軍 印，以兵屬太尉，請梁王亦歸相國印，與大臣盟而之國？
entries.en: Why not promptly return your general's seal and hand the troops over to the Grand Commandant? Ask the King of Liang to return his chancellor's seal as well, swear an oath with the ministers, and go back to your own state?
entries.literal: Why not quickly return the general's seal and entrust the troops to the Grand Commandant? Request that the King of Liang also return the chancellor's seal, ally with the ministers, and return to your state?

entries.zh: 齊兵必罷，大臣得安，足下高枕而王千里，此萬世之利也。」
entries.en: The Qi troops will certainly withdraw, allowing the ministers to rest easy. You can recline on your pillow and rule as king of a thousand li territory - this is a benefit for ten thousand generations.'
entries.literal: Qi troops certainly will stop, ministers can be at peace, you can recline pillow and be king of a thousand li, this is ten thousand generations' benefit.'

entries.zh: 祿然其計，使人報產及諸呂老人。
entries.en: Lü Lu approved the plan and sent messengers to inform Lü Chan and the elders of the Lü clan.
entries.literal: Lü Lu approved the plan and sent men to report to Lü Chan and the elders of the Lü clan.

entries.zh: 或以為不 便，計猶豫未有所決。
entries.en: Some considered it inappropriate, and the plan remained undecided amid hesitation.
entries.literal: Some considered it inappropriate, the plan hesitated not yet decided.

entries.zh: 祿信寄，與俱出遊，過其姑呂嬃。
entries.en: Lü Lu trusted Ji and went out touring with him, passing by his aunt Lü Xu.
entries.literal: Lü Lu trusted Ji, went out touring with him, and passed his aunt Lü Xu.

entries.zh: 嬃怒曰：「奴為將而棄軍，呂氏今無處矣！」
entries.en: Lü Xu said angrily: 'You slave—as a general you abandon the army; the Lü clan now has nowhere to turn!'
entries.literal: Xu said angrily: 'You slave—as a general you abandon the army; the Lü clan now has nowhere to turn!'

entries.zh: 乃悉出珠玉寶器散堂下，曰：「無為它人守也！」
entries.en: She then took out all the pearls, jade, and precious vessels, scattering them below the hall, saying: 'Don't guard these for other people!'
entries.literal: Then completely took out pearls jade precious vessels scattered below the hall, said: 'Do not guard for other people!'

entries.zh: 八月庚申，平陽侯窋行御史大夫事，見相國產計事。
entries.en: On the geng-shen day of the eighth month, Pingyang Marquis Kui, acting as Imperial Censor-in-Chief, went to see Chancellor of State Lü Chan to discuss affairs.
entries.literal: Eighth month, geng-shen day: Pingyang Marquis Kui, acting as Imperial Censor-in-Chief, went to see Chancellor of State Lü Chan to discuss affairs.

entries.zh: 郎中令賈壽使從齊來，因數產曰：「王不早之國，今 雖欲行，尚可得邪？」
entries.en: Jia Shou, the Palace Attendant Commander, came as an envoy from Qi and took the occasion to rebuke Lü Chan, saying, 'Your Majesty did not go to your state early. Even if you want to leave now, will you still be able to?'
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Commander Jia Shou came as an envoy from Qi and on this occasion rebuked Chan, saying: 'The king did not return to his state early; now even if he wishes to go, can he still do so?'

entries.zh: 具以灌嬰與齊楚合從狀告產。
entries.en: He fully reported to Chan the situation of Guan Ying's alliance with Qi and Chu.
entries.literal: He fully reported to Chan the situation of Guan Ying's alliance with Qi and Chu.

entries.zh: 平陽侯窋聞其語，馳告丞相平、太尉勃。
entries.en: Pingyang Marquis Kui heard their conversation and galloped to inform Chancellor Chen Ping and Grand Commandant Zhou Bo.
entries.literal: Pingyang Marquis Kui heard their words and galloped to inform Chancellor Chen Ping and Grand Commandant Zhou Bo.

entries.zh: 勃欲入北軍，不得入。
entries.en: Zhou Bo wished to enter the Northern Army but was unable to do so.
entries.literal: Zhou Bo wished to enter the Northern Army but could not.

entries.zh: 襄平侯紀通尚符節，乃令持節矯內勃北軍。
entries.en: Xiangping Marquis Ji Tong still held the tally and credentials. They then ordered him to use the credentials to forge a command admitting Zhou Bo into the Northern Army.
entries.literal: Xiangping Marquis Ji Tong still held the tally and credentials; they then ordered him to use the credentials to forge a command admitting Zhou Bo into the Northern Army.

entries.zh: 勃復 令酈寄、典客劉揭說祿，曰：「帝使太尉守北軍，欲令足下之國，急歸將軍印辭去。
entries.en: Zhou Bo then ordered Li Ji and Protocol Director Liu Jie to persuade Lü Lu, saying: 'The emperor has made the Grand Commandant guard the Northern Army and wishes you to return to your state. Urgently return the general's seal and depart.
entries.literal: Zhou Bo again ordered Li Ji and Protocol Director Liu Jie to persuade Lü Lu, saying: 'The emperor has made the Grand Commandant guard the Northern Army and wishes you to return to your state. Urgently return the general's seal and depart.

entries.zh: 不然，禍且起。」
entries.en: Otherwise, calamity will ensue.'
entries.literal: If not, calamity will arise.'

entries.zh: 祿遂解印屬典客，而以兵授太尉勃。
entries.en: Lü Lu then removed his seal and entrusted it to the Protocol Director, handing command of the troops over to Grand Commandant Zhou Bo.
entries.literal: Lü Lu then removed his seal and entrusted it to the Protocol Director, and handed the troops over to Grand Commandant Zhou Bo.

entries.zh: 勃入軍門，行令軍中曰： 「為呂氏右袒，為劉氏左袒。」
entries.en: Zhou Bo entered the army gate and issued a command throughout the army: 'Those for the Lü clan, bare the right shoulder; those for the Liu clan, bare the left shoulder.'
entries.literal: Zhou Bo entered the army gate and issued a command in the army, saying: 'Those for the Lü clan, bare the right shoulder; those for the Liu clan, bare the left shoulder.'

entries.zh: 軍皆左袒。
entries.en: The entire army bared their left arms.
entries.literal: The army all bared left arms.

entries.zh: 勃遂將北軍。
entries.en: Zhou Bo then took command of the Northern Army.
entries.literal: Zhou Bo then took command of the Northern Army.

entries.zh: 然尚有南軍，丞相平召朱虛侯章佐勃。
entries.en: However, the Southern Army still remained. Chancellor Chen Ping summoned Zhu Xu Marquis Zhang to assist Zhou Bo.
entries.literal: However, the Southern Army still remained; Chancellor Chen Ping summoned Zhu Xu Marquis Zhang to assist Zhou Bo.

entries.zh: 勃令章監軍門，令平陽侯告衛尉，毋內相國產殿門。
entries.en: Zhou Bo ordered Liu Zhang to watch the military gate, and sent the Marquis of Pingyang to tell the Guard Commander not to admit Chancellor of State Lü Chan through the palace gate.
entries.literal: Zhou Bo ordered Zhang to oversee the army gate and commanded Pingyang Marquis to inform the Guard Commander not to admit Chancellor of State Lü Chan through the palace gate.

entries.zh: 產不知祿已去北 軍，入未央宮欲為亂。
entries.en: Unaware that Lü Lu had already left the Northern Army, Lü Chan entered Weiyang Palace intending to start a rebellion.
entries.literal: Lü Chan, not knowing that Lü Lu had already left the Northern Army, entered Weiyang Palace intending to make rebellion.

entries.zh: 殿門弗內，徘徊往來。
entries.en: The palace gate would not admit him, so he paced back and forth outside.
entries.literal: Palace gate not admitted, paced back and forth.

entries.zh: 平陽侯馳語太尉勃，勃尚恐不勝，未敢誦言誅之，乃謂朱虛侯章曰：「急入宮衛帝。」
entries.en: The Marquis of Pingyang galloped back to inform Grand Commandant Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo still feared they might not prevail and did not yet dare openly call for Lü Chan's execution, so he said to Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu, 'Enter the palace at once and guard the emperor.'
entries.literal: Pingyang Marquis galloped to inform Grand Commandant Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo still feared they might not prevail and dared not openly proclaim the order to execute him. He then said to Zhu Xu Marquis Zhang: 'Enter the palace at once to guard the emperor.'

entries.zh: 章從勃請卒千人，入未央宮掖 門，見產廷中。
entries.en: Zhang requested one thousand troops from Zhou Bo and entered Weiyang Palace through the side gate, where he saw Lü Chan in the courtyard.
entries.literal: Zhang requested one thousand troops from Zhou Bo, entered Weiyang Palace through the side gate, and saw Lü Chan in the courtyard.

entries.zh: 日餔時，遂擊產。
entries.en: They attacked Lü Chan at the hour of the afternoon meal.
entries.literal: At the hour of the afternoon meal, they attacked Lü Chan.

entries.zh: 產走。
entries.en: Lü Chan fled from the scene.
entries.literal: Lü Chan fled.

entries.zh: 天大風，從官亂，莫敢鬥者。
entries.en: A fierce wind arose; the attendant officials were thrown into chaos, and none dared to fight.
entries.literal: A fierce wind arose; the attendant officials were thrown into chaos, and none dared fight.

entries.zh: 逐產，殺之郎中府吏舍廁中。
entries.en: They pursued Lü Chan and killed him in a latrine attached to the clerks' quarters at the Langzhong offices.
entries.literal: They pursued Lü Chan and killed him in the privy of the clerk's quarters in the Langzhong office.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也，母曰薄姬。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen was the middle son of Emperor Gaozu, born to Lady Bo.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son, his mother was named Lady Bo.

entries.zh: 高祖十一年，誅陳豨，定代地，立為代王，都中都。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after executing Chen Xi and pacifying the Dai region, he was established as King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's eleventh year, executed Chen Xi, pacified Dai territory, established as King of Dai, capital at Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 十七年秋，高后崩，諸呂謀為亂，欲危劉氏。
entries.en: In the autumn of the seventeenth year, Empress Gao passed away, and the Lü clan plotted rebellion in an attempt to threaten the Liu family.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year autumn, Empress Gao passed away, the Lü clan plotted rebellion, desiring to endanger the Liu clan.

entries.zh: 丞相陳平、太尉周勃、朱虛侯劉章等共誅之，謀立代王。
entries.en: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang, and others joined together to execute the Lü clan and plotted to establish the King of Dai on the throne.
entries.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and others together executed them, plotted to establish the King of Dai.

entries.zh: 語在高后紀、高五王傳。
entries.en: The full account appears in the Annals of Empress Gao and the Biographies of the Five Kings of Gao.
entries.literal: The account is in the Annals of Empress Gao and the Biographies of the Five Kings of Gao.

entries.zh: 大臣遂使人迎代王。
entries.en: The ministers then dispatched envoys to welcome the King of Dai.
entries.literal: The ministers then sent people to welcome the King of Dai.

entries.zh: 郎中令張武等議，皆曰：「漢大臣皆故高帝時將，習兵事，多謀詐，其屬意非止此 也，特畏高帝、呂太后威耳。
entries.en: The Commandant of the Imperial Household Zhang Wu and his colleagues discussed the matter and all said: 'The Han ministers are all veteran generals from Emperor Gao's era, skilled in military affairs and full of treacherous schemes. Their ambitions extend far beyond this—they only fear the intimidating authority of Emperor Gao and Empress Lü.
entries.literal: The Commandant of the Langzhong Zhang Wu and others discussed it, all saying: 'The Han ministers are all former generals from Emperor Gao's time, experienced in military affairs, full of cunning schemes. Their ambitions are not limited to this, they only fear the authority of Emperor Gao and Empress Lü.

entries.zh: 今已誅諸呂，新喋血京師，以迎大王為名，實不可信。
entries.en: Now that the Lü clan has been executed and the capital still runs with fresh blood, their claim of welcoming Your Majesty is utterly untrustworthy.
entries.literal: Now that the Lü clan has been executed and the capital is fresh with blood, using the name of welcoming Your Majesty, it is truly not trustworthy.

entries.zh: 願稱疾無往，以觀其變。」
entries.en: We urge Your Majesty to feign illness and decline to go, so that we may observe how the situation develops.'
entries.literal: We wish you would feign illness and not go, to observe how things change.'

entries.zh: 中尉宋昌進曰：「群臣之議皆非也。
entries.en: Song Chang, the Superintendent of the Imperial Household, stepped forward and declared: 'All the ministers' advice is mistaken.
entries.literal: The Superintendent of the Imperial Household Song Chang stepped forward and said: 'The ministers' discussions are all wrong.

entries.zh: 夫秦失其政，豪 傑並起，人人自以為得之者以萬數，然卒踐天子位者，劉氏也，天下絕望，一矣。
entries.en: When Qin lost its grip on power, countless heroes rose up, each believing they could claim the throne—numbering in the tens of thousands. Yet in the end, it was the Liu clan who ascended the imperial throne. The world had given up all hope—that is the first reason.
entries.literal: When Qin lost its governance, heroic figures rose up together, those who considered themselves worthy of it numbered in the tens of thousands, yet in the end the one who ascended the imperial throne was the Liu clan. The world had lost all hope, this is the first reason.

entries.zh: 高帝王子弟，地犬牙相制，所謂盤石之宗也，天下服其彊，二矣。
entries.en: Emperor Gao's sons and brothers hold territories that interlock like jagged teeth, creating what is known as an unbreakable clan foundation. The world submits to their power—that is the second reason.
entries.literal: The sons and younger brothers of Emperor Gao hold territories that interlock like dog teeth, forming what is called an unshakable clan. The world submits to their strength, this is the second reason.

entries.zh: 漢興，除秦煩 苛，約法令，施德惠，人人自安，難動搖，三矣。
entries.en: Since the Han dynasty rose to power, it has abolished Qin's burdensome harshness, simplified the laws and regulations, and extended benevolence and favor to all. The people live in security, making the regime difficult to overthrow—that is the third reason.
entries.literal: Since the Han arose, it has eliminated Qin's oppressive harshness, simplified laws and commands, and bestowed benevolence and favor. Everyone feels secure, making it difficult to shake, this is the third reason.

entries.zh: 夫以呂太后之嚴，立諸呂為三王，擅權專制，然而太尉以一節入北軍，一呼士皆袒左，為劉氏，畔諸呂，卒以滅 之。
entries.en: Despite Empress Lü's iron-fisted rule in establishing three Lü kings and monopolizing power with dictatorial control, the Grand Commandant Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army with just one imperial tally. With a single command, all the soldiers bared their left arms in loyalty to the Liu clan, rebelled against the Lü faction, and ultimately destroyed them.
entries.literal: Despite Empress Lü's severity in establishing the Lü clan as three kings, monopolizing power and ruling dictatorially, the Grand Commandant entered the Northern Army with just one tally, called out once and all the soldiers bared their left arms for the Liu clan, rebelled against the Lü clan, and ultimately destroyed them.

entries.zh: 此乃天授，非人力也。
entries.en: This was a gift from Heaven, not something accomplished through human endeavor.
entries.literal: This was bestowed by Heaven, not achieved by human effort.

entries.zh: 今大臣雖欲為變，百姓弗為使，其黨寧能專一邪？
entries.en: Even if the ministers wanted to rebel, the common people wouldn't follow their orders. How could such a faction ever unite?
entries.literal: Now even if the ministers desire to make changes, the common people will not serve as their envoys. How could their faction achieve unity?

entries.zh: 內有朱虛、東牟之親，外畏吳、楚、淮南、琅邪、齊、代之彊。
entries.en: Within the court they have the support of the Zhuxu and Dongmu marquises, while externally they fear the military power of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langya, Qi, and Dai.
entries.literal: Internally there are the close relations of Zhuxu and Dongmu, externally they fear the strength of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langya, Qi, and Dai.

entries.zh: 方今高帝子獨淮南王與 大王，大王又長，賢聖仁孝，聞於天下，故大臣因天下之心而欲迎立大王，大王勿疑也。」
entries.en: Of Emperor Gaozu's surviving sons, only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty remain. You are the elder brother, renowned throughout the empire for your virtue, wisdom, benevolence, and filial piety. The ministers, following the will of the people, wish to welcome you as emperor. Do not doubt this.'
entries.literal: Nowadays among Gaozu's sons only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty remain. Your Majesty is also the eldest, virtuous, sage-like, benevolent and filial, renowned throughout the world. Therefore the ministers, following the will of the world, desire to welcome and establish Your Majesty. Your Majesty should not doubt this.'

entries.zh: 代王報太后，計猶豫未定。
entries.en: The King of Dai informed the Empress Dowager, but his plans remained uncertain and unresolved.
entries.literal: The King of Dai reported to the Empress Dowager; his plans were hesitant and undecided.

entries.zh: 卜之，兆得大橫。
entries.en: He consulted the oracle, and received the omen of 'great horizontal.'
entries.literal: He divined it; the omen obtained was 'great horizontal.'

entries.zh: 占曰：「大橫庚庚，余為天 王，夏啟以光。」
entries.en: The diviner interpreted: 'Great horizontal omen, bright and clear—I shall become the heavenly king, radiant like Xia Qi.'
entries.literal: The interpretation said: 'Great horizontal geng geng, I become the heavenly king, Xia Qi with radiance.'

entries.zh: 代王曰：「寡人固已為王，又何王乎？」
entries.en: The King of Dai replied: 'I am already a king—what greater kingship could there be?'
entries.literal: The King of Dai said: 'I am already a king, what more kingship is there?'

entries.zh: 卜人曰：「所謂天王者，乃天子也。」
entries.en: The diviner explained: 'The heavenly king of which I speak is none other than the emperor himself.'
entries.literal: The diviner said: 'What is called heavenly king is precisely the Son of Heaven.'

entries.zh: 於是代王乃遣太后弟薄昭見太尉勃，勃等具言所以迎立王者。
entries.en: At this the King of Dai dispatched Bo Zhao, the Empress Dowager's younger brother, to meet with Grand Commandant Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo and his colleagues explained in detail the reasons for welcoming and enthroning the king.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King of Dai sent the Empress Dowager's younger brother Bo Zhao to see Grand Commandant Zhou Bo; Zhou Bo and the others fully explained the reasons for welcoming and establishing the king.

entries.zh: 昭還 報曰：「信矣，無可疑者。」
entries.en: Bo Zhao returned and reported: 'It is trustworthy indeed—nothing to doubt.'
entries.literal: Zhao returned and reported: 'It is trustworthy, there is nothing to doubt.'

entries.zh: 代王笑謂宋昌曰：「果如公言。」
entries.en: The King of Dai smiled and told Song Chang: 'Just as you predicted.'
entries.literal: The King of Dai smiled and said to Song Chang: 'Indeed as you said.'

entries.zh: 乃令宋昌驂乘，張武等六人乘六乘傳詣長安。
entries.en: He then commanded Song Chang to serve as his chariot companion, while Zhang Wu and five others rode six relay carriages to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Then he ordered Song Chang to ride as charioteer, and Zhang Wu and five others to ride six relay carriages to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 至高陵止，而使宋昌先之長安觀變。
entries.en: They halted at Gaoling and sent Song Chang ahead to Chang'an to assess the situation.
entries.literal: They stopped at Gaoling, and sent Song Chang ahead to Chang'an to observe the situation.

entries.zh: 閏月己酉，入代邸。
entries.en: On the jiyou day of the intercalary month, he entered the Dai residence.
entries.literal: On the jiyou day of the intercalary month, he entered the Dai residence.

entries.zh: 群臣從至，上議曰：「丞相臣平、太尉臣勃、大將軍臣武、御史大夫臣蒼、宗正臣郢、朱虛侯臣章、東牟侯臣興居、典客臣揭再拜言大王足下：子弘等皆非孝惠皇帝子，不當奉宗廟。
entries.en: The ministers followed and arrived. The court deliberated, saying: "Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chai Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dong Mou Liu Xingju, and Court Receptionist Liu Jie bowed twice and addressed Your Majesty: Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and should not serve at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: The ministers followed and arrived. The court deliberated, saying: "Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chai Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dong Mou Liu Xingju, and Court Receptionist Liu Jie bowed twice and addressed Your Majesty: Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and ought not serve at the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 臣謹請陰安侯、頃王后、琅邪王、列侯、吏二千石議，大王高皇帝子，宜為嗣。
entries.en: We ministers respectfully requested deliberation by the Marquis of Yin'an, the queen dowager of King Qing, the King of Langye, the ranked marquises, and officials of two thousand shi. They agree that Your Majesty, as a son of Emperor Gao, should be the successor.
entries.literal: We ministers respectfully request that the Marquis of Yin'an, the Queen Dowager of King Qing, the King of Langye, the ranked marquises, and officials of two thousand shi deliberate. Your Majesty is a son of Emperor Gao and should be the successor.

entries.zh: 願大王即天子位。」
entries.en: We wish Your Majesty to immediately ascend the imperial throne."
entries.literal: We wish Your Majesty to immediately ascend the imperial throne."

entries.zh: 代王曰：「奉高帝宗廟，重事也。
entries.en: The King of Dai said: "Serving at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple is a grave matter.
entries.literal: The King of Dai said: "Serving at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple is a grave matter.

entries.zh: 寡人不佞，不足以稱。
entries.en: I am unworthy and insufficient for the role.
entries.literal: I am unworthy and insufficient for the role.

entries.zh: 願請楚王計宜者，寡人弗敢當。」
entries.en: I wish to request that the King of Chu be consulted on what is appropriate. I do not dare accept."
entries.literal: I wish to request that the King of Chu be consulted on what is appropriate. I do not dare accept."

entries.zh: 群臣皆伏，固請。
entries.en: All the ministers prostrated themselves and pressed their request.
entries.literal: All the ministers prostrated themselves and pressed their request.

entries.zh: 代王西鄉讓者三，南鄉讓者再。
entries.en: The King of Dai declined three times while facing west and twice while facing south.
entries.literal: The King of Dai declined three times while facing west and twice while facing south.

entries.zh: 丞相平等皆曰：「臣伏計之，大王奉高祖宗廟最宜稱，雖天下諸侯萬民皆以為宜。
entries.en: Chancellor Ping and the others said: "We ministers have considered this carefully. Your Majesty is most fitting and worthy to serve at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple, and the feudal lords and people throughout the realm all agree.
entries.literal: Chancellor Ping and the others all said: "We ministers have considered this carefully. Your Majesty is most fitting and worthy to serve at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple, and the feudal lords and myriad people throughout the realm all consider it fitting.

entries.zh: 臣等為宗廟社稷計，不敢忽。
entries.en: For the sake of the ancestral temple and the state, we ministers dare not be negligent.
entries.literal: For the sake of the ancestral temple and the state, we ministers dare not be negligent.

entries.zh: 願大王幸聽臣等。
entries.en: We beg Your Majesty to hear your ministers.
entries.literal: May Your Majesty graciously hear your ministers.

entries.zh: 臣謹奉天子璽符再拜上。」
entries.en: We ministers respectfully present the imperial seal and tally, bowing twice in offering."
entries.literal: We ministers respectfully present the imperial seal and tally, bowing twice in offering."

entries.zh: 代王曰：「宗室將相王列侯以為其宜寡人，寡人不敢辭。」
entries.en: The King of Dai said: "The imperial clan, generals, chancellors, kings, and marquises all consider me the suitable one. I do not dare decline."
entries.literal: The King of Dai said: "The imperial clan, generals, chancellors, kings, and marquises all consider me the suitable one. I do not dare decline."

entries.zh: 遂即天子位。
entries.en: He immediately ascended the imperial throne.
entries.literal: He then immediately ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 群臣以次侍。
entries.en: The ministers attended in proper order.
entries.literal: The ministers attended in proper order.

entries.zh: 使太僕嬰、東牟侯興居先清宮，奉天子法駕迎代邸。
entries.en: He ordered Grand Coachman Xiahou Ying and Liu Xingju, Marquis of Dongmou, to clear the palace first, then bring the imperial ceremonial carriage to welcome him at the Dai residence.
entries.literal: He ordered Grand Coachman Ying and Marquis Dong Mou Xingju first to clear the palace and bring the imperial ceremonial carriage to welcome him at the Dai residence.

entries.zh: 皇帝即日夕入未央宮。
entries.en: The emperor entered Weiyang Palace that same evening.
entries.literal: That evening the emperor entered Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 夜拜宋昌為衛將軍，領南北軍，張武為郎中令，行殿中。
entries.en: That night he appointed Song Chang General of the Guards, commanding the Northern and Southern Armies, and Zhang Wu Chamberlain for Attendants, managing affairs inside the palace.
entries.literal: That night he appointed Song Chang as General of the Guards to command the Northern and Southern Armies, and Zhang Wu as Chamberlain for Attendants to oversee affairs within the palace halls.

entries.zh: 還坐前殿，下詔曰：「制詔丞相、太尉、御史大夫：間者諸呂用事擅權，謀為大逆，欲危劉氏宗廟，賴將相列侯宗室大臣誅之，皆伏其辜。
entries.en: He returned and sat in the front hall, then issued an edict, saying: "By imperial decree to the Chancellor, Grand Commandant, and Grandee Secretary: Recently the Lü clansmen handled affairs and monopolized power, plotting great rebellion to endanger the Liu clan ancestral temple. Thanks to the generals, chancellors, marquises, imperial clan, and ministers who executed them, they all received their just punishment.
entries.literal: He returned and sat in the front hall, then issued an edict, saying: "By imperial decree to the Chancellor, Grand Commandant, and Grandee Secretary: Recently the Lü clansmen handled affairs and monopolized power, plotting great rebellion and seeking to endanger the Liu clan ancestral temple. Relying on the generals, chancellors, marquises, imperial clan, and ministers who executed them, they all submitted to their punishment.

entries.zh: 朕初即位，其赦天下，賜民爵一級，女子百戶牛酒，酺五日。」
entries.en: Since I have only just ascended the throne, let there be a general amnesty under Heaven. Grant the people one rank of nobility, and in every hundred households grant the women oxen and wine. Hold drinking celebrations for five days."
entries.literal: Since I have only just ascended the throne, let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm, grant the people one rank of nobility, and in every hundred households grant the women oxen and wine. Hold drinking celebrations for five days."

entries.zh: 元年冬十月辛亥，皇帝見于高廟。
entries.en: On the xinhai day of the tenth month of winter in the first year, the emperor appeared at Gaozu's ancestral temple.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day of the tenth month of winter in the first year, the emperor appeared at the Gao ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 遣車騎將軍薄昭迎皇太后于代。
entries.en: He dispatched Chariot Cavalry General Bo Zhao to welcome the empress dowager from Dai.
entries.literal: He dispatched Chariot Cavalry General Bo Zhao to welcome the empress dowager from Dai.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「前呂產自置為相國，呂祿為上將軍，擅遣將軍灌嬰將兵擊齊，欲代劉氏。
entries.en: An edict said: "Formerly Lü Chan set himself up as Chancellor of State, while Lü Lu became Supreme General. They sent General Guan Ying with troops to attack Qi on their own authority, intending to replace the Liu clan.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Previously Lü Chan appointed himself Chancellor of State, and Lü Lu was made Supreme General. They arbitrarily dispatched General Guan Ying with troops to attack Qi, intending to replace the Liu clan.

entries.zh: 嬰留滎陽，與諸侯合謀以誅呂氏。
entries.en: Ying remained at Xingyang and joined the feudal lords in plotting to execute the Lü clan.
entries.literal: Ying remained at Xingyang and joined the feudal lords in plotting to execute the Lü clan.

entries.zh: 呂產欲為不善，丞相平與太尉勃等謀奪產等軍。
entries.en: Lü Chan intended to do evil, and Chancellor Ping and Grand Commandant Bo and others plotted to seize the armies of Chan and his associates.
entries.literal: Lü Chan intended to do evil, so Chancellor Ping and Grand Commandant Bo and others plotted to seize the armies of Chan and his associates.

entries.zh: 朱虛侯章首先捕斬產。
entries.en: Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang was first to capture and execute Chan.
entries.literal: Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang was first to capture and execute Chan.

entries.zh: 太尉勃身率襄平侯通持節承詔入北軍。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Bo personally led Marquis Xiangping Tong, holding the imperial tally and edict, into the Northern Army.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Bo personally led Marquis Xiangping Tong, holding the imperial tally and edict, into the Northern Army.

entries.zh: 典客揭奪呂祿印。
entries.en: Court Receptionist Jie seized Lü Lu's seal.
entries.literal: Court Receptionist Jie seized Lü Lu's seal.

entries.zh: 其益封太尉勃邑萬戶，賜金五千斤。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Bo was granted an additional fief of ten thousand households and five thousand jin of gold.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Bo was granted an additional fief of ten thousand households and five thousand jin of gold.

entries.zh: 丞相平、將軍嬰邑各三千戶，金二千斤。
entries.en: Chancellor Ping and General Ying each received a fief of three thousand households and two thousand jin of gold.
entries.literal: Chancellor Ping and General Ying each received a fief of three thousand households and two thousand jin of gold.

entries.zh: 朱虛侯章、襄平侯通邑各二千戶，金千斤。
entries.en: Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang and Marquis Xiangping Tong each received a fief of two thousand households and one thousand jin of gold.
entries.literal: Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang and Marquis Xiangping Tong each received a fief of two thousand households and one thousand jin of gold.

entries.zh: 封典客揭為陽信侯，賜金千斤。」
entries.en: Court Receptionist Jie was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin and granted one thousand jin of gold."
entries.literal: Court Receptionist Jie was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin and granted one thousand jin of gold."

entries.zh: 正月，有司請蚤建太子，所以尊宗廟也。
entries.en: In the first month, the officials petitioned to establish the crown prince without delay, in order to honor the ancestral temples.
entries.literal: In the first month, the officials requested to establish the crown prince early, in order to honor the ancestral temples.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕既不德，上帝神明未歆饗也，天下人民未有轺志。
entries.en: The imperial edict stated: 'Lacking virtue as I do, I have not yet won the acceptance of the gods above for my offerings. The people of the realm have not yet attained settled hearts.
entries.literal: The edict said: 'I, being without virtue, have not yet caused the gods above to accept my offerings. The people of the world do not yet have settled hearts.

entries.zh: 今 縱不能博求天下賢聖有德之人而嬗天下焉，而曰豫建太子，是重吾不德也。
entries.en: Even if I cannot seek out the worthy sages and virtuous men of the world to entrust the realm to them, to speak of establishing a crown prince prematurely would only compound my lack of virtue.
entries.literal: Now even if I cannot extensively seek out the worthy sages and virtuous people of the world to transfer the realm to them, yet to speak of establishing a crown prince in advance is to compound my lack of virtue.

entries.zh: 謂天下何？
entries.en: What would the people of the world think?
entries.literal: What would the world think?

entries.zh: 其安之。」
entries.en: Let the matter rest.'
entries.literal: Leave it be.'

entries.zh: 有司曰：「豫建太子，所以重宗廟社稷，不忘天下也。」
entries.en: The officials replied: 'Establishing the crown prince in advance honors the ancestral temples and the altars of state, and shows concern for the welfare of the world.'
entries.literal: The officials said: 'Establishing the crown prince in advance honors the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and does not forget the world.'

entries.zh: 上曰： 「楚王，季父也，春秋高，閱天下之義理多矣，明於國家之體。
entries.en: The emperor replied: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. Advanced in years and experienced in the world's moral principles, he understands the proper order of the state.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. He is advanced in age, has seen much of the world's principles and righteousness, understands the structure of the state.

entries.zh: 吳王於朕，兄也；
entries.en: The King of Wu is like an elder brother to me;
entries.literal: The King of Wu is an elder brother to me;

entries.zh: 淮南王，弟也：皆秉德以陪朕，豈為不豫哉！
entries.en: The King of Huainan is like a younger brother to me. All of them uphold virtue to support me—how could they not stand ready as successors!
entries.literal: The King of Huainan is my younger brother: all uphold virtue to assist me, how could they not be prepared!

entries.zh: 諸侯王宗室昆弟有功臣，多賢及有德 義者，若舉有德以陪朕之不能終，是社稷之靈，天下之福也。
entries.en: Among the feudal kings and imperial clansmen who have rendered meritorious service, many are worthy and virtuous. If we select those with virtue to compensate for my deficiencies, this would be a blessing to the altars of state and bring fortune to the world.
entries.literal: Among the feudal kings, imperial clan brothers, and kinsmen who have rendered merit, many are worthy and virtuous. If we raise those with virtue to assist my shortcomings, this would be the blessing of the altars of state and the fortune of the world.

entries.zh: 今不選舉焉，而曰必子，人其以朕為忘賢有德者而專於子，非所以憂天下也。
entries.en: Now if we refuse to select from among them and insist it must be my own son, people will think I disregard the worthy and virtuous while favoring my own child—this is not how to show concern for the world.
entries.literal: Now if we do not select from among them and insist it must be my son, people will think I forget the worthy and virtuous and am partial to my son—this is not the way to care for the world.

entries.zh: 朕甚不取。」
entries.en: I find this most unacceptable.'
entries.literal: I strongly disagree.'

entries.zh: 有司固請 曰：「古者殷周有國，治安皆且千歲，有天下者莫長焉，用此道也。
entries.en: The officials persisted in their petition, saying: 'In ancient times, the Yin and Zhou dynasties possessed their realms, and their peace and stability lasted nearly a thousand years. No rulers who possessed the world lasted longer than they did, and this was the method they used.
entries.literal: The officials firmly petitioned, saying: 'In ancient times, Yin and Zhou possessed their states, their peace and security lasted nearly a thousand years. None who possessed the world lasted longer than this, using this way.

entries.zh: 立嗣必子，所從來遠矣。
entries.en: Establishing heirs must be one's own sons—this tradition stretches far back in time.
entries.literal: Establishing heirs must be sons—the tradition comes from far back.

entries.zh: 高帝始平天下，建諸侯，為帝者太祖。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu first pacified the world and established the feudal lords, he became the great ancestor for all emperors.
entries.literal: When Gaozu first pacified the world and established the feudal lords, for emperors he became the great ancestor.

entries.zh: 諸侯王列侯始受國者亦皆為其國 祖。
entries.en: The feudal kings and marquises who first received their fiefs also all became the founding ancestors of their states.
entries.literal: The feudal kings and marquises who first received their states also all became ancestors of their states.

entries.zh: 子孫繼嗣，世世不絕，天下之大義也。
entries.en: Sons and grandsons succeeding one another, generation after generation without interruption—this is the supreme moral principle of the world.
entries.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeding each other, generation after generation without end—this is the great righteousness of the world.

entries.zh: 故高帝設之以撫海內。
entries.en: Therefore Emperor Gaozu established this system to pacify the empire.
entries.literal: Therefore Gaozu established this to pacify the realm.

entries.zh: 今釋宜建而更選於諸侯宗室，非高帝之志也。
entries.en: Now to abandon what should rightfully be established and instead select from among the feudal kings and imperial clansmen—this was not Emperor Gaozu's intention.
entries.literal: Now to abandon what should properly be established and instead select from the feudal kings and imperial clan—this is not Gaozu's intention.

entries.zh: 更議不宜。
entries.en: Further debate would be inappropriate.
entries.literal: Further discussion is not appropriate.

entries.zh: 子啟最長，敦厚慈仁，請建以為太子。」
entries.en: Prince Qi is the eldest son, honest and sincere, kind and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'
entries.literal: Prince Qi is the eldest, honest, kind, and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'

entries.zh: 上乃許之。
entries.en: The emperor then gave his approval.
entries.literal: The emperor then consented.

entries.zh: 因賜天下民當為父後者爵一級。
entries.en: Therefore he granted one rank of nobility to all people throughout the empire who were designated to succeed their fathers as heirs.
entries.literal: Therefore he granted one rank of nobility to all people in the world who were to succeed their fathers.

entries.zh: 封將軍薄昭為軹侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed General Bo Zhao as the Marquis of Zhi.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed General Bo Zhao as Marquis of Zhi.

entries.zh: 六月，令郡國無來獻。
entries.en: In the sixth month, he issued a command prohibiting the commanderies and kingdoms from presenting tribute.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, he commanded the commanderies and kingdoms not to come with tribute.

entries.zh: 施惠天下，諸侯四夷遠近驩洽。
entries.en: He bestowed benevolence upon the empire, and the feudal lords and the four barbarian tribes, both near and far, lived in harmonious concord.
entries.literal: He extended favor to the world, and the feudal lords and four barbarians, near and far, were harmoniously united.

entries.zh: 乃脩代來功。
entries.en: He then recompensed the merits earned during his time as King of Dai.
entries.literal: He then rewarded the merits from the time in Dai.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「方大臣誅諸呂迎朕，朕狐 疑，皆止朕，唯中尉宋昌勸朕，朕已得保宗廟。
entries.en: The imperial edict stated: 'When the ministers executed the Lü clan and came to welcome me, I was filled with hesitation and doubt. All tried to dissuade me, but only Superintendent Song Chang urged me forward. Thus I was able to preserve the ancestral temples.
entries.literal: The edict said: 'When the ministers executed the Lü clan and welcomed me, I was hesitant and doubtful, all tried to stop me, only Superintendent Song Chang urged me, and thus I was able to preserve the ancestral temples.

entries.zh: 已尊昌為衛將軍，其封昌為壯武侯。
entries.en: I have already honored Song Chang as General of the Guard. Now I enfeoff him as the Marquis of Zhuangwu.
entries.literal: I have already honored Chang as General of the Guard, now I enfeoff Chang as Marquis of Zhuangwu.

entries.zh: 諸從朕六人，官皆至九卿。」
entries.en: The six men who accompanied me shall all be appointed to the rank of the Nine Ministers.'
entries.literal: The six people who followed me, their offices all reached the Nine Ministers.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「列侯從高帝入蜀漢者六十八人益邑各三百 戶。
entries.en: He further declared: 'The marquises who followed Emperor Gaozu into Shu and Han—sixty-eight men in total—shall each have their fiefs increased by three hundred households.
entries.literal: He also said: 'The marquises who followed Gaozu into Shu and Han, sixty-eight persons, increase their fiefs by three hundred households each.

entries.zh: 吏二千石以上從高帝潁川守尊等十人食邑六百戶，淮陽守申屠嘉等十人五百戶，衛尉足等十人四百戶。」
entries.en: For officials of two thousand shi rank and above who followed Emperor Gaozu: Governor Zun of Yingchuan and nine others shall receive food revenues of six hundred households each; Governor Shentu Jia of Huaiyang and nine others shall receive five hundred households each; Guard Commander Zu and nine others shall receive four hundred households each.'
entries.literal: Officials of two thousand shi and above who followed Gaozu: Yingchuan Governor Zun and nine others shall have food revenues of six hundred households, Huaiyang Governor Shen Tu Jia and nine others five hundred households, Guard Commander Zu and nine others four hundred households.'

entries.zh: 封淮南王舅趙兼為周陽侯，齊王舅駟鈞為靖郭侯，故常 山丞相蔡兼為樊侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Zhao Jian, uncle of the King of Huainan, as Marquis of Zhouyang; Si Jun, uncle of the King of Qi, as Marquis of Jingguo; and Cai Jian, former chancellor of Changshan, as Marquis of Fan.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed the uncle of the King of Huainan Zhao Jian as Marquis of Zhouyang, the uncle of the King of Qi Si Jun as Marquis of Jingguo, and the former Chancellor of Changshan Cai Jian as Marquis of Fan.

entries.zh: 二月，出孝惠皇帝後宮美人，令得嫁。
entries.en: In the second month, he released the palace ladies from Emperor Hui's harem and allowed them to marry.
entries.literal: Second month, he released the beautiful women from the harem of Emperor Hui and permitted them to marry.

entries.zh: 楚元王交薨。
entries.en: King Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao, died.
entries.literal: King Yuan of Chu, Jiao, died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「前日詔遣列侯之國，辭未行。
entries.en: He issued an edict: 'I previously ordered the marquises to return to their fiefs, but the command has not been executed.
entries.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'Previously I issued an edict sending the marquises to their fiefs, but the orders have not yet been carried out.

entries.zh: 丞相朕之所重，其為遂率列侯之國。」
entries.en: The chancellor is a man I greatly respect; let him therefore escort the marquises back to their fiefs.'
entries.literal: The chancellor is one whom I hold in high regard; let him therefore lead the marquises to their fiefs.'

entries.zh: 遂免丞相勃，遣就國。
entries.en: As a result, he dismissed Chancellor Zhou Bo from office and sent him back to his fief.
entries.literal: Consequently he dismissed Chancellor Zhou Bo and sent him to his fief.

entries.zh: 十二月，太尉潁陰侯灌嬰為丞相。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Marquis Yingyin Guan Ying was appointed chancellor.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Marquis Yingyin Guan Ying became chancellor.

entries.zh: 罷太尉官，屬丞相。
entries.en: He abolished the position of Grand Commandant and transferred its responsibilities to the chancellor.
entries.literal: He abolished the office of Grand Commandant and attached its functions to the chancellor.

entries.zh: 四年冬十二月，丞相灌嬰薨。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter in the fourth year, Chancellor Guan Ying passed away.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, winter, twelfth month, Chancellor Guan Ying died.

entries.zh: 五月，匈奴入居北地、河南為寇。
entries.en: In the fifth month, the Xiongnu invaded and occupied Beidi and Henan territories as raiding forces.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, the Xiongnu entered and settled in Beidi and Henan as raiders.

entries.zh: 上幸甘泉，遣丞相灌嬰擊匈奴，匈奴去。
entries.en: The emperor journeyed to Ganquan and sent Chancellor Guan Ying to attack the Xiongnu invaders, who then retreated.
entries.literal: The emperor traveled to Ganquan and dispatched Chancellor Guan Ying to attack the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu withdrew.

entries.zh: 發中尉材官屬衛將軍，軍長安。
entries.en: He mobilized the skilled troops under the Commandant of the Capital and placed them under the Guard General's command, stationing the army at Chang'an.
entries.literal: He mobilized the Commandant of the Capital's skilled troops and attached them to the Guard General, stationing the army at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 三月，有司請立皇子為諸侯王。
entries.en: In the third month, the officials petitioned to enfeoff imperial princes as feudal kings.
entries.literal: In the third month, the officials petitioned to establish imperial princes as feudal kings.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「前趙幽王幽死，朕甚憐之，已立其太子遂為趙王。
entries.en: The imperial edict stated: 'Previously King You of Zhao died while imprisoned. I greatly pity him and have already enthroned his crown prince Sui as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: The edict said: 'Previously King You of Zhao died in confinement. I greatly pity him and have already established his crown prince Sui as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 遂弟辟彊及齊悼惠王子朱虛侯章、東牟侯興居有功，可王。」
entries.en: Sui's younger brother Pi Qiang, and the sons of King Dao Hui of Qi—the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and the Marquis of Dongmu Liu Xingju—have rendered merit and may be made kings.'
entries.literal: Sui's younger brother Pi Qiang, and the sons of King Dao Hui of Qi—the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and the Marquis of Dongmu Liu Xingju—have merit and may be made kings.'

entries.zh: 乃遂立辟彊為河間王，章為城陽王，興居為濟北王。
entries.en: He then established Pi Qiang as King of Hejian, Zhang as King of Chengyang, and Xingju as King of Jibei.
entries.literal: Then he proceeded to establish Pi Qiang as King of Hejian, Zhang as King of Chengyang, and Xingju as King of Jibei.

entries.zh: 因立皇子武為代王，參為太原王，揖為梁王。
entries.en: As a result, he established his sons Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.
entries.literal: Consequently he established the imperial princes Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.

entries.zh: 六月，代王參薨。
entries.en: In the sixth month, Can, King of Dai, died.
entries.literal: Sixth month: Can, King of Dai, died.

entries.zh: 匈奴和親。
entries.en: The Xiongnu established peaceful relations through marriage alliance.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu made peace and became relatives by marriage.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕既不明，不能遠德，使方外之國或不寧息。
entries.en: He issued an edict: 'I, being unenlightened and unable to extend virtue to distant lands, have caused the countries beyond our frontiers to sometimes lack peace and tranquility.
entries.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'I being unenlightened and unable to extend virtue far, have caused the countries beyond our borders to sometimes not have peace and rest.

entries.zh: 夫四荒之外不安其 生，封圻之內勤勞不處，二者之咎，皆自於朕之德薄而不能達遠也。
entries.en: Beyond the four wildernesses, people lack security in their lives; within the borders, there is constant toil without respite. The blame for both situations stems from my inadequate virtue and inability to extend my influence far.
entries.literal: Those beyond the four wildernesses do not have security in their lives, within the borders there is toil without rest. The fault in both cases comes from my thin virtue and inability to reach far.

entries.zh: 間者累年，匈奴並暴邊境，多殺吏民，邊臣兵吏入不能諭其內志，以重吾不德。
entries.en: In recent years, the Xiongnu have repeatedly assaulted the border regions, killing many officials and civilians. The border officials and military officers have failed to communicate my inner intentions clearly, thereby aggravating my lack of virtue.
entries.literal: In recent years, the Xiongnu have repeatedly ravaged the border regions, killing many officials and people. The border officials and military officers have not been able to make clear my inner intentions, thereby compounding my lack of virtue.

entries.zh: 夫久結難連兵， 中外之國將何以自寧？
entries.en: With long-standing enmity and continuous warfare, how can the empire within and the states beyond achieve peace?
entries.literal: With long-standing enmity and continuous warfare, how can the inner and outer states achieve peace?

entries.zh: 今朕夙興夜寐，勤勞天下，憂苦萬民，為之惻怛不安，未嘗一日忘於心，故遣使者冠蓋相望，結徹於道，以諭朕志於單于。
entries.en: Now I rise at dawn and retire at night, laboring diligently for the empire, worrying and suffering on behalf of the myriad people, feeling compassion and unrest for them, never forgetting it for even a single day. Therefore I have sent envoys with their ceremonial umbrellas in constant succession, filling the roads, to communicate my intentions clearly to the Chanyu.
entries.literal: Now I rise early and retire late, laboring diligently for the world, worrying and suffering for the myriad people, feeling compassion and unease for them, never forgetting it for a single day. Therefore I have dispatched envoys with their ceremonial canopies in constant succession, crowding the roads, to make clear my intentions to the Chanyu.

entries.zh: 今單于反古之道， 計社稷之安，便萬民之利，新與朕俱棄細過，偕之大道，結兄弟之義，以全天下元元之民。
entries.en: Now the Chanyu has returned to the ancient way, considering the security of the state and the benefit of the myriad people. Together with me he sets aside minor grievances and follows the great path, forming brotherly bonds to preserve the common people of the entire world.
entries.literal: Now the Chanyu has returned to the ancient way, considering the security of the altars of state and the benefit of the myriad people. Together with me he abandons minor grievances and follows the great way, forming brotherly relations to preserve the common people of the world.

entries.zh: 和親以定，始于今年。」
entries.en: Peaceful relations through marriage are established, beginning this year.'
entries.literal: Peace and kinship are established, beginning this year.'

entries.zh: 孝景皇帝，文帝太子也。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaojing was Emperor Wen's crown prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing was the crown prince of Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 母曰竇皇后。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Dou.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Dou.

entries.zh: 後七年六月，文帝崩。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the Later era, in the sixth month, Emperor Wen passed away.
entries.literal: In the seventh year thereafter, sixth month, Emperor Wen passed away.

entries.zh: 丁未，太子即皇帝位，尊皇太后薄氏曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: On the day Dingwei, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne, honoring Empress Dowager Bo as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: On the Dingwei day, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne, honoring Empress Dowager Bo as Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 贊曰：孔子稱「斯民，三代之所以直道而行也」，信哉！
entries.en: Appraisal: Confucius said, 'This people is why the Three Dynasties could follow the straight path'—how true!
entries.literal: Appraisal: Confucius said, 'This people is the reason the Three Dynasties could follow the straight path,' how true!

entries.zh: 周秦之敝，罔密文峻，而姦軌不勝。
entries.en: The downfall of Zhou and Qin resulted from excessively detailed laws and severe punishments, yet evil and corruption could not be prevented.
entries.literal: The decline of Zhou and Qin came from overly strict laws and harsh punishments, yet evil and wrongdoing could not be contained.

entries.zh: 漢興，掃除煩苛，與民休息。
entries.en: When the Han dynasty arose, it eliminated burdensome and harsh regulations, allowing the people to recover.
entries.literal: When Han arose, it swept away the vexatious and harsh measures, allowing the people to rest.

entries.zh: 至于孝文，加之以恭儉，孝景遵業，五六十載之間，至於移風易俗，黎民醇厚。
entries.en: When it came to Emperor Xiaowen, he added reverence and frugality; Emperor Xiaojing followed his precedent, and within fifty to sixty years, they transformed the prevailing customs, making the common people pure and upright.
entries.literal: When it came to Xiaowen, he added reverence and frugality; Xiaojing followed his example, and in the span of fifty to sixty years, they transformed customs and mores, making the common people pure and honest.

entries.zh: 周云成康，漢言文景，美矣！
entries.en: Zhou is praised for Cheng and Kang, Han for Wen and Jing—what excellence!
entries.literal: Zhou speaks of Cheng and Kang, Han speaks of Wen and Jing—how splendid!

entries.zh: 甲子，帝崩于未央宮。
entries.en: On the Jiazi day, the Emperor passed away in the Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: On the Jiazi day, the Emperor passed away in the Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 遺詔賜諸侯王列侯馬二駟，吏二千石黃金二斤，吏民戶百錢。
entries.en: His testamentary edict granted two teams of horses each to the regional kings and marquises, two jin of gold each to Two Thousand Bushel officials, and one hundred cash per household to officials and commoners.
entries.literal: His testamentary edict granted to the regional kings and marquises two teams of horses each, to Two Thousand Bushel officials two jin of gold each, and to officials and commoners one hundred cash per household.

entries.zh: 出宮人歸其家，復終身。
entries.en: He released the palace women to return to their homes, granting them lifelong tax exemption.
entries.literal: He released the palace women to return to their homes, exempting them from taxes for life.

entries.zh: 二月癸酉，葬陽陵。
entries.en: On the Guiyou day of the second month, he was buried at Yangling.
entries.literal: On the Guiyou day of the second month, he was buried at Yangling.

entries.zh: 春三月，立皇子德為河間王，閼為臨江王，餘為淮陽王，非為汝南王，彭祖為廣川王，發為長沙王。
entries.en: In the third month of spring, he enfeoffed his imperial sons De as King of Hejian, Yan as King of Linjiang, Yu as King of Huaiyang, Fei as King of Runan, Pengzu as King of Guangchuan, and Fa as King of Changsha.
entries.literal: Spring, third month: He enfeoffed imperial son De as King of Hejian, Yan as King of Linjiang, Yu as King of Huaiyang, Fei as King of Runan, Pengzu as King of Guangchuan, and Fa as King of Changsha.

entries.zh: 諸將破七國，斬首十餘萬級。
entries.en: The imperial generals defeated the seven kingdoms, taking more than 100,000 heads.
entries.literal: The various generals defeated the seven kingdoms, beheading more than 100,000 heads.

entries.zh: 追斬吳王濞於丹徒。
entries.en: They pursued and executed King Pi of Wu at Dantu.
entries.literal: They pursued and beheaded King Pi of Wu at Dantu.

entries.zh: 膠西王卬、楚王戊、趙王遂、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、 膠東王雄渠皆自殺。
entries.en: Kings Ang of Jiaoxi, Wu of Chu, Sui of Zhao, Bi Guang of Jinan, Xian of Zichuan, and Xiong Qu of Jiaodong all committed suicide.
entries.literal: King of Jiaoxi Ang, King of Chu Wu, King of Zhao Sui, King of Jinan Bi Guang, King of Zichuan Xian, and King of Jiaodong Xiong Qu all committed suicide.

entries.zh: 夏六月，詔曰：「乃者吳王濞等為逆，起兵相脅，詿誤吏民，吏民不得已。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer, he issued an edict: 'Recently King Pi of Wu and others committed rebellion, raised troops and coerced one another, deceived and misled officials and civilians alike, leaving officials and people with no choice.
entries.literal: Summer, sixth month: He issued an edict saying: 'Recently King Pi of Wu and others committed rebellion, raised troops and coerced each other, deceived and misled officials and people, and officials and people had no choice.

entries.zh: 今濞等已滅，吏民當坐濞等及逋逃亡軍者，皆赦之。
entries.en: Now that Pi and his confederates have been destroyed, all officials and civilians liable for following them, as well as deserters and fugitives from military service, shall be pardoned.
entries.literal: Now that Pi and others have been destroyed, officials and people who should be punished for following Pi and others, and deserters and fugitives from the army, all shall be pardoned.

entries.zh: 楚元王子蓺等與 濞等為逆，朕不忍加法，除其籍，毋令汙宗室。」
entries.en: King Yuan of Chu's son Yi and others participated in Pi's rebellion. I cannot bear to apply the full force of the law to them, so I remove their names from the imperial registers to prevent them from tarnishing the imperial clan.'
entries.literal: King Yuan of Chu's son Yi and others joined Pi and others in rebellion; I cannot bear to apply the law to them, so I remove their names from the registers and do not let them defile the imperial clan.'

entries.zh: 立平陸侯劉禮為楚王，續元王後。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Pinglu Marquis Liu Li as King of Chu to continue the line of King Yuan.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Pinglu Marquis Liu Li as King of Chu, continuing the line of King Yuan.

entries.zh: 立皇子端為膠西王，勝為中山王。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his imperial sons Duan as King of Jiaoxi and Sheng as King of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed imperial son Duan as King of Jiaoxi, Sheng as King of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 賜民爵一級。
entries.en: He granted all the people advancement in noble rank by one level.
entries.literal: He granted the people advancement in noble rank by one level.

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，立皇子榮為皇太子，徹為膠東王。
entries.en: On the day Jisi in the fourth month of summer, he established his imperial son Rong as crown prince and Che as King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day Jisi: He established imperial son Rong as crown prince, Che as King of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 立皇子越為廣川王，寄為膠東王。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his imperial sons Yue as King of Guangchuan and Ji as King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed imperial son Yue as King of Guangchuan, Ji as King of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 立皇子乘為清河王。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his imperial son Cheng as King of Qinghe.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed imperial son Cheng as King of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 五年夏，立皇子舜為常山王。
