entries.en: In summer of the fifth year, he enfeoffed his imperial son Shun as King of Changshan.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, summer: He enfeoffed imperial son Shun as King of Changshan.

entries.zh: 六月，赦天下，賜民爵一級。
entries.en: In the sixth month, he granted general amnesty throughout the empire and advanced all the people's noble ranks by one level.
entries.literal: Sixth month: He granted amnesty to the world and advanced the people's noble ranks by one level.

entries.zh: 遣公主嫁匈奴單于。
entries.en: He sent an imperial princess to marry the Xiongnu Chanyu.
entries.literal: He sent a princess to marry the Xiongnu Chanyu.

entries.zh: 秋九月，皇后薄氏廢。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn, Empress Bo was deposed.
entries.literal: Autumn, ninth month: Empress Bo was deposed.

entries.zh: 夏四月乙巳，立皇后王氏。
entries.en: On the day Yisi in the fourth month of summer, he established Empress Wang.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day Yisi: He established Empress Wang.

entries.zh: 夏四月，梁王薨，分梁為五國，立孝王子五人皆為王。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, the King of Liang died. Liang was divided into five kingdoms, and King Xiao's five sons were each made kings.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month: the King of Liang died; Liang was divided into five kingdoms, and King Xiao's five sons were all made kings.

entries.zh: 元年冬十月，詔曰：「蓋聞古者祖有功而宗有德，制禮樂各有由。
entries.en: In the first year, during the tenth month of winter, he issued an edict: 'I have heard that in ancient times those with merit were honored as zu and those with virtue as zong, and that rites and music each had their proper origins.
entries.literal: In the first year, winter, tenth month, he issued an edict saying: 'I have heard that in ancient times those with merit were honored as zu and those with virtue as zong, and the establishment of rites and music each had its origin.

entries.zh: 歌者，所以發德也；
entries.en: Singing serves to express virtue;
entries.literal: Singing is what expresses virtue;

entries.zh: 舞者，所以明功 也。
entries.en: dancing serves to illuminate merit.
entries.literal: Dancing is what illuminates merit.

entries.zh: 高廟酎，奏武德、文始、五行之舞。
entries.en: At the autumn sacrifices in the High Temple, perform the dances of Martial Virtue, Literary Beginning, and the Five Elements.
entries.literal: At the High Temple autumn sacrifices, perform the dances of Martial Virtue, Literary Beginning, and the Five Elements.

entries.zh: 孝惠廟酎，奏文始、五行之舞。
entries.en: At the autumn sacrifices in Emperor Hui's Temple, perform the dances of Literary Beginning and the Five Elements.
entries.literal: At the Temple of Emperor Hui's autumn sacrifices, perform the dances of Literary Beginning and the Five Elements.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝臨天下，通關梁，不異遠方；
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen, in governing the realm, opened the passes and bridges, making no distinction between distant and nearby regions;
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, ruling the world, opened the passes and bridges, treating distant regions no differently;

entries.zh: 除誹謗，去肉刑，賞賜長老，收恤孤獨，以遂群生；
entries.en: he abolished slander laws, eliminated mutilating punishments, rewarded the elderly, and provided relief to orphans and widows, thereby sustaining all living beings;
entries.literal: abolished slander laws, eliminated mutilating punishments, rewarded the elderly, and provided relief to orphans and widows, so as to fulfill the lives of all people;

entries.zh: 減耆欲，不受獻，罪人不帑，不誅亡罪，不私其利也；
entries.en: he reduced his desires, declined tribute offerings, spared the families of criminals, did not execute the innocent, and did not monopolize benefits for personal gain;
entries.literal: reduced his desires, did not accept tribute, did not implicate the families of criminals, did not execute those without guilt, and did not monopolize benefits for himself;

entries.zh: 除宮刑，出美人，重絕人之世也。
entries.en: he abolished palace punishments, released the palace ladies, and valued the preservation of family lines.
entries.literal: abolished palace punishments, released the palace ladies, valuing the continuation of people's lineages.

entries.zh: 朕既不敏，弗能勝識。
entries.en: Being unenlightened as I am, I cannot fully comprehend this.
entries.literal: I, being unenlightened, am unable to fully comprehend this.

entries.zh: 此皆上世之所不及，而孝文皇帝親行之。
entries.en: These are all achievements that previous eras did not attain, yet Emperor Xiaowen personally accomplished them.
entries.literal: These are all things that previous generations did not achieve, yet Emperor Xiaowen personally implemented them.

entries.zh: 德厚侔天 地，利澤施四海，靡不獲福。
entries.en: His virtue equaled the thickness of Heaven and Earth, his beneficial influence reached to the four seas, and all received good fortune.
entries.literal: His virtue was as thick as Heaven and Earth, his beneficial influence extended to the four seas, and none did not receive fortune.

entries.zh: 明象乎日月，而廟樂不稱，朕甚懼焉。
entries.en: His brilliance shone like the sun and moon, yet the temple music does not befit it—I am greatly apprehensive about this.
entries.literal: His brightness was like the sun and moon, yet the temple music does not match it—I am greatly fearful of this.

entries.zh: 其為孝文皇帝廟為昭德之舞，以明休德。
entries.en: Therefore, create the Dance of Illustrious Virtue for Emperor Xiaowen's temple, to illuminate his blessed virtue.
entries.literal: Therefore, for Emperor Xiaowen's temple create the dance of Illustrious Virtue, to illuminate his blessed virtue.

entries.zh: 然后祖宗之功德，施于萬世，永永無窮，朕甚嘉之。
entries.en: Then the merit and virtue of our ancestors will extend to ten thousand generations, forever without end—I greatly approve of this.
entries.literal: Then the merit and virtue of the ancestors will extend to ten thousand generations, forever without end—I greatly commend this.

entries.zh: 其 與丞相、列侯、中二千石、禮官具禮儀奏。」
entries.en: Therefore, together with the chancellor, marquises, officials of two thousand shi rank, and ritual officials, prepare the ceremonies and submit them.'
entries.literal: Therefore, together with the chancellor, marquises, officials of two thousand shi rank, and ritual officials, prepare the rites and submit them.'

entries.zh: 丞相臣嘉等奏曰：「陛下永思孝道，立昭德之舞以明孝文皇帝之盛德，皆臣嘉等愚所不及。
entries.en: Chancellor Jia and others submitted: 'Your Majesty perpetually reflects on the path of filial piety, establishing the Dance of Illustrious Virtue to illuminate Emperor Xiaowen's abundant virtue—all of this exceeds what we foolish ministers can fathom.
entries.literal: Chancellor Jia and others submitted: 'Your Majesty perpetually contemplates the way of filial piety, establishing the dance of Illustrious Virtue to illuminate Emperor Xiaowen's abundant virtue—all of this surpasses what we foolish ministers can comprehend.

entries.zh: 臣謹議：世功莫大於高皇 帝，德莫盛於孝文皇帝。
entries.en: We respectfully propose: No achievement in history surpasses Emperor Gao's, no virtue is more abundant than Emperor Xiaowen's.
entries.literal: We respectfully propose: No merit in history surpasses Emperor Gao's, no virtue is more abundant than Emperor Xiaowen's.

entries.zh: 高皇帝廟宜為帝者太祖之廟，孝文皇帝廟宜為帝諸太宗之廟。
entries.en: Emperor Gao's temple should serve as the Grand Ancestral Temple of the emperors; Emperor Xiaowen's temple should serve as the Grand Progenitor Temple of the emperors.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao's temple should be the Grand Ancestral Temple of the emperors; Emperor Xiaowen's temple should be the Grand Progenitor Temple of the emperors.

entries.zh: 天子宜世世獻祖宗之廟。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven should offer sacrifices at the ancestral temples for generation after generation.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven should generation after generation offer sacrifices at the ancestral temples.

entries.zh: 郡國諸侯宜各為孝文皇帝立太宗之廟。
entries.en: The feudal lords of the commanderies and kingdoms should each establish a Grand Progenitor Temple for Emperor Xiaowen.
entries.literal: The feudal lords of the commanderies and kingdoms should each establish a Grand Progenitor Temple for Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 諸侯王列侯使 者侍祠天子所獻祖宗之廟。
entries.en: The envoys of the feudal kings and marquises should attend and perform sacrifices at the ancestral temples where the Son of Heaven offers his sacrifices.
entries.literal: The envoys of the feudal kings and marquises should attend and offer sacrifices at the ancestral temples where the Son of Heaven offers sacrifices.

entries.zh: 請宣布天下。」
entries.en: We request that this be proclaimed throughout the empire.'
entries.literal: We request that this be proclaimed throughout the world.'

entries.zh: 制曰「可」。
entries.en: The imperial decree stated 'Approved.'
entries.literal: The imperial decree said 'Approved.'

entries.zh: 春正月，詔曰：「間者歲比不登，民多乏食，夭絕天年，朕甚痛之。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, he issued an edict: 'In recent years, harvests have failed repeatedly, most people lack sufficient food, dying prematurely and cutting short their natural lifespans—I am deeply pained by this.
entries.literal: Spring, first month: He issued an edict saying: 'In recent years the harvests have repeatedly failed, the people mostly lack food, dying prematurely and cutting short their natural lifespans—I am greatly pained by this.

entries.zh: 郡國或磽骥，無所農桑诒畜；
entries.en: Some commanderies and kingdoms have barren or saline soil, unsuitable for farming, mulberry cultivation, or raising livestock;
entries.literal: Some commanderies and kingdoms have barren or saline land, with no place for farming, mulberry cultivation, or livestock rearing;

entries.zh: 或地饒廣，薦草莽，水泉利，而不得徙。
entries.en: others have fertile and expansive lands with lush grasslands and beneficial water sources, yet cannot relocate there.
entries.literal: others have fertile and broad lands, lush grass, and beneficial water sources, yet cannot relocate there.

entries.zh: 其議民欲徙寬大地者，聽之。」
entries.en: Let officials discuss permitting those among the people who wish to relocate to broad and fertile lands, and grant permission.'
entries.literal: Let officials discuss those among the people who wish to relocate to broad and fertile lands, and permit it.'

entries.zh: 秋七月，詔曰：「吏受所監臨，以飲食免，重；
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, he issued an edict: 'When officials accept what they supervise, being dismissed merely for accepting food and drink is too severe;
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month: He issued an edict saying: 'When officials accept what they supervise, being dismissed for accepting food and drink is severe;

entries.zh: 受財物，賤買貴賣，論輕。
entries.en: accepting wealth and goods, buying cheap and selling dear, the punishment is too light.
entries.literal: accepting wealth and goods, buying cheap and selling dear, the punishment is light.

entries.zh: 廷尉與丞相更議著令。」
entries.en: Let the Chamberlain for Law and the chancellor jointly deliberate and establish this as law.'
entries.literal: Let the Chamberlain for Law and the chancellor jointly deliberate and establish this as law.'

entries.zh: 廷尉 信謹與丞相議曰：「吏及諸有秩受其官屬所監、所治、所行、所將，其與飲食計償費，勿論。
entries.en: Chamberlain for Law Xin and the chancellor proposed: "When officials or other ranked personnel receive food and drink from subordinates under their supervision, jurisdiction, administration, or command, and the amount merely repays expenses, no charge should be brought.
entries.literal: Chamberlain for Law Xin and the chancellor proposed: 'Officials and all ranked personnel who accept from their subordinates what they supervise, govern, execute, or command—if it is food and drink calculated to compensate for expenses, do not prosecute.

entries.zh: 它物，若買故賤，賣故貴，皆坐臧為盜，沒入臧縣官。
entries.en: For other goods, if bought deliberately cheap or sold deliberately expensive, all shall be convicted of corruption as theft, with the corrupt goods confiscated by the county authorities.
entries.literal: Other goods, if bought cheap on purpose or sold expensive on purpose, all shall be convicted of corruption as theft, with the corrupt goods confiscated by the county authorities.

entries.zh: 吏遷徙免罷，受 其故官屬所將監治送財物，奪爵為士伍，免之。
entries.en: When officials are transferred, reassigned, dismissed, or removed, and they accept money or goods sent by former subordinates whom they had commanded, supervised, or governed, their noble rank should be reduced to commoner status and they should be dismissed.
entries.literal: When officials are transferred, relocated, dismissed, or removed, if they accept wealth and goods sent by their former subordinates whom they commanded, supervised, or governed, strip their noble rank to commoner status and dismiss them.

entries.zh: 無爵，罰金二斤，令沒入所受。
entries.en: If they have no noble rank, fine them two jin of gold, and order confiscation of what they received.
entries.literal: If they have no noble rank, fine them two jin of gold, and order confiscation of what they received.

entries.zh: 有能捕告，畀其所受臧。」
entries.en: Those who can capture and report such cases shall be rewarded with the confiscated corrupt goods.'
entries.literal: Those who can capture and report such cases shall be given the confiscated corrupt goods.'

entries.zh: 三年冬十二月，詔曰：「襄平侯嘉子恢說不孝，謀反，欲以殺嘉，大逆無道。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter in the third year, he issued an edict: 'Xiangping Marquis Jia's son Hui Shuo was unfilial and plotted rebellion, desiring to kill his father Jia—this constitutes great rebellion and moral depravity.
entries.literal: In the third year, winter, twelfth month, he issued an edict saying: 'Xiangping Marquis Jia's son Hui Shuo was unfilial, plotted rebellion, desiring to kill Jia—greatly rebellious and without moral principle.

entries.zh: 其赦嘉為襄平侯，及妻子當坐者復故爵。
entries.en: Therefore, pardon Jia and restore him as Xiangping Marquis, and restore the original ranks to his wives and children who would have been implicated.
entries.literal: Therefore, pardon Jia as Xiangping Marquis, and restore the original ranks to his wives and children who should have been implicated.

entries.zh: 論恢說及妻子如法。」
entries.en: Sentence Hui Shuo and his wives and children according to the law.'
entries.literal: Judge Hui Shuo and his wives and children according to law.'

entries.zh: 九月，詔曰：「法令度量，所以禁暴止邪也。
entries.en: In the ninth month, he issued an edict: 'Laws, commands, and standards of measurement serve to prohibit violence and halt evil.
entries.literal: Ninth month: He issued an edict saying: 'Laws, commands, and measurements are what prohibit violence and stop evil.

entries.zh: 獄，人之大命，死者不可復生。
entries.en: Legal cases are a matter of life and death for people; once dead, they cannot be revived.
entries.literal: Prisons are a matter of great importance to people; the dead cannot be brought back to life.

entries.zh: 吏或不奉法令，以貨賂為市，朋黨比周，以苛為察，以刻為明，令亡罪者失職，朕甚憐之。
entries.en: Some officials fail to observe laws and commands, treating bribes as merchandise, forming factions and colluding together, mistaking harshness for thoroughness and severity for wisdom, causing the innocent to lose their positions—I deeply pity this situation.
entries.literal: Some officials do not follow laws and commands, making commerce of bribes, forming cliques and colluding, considering harshness to be thoroughness, considering severity to be clarity, causing those without guilt to lose their positions—I greatly pity this.

entries.zh: 有罪者不伏罪，姦法為暴，甚亡謂也。
entries.en: Those who are guilty refuse to admit their crimes, corrupt the law and turn violent—this is utterly without principle.
entries.literal: Those who have guilt do not admit their crimes, corrupt the law and become violent—this is truly without principle.

entries.zh: 諸獄疑，若雖文致於法而於人心不厭者，輒讞之。」
entries.en: For all doubtful legal cases, if they technically conform to the law but do not satisfy human conscience, immediately review them.'
entries.literal: For all doubtful prison cases, if although they fit the letter of the law but do not satisfy human conscience, immediately review them.'

entries.zh: 五月，詔曰：「夫吏者，民之師也，車駕衣服宜稱。
entries.en: In the fifth month, he issued an edict: 'Officials serve as teachers to the people; their carriages, horses, clothing, and accessories should befit their status.
entries.literal: Fifth month: He issued an edict saying: 'Officials are the teachers of the people; their carriages, horses, clothing, and accessories should be appropriate.

entries.zh: 吏六百石以上，皆長吏也，亡度者或不吏服，出入閭 里，與民亡異。
entries.en: Officials of six hundred shi rank and above are all senior officials. Those lacking proper decorum sometimes fail to wear official robes, entering and leaving neighborhoods and alleys indistinguishable from commoners.
entries.literal: Officials of six hundred shi and above are all senior officials; those without propriety sometimes do not wear official robes, entering and leaving neighborhoods and alleys, indistinguishable from commoners.

entries.zh: 令長吏二千石車朱兩轓，千石至六百石朱左轓。
entries.en: Order that senior officials of two thousand shi rank have carriages with vermilion decoration on both sides, while those from one thousand shi to six hundred shi have vermilion on the left side only.
entries.literal: Command that senior officials of two thousand shi have carriages with vermilion on both sides, those from one thousand shi to six hundred shi have vermilion on the left side.

entries.zh: 車騎從者不稱其官衣服，下吏出入閭巷亡吏體者，二千石上其官屬，三輔舉不如法令者，皆上丞相御 史請之。」
entries.en: If carriages, horses, or attendants do not befit their official rank and clothing, or if subordinate officials enter alleys lacking proper official demeanor, officials of two thousand shi shall report their subordinates, and the Three Adjuncts shall impeach those who fail to conform to laws and commands—all shall be reported to the chancellor and grandee secretary for punishment.'
entries.literal: If carriages, horses, and attendants do not match their official clothing, or if subordinate officials enter alleys without official bearing, officials of two thousand shi shall report their subordinates, and the Three Adjuncts shall impeach those who do not conform to laws and commands—all shall be reported to the chancellor and grandee secretary for punishment.'

entries.zh: 先是吏多軍功，車服尚輕，故為設禁。
entries.en: Previously, most officials were military veterans who preferred simple carriages and clothing, so regulations were established to curb this.
entries.literal: Previously, officials were mostly military men, and they preferred light carriages and clothing, so prohibitions were established for them.

entries.zh: 又惟酷吏奉憲失中，乃詔有司減笞法，定箠令。
entries.en: Furthermore, considering that harsh officials in enforcing the law had lost all moderation, he ordered the relevant officials to reduce the severity of beatings and establish regulations for bamboo cane punishments.
entries.literal: Moreover, considering that cruel officials in enforcing the constitution lost the mean, he commanded the relevant officials to reduce the beating punishments and establish the bamboo cane regulations.

entries.zh: 語在刑法志。
entries.en: The details are recorded in the 'Treatise on Criminal Law.'
entries.literal: The words are in the 'Treatise on Punishments and Laws.'

entries.zh: 後元年春正月，詔曰：「獄，重事也。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the first year of the Hou period, he issued an edict: 'Legal cases are matters of grave importance.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Hou period, spring, first month: He issued an edict saying: 'Legal cases are weighty matters.

entries.zh: 人有智愚，官有上下。
entries.en: People differ in wisdom and folly, officials differ in rank and status.
entries.literal: People have varying intelligence, officials have different ranks.

entries.zh: 獄疑者讞有司。
entries.en: Doubtful legal cases should be reviewed by the appropriate officials.
entries.literal: Doubtful cases should be reviewed by the relevant officials.

entries.zh: 有司所不能決，移廷尉。
entries.en: Cases that the relevant officials cannot adjudicate should be transferred to the Chamberlain for Law.
entries.literal: Cases that the relevant officials cannot decide should be transferred to the Chamberlain for Law.

entries.zh: 有令讞而後不當，讞者不為失。
entries.en: If there is an order to review a case and it later proves to be incorrect, the reviewer shall not be held accountable.
entries.literal: If there is a command to review and afterward it proves incorrect, the reviewer shall not be considered at fault.

entries.zh: 欲令治獄者務先寬。」
entries.en: The intent is to ensure that those who handle legal cases prioritize leniency.'
entries.literal: The desire is to make those who handle legal cases prioritize leniency.'

entries.zh: 三月，赦天下，賜民爵一級，中二千石諸侯相爵右庶長。
entries.en: In the third month, he granted general amnesty throughout the empire, advanced all the people's noble ranks by one level, and granted officials of two thousand shi rank and feudal lords' chancellors the noble rank of Right Senior.
entries.literal: Third month: He granted amnesty to the world, advanced the people's noble ranks by one level, and granted officials of two thousand shi and feudal lords' chancellors the rank of Right Senior.

entries.zh: 夏，大酺五日，民得酤酒。
entries.en: In summer, there was a grand celebration lasting five days, during which the common people were allowed to sell wine.
entries.literal: Summer: There was a great celebration for five days, during which the people were permitted to sell wine.

entries.zh: 夏四月，詔曰：「雕文刻鏤，傷農事者也；
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, he issued an edict: 'Carved and engraved decorations harm agricultural work;
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month: He issued an edict saying: 'Carved and engraved decorations harm agricultural work;

entries.zh: 錦繡纂組，害女紅者也。
entries.en: brocades, embroideries, and elaborate fabrics harm women's work.
entries.literal: brocades, embroideries, and silk fabrics harm women's work.

entries.zh: 農事傷則飢之本也，女紅害則寒之原 也。
entries.en: When farming is harmed, it is the root of hunger; when women's work is harmed, it is the source of cold.
entries.literal: When agricultural work is harmed, it is the root of hunger; when women's work is harmed, it is the source of cold.

entries.zh: 夫飢寒並至，而能亡為非者寡矣。
entries.en: When hunger and cold arrive together, those who can avoid wrongdoing are indeed few.
entries.literal: When hunger and cold arrive together, those who can avoid wrongdoing are few indeed.

entries.zh: 朕親耕，后親桑，以奉宗廟粢盛祭服，為天下先；
entries.en: I personally plow the fields, the Empress personally tends the silkworms, to provide grain offerings and sacrificial robes for the ancestral temples, setting an example for the world;
entries.literal: I personally plow, the Empress personally tends silkworms, to provide grain offerings and sacrificial robes for the ancestral temples, leading the world;

entries.zh: 不受獻，減太官，省繇賦，欲天下務農蠶，素有畜積，以備災害。
entries.en: I do not accept tribute offerings, reduce expenditures in the Grand Kitchen, lessen corvee labor and taxes, desiring that the entire world focus on farming and silk production, maintaining simple stores to prepare for disasters.
entries.literal: I do not accept tributes, reduce the Grand Kitchen expenditures, lessen corvee and taxes, desiring that the world focus on farming and silk production, having plain accumulations to prepare for disasters.

entries.zh: 彊毋攘 弱，眾毋暴寡，老耆以壽終，幼孤得遂長。
entries.en: The strong should not plunder the weak, the majority should not oppress the minority, the elderly should live out their natural lifespan, and orphans should grow up successfully.
entries.literal: The strong do not plunder the weak, the many do not oppress the few, the elderly reach the end of their natural lifespan, orphans grow to adulthood successfully.

entries.zh: 今歲或不登，民食頗寡，其咎安在？
entries.en: Nowadays, some years bring poor harvests and the people's food supplies are quite meager—who is to blame for this?
entries.literal: Now in some years the harvest fails, the people's food is rather scarce, where does the blame lie?

entries.zh: 或詐偽為吏，吏以貨賂為市，漁奪百姓，侵牟萬民。
entries.en: Some fraudulently become officials, officials treat bribery as their business, plundering and seizing from the common people, encroaching upon and profiting from the masses.
entries.literal: Some falsely become officials, officials use bribes as their market, plundering and seizing the common people, encroaching upon and profiting from the myriad people.

entries.zh: 縣丞，長吏也，奸法與盜盜，甚 無謂也。
entries.en: The county assistant magistrate is a senior official, yet he corrupts the law and acts like a thief—it is utterly senseless.
entries.literal: The county assistant magistrate is a senior official, yet he corrupts the law and acts like a thief—this is utterly senseless.

entries.zh: 其令二千石修其職；
entries.en: Let the Two Thousand Bushel officials properly perform their duties;
entries.literal: Let the Two Thousand Bushel officials rectify their duties;

entries.zh: 不事官職耗亂者，丞相以聞，請其罪。
entries.en: Those who neglect their official duties and cause disruption should be reported by the Chancellor, who will request their punishment.
entries.literal: Those who do not attend to their official duties and cause disorder, let the Chancellor report them and request their punishment.

entries.zh: 布告天下，使明知朕意。」
entries.en: Proclaim this throughout the realm so that everyone clearly understands My intentions.'
entries.literal: Proclaim this to the world, so that all clearly understand My intentions.'

entries.zh: 五月，詔曰：「人不患其不知，患其為詐也；
entries.en: In the fifth month, he issued an edict: 'The trouble with people is not that they lack knowledge, but that they practice deceit;
entries.literal: Fifth month: He issued an edict saying: 'The trouble with people is not that they lack knowledge, but that they practice deceit;

entries.zh: 不患其不勇，患其為暴也；
entries.en: the trouble is not that they lack courage, but that they act with violence;
entries.literal: the trouble is not that they lack courage, but that they act with violence;

entries.zh: 不患其不富，患其亡厭也。
entries.en: the trouble is not that they lack wealth, but that they never know when they have enough.
entries.literal: the trouble is not that they lack wealth, but that they never know when they have enough.

entries.zh: 其唯廉士，寡欲易足。
entries.en: Only the incorruptible gentleman, with modest desires, is easily content.
entries.literal: Only the incorruptible scholar, with few desires, is easily satisfied.

entries.zh: 今訾算十以上乃得宦，廉士算不必眾。
entries.en: Nowadays, only those with property worth ten units or more can enter official service, but incorruptible scholars do not necessarily have abundant property.
entries.literal: Now, only those with property assessment of ten or more can become officials, but incorruptible scholars do not necessarily have much property.

entries.zh: 有市籍不得宦，無訾又不得宦，朕甚愍之。
entries.en: Those registered as merchants cannot enter official service, nor can those without property—I greatly pity this situation.
entries.literal: Those with merchant registration cannot become officials, those without property cannot become officials—I greatly pity this.

entries.zh: 訾算四得宦，亡令廉士久失職，貪夫長利。」
entries.en: Let those with property worth four units enter official service; do not allow incorruptible scholars to remain out of office for long, nor permit greedy men to benefit forever.'
entries.literal: Let those with property assessment of four enter official service, do not let incorruptible scholars remain unemployed for long, nor let greedy men profit perpetually.'

entries.zh: 三年春正月，詔曰：「農，天下之本也。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of the third year, he issued an edict: 'Agriculture is the foundation of the realm.
entries.literal: Third year, first month of spring: He issued an edict saying: 'Agriculture is the foundation of the world.

entries.zh: 黃金珠玉，飢不可食，寒不可衣，以為幣用，不識其終始。
entries.en: Gold, pearls, and jade cannot satisfy hunger or provide warmth; when used as money, they have no clear beginning or end.
entries.literal: Gold, pearls, and jade cannot be eaten when hungry, cannot clothe one when cold; when used as currency, they have no known beginning or end.

entries.zh: 間歲或不登，意為末者眾，農民寡也。
entries.en: In some years the harvest fails, yet those engaged in commerce are numerous, while farmers are few.
entries.literal: In alternate years harvests sometimes fail, yet those who pursue trade are many, while farmers are few.

entries.zh: 其令郡國務勸農桑，益種樹，可得衣食物。
entries.en: Let the commanderies and kingdoms vigorously promote agriculture and sericulture, plant more trees, so that people may obtain clothing and food.
entries.literal: Let the commanderies and kingdoms diligently encourage farming and silk production, increase tree planting, so that clothing and food may be obtained.

entries.zh: 吏發民若取庸采黃金珠玉者，坐臧為盜。
entries.en: Officials who mobilize people or hire workers to mine gold, pearls, and jade shall be convicted of corruption and punished as robbers.
entries.literal: Officials who mobilize the people or hire laborers to mine for gold, pearls, and jade shall be convicted of corruption and treated as thieves.

entries.zh: 二千石聽者，與同罪。」
entries.en: Two Thousand Bushel officials who allow this shall receive the same punishment.'
entries.literal: The Two Thousand Bushel officials who permit this shall share the same punishment.'

entries.zh: 二年冬十二月，有星孛于西南。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter in the second year, a comet appeared in the southwest.
entries.literal: In the second year, winter, twelfth month, there was a sweeping star in the southwest.

entries.zh: 吳王濞、膠西王卬、楚王戊、趙王遂、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠皆舉兵反。
entries.en: Kings Pi of Wu, Ang of Jiaoxi, Wu of Chu, Sui of Zhao, Bi Guang of Jinan, Xian of Zichuan, and Xiong Qu of Jiaodong all raised troops in rebellion.
entries.literal: King of Wu Pi, King of Jiaoxi Ang, King of Chu Wu, King of Zhao Sui, King of Jinan Bi Guang, King of Zichuan Xian, and King of Jiaodong Xiong Qu all raised troops in rebellion.

entries.zh: 大赦天下。
entries.en: He granted a general amnesty throughout the empire.
entries.literal: He granted a great amnesty to the world.

entries.zh: 遣太尉亞夫、大將軍竇嬰將兵擊之。
entries.en: He sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu and General Dou Ying to lead troops against the rebels.
entries.literal: He dispatched Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu and General Dou Ying to lead troops and attack them.

entries.zh: 斬御史大夫晁錯以謝七國。
entries.en: He executed Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo to appease the seven rebellious kingdoms.
entries.literal: He executed Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo to apologize to the seven kingdoms.

entries.zh: 四年春，復置諸關用傳出入。
entries.en: In spring of the fourth year, he reinstated the requirement for travel documents at all border passes.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, spring: He reestablished the use of travel documents for entering and leaving the various passes.

entries.zh: 五年春正月，作陽陵邑。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the fifth year, he established the town of Yangling.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, spring, first month: He established Yangling town.

entries.zh: 夏，募民徙陽陵，賜錢二十萬。
entries.en: In summer, he recruited commoners to relocate to Yangling, granting each 200,000 cash coins.
entries.literal: Summer: He recruited people to relocate to Yangling, granting 200,000 cash.

entries.zh: 六年冬十二月，雷，霖雨。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter in the sixth year, there was thunder followed by continuous rain.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, winter, twelfth month: There was thunder and continuous rain.

entries.zh: 七年冬十一月庚寅晦，日有蝕之。
entries.en: On the last day of the eleventh month of winter in the seventh year, the day Gengyin, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, winter, eleventh month, on the day Gengyin, the last day of the month: There was an eclipse of the sun.

entries.zh: 春正月，廢皇太子榮為臨江王。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, he deposed Crown Prince Rong and made him King of Linjiang.
entries.literal: Spring, first month: He deposed Crown Prince Rong, making him King of Linjiang.

entries.zh: 丁巳，立膠東王徹為皇太子。
entries.en: On the day Dingsi, he established King Che of Jiaodong as crown prince.
entries.literal: Day Dingsi: He established King Che of Jiaodong as crown prince.

entries.zh: 賜民為父後者爵一級。
entries.en: He granted advancement in noble rank by one level to those who served as their fathers' heirs.
entries.literal: He granted advancement in noble rank by one level to people who served as heirs to their fathers.

entries.zh: 中元年夏四月，赦天下，賜民爵一級。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer in the first year of the Middle period, he granted general amnesty throughout the empire and advanced all the people's noble ranks by one level.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Middle period, summer, fourth month: He granted amnesty to the world and advanced the people's noble ranks by one level.

entries.zh: 封故御史大夫周苛、周昌孫子為列侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed the grandsons of the former Grandee Secretaries Zhou Ke and Zhou Chang as marquises.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed the grandsons of the former Grandee Secretaries Zhou Ke and Zhou Chang as marquises.

entries.zh: 二年春二月，令諸侯王薨、列侯初封及之國，大鴻臚奏諡、誄、策。
entries.en: In the second month of spring in the second year, he ordered that when feudal kings die, and when marquises are first enfeoffed and proceed to their fiefs, the Chamberlain for Dependencies should submit posthumous names, elegies, and imperial edicts.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, second month: He commanded that when feudal lords die, and when marquises are first enfeoffed and go to their fiefs, the Chamberlain for Dependencies should submit posthumous names, dirges, and edicts.

entries.zh: 列侯薨及諸侯太傅初除之官，大行奏諡、誄、策。
entries.en: When marquises die and when feudal lords' tutors are first appointed to office, the Chamberlain for Ceremonial should submit posthumous names, elegies, and imperial edicts.
entries.literal: When marquises die and when feudal lords' tutors are first appointed to office, the Chamberlain for Ceremonial should submit posthumous names, dirges, and edicts.

entries.zh: 王薨，遣光祿大夫弔襚祠賵，視喪事，因立嗣子。
entries.en: When kings die, dispatch Gentlemen of the Palace to offer condolences, sacrificial garments, perform sacrifices, and present gifts. They shall oversee the funeral arrangements and thereby establish the heir.
entries.literal: When kings die, dispatch Gentlemen of the Palace to offer condolences, sacrificial garments, sacrifices, and gifts, oversee the funeral arrangements, and thereby establish the heir.

entries.zh: 列侯薨，遣大中大夫弔祠，視喪事，因立嗣。
entries.en: When marquises die, dispatch Court Gentlemen to offer condolences and perform sacrifices. They shall oversee the funeral arrangements and thereby establish the heir.
entries.literal: When marquises die, dispatch Court Gentlemen to offer condolences and sacrifices, oversee the funeral arrangements, and thereby establish the heir.

entries.zh: 其薨葬，國得發民輓喪，穿復土，治墳無過三百人畢事。
entries.en: For their deaths and burials, the fiefs may mobilize commoners to pull the funeral carriages, excavate the tomb chamber, and construct the burial mound, with no more than three hundred people completing all the work.
entries.literal: For their deaths and burials, the fiefs may mobilize people to pull the funeral carriages, excavate the tomb, and construct the mound, with no more than three hundred people completing the work.

entries.zh: 三月，臨江王榮坐侵太宗廟地，徵詣中尉，自殺。
entries.en: In the third month, King Rong of Linjiang was convicted of encroaching on the Grand Progenitor Temple grounds. He was summoned before the Commandant of the Capital and committed suicide.
entries.literal: Third month: King Rong of Linjiang was convicted of encroaching on the Grand Progenitor Temple grounds; he was summoned before the Commandant of the Capital and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 三年冬十一月，罷諸侯御史大夫官。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of winter in the third year, he abolished the office of Grandee Secretary in all the feudal kingdoms.
entries.literal: In the third year, winter, eleventh month: He abolished the office of Grandee Secretary in the feudal kingdoms.

entries.zh: 春正月，皇太后崩。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, the Empress Dowager passed away.
entries.literal: Spring, first month: The Empress Dowager passed away.

entries.zh: 四年春三月，起德陽宮。
entries.en: In the third month of spring in the fourth year, he began construction of the Deyang Palace.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, spring, third month: He began construction of the Deyang Palace.

entries.zh: 御史大夫綰奏禁馬高五尺九寸以上，齒未平，不得出關。
entries.en: Grandee Secretary Wan submitted a proposal prohibiting horses taller than five feet nine inches with unerupted teeth from crossing the border passes.
entries.literal: Grandee Secretary Wan submitted a proposal to prohibit horses taller than five feet nine inches, whose teeth are not yet flat, from leaving the passes.

entries.zh: 六年冬十月，行幸雍，郊五畤。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter in the sixth year, he traveled to Yong and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Five Altars.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, winter, tenth month: He traveled to Yong and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Five Altars.

entries.zh: 條侯周亞夫下獄死。
entries.en: Marquis Tiao Zhou Yafu was thrown into prison and died there.
entries.literal: Marquis Tiao Zhou Yafu was imprisoned and died.

entries.zh: 二年冬十月，省徹侯之國。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter in the second year, he exempted marquises from the requirement to reside in their fiefs.
entries.literal: In the second year, winter, tenth month: He exempted marquises from residing in their fiefs.

entries.zh: 春，匈奴入鴈門，太守馮敬與戰死。
entries.en: In spring, the Xiongnu invaded Yanmen; Grand Administrator Feng Jing fought against them and was killed.
entries.literal: Spring: The Xiongnu entered Yanmen; Grand Administrator Feng Jing fought them and died.

entries.zh: 發車騎材官屯。
entries.en: He mobilized chariots, cavalry, and skilled troops to garrison the frontier.
entries.literal: He mobilized chariots, cavalry, and infantry to garrison the borders.

entries.zh: 皇太子冠，賜民為父後者爵一級。
entries.en: The Crown Prince underwent the capping ceremony; he granted one level of noble rank advancement to those who served as heirs to their fathers.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince was capped in ceremony; he granted advancement in noble rank by one level to those who served as their fathers' heirs.

entries.zh: 建元元年冬十月，詔丞相、御史、列侯、中二千石、二千石、諸侯相舉賢良方正直言極諫之士。
entries.en: In winter, in the tenth month of the first year of Jianyuan, an edict ordered the Chancellor, the Imperial Secretary, the marquises, senior court officials, and the chancellors of the feudal states to recommend men of worth and integrity who could speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month of the first year of Jianyuan, an edict ordered the Chancellor, the Imperial Secretary, the listed marquises, officials of the middle two-thousand-bushel rank, officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the chancellors of the feudal states to recommend men who were worthy and good, upright and forthright, and able to speak directly and remonstrate to the utmost.

entries.zh: 丞相綰奏：「所舉賢良，或治申、商、韓非、蘇秦、張儀之言，亂國政，請皆罷。」
entries.en: Chancellor Wan memorialized: "Some of the men recommended for worth study Shen Buhai, Shang Yang, Han Fei, Su Qin, and Zhang Yi, doctrines that disorder state government. I request that they all be dismissed."
entries.literal: Chancellor Wan memorialized: "Among those recommended as worthy and good, some study the teachings of Shen, Shang, Han Fei, Su Qin, and Zhang Yi, which disorder the government of the state; I request that all be dismissed."

entries.zh: 奏可。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: The memorial was approved.

entries.zh: 孝武皇帝，景帝中子也，母曰王美人。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was Emperor Jing's middle son. His mother was Lady Wang, a royal beauty.
entries.literal: Filial Martial Emperor, Emperor Jing's middle son; his mother was called Lady Wang, the Beauty.

entries.zh: 年四歲立為膠東王。
entries.en: At age four, he was made King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: Age four years established as Jiaodong King.

entries.zh: 七歲為皇太子，母為皇后。
entries.en: At age seven, he became crown prince, and his mother was made empress.
entries.literal: Seven years old became Crown Prince, mother became Empress.

entries.zh: 十六歲，後三年正月，景帝崩。
entries.en: At age sixteen, in the first month of the third year of Houyuan, Emperor Jing passed away.
entries.literal: Sixteen years old, in the first month of the third year of Houyuan, Emperor Jing passed away.

entries.zh: 甲子，太子即皇帝位，尊皇太后竇氏曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: On the jiazi day, the crown prince ascended the throne as emperor. He honored Empress Dowager Dou as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Jiazi day, Crown Prince ascended emperor position, honored Empress Dowager Dou clan as Grand Empress Dowager, Empress as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 三月，封皇太后同母弟田蚡、勝皆為列侯。
entries.en: In the third month, he enfeoffed the Empress Dowager's uterine brothers Tian Fen and Sheng as marquises.
entries.literal: Third month, enfeoffed Empress Dowager same-mother younger brothers Tian Fen, Sheng all as marquises.

entries.zh: 孝昭皇帝，武帝少子也。
entries.en: Emperor Zhao, the Filial, was Emperor Wu's youngest son.
entries.literal: Filial Emperor Zhao, Emperor Wu youngest son also.

entries.zh: 母曰趙婕妤，本以有奇異得幸，及生帝，亦奇異。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Zhao, a concubine who had gained favor through her extraordinary qualities, and the circumstances of his birth were also extraordinary.
entries.literal: Mother called Zhao Jieyu, originally by having extraordinary gained favor, and when gave birth to emperor, also extraordinary.

entries.zh: 語在外戚傳。
entries.en: The story is told in the Biography of the Imperial Relatives.
entries.literal: Words in outer relatives biography.

entries.zh: 武帝末，戾太子 敗，燕王旦、廣陵王胥行驕嫚，後元二年二月上疾病，遂立昭帝為太子，年八歲。
entries.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign, after the defeat of Crown Prince Li, King Dan of Yan and King Xu of Guangling both acted with arrogance and contempt. In the second month of Houyuan 2, when Emperor Wu fell ill, he made the future Emperor Zhao crown prince; Zhao was eight years old.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu's later years, after Crown Prince Li was defeated, King Dan of Yan and King Xu of Guangling behaved arrogantly and insolently. In the second month of the second year of Houyuan, when the emperor fell ill, he established Zhao as crown prince at age eight.

entries.zh: 以侍中奉車都尉霍光為大司馬大將軍，受遺詔輔少主。
entries.en: He appointed Huo Guang, Chamberlain of the Palace and Chariot Commandant, as Grand Marshal and Grand General; he received the testamentary decree to assist the young ruler.
entries.literal: He appointed Huo Guang, Chamberlain of the Palace and Chariot Commandant, as Grand Marshal and Grand General, who received the testamentary decree to assist the young ruler.

entries.zh: 明日，武帝崩。
entries.en: The next day, Emperor Wu passed away.
entries.literal: Next day, Emperor Wu passed away.

entries.zh: 戊辰，太子 即皇帝位，謁高廟。
entries.en: On the Wuchen day, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne and paid respects at the High Temple.
entries.literal: Wuchen day, crown prince ascended emperor position, paid respects at high temple.

entries.zh: 帝姊鄂邑公主益湯沐邑，為長公主，共養省中。
entries.en: The emperor's elder sister, Princess Eyi, had her bath fief increased and was made Elder Princess; she and others jointly raised and cared for the emperor in the inner palace.
entries.literal: The emperor's elder sister, Princess Eyi, had her bath fief increased and was made Elder Princess, and together they cared for the emperor in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 大將軍光秉政，領尚書事，車騎將軍金日磾、左將軍上官桀副焉。
entries.en: Grand General Guang held the government, led the Secretariat affairs, with Chariot Cavalry General Jin Midi and Left General Shangguan Jie as his assistants.
entries.literal: Grand general Guang held government, led Secretariat affairs, Chariot Cavalry General Jin Midi, Left General Shangguan Jie assisted.

entries.zh: 夏四月癸未，帝崩于未央宮。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on a Guiwei day, the Emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month Guiwei: Emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 六月壬申，葬平陵。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on a Renshen day, he was buried at Pingling.
entries.literal: Sixth month Renshen: Buried at Pingling.

entries.zh: 贊曰：昔周成以孺子繼統，而有管、蔡四國流言之變。
entries.en: In appraisal: In antiquity King Cheng of Zhou succeeded to the throne as a young child, and there arose the affair of the four states of Guan and Cai spreading slanderous rumors.
entries.literal: Appraisal says: In antiquity King Cheng of Zhou succeeded to the lineage as a young child, and there was the affair of the four states of Guan and Cai spreading slanderous rumors.

entries.zh: 孝昭幼年即位，亦有燕、盍、上官逆亂之謀。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhao the Filial ascended the throne in his youth, there were likewise conspiracies of rebellion involving King Yan, the Elder Princess, and the Shangguan faction.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhao the Filial ascended the throne in his youth, and likewise there were plots of rebellion by Yan, Gai, and Shangguan.

entries.zh: 成王不疑周公，孝昭委任霍光，各因其時以成名，大矣哉！
entries.en: King Cheng did not doubt the Duke of Zhou; Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang with power. Each, in his own time, achieved renown thereby. How great this was!
entries.literal: King Cheng did not doubt the Duke of Zhou; Emperor Zhao the Filial entrusted power to Huo Guang—each in his time achieved renown thereby. How great!

entries.zh: 承孝武奢侈餘敝師旅之後，海內虛耗，戶口減半，光知時務之要，輕繇薄賦，與民休息。
entries.en: Inheriting the aftermath of Emperor Wu's extravagance, the lingering exhaustion of military campaigns, and widespread depletion across the realm, with household registers reduced by half, Huo Guang understood what the times required: he lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes, allowing the people to recover.
entries.literal: Inheriting after Emperor Wu's extravagance, residual exhaustion, and military campaigns, within the seas there was depletion and household registers were halved. Guang knew the essentials of timely affairs—light corvée and thin taxes—and let the people rest.

entries.zh: 至始元、元鳳之間，匈奴和親，百姓充實。
entries.en: By the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng eras, the Xiongnu had entered into marriage alliances for peace, and the common people had become prosperous.
entries.literal: By the time between Shiyuan and Yuanfeng, the Xiongnu made peace through marriage alliance, and the common people were replenished.

entries.zh: 舉賢良文學，問民所疾苦，議鹽鐵而罷榷酤，尊號曰「昭」，不亦宜乎！
entries.en: Worthy and good men and literary scholars were recommended, the people's grievances were investigated, the debates on salt and iron led to the abolition of the liquor monopoly, and the honored title "Zhao" was bestowed—is this not most fitting!
entries.literal: Worthy and good men and literary scholars were recommended; the people's sufferings were inquired into; salt and iron monopolies were debated and the liquor excise abolished; the honored title "Zhao" was applied—is this not fitting!

entries.zh: 九月，鄂邑長公主、燕王旦與左將軍上官桀、桀子票騎將軍安、御史大夫桑弘羊皆謀反，伏誅。
entries.en: In the ninth month, the Elder Princess of Eyi, King Dan of Yan, Left General Shangguan Jie, Jie's son Flying Cavalry General An, and Imperial Secretary Sang Hongyang all plotted rebellion and were executed.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Eyi Elder Princess, Yan King Dan with Left General Shangguan Jie, Jie son Flying Cavalry General An, Imperial Secretary Sang Hongyang all plotted rebellion, suffered execution.

entries.zh: 初，桀、 安父子與大將軍光爭權，欲害之，詐使人為燕王旦上書言光罪。
entries.en: Initially, Shangguan Jie and his son An contended for power with Grand General Huo Guang and wished to harm him. They falsely had someone submit a memorial in the name of King Dan of Yan accusing Guang of crimes.
entries.literal: Initially, Jie, An father son with Grand General Guang contended power, wished to harm him, falsely made person for Yan King Dan memorial speak Guang crimes.

entries.zh: 時上年十四，覺其詐。
entries.en: At that time the emperor was fourteen years old and perceived their deception.
entries.literal: At that time emperor age fourteen, perceived their deception.

entries.zh: 後有譖光者，上輒怒曰：「大將軍國家忠臣，先帝所屬，敢有譖毀者，坐 之。」
entries.en: Later, when anyone slandered Guang, the emperor would always say angrily, 'The Grand General is a loyal minister of the state, entrusted with his charge by the late emperor. Anyone who dares slander him will be punished.'
entries.literal: Later, when there were those who slandered Guang, the emperor would always angrily say: The Grand General is a loyal minister of the state, whom the late emperor entrusted; anyone who dares to slander or defame him shall be punished.

entries.zh: 光由是得盡忠。
entries.en: Because of this, Guang was able to serve with complete loyalty.
entries.literal: Guang thereby able to exhaust loyalty.

entries.zh: 語在燕王、霍光傳。
entries.en: The story is told in the Biographies of King Yan and Huo Guang.
entries.literal: Words in Yan King, Huo Guang biographies.

entries.zh: 冬十月，詔曰：「左將軍安陽侯桀、票騎將軍桑樂侯安、御史大夫弘羊皆數以邪枉干輔政，大將軍不聽， 而懷怨望，與燕王通謀，置驛往來相約結。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, an edict stated: 'Left General Marquis Jie of Anyang, Flying Cavalry General Marquis An of Sang Le, and Imperial Secretary Hongyang all repeatedly interfered in the auxiliary government with crooked and perverse actions. The Grand General would not listen, so they harbored resentment and communicated with King Yan in plotting, establishing post stations for coming and going and mutually agreeing to join together.
entries.literal: Winter tenth month, edict said: Left general Anyang marquis Jie, flying cavalry general Sang Le marquis An, imperial secretary Hongyang all repeatedly with crooked perverse interfered auxiliary government, grand general not listen, and harbored resentment, with Yan King communicated plotted, established post stations come go mutually agreed joined.

entries.zh: 燕王遣壽西長、孫縱之等賂遺長公主、丁外人、謁者杜延年、大將軍長史公孫遺等，交通私書，共謀令長公主置酒，伏兵 殺大將軍光，徵立燕王為天子，大逆毋道。
entries.en: King Yan sent Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, and others to bribe and give gifts to the Elder Princess, Ding Wai, Usher Du Yannian, the Grand General's Chief Secretary Gongsun Yi, and others. They communicated with private letters and together plotted to have the Elder Princess host a wine banquet with ambush troops to kill Grand General Guang, and summon and establish King Yan as Son of Heaven - a great rebellion against the proper way.
entries.literal: Yan King sent Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi etc. bribed gave elder princess, Ding outsider, usher Du Yannian, grand general chief secretary Gongsun Yi etc., communicated private letters, together plotted made elder princess set wine, ambush troops kill grand general Guang, summoned established Yan King as heavenly son, great rebellion without way.

entries.zh: 故稻田使者燕倉先發覺，以告大司農敞，敞告諫大夫延年，延年以聞。
entries.en: The former rice field envoy Yan Cang first discovered this and informed Grand Minister of Agriculture Chang. Chang informed Remonstrance Grand Master Yannian, who reported it to the emperor.
entries.literal: Former rice field envoy Yan Cang first discovered, with told grand minister agriculture Chang, Chang told remonstrance Grand Master Yannian, Yannian with heard.

entries.zh: 丞相徵事任宮手捕斬桀，丞相少史王壽誘將安入府 門，皆已伏誅，吏民得以安。
entries.en: The Chancellor's investigator Ren Gong personally captured and beheaded Jie. The Chancellor's junior secretary Wang Shou lured An to enter the office gate. They all suffered execution, and officials and people were thereby able to live in peace.
entries.literal: Chancellor investigating affairs Ren Gong hand captured beheaded Jie, chancellor junior secretary Wang Shou lured led An entered office gate, all already suffered execution, officials people thereby able peaceful.

entries.zh: 封延年、倉、宮、壽皆為列侯。」
entries.en: Yannian, Cang, Gong, and Shou were all enfeoffed as marquises.'
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Yannian, Cang, Gong, Shou all as marquises."

entries.zh: 又曰：「燕王迷惑失道，前與齊王子劉澤等為逆，抑而不揚，望王反道自新，今乃與長公主及左將軍 桀等謀危宗廟。
entries.en: The edict continued: 'The King of Yan was confused and lost his way. He had previously joined Prince Liu Ze of Qi and others in rebellion. Though this was suppressed and not widely publicized in the hope that the king would reform and return to the proper path, he has now conspired with the Long Princess and General of the Left Jie to endanger the ancestral temples.
entries.literal: Further said: 'Yan King was confused and lost the Way, previously with Qi Prince Liu Ze and others committed rebellion, suppressed and not raised, hoped King would return to Way and renew himself, now instead with Long Princess and General of the Left Jie and others plotted to endanger ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 王及公主皆自伏辜。
entries.en: The king and the princess both submitted to punishment for their guilt.
entries.literal: The king and the princess both took their guilt upon themselves.

entries.zh: 其赦王太子建、公主子文信及宗室子與燕王、上官桀等謀反父母同產當坐者，皆免為庶人。
entries.en: The king's heir apparent Jian, the princess's son Wenxin, and the imperial clansmen who had plotted rebellion with the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie, together with their parents and full siblings who would normally be implicated, were all pardoned and reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: Pardon the king's heir apparent Jian, the princess's son Wenxin, and the imperial clansmen who with the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie and others plotted rebellion, and their parents and full siblings who should be implicated—all reduce to commoners.

entries.zh: 其吏為桀等所詿誤，未發覺在吏者， 除其罪。」
entries.en: The officials who had been deceived and misled by Jie and his confederates, and whose involvement had not yet been discovered while they remained in office, were pardoned of their crimes."
entries.literal: Their officials who were deceived and misled by Jie and others, not yet discovered while in office, remove their crimes."

entries.zh: 孝元皇帝，宣帝太子也。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan was the son whom Emperor Xuan had designated as crown prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan was the heir apparent of Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 母曰共哀許皇后，宣帝微時生民間。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Xu, honored posthumously as Gongaiai; she gave birth to him while the future Emperor Xuan was still a private man living outside the court.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Xu, titled Gongaiai; she had borne him among the common people when Emperor Xuan was still obscure.

entries.zh: 年二歲，宣帝即位。
entries.en: He was two years old when Emperor Xuan came to the throne.
entries.literal: At age two, Emperor Xuan ascended the throne.

entries.zh: 八歲，立為太子。
entries.en: At the age of eight he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: At eight, he was established as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 壯大，柔仁好儒。
entries.en: As he grew to manhood he showed a gentle, humane temperament and a strong leaning toward Confucian learning.
entries.literal: When grown, he was soft, humane, and fond of Confucianism.

entries.zh: 見宣帝所用多文法吏，以刑名繩下，大臣楊惲、盍寬饒等坐刺譏辭語為罪而誅，嘗侍燕從容言：「
entries.en: He saw that Emperor Xuan employed many officials versed in statutes, used penal law to restrain his subordinates, and had executed high ministers such as Yang Yun and Gai Kuangrao for words of criticism or satire. Once, while attending an informal banquet, he said, “
entries.literal: Seeing that Emperor Xuan employed many clerks versed in statutes and doctrine, used penal prescriptions and Legalist formulas to bind subordinates, and that great ministers such as Yang Yun and Gai Kuangrao were executed on charges arising from satirical or cutting language, when he once attended a banquet he remarked at leisure: "

entries.zh: 陛下持刑太深，宜用儒生。」
entries.en: Your Majesty holds punishments too severely; you should employ Confucian scholars."
entries.literal: Your Majesty holds punishments too deeply; you should employ Confucian scholars."

entries.zh: 宣帝作色曰：「漢家自有制度，本以霸王道雜之，奈何純住德教，用周政 乎！
entries.en: Emperor Xuan's expression changed, and he said: "The Han house has its own system, originally mixing hegemonic and kingly ways—why rely solely on moral teaching and adopt Zhou government?
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan changed color and said: "The Han house has its own system, originally mixing hegemon and king ways—why rely solely on virtue teachings and use Zhou government?

entries.zh: 且俗儒不達時宜，好是古非今，使人眩於名實，不知所守，何足委任！」
entries.en: Moreover, vulgar Confucians do not grasp what the times require. They like to praise antiquity and condemn the present, until people are dazzled by names and realities and no longer know what to uphold—how can they be entrusted with office?"
entries.literal: Moreover vulgar Confucians do not grasp timely suitability; they like to affirm the ancient and negate the present, causing people to be dazzled by names and realities and not know what to uphold—how are they fit to be entrusted and employed?"

entries.zh: 乃歎曰：「亂我家者，太子也！」
entries.en: Then he sighed and said: "The one who will disorder my house is the Crown Prince!"
entries.literal: Then he sighed and said: "The one who will disorder my house is the Crown Prince!"

entries.zh: 繇是疏太子而愛淮陽王，曰：「淮陽王明察好法，宜 為吾子。」
entries.en: Because of this he kept his distance from the Crown Prince and favored King Huaiyang, saying: "King Huaiyang is clear-sighted and fond of law—he should be my son."
entries.literal: Because of this he distanced the Crown Prince and favored King Huaiyang, saying: "King Huaiyang is clear-sighted and fond of law—he should be my son."

entries.zh: 而王母張婕妤尤幸。
entries.en: And the king's mother, Lady Zhang, was especially favored.
entries.literal: And the king's mother, Lady Zhang, was especially favored.

entries.zh: 上有意欲用淮陽王代太子，然以少依許氏，俱從微起，故終不背焉。
entries.en: His Majesty had the intention to use King Huaiyang to replace the Crown Prince, but because he had relied on the Xu clan since youth and both had risen from humble origins, he finally did not turn his back on them.
entries.literal: His Majesty had intention wished use Huaiyang King replace Crown Prince, yet because young relied Xu clan, both from humble rise, therefore finally not turn back from.

entries.zh: 黃龍元年十二月，宣帝崩。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Huanglong, Emperor Xuan collapsed.
entries.literal: Huanglong first year twelfth month, Emperor Xuan collapsed.

entries.zh: 癸巳，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟。
entries.en: On Guisi, the Crown Prince ascended to the emperor's position and made audience at the High Temple.
entries.literal: Guisi, Crown Prince ascended emperor position, audience high temple.

entries.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: Honored the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Honored Empress Dowager called Grand Empress Dowager, Empress called Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 五月壬辰，帝崩于未央宮。
entries.en: On Renchen of the fifth month, the Emperor collapsed at Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: Fifth month Renchen, Emperor collapsed at Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 初元元年春正月辛丑，孝宣皇帝葬杜陵。
entries.en: On Xinchou of the first month of spring in the first year of Chuyuan, Emperor Xuan was buried at Duling.
entries.literal: Chuyuan first year spring first month Xinchou, Filial Xuan Emperor buried Duling.

entries.zh: 賜諸侯王、公主、列侯黃金，吏二千石以下錢帛，各有差。
entries.en: Granted gold to feudal kings, princesses, and marquises; money and silks to officials of 2000 piculs and below, each according to their rank.
entries.literal: Granted feudal lords kings, princesses, marquises gold, officials 2000 piculs below money silks, each had difference.

entries.zh: 大赦 天下。
entries.en: Granted a great pardon to the empire.
entries.literal: Great pardon empire.

entries.zh: 三月，封皇太后兄侍中中郎將王舜為安平侯。
entries.en: In the third month, enfeoffed Wang Shun, brother of the Empress Dowager and Commandant of the Gentlemen of the Palace, as Marquis of Anping.
entries.literal: Third month, enfeoffed Empress Dowager brother Attendant at the Palace Commandant of the Gentlemen Wang Shun as Anping Marquis.

entries.zh: 丙午，立皇后王氏。
entries.en: On Bingwu, established a lady of the Wang clan as Empress.
entries.literal: Bingwu, established Empress Wang clan.

entries.zh: 以三輔、太常、郡國公田及苑可省者振業貧民，貲不滿千錢者賦貸種、食。
entries.en: Used public fields from Sanfu, the Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and the commanderies and kingdoms, as well as parks that could be reduced, to relieve and assist poor people. For those whose property did not reach 1000 cash, assigned loans of seeds and food.
entries.literal: Used Sanfu, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, commanderies kingdoms public fields and parks can reduce ones relieve assist poor people, property not full thousand cash ones assign lend seeds, food.

entries.zh: 封外祖父平恩戴侯同產弟子中常侍許嘉為平恩侯，奉戴侯後。
entries.en: Enfeoffed Xu Jia, Palace Regular Attendant and son of a full younger brother of the emperor's maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Xu Jia, Palace Regular Attendant and son of a full younger brother of the maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.

entries.zh: 永光元年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
entries.literal: Yongguang first year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

entries.zh: 赦雲陽徒。
entries.en: Pardon the convicts at Yunyang.
entries.literal: Pardon Yunyang convicts.

entries.zh: 賜民爵一級，女子百戶牛酒，高年帛。
entries.en: Granted the people one noble rank, women who head 100 households cattle and wine, and the aged silk.
entries.literal: Granted people noble ranks one level, women 100 households cattle wine, aged silk.

entries.zh: 行所過毋出租賦。
entries.en: Places the procession passed shall not pay rents and taxes.
entries.literal: Procession passed places not pay rent taxes.

entries.zh: 建昭元年春三月，上幸雍，祠五畤。
entries.en: In the third month of spring in the first year of Jianzhao, His Majesty favored Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
entries.literal: Jianzhao first year spring third month, His Majesty favored Yong, sacrificed Five Altars.

entries.zh: 竟寧元年春正月，匈奴虖韓邪單于來朝。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the first year of Jingning, Chanyu Huhanye of the Xiongnu came to court.
entries.literal: Jingning first year spring first month, Xiongnu Huhanye Chanyu came to court.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「匈奴郅支單于背叛禮義，既伏其辜，虖韓邪單于不忘恩德，鄉慕禮義，復修朝賀之禮，願保塞傳之無窮，邊垂長無兵革之事。
entries.en: An edict declared: 'Chanyu Zhizhi of the Xiongnu turned his back and rebelled against ritual and righteousness, and has already submitted to his guilt. Chanyu Huhanye has not forgotten kindness and virtue, faces and admires ritual and righteousness, again repairs the ritual of court congratulations, wishes to protect the border pass and transmit it endlessly, so the border regions long have no affairs of weapons and armor.
entries.literal: Edict said: 'Xiongnu Zhizhi Chanyu turned back rebelled ritual righteousness, already submitted his guilt, Huhanye Chanyu not forget kindness virtue, faces admires ritual righteousness, again repaired court congratulations ritual, wishes protect border pass transmit endless, border regions long without weapons armor affairs.

entries.zh: 其改元為竟寧，賜單于待詔掖庭王檣為閼氏。」
entries.en: Cause the era name to be changed to Jingning, granted Chanyu the awaiting edict of the Rear Court Wang Jiang as Yanzhi.'
entries.literal: Cause change era name to Jingning, granted Chanyu awaiting edict Rear Court Wang Jiang as Yanzhi.'

entries.zh: 立弟竟為清河王。
entries.en: Established younger brother Jing as King of Qinghe.
entries.literal: Established younger brother Jing as Qinghe King.

entries.zh: 夏四月丁巳，立皇太子。
entries.en: On Dingsi of the fourth month of summer, established the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month Dingsi, established Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 賜御史大夫爵關內侯，中二千石右庶長，天下當為父後者爵一級，列侯錢各二十萬，五大夫十萬。
entries.en: Granted the Imperial Secretary Grandee the noble rank of Guannei Marquis, and officials of 2000 piculs the Right Shaolao rank. Throughout the empire, those who should succeed their fathers were granted one noble rank. Marquises received 200,000 cash each, and Grandees of the Fifth Rank received 100,000.
entries.literal: Granted Imperial Secretary Grandee noble rank Guannei Marquis, 2000 piculs Right Shaolao, empire should succeed fathers ones noble rank one level, marquises money each 200,000, Grandee of the Fifth Rank 100,000.

entries.zh: 三月，立皇子康為濟陽王。
entries.en: In the third month, the emperor's son Kang was made King of Jiyang.
entries.literal: In the third month, the emperor's son Kang was made King of Jiyang.

entries.zh: 六月，立皇子興為信都王。
entries.en: In the sixth month, the emperor's son Xing was made King of Xindu.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, the emperor's son Xing was made King of Xindu.

entries.zh: 閏月丁酉，太皇太后上官氏崩。
entries.en: On Dingyou of the intercalary month, the Grand Empress Dowager of the Shangguan clan collapsed.
entries.literal: Intercalary month Dingyou, Grand Empress Dowager Shangguan clan collapsed.

entries.zh: 二年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the second year, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
entries.literal: Second year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

entries.zh: 賜雲陽民爵一級，女子百戶牛酒。
entries.en: Granted the people of Yunyang one noble rank, and women who head 100 households cattle and wine.
entries.literal: Granted Yunyang people noble ranks one level, women 100 households cattle wine.

entries.zh: 夏四月，詔曰：「朕承先帝之聖緒，獲奉宗廟，戰戰兢兢。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, an edict declared: 'I bear the sage succession of the Former Emperor and have obtained the service of ancestral temples, trembling with fear.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month, edict said: 'I bear Former Emperor's sage succession, obtained serve ancestral temples, trembling fearful.

entries.zh: 間者地數動而未靜，懼於天地之戒，不知所 繇。
entries.en: Recently the earth has frequently moved and not been quiet. I fear the warnings of heaven and earth, not knowing what they stem from.
entries.literal: Recently earth frequently moved and not quiet, fear at heaven earth warnings, not know what from.

entries.zh: 方田作時，朕憂蒸庶之失業，臨遣光祿大夫褒等十二人循行天下，存問耆老鰥寡孤獨困乏失職之民，延登賢俊，招顯側陋，因覽風俗之化。
entries.en: Just at farming time, I worry that the numerous common people will lose their occupations. I am about to send Chamberlain for Attendants Bao and eleven others to tour the empire, visit and inquire about the aged, widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, the distressed, those lacking, and those who have lost their duties. Extend and ascend the worthy and talented, recruit and display the secluded and obscure, and thereby view the transformations of customs.
entries.literal: Just farming work time, I worry numerous common people lose occupations, about to send Chamberlain for Attendants Bao etc. twelve people tour empire, visit inquire aged widowers widows orphans solitary distressed lacking lost duty people, extend ascend worthy talented, recruit display secluded obscure, because view customs transformations.

entries.zh: 相守二千石誠能正躬 勞力，宣明教化，以親萬姓，則六合之內和親，庶幾虖無憂矣。
entries.en: If the chancellors and governors at the two-thousand-picul level can sincerely correct themselves and labor diligently, proclaim and clarify teaching and transformation to draw near the myriad people, then within the realm there will be harmony and kinship, and we may come close to being free of worry.
entries.literal: If the chancellors and governors at the two-thousand-picul level can sincerely correct themselves and labor with strength, proclaim and clarify teaching and transformation to draw near the myriad surnames, then within the six directions there will be harmony and kinship, and perhaps we may be nearly free of worry.

entries.zh: 書不云乎？
entries.en: Does the Book not say?
entries.literal: Book not say?

entries.zh: 『股肱良哉，庶事康哉！』
entries.en: 'The limbs are good! All affairs are peaceful!'
entries.literal: 'Thigh arm good ah, numerous affairs peaceful ah!'

entries.zh: 布告天下，使明知朕意。」
entries.en: Proclaim and announce to the empire, so that they clearly know my intention.'
entries.literal: Proclaim announce empire, cause clearly know my intention.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「關東今年穀不登，民多困 乏。
entries.en: Further declared: 'East of the passes this year the grain did not ascend, the people are many and distressed and lacking.
entries.literal: Further said: 'East of passes this year grain not ascend, people many distressed lacking.

entries.zh: 其令郡國被災害甚者毋出租賦。
entries.en: Cause those commanderies and kingdoms that suffered severe disasters not to pay rents and taxes.
entries.literal: Cause commanderies kingdoms suffered disasters severe ones not pay rent taxes.

entries.zh: 江海陂湖園池屬少府者以假貧民，勿租賦。
entries.en: Those river and sea dikes, lakes, gardens, and ponds that belong to the Privy Treasury shall be lent to poor people, without rent or taxes.
entries.literal: Rivers seas dikes lakes gardens ponds belong Privy Treasury ones use lend poor people, not rent taxes.

entries.zh: 賜宗室有屬籍者馬一匹至二駟，三老、孝者帛五匹，弟者、力田三匹，鰥寡孤獨二 匹，吏民五十戶牛酒。」
entries.en: Granted to members of the imperial clan who have genealogy registers horses from one mount to two teams; to the three elders and filial ones five bolts of silk; to younger brothers and diligent farmers three bolts; to widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary two bolts; and to officials and common people who head fifty households cattle and wine.'
entries.literal: Granted imperial clan have genealogy registers ones horses one mount to two teams, three elders, filial ones silk five bolts, younger brothers, diligent farming three bolts, widowers widows orphans solitary two bolts, officials common people fifty households cattle wine.'

entries.zh: 四年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the fourth year, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
entries.literal: Fourth year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

entries.zh: 三月，行幸河東，祠后土。
entries.en: In the third month, His Majesty proceeded to Hedong and sacrificed to Houtu.
entries.literal: Third month, proceeded favored Hedong, sacrificed Houtu.

entries.zh: 赦汾陰徒。
entries.en: Pardon the convicts at Fenying.
entries.literal: Pardon Fenying convicts.

entries.zh: 賜民爵一級，女子百戶牛酒，鰥寡高年帛。
entries.en: Granted the people one noble rank, women who head 100 households cattle and wine, and widowers, widows, and the aged silk.
entries.literal: Granted people noble ranks one level, women 100 households cattle wine, widowers widows aged silk.

entries.zh: 行所過無出租賦。
entries.en: Places the procession passed shall not pay rents and taxes.
entries.literal: Procession passed places not pay rent taxes.

entries.zh: 三月，行幸雍，祠五畤。
entries.en: In the third month, His Majesty proceeded to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
entries.literal: Third month, proceeded favored Yong, sacrificed Five Altars.

entries.zh: 三月，行幸雍，祠五畤。
entries.en: In the third month, His Majesty proceeded to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
entries.literal: Third month, proceeded favored Yong, sacrificed Five Altars.

entries.zh: 五年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the fifth year, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
entries.literal: Fifth year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

entries.zh: 三月，上幸河東，祠后土。
entries.en: In the third month, His Majesty favored Hedong and sacrificed to Houtu.
entries.literal: Third month, His Majesty favored Hedong, sacrificed Houtu.

entries.zh: 冬，上幸長楊射熊館，布車騎，大獵。
entries.en: In winter, His Majesty favored the Changyang shoot bear pavilion, spread chariots and cavalry, and conducted a great hunt.
entries.literal: Winter, His Majesty favored Changyang shoot bear pavilion, spread chariots cavalry, great hunt.

entries.zh: 二年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the second year, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
entries.literal: Second year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

entries.zh: 三月，行幸河東，祠后土。
entries.en: In the third month, His Majesty proceeded to Hedong and sacrificed to Houtu.
entries.literal: Third month, proceeded favored Hedong, sacrificed Houtu.

entries.zh: 益三河郡太守秩。
entries.en: The rank of the Sanhe commandery governor was increased.
entries.literal: Increased Sanhe commandery governor rank.

entries.zh: 戶十二萬為大郡。
entries.en: Commanderies with 120,000 households were considered great commanderies.
entries.literal: Households 120,000 as great commandery.

entries.zh: 夏四月，詔曰：「朕承先帝之休烈，夙夜栗栗，懼不克任。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, an edict declared: 'I bear the fortunate achievements of the Former Emperor, from early to late trembling, fearing I am not able to bear it.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month, edict said: 'I bear Former Emperor's fortunate achievements, early late tremble tremble, fear not able bear.

entries.zh: 間者陰陽不調，五行失序，百姓饑饉。
entries.en: Recently yin and yang have not been harmonized, the five phases have lost their order, and the common people suffer famine and hunger.
entries.literal: Recently yin yang not harmonized, five phases lost order, common people famine hunger.

entries.zh: 惟烝庶之失業，臨遣諫大夫博士賞等二十一人循行天下，存問耆老鰥寡孤獨乏困失職之人，舉茂材特立之士。
entries.en: Only thinking of the numerous common people who lose their occupations, I am about to send Remonstrance Grandee, Doctor Shang, and twenty others to tour the empire, visit and inquire about the aged, widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, the distressed, those lacking, and those who have lost their duties, and recommend excellent talents and outstanding independent gentlemen.
entries.literal: Only numerous common people lose occupations, about to send Remonstrance Grandee Doctor Shang etc. twenty one people tour empire, visit inquire aged widowers widows orphans solitary distressed lacking lost duty people, recommend excellent talents outstanding independent gentlemen.

entries.zh: 相將九卿，其帥意毋怠，使朕獲觀教化之流焉。」
entries.en: Assistant and lead the Nine Ministers, their leading intention shall not be weary, so that I may obtain to view the flow of teachings and transformations there.'
entries.literal: Assistant lead Nine Ministers, their lead intention not weary, cause I obtain view teachings transformations flow there.'

entries.zh: 夏六月甲戌，孝宣園東闕災。
entries.en: On Jiaxu of the sixth month of summer, the east gate of the Filial Xuan park suffered a disaster.
entries.literal: Summer sixth month Jiaxu, Filial Xuan park east gate disaster.

entries.zh: 六月甲申，中山王竟薨。
entries.en: On Jiashen of the sixth month, King Jing of Zhongshan passed away.
entries.literal: Sixth month Jiashen, Zhongshan King Jing passed away.

entries.zh: 夏四月乙未晦，茂陵白鶴館災。
entries.en: On the last day of the fourth month of summer, which fell on Yiwei, the white crane pavilion at Maoling suffered a disaster.
entries.literal: On the last day of the fourth month of summer, an Yiwei day, the White Crane Lodge at Maoling burned.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「乃者火災降於孝武園館，朕戰栗恐懼。
entries.en: An edict declared: 'Recently fire disaster descended on the Filial Wu park pavilions. I tremble with fear.
entries.literal: Edict said: 'Recently fire disaster descended on Filial Wu park pavilions, I tremble fear fear.

entries.zh: 不燭變異，咎在朕躬。
entries.en: I did not illuminate the anomalous changes—the fault is in my person.
entries.literal: Not illuminate anomalies changes, fault in my person.

entries.zh: 群司又未肯極言朕過，以至於斯，將何以寤焉！
entries.en: The host of officials moreover were unwilling to speak frankly of my faults, until it has come to this—how am I to awaken!
entries.literal: The host of officials moreover were unwilling to speak to the utmost of my faults, until it has come to this—how am I to awaken!

entries.zh: 百姓仍遭凶阨，無以相振，加以煩擾虖苛吏，拘牽乎微文，不得永終性命，朕甚閔焉。
entries.en: The common people still encounter inauspicious distress, with nothing to mutually relieve them. Moreover, they are troubled and disturbed by harsh officials, constrained and pulled by minute writings, unable to forever end their life and fate. I greatly pity them.
entries.literal: Common people still encounter inauspicious distress, none to mutually relieve, moreover troubled disturbed by harsh officials, constrained pulled by minute writings, not able forever end life fate, I greatly pity them.

entries.zh: 其赦天下。」
entries.en: Cause the empire to be pardoned.'
entries.literal: Cause pardon empire.'

entries.zh: 二年春二月，詔曰：「蓋聞唐虞象刑而民不犯，殷周法行而姦軌服。
entries.en: In the second month of spring in the second year, an edict declared: 'Indeed I have heard that Tang and Yu symbolized punishments and the people did not violate, Yin and Zhou practiced laws and wicked ruffians submitted.
entries.literal: Second year spring second month, edict said: 'Indeed heard Tang Yu symbolized punishments and people not violate, Yin Zhou laws practiced and wicked ruffians submit.

entries.zh: 今朕獲承高祖之洪業，託位公侯之 上，夙夜戰栗，永惟百姓之急，未嘗有忘焉。
entries.en: Now I have obtained to bear Gaozu's grand enterprise, entrusted with position above the dukes and marquises. From early to late I tremble with fear, forever thinking of the common people's urgent matters, never once having forgotten them.
entries.literal: Now I obtained bear Gaozu's grand enterprise, entrusted position dukes marquises above, early late tremble fear, forever think common people urgent matters, not once had forget them.

entries.zh: 然而陰陽未調，三光晻昧。
entries.en: However, yin and yang are not harmonized, the three luminaries are dark and obscure.
entries.literal: However yin yang not harmonized, three luminaries dark obscure.

entries.zh: 元元大困，流散道路，盜賊並興。
entries.en: The common people are greatly distressed, flowing and scattered on the roads, bandits and robbers arising together.
entries.literal: Common people greatly distressed, flowed scattered roads, bandits robbers together arise.

entries.zh: 有司又長殘賊，失牧民之術。
entries.en: The officials moreover constantly practice cruelty, losing the art of shepherding the people.
entries.literal: The officials moreover constantly practice cruelty, losing the art of shepherding the people.

entries.zh: 是皆朕之不明，政有所虧。
entries.en: This is all because I am not bright, governance has deficiencies.
entries.literal: This all my not bright, governance has deficiency.

entries.zh: 咎至於此，朕甚自恥。
entries.en: Fault has arrived to this point, I greatly am ashamed of myself.
entries.literal: Fault arrives to this, I greatly self ashamed.

entries.zh: 為民父母，若是之薄，謂百姓何！
entries.en: As parents to the people, if I am this inadequate, what can I say to the common people!
entries.literal: As parents to the people, if I am this inadequate, what can I say to the common people!

entries.zh: 其大赦天下，賜民爵一級，女子百戶牛酒，鰥寡孤獨高年、三老、孝弟力田帛。」
entries.en: Cause a great pardon of the empire, grant the people one noble rank, women who head 100 households cattle and wine, and widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, the aged, three elders, filial younger brothers, and diligent farmers silk.'
entries.literal: Cause great pardon empire, grant people noble ranks one level, women 100 households cattle wine, widowers widows orphans solitary aged, three elders, filial younger brothers diligent farming silk.'

entries.zh: 又賜諸侯王、公主、列侯 黃金，中二千石以下至中都官長吏各有差，吏六百石以上爵五大夫，勤事吏各二級。
entries.en: Further granted feudal kings, princesses, and marquises gold; from 2000 piculs below to central capital officials and chief clerks each according to rank; officials of 600 piculs and above the noble rank of Grandee of the Fifth Rank; and diligent affairs officials each two levels.
entries.literal: Further granted feudal lords kings, princesses, marquises gold, 2000 piculs below to central capital officials chief clerks each had difference, officials 600 piculs above noble rank Grandee of the Fifth Rank, diligent affairs officials each two levels.

entries.zh: 十二月乙酉，毀太上皇、孝惠皇帝寢廟園。
entries.en: On Yiyou of the twelfth month, the sleeping temple gardens of the Grand Emperor Ancestor and Emperor Hui were destroyed.
