entries.literal: Twelfth month Yiyou, destroyed Grand Emperor Ancestor, Filial Hui Emperor sleeping temple gardens.

entries.zh: 三月癸未，復孝惠皇帝寢廟園、孝文太后、孝昭太后寢園。
entries.en: On Guiwei of the third month, the sleeping temple gardens of the Filial Hui Emperor, Filial Wen Empress Dowager, and Filial Zhao Empress Dowager were restored.
entries.literal: Third month Guiwei, restored Filial Hui Emperor sleeping temple gardens, Filial Wen Empress Dowager, Filial Zhao Empress Dowager sleeping gardens.

entries.zh: 毀太上皇、孝惠、孝景皇帝廟。
entries.en: The temples of the Grand Emperor Ancestor, Filial Hui Emperor, and Filial Jing Emperor were destroyed.
entries.literal: Destroyed Grand Emperor Ancestor, Filial Hui, Filial Jing Emperor temples.

entries.zh: 罷孝文、孝昭太后、昭靈后、武哀王、昭哀后寢園。
entries.en: The sleeping gardens of the Filial Wen and Filial Zhao Empress Dowagers, Zhao Ling Empress, Wu Ai King, and Zhao Ai Empress were abolished.
entries.literal: Abolished Filial Wen, Filial Zhao Empress Dowagers, Zhao Ling Empress, Wu Ai King, Zhao Ai Empress sleeping gardens.

entries.zh: 贊曰：臣外祖兄弟為元帝侍中，語臣曰元帝多材藝，善史書。
entries.en: The appraisal says: My maternal grandfather's brothers served Emperor Yuan as palace attendants. They told me that Emperor Yuan possessed many talents and was skilled in historical writing.
entries.literal: Appraisal says: My maternal grandfather's brothers were Attendants at the Palace for Emperor Yuan; they told me that Emperor Yuan had many talents and skills and was skilled in historical writing.

entries.zh: 鼓琴瑟，吹洞簫，自度曲，被歌聲，分刌節度，窮極幼眇。
entries.en: He played the qin and se zithers, performed on the vertical flute, composed his own melodies, set them for singing, and worked out their sections and rhythms with the utmost subtlety.
entries.literal: He played the qin and se, blew the vertical flute, composed tunes himself, set them to song, divided and marked the sections and measures, reaching the utmost refinement.

entries.zh: 少而好儒，及即位，徵用儒生，委之以政，貢、薛、韋、匡迭為宰相。
entries.en: From youth he loved Confucian learning, and after he took the throne he summoned Confucian scholars, employed them, and entrusted government to them; Gong, Xue, Wei, and Kuang served in turn as chancellors.
entries.literal: From youth he loved Confucianism; when he ascended the throne, he summoned and employed Confucian scholars and entrusted government to them; Gong, Xue, Wei, and Kuang became chancellors in turn.

entries.zh: 而上牽制文義，優游不斷，孝宣之業衰焉。
entries.en: Yet at court he was hamstrung by textual niceties, lingered without deciding, and the achievements of Emperor Xuan declined.
entries.literal: Yet at court he was hamstrung by textual niceties, lingered without deciding, and the achievements of Emperor Xuan declined.

entries.zh: 然寬弘盡下，出於恭儉，號令溫雅，有古之風烈。
entries.en: Yet he was generous and broad-minded toward his subordinates, and his conduct arose from reverence and frugality. His commands were mild and refined, with something of the noble manner of antiquity.
entries.literal: Yet he was magnanimous and exhaustive toward those below, acting from respectful frugality; his orders and commands were mild and elegant, with something of the heroic style of antiquity.

entries.zh: 秋七月丙戌，葬渭陵。
entries.en: On Bingxu of the seventh month of autumn, buried at Weiling.
entries.literal: Autumn seventh month Bingxu, buried Weiling.

entries.zh: 孝成皇帝，元帝太子也。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaocheng was Emperor Yuan's crown prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaocheng was the crown prince of Emperor Yuan.

entries.zh: 母曰王皇后，元帝在太子宮生甲觀畫堂，爲世嫡皇孫。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Wang. He was born in the Painted Hall of the Jia Lodge while Emperor Yuan was still living in the Crown Prince's palace, and he became the legitimate imperial grandson.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Wang; when Emperor Yuan was in the Crown Prince's palace, he was born in the Painted Hall of the Jia Lodge and became the legitimate imperial grandson.

entries.zh: 宣帝愛之，字曰太孫，常置左右。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan loved him, gave him the courtesy designation Grandson of the Emperor, and often kept him close by.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan loved him, styled him Grandson of the Emperor, and often kept him at his side.

entries.zh: 年三歳而宣帝崩，元帝即位，帝爲太子。
entries.en: When he was three, Emperor Xuan died. Emperor Yuan took the throne, and the future emperor became crown prince.
entries.literal: When he was three years old Emperor Xuan died; Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, and the emperor became crown prince.

entries.zh: 壯好經書，寬博謹慎。
entries.en: As he grew up, he loved the Classics and other writings, and he was broad-minded, generous, cautious, and respectful.
entries.literal: When grown, he loved the Classics and writings, and was broad-minded, generous, careful, and respectful.

entries.zh: 初居桂宮，上嘗急召，太子出龍樓門，不敢絶馳道，西至直城門，得絶乃度，還入作室門。
entries.en: When he first lived in Gui Palace, the emperor once summoned him urgently. The crown prince left through Dragon Tower Gate but did not dare cross the imperial roadway; he went west to Straight City Gate, crossed only where it was permitted, and then came back in through Workshop Gate.
entries.literal: When he first lived in Gui Palace, the emperor once summoned him urgently; the crown prince went out through Dragon Tower Gate, did not dare cross the imperial roadway, went west to Straight City Gate, crossed only where he could, and returned through Workshop Gate.

entries.zh: 上遲之，問其故，以狀對。
entries.en: The emperor thought he had been slow and asked why; the crown prince explained what had happened.
entries.literal: The emperor thought him late and asked the reason; he answered with the circumstances.

entries.zh: 上大説，乃著令，令太子得絶馳道云。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an order allowing the crown prince to cross the imperial roadway.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, and then established an order allowing the crown prince to cross the imperial roadway.

entries.zh: 其後幸酒，樂燕樂，上不以爲能。
entries.en: Later he became fond of wine and enjoyed banquets and music, and the emperor did not regard him as capable.
entries.literal: Afterward he liked wine and delighted in banquets and music; the emperor did not consider him capable.

entries.zh: 而定陶恭王有材藝，母傅昭儀又愛幸，上以故常有意欲以恭王爲嗣。
entries.en: King Gong of Dingtao, however, had talent and accomplishments, and his mother Consort Fu was much loved and favored, so the emperor often thought of making King Gong his heir.
entries.literal: But King Gong of Dingtao had talents and accomplishments, and his mother, Consort Fu, was also loved and favored; for this reason the emperor often intended to make King Gong his heir.

entries.zh: 賴侍中史丹護太子家，輔助有力，上亦以先帝尤愛太子，故得無廢。
entries.en: Because Attendant Shi Dan strongly protected and supported the crown prince's household, and because the emperor remembered that the late emperor had especially loved the crown prince, the crown prince was not deposed.
entries.literal: Thanks to Attendant Shi Dan protecting the crown prince's household and assisting him forcefully, and because the emperor also considered that the former emperor had especially loved the crown prince, he was not deposed.

entries.zh: 竟寧元年五月，元帝崩。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Jingning, Emperor Yuan died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jingning, Emperor Yuan died.

entries.zh: 六月己未，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟。
entries.en: On jiwei in the sixth month, the crown prince ascended the imperial throne and paid respects at the temple of Gaozu.
entries.literal: On jiwei in the sixth month, the crown prince took the imperial throne and paid respects at Gao Temple.

entries.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: He honored the Empress Dowager with the title Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress with the title Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: He honored the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 以元舅侍中衞尉陽平侯王鳳爲大司馬大將軍，領尚書事。
entries.en: He appointed his maternal uncle Wang Feng, then Attendant, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Yangping, as Grand Marshal and General-in-Chief, with charge of the affairs of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He made his maternal uncle Wang Feng, Attendant, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Yangping, Grand Marshal and General-in-Chief, overseeing the affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 乙未，有司言：「乘輿車、牛馬、禽獸皆非禮，不宜以葬。」
entries.en: On Yiwu, the officials stated: 'The imperial chariot, oxen, horses, birds, and beasts are all against ritual propriety and should not be used in burial.'
entries.literal: Yiwu, officials said: 'Imperial chariot, oxen horses, birds beasts all not ritual, not proper to bury with.'

entries.zh: 奏可。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: Memorial approved.

entries.zh: 冬，京兆尹王章有罪，下獄死。
entries.en: In winter, Jingzhao Governor Wang Zhang had a crime and was sent to prison where he died.
entries.literal: Winter, Jingzhao Governor Wang Zhang had crime, sent to prison died.

entries.zh: 秋八月乙卯，孝景廟闕災。
entries.en: On Yimao of the eighth month of autumn, the Filial Jing temple gate tower suffered a disaster.
entries.literal: Autumn eighth month Yimao, Filial Jing temple gate tower disaster.

entries.zh: 二月癸丑，詔曰：「朕承太祖鴻業，奉宗廟二十五年，德不能綏理宇內，百姓怨望者眾。
entries.en: On guichou day of the second month, an edict declared: 'I bear the Grand Ancestor's great enterprise, have served the ancestral temples for twenty-five years, my virtue cannot pacify and govern within the domain, and the common people who resent and hope are numerous.
entries.literal: Second month guichou day, edict said: 'I bear Grand Ancestor great enterprise, serve ancestral temples twenty five years, virtue cannot pacify govern within domain, common people resent hope ones numerous.

entries.zh: 不蒙天祐，至今未有繼嗣，天下無所係心。
entries.en: Not receiving heaven's blessing, until now there has been no successor heir, and the empire has nothing to attach its heart to.
entries.literal: Not receive heaven blessing, until now not have successor heir, empire nothing attach heart.

entries.zh: 觀于往古近事之戒，禍亂之萌，皆由斯焉。
entries.en: Observing the warnings of past ancient and recent affairs, the sprouts of calamities and disorders all come from this.
entries.literal: Observe at past ancient recent affairs warnings, calamities disorders sprouts, all from this there.

entries.zh: 定陶王欣於朕為子，慈仁孝順，可以承天序，繼祭祀。
entries.en: Dingtao King Xin is my son, compassionate, benevolent, filial, and obedient, and can bear the heaven's order and continue the sacrifices.
entries.literal: Dingtao King Xin to me is son, compassionate benevolent filial obedient, can bear heaven order, continue sacrifices.

entries.zh: 其立欣為皇太子。
entries.en: Let Xin be established as crown prince.
entries.literal: Let Xin be established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 封中山王舅諫大夫馮參為宜鄉侯，益中山國三萬戶，以慰其意。
entries.en: Enfeoffed Zhongshan King's maternal uncle Remonstrance Grandee Feng Can as Marquis of Yixiang, increased the Zhongshan kingdom by 30,000 households, to console his intention.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Zhongshan King maternal uncle Remonstrance Grandee Feng Can as Yixiang Marquis, increased Zhongshan kingdom 30,000 households, to console his intention.

entries.zh: 賜諸侯王、列侯金，天下當為父後者爵，三老、孝弟力田帛，各有差。」
entries.en: Granted feudal kings and marquises gold, throughout the empire those who should succeed their fathers noble rank, three elders, filial younger brothers and diligent farmers silk, each according to rank.'
entries.literal: Granted feudal lords kings, marquises gold, empire should succeed fathers ones noble rank, three elders, filial younger brothers diligent farmers silk, each had differences.'

entries.zh: 孝哀皇帝，元帝庶孫，定陶恭王子也。
entries.en: Emperor Ai was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.
entries.literal: Emperor Ai (posthumous title Filial-Lamenting) was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.

entries.zh: 母曰丁姬。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Ding.
entries.literal: His mother was named Lady Ding.

entries.zh: 年三歲嗣立為王，長好文辭法律。
entries.en: At the age of three, he succeeded as king, and as he grew up he came to favor literary composition and the study of law.
entries.literal: At age three he succeeded to the throne as king, and when grown he favored literary compositions and laws.

entries.zh: 元延四年入朝，盡從傅、相、中尉。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (9 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyan, he came to court, his tutor, chancellor, and commandant all accompanying him.

entries.zh: 時成帝少弟中山孝王亦來朝，獨從傅。
entries.en: At the same time, Emperor Cheng's younger brother, King Xiao of Zhongshan, also came to court but brought only his tutor.
entries.literal: At this time, Emperor Cheng's younger brother King Xiao of Zhongshan also came to court, bringing only his tutor.

entries.zh: 上怪之，以問定陶王，對曰：「令，諸侯王朝，得從其國二千石。
entries.en: The emperor found this strange and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they are allowed to bring officials ranked at two thousand bushels from their domains.
entries.literal: The emperor was surprised by this and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they may bring officials of two thousand bushels from their fiefs.

entries.zh: 傅、相、中尉皆國二千石，故盡從之。」
entries.en: The tutor, chancellor, and commandant are all two-thousand-bushel officials in my domain, so I brought them all with me.'
entries.literal: The tutor, chancellor, and commandant are all officials of two thousand bushels in the state, so I brought all of them.'

entries.zh: 上令誦詩，通習，能說。
entries.en: The emperor had him recite poetry; he was fluent in it and could explain its meaning.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him to recite poetry; he was fluent and could explain it.

entries.zh: 他日問中山王：「
entries.en: Another day he asked the King of Zhongshan: '
entries.literal: Another day he asked the King of Zhongshan: '

entries.zh: 孝元廟殿門銅龜蛇鋪首鳴。
entries.en: The copper turtle-serpent door knockers on the gate of Emperor Yuan's temple hall rang out.
entries.literal: The copper turtle-snake door knockers on the temple hall gate of Filial Emperor Yuan made sound.

entries.zh: 獨從傅在何法令？」
entries.en: What regulation allows you to bring only your tutor?'
entries.literal: What regulation says you may bring only your tutor?'

entries.zh: 不能對。
entries.en: He was unable to answer.
entries.literal: He could not answer.

entries.zh: 令誦尚書，又廢。
entries.en: He then had him recite from the Book of Documents, but he failed once more.
entries.literal: He ordered him to recite the Book of Documents, but he failed again.

entries.zh: 及賜食於前，後飽；
entries.en: When food was set before him, he ate only after he was already full;
entries.literal: When food was bestowed before him, he ate after becoming full;

entries.zh: 起下，陉係解。
entries.en: When he stood up to leave, his belt came untied.
entries.literal: When he rose to descend, the belt cord came undone.

entries.zh: 成帝由此以為不能，而賢定陶王，數稱其材。
entries.en: From this, Emperor Cheng concluded that the King of Zhongshan was incompetent, but he came to admire the King of Dingtao and often praised his talents.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng thereby considered the King of Zhongshan incapable, but esteemed the King of Dingtao and frequently praised his abilities.

entries.zh: 時王祖母傅太后隨王來朝，私賂遺上所幸趙昭儀及帝舅票騎將軍曲陽侯王根。
entries.en: Meanwhile, the king's grandmother, Empress Dowager Fu, had accompanied him to court and secretly bribed both the emperor's favorite, Consort Zhao, and the emperor's uncle, General Wang Gen, Marquis of Quyang.
entries.literal: At this time, the king's grandmother Empress Dowager Fu accompanied the king to court and privately bribed and gifted the emperor's favored Consort Zhao and the emperor's uncle General of Chariots and Cavalry Marquis Quyang Wang Gen.

entries.zh: 昭儀及根見上亡子，亦欲豫自結為長久計，皆更稱定陶王，勸帝以為嗣。
entries.en: Consort Zhao and Wang Gen, observing that the emperor had no sons, wanted to secure their own long-term interests. They both spoke highly of the King of Dingtao and urged the emperor to name him as heir.
entries.literal: Consort Zhao and Wang Gen, seeing that the emperor had no sons, also wished to secure themselves for the long term, and both spoke favorably of the King of Dingtao, urging the emperor to make him heir.

entries.zh: 成帝亦自美其材，為加元服而遣之，時年十七矣。
entries.en: Emperor Cheng himself admired the young man's talents, performed the coming-of-age capping ceremony for him, and sent him back home. He was seventeen at the time.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng himself admired his abilities, performed the capping ceremony for him, and sent him away; he was then seventeen years old.

entries.zh: 明年，使執金吾任宏守大鴻臚，持節徵定陶王，立為皇太子。
entries.en: The following year, Emperor Cheng sent Colonel Ren Hong, temporarily serving as Grand Herald, to summon the King of Dingtao with imperial credentials and establish him as Crown Prince.
entries.literal: The next year, he sent Colonel of the City Gates Ren Hong, acting as Grand Herald, bearing credentials to summon the King of Dingtao and establish him as Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 謝曰：「臣幸得繼父守藩為諸侯王，材質不足以假充太子之宮。
entries.en: He respectfully declined, saying: 'I am fortunate to have succeeded my father in holding my fief as a feudal king. My talents and character are inadequate to serve even temporarily as Crown Prince.
entries.literal: He declined, saying: 'Your servant has fortunately succeeded his father in guarding the border as a feudal lord king. My abilities and qualities are insufficient to temporarily fill the position of Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 陛下聖德寬仁，敬承祖宗，奉順神祇，宜蒙福祐子孫千億之報。
entries.en: Your Majesty's wisdom and benevolence are boundless. You honor your ancestors and obey the gods, and surely you will be blessed with countless descendants.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's sage virtue is broad and benevolent; reverently continuing the ancestors, complying with the spirits, you should receive blessed protection for your descendants numbering thousands and myriads.

entries.zh: 臣願且得留國邸，旦夕奉問起居，俟有聖嗣，歸國守藩。」
entries.en: I wish only to remain in my residence for now, serving you faithfully by inquiring daily about your well-being, until you have a worthy heir, and then return to guard my domain.'
entries.literal: I wish to remain in my country's residence for now, morning and evening attending to your inquiries about your condition, awaiting a sage heir, then return to my country to guard the border.'

entries.zh: 書奏，天子報聞。
entries.en: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor acknowledged it.
entries.literal: The memorial was presented; the Son of Heaven acknowledged receipt.

entries.zh: 後月餘，立楚孝王孫景為定陶王，奉恭王祀，所以獎厲太子專為後之誼。
entries.en: Over a month later, he installed Jing, grandson of King Xiao of Chu, as King of Dingtao to maintain the sacrifices to King Gong, thereby encouraging the Crown Prince to concentrate solely on securing the succession.
entries.literal: More than a month later, he established King Xiao of Chu's grandson Jing as King of Dingtao to continue King Gong's sacrifices, in order to encourage and exhort the Crown Prince to focus single-mindedly on succession.

entries.zh: 語在外戚傳。
entries.en: The full story is told in the biographies of the imperial relatives.
entries.literal: The account is in the Biographies of the Imperial Affines.

entries.zh: 五月丙戌，立皇后傅氏。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, he installed Lady Fu as empress.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Bingxu, he established Empress Fu.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「春秋『母以子貴』，尊定陶太后曰恭皇太后，丁姬曰恭皇后，各置左右詹事，食邑如長信宮、中宮。」
entries.en: An imperial edict declared: 'As the Spring and Autumn Annals teach, "The mother gains honor through her son." The Empress Dowager of Dingtao shall be honored as Empress Dowager Gong, and Lady Ding as Empress Gong. Each shall have their own attendants, with estates equal to the Changxin Palace and the imperial residence.'
entries.literal: An edict stated: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals say "The mother is honored through the son." Honor the Empress Dowager of Dingtao as Empress Dowager Gong, and Lady Ding as Empress Gong. Each shall have left and right palace attendants established, with fiefs equal to the Changxin Palace and the Central Palace.'

entries.zh: 追尊傅父為崇祖侯、丁父為褒德侯。
entries.en: He granted posthumous honors: Fu's father became Marquis Chongzu, and Ding's father became Marquis Baode.
entries.literal: He posthumously honored Fu's father as Marquis Chongzu, and Ding's father as Marquis Baode.

entries.zh: 封舅丁明為陽安侯，舅子滿為平周侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis of Yang'an, and his maternal uncle's son Man as Marquis of Pingzhou.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis Yang'an, and maternal uncle's son Man as Marquis Pingzhou.

entries.zh: 追諡滿父忠為平周懷侯，皇后父晏為孔鄉侯，皇太后弟侍中光祿大夫趙欽為新成侯。
entries.en: He granted posthumous titles: Marquis Huai of Pingzhou to Man's father Zhong; Marquis Kongxiang to the Empress's father Yan; and Marquis Xincheng to the Empress Dowager's younger brother, Chamberlain Zhao Qin.
entries.literal: He posthumously conferred the title Marquis Huai of Pingzhou on Man's father Zhong; the Empress's father Yan as Marquis Kongxiang; and the Empress Dowager's younger brother Chamberlain for Attendants Gentleman of the Interior Zhao Qin as Marquis Xincheng.

entries.zh: 冬，中山孝王太后媛、弟宜鄉侯馮參有罪，皆自殺。
entries.en: In winter, Empress Dowager Yuan of King Xiao of Zhongshan and her younger brother, Marquis Feng Can of Yixiang, were found guilty and both committed suicide.
entries.literal: In winter, King Xiao of Zhongshan's Empress Dowager Yuan and younger brother Marquis Yixiang Feng Can had crimes; both committed suicide.

entries.zh: 贊曰：孝哀自為藩王及充太子之宮，文辭博敏，幼有令聞。
entries.en: Appraisal: Emperor Ai, from his time as a feudal king to his tenure as Crown Prince, displayed extensive and nimble literary skills, earning an excellent reputation from his youth.
entries.literal: Appraisal says: Filial and Lamented, from being a feudal king and filling the position of Crown Prince, had broad and quick literary compositions, from youth had excellent reputation.

entries.zh: 睹孝成世祿去王室，權柄外移，是故臨朝婁誅大臣，欲彊主威，以則武、宣。
entries.en: Witnessing how in Emperor Cheng's era, hereditary stipends left the imperial family and power shifted to outsiders, he frequently executed ministers upon ascending the throne, seeking to strengthen imperial authority and emulate Emperors Wu and Xuan.
entries.literal: He observed that in the generation of Filial Cheng, emoluments departed from the imperial house, authority shifted outward, therefore upon ascending the throne he frequently executed ministers, desiring to strengthen imperial authority, to follow Wu and Xuan.

entries.zh: 雅性不好聲色，時覽卞射武戲。
entries.en: His refined character showed no interest in music or sensual pleasures; he occasionally enjoyed watching archery contests and martial demonstrations.
entries.literal: His elegant nature did not favor music and sex; he occasionally viewed archery and martial displays.

entries.zh: 即位痿痺，末年寖劇。
entries.en: Upon ascending the throne, he suffered from paralysis; in his later years, the condition steadily deteriorated.
entries.literal: Upon ascending the throne he had flaccid paralysis; in his final years it gradually worsened.

entries.zh: 饗國不永，哀哉！
entries.en: His reign over the nation was brief; alas!
entries.literal: He enjoyed the state not for long; alas!

entries.zh: 楚元王交
entries.en: Chu Yuan King Jiao
entries.literal: Chu Yuan King Jiao

entries.zh: 高帝弟。
entries.en: Younger brother of Emperor Gao
entries.literal: Younger brother of Gao Di

entries.zh: 六年正月丙午立，二十三年薨。
entries.en: Enfeoffed on the Bingwu day of the first month in the sixth year; died after twenty-three years
entries.literal: Established in the sixth year, first month, Bingwu day; died after twenty-three years

entries.zh: 孝文二年，夷王郢客嗣，四年薨。
entries.en: In Emperor Wen's second year, King Yi Yingke succeeded to the throne; died after four years
entries.literal: Xiaowen second year, Yi King Yingke succeeded; died after four years

entries.zh: 六年，王戊嗣，二十一年，孝景三年，反，誅。
entries.en: In the sixth year, King Wu succeeded to the throne; after twenty-one years, in Emperor Jing's third year, he rebelled and was executed
entries.literal: Sixth year, King Wu succeeded; after twenty-one years, Xiaojing third year, rebelled, executed

entries.zh: 城陽孝文二年二月乙卯，景王章以悼惠王子朱虛侯立，二年薨。
entries.en: Chengyang: On the Yimao day of the second month in Emperor Wen's second year, King Jing Zhang was established as Zhu Xu Marquis from the Dao Hui King's line; died after two years
entries.literal: Chengyang: Xiaowen second year second month Yimao day, Jing King Zhang established as Zhu Xu Marquis from Dao Hui King's son; died after two years

entries.zh: 四年，共王喜嗣，八年，徙淮南，四年，復還，凡三十三年薨。
entries.en: In the fourth year, King Gong Xi succeeded to the throne; in the eighth year, he was moved to Huainan, and in the fourth year after that, returned again; he died after a total of thirty-three years
entries.literal: Fourth year, Gong King Xi succeeded; eighth year, moved to Huainan, fourth year, returned again, total thirty-three years died

entries.zh: 孝景後元年，頃王延嗣，二十六年薨。
entries.en: In the first year of the Xiaojing Hou period, King Qing Yan succeeded to the throne; died after twenty-six years
entries.literal: Xiaojing Hou first year, Qing King Yan succeeded; died after twenty-six years

entries.zh: 元狩六年，敬王義嗣，九年薨。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yuanshou, King Jing Yi succeeded to the throne; died after nine years
entries.literal: Yuanshou sixth year, Jing King Yi succeeded; died after nine years

entries.zh: 元封三年，惠王武嗣，十一年薨。
entries.en: In the third year of Yuanfeng, King Hui Wu succeeded to the throne; died after eleven years
entries.literal: Yuanfeng third year, Hui King Wu succeeded; died after eleven years

entries.zh: 天漢四年，荒王順嗣，四十六年薨。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tianhan, King Huang Shun succeeded to the throne; died after forty-six years
entries.literal: Tianhan fourth year, Huang King Shun succeeded; died after forty-six years

entries.zh: 梁孝王武
entries.en: Liang Xiao King Wu
entries.literal: Liang Xiao King Wu

entries.zh: 文帝子。
entries.en: Son of Emperor Wen
entries.literal: Wen Di's son

entries.zh: 二月乙卯，立為代王，三年，徙為淮陽王，十年，徙梁，三十五年薨。
entries.en: On the Yimao day of the second month, he was established as Dai King; in the third year, he was moved to become Huaiyang King; in the tenth year, he was moved to Liang, and died after thirty-five years
entries.literal: Second month Yimao day, established as Dai King; third year, moved to become Huaiyang King; tenth year, moved to Liang, died after thirty-five years

entries.zh: 孝景後元年，恭王買嗣，七年薨。
entries.en: In the first year of the Xiaojing Hou period, King Gong Mai succeeded to the throne; died after seven years
entries.literal: Xiaojing Hou first year, Gong King Mai succeeded; died after seven years

entries.zh: 建元五年，平王襄嗣，四十年薨。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jianyuan, King Ping Xiang succeeded to the throne; died after forty years
entries.literal: Jianyuan fifth year, Ping King Xiang succeeded; died after forty years

entries.zh: 太始元年，貞王毋傷嗣，十一年薨。
entries.en: In the first year of Taishi, King Zhen Wushang succeeded to the throne; died after eleven years
entries.literal: Taishi first year, Zhen King Wushang succeeded; died after eleven years

entries.zh: 始元二年，敬王定國嗣，四十年薨。
entries.en: In the second year of Shiyuan, King Jing Dingguo succeeded to the throne; died after forty years
entries.literal: Shiyuan second year, Jing King Dingguo succeeded; died after forty years

entries.zh: 初元四年，夷王遂嗣，六年薨。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Chuyuan, King Yi Sui succeeded to the throne; died after six years
entries.literal: Chuyuan fourth year, Yi King Sui succeeded; died after six years

entries.zh: 永光五年，荒王嘉嗣，十五年薨。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Yongguang, King Huang Jia succeeded to the throne; died after fifteen years
entries.literal: Yongguang fifth year, Huang King Jia succeeded; died after fifteen years

entries.zh: 八世陽朔元年，王立嗣，二十七年，元始三年，有罪，廢，徙漢中，自殺。元始五年二月丁酉，王音以孝王玄孫之曾孫紹封，五年，王莽篡位，貶為公，明年廢。
entries.en: In the first year of Yangshuo of the eighth generation, King Li succeeded to the throne; in the twenty-seventh year, during the third year of Yuanshi, he was found guilty of a crime, abolished as king, exiled to Hanzhong, and committed suicide. On the Dingyou day of the second month in the fifth year of Yuanshi, King Yin succeeded as the great-grandson of Xiao King Xuansun; in the fifth year, Wang Mang usurped the throne, demoted him to duke, and abolished the kingdom the following year
entries.literal: Eighth generation Yangshuo first year, King Li succeeded; twenty-seventh year, Yuanshi third year, guilty of crime, abolished, moved to Hanzhong, committed suicide. Yuanshi fifth year second month Dingyou day, King Yin succeeded as Xiao King Xuansun's great-grandson; fifth year, Wang Mang usurped the throne, demoted to duke, next year abolished

entries.zh: 濟川孝景中六年五月丙戌，王明以孝王子桓邑侯立，七年，建元三年，坐殺中傅，廢遷房陵。
entries.en: Jichuan: On the Bingxu day of the fifth month in the middle sixth year of Emperor Jing, King Ming was established as Huanyi Marquis from the Xiao King's line; in the seventh year, during the third year of Jianyuan, he was convicted of killing the imperial tutor, abolished as king, and exiled to Fangling
entries.literal: Jichuan: Xiaojing middle sixth year fifth month Bingxu day, King Ming established as Huanyi Marquis from Xiao King's son; seventh year, Jianyuan third year, convicted of killing the tutor, abolished and moved to Fangling

entries.zh: 濟東五月丙戌，王彭離以孝王子立，二十九年，坐殺人，廢遷上庸。
entries.en: Jidong: On the Bingxu day of the fifth month, King Pengli was established from the Xiao King's line; in the twenty-ninth year, he was convicted of murder, abolished as king, and exiled to Shangyong
entries.literal: Jidong: Fifth month Bingxu day, King Pengli established from Xiao King's son; twenty-ninth year, convicted of murder, abolished and moved to Shangyong

entries.zh: 山陽五月丙戌，哀王定以孝王子立，九年薨，亡後。
entries.en: Shanyang: On the Bingxu day of the fifth month, King Ai Ding was established from the Xiao King's line; died after nine years with no heir
entries.literal: Shanyang: Fifth month Bingxu day, Ai King Ding established from Xiao King's son; died after nine years, no heir

entries.zh: 濟陰五月丙戌，哀王不識以孝王子立，二年薨，亡後。
entries.en: Jiyin: On the Bingxu day of the fifth month, King Ai Bushi was established from the Xiao King's line; died after two years with no heir
entries.literal: Jiyin: Fifth month Bingxu day, Ai King Bushi established from Xiao King's son; died after two years, no heir

entries.zh: 昔周監於二代，三聖制法，立爵五等，封國八百，同姓五十有餘。
entries.en: In ancient times, the Zhou observed the Xia and Shang dynasties. Three sages established laws, creating five ranks of nobility and enfeoffing eight hundred states, with over fifty bearing the same surname.
entries.literal: In ancient times the Zhou observed the Xia and Shang, three sages established laws, set up five ranks of nobility, enfeoffed eight hundred states, with over fifty of the same surname.

entries.zh: 周公、康叔建於魯、衛，各數百里；
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou and Duke Kang were established in Lu and Wei, each several hundred li in size;
entries.literal: Zhou Gong and Kang Shu were established in Lu and Wei, each several hundred li;

entries.zh: 太公於齊，亦五侯九伯之地。
entries.en: The Grand Duke in Qi also held territory equivalent to five marquises and nine earls.
entries.literal: Tai Gong in Qi was also the territory of five marquises and nine earls.

entries.zh: 詩載其制曰：「介人惟藩，大師惟垣。
entries.en: The Book of Poetry records their system: 'The great men serve as the screen, the Grand Master as the wall.
entries.literal: The Poetry records their system: 'The great men are the screen, the Grand Master is the wall.

entries.zh: 大邦惟屏，大宗惟翰。
entries.en: The great states serve as the screen, the great lineage as the pillar.
entries.literal: The great states are the screen, the great lineage is the pillar.

entries.zh: 懷德惟寧，宗子惟城。
entries.en: Cherishing virtue brings peace, the lineage sons serve as the ramparts.
entries.literal: Cherishing virtue brings peace, the lineage sons are the ramparts.

entries.zh: 母俾城壞，毋獨斯畏。」
entries.en: Do not let the ramparts crumble; do not stand alone in fear.'
entries.literal: Do not let the ramparts crumble, do not stand alone in fear.'

entries.zh: 所以親親賢賢，褒表功德，關諸盛衰，深根固本，為不可拔者也。
entries.en: This served to favor relatives and honor the worthy, to praise and display meritorious deeds, connecting it to prosperity and decline, deeply rooting and solidifying the foundation, making it unshakeable.
entries.literal: This was to favor relatives and honor the worthy, to praise and display meritorious virtue, related to prosperity and decline, to deeply root and solidify the foundation, making it unremovable.

entries.zh: 故盛則周、邵相其治，致刑錯；
entries.en: Therefore in times of prosperity, Zhou and Shao assisted in governance, leading to the laying aside of punishments;
entries.literal: Therefore in prosperity Zhou and Shao assisted in governing, bringing about the laying aside of punishments;

entries.zh: 衰則五伯扶其弱，與共守。
entries.en: In times of decline, the five hegemons supported its weakness and guarded it together.
entries.literal: in decline the five hegemons supported its weakness and guarded it together.

entries.zh: 自幽、平之後，日以陵夷，至虖阨挢河洛之間，分為二周，有逃責之臺，被竊鈇之言。
entries.en: After Kings You and Ping, it declined day by day, until it was confined between the Yellow River and Luo River, divided into two Zhou states, with the Terrace of Evading Responsibility, suffering the reproach of the stolen axe.
entries.literal: After King You and King Ping, day by day it declined, until it was cramped between the Yellow River and Luo River, divided into two Zhou, with the Terrace of Fleeing Responsibility, suffering the words of the stolen axe.

entries.zh: 然天下謂之共主，彊大弗之敢傾。
entries.en: Yet the world still regarded it as the common ruler, and even the powerful dared not overthrow it.
entries.literal: Yet the world called it the common lord, and the powerful did not dare overthrow it.

entries.zh: 歷載八百餘年，數極德盡，既於王赧，降為庶人，用天年終。
entries.en: It lasted over eight hundred years, its mandate exhausted and virtue depleted, until King Nan descended to commoner status and died a natural death.
entries.literal: It lasted over eight hundred years, its mandate exhausted and virtue depleted, until King Nan, who descended to commoner status and ended with a natural lifespan.

entries.zh: 號位已絕於天下，尚猶枝葉相持，莫得居其虛位，海內無主，三十餘年。
entries.en: Its title and position were already extinguished from the world, yet like branches and leaves supporting each other, none could occupy its empty throne, leaving the realm without a master for over thirty years.
entries.literal: Its title and position already extinguished from the world, yet branches and leaves still supported each other, none could occupy its empty position, the realm had no master for over thirty years.

entries.zh: 號諡
entries.en: Titles and Posthumous Names
entries.literal: Titles and Posthumous Names

entries.zh: 屬
entries.en: Branch/Category
entries.literal: Category/branch

entries.en: First Enfeoffed
entries.literal: Initially enfeoffed

entries.zh: 子
entries.en: Son
entries.literal: Son

entries.zh: 孫
entries.en: Grandson
entries.literal: Grandson

entries.zh: 曾孫
entries.en: Great-grandson
entries.literal: Great-grandson

entries.zh: 玄孫
entries.en: Great-great-grandson
entries.literal: Great-great-grandson

entries.zh: 六世
entries.en: Sixth Generation
entries.literal: Sixth generation

entries.zh: 七世
entries.en: Seventh Generation
entries.literal: Seventh generation

entries.zh: 傳曰：譬如堯舜，禹、稷、镨與之為善則行，鯀、讙兜欲與為惡則誅。
entries.en: As the Tradition says: take Yao and Shun. When Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing what was right, those policies were put into effect; when Gun and Huan Dou sought to join them in wrongdoing, they were punished to death.
entries.literal: The Tradition says: For example, with Yao and Shun, when Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing good, it was carried out; when Gun and Huan Dou wished to join them in doing evil, they were executed.

entries.zh: 可與為善，不可與為惡，是謂上智。
entries.en: To be able to cooperate in good but never in evil: this is what is called highest wisdom.
entries.literal: One can act in goodness with them, but cannot act in evil with them - this is called highest wisdom.

entries.zh: 桀紂，龍逢、比干欲與之為善則誅，于莘、崇侯與之為惡則行。
entries.en: By contrast, with Jie and Zhou, Long Feng and Bi Gan were executed for trying to do what was right with them, while Yu Xin and the Marquis of Chong were followed when they proposed evil.
entries.literal: As for Jie and Zhou, when Long Feng and Bi Gan wished to do good with them, they were executed; when Yu Xin and the Marquis of Chong did evil with them, it was carried out.

entries.zh: 可與為惡，不可與為善，是謂下愚。
entries.en: To be capable only of joining in evil, never in good: this is what is called utter folly.
entries.literal: One can act in evil with them, but cannot act in goodness with them - this is called lowest foolishness.

entries.zh: 齊桓公，管仲相之則霸，豎貂輔之則亂。
entries.en: Duke Huan of Qi became hegemon when Guan Zhong was his minister, but fell into disorder when Shu Diao aided him.
entries.literal: As for Duke Huan of Qi, when Guan Zhong assisted him, he became hegemon; when Shu Diao aided him, there was disorder.

entries.zh: 可與為善，可與為惡，是謂中人。
entries.en: Those who can join either good or evil are what we call people of the middle rank.
entries.literal: One can act in goodness with them, and can act in evil with them - this is called the middle type of people.

entries.zh: 因茲以列九等之序，究極經傳，繼世相次，總備古今之略要云。
entries.en: On this basis, I set out a sequence of nine grades, tracing the classics and commentaries as far as possible, arranging each generation in order, and providing in sum a concise outline of notable figures from ancient to later times.
entries.literal: Accordingly, based on this, the order of nine grades is arranged, the classics and commentaries are exhaustively examined, generations are linked in sequence, and in sum the essential outline of antiquity and the present is prepared.

entries.zh: 張晏曰：「老子玄默，仲尼所師，雖不在聖，要為大賢，文伯之母達於禮典，動為聖人所歎，言為後世所則，而在第四。田單以即墨孤城復強齊之大，魯連之博通，忽於榮利，藺子申威秦王，退讓廉頗，乃在第五。大姬巫怪，好祭鬼神，陳人化之，國多淫祀，寺人孟子違於大雅，以保其身，旣被宮刑，怨刺而作，乃在第三。嫪毐上烝，昬亂禮度，惡不忍聞，乃在第七。其餘差違紛錯不少，略舉揚較，以起失謬。獨馳騖於數千歲之中，旁觀諸子，事業未究，而尋遇竇氏之難，使之然乎？」
entries.en: Zhang Yan said, "Laozi was deep and silent, and Confucius regarded him as a teacher. Though not ranked among sages, he surely counts as a great worthy. Wenbo's mother mastered the ritual classics; the sage praised her conduct and later ages took her words as a model—yet she appears in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored great Qi from the isolated city of Jimo; Lu Lian was broadly learned yet disdained fame and profit; Lord Lin awed the King of Qin and yielded to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced sorcery and loved sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state was full of improper cults. The eunuch Mengzi, turning from the great elegant style to preserve himself—after castration, wrote in resentment—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest at court and threw ritual order into chaos, in deeds too foul to bear hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Discrepancies and errors are many; I have cited a few to expose the faults. Did he gallop alone across thousands of years, looking on at the various masters while his work remained unfinished, then soon meet the Dou family's disaster—and did that make it turn out this way?"
entries.literal: Zhang Yan said: "Laozi was profound and reticent, and Confucius took him as teacher. Though not among the sages, he ought to count as a great worthy. The mother of Wenbo was versed in ritual classics; her conduct won the sage's praise and her words became a model for later ages—yet she is placed in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored mighty Qi from the lone fortress of Jimo; Lu Lian was broadly learned yet scorned glory and gain; Lord Lin intimidated the King of Qin and yielded ground to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced witchcraft and delighted in sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state abounded in licentious worship. The eunuch Mengzi, departing from great elegance to preserve his person—after suffering castration, wrote in resentment and censure—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest with the sovereign, befouling ritual norms in ways too vile to endure hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Other discrepancies and errors are numerous; I have raised a few for comparison to expose the mistakes. Did he rush alone through thousands of years, observing the various masters while his work remained incomplete, then soon encounter the Dou family's calamity—which made it come out this way?"

entries.zh: 師古曰：「六家之論，輕重不同；百行所存，趣拾難壹。張氏輒申所見，掎摭班史，然其所論，又自差錯。且年代乆遠，墳典隟亡，學者舛駮，師論分異，是以表載古人名氏，或與諸書不同。今則特有發明，用暢厥旨。自女媧以下，帝鴻以前，諸子傳記，互有舛駮，敘說不同，無所取正，大要知其古帝之號而已。諸人士見於史傳，彰灼可知者，無待解釋，其間幽昧者，時復及焉。」
entries.en: Yan Shigu said, "The six schools' doctrines differ in what they value; the conduct preserved across the hundred practices is hard to gather into one standard. Master Zhang then set forth his own views, picking at Ban Gu's history—yet his arguments are themselves mistaken. Moreover, the ages are distant, canonical texts have gaps and losses, scholars contradict one another, and teachers' explanations diverge; for this reason the names recorded in the table may differ from other books. Here I add explanations of my own to make the meaning clear. From Nüwa down to before Emperor Hong, the various masters' records conflict and their accounts differ, with no way to decide which is right; in general one need only know the designations of the ancient emperors. Persons who appear in historical records and are plainly identifiable need no commentary; where matters are obscure, I sometimes explain them."
entries.literal: Yan Shigu said: "The theories of the six schools differ in what they weigh heavily or lightly; the conduct preserved in the hundred practices is hard to reduce to a single standard. Master Zhang thereupon stated his own views, picking at Ban's history—yet what he argued is itself full of errors. Moreover, the ages are remote and canonical texts are lost in the gaps; scholars contradict one another and teachers' doctrines diverge—for this reason the names recorded in the table may differ from other books. Here I offer special explanations to clarify the intent. From Nüwa downward to before Emperor Hong, the various masters' records contradict one another and their accounts differ, with no basis for deciding which is correct; in general one need only know the ancient emperors' designations. Persons visible in historical records who are clearly identifiable need no explanation; where matters are obscure, I occasionally address them."

entries.zh: 自書契之作，先民可得而聞者，經傳所稱，唐虞以上，帝王有號諡。
entries.en: From the time writing was first made, what we can still know of the ancients through the Classics and their commentaries is this: for the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier, rulers bore formal titles and posthumous names.
entries.literal: Since the making of written records, what can be heard of the men of old, as named in the classics and commentaries, from Tang and Yu upward, is that emperors and kings had titles and posthumous names.

entries.zh: 輔佐不可得而稱矣，而諸子頗言之，雖不考虖孔氏，然猶著在篇籍，歸乎顯善昭惡，勸戒後人，故博采焉。
entries.en: The ministers and aides who supported those rulers cannot all be fully identified. Still, the various philosophical writings discuss many of them. Even where these accounts cannot be fully confirmed by the Confucian tradition, they remain preserved in the texts and serve a common purpose: to display virtue, expose wrongdoing, and admonish later generations. For that reason, they are broadly collected here.
entries.literal: As for those who assisted and supported them, they cannot be fully named; yet the various masters speak of them somewhat. Though not all can be verified by the Confucian school, they are still recorded in written texts, and all return to making good manifest, making evil clear, exhorting and warning later people; therefore they are broadly collected here.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？」
entries.en: Confucius said, "As for claiming sagehood and perfect benevolence, how could I dare?"
entries.literal: Confucius said: "As for being sage and benevolent, how would I dare?"

entries.zh: 又曰：「何事於仁，必也聖乎！」
entries.en: He also said, "Why speak only of benevolence? One must reach sagehood!"
entries.literal: He also said: "Why speak only of benevolence? It must be sagehood!"

entries.zh: 「未知，焉得仁？」
entries.en: He also said, "If one does not yet understand, how can one possess benevolence?"
entries.literal: He also said: "If one does not yet know, how can one attain benevolence?"

entries.zh: 「生而知之者，上也；
entries.en: "Those born already knowing stand at the top;
entries.literal: "Those who know by birth are highest;

entries.zh: 學而知之者，次也；
entries.en: those who come to knowledge through study are next;
entries.literal: those who learn and then know are next;

entries.zh: 困而學之，又其次也；
entries.en: those who learn under hardship come next;
entries.literal: those who are troubled and then learn are again next;

entries.zh: 困而不學，民斯為下矣。」
entries.en: and those who suffer hardship yet refuse to learn are the lowest of all."
entries.literal: those who are troubled and yet do not learn - among the people, these are the lowest."

entries.zh: 又曰：「中人以上，可以語上也。」
entries.en: He also said, "With people of average ability and above, one can discuss what is higher."
entries.literal: He also said: "With those of middle level and above, one may speak of higher things."

entries.zh: 「唯上智與下愚不移。」
entries.en: "Only the supremely wise and the utterly foolish cannot be changed."
entries.literal: "Only the highest wisdom and the lowest foolishness do not change."

entries.zh: 上上聖人
entries.en: Highest grade: sages
entries.literal: Upper-upper: sages

entries.zh: 上中仁人
entries.en: Second highest grade: men of benevolence
entries.literal: Upper-middle: benevolent men

entries.zh: 上下智人
entries.en: Third grade: men of wisdom
entries.literal: Upper-lower: wise men

entries.zh: 中上
entries.en: Middle grade, upper tier
entries.literal: Middle-upper

entries.zh: 中中
entries.en: Middle grade, middle tier
entries.literal: Middle-middle

entries.zh: 中下
entries.en: Middle grade, lower tier
entries.literal: Middle-lower

entries.zh: 下上
entries.en: Lower grade, upper tier
entries.literal: Lower-upper

entries.zh: 下中
entries.en: Lower grade, middle tier
entries.literal: Lower-middle

entries.zh: 下下愚人
entries.en: Lowest grade: the foolish
entries.literal: Lower-lower: foolish men

entries.zh: 自書契之作，先民可得而聞者，經傳所稱，唐虞以上，帝王有號謚。
entries.en: From the time writing first appeared, what the classics and commentaries preserve about the earliest ages is that rulers from the era of Yao and Shun and earlier were remembered with formal titles and posthumous names.
entries.literal: Since the creation of writing, what can be heard of the former people, as named in the classics and commentaries, from the age of Yao and Shun upward, is that emperors and kings had titles and posthumous names.

entries.zh: 輔佐不可得而稱矣，而諸子頗言之，雖不考虖孔氏，然猶著在篇籍，歸乎顯善昭惡，勸戒後人，故博采焉。
entries.en: The chief ministers who aided those rulers cannot all be securely identified. Still, the various philosophical writings speak of them. Even when such accounts are not confirmed by the Confucian canon, they remain in the textual record and serve to highlight virtue, expose wrongdoing, and admonish later generations, so I have gathered them widely.
entries.literal: Their assistants and supporters cannot be fully named. Yet the various masters discuss them somewhat; although these accounts are not verified by the Confucian tradition, they are still recorded in writings, and their purpose returns to making good manifest and evil clear, exhorting and warning later people, therefore I have collected them broadly.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？」
entries.en: Confucius said, "If you speak of sageliness and perfect benevolence, I would not presume to claim them."
entries.literal: Confucius said: "As for being sage and benevolent, how could I dare claim that?"

entries.zh: 又曰：「何事於仁，必也聖乎！」
entries.en: He also said, "Why speak only of benevolence? One would have to reach sagehood."
entries.literal: He also said: "How could one stop at benevolence? It would have to be sagehood!"

entries.zh: 「未知，焉得仁？」
entries.en: "Without understanding, how could one realize true benevolence?"
entries.literal: "If one does not yet know, how can one attain benevolence?"

entries.zh: 「生而知之者，上也；
entries.en: "Those born with knowledge are the highest type;
entries.literal: "Those who know from birth are the highest;

entries.zh: 學而知之者，又其次也；
entries.en: those who gain knowledge through study come next;
entries.literal: those who know through learning are next;

entries.zh: 困而不學，民斯為下矣。」
entries.en: and those who face difficulty yet refuse to learn are the lowest among the people."
entries.literal: those who are troubled yet do not learn, among the people these are the lowest."

entries.zh: 又曰：「中人以上，可以語上也。」
entries.en: He also said, "With people above the middle level, you can discuss higher teachings."
entries.literal: He also said: "With those above the middle grade, one may speak of higher things."

entries.zh: 「唯上智與下愚不移。」
entries.en: "Only those of the highest wisdom and the deepest folly are unchangeable."
entries.literal: "Only the highest wisdom and the lowest stupidity do not change."

entries.zh: 傳曰：譬如堯舜，禹、稷、禼與之為善則行，鮌、讙兜欲與為惡則誅。
entries.en: As the Tradition says: take Yao and Shun. When Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing what was right, it was carried out; when Gun and Huan Dou sought to join them in wrongdoing, they were executed.
entries.literal: The Tradition says: For example, with Yao and Shun, when Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing good, it was carried out; when Gun and Huan Dou wished to join them in doing evil, they were executed.

entries.zh: 可與為善，不可與為惡，是謂上智。
entries.en: To be able to cooperate in good but never in evil—that is what is called highest wisdom.
entries.literal: One can join them in doing good, but cannot join them in doing evil; this is called highest wisdom.

entries.zh: 桀紂，龍逢、比干欲與之為善則誅，于莘、崇侯與之為惡則行。
entries.en: By contrast, with Jie and Zhou, Long Feng and Bi Gan were executed for trying to do what was right with them, while Yuxin and the Marquis of Chong were followed when they proposed evil.
entries.literal: As for Jie and Zhou, when Long Feng and Bi Gan wished to join them in doing good, they were executed; when Yuxin and the Marquis of Chong joined them in doing evil, it was carried out.

entries.zh: 可與為惡，不可與為善，是謂下愚。
entries.en: To be capable only of joining in evil, never in good—that is what is called utter folly.
entries.literal: One can join them in doing evil, but cannot join them in doing good; this is called lowest stupidity.

entries.zh: 齊桓公，管仲相之則霸，竪貂輔之則亂。
entries.en: Duke Huan of Qi became hegemon when Guan Zhong served as his minister, but fell into disorder when Shu Diao assisted him.
entries.literal: As for Duke Huan of Qi, when Guan Zhong served as his minister, he became hegemon; when Shu Diao assisted him, there was disorder.

entries.zh: 可與為善，可與為惡，是謂中人。
entries.en: Those with whom one can cooperate in either good or evil are what is called the middle type.
entries.literal: One can join them in doing good and can join them in doing evil; this is called the middle type.

entries.zh: 因茲以列九等之序，究極經傳，繼世相次，緫備古今之略要云。
entries.en: On this basis, I set out a nine-rank order, drawing fully from the classics and commentaries, tracing each age in sequence, and assembling a concise outline of key figures from antiquity to later times.
entries.literal: Accordingly I arranged the sequence of nine grades, exhausting the classics and commentaries, following generations in succession, and in sum providing the essentials of antiquity and the present.

entries.zh: 〈師古曰：「但次古人而不表今人者，其書未畢故也。」〉
entries.en: 〈As Yan Shigu notes: "It lists only figures of antiquity and not contemporaries because this work was left unfinished."〉
entries.literal: 〈Yan Shigu says: "The reason it only arranges ancient people and does not chart present people is that the book was not yet finished."〉

entries.zh: 周道衰，法度颦，至齊桓公任用管仲，而國富民安。
entries.en: As Zhou order eroded, Qi's reform under Guan Zhong restored wealth and stability.
entries.literal: When Zhou declined and norms wrinkled, Duke Huan of Qi employed Guan Zhong, and the state became wealthy and the people secure.

entries.zh: 公問行伯用師之道，管仲曰：「公欲定卒伍，修甲兵，大國亦將修之，而小國設備，則難以速得志矣。」
entries.en: The duke asked about the way to pursue hegemony through military force. Guan Zhong said: 'If Your Grace wishes to organize the ranks and prepare armor and weapons, the great states will also prepare theirs, and the small states will set up defenses. Then it will be hard to achieve your aim quickly.'
entries.literal: The duke asked about hegemony by military means. Guan Zhong said: 'If Your Grace wishes to fix ranks and repair armor and weapons, great states will also repair theirs, and small states will ready defenses, so quick success will be hard.'

entries.zh: 於是乃作內政而寓軍令焉，故卒伍定虖里，而軍政成虖郊。
entries.en: He embedded military organization within civil administration, creating readiness without provoking immediate counter-mobilization.
entries.literal: So he made internal governance and lodged military command within it; thus ranks were fixed in the villages and military administration completed in suburbs.

entries.zh: 連其什伍，居處同樂，死生同憂，禍福共之，故夜戰則其聲相聞，晝戰則其目相見，緩急足以相死。
entries.en: By tightly integrating local units into shared daily life, he produced battlefield cohesion and mutual commitment under stress.
entries.literal: He linked tens and fives so they lived and rejoiced together, shared sorrow in life and death, and shared fortune and misfortune. Thus in night battle they heard one another, in day battle saw one another, and in emergencies could die for one another.

entries.zh: 其教已成，外攘夷狄，內尊天子，以安諸夏。
entries.en: Once internal discipline matured, Qi could defend frontiers, uphold royal legitimacy, and secure the central states.
entries.literal: With this training complete, he repelled barbarians abroad, honored the Son of Heaven within, and stabilized the Huaxia states.

entries.zh: 齊威既沒，晉文接之，亦先定其民，作被廬之法，總帥諸侯，迭為盟主。
entries.en: Jin's Duke Wen continued the model: domestic consolidation first, then interstate leadership.
entries.literal: After Qi's prestige declined, Duke Wen of Jin followed, first settling his people, creating the Bilu system, commanding the lords and alternating as hegemon.

entries.zh: 然其禮已頗僭差，又隨時苟合以求欲速之功，故不能充王制。
entries.en: But hegemonic politics remained institutionally compromised and short-term, never achieving true kingly order.
entries.literal: Yet their rites were already somewhat usurping and uneven; they also made expedient compromises for quick gains, so they could not fulfill kingly institutions.

entries.zh: 二伯之後，寖以陵夷，至魯成公作丘甲，哀公用田賦，搜狩治兵大閱之事皆失其正。
entries.en: Post-hegemonic states distorted older military-ritual norms into ad hoc extraction and display.
entries.literal: After the two hegemons, decline deepened: by Duke Cheng of Lu creating qiu-armor and Duke Ai using field levy, military hunts and grand reviews all lost correctness.

entries.zh: 春秋書而譏之，以存王道。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals condemned these practices to preserve the normative ideal.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn records and criticizes this, to preserve kingly way.

entries.zh: 於是師旅亟動，百姓罷敝，無伏節死難之誼。
entries.en: Frequent campaigning wore down the populace and eroded sacrificial civic ethos.
entries.literal: Thus armies moved repeatedly and the people were exhausted, lacking loyalty to die for duty and hardship.

entries.zh: 孔子傷焉，曰：「以不教民戰，是謂棄之。」
entries.en: Confucius lamented it, saying: 'To send the people to war without teaching them is to abandon them.'
entries.literal: Confucius lamented it, saying: 'To send the people to war without teaching them is to abandon them.'

entries.zh: 春秋之後，滅弱吞小，並為戰國，稍增講武之禮，以為戲樂，用相夸視。
entries.en: In the Warring States era, military ritual became spectacle and competitive display.
entries.literal: After the Spring and Autumn, strong destroyed weak and swallowed small, becoming the Warring States; they gradually increased martial display rites as amusements for mutual boasting.

entries.zh: 而秦更名角抵，先王之禮沒於淫樂中矣。
entries.en: By Qin, old ritual forms had been recast as entertainments, their normative substance lost.
entries.literal: Qin then renamed it jiaodi; former kings' rites were submerged in licentious entertainment.

entries.zh: 雄桀之士因勢輔時，作為權詐以相傾覆，吳有孫武，齊有孫臏，魏有吳起，秦有商鞅，皆禽敵立勝，垂著篇籍。
entries.en: Strategists such as Sun Wu, Sun Bin, Wu Qi, and Shang Yang turned military thought toward power and deception, with influential textual legacies.
entries.literal: Heroic and ruthless men, taking advantage of the age, made power techniques and deception to overturn one another: Wu had Sun Wu, Qi had Sun Bin, Wei had Wu Qi, Qin had Shang Yang-all captured enemies and secured victories, leaving written works.

entries.zh: 當此之時，合從連衡，轉相攻伐，代為雌雄。
entries.en: Alliance blocs constantly realigned, producing perpetual competitive warfare.
entries.literal: At this time, vertical and horizontal alliances formed; states attacked each other in rotation, taking turns as strong and weak.

entries.zh: 齊愍以技擊彊，魏惠以武卒奮，秦昭以銳士勝。
entries.en: King Min of Qi drew strength from skilled fighters, King Hui of Wei rose through elite troops, and King Zhao of Qin prevailed through crack soldiers.
entries.literal: Qi Min relied on technical fighters for strength, Wei Hui on martial graduates for vigor, Qin Zhao on elite troops for victory.

entries.zh: 世方爭於功利，而馳說者以孫、吳為宗。
entries.en: With utility dominant, military discourse canonized the Sun-Wu tradition.
entries.literal: As the age contended over profit and utility, persuasive theorists took Sun and Wu as their lineage.

entries.zh: 時唯孫卿明於王道，而非之曰：「彼孫、吳者，上勢利而貴變詐；
entries.en: Only Xunzi was clear on the kingly way and criticized them, saying: 'Those Sun and Wu strategists esteem advantage and prize changing deception;
entries.literal: Only Xunzi was clear on the kingly way and criticized them, saying: 'Those Sun and Wu strategists esteem advantage and prize changing deception;

entries.zh: 施於暴亂昏嫚之國，君臣有間，上下離心，政謀不良，故可變而詐也。
entries.en: Such methods work only in already disordered polities fractured by distrust and poor governance.
entries.literal: Applied in violent, chaotic, and insolent states where ruler and minister are estranged and upper and lower are divided, with bad policy planning, therefore one can rely on change and deception.

entries.zh: 夫仁人在上，為下所卬，猶子弟之衛父兄，若手足之扞頭目，何可當也？
entries.en: Under genuine benevolent authority, social cohesion resembles familial protection; such a polity is not easily defeated.
entries.literal: If a benevolent person is above and is looked up to below, as younger kin protect fathers and elder brothers, as hands and feet defend head and eyes-how could he be withstood?

entries.zh: 鄰國望我，歡若親戚，芬若椒蘭，顧視其上，猶焚灼仇讎。
entries.en: If we govern well, neighbors are drawn to us warmly, while resenting their own oppressive rulers.
entries.literal: Neighboring states look upon us with joy as kin, fragrant as pepper and orchid; yet when they look at their own rulers, it is as burning enemies.

entries.zh: 人情豈肯為其所惡而攻其所好哉？
entries.en: People do not willingly fight for what they detest against what they admire.
entries.literal: Would human feeling ever willingly attack what it likes on behalf of what it hates?

entries.zh: 故以桀攻桀，猶有巧拙；
entries.en: Even tyrant-against-tyrant conflict leaves room for tactical skill;
entries.literal: Therefore when tyrants attack tyrants, there is still skill and clumsiness;

entries.zh: 以桀詐堯，若卵投石，夫何幸之有！
entries.en: But trying to defeat true sage rule by trickery is like hurling an egg at rock.
entries.literal: But when a tyrant deceives Yao, it is like throwing an egg at stone—how could there be any lucky outcome!

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：『武王載旆，有虔秉鉞，如火烈烈，則莫我敢遏。』
entries.en: As the Odes describes King Wu's campaign, moral legitimacy generated unstoppable force.
entries.literal: The Odes says: 'King Wu raised his banners, reverently grasped the axe, blazing like fire-none dared block us.

entries.zh: 言以仁誼綏民者，無敵於天下也。
entries.en: Rule grounded in benevolence and justice is strategically unmatched.
entries.literal: This says that one who pacifies people with benevolence and righteousness has no enemy under heaven.

entries.zh: 若齊之技擊，得一首則受賜金。
entries.en: Qi incentivized shock troops through cash-for-head rewards.
entries.literal: For Qi's technical fighters, obtaining one head brought a reward in gold.

entries.zh: 事小敵鲧，則媮可用也；
entries.en: Such troops may work against minor opponents;
entries.literal: Against small and weak enemies, this may be usable by opportunists;

entries.zh: 事鉅敵堅，則渙然離矣。
entries.en: But against strong adversaries they quickly disintegrate.
entries.literal: Against great and firm enemies, they scatter apart.

entries.zh: 是亡國之兵也。
entries.en: That is a military model fit for state collapse.
entries.literal: This is the army of a doomed state.

entries.zh: 魏氏武卒，衣三屬之甲，操十二石之弩，負矢五十丢，置戈其上，冠冑帶劍，贏三日之糧，日中而趨百里，中試則復其戶，利其田宅。
entries.en: Wei's elite infantry were heavily equipped and physically tested, then compensated through tax and property privileges.
entries.literal: Wei's martial graduates wore triple-layer armor, handled twelve-stone crossbows, carried fifty arrows, set halberds atop loads, with helmets and swords, carrying three days' grain, and could march one hundred li by noon; if they passed tests, their household obligations were remitted and their fields and houses advantaged.

entries.zh: 如此，則其地雖廣，其稅必寡，其氣力數年而衰。
entries.en: Such a force imposes heavy fiscal burdens and erodes demographic strength over time.
entries.literal: Thus even if the territory is broad, taxes must be sparse, and its manpower declines after several years.

entries.zh: 是危國之兵也。
entries.en: That too is a dangerous military model.
entries.literal: This is the army of a perilous state.

entries.zh: 秦人，其生民也骥阨，其使民也酷烈。
entries.en: Qin organized society through strict coercive discipline and severe extraction.
entries.literal: As for Qin, its people in life were constrained and its use of the people was harsh and severe.

entries.zh: 劫之以勢，隱之以阨，狃之以賞慶，道之以刑罰，使其民所以要利於上者，非戰無由也。
entries.en: By combining pressure, reward conditioning, and punishment, Qin made military performance the sole path of advancement.
entries.literal: Coercing them by power, pressing them by hardship, habituating them with rewards and celebrations, guiding them with punishments, making the only way to gain benefit from above be through war.

entries.zh: 功賞相長，五甲首而隸五家，是最為有數，故能四世有勝於天下。
entries.en: Its quantified merit system produced sustained multi-generational battlefield success.
entries.literal: Merit and reward reinforced each other; five enemy heads bound five households-this was most numerically exact, so for four generations Qin had victory over the realm.

entries.zh: 然皆干賞蹈利之兵，庸徒鬻賣之道耳，未有安制矜節之理也。
entries.en: But such forces were fundamentally transactional, lacking stable moral-institutional discipline.
entries.literal: Yet these were all armies chasing reward and profit, merely a way of common men selling themselves, without principles of settled institutions and restrained norms.

entries.zh: 故雖地廣兵彊，鰓鰓常恐天下之一合而共軋己也。
entries.en: Hence even at peak strength, Qin lived in strategic fear of coalition encirclement.
entries.literal: Therefore though lands were broad and troops strong, Qin always anxiously feared that if the world united it would crush Qin.

entries.zh: 至乎齊桓、晉文之兵，可謂入其域而有節制矣，然猶未本仁義之統也。
entries.en: Huan and Wen improved discipline but still fell short of a fully benevolent-just political foundation.
entries.literal: As for the armies of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, they may be said to have entered their domain with restraint, yet still did not root in the unifying principle of benevolence and righteousness.

entries.zh: 故齊之技擊不可以遇魏之武卒，魏之武卒不可以直秦之銳士，秦之銳士不可以當桓、文之節制，桓、文之節制不可以敵湯、武之仁義。」
entries.en: Thus Qi's skilled fighters cannot match Wei's trained soldiers; Wei's trained soldiers cannot stand against Qin's elite warriors; Qin's elite warriors cannot withstand the discipline of Duke Huan and Duke Wen; and the discipline of Huan and Wen cannot rival the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu.'
entries.literal: Thus Qi's technical fighters cannot meet Wei's martial graduates; Wei's martial graduates cannot directly face Qin's elites; Qin's elites cannot withstand Huan and Wen's disciplined system; Huan and Wen's discipline cannot rival Tang and Wu's benevolence and righteousness.'

entries.zh: 故曰：「善師者不陳，善陳者不戰，善戰者不敗，善敗者不亡。」
entries.en: Therefore it is said: 'One who is good at commanding does not form ranks; one who is good at forming ranks does not fight; one who is good at fighting is not defeated; one who is good even in defeat does not perish.'
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: 'One good at commanding does not deploy; one good at deployment does not fight; one good at fighting does not lose; one good at losing does not perish.'

entries.zh: 若夫舜修百僚，咎繇作士，命以「蠻夷猾夏，寇賊姦軌」，而刑無所用，所謂善師不陳者也。
entries.en: As for Shun ordering the hundred officials and Gao Yao serving as judicial officer, entrusted with cases of 'Man and Yi disturbing Xia, bandits, rebels, and traitors,' yet with punishments having no occasion to be used: this is what is meant by one who is good at commanding not forming ranks.
entries.literal: When Shun ordered the hundred officials and Gao Yao served as judicial officer, tasked with 'barbarians troubling Xia, bandits and rebels,' yet punishment had no use—this is what is meant by one good at commanding not deploying.

entries.zh: 湯、武征伐，陳師誓眾，而放禽桀、紂，所謂善陳不戰者也。
entries.en: Tang and Wu's legitimacy made victory decisive once forces were arrayed, minimizing prolonged combat.
entries.literal: Tang and Wu launched punitive campaigns, deployed armies and swore the troops, yet overthrew and captured Jie and Zhou-this is what is meant by one good at deployment not fighting.

entries.zh: 齊桓南服彊楚，使貢周室，北伐山戎，為燕開路，存亡繼絕，功為伯首，所謂善戰不敗者也。
entries.en: Huan's record shows effective campaigning and interstate stabilization without strategic defeat.
entries.literal: Duke Huan of Qi subdued powerful Chu in the south, made it tribute to Zhou court, campaigned north against mountain Rong and opened routes for Yan, preserving fallen states and continuing severed lines, becoming foremost hegemon-this is what is meant by one good at fighting not losing.

entries.zh: 楚昭王遭闔廬之禍，國滅出亡，父老送之。
entries.en: Even after catastrophic defeat under Wu pressure, King Zhao entered exile with popular support.
entries.literal: King Zhao of Chu suffered the disaster of Helu; his state was destroyed and he fled in exile, with elders seeing him off.

entries.zh: 王曰：「父老反矣！
entries.en: The king said: 'Elders, return home!
entries.literal: The king said: 'Elders, return home!

entries.zh: 何患無君？」
entries.en: Why worry that there will be no ruler?'
entries.literal: Why worry that there will be no ruler?'

entries.zh: 父老曰：「有君如是其賢也！」
entries.en: The elders replied, 'We have a ruler as worthy as this!'
entries.literal: The elders said: 'We have a ruler as worthy as this!'

entries.zh: 相與從之。
entries.en: They all followed him together.
entries.literal: And together they followed him.

entries.zh: 或奔走赴秦，號哭請救，秦人憐之謂之出兵。
entries.en: Others appealed to Qin in tears, and Qin was moved to dispatch aid.
entries.literal: Some ran to Qin crying and requesting rescue; Qin people pitied them and discussed sending troops.

entries.zh: 二國并力，遂走吳師，昭王返國，所謂善敗不亡者也。
entries.en: With allied support Chu recovered, illustrating how political legitimacy can survive even major military defeat.
entries.literal: The two states joined force and routed Wu's army; King Zhao returned to his state-this is what is meant by one good at losing not perishing.

entries.zh: 若秦因四世之勝，據河山之阻，任用白起、王翦豺狼之徒，奮其爪牙，禽獵六國，以并天下。
entries.en: Qin then pursued total conquest through accumulated advantage, strategic geography, and ruthless generals.
entries.literal: But Qin, relying on four generations of victories, the barrier of rivers and mountains, and employing men like Bai Qi and Wang Jian as wolfish types, exerted claws and fangs, hunting the six states to unite the realm.

entries.zh: 窮武極詐，士民不附，卒隸之徒，還為敵讎，猋起雲合，果共軋之。
entries.en: By overreliance on coercion and deceit, Qin alienated society; its own lower ranks eventually joined the coalition that destroyed it.
entries.literal: Exhausting martial force and utmost deception, it lacked attachment of soldiers and people; convict and servile troops turned into enemies, rising like whirlwind and clouds, and indeed together crushed Qin.

entries.zh: 斯為下矣。
entries.en: That is the lowest strategic outcome.
entries.literal: This is the lowest condition.

entries.zh: 凡兵，所以存亡繼絕，救亂除害也。
entries.en: The proper function of military force is restorative: preserving order, rescuing the endangered, and eliminating harm.
entries.literal: In general, armies exist to preserve states on the edge of ruin and continue severed lines, to rescue from chaos and remove harm.

entries.zh: 故伊、呂之將，子孫有國，與商周並。
entries.en: Thus, when Yi Yin and Lü Shang served as commanders, their descendants received states that endured alongside Shang and Zhou.
entries.literal: Therefore commanders like Yi Yin and Lü Shang had descendants with states, standing alongside Shang and Zhou.

entries.zh: 至於末世，苟任詐力，以快貪殘，爭城殺人盈城，爭地殺人滿野。
entries.en: In decadent times, rulers chased gain through fraud and violence, producing mass slaughter in both urban sieges and territorial wars.
entries.literal: By late ages, men recklessly relied on deceit and force to satisfy greed and cruelty; contesting for cities they killed until cities were full of dead, contesting for land they killed until fields were covered.

entries.zh: 孫、吳、商、白之徒，皆身誅戮於前，而功滅亡於後。
entries.en: The lineages of Sunzi, Wuzi, Shang Yang, and Bai Qi ended in violent ruin, and their victories did not endure.
entries.literal: Followers of Sun, Wu, Shang, and Bai were all themselves executed in front, and their achievements perished afterward.

entries.zh: 報應之勢，各以類至，其道然矣。
entries.en: Consequences answer in kind; that is how moral causation operates.
entries.literal: The tendency of retribution comes by kind; so the Way naturally works.

entries.zh: 漢興，高祖躬神武之材，行寬仁之厚，總攬英雄，以誅秦、項。
entries.en: At Han's founding, Gaozu combined military charisma with political magnanimity, uniting talent to defeat Qin and Xiang Yu.
entries.literal: When Han arose, Gaozu personally possessed numinous martial talent and practiced broad benevolent generosity, gathering heroes to punish Qin and Xiang.

entries.zh: 任蕭、曹之文，用良、平之謀，騁陸、酈之辯，明叔孫通之儀，文武相配，大略舉焉。
entries.en: Gaozu employed Xiao He and Cao Shen in civil administration, used Zhang Liang and Chen Ping for strategy, gave free rein to Lu Jia and Li Yiji in persuasion, and established Shusun Tong’s ceremonial system; civil and military complemented each other, and the broad program was realized.
entries.literal: He employed Xiao and Cao in civil administration, used Liang and Ping in strategy, gave rein to Lu and Li in persuasion, and made clear Shusun Tong's ceremonial system; civil and military matched, and the broad program was established.

entries.zh: 天下既定，踵秦而置材官於郡國，京師有南北軍之屯。
entries.en: Once unified, Han retained Qin-style local military offices and permanent capital garrisons.
entries.literal: After the realm was settled, he followed Qin in placing material officers in commanderies and kingdoms, and in the capital there were garrisons of northern and southern armies.

entries.zh: 至武帝平百粵，內增七校，外有樓船，皆歲時講肄，修武備云。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu's southern campaigns, Han expanded both land and naval forces and institutionalized regular training.
entries.literal: By Emperor Wu's pacification of Baiyue, seven internal regiments were added and outside there were towered warships; all were drilled yearly and seasonally, maintaining martial preparedness.

entries.zh: 至元帝時，以貢禹議，始罷角抵，而未正治兵振旅之事也。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan, jiaodi spectacle was removed, but proper military-ritual discipline was still not fully reestablished.
entries.literal: By Emperor Yuan's time, on Gong Yu's advice, jiaodi was first abolished, though military training and inspections were not yet properly restored.

entries.zh: 漢興，高祖初入關，約法三章曰：「殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。」
entries.en: When Han arose and Gaozu first entered the passes, he made the Three Articles: 'Those who kill shall die; those who injure others or steal shall be punished according to the crime.'
entries.literal: When Han arose, Gaozu upon first entering the passes made the Three Articles: 'Killers die; injuring others and theft are punished according to the crime.'

entries.zh: 蠲削煩苛，兆民大說。
entries.en: Abolition of oppressive clauses won broad popular support.
entries.literal: He remitted and cut burdensome harshness, and the myriad people greatly rejoiced.

entries.zh: 其後四夷未附，兵革未息，三章之法不足以禦姦，於是相國蕭何雳摭秦法，取其宜於時者，作律九章。
entries.en: As security pressures rose, Han expanded from minimal law to Xiao He's Nine-Chapter code.
entries.literal: Later, with frontier peoples not yet attached and warfare not yet ceased, the Three Articles were insufficient against crime; so Chancellor Xiao He selected from Qin law those fitting the time and made Nine-Chapter statutes.

entries.zh: 及至孝武即位，外事四夷之功，內盛耳目之好，徵發煩數，百姓貧耗，窮民犯法，酷吏擊斷，姦軌不勝。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu, military expansion and fiscal extraction intensified social strain, while harsh enforcement failed to control rising crime.
entries.literal: By Emperor Wu's accession, externally he pursued achievements against frontier peoples, internally indulged sensory tastes; levies and conscriptions were frequent, people impoverished and depleted; poor people broke law, harsh officials struck and condemned, and wrongdoing could not be exhausted.

entries.zh: 於是招進張湯、趙禹之屬，條定法令，作見知故縱、監臨部主之法，緩深故之罪，急縱出之誅。
entries.en: Legal technocrats expanded doctrinal categories and tightened accountability frameworks, especially around supervisory responsibility.
entries.literal: Then Zhang Tang, Zhao Yu and their type were recruited, sorting and fixing laws and ordinances, making statutes on 'seeing and knowing, intentional release,' and 'supervisory department heads,' relaxing deep-old crimes yet sharpening punishment for deliberate release.

entries.zh: 其後姦猾巧法，轉相比況，禁罔寖密。
entries.en: Both officials and offenders exploited technical legal analogies, producing ever denser legal restrictions.
entries.literal: Afterward, crafty offenders manipulated law, analogizing case to case; prohibitive nets grew increasingly dense.

entries.zh: 律令凡三百五十九章，大辟四百九條，千八百八十二事，死罪決事比萬三千四百七十二事。
entries.en: The statutes and ordinances came to 359 chapters; capital punishment had 409 clauses and 1,882 matters; and precedent analogies used to decide capital cases numbered 13,472 matters.
entries.literal: Statutes and ordinances totaled 359 chapters; capital clauses 409; 1,882 matters; and precedent analogies deciding death cases 13,472 matters.

entries.zh: 文書盈於几閣，典者不能遍睹。
entries.en: The legal archive grew beyond practical administrative mastery.
entries.literal: Documents filled desks and shelves; custodians could not view them all.

entries.zh: 是以郡國承用者駮，或罪同而論異。
entries.en: Uneven implementation generated sentencing inconsistency across jurisdictions.
entries.literal: Thus commanderies and kingdoms used them inconsistently; sometimes same crime received different judgments.

entries.zh: 姦吏因緣為市，所欲活則傅生議，所欲陷則予死比，議者咸冤傷之。
entries.en: Legal complexity enabled prosecutorial rent-seeking, with life/death outcomes manipulated through selective precedent.
entries.literal: Corrupt officials used this as market leverage: those they wished to save got arguments for life, those they wished to trap got death precedents; discussants all lamented this injustice.

entries.zh: 至元帝初立，乃下詔曰：「夫法令者，所以抑暴扶弱，欲其難犯而易避也。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan first ascended the throne, he issued an edict: 'Laws and ordinances are meant to restrain the violent and support the weak, and should be difficult to violate but easy to avoid.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan first ascended, he issued an edict: 'Laws and ordinances are meant to restrain the violent and support the weak, so they should be hard to violate and easy to avoid.

entries.zh: 今律令煩多而不約，自典文者不能分明，而欲羅元元之不逮，斯豈刑中之意哉！
entries.en: The edict criticized legal overcomplexity that trapped ordinary people even when experts struggled to interpret it.
entries.literal: Now statutes are numerous and not concise; even legal specialists cannot distinguish them clearly, yet we would net the common people for what they cannot reach-is this the meaning of proper punishment?

entries.zh: 其議律令可蠲除輕減者，條奏，唯在便安萬姓而已。」
entries.en: Deliberate what can be remitted, removed, or reduced; submit by categories, with only the convenience and safety of the myriad people in view.'
entries.literal: Deliberate what can be remitted, removed, or reduced; submit by categories, with only the convenience and safety of the myriad people in view.'

entries.zh: 當孝惠、高后時，百姓新免毒酿，人欲長幼養老。
entries.en: Early Han society sought recovery and household stability after Qin-era trauma.
entries.literal: In Emperor Hui and Empress Gao's time, people had only newly escaped toxic cruelty and desired to raise young and support elders.

entries.zh: 蕭、曹為相，填以無為，從民之欲，而不擾亂，是以衣食滋殖，刑罰用稀。
entries.en: Under Huang-Lao style minimal interference, economic recovery accelerated and penal severity declined.
entries.literal: Xiao and Cao were chancellors, filling governance with nonaction, following people's desires without disturbance, so clothing and food multiplied and punishments were rarely used.

entries.zh: 景帝元年，下詔曰：「加笞與重罪無異，幸而不死，不可為人。
entries.en: In Emperor Jing's first year he issued an edict: "Increasing flogging is no different from a heavy crime; if one fortunately does not die, one cannot remain a whole person.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jing's first year he issued an edict: "Increasing flogging is no different from heavy crime; if one fortunately does not die, one cannot remain a person.

entries.zh: 其定律：笞五百曰三百，笞三百曰二百。」
entries.en: Fix the statutes: five hundred lashes becomes three hundred, three hundred becomes two hundred."
entries.literal: Fix the statutes: five hundred lashes becomes three hundred, three hundred becomes two hundred."

entries.zh: 猶尚不全。
entries.en: Even so the reform was still incomplete.
entries.literal: Even so it was still not complete.

entries.zh: 至中六年，又下詔曰：「加笞者，或至死而笞未畢，朕甚憐之。
entries.en: By the middle sixth year he again issued an edict: "When flogging is increased, some die before the strokes are finished; I deeply pity this.
entries.literal: By the middle sixth year, he again issued an edict: "Those subjected to additional flogging sometimes die before the strokes are completed; I deeply pity them."

entries.zh: 其減笞三百曰二百，笞二百曰一百。」
entries.en: Reduce: three hundred lashes becomes two hundred, two hundred becomes one hundred."
entries.literal: Reduce: three hundred lashes becomes two hundred, two hundred becomes one hundred."

entries.zh: 又曰：「笞者，所以教之也，其定箠令。」
entries.en: He also said: "Flogging is meant to instruct—establish the rod ordinance."
entries.literal: He also said: "Flogging is meant to instruct—establish the rod ordinance."

entries.zh: 丞相劉舍、御史大夫衛綰請：「笞者，箠長五尺，其本大一寸，其竹也，末薄半寸，皆平其節。
