entries.en: Chancellor Liu She and Censor-in-Chief Wei Wan requested: "For flogging, the rod should be five chi long, one cun thick at the base, made of bamboo, and half a cun thin at the tip, with all its nodes smoothed flat.
entries.literal: Chancellor Liu She and Censor-in-chief Wei Wan memorialized: "For flogging, the rod is five chi long, one cun thick at the root; it is bamboo, half a cun thin at the tip, with all nodes smoothed flat.

entries.zh: 當笞者笞臀。
entries.en: Those due flogging are flogged on the buttocks.
entries.literal: Those due flogging are flogged on the buttocks.

entries.zh: 毋得更人，畢一罪乃更人。」
entries.en: No substitute person may be used; only after one offense is finished may another person be substituted."
entries.literal: No substitute person may be used; only after one crime is finished may another person be substituted."

entries.zh: 自是笞者得全，然酷吏猶以為威。
entries.en: From this, those flogged could survive, yet harsh officials still used flogging as terror.
entries.literal: From this, those flogged could preserve life, yet harsh officials still used it as terror.

entries.zh: 死刑既重，而生刑又輕，民易犯之。
entries.en: Capital punishment was already heavy, yet living punishments were light, so the people easily offended the law.
entries.literal: Capital punishment was already heavy, yet living punishments were light, so the people easily offended.

entries.zh: 宣帝自在閭閻而知其若此，及即尊位，廷史路溫舒上疏，言秦有十失，其一尚存，治獄之吏是也。
entries.en: Because Emperor Xuan knew grassroots legal abuse firsthand, memorial criticism of judicial bureaucracy resonated with him.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan, from commoner life, knew it was so; after taking the throne, court historian Lu Wenshu memorialized that Qin had ten failures, one still remaining: officials who manage prisons.

entries.zh: 語在溫舒傳。
entries.en: The memorial text is preserved in Lu Wenshu's biography.
entries.literal: The words are in Wenshu's biography.

entries.zh: 上深愍焉，乃下詔曰：「間者吏用法，巧文寖深，是朕之不德也。
entries.en: The emperor deeply pitied this, and issued edict: 'Recently officials using law have grown deeply into clever wording-this is my lack of virtue.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply pitied this, and issued edict: 'Recently officials using law have grown deeply into clever wording-this is my lack of virtue.

entries.zh: 夫決獄不當，使有罪興邪，不辜蒙戮，父子悲恨，朕甚傷之。
entries.en: Misjudged cases both embolden true criminals and destroy innocents, causing profound social trauma.
entries.literal: If judgments are improper, the guilty rise in wickedness and innocents suffer execution; fathers and sons grieve with hatred-I am deeply pained by this.

entries.zh: 今遣廷史與郡鞠獄，任輕祿薄，其為置廷平，秩六百石，員四人。
entries.en: He created four 'Court Equalizer' posts to participate in local adjudication and improve balance.
entries.literal: Now dispatch court historians to join commandery case-hearings; their rank is light and salary thin, so establish Court Equalizers, rank six-hundred shi, four positions.

entries.zh: 其務平之，以稱朕意。」
entries.en: Their task is to level judgments, so as to accord with my intent.'
entries.literal: Their task is to level judgments, so as to accord with my intent.'

entries.zh: 於是選于定國為廷尉，求明察寬恕黃霸等以為廷平，季秋後請讞。
entries.en: He appointed capable judicial leadership and staffed equalizer roles with officials known for careful and lenient judgment.
entries.literal: Accordingly Yu Dingguo was selected as chief justice, and bright, observant, lenient men like Huang Ba sought as Court Equalizers; after late autumn, review memorials were requested.

entries.zh: 時上常幸宣室，齋居而決事，獄刑號為平矣。
entries.en: With direct imperial attention to adjudication, penal practice was for a time regarded as comparatively fair.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor often went to Xuanshi Hall, residing in fasting while deciding affairs, and prison judgments were called level.

entries.zh: 時涿郡太守鄭昌上疏言：「聖王置諫爭之臣者，非以崇德，防逸豫之生也；
entries.en: At that time, Zheng Chang, Governor of Zhuo Commandery, submitted a memorial saying: 'When sage kings established ministers of remonstrance, it was not merely to exalt virtue, but to prevent indulgence and ease from arising;
entries.literal: At that time Zhuojun governor Zheng Chang memorialized: 'Sage kings establish remonstrating ministers not to ornament virtue, but to prevent the rise of indulgent ease;

entries.zh: 立法明刑者，非以為治，救衰亂之起也。
entries.en: law is remedial for disorder, not the highest form of rule.
entries.literal: and establishing law and clear punishments is not for governance itself, but to rescue the rise of decline and disorder.

entries.zh: 今明主躬垂明聽，雖不置廷平，獄將自正；
entries.en: Given active imperial oversight, he argued, adjudication could already be corrected;
entries.literal: Now the bright ruler personally hangs clear hearing; even without Court Equalizers, judgments would self-correct;

entries.zh: 若開後嗣，不若刪定律令。
entries.en: For the benefit of posterity, revising and fixing statutes and ordinances mattered more than temporary offices.
entries.literal: But for the sake of posterity, nothing is better than to revise and fix statutes and ordinances.

entries.zh: 律令一定，愚民知所避，姦吏無所弄矣。
entries.en: A clear, stable code would both guide commoners and reduce discretionary abuse by officials.
entries.literal: Once statutes and ordinances are fixed, foolish people know what to avoid, and corrupt officials have nothing to manipulate.

entries.zh: 今不正其本，而置廷平以理其末也，政衰聽怠，則廷平將招權而為亂首矣。」
entries.en: If fundamentals are left untouched and only procedural offices are added, those offices can eventually become new centers of abuse."
entries.literal: Now if one does not correct the root but sets Court Equalizers to manage the branches, when governance declines and hearings grow lax, the Court Equalizers will gather power and become the head of disorder."

entries.zh: 宣帝未及修正。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan never fully carried out structural reform.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan did not have time to correct it.

entries.zh: 漢興之初，雖有約法三章，網漏吞舟之魚，然其大辟，尚有夷三族之令。
entries.en: At the beginning of Han's rise, though there were the Three Articles and the net let through fish large enough to swallow a boat, capital law still included extermination of three clans.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han's rise, though there were the Three Articles, and the net leaked fish large enough to swallow a boat, among capital punishments there remained the ordinance exterminating three clans.

entries.zh: 令曰：「當三族者，皆先黥，劓，斬左右止，笞殺之，梟其首，菹其骨肉於市。
entries.en: The ordinance said: "Those sentenced to punishment of the three clans shall all first be tattooed, have their noses cut off, have their left and right feet amputated, be beaten to death, have their heads displayed, and have their flesh and bones minced in the marketplace.
entries.literal: The ordinance said: "Those due for three-clan punishment all first receive tattooing, nose-cutting, amputation of left and right feet, beating to death, display of the head, and mincing of flesh and bone in the market.

entries.zh: 其誹謗詈詛者，又先斷舌。」
entries.en: Those who slander and curse also first have the tongue cut off."
entries.literal: Those who slander and curse also first have the tongue cut off."

entries.zh: 故謂之具五刑。
entries.en: Therefore it was called the complete five punishments.
entries.literal: Therefore it was called the complete five punishments.

entries.zh: 彭越、韓信之屬皆受此誅。
entries.en: Peng Yue, Han Xin, and their kind all received this execution.
entries.literal: Peng Yue, Han Xin, and their kind all received this execution.

entries.zh: 至高后元年，乃除三族罪、祅言令。
entries.en: By Empress Gao's first year, the three-clan crime and omens-slander ordinance were abolished.
entries.literal: By Empress Gao's first year, the three-clan crime and omens-slander ordinance were abolished.

entries.zh: 孝文二年，又詔丞相、太尉、御史：「法者，治之正，所以禁暴而衛善人也。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Wen, he again issued an edict to the chancellor, grand commandant, and imperial secretary: "Law is the standard of government, the means by which violence is forbidden and good people are protected.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wen's second year, he again commanded the chancellor, grand commandant, and imperial secretary: "Law is the uprightness of governance, by which violence is forbidden and good people protected.

entries.zh: 今犯法者已論，而使無罪之父母妻子同產坐之及收，朕甚弗取。
entries.en: Now offenders have already been judged, yet innocent parents, wives, children, and siblings are implicated and seized along with them. We deeply disapprove of this.
entries.literal: Now when offenders have already been judged, yet innocent parents, wives, children, and household members of the same birth-line are implicated and seized—I deeply do not approve.

entries.zh: 其議。」
entries.en: Deliberate on this."
entries.literal: Deliberate on this."

entries.zh: 左右丞相周勃、陳平奏言：「父母妻子同產相坐及收，所以累其心，使重犯法也。
entries.en: The left and right chancellors, Zhou Bo and Chen Ping, memorialized: "Implicating and seizing parents, wives, children, and siblings is meant to burden people's minds and make them take the violation of law seriously.
entries.literal: The left and right chancellors Zhou Bo and Chen Ping memorialized: "Implicating and seizing parents, wives, children, and household members of the same birth-line is to burden their hearts and make them fear offending the law again.

entries.zh: 收之之道，所由來久矣。
entries.en: The way of seizure has long existed.
entries.literal: The way of seizure has long existed.

entries.zh: 臣之愚計，以為如其故便。」
entries.en: Your servants' foolish plan is to think it convenient to leave it as before."
entries.literal: Your servants' foolish plan is to think it convenient to leave it as before."

entries.zh: 文帝復曰：「朕聞之，法正則民愨，罪當則民從。
entries.en: Emperor Wen replied: "I have heard that when law is upright the people are earnest, and when guilt is fitting the people comply.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen replied: "I have heard that when law is upright the people are earnest, and when guilt is fitting the people comply.

entries.zh: 且夫牧民而道之以善者，吏也；
entries.en: Moreover, those who tend the people and lead them with goodness are officials;
entries.literal: Moreover, those who tend the people and lead them with goodness are officials;

entries.zh: 既不能道，又以不正之法罪之，是法反害於民，為暴者也。
entries.en: if they cannot lead and yet punish with improper law, then law turns to harm the people and becomes violence.
entries.literal: if they cannot lead and yet punish with improper law, then law turns to harm the people and becomes violence.

entries.zh: 朕未見其便，宜孰計之。」
entries.en: I do not see the advantage—you should weigh this carefully."
entries.literal: I do not see the advantage—you should weigh this carefully."

entries.zh: 平、勃乃曰：「陛下幸加大惠於天下，使有罪不收，無罪不相坐，甚盛德，臣等所不及也。
entries.en: Chen Ping and Zhou Bo then said: "Your Majesty has graciously extended great favor to the realm, so that the guilty are not seized and the innocent are not implicated. This is exceedingly great virtue, beyond what your servants can match.
entries.literal: Chen Ping and Zhou Bo then said: "Your Majesty has fortunately extended great favor to the realm, so that the guilty are not seized and the guiltless are not implicated—such surpassing virtue is beyond your servants.

entries.zh: 臣等謹奉詔，盡除收律、相坐法。」
entries.en: Your servants respectfully receive the edict and completely abolish seizure statutes and mutual-implication law."
entries.literal: Your servants respectfully receive the edict and completely abolish seizure statutes and mutual-implication law."

entries.zh: 其後，新垣平謀為逆，復行三族之誅。
entries.en: Afterward, when Xinyuan Ping plotted rebellion, extermination of three clans was again applied.
entries.literal: Afterward, when Xinyuan Ping plotted rebellion, extermination of three clans was again applied.

entries.zh: 由是言之，風俗移易，人性相近而習相遠，信矣。
entries.en: From this it is said: customs shift and change—human nature is close yet practice diverges widely; indeed.
entries.literal: From this it is said: customs shift and change—human nature is close yet practice diverges widely; indeed.

entries.zh: 夫以孝文之仁，平、勃之知，猶有過刑謬論如此甚也，而況庸材溺於末流者乎？
entries.en: If even with Emperor Wen's benevolence and the wisdom of Chen Ping and Zhou Bo, errors about excessive punishment could be this severe, how much more so with mediocre talents submerged in the later current?
entries.literal: If even with Emperor Wen's benevolence and Chen Ping and Zhou Bo's wisdom there were such grave errors in excessive punishment discourse, how much more for mediocre talents drowning in declining currents?

entries.zh: 周官有五聽、八議、三刺、三宥、三赦之法。
entries.en: The offices of Zhou employed the procedures of the Five Hearings, Eight Deliberations, Three Inquiries, Three Pardons, and Three Exemptions.
entries.literal: Zhou offices had methods of Five Hearings, Eight Deliberations, Three Inquiries, Three Pardons, and Three Exemptions.

entries.zh: 五聽：一曰辭聽，二曰色聽，三曰氣聽，四曰耳聽，五曰目聽。
entries.en: The Five Hearings evaluated testimony through words, expression, breath, auditory clues, and visual observation.
entries.literal: Five Hearings: first speech-hearing, second color-hearing, third qi-hearing, fourth ear-hearing, fifth eye-hearing.

entries.zh: 八議：一曰議親，二曰議故，三曰議賢，四曰議能，五曰議功，六曰議貴，七曰議勤，八曰議賓。
entries.en: The Eight Deliberations were status-based mitigating categories covering kinship, merit, office, and diplomatic standing.
entries.literal: Eight Deliberations: deliberation of kinship, old ties, worthiness, ability, merit, rank, diligence, and guest status.

entries.zh: 三刺：一曰訊群臣，二曰訊群吏，三曰訊萬民。
entries.en: Judgment involved consultation across ministers, administrators, and populace.
entries.literal: Three Inquiries: inquire of ministers, inquire of officials, inquire of the people.

entries.zh: 三宥：一曰弗識，二曰過失，三曰遺忘。
entries.en: Three pardonable conditions were non-knowledge, mistake, and lapse of memory.
entries.literal: Three Pardons: ignorance, error, forgetfulness.

entries.zh: 三赦：一曰幼弱，二曰老眊，三曰憃愚。
entries.en: Legal exemption categories included very young, very old, and intellectually limited persons.
entries.literal: Three Exemptions: young weakness, aged senility, and foolish dullness.

entries.zh: 凡囚，「上罪梏拲而桎，中罪梏桎，下罪梏；
entries.en: As for prisoners: 'Upper crimes cuffed and fettered; middle crimes cuffed and fettered; lower crimes cuffed;
entries.literal: As for prisoners: 'Upper crimes cuffed and fettered; middle crimes cuffed and fettered; lower crimes cuffed;

entries.zh: 王之同族拲，有爵者桎，以待弊。」
entries.en: members of the king's own clan are only cuffed; those with rank only fettered, awaiting final outcome.'
entries.literal: members of the king's own clan are only cuffed; those with rank only fettered, awaiting final outcome.'

entries.zh: 高皇帝七年，制詔御史：「獄之疑者，吏或不敢決，有罪者久而不論，無罪者久繫不決。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Gaozu, an edict to the censors said: 'In doubtful cases, officials sometimes dare not decide; the guilty remain long without judgment, while the innocent remain long detained without decision.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year seven, an edict to Censors said: 'In doubtful cases officials sometimes dare not decide; the guilty remain long untried and innocents remain long detained undecided.

entries.zh: 自今以來，縣道官獄疑者，各讞所屬二千石官，二千石官以其罪名當報之。
entries.en: From now on, when county and district officials have doubtful prison cases, each should refer them to the relevant 2,000-shi official, and that official shall report the fitting charge.
entries.literal: From now, doubtful county and district prison cases should each be reviewed by the relevant 2,000-shi official, and that official shall report applicable charge names.

entries.zh: 所不能決者，皆移廷尉，廷尉亦當報之。
entries.en: What they cannot decide all transfer to the Commandant of Justice, who should also report.
entries.literal: What they cannot decide all transfer to the Chief Justice, who should also report.

entries.zh: 廷尉所不能決，謹具為奏，傅所當比律令以聞。」
entries.en: What the Chief Justice cannot decide, carefully memorialize and attach the matching statutes and ordinances for hearing.'
entries.literal: What the Chief Justice cannot decide, carefully memorialize and attach the matching statutes and ordinances for hearing.'

entries.zh: 上恩如此，吏猶不能奉宣。
entries.en: Despite clear directives, administrative implementation remained weak.
entries.literal: Such was imperial grace, yet officials still could not properly promulgate and execute.

entries.zh: 故孝景中五年復下詔曰：「諸獄疑，雖文致於法而於人心不厭者，輒讞之。」
entries.en: Therefore, in the fifth middle year of Emperor Jing, another edict said: 'In all doubtful cases, even if the written text can be made to fit the law, if it does not satisfy human feeling, refer it at once for review.'
entries.literal: Therefore in Jingdi middle year five another edict said: 'In all doubtful prisons, though textually fitting statute but not satisfying human feeling, immediately refer them for review.'

entries.zh: 其後獄吏復避微文，遂其愚心。
entries.en: Yet legal formalism reasserted itself through pedantic loopholing.
entries.literal: Afterward prison officials again hid behind minor textualities, following their own foolish intent.

entries.zh: 至後元年，又下詔曰：「獄，重事也。
entries.en: In Houyuan year one another edict said: 'Prisons are weighty matters.
entries.literal: In Houyuan year one another edict said: 'Prisons are weighty matters.

entries.zh: 人有愚智，官有上下。
entries.en: Human and administrative capacities vary;
entries.literal: People have wisdom or stupidity; officials have high and low rank.

entries.zh: 獄疑者讞，有令讞者已報讞而後不當，讞者不為失。」
entries.en: Doubtful cases should be reviewed; when ordered review has already reported review but later proves improper, the reviewer is not counted at fault.'
entries.literal: Doubtful cases should be reviewed; when ordered review has already reported review but later proves improper, the reviewer is not counted at fault.'

entries.zh: 自此之後，獄刑益詳，近於五聽三宥之意。
entries.en: The system moved somewhat closer to classical evidentiary and mitigation principles.
entries.literal: After this, prison penalties became more detailed, approaching the intent of Five Hearings and Three Pardons.

entries.zh: 三年復下詔曰：「高年老長，人所尊敬也；
entries.en: Three years later another edict said: 'The very old are those people honor and respect;
entries.literal: Three years later another edict said: 'The very old are those people honor and respect;

entries.zh: 鰥寡不屬逮者，人所哀憐也。
entries.en: Widowers and widows not subject to summons were also persons whom people pitied.
entries.literal: Widowers and widows whom authorities do not summon are those whom people pity.

entries.zh: 其著令：年八十以上，八歲以下，及孕者未乳，師、朱儒當鞠繫者，頌繫之。」
entries.en: Set this in statute: those over eighty, those under eight, pregnant women who have not yet given birth, music masters, and dwarfs who must be arrested and detained shall be held under summons rather than in bonds.'
entries.literal: Set this in statute: those over eighty, below eight, and pregnant women who have not yet given birth, as well as music masters and dwarfs who should be arrested, are to be held by summons rather than bound detention.'

entries.zh: 至孝宣元康四年，又下詔曰：「
entries.en: By Emperor Xuan Yuankang year four, another edict said: '
entries.literal: By Emperor Xuan Yuankang year four, another edict said: '

entries.zh: 自建武、永平，民亦新免兵革之禍，人有樂生之慮，與高、惠之間同，而政在抑彊扶弱，朝無威福之臣，邑無豪桀之俠。
entries.en: From the Jianwu through Yongping eras, the people had only recently emerged from the disasters of war and were mindful of preserving life, as in the time of Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Hui. Government policy restrained the strong and supported the weak; at court no minister privately wielded the power to inspire fear or grant favors, and in the localities there were no domineering magnates.
entries.literal: Since Jianwu and Yongping, people had newly escaped war calamities and cherished life, as between Gaozu and Hui; governance suppressed the strong and supported the weak, court lacked ministers wielding private awe and favor, and localities lacked heroic magnates.

entries.zh: 以口率計，斷獄少於成、哀之間什八，可謂清矣。
entries.en: On a per capita basis, adjudicated criminal cases were less than two-tenths as numerous as during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai; the administration could be called clear.
entries.literal: By per-capita calculation, adjudicated prison cases were less than two-tenths of the Cheng-Ai interval, and may be called clear.

entries.zh: 然而未能稱意比隆於古者，以其疾未盡除，而刑本不正。
entries.en: Even improved conditions fell short while structural causes and penal foundations remained uncorrected.
entries.literal: Yet it still could not satisfy intent or equal antiquity's grandeur, because these diseases were not fully removed and punishment roots were not corrected.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「如有王者，必世而後仁；
entries.en: Confucius said: 'If there were a true king, it would take a generation before benevolence;
entries.literal: Confucius said: 'If there were a true king, it would take a generation before benevolence;

entries.zh: 善人為國百年，可以勝殘去殺矣。」
entries.en: A good man governing a state for a hundred years could overcome cruelty and remove killing.'
entries.literal: A good man governing a state for a hundred years could overcome cruelty and remove killing.'

entries.zh: 言聖王承衰撥亂而起，被民以德教，變而化之，必世然後仁道成焉；
entries.en: Moral transformation is gradual and depends on long-term virtue-centered statecraft.
entries.literal: He meant that a sage king arising after decline and disorder, covering people with virtue and teaching, transforming them, requires a generation before benevolent order is completed;

entries.zh: 至於善人，不入於室，然猶百年勝殘去殺矣。
entries.en: Even second-best rulers, if persistent, can still greatly reduce penal violence over time.
entries.literal: As for a good man, though not entering the inner chamber, still after a hundred years can overcome cruelty and remove killing.

entries.zh: 此為國者之程式也。
entries.en: This sets the proper timeline expectation for political reform.
entries.literal: This is the standard procedure for those governing states.

entries.zh: 今漢道至盛，歷世二百餘載，考自昭、宣、元、成、哀、平六世之間，斷獄殊死，率歲千餘口而一人，耐罪上至右止，三倍有餘。
entries.en: The Han way had now flourished for more than two hundred years. Across the six reigns of Emperor Zhao, Emperor Xuan, Emperor Yuan, Emperor Cheng, Emperor Ai, and Emperor Ping, capital cases ending in death averaged a little more than one person in every thousand each year; sentences ranging from shaving punishment to amputation of the right foot were more than three times as numerous.
entries.literal: The Han way had now flourished for more than two hundred years. Examining the six reigns of Zhao, Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, capital cases ending in death averaged a little more than one person in every thousand each year; punishments from shaving the beard through amputation of the right foot were more than three times as numerous.

entries.zh: 古人有言：「滿堂而飲酒，有一人鄉隅而悲泣，則一堂皆為之不樂。」
entries.en: An old saying says: 'If a hall is drinking and one person in a corner weeps, then the whole hall is unhappy.'
entries.literal: An old saying says: 'If a hall is drinking and one person in a corner weeps, then the whole hall is unhappy.'

entries.zh: 王者之於天下，譬猶一堂之上也，故一人不得其平，為之悽愴於心。
entries.en: A ruler should treat each unjust case as a stain on the whole polity.
entries.literal: For a king toward all under heaven, it is like one hall; therefore if one person does not obtain fairness, the king is pained in heart.

entries.zh: 今郡國被刑而死者歲以萬數，天下獄二千餘所，其冤死者多少相覆，獄不減一人，此和氣所以未洽者也。
entries.en: Now those executed by punishment in the commanderies and kingdoms number in the tens of thousands each year; there are over two thousand prisons under heaven; how many die unjustly, overlapping beyond count! If prisoners do not decrease by even one, this is why harmonious qi has not fully spread.
entries.literal: Now those executed by punishment in commanderies and kingdoms are in tens of thousands yearly; there are over two thousand prisons under heaven; how many unjust deaths overlap! If prisoners do not decrease by even one person, this is why harmonious qi has not fully spread.

entries.zh: 朕念夫耆老之人，髮齒墮落，血氣既衰，亦無暴逆之心，今或羅于文法，執于囹圄，不得終其年命，朕甚憐之。
entries.en: 'I think of old people whose hair and teeth have fallen, blood and qi declined, with no violent rebellious heart; now some are trapped in legal text, seized in prisons, unable to finish their lifespan—I deeply pity this.'
entries.literal: 'I think of old people whose hair and teeth have fallen, blood and qi declined, with no violent rebellious heart; now some are trapped in legal text, seized in prisons, unable to finish their lifespan-I deeply pity this.'

entries.zh: 自今以來，諸年八十非誣告殺傷人，它皆勿坐。」
entries.en: From now on, all those aged eighty or more shall not be convicted except for false accusation, killing, or injuring others.'
entries.literal: From now on, all those aged eighty or more shall not be convicted except for false accusation, killing, or injuring others.'

entries.zh: 至成帝鴻嘉元年，定令：「年未滿七歲，賊鬥殺人及犯殊死者，上請廷尉以聞，得減死。」
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Cheng's Hongjia era, an order was fixed: 'When someone not yet seven years old kills a person in robbery or fighting, or commits an offense deserving exceptional death, submit the case to the Commandant of Justice for report, and the death penalty may be reduced.'
entries.literal: In Chengdi Hongjia year one, an order fixed: 'If not yet seven years old, and in robbery-fighting homicide or capital offenses, submit to Chief Justice for hearing and may receive commuted death.'

entries.zh: 合於三赦幼弱老眊之人。
entries.en: The measure was framed as consistent with classical exemption doctrine.
entries.literal: This accords with the three-exemption principle for young and old-senile persons.

entries.zh: 此皆法令稍定，近古而便民者也。
entries.en: Such revisions are presented as successful examples of humane legal normalization.
entries.literal: These are all cases where statutes gradually stabilized, approached antiquity, and benefited the people.

entries.zh: 孫卿之言既然，又因俗說而論之曰：禹承堯舜之後，自以德衰而制肉刑，湯武順而行之者，以俗薄於唐虞故也。
entries.en: Xunzi, having made this argument, went on to reason from the conventional account: Yu succeeded Yao and Shun but, believing that moral virtue had declined, instituted mutilating punishments; Tang and King Wu retained them because customs were less refined than in the age of Yao and Shun.
entries.literal: Xunzi's words being so, he further reasoned from the conventional account: Yu succeeded Yao and Shun, but believing virtue had declined, instituted mutilating punishments; Tang and Wu continued them because customs were less refined than in the age of Yao and Shun.

entries.zh: 今漢承衰周暴秦極敝之流，俗已薄於三代，而行堯舜之刑，是猶以鞿而御駻突，違救時之宜矣。
entries.en: Now Han has inherited the utter exhaustion left by declining Zhou and violent Qin. Customs are already less refined than under the Three Dynasties, yet to apply the punishments of Yao and Shun would be like trying to control a savage, bolting horse with a light bridle: it would run contrary to what the times require.
entries.literal: Now Han inherits the utter exhaustion left by declining Zhou and violent Qin. Customs are already less refined than under the Three Dynasties, yet applying the punishments of Yao and Shun is like controlling a fierce, bolting horse with a light bridle, contrary to what the times require.

entries.zh: 且除肉刑者，本欲以全民也，今去髡鉗一等，轉而入於大辟。
entries.en: Commutation policy can perversely increase death sentencing if replacement scales are misdesigned.
entries.literal: Moreover, abolishing corporal punishment originally intended preserving life; now removing one level of shaving-shackling turns into entry into capital punishment.

entries.zh: 以死罔民，失本惠矣。
entries.en: That outcome betrays the reform's humanitarian purpose.
entries.literal: To net people with death is to lose the original benevolent intent.

entries.zh: 故死者歲以萬數，刑重之所致也。
entries.en: High annual execution counts are attributed to excessive penal severity.
entries.literal: Therefore yearly deaths in tens of thousands are caused by over-heavy punishment.

entries.zh: 至乎穿窬之盜，忿怒傷人，男女淫佚，吏為姦臧，若此之惡，髡鉗之罰又不足以懲也。
entries.en: Conversely, many offenses are under-deterred by too-light sanctions.
entries.literal: As for burglars tunneling walls, rage-injury assaults, sexual licentiousness, and officials committing corruption-these evils are not sufficiently deterred by shaving-shackling penalties.

entries.zh: 故刑者歲十萬數，民既不畏，又曾不恥，刑輕之所生也。
entries.en: Mass punishment without moral effect indicates miscalibration at the lenient end too.
entries.literal: Therefore yearly punishments number in hundred-thousands; people neither fear nor feel shame-this is born of overly light punishment.

entries.zh: 故俗之能吏，公以殺盜為威，專殺者勝任，奉法者不治，亂名傷制，不可勝條。
entries.en: Administrative culture came to reward lethal zeal over lawful balance, corroding institutional norms.
entries.literal: Thus capable officials by custom make killing bandits their prestige; those specializing in killing are deemed competent, those following law are called incapable; reputations and institutions are damaged beyond listing.

entries.zh: 是以罔密而姦不塞，刑蕃而民愈嫚。
entries.en: Legal expansion without legitimacy produces both more law and more defiance.
entries.literal: Therefore nets grow denser but crime not blocked; punishments proliferate and people grow more insolent.

entries.zh: 必世而未仁，百年而不勝殘，誠以禮樂闕而刑不正也。
entries.en: Failure over long horizons is traced to absent ritual order and distorted penal structure.
entries.literal: A generation passes without benevolence, a hundred years without overcoming cruelty-truly because rites and music are lacking and punishment is not correct.

entries.zh: 豈宜惟思所以清原正本之論，刪定律令，篹二百章，以應大辟。
entries.en: The text calls for foundational legal redrafting into a coherent, compressed code.
entries.literal: Should one not only think on arguments for clearing source and correcting root, revising statutes and ordinances, compiling two hundred chapters matching capital law?

entries.zh: 其餘罪次，於古當生，今觸死者，皆可募行肉刑。
entries.en: It proposes commuting many currently capital crimes to calibrated corporal sanctions.
entries.literal: As for remaining offenses, those that in antiquity should have lived but now touch death may all be allowed to substitute corporal punishment.

entries.zh: 及傷人與盜，吏受賕枉法，男女淫亂，皆復古刑，為三千章。
entries.en: For assault, theft, corrupt officials who pervert the law, and sexual misconduct, penalties should be reset to the older classical scale, yielding a code of three thousand provisions.
entries.literal: As for injuring others and theft, officials taking bribes and twisting the law, and sexual disorder between men and women, all should return to ancient punishments, forming three thousand articles.

entries.zh: 詆欺文致微細之法，悉蠲除。
entries.en: All petty, manipulative, and overly technical legal provisions should be abolished entirely.
entries.literal: All laws of slanderous trickery and hair-splitting textual framing should be completely removed.

entries.zh: 如此，則刑可畏而禁易避，吏不專殺，法無二門，輕重當罪，民命得全，合刑罰之中，殷天人之和，順稽古之制，成時雍之化。
entries.en: If this is done, the law will be stern yet navigable, officials will no longer wield death arbitrarily, punishments will fit offenses, and lives will be preserved. It would restore balanced penal governance, deepen harmony between Heaven and human society, align with tested ancient institutions, and produce an age of social concord.
entries.literal: If so, punishments will be fearsome yet prohibitions easy to avoid; officials will not monopolize killing; law will have no second gate; light and heavy will match crimes; people's lives can be preserved; this accords with proper balance in punishments, enriches harmony between Heaven and humans, follows and examines ancient institutions, and completes a transformation of timely concord.

entries.zh: 成康刑錯，雖未可致，孝文斷獄，庶幾可及。
entries.en: We may not reach the ideal era of Cheng and Kang, when punishment was scarcely needed, but we can still aspire to the humane judicial standard associated with Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Though we may not yet attain the age of Cheng and Kang when punishments were set aside, we may perhaps approach Emperor Wen's judgments in criminal cases.

entries.zh: 《詩》云「宜民宜人，受祿于天」。
entries.en: As the Odes says, 'When governance truly suits the people, Heaven grants its favor.'
entries.literal: The Odes says: 'Making the people fitting, making persons fitting, one receives Heaven's blessing.'

entries.zh: 《書》曰「立功立事，可以永年」。
entries.en: The Documents says: 'Establish achievement and establish institutions, and one can endure for long years.'
entries.literal: The Documents says: 'Establish achievement and establish institutions, and one can endure for long years.'

entries.zh: 言為政而宜於民者，功成事立，則受天祿而永年命，所謂「一人有慶，萬民賴之」者也。
entries.en: In other words, governance that truly benefits the people creates lasting achievement and institutions. Such rule receives Heaven's favor and endures, fulfilling the saying: 'When one person is blessed, all the people depend on it.'
entries.literal: This means that if one governs in a way suitable to the people, achievements are completed and institutions established; then one receives Heaven's blessing and long life, which is what is called 'when one person has good fortune, the myriad people rely on it.'

entries.zh: 夫人宵天地之䫉，懷五常之性，聰明精粹，有生之最靈者也。
entries.en: Human beings, bearing the form of Heaven and Earth and the nature of the Five Constants, are the most numinous of living creatures.
entries.literal: Humans receive the form of Heaven and Earth, bear the nature of the Five Constants, and in clarity and refined essence are the most numinous among living things.

entries.zh: 爪牙不足以供耆欲，趨走不足以避利害，無毛羽以禦寒暑，必將役物以為養，任智而不恃力，此其所以為貴也。
entries.en: Because humans lack natural weapons and coverings, they survive by organizing the world through intelligence, not brute strength; that is what makes them distinctive.
entries.literal: Claws and fangs are not enough to satisfy desires; running is not enough to avoid harm; with no fur or feathers against heat and cold, people must employ things for sustenance, rely on intelligence rather than force; this is why they are precious.

entries.zh: 故不仁愛則不能群，不能群則不勝物，不勝物則養不足。
entries.en: Without humane solidarity, people cannot form society; without society, they cannot secure resources for life.
entries.literal: Therefore without benevolence and love one cannot form community; without community one cannot prevail over things; without prevailing over things, nourishment is insufficient.

entries.zh: 群而不足，爭心將作，上聖卓然先行敬讓博愛之德者，眾心說而從之。
entries.en: When scarcity persists, conflict begins. The sages preempted this by modeling respect, deference, and universal concern, winning willing allegiance.
entries.literal: If in community there is still insufficiency, contentious hearts will arise. The highest sages first practiced reverence, yielding, and broad love; people's hearts delighted and followed them.

entries.zh: 從之成群，是為君矣；
entries.en: Once people gathered under such leadership, that person became a ruler;
entries.literal: When followers formed into a community, this was called a ruler;

entries.zh: 歸而往之，是為王矣。
entries.en: When all under heaven gravitated to him, he became a true king.
entries.literal: When all turned and went to him, this was called a king.

entries.zh: 洪範曰：「天子作民父母，為天下王。」
entries.en: The Great Plan says: 'The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother of the people, becoming king for all under heaven.'
entries.literal: The Great Plan says: 'The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother of the people, becoming king for all under heaven.'

entries.zh: 聖人取類以正名，而謂君為父母，明仁愛德讓，王道之本也。
entries.en: Calling the ruler 'parent' emphasized that humane care and moral deference are the foundation of legitimate kingship.
entries.literal: Sages took analogies to rectify names and called the ruler father and mother, making clear that benevolence, love, virtue, and yielding are the root of kingly way.

entries.zh: 愛待敬而不敗，德須威而久立，故制禮以崇敬，作刑以明威也。
entries.en: Affection alone is unstable; it must be paired with respect, and virtue must be backed by enforceable authority. Hence both ritual and penal law.
entries.literal: Love must be supported by reverence or it fails; virtue requires authority to endure. Therefore rites were established to exalt reverence and punishments made to clarify authority.

entries.zh: 聖人既躬明悊之性，必通天地之心，制禮作教，立法設刑，動緣民情，而則天象地。
entries.en: Because sages understood both human nature and cosmic principle, they built ritual, education, law, and punishment around real human emotions while mirroring cosmic order.
entries.literal: Since sages personally embodied bright and wise nature, they necessarily communicated with Heaven-and-Earth's intent, making rites and teaching, establishing law and punishment, acting in accord with human feelings and modeling Heaven and Earth.

entries.zh: 故曰先王立禮，「則天之明，因地之性」也。
entries.en: Therefore it is said former kings established rites by 'patterning Heaven's brightness and following Earth's nature.'
entries.literal: Therefore it is said former kings established rites by 'patterning Heaven's brightness and following Earth's nature.'

entries.zh: 刑罰威獄，以類天之震曜殺戮也；
entries.en: Punitive law mirrors the coercive side of cosmic power—thunder, lightning, and lethal force;
entries.literal: Penal punishments and prisons correspond to Heaven's thunder, lightning, and killing strokes;

entries.zh: 溫慈惠和，以效天之生殖長育也。
entries.en: while benevolence and care imitate Heaven's life-giving and nurturing functions.
entries.literal: Warmth, kindness, beneficence, and harmony emulate Heaven's generation, growth, and nurture.

entries.zh: 《書》云「天秩有禮」，「天討有罪」。
entries.en: The Documents says, 'Heaven's ordered ranks have rites,' and 'Heaven punishes the guilty.'
entries.literal: The Documents says, 'Heaven's ordered ranks have rites,' and 'Heaven punishes the guilty.'

entries.zh: 故聖人因天秩而制五禮，因天討而作五刑。
entries.en: So the sages derived both ritual classification and penal classification from Heaven's own ordering and sanction.
entries.literal: Therefore sages, following Heaven's order, made the Five Rites; following Heaven's punishment, made the Five Penalties.

entries.zh: 大刑用甲兵，其次用斧鉞；
entries.en: At the highest level, punishment means military force; next comes execution by weapons;
entries.literal: The greatest punishment uses armored troops; next uses axes and halberds;

entries.zh: 中刑用刀鋸，其次用鑽鑿；
entries.en: Middle grades involved mutilating instruments;
entries.literal: Middle punishments use knives and saws; next use boring and chiseling;

entries.zh: 薄刑用鞭扑。
entries.en: Lighter ones used flogging.
entries.literal: Lighter punishments use whips and rods.

entries.zh: 大者陳諸原野，小者致之市朝，其所繇來者上矣。
entries.en: Major penalties were public in open ground, lesser penalties in urban spaces-a very old institutional pattern.
entries.literal: Great cases are displayed in fields and wilds; smaller are carried out in markets and courts; their origin is ancient and elevated.

entries.zh: 漢興，接秦之敝，諸侯並起，民失作業，而大饑饉。
entries.en: At the founding of Han, inheriting Qin's collapse, rival lords rose everywhere, farming broke down, and famine followed.
entries.literal: When Han arose, taking over Qin's exhaustion, feudal lords rose together, the people lost their occupations, and there was great famine.

entries.zh: 凡米石五千，人相食，死者過半。
entries.en: Rice reached five thousand cash per shi; cannibalism spread and more than half the population perished.
entries.literal: Rice reached five thousand per shi; people ate one another, and more than half died.

entries.zh: 高祖乃令民得賣子，就食蜀漢。
entries.en: Gaozu then permitted families to sell children and migrate to Shu and Han for food.
entries.literal: Gaozu then allowed the people to sell their children and go to Shu and Han to obtain food.

entries.zh: 天下既定，民亡蓋臧，自天子不能具醇駟，而將相或乘牛車。
entries.en: After unification, stores were exhausted everywhere: the throne could not field a matched four-horse team, and some ministers rode in ox carts.
entries.literal: When the realm was settled, the people had no surplus stores; even the Son of Heaven could not supply a team of four matched horses, and some generals and chancellors rode ox carts.

entries.zh: 上於是約法省禁，輕田租，什五而稅一，量吏祿，度官用，以賦於民。
entries.en: He then eased law and prohibition, cut land tax to one-fifteenth, sized official salaries and state spending, and aligned levies with that budget.
entries.literal: The emperor then simplified laws and reduced prohibitions, lightened land tax to one part in fifteen, measured official salaries, estimated governmental expenditure, and made levies upon the people accordingly.

entries.zh: 而山川園池市肆租稅之入，自天子以至封君湯沐邑，皆各為私奉養，不領於天子之經費。
entries.en: Revenue from mountains, rivers, parks, ponds, and markets, from the throne down to feudal bath fiefs, funded private household upkeep rather than central routine expenditure.
entries.literal: Revenue from rents and taxes on mountains, rivers, parks, ponds, and market stalls, from the Son of Heaven down to the enfeoffed lords' bath-fief domains, each served private maintenance and did not enter the Son of Heaven's regular state expenditure.

entries.zh: 漕轉關東粟以給中都官，歲不過數十萬石。
entries.en: Canal transport moved eastern-pass grain to the capital offices, at most several hundred thousand shi a year.
entries.literal: Grain from east of the passes was transported by water to supply the central capital offices, never exceeding several hundred thousand shi per year.

entries.zh: 孝惠、高后之間，衣食滋殖。
entries.en: Between Emperor Hui and Empress Lü, food and clothing gradually became more plentiful.
entries.literal: Between Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gaohou, food and clothing gradually multiplied.

entries.zh: 文帝即位，躬修儉節，思安百姓。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he personally practiced austerity and sought to settle the common people.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he personally cultivated frugality and thought to settle the common people.

entries.zh: 時民近戰國，皆背本趨末，賈誼說上曰：筦子曰「倉廩實而知禮節」。
entries.en: At the time popular life resembled the Warring States era, with everyone abandoning farming for marginal trades. Jia Yi urged the emperor, saying: Guanzi says, "When granaries are full, the people know ritual propriety."
entries.literal: At the time the people were close to Warring States conditions, all turning from the fundamental to the marginal. Jia Yi persuaded the emperor, saying: Guanzi says, "When granaries are full, the people know ritual propriety."

entries.zh: 民不足而可治者，自古及今，未之嘗聞。
entries.en: No regime has stably governed a population in chronic deprivation.
entries.literal: That people lacking means can still be governed-from ancient to present, this has never been heard.

entries.zh: 古之人曰：「一夫不耕，或受之飢；
entries.en: The ancients said, 'If one man does not farm, someone will go hungry;
entries.literal: Ancients said: 'If one man does not farm, someone suffers hunger;

entries.zh: 一女不織，或受之寒。」
entries.en: if one woman does not weave, someone will suffer cold.'
entries.literal: if one woman does not weave, someone suffers cold.'

entries.zh: 生之有時，而用之亡度，則物力必屈。
entries.en: If consumption outruns seasonal production, the economy inevitably buckles.
entries.literal: Production has its timing, but use has no measure-then productive force must collapse.

entries.zh: 古之治天下，至孅至悉也，故其畜積足恃。
entries.en: Classical states built high-resolution management, which is why reserves were dependable.
entries.literal: Ancient governance of the realm was meticulous to the finest degree; therefore their stores were sufficient to rely on.

entries.zh: 今背本而趨末，食者甚眾，是天下之大殘也；
entries.en: When society abandons productive fundamentals for secondary pursuits, macroeconomic damage follows.
entries.literal: Now people turn away from root and rush to branch, while consumers are many-this is the realm's great injury;

entries.zh: 淫侈之俗，日日以長，是天下之大賊也。
entries.en: Escalating luxury culture is treated as parasitic extraction from real production.
entries.literal: and luxurious, extravagant custom grows daily-this is the realm's great thief.

entries.zh: 殘賊公行，莫之或止；
entries.en: Predatory behavior has become normalized and unchecked;
entries.literal: Injury and theft run openly, with none to stop them;

entries.zh: 大命將泛，莫之振救。
entries.en: political legitimacy itself is nearing systemic failure.
entries.literal: the great mandate is about to drift, with none to rescue and stabilize it.

entries.zh: 生之者甚少而靡之者甚多，天下財產何得不蹶！
entries.en: A widening producer-consumer imbalance makes fiscal collapse unavoidable.
entries.literal: Those who produce are very few while those who consume are very many-how can the realm's wealth not collapse!

entries.zh: 漢之為漢幾四十年矣，公私之積猶可哀痛。
entries.en: Even after decades, both state and household reserves remained fragile.
entries.literal: Han has been Han nearly forty years, yet public and private accumulations are still pitiably painful.

entries.zh: 失時不雨，民且狼顧；
entries.en: Any weather shock immediately triggers social anxiety and scarcity behavior;
entries.literal: If seasonal rain fails, people already look about like wolves;

entries.zh: 歲惡不入，請賣爵、子。
entries.en: In severe scarcity, people seek desperate liquidity-including status sales and family liquidation.
entries.literal: if bad harvest yields no intake, they request selling ranks and even children.

entries.zh: 既聞耳矣，安有為天下阽危者若是而上不驚者！
entries.en: Given such warning signs, elite complacency is inexcusable.
entries.literal: We have already heard this-how can the realm be in such peril and those above not be alarmed!

entries.zh: 後十三歲，孝景二年，令民半出田租，三十而稅一也。
entries.en: Thirteen years later, in the second year of Emperor Jing, the people were ordered to pay half the field rent, a tax of one in thirty.
entries.literal: Thirteen years later, in Jing year two, people were ordered to pay half field rent, taxing one in thirty.

entries.zh: 其後，上郡以西旱，復修賣爵令，而裁其賈以招民；
entries.en: In western drought conditions, rank-for-grain measures were revived with revised terms.
entries.literal: Afterward, when drought struck west of Shang commandery, the rank-selling order was again repaired, adjusting prices to attract people;

entries.zh: 及徒復作，得輸粟於縣官以除罪。
entries.en: Grain submission also became a channel for sentence commutation.
entries.literal: and with convict labor restored, one could submit grain to county offices to remove penalties.

entries.zh: 始造苑馬以廣用，宮室列館車馬益增修矣。
entries.en: At the same time, elite expenditure on court infrastructure and transport continued to expand.
entries.literal: Parks for horses were first expanded for broader use, and palace halls, pavilions, carriages, and horses were increasingly augmented.

entries.zh: 然婁敕有司以農為務，民遂樂業。
entries.en: Even so, repeated pro-agriculture directives helped keep productive commitment relatively high.
entries.literal: Yet repeated imperial orders made agriculture the priority, and people thus delighted in their occupations.

entries.zh: 至武帝之初七十年間，國家亡事，非遇水旱，則民人給家足，都鄙廩庾盡滿，而府庫餘財。
entries.en: For about seventy years down to the start of Emperor Wu's reign, relative stability produced broad fiscal abundance and full granaries.
entries.literal: For seventy years to the start of Emperor Wu, the state had no major troubles; unless water or drought struck, households were provided for, granaries in capital and countryside full, and treasuries with surplus.

entries.zh: 京師之錢累百鉅萬，貫朽而不可校。
entries.en: Monetary surplus grew so large that cash strings physically decayed in storage.
entries.literal: Capital coin accumulated in hundreds of millions, with strings rotted and uncountable.

entries.zh: 太倉之粟陳陳相因，充溢露積於外，腐敗不可食。
entries.en: State grain reserves became so excessive that some stock spoiled in open overflow storage.
entries.literal: Taicang grain piles layer on layer, overflowing and heaped outside, rotting unusable.

entries.zh: 眾庶街巷有馬，仟伯之間成群，乘牸牝者擯而不得會聚。
entries.en: Livestock ownership had become so common that social distinction emerged even within horse ownership.
entries.literal: Common people in streets and lanes had horses in groups; those riding mares were shunned and not allowed to join gatherings.

entries.zh: 守閭閻者食粱肉；
entries.en: Even low urban functionaries consumed high-status diets;
entries.literal: Gate-and-lane keepers ate fine grain and meat;

entries.zh: 為吏者長子孫；
entries.en: official families entrenched multigenerational office holding;
entries.literal: those serving as officials grew their sons and grandsons in office;

entries.zh: 居官者以為姓號。
entries.en: and office identity became hereditary social branding.
entries.literal: those residing in office took office-title as clan name.

entries.zh: 人人自愛而重犯法，先行誼而黜媿辱焉。
entries.en: At this stage, social norms still favored propriety and legal caution.
entries.literal: People cherished themselves and feared violating law, first practicing righteousness and rejecting shameful conduct.

entries.zh: 於是罔疏而民富，役財驕溢，或至并兼豪黨之徒以武斷於鄉曲。
entries.en: Prosperity eventually bred private coercive networks and rural strongman politics.
entries.literal: Then legal nets grew sparse while people rich; with wealth and labor arrogant and excessive, some reached annexing powerful cliques and using force to dominate local districts.

entries.zh: 宗室有土，公卿大夫以下爭於奢侈，室廬車服僭上亡限。
entries.en: Elite consumption escalated into status transgression across social strata.
entries.literal: Imperial clans with lands, and from ministers downward, competed in luxury; houses, carriages, and dress usurped higher ranks without limit.

entries.zh: 物盛而衰，固其變也。
entries.en: Prosperity's reversal is built into political cycles.
entries.literal: When things flourish they decline-this is fixed transformation.

entries.zh: 武帝末年，悔征伐之事，乃封丞相為富民侯。
entries.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign, he regretted the campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.
entries.literal: At Emperor Wu's late years, he regretted campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.

entries.zh: 下詔曰：「
entries.en: He issued edict: "
entries.literal: He issued edict: "

entries.zh: 故事，歲漕關東穀四百萬斛以給京師，用卒六萬人。
entries.en: By established practice, four million hu of grain are transported yearly from east of the passes to supply the capital, using sixty thousand laborers.
entries.literal: By old practice, yearly transporting four million hu from east of passes to supply the capital uses sixty thousand laborers.

entries.zh: 宜糴三輔、弘農、河東、上黨、太原郡穀足供京師，可以省關東漕卒過半。」
entries.en: It would be better to purchase grain from the Three Adjacent Regions, Hongnong, Hedong, Shangdang, and Taiyuan to supply the capital, saving more than half the eastern transport laborers.”
entries.literal: Better buy grain from Three Adjacent, Hongnong, Hedong, Shangdang, and Taiyuan to supply the capital, which can save more than half the eastern transport laborers.”

entries.zh: 又白增海租三倍，天子皆從其計。
entries.en: He further proposed higher maritime tax rates, and the emperor approved.
entries.literal: He also requested tripling sea-tax, and the Son of Heaven followed all his plans.

entries.zh: 御史大夫蕭望之奏言：「故御史屬徐宮家在東萊，言往年加海租，魚不出。
entries.en: Censor-in-chief Xiao Wangzhi memorialized: "The household of Xu Gong, formerly a subordinate in the Censorate, is in Donglai. They say that in earlier years, when the sea tax was increased, the fish stopped appearing.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief Xiao Wangzhi memorialized: 'Former censor subordinate Xu Gong's family in Donglai says in past years when sea tax was raised, fish did not come out.

entries.zh: 長老皆言武帝時縣官嘗自漁，海魚不出，後復予民，魚乃出。
entries.en: Elders all say that in Emperor Wu's time, when the county offices themselves fished, sea fish did not appear; later, when fishing was returned to the people, the fish then appeared.
entries.literal: Elders all say that in Emperor Wu's time when county offices fished themselves, sea fish did not emerge; later returned to people, fish then emerged.

entries.zh: 夫陰陽之感，物類相應，萬事盡然。
entries.en: He framed the argument in correlative cosmology: policy pressure can suppress natural-economic response.
entries.literal: As for resonance of yin and yang, things respond by kind; all affairs are like this.

entries.zh: 今壽昌欲近糴漕關內之穀，築倉治船，費直二萬萬餘，有動眾之功，恐生旱氣，民被其災。
entries.en: He warned that Shouchang's plan to buy grain nearby and ship it into the passes would require granaries, boats, more than two hundred million cash, and mass labor, potentially provoking drought and disaster for the people.
entries.literal: Now Shouchang wants to buy grain nearby and ship it by water into the passes, building granaries and repairing boats at a cost of more than two hundred million cash. Such a mobilization of labor, I fear, will generate drought qi and bring disaster upon the people.

entries.zh: 壽昌習於商功分銖之事，其深計遠慮，誠未足任，宜且如故。」
entries.en: He characterized Shouchang as narrowly calculative and urged policy conservatism."
entries.literal: Shouchang is practiced in merchant-like calculations down to fractions; his deep planning and long foresight truly may not suffice-should temporarily remain as before."

entries.zh: 上不聽。
entries.en: The throne rejected that objection.
entries.literal: The emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 漕事果便，壽昌遂白令邊郡皆築倉，以穀賤時增其賈而糴，以利農，穀貴時減賈而糶，名曰常平倉。
entries.en: The policy worked, and Shouchang formalized the Ever-Normal system: buy high enough to support farmers in glut years, sell low enough to stabilize scarcity years.
entries.literal: Transport matters proved convenient; Shouchang then requested border commanderies all build warehouses, buying grain when cheap by raising official price to benefit farmers, and selling when expensive by lowering price, named Ever-Normal Granary.

entries.zh: 民便之。
entries.en: The populace broadly welcomed the system.
entries.literal: People found it convenient.

entries.zh: 上乃下詔，賜壽昌爵關內侯。
entries.en: Shouchang was rewarded with marquis rank for the reform.
entries.literal: The emperor then issued edict granting Shouchang rank Guannei Marquis.

entries.zh: 而蔡癸以好農使勸郡國，至大官。
entries.en: Agrarian advocacy also advanced other officials such as Cai Gui into major posts.
entries.literal: And Cai Gui, by loving agriculture, was sent to encourage commanderies and states, rising to high office.

entries.zh: 是後，外事四夷，內興功利，役費並興，而民去本。
entries.en: External campaigns and internal extraction jointly pulled society away from productive fundamentals.
entries.literal: After this, foreign affairs with border peoples and internal projects for profit both rose, service costs grew together, and people left the root.

entries.zh: 董仲舒說上曰：「春秋它穀不書，至於麥禾不成則書之，以此見聖人於五穀最重麥與禾也。
entries.en: Dong Zhongshu said to the emperor, 'In the Spring and Autumn Annals other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail to ripen it is recorded—showing that the sage gave greatest weight among the five grains to wheat and millet.
entries.literal: Dong Zhongshu advised the emperor: 'In Spring and Autumn, other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail it is recorded-showing sages gave greatest weight among grains to wheat and millet.

entries.zh: 今關中俗不好種麥，是歲失春秋之所重，而損生民之具也。
entries.en: Now the Guanzhong region dislikes planting wheat, and each year it neglects what the Annals values most, diminishing the people's means of livelihood.
entries.literal: Now Guanzhong customs do not like sowing wheat, so each year they lose what Spring and Autumn values and damage the means of people's life.

entries.zh: 願陛下幸詔大司農，使關中民益種宿麥，令毋後時。」
entries.en: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture to have the people of Guanzhong plant more winter wheat and not miss the season.'
entries.literal: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture that Guanzhong people increase winter wheat and not miss seasonal timing.'

entries.zh: 又言：「古者稅民不過什一，其求易共；
entries.en: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;
entries.literal: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;

entries.zh: 使民不過三日，其力易足。
entries.en: and labor demands were limited enough to preserve household capacity.
entries.literal: using people's labor no more than three days, their strength easy to suffice.

entries.zh: 民財內足以養老盡孝，外足以事上共稅，下足以畜妻子極愛，故民說從上。
entries.en: When household subsistence and obligations were simultaneously manageable, political obedience was voluntary.
entries.literal: People's means were enough internally to care for elders and fulfill filiality, externally to serve superiors and taxes, below to support wives and children with full love, thus people gladly followed superiors.

entries.zh: 至秦則不然，用商鞅之法，改帝王之制，除井田，民得賣買，富者田連仟伯，貧者亡立錐之地。
entries.en: Qin reforms enabled severe land concentration and peasant landlessness.
entries.literal: By Qin, not so: using Shang Yang's law, changing imperial kings' institutions, removing well-fields and allowing sale-purchase, rich fields stretched by tens and hundreds while poor had no ground to stand an awl.

entries.zh: 又顓川澤之利，管山林之饒，荒淫越制，踰侈以相高；
entries.en: State and elite control over resource rents fueled escalating luxury and inequality.
entries.literal: It monopolized river-marsh profits and managed mountain-forest riches; wild excess surpassed norms, competing in extravagance.

entries.zh: 邑有人君之尊，里有公侯之富，小民安得不困？
entries.en: Sub-state elite power became so great that ordinary households had little room to survive.
entries.literal: In towns there was lordly dignity, in villages marquis-level wealth-how could small people not be trapped?

entries.zh: 又加月為更卒，已復為正，一歲屯戍，一歲力役，三十倍於古；
entries.en: Labor conscription expanded to levels far above classical precedent.
entries.literal: Further, adding monthly service as garrison labor and regular labor in sequence-one year frontier garrison, one year corvée-threefold ten times antiquity.

entries.zh: 田租口賦，鹽鐵之利，二十倍於古。
entries.en: The combined tax burden became vastly heavier than classical norms.
entries.literal: Field rent and head tax, plus salt and iron revenues, were twenty times antiquity.

entries.zh: 或耕豪民之田，見稅什五。
entries.en: Tenancy under great households imposed predatory effective rates.
entries.literal: Some tilled powerful households' fields and were taxed at five parts in ten.

entries.zh: 故貧民常衣牛馬之衣，而食犬彘之食。
entries.en: Peasant living standards degraded to near-animal subsistence.
entries.literal: Thus poor people often wore ox-and-horse clothing and ate dog-and-pig food.

entries.zh: 重以貪暴之吏，刑戮妄加，民愁亡聊，亡逃山林，轉為盜賊，赭衣半道，斷獄歲以千萬數。
entries.en: Administrative violence plus poverty drove flight, crime, and mass penalization.
entries.literal: Added to this were greedy violent officials with arbitrary executions, people grieving without livelihood, fleeing into hills and forests turning to banditry, red convict clothes half the roads, and yearly prison judgments in tens of millions.

entries.zh: 漢興，循而未改。
entries.en: Early Han inherited much of this structure before reform.
entries.literal: When Han arose, it followed this and had not changed.

entries.zh: 古井田法雖難卒行，宜少近古，限民名田，以澹不足，塞并兼之路。
entries.en: Full restoration may be impossible, but partial anti-concentration land limits were urged.
entries.literal: Though the old well-field law is hard to suddenly enact, one should somewhat approach antiquity: limit titled land holdings to relieve insufficiency and block annexation paths.

entries.zh: 鹽鐵皆歸於民。
entries.en: He advocated devolving salt and iron profits away from monopolistic control.
entries.literal: Salt and iron should all return to the people.

entries.zh: 去奴婢，除專殺之威。
entries.en: He also called for reducing coercive private domination.
entries.literal: Remove slave categories and eliminate power of arbitrary killing.

entries.zh: 薄賦斂，省繇役，以寬民力。
entries.en: Tax and labor burdens should be reduced to restore social stamina.
entries.literal: Lighten taxes and levies, reduce corvée, to relax people's strength.

entries.zh: 然後可善治也。」
entries.en: Only under those conditions could stable good government emerge."
entries.literal: Only then can governance be good."

entries.zh: 仲舒死後，功費愈甚，天下虛耗，人復相食。
entries.en: After his death, fiscal overextension intensified and extreme famine reappeared.
entries.literal: After Zhongshu's death, expenditures and projects grew still greater; the realm emptied and consumed, people again ate one another.

entries.zh: 方今之務，在於力農。」
entries.en: The foremost task now is to strengthen agriculture."
entries.literal: At present the main task lies in strengthening agriculture."

entries.zh: 以趙過為搜粟都尉。
entries.en: He appointed Zhao Guo as Commandant for Grain Collection.
entries.literal: He made Zhao Guo Commandant for Grain Collection.

entries.zh: 過能為代田，一畝三甽。
entries.en: Zhao Guo introduced the three-furrow alternating-field technique.
entries.literal: Guo could make alternating-field method, one mu with three furrows.

entries.zh: 歲代處，故曰代田，古法也。
entries.en: Annual rotation gave the method its name and linked it to older agronomy.
entries.literal: Each year the position alternates, hence called alternating fields-an ancient method.

entries.zh: 后稷始甽田，以二耜為耦，廣尺深尺曰甽，長終畝。
entries.en: The text traces furrow agriculture to Houji with paired-plow technique and fixed furrow dimensions.
entries.literal: Houji first furrowed fields, using two plows as a pair; width one chi and depth one chi was one furrow, running full mu length.

entries.zh: 一畝三甽，一夫三百甽，而播種於甽中。
entries.en: The system quantified furrow units per laborer and sowing pattern.
entries.literal: One mu has three furrows; one man has three hundred furrows, with seed broadcast in furrows.

entries.zh: 苗生葉以上，稍耨隴草，因隤其土以附根苗。
entries.en: As seedlings grew, repeated weeding and hilling reinforced root stability.
entries.literal: When seedlings had leaves, they gradually weeded ridge grass and banked earth onto roots and seedlings.

entries.zh: 故其詩曰：「或芸或芓，黍稷儗儗。」
entries.en: Therefore its poem says: 'Some weed, some hoe; millet and broomcorn stand thick.'
entries.literal: Therefore its poem says: 'Some weed, some hoe; millet and broomcorn stand thick.'

entries.zh: 芸，除草也。
entries.en: 'Yun' is glossed as weed removal.
entries.literal: Yun means removing weeds.

entries.zh: 刭，附根也。
entries.en: The technical term is glossed as hilling soil around roots.
entries.literal: Jing means attaching to roots.

entries.zh: 言苗稍壯，每耨輒附根，比盛暑，隴盡而根深，能風與旱，故儗儗而盛也。
entries.en: Repeated hilling deepens rooting, improving resistance to wind and drought and producing robust growth.
entries.literal: It means as seedlings gradually strengthen, each weeding adds root earth; by peak summer ridges are exhausted and roots deep, able against wind and drought, therefore lush and flourishing.

entries.zh: 其耕耘下種田器，皆有便巧。
entries.en: The method depended on purpose-built, efficiency-oriented tools.
entries.literal: Its plowing, weeding, and sowing implements all had convenient craftsmanship.

entries.zh: 率十二夫為田一井一屋，故具五頃，用耦犁，二牛三人，一歲之收常過縵田具一斛以上，善者倍之。
entries.en: At team scale, paired-plow cultivation produced significant yield gains over conventional broad-field farming.
entries.literal: Generally twelve men farm one well and one household block, thus furnishing five qing, using paired-plow, two oxen and three men; annual harvest commonly exceeds broad-field method by over one hu per mu, and good cases double it.

entries.zh: 過使教田太常、三輔，大農置工巧奴與從事，為作田器。
entries.en: Zhao Guo coordinated central and regional agencies to mass-produce appropriate agricultural implements.
entries.literal: Guo had Grand Ritual, Three Adjacent Regions, and Grand Agriculture set craftsmen slaves and staff to make farming tools.

entries.zh: 二千石遣令長、三老、力田及里父老善田者受田器，學耕種養苗狀。
entries.en: Implementation used official plus local knowledge networks for technique transfer.
entries.literal: Two-thousand-shi officials sent county heads, elder worthies, model farmers, and skilled village elders to receive tools and learn plowing, sowing, and seedling-care methods.

entries.zh: 民或苦少牛，亡以趨澤，故平都令光教過以人輓犁。
entries.en: Some people suffered from too few oxen and had no way to hurry cultivation, so Pingdu magistrate Guang taught Guo human-drawn plowing.
entries.literal: Some people suffered from too few oxen and had no way to hurry cultivation, so Pingdu magistrate Guang taught Guo human-drawn plowing.

entries.zh: 過奏光以為丞，教民相與庸輓犁。
entries.en: Guo recommended Guang as assistant and taught the people to hire one another to pull plows.
entries.literal: Guo recommended Guang as assistant, teaching people to hire together for pulling plows.

entries.zh: 率多人者田日三十畝，少者十三畝，以故田多墾闢。
entries.en: Labor pooling sharply expanded daily tillage and total reclaimed acreage.
entries.literal: Teams with many workers farmed thirty mu per day, fewer workers thirteen mu, therefore much more land was opened.

entries.zh: 過試以離宮卒田其宮壖地，課得穀皆多其旁田畝一斛以上。
entries.en: Controlled trials on palace lands showed consistent yield advantage over adjacent plots.
entries.literal: Guo tested with detached-palace soldiers farming palace perimeter lands; assessed grain was all over one hu per mu more than neighboring fields.

entries.zh: 令命家田三輔公田，又教邊郡及居延城。
entries.en: The method was extended from core regions to frontier administrative zones.
entries.literal: Orders instructed household farming of Three Adjacent Regions public lands, and also taught border commanderies and Juyan city.

entries.zh: 是後邊城、河東、弘農、三輔、太常民皆便代田，用力少而得穀多。
entries.en: Adoption spread widely because it reduced labor while raising output.
entries.literal: After this, border cities, Hedong, Hongnong, Three Adjacent Regions, and Taichang people all found alternating fields convenient, using less labor and gaining more grain.

entries.zh: 至昭帝時，流民稍還，田野益闢，頗有畜積。
entries.en: Under Zhao, population return and land reopening restored modest surplus capacity.
entries.literal: By Emperor Zhao's time, migrants gradually returned, fields further opened, and there were somewhat accumulations.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，用吏多選賢良，百姓安土，歲數豐穰，穀至石五錢，農人少利。
entries.en: Even in abundance under Xuan, very low grain prices squeezed farmer profitability.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended, he used officials often selecting worthy and good; people settled to land, years were often abundant, grain reached five cash per shi, and farmers gained little profit.

entries.zh: 時大司農中丞耿壽昌以善為算能商功利得幸於上，五鳳中奏言：「
entries.en: Then Grand Agriculture vice-director Geng Shouchang, skilled in calculation and discussing utility, favored by the emperor, memorialized in the Wufeng period: “
entries.literal: Then Grand Agriculture vice-director Geng Shouchang, skilled in calculation and discussing utility, favored by the emperor, memorialized in the Wufeng period: “

entries.zh: 平帝崩，王莽居攝，遂篡位。
entries.en: After Ping's death, Wang Mang moved from regency to usurpation.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ping died, Wang Mang as regent then usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 王莽因漢承平之業，匈奴稱藩，百蠻賓服，舟車所通，盡為臣妾，府庫百官之富，天下晏然。
entries.en: He inherited a highly favorable geopolitical and fiscal baseline.
entries.literal: Wang Mang inherited Han's pacified enterprise: Xiongnu as vassals, many southern peoples submitting, where boats and carts reached all became subjects, treasuries and offices wealthy, and the realm tranquil.

entries.zh: 莽一朝有之，其心意未滿，骥小漢家制度，以為疏闊。
entries.en: Though he seized this inheritance in a morning, he was not satisfied and regarded Han institutions as lax and overbroad.
entries.literal: Mang possessed this in a single morning, yet his intentions were not satisfied; he looked down on Han institutions as loose and broad.

entries.zh: 宣帝始賜單于印璽，與天子同，而西南夷鉤町稱王。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan first granted the Chanyu a seal and ribbon equal to the Son of Heaven's, while Gouting among the southwestern Yi claimed the title of king.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan first gave Chanyu seal matching the Son of Heaven's, and in southwest the Gou-ding ruler was called king.

entries.zh: 莽乃遣使易單于印，貶鉤町王為侯。
entries.en: Mang then sent envoys to replace the Chanyu's seal and demoted the King of Gouting to marquis.
entries.literal: Mang then sent envoys to exchange the Chanyu's seal and demoted the King of Gouting to marquis.

entries.zh: 二方始怨，侵犯邊境。
entries.en: Both frontiers reacted with hostility and cross-border aggression.
entries.literal: The two regions then became resentful and invaded borderlands.

entries.zh: 莽遂興師，發三十萬眾，欲同時十道並出，一舉滅匈奴；
entries.en: He planned a massive multi-column campaign for decisive destruction of the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Mang then raised armies, mobilizing three hundred thousand, wanting ten routes to move out simultaneously to destroy Xiongnu in one stroke;

entries.zh: 募發天下囚徒丁男甲卒轉委輸兵器，自負海江淮而至北邊，使者馳傳督趣，海內擾矣。
entries.en: This empire-wide mobilization and logistics drive overstrained society and destabilized the interior.
entries.literal: he recruited convicts and adult males and armored troops from all under heaven, transporting and delivering weapons from sea, river, and Huai to the north frontier; envoys sped by relay to urge them on, and the realm was disturbed.

entries.zh: 又動欲慕古，不度時宜，分裂州郡，改職作官，下令曰：「漢氏減輕田租，三十而稅一，常有更賦，罷癃咸出，而豪民侵陵，分田劫假，厥名三十，實什稅五也。
entries.en: Still eager to imitate antiquity without judging what suited the age, he divided commanderies and provinces, changed offices, created new posts, and issued an order: "The Han reduced the field tax to one part in thirty, yet there were constant labor dues; even the aged and disabled paid them. Powerful households encroached on others, divided up their fields, and seized them under forced or fraudulent loans. In name the tax was one in thirty; in reality it took five parts in ten.
entries.literal: Again desiring to imitate antiquity without measuring present suitability, he split commanderies and altered offices, issuing order: 'Han reduced field rent, taxing one in thirty, with regular additional levies; even infirm and weak all paid, while wealthy households invaded and annexed fields by force and fake loans; nominally one-in-thirty, actually tax one-in-five.

entries.zh: 富者驕而為邪，貧者窮而為姦，俱陷於辜，刑用不錯。
entries.en: Class polarization, he claimed, drove both elite predation and mass criminalization.
entries.literal: The rich grew arrogant and became wicked, the poor desperate and became criminal; both fell into guilt, and punishments were never set aside.

entries.zh: 今更名天下田曰王田，奴婢曰私屬，皆不得賣買。
entries.en: He nationalized land nomenclature and banned buying/selling of land and bonded persons.
entries.literal: Now rename all fields under heaven as King's Fields, and slaves as private dependents, all not allowed to buy or sell.

entries.zh: 其男口不滿八，而田過一井者，分餘田與九族鄉黨。」
entries.en: Where male mouths fewer than eight and fields exceed one well, divide surplus fields to nine-clan and local party.'
entries.literal: Where male mouths fewer than eight and fields exceed one well, divide surplus fields to nine-clan and local party.'

entries.zh: 犯令，法至死，制度又不定，吏緣為姦，天下謷謷然，陷刑者眾。
entries.en: Harsh penalties plus unstable implementation generated widespread administrative abuse and social backlash.
entries.literal: Violating order reached death penalty; institutions were also unstable, officials exploited to commit wickedness, the realm clamored, and many fell into punishment.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，天下大水，關東郡十一尤甚。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, catastrophic floods struck the realm, especially eleven commanderies east of the passes.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, the realm suffered great floods; eleven commanderies east of the passes were especially hard hit.

entries.zh: 二年，齊地飢，穀石三百餘，民多餓死，琅邪郡人相食。
entries.en: In year two Qi suffered famine; grain exceeded three hundred per shi, many starved to death, and in Langya commandery people resorted to cannibalism.
entries.literal: In year two, Qi territory suffered famine; grain was over three hundred per shi, many people died of starvation, and in Langya commandery people ate one another.

entries.zh: 在位諸儒多言鹽鐵官及北假田官、常平倉可罷，毋與民爭利。
entries.en: Office-holding scholars widely urged abolishing the salt-and-iron offices, Beijia field offices, and Ever-Normal Granaries so the state would not compete with the people for profit.
entries.literal: The Confucian scholars in office widely said the salt-and-iron offices, the Beijia field offices, and the Ever-Normal Granaries could be abolished, and that the state should not compete with the people for profit.

entries.zh: 上從其議，皆罷之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted their counsel and abolished them all.
entries.literal: The emperor followed their counsel and abolished them all.

entries.zh: 又罷建章、甘泉宮衛，角抵，齊三服官，省禁苑以予貧民，減諸侯王廟衛卒半。
entries.en: He also abolished Jianzhang and Ganquan palace guards, wrestling entertainment, and Qi's three clothing offices; trimmed the imperial parks for poor commoners; and cut feudal kings' temple guards by half.
entries.literal: He also abolished the Jianzhang and Ganquan palace guards, wrestling entertainment, and Qi's three clothing offices; reduced the forbidden parks and gave portions to poor commoners; and halved the temple guard soldiers of the feudal kings.

entries.zh: 又減關中卒五百人，轉穀振貸窮乏。
entries.en: He also cut Guanzhong garrison troops by five hundred, moved grain, and extended relief loans to the destitute.
entries.literal: He also reduced Guanzhong garrison troops by five hundred, transported grain, and lent relief to the destitute.

entries.zh: 其後用度不足，獨復鹽鐵官。
entries.en: Later, when revenue fell short, he alone restored the salt-and-iron offices.
entries.literal: Afterward, when expenditures proved insufficient, he alone restored the salt-and-iron offices.

entries.zh: 哀帝即位，師丹輔政，建言：「古之聖王莫不設井田，然後治乃可平。
entries.en: When Emperor Ai took the throne, Shi Dan assisted in governance and proposed: "The sage kings of antiquity all established well-field systems; only then could government be made even.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ai took the throne, Shi Dan assisted in governance and proposed: "The sage kings of antiquity all established well-field systems; only then could rule be made even.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝承亡周亂秦兵革之後，天下空虛，故務勸農桑，帥以節儉。
entries.en: Emperor Wen inherited the ruin left by the fall of Zhou and Qin's wars; the realm was empty, so he urged farming and sericulture and led by austerity.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen inherited the era after the fall of Zhou and Qin's disorder and warfare; the realm was empty, so he devoted himself to encouraging farming and sericulture and led by frugality.

entries.zh: 民始充實，未有并兼之害，故不為民田及奴婢為限。
entries.en: The people first became sufficient; annexation had not yet become a problem, so no limits were set on commoners' fields or on slaves and maidservants.
entries.literal: The people first grew sufficient; there was as yet no harm of annexation, so he did not set limits on common people's fields or on slaves and maidservants.

entries.zh: 今累世承平，豪富吏民訾數鉅萬，而貧弱俞困。
entries.en: Now, after generations of peace, powerful officials and wealthy commoners amass fortunes of tens of thousands, while the poor and weak grow ever more distressed.
entries.literal: Now, after generations of peace, powerful and wealthy officials and commoners accumulate tens of thousands in assets, while the poor and weak grow ever more distressed.

entries.zh: 蓋君子為政，貴因循而重改作，然所以有改者，將以救急也。
entries.en: In governance a gentleman values continuity and is wary of reform, yet reform exists precisely to meet emergencies.
entries.literal: Generally in governance the gentleman values continuity and is wary of renovation; yet renovation exists to rescue emergencies.

entries.zh: 亦未可詳，宜略為限。」
entries.en: The details cannot yet be fixed; limits should be set only in outline."
entries.literal: It also cannot yet be made detailed; limits should be set in outline."

entries.zh: 天子下其議。
entries.en: The emperor circulated the proposal for discussion.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven transmitted his proposal for discussion.

entries.zh: 丞相孔光、大司空何武奏請：「諸侯王、列侯皆得名田國中。
entries.en: Chief Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized: "Feudal kings and ranked marquises may all hold titled fields within their domains.
entries.literal: Chief Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized requesting: "Feudal kings and ranked marquises may all hold titled fields within their states.

entries.zh: 列侯在長安，公主名田縣道，及關內侯、吏民名田皆毋過三十頃。
entries.en: For ranked marquises in Chang'an, princesses' titled fields along counties and highways, and titled fields of interior marquises, officials, and commoners, none may exceed thirty qing.
entries.literal: Ranked marquises in Chang'an, princesses' titled fields along counties and highways, and titled fields of interior marquises, officials, and commoners may none exceed thirty qing.

entries.zh: 諸侯王奴婢二百人，列侯、公主百人，關內侯、吏民三十人。
entries.en: Feudal kings might hold two hundred slaves and maidservants; ranked marquises and princesses one hundred; interior marquises, officials, and commoners thirty.
entries.literal: Feudal kings: two hundred slaves and maidservants; ranked marquises and princesses: one hundred; interior marquises, officials, and commoners: thirty.

entries.zh: 期盡三年，犯者沒入官。」
entries.en: Within three years, violators would be confiscated to the state."
entries.literal: Within three years' time, violators would be confiscated to the state."

entries.zh: 時田宅奴婢賈為減賤，丁、傅用事，董賢隆貴，皆不便也。
entries.en: Field, residence, and slave prices had already fallen under the proposal; the Ding and Fu factions held power, Dong Xian was rising in rank, and all found it inconvenient.
entries.literal: At the time the prices of fields, residences, slaves, and maidservants had fallen because of the proposal; the Ding and Fu cliques held power, Dong Xian was exalted in rank, and all found it inconvenient.

entries.zh: 詔書且須後，遂寢不行。
entries.en: An edict said to wait, and the measure was eventually shelved.
entries.literal: An edict said to wait for later, and the matter was eventually shelved and not implemented.

entries.zh: 宮室苑囿府庫之臧已侈，百姓訾富雖不及文景，然天下戶口最盛矣。
entries.en: Palaces, parks, and treasuries were already extravagant; popular wealth still fell short of the Wen and Jing reigns, yet registered households reached their peak.
entries.literal: Palaces, parks, and treasury stores were already extravagant; the people's accumulated wealth, though not equaling the Wen-Jing era, yet the realm's registered households were at their greatest number.

entries.zh: 洪範八政，一曰食，二曰貨。
entries.en: Among the Great Plan's eight state priorities, food comes first and economic goods second.
entries.literal: In the Great Plan's eight policies, first is food, second is goods.

entries.zh: 食謂農殖嘉穀可食之物，貨謂布帛可衣，及金刀龜貝，所以分財布利通有無者也。
entries.en: Here 'food' means agricultural staples, while 'goods' includes textiles and exchange media that move wealth and balance scarcity.
entries.literal: Food means cultivated grain and edible produce; goods mean cloth and silk for clothing, as well as metal, knives, turtle shell, and shells, by which wealth is distributed and surpluses and shortages are exchanged.

entries.zh: 二者，生民之本，興自神農之世。
entries.en: These two pillars of livelihood date back to the era of Shennong.
entries.literal: These two are the basis of people's livelihood, rising from Shennong's age.

entries.zh: 「斲木為耜，煣木為耒，耒鲈之利以教天下」，而食足；
entries.en: "He cut wood into plowshares and bent wood into plow handles; by teaching the world the use of plow and hoe," food became sufficient;
entries.literal: 'He cut wood to make plowshares, bent wood to make handles; with the benefit of plow and hoe he taught the world,' and food became sufficient;

entries.zh: 「日中為市，致天下之民，聚天下之貨，交易而退，各得其所」，而貨通。
entries.en: "At midday they held markets, drew together the people of the world, and gathered the world's goods; after trading, each went away with what he needed," and goods circulated.
entries.literal: 'At midday they made markets, bringing the world's people and gathering the world's goods; they traded and departed, each obtaining what was needed,' and goods circulated.

entries.zh: 食足貨通，然後國實民富，而教化成。
entries.en: When subsistence and exchange are both secure, the state stabilizes, prosperity grows, and governance can truly civilize.
entries.literal: Only when food is sufficient and goods circulate does the state become solid, the people rich, and civil transformation succeed.

entries.zh: 黃帝以下「通其變，使民不倦」。
