entries.en: From the Yellow Emperor onward, rulers 'adapted to change so the people would not weary.'
entries.literal: From the Yellow Emperor onward they 'adapted to change so people would not tire.'

entries.zh: 堯命四子以「敬授民時」，舜命后稷以「黎民祖飢」，是為政首。
entries.en: Yao ordered the Four Sons to "reverently give the people the seasons," and Shun charged Houji with the saying that "the common people first suffered hunger"; these matters stood at the head of government.
entries.literal: Yao ordered the Four Sons to 'reverently deliver the seasons to the people'; Shun ordered Houji regarding 'when the common people first faced hunger'-this was first among governance tasks.

entries.zh: 禹平洪水，定九州，制土田，各因所生遠近，賦入貢棐，楙遷有無，萬國作乂。
entries.en: After flood control, Yu built a territorial-fiscal system that matched local ecology and enabled interregional balancing.
entries.literal: Yu controlled floods, fixed the nine provinces, regulated land by local conditions and distance, set taxes and tribute, shifted surplus and shortage, and the myriad states became orderly.

entries.zh: 殷周之盛，詩書所述，要在安民，富而教之。
entries.en: Classical accounts of Shang and Zhou stress a sequence: stabilize, enrich, then instruct.
entries.literal: In Shang and Zhou's flourishing, as narrated in Odes and Documents, the key was to settle the people, enrich them, and then educate them.

entries.zh: 故易稱「天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位；
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, 'Heaven and Earth's great virtue is to give life; the sage's great treasure is position;
entries.literal: Therefore the Changes says: 'Heaven and Earth's great virtue is giving life; the great treasure of sages is position;

entries.zh: 何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。」
entries.en: what preserves position is benevolence; what gathers the people is wealth.'
entries.literal: what preserves position is benevolence; what gathers people is wealth.'

entries.zh: 財者，帝王所以聚人守位，養成群生，奉順天德，治國安民之本也。
entries.en: Fiscal capacity is thus foundational to humane governance, social reproduction, and political order.
entries.literal: Wealth is what emperors and kings use to gather people and keep position, nourish living beings, follow Heaven's virtue, and govern and settle the state.

entries.zh: 故曰：「不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安；
entries.en: Hence the saying: 'Do not worry about scarcity; worry about uneven distribution. Do not worry about poverty; worry about instability.
entries.literal: So it is said: 'Do not fear fewness; fear unevenness. Do not fear poverty; fear instability;

entries.zh: 蓋均亡貧，和亡寡，安亡傾。」
entries.en: With equity there is no poverty, with harmony no scarcity, and with stability no collapse.'
entries.literal: for with evenness there is no poverty, with harmony no fewness, with stability no collapse.'

entries.zh: 是以聖王域民，築城郭以居之，制廬井以均之，開市肆以通之，設庠序以教之；
entries.en: Sage statecraft combined spatial planning, market integration, and education into one social system.
entries.literal: Therefore sage kings settled the people by defining domains, building walls and cities, regulating hamlets and fields to equalize, opening markets to circulate, and establishing schools to teach.

entries.zh: 士農工商，四民有業。
entries.en: Society was organized into four functional estates: scholar, farmer, artisan, merchant.
entries.literal: Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants-the four peoples each had occupations.

entries.zh: 學以居位曰士，闢土殖穀曰農，作巧成器曰工，通財鬻貨曰商。
entries.en: The categories were occupational and institutional, not merely status labels.
entries.literal: Those who studied to hold office were scholars; those who opened land and grew grain were farmers; those who made skill and crafted tools were artisans; those who moved wealth and sold goods were merchants.

entries.zh: 聖王量能授事，四民陳力受職，故朝亡廢官，邑亡敖民，地亡曠土。
entries.en: By matching talent to function, they reduced bureaucratic idleness, social disorder, and agricultural waste.
entries.literal: Sage kings measured ability and assigned tasks; the four peoples offered strength and accepted office. Thus in court there were no idle offices, in towns no unruly people, and on land no wasted fields.

entries.zh: 太公退，又行之于齊。
entries.en: Taigong later implemented similar principles in the state of Qi.
entries.literal: After Taigong retired, he again practiced this in Qi.

entries.zh: 至管仲相桓公，通輕重之權，曰：「歲有凶穰，故穀有貴賤；
entries.en: When Guan Zhong served as chancellor to Duke Huan, he mastered the regulation of light and heavy [prices], saying, "Years have famine and abundance, so grain has high and low prices;
entries.literal: When Guan Zhong served as chancellor to Duke Huan, he mastered the regulation of light and heavy [prices], saying: "Years have famine and abundance, so grain has high and low prices;

entries.zh: 令有緩急，故物有輕重。
entries.en: when government orders are urgent or lax, commodities become cheap or dear;
entries.literal: when government orders are urgent or lax, commodities become cheap or dear;

entries.zh: 人君不理，則畜賈游於市，乘民之不給，百倍其本矣。
entries.en: If the ruler does not regulate this, hoarding merchants roam the markets, exploiting the people's shortages and multiplying principal a hundredfold.
entries.literal: If the ruler does not regulate this, hoarding merchants roam the markets, exploiting the people's shortages and multiplying principal a hundredfold.

entries.zh: 故萬乘之國必有萬金之賈，千乘之國必有千金之賈者，利有所并也。
entries.en: Thus a state of ten thousand chariots must have merchants of ten thousand in gold, and a state of a thousand chariots merchants of a thousand in gold—because profit is concentrated.
entries.literal: Therefore a ten-thousand-chariot state must have ten-thousand-gold merchants, a thousand-chariot state must have thousand-gold merchants—because gains are concentrated.

entries.zh: 計本量委則足矣。
entries.en: If one calculates capital and measures stored goods, that is enough.
entries.literal: If one calculates base and measures accumulation, it is enough.

entries.zh: 然而民有飢餓者，穀有所臧也。
entries.en: Yet the people may still go hungry because grain is hoarded.
entries.literal: Yet people may still be hungry because grain is hoarded.

entries.zh: 民有餘則輕之，故人君斂之以輕；
entries.en: When the people have surplus, prices are light, so the ruler collects when prices are light;
entries.literal: When people have surplus, prices are light, so rulers collect with light prices;

entries.zh: 民不足則重之，故人君散之以重。
entries.en: when the people lack, prices are heavy, so the ruler releases when prices are heavy.
entries.literal: when people lack, prices are heavy, so rulers release with heavy prices.

entries.zh: 凡輕重斂散之以時，則準平。
entries.en: Whenever collecting and releasing by light and heavy is timed to the season, prices are level.
entries.literal: If collecting and releasing by light and heavy are timed, standards become level.

entries.zh: 使萬室之邑必有萬鍾之臧，臧繈千萬；
entries.en: Let a city of ten thousand households have stores of ten thousand zhong of grain and ten million strings of cash in reserve;
entries.literal: Let a ten-thousand-household city have ten-thousand-zhong stores and ten-million cash strings in reserve;

entries.zh: 千室之邑必有千鍾之臧，臧繈百萬。
entries.en: a city of a thousand households stores of a thousand zhong and a million strings.
entries.literal: a thousand-household city have thousand-zhong stores and one-million cash strings.

entries.zh: 春以奉耕，夏以奉耘，耒耜器械，種饟糧食，必取澹焉。
entries.en: In spring to supply plowing, in summer to supply hoeing—plows, tools, seed, and food must all be drawn from these stores.
entries.literal: In spring provide for plowing, in summer for weeding-plows, tools, seed and food supplies-must all be drawn from these stores.

entries.zh: 故大賈畜家不得豪奪吾民矣。」
entries.en: Then great merchant houses cannot violently seize our people."
entries.literal: Then great merchant houses cannot violently seize our people."

entries.zh: 桓公遂用區區之齊合諸侯，顯伯名。
entries.en: With this policy Duke Huan used small Qi to unite the feudal lords and make his hegemonic name manifest.
entries.literal: Duke Huan then used small Qi to unite the lords and make his hegemonic name manifest.

entries.zh: 上不聽。
entries.en: The emperor did not listen.
entries.literal: The emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 是時，吳以諸侯即山鑄錢，富埒天子，後卒叛逆。
entries.en: Wu's independent minting power enriched it to near-imperial scale and fed later rebellion.
entries.literal: At that time, Wu as feudal state cast coins from mountains, wealth matching the Son of Heaven, and later finally rebelled.

entries.zh: 鄧通，大夫也，以鑄錢財過王者。
entries.en: Deng Tong's private mint fortune became politically notorious.
entries.literal: Deng Tong, though a grandee, in coin-casting wealth exceeded kings.

entries.zh: 故吳、鄧錢布天下。
entries.en: Their privately associated currencies spread widely.
entries.literal: Thus Wu and Deng coin circulated under heaven.

entries.zh: 宣、元、成、哀、平五世，亡所變改。
entries.en: Across the five reigns of Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, nothing was changed.
entries.literal: Across the five reigns of Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, nothing was changed.

entries.zh: 元帝時嘗罷鹽鐵官，三年而復之。
entries.en: During Emperor Yuan's reign, the salt-and-iron offices were once abolished, but they were restored after three years.
entries.literal: During Emperor Yuan's reign, the salt-and-iron offices were once abolished, but they were restored after three years.

entries.zh: 貢禹言：「鑄錢采銅，一歲十萬人不耕，民坐盜鑄陷刑者多。
entries.en: Gong Yu said: 'Minting coin and mining copper keep one hundred thousand men each year from farming, and many people fall into punishment for illicit coining.
entries.literal: Gong Yu said: 'Minting coin and mining copper keeps one hundred thousand men each year from farming, and many people are punished for illicit coining.

entries.zh: 富人臧錢滿室，猶無厭足。
entries.en: The rich hoard rooms full of cash and still are never satisfied.
entries.literal: The rich hoard rooms full of cash and still are never satisfied.

entries.zh: 民心動搖，棄本逐末，耕者不能半，姦邪不可禁，原起於錢。
entries.en: People's hearts are unsettled: they abandon the root and chase the branch; fewer than half remain farmers, and wickedness cannot be curbed. The source lies in money.
entries.literal: People's hearts are unsettled: they abandon the root and chase the branch; fewer than half remain farmers; wickedness cannot be curbed. The source is money.

entries.zh: 疾其末者絕其本，宜罷采珠玉金銀鑄錢之官，毋復以為幣，除其販賣租銖之律，租稅祿賜皆以布帛及穀，使百姓壹意農桑。」
entries.en: If one wants to cure the branch, one must cut off the root. The offices for collecting pearls, jade, gold, and silver and casting coin should be abolished; coin should no longer be used as currency; laws levying taxes by zhu in trade should be removed; and rents, taxes, salaries, and rewards should all be paid in cloth and grain, so the people can devote themselves wholly to farming and sericulture.'
entries.literal: If you want to stop the branch, cut off the root. The offices for mining pearls, jade, gold, and silver and minting coin should be abolished; coin should no longer serve as currency; laws taxing tiny monetary units in trade should be removed; and rents, taxes, salaries, and rewards should all be paid in cloth and grain, so the people can focus wholly on farming and sericulture.'

entries.zh: 議者以為交易待錢，布帛不可尺寸分裂。
entries.en: Discussants replied that exchange depends on money, and cloth cannot be divided precisely by inch and foot.
entries.literal: Discussants replied that exchange depends on money, and cloth cannot be divided precisely by inch and foot.

entries.zh: 禹議亦寢。
entries.en: So Yu's proposal was shelved.
entries.literal: So Yu's proposal was shelved.

entries.zh: 凡貨，金錢布帛之用，夏殷以前其詳靡記云。
entries.en: As for currency in trade—gold, coin, cloth, and silk—what was used before the Xia and Shang is poorly documented.
entries.literal: As for goods in trade—the use of gold, money, cloth, and silk—before the Xia and Shang dynasties the details are not well recorded.

entries.zh: 太公為周立九府圜法：黃金方寸，而重一斤；
entries.en: The Grand Duke of Qi established for Zhou the Nine Treasuries circular standard, fixing the weight of gold first: one square inch of yellow gold weighed one jin;
entries.literal: The Grand Duke of Qi established for Zhou the Nine Treasuries circular standard: a square inch of yellow gold weighed one jin;

entries.zh: 錢圜函方，輕重以銖；
entries.en: coins were round outside and square within, with weight measured in zhu;
entries.literal: coins were round on the outside and square in the hollow, their weight measured in zhu;

entries.zh: 布帛廣二尺二寸為幅，長四丈為匹。
entries.en: A bolt of cloth was two chi two cun wide and four zhang long.
entries.literal: A bolt of cloth was two chi two cun wide and four zhang long.

entries.zh: 故貨寶於金，利於刀，流於泉，布於布，束於帛。
entries.en: Thus wealth was stored in gold, advantage lay in knife-money, circulation in spring-coin, spread in cloth, and bundling in silk.
entries.literal: Thus wealth was treasured in gold, advantage in knife-money, circulation in spring-coin, spread in cloth, bundled in silk.

entries.zh: 其後三十六歲，孝武元光中，河決於瓠子，東南注鉅野，通於淮、泗。
entries.en: Thirty-six years after that, in Emperor Wu's Yuanguang period, a breach at Huzi sent the river southeast into Juye, where it linked to the Huai and Si.
entries.literal: Thirty-six years later, in Emperor Wu's Yuanguang era, the river burst at Huzi, flowing southeast into Juye and connecting with Huai and Si.

entries.zh: 上使汲黯、鄭當時興人徒塞之，輒復壞。
entries.en: The emperor dispatched Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to mobilize workers for repairs, but each closure failed and broke open again.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to mobilize laborers to block it, but it repeatedly broke again.

entries.zh: 是時武安侯田蚡為丞相，其奉邑食鄃。
entries.en: At the time, Chancellor Tian Fen, Marquis of Wu'an, drew his sustenance revenues from Yu.
entries.literal: At that time Marquis Wu'an Tian Fen was chancellor, and his sustenance fief was at Yu.

entries.zh: 鄃居河北，河決而南則鄃無水災，邑收入多。
entries.en: Yu stood north of the river, so a southward breach spared his territory from floods and increased his fief income.
entries.literal: Yu lay north of the river; if the river broke southward then Yu had no flood disaster, and fief income was greater.

entries.zh: 蚡言於上曰：「江河之決皆天事，未易以人力彊塞，彊塞之未必順天。」
entries.en: Tian Fen told the emperor, "Major river breaches are Heaven's doing. Human force cannot easily compel them shut, and forcing closure may violate Heaven's pattern."
entries.literal: Fen said to the emperor: "Breaches of great rivers are all Heaven's affairs; it is not easy to force closure by human strength, and forced closure may not accord with Heaven."

entries.zh: 而望氣用數者亦以為然，是以久不復塞也。
entries.en: Diviners and numerological experts agreed, so the breach remained unsealed for a long period.
entries.literal: Those who observed qi and used calculations also agreed, and therefore for a long time it was not blocked again.

entries.zh: 自河決瓠子後二十餘歲，歲因以數不登，而梁楚之地尤甚。
entries.en: Over twenty years after the Huzi breach, harvest failures persisted, with Liang and Chu hit especially hard.
entries.literal: More than twenty years after the Huzi breach, harvests repeatedly failed year by year, especially in Liang and Chu.

entries.zh: 上既封禪，巡祭山川，其明年，乾封少雨。
entries.en: After the emperor completed the Feng-Shan and toured sacrificial sites, the next year brought scant rainfall.
entries.literal: After the emperor had performed Feng and Shan sacrifices and toured mountain-river rites, the following year in Qianfeng had little rain.

entries.zh: 上乃使汲仁、郭昌發卒數萬人塞瓠子決河。
entries.en: He then dispatched Ji Ren and Guo Chang, mobilizing tens of thousands to close the Huzi breach.
entries.literal: The emperor then sent Ji Ren and Guo Chang to mobilize tens of thousands to block the Huzi breach.

entries.zh: 於是上以用事萬里沙，則還自臨決河，湛白馬玉璧，令群臣從官自將軍以下皆負薪寘決河。
entries.en: While conducting rites at Wansha, the emperor personally returned to the breach, offered a white horse and jade disc to the river, and required all officials from the generals down to carry fuel bundles into the closure works.
entries.literal: At this time the emperor, while conducting rites at Wansha, returned to inspect the breach, sank white horse and jade disk offerings, and ordered all ministers and attendants from generals downward to carry firewood and place it in the breach.

entries.zh: 是時東郡燒草，以故薪柴少，而下淇園之竹以為揵。
entries.en: Because burned grasslands in Dong Commandery left little timber, bamboo from Qiyuan was felled for piling stakes.
entries.literal: At this time Dong Commandery had burned grasslands, so fuel was scarce; bamboo from Qiyuan was cut down for stakes.

entries.zh: 上既臨河決，悼功之不成，乃作歌曰：
entries.en: Standing at the breached river and grieving the unfinished work, the emperor composed this song:
entries.literal: After the emperor came to the river breach and lamented unfinished labor, he composed a song:

entries.zh: 瓠子決兮將奈何？
entries.en: Huzi has broken - what are we to do?
entries.literal: Huzi has burst - what can be done?

entries.zh: 浩浩洋洋，慮殫為河。
entries.en: The waters roll boundless; all my thoughts are consumed by the river.
entries.literal: Vast and surging, all my thoughts are exhausted by the river.

entries.zh: 殫為河兮地不得寧，功無已時兮吾山平。
entries.en: Spent in struggle with the river, the land finds no rest; the labor never ends, and my sacred hills are worn flat.
entries.literal: Exhausted by the river, the land cannot be at peace; the work has no end, and my mountain is leveled.

entries.zh: 吾山平兮鉅野溢，魚弗鬱兮柏冬日。
entries.en: When the mountain sinks low, Juye floods wide; fish will not stay confined, and cypress stands through winter glare.
entries.literal: When my mountain is leveled, Juye overflows; fish are not pent in, and cypress endures winter sun.

entries.zh: 正道弛兮離常流，蛟龍騁兮放遠游。
entries.en: The true course is loosened from its ancient flow; dragons and river-serpents run wild in distant wanderings.
entries.literal: The proper channel slackens and leaves its constant current; dragons and flood-serpents race and roam afar.

entries.zh: 歸舊川兮神哉沛，不封禪兮安知外！
entries.en: Return, river, to your old bed - divine and overflowing! Had I not made Feng and Shan, how could I know these outer realms?
entries.literal: Return to old channels - O spirits, abundant! Had I not performed Feng and Shan, how would I know what lies beyond!

entries.zh: 皇謂河公兮何不仁，泛濫不止兮愁吾人！
entries.en: I, the emperor, ask the River Lord: why this cruelty? Your endless floods bring only sorrow to my people.
entries.literal: I, the august one, ask Lord River: why so unbenevolent? You flood without ceasing and grieve my people!

entries.zh: 齧桑浮兮淮、泗滿，久不反兮水維緩。
entries.en: You tear at mulberry banks and drift onward; Huai and Si run full to bursting, and long have not returned to bounds.
entries.literal: Gnawing mulberry banks afloat, Huai and Si are full; long without return, the waters' cords slacken.

entries.zh: 一曰：
entries.en: Another stanza says:
entries.literal: Another verse says:

entries.zh: 河湯湯兮激潺湲，北渡回兮迅流難。
entries.en: The river roars and foams in racing torrents; crossing north then turning back, the current is too fierce.
entries.literal: The river boils and surges in rushing rapids; crossing north and wheeling back, swift currents are hard.

entries.zh: 搴長茭兮湛美玉，河公許兮薪不屬。
entries.en: We raise long reeds and sink bright jade; though the River Lord accepts, the timber lines still do not join.
entries.literal: Lifting long reeds, we sink fine jade; Lord River consents, yet firewood does not connect.

entries.zh: 薪不屬兮衛人罪，燒蕭條兮噫乎何以御水！
entries.en: If timber fails to link, the fault is Wey's; with all scrub burned bare, alas, how are we to master the flood?
entries.literal: Timber not connected - this is the fault of Wey people; with withered brush burned away, alas, how can we control the waters!

entries.zh: 隤林竹兮揵石菑，宣防塞兮萬福來。
entries.en: Cut bamboo from the woods, drive stakes, and brace stone embankments; when Xuanfang is sealed, a myriad blessings will arrive.
entries.literal: Felled forest bamboo forms stakes and stone barriers; once Xuanfang is sealed, ten thousand blessings come.

entries.zh: 自塞宣房後，河復北決於館陶，分為屯氏河，東北經魏郡、清河、信都、勃海入海，廣深與大河等，故因其自然，不隄塞也。
entries.en: After the Xuanfang closure, the river again breached north at Guantao and formed the Tunshi branch, running northeast through Wei, Qinghe, Xindu, and Bohai to the sea. Its size matched the main stream, so officials let it run naturally rather than force closure.
entries.literal: After Xuanfang was blocked, the River again broke north at Guantao, split as Tunshi River, and flowed northeast through Wei, Qinghe, Xindu, and Bohai to the sea, equal in width and depth to the main river; therefore they followed its natural course and did not dike it shut.

entries.zh: 此開通後，館陶東北四五郡雖時小被水害，而兗州以南六郡無水憂。
entries.en: Afterward, though four or five northeastern commanderies around Guantao suffered occasional minor flooding, the six commanderies south of Yan were largely free from water disasters.
entries.literal: After this opening, although four or five commanderies northeast of Guantao were sometimes slightly harmed by floods, the six commanderies south of Yan had no flood worries.

entries.zh: 宣帝地節中，光祿大夫郭昌使行河。
entries.en: During Emperor Xuan's Dijie period, Grand Master Guo Chang was dispatched to inspect the Yellow River.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xuan's Dijie era, Guo Chang, Grand Master of Palace Revenue, was sent to inspect the river.

entries.zh: 北曲三所水流之勢皆邪直貝丘縣。
entries.en: He found that all three northern bends drove the current obliquely toward Beiqiu County.
entries.literal: At three northern bends, the water flow all slanted directly toward Beiqiu County.

entries.zh: 恐水盛，隄防不能禁，乃各更穿渠，直東，經東郡界中，不令北曲。
entries.en: Fearing that floodwater might overwhelm the dikes, he cut fresh channels straight east through Dong Commandery to prevent the current from returning northward.
entries.literal: Fearing high waters the dikes could not restrain, he reopened channels, each running straight east through Dong Commandery, not allowing northern bends.

entries.zh: 渠通利，百姓安之。
entries.en: The new channels worked well, and local people accepted them.
entries.literal: The channels flowed smoothly and the people were at ease with them.

entries.zh: 元帝永光五年，河決清河靈鳴犢口，而屯氏河絕。
entries.en: In Yongguang year five under Emperor Yuan, the river breached at Lingmingdukou in Qinghe, and the Tunshi branch was severed.
entries.literal: In Emperor Yuan's Yongguang year five, the River broke at Lingmingdukou in Qinghe, and the Tunshi River was cut off.

entries.zh: 夏書：禹堙洪水十三年，過家不入門。
entries.en: The Book of Xia says that Yu spent thirteen years controlling the great flood, even passing his own home without going inside.
entries.literal: In the Book of Xia it says: Yu dammed the great floods for thirteen years, passing his home without entering its gate.

entries.zh: 陸行載車，水行乘舟，泥行乘毳，山行則梮，以別九州；
entries.en: He used carts on dry ground, boats on water, drag-sleds in marsh, and spiked footwear in the mountains, mapping out the nine provinces.
entries.literal: On land he rode carts; on water he rode boats; in mud he rode sledges; in mountains he used spiked shoes, thereby distinguishing the nine provinces.

entries.zh: 隨山浚川，任土作貢；
entries.en: Tracing the mountain ranges, he dredged the waterways and set tribute quotas according to local soils.
entries.literal: He followed the mountains and dredged the rivers; according to the soils he established tribute.

entries.zh: 通九道，陂九澤，度九山。
entries.en: He cleared the nine transport routes, regulated the nine marshlands, and surveyed the nine major mountain systems.
entries.literal: He opened the nine routes, embanked the nine marshes, and measured the nine mountains.

entries.zh: 然河災之羨溢，害中國也尤甚。
entries.en: Of all flood disasters, the Yellow River's overflows were the most destructive to the central plains.
entries.literal: Yet among river disasters, the overflow of the Yellow River harmed the central states most severely.

entries.zh: 唯是為務，故道河自積石，歷龍門，南到華陰，東下底柱，及盟津、雒內，至于大伾。
entries.en: So Yu focused on this above all: he redirected the Yellow River from Jishi through Longmen, south to Huayin, east past Dizhu, through Mengjin and the Luo region, and on to Dapi.
entries.literal: Because this was the urgent task, he guided the River from Jishi, through Longmen, south to Huayin, east down Dizhu, then through Mengjin and within Luo, reaching Dapi.

entries.zh: 於是禹以為河所從來者高，水湍悍，難以行平地，數為敗，乃釃二渠以引其河，北載之高地，過洚水，至於大陸，播為九河，同為迎河，入于勃海。
entries.en: Yu recognized that the river descended from great height with ferocious current, impossible to tame on open plain and repeatedly breaching control. He therefore cut two diversion channels, led the flow north over higher terrain, past the Hong waters to the Dalu plain, where it dispersed into the Nine Rivers, rejoined as the Ying River system, and emptied into the Bohai.
entries.literal: Then Yu considered that the river source was high and the waters swift and violent, hard to move across flatland and often causing failures. So he split two channels to divert the river, carrying it north onto high ground, passing Hong waters, reaching Dalu, where it spread as the Nine Rivers, joined as Ying River, and entered Bohai.

entries.zh: 九川既疏，九澤既陂，諸夏乂安，功施乎三代。
entries.en: With the nine rivers dredged and the marshes regulated, the Xia heartland was pacified, and the benefit lasted through three dynasties.
entries.literal: Once the nine rivers were dredged and the nine marshes embanked, the Xia lands were governed and at peace; this achievement benefited three dynasties.

entries.zh: 高祖為布衣時，嘗從耳遊。
entries.en: Before he rose to power, Gaozu had once traveled with Zhang Er.
entries.literal: Before he rose to power, Gaozu had once traveled with Zhang Er.

entries.zh: 秦滅魏，購求耳千金，餘五百金。
entries.en: After Qin conquered Wei, bounties were posted: one thousand jin for Zhang Er and five hundred for Chen Yu.
entries.literal: After Qin conquered Wei, bounties were posted: one thousand jin for Zhang Er and five hundred for Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 兩人變名姓，俱之陳，為里監門。
entries.en: They changed their identities, fled to Chen, and worked as local gatekeepers.
entries.literal: They changed their identities, fled to Chen, and worked as local gatekeepers.

entries.zh: 吏嘗以過笞餘，餘欲起，耳攝使受笞。
entries.en: Once an official flogged Chen Yu over a minor offense. Chen Yu wanted to rise up against him, but Zhang Er held him back and made him take the beating.
entries.literal: Once, when an official beat Chen Yu for a minor fault, Chen Yu tried to resist, but Zhang Er restrained him and made him endure it.

entries.zh: 吏去，耳數之曰：「始吾與公言何如？
entries.en: After the official left, Zhang Er rebuked him, saying, "What did I tell you from the start?
entries.literal: After the official left, Zhang Er rebuked him, saying, "What did I tell you from the beginning?

entries.zh: 今見小辱而欲死一吏乎？」
entries.en: Would you throw your life away over a petty insult from a minor clerk?"
entries.literal: Would you throw away your life over a petty humiliation from a minor clerk?"

entries.zh: 餘謝罪。
entries.en: Chen Yu apologized.
entries.literal: Chen Yu apologized.

entries.zh: 耳之國，餘愈怒曰：「耳與餘功等也，今耳王，餘獨侯。」
entries.en: When Zhang Er took his kingdom, Chen Yu grew even angrier and said, "Zhang Er and I rendered equal service, yet he is king while I am only a marquis."
entries.literal: When Zhang Er took his kingdom, Chen Yu grew even angrier and said, "Zhang Er and I rendered equal service, yet now he is king while I am only a marquis."

entries.zh: 及齊王田榮叛楚，餘乃使夏說說田榮曰：「項羽為天下宰不平，盡王諸將善地，徙故王王惡地，今趙王乃居代！
entries.en: When Qi's king Tian Rong rebelled against Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yue to persuade Tian Rong, saying: "Xiang Yu is unfair as steward of all under heaven. He made all his generals kings over good lands and moved former kings to bad lands; now the King of Zhao actually dwells in Dai!
entries.literal: When Qi's king Tian Rong rebelled against Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yue to persuade Tian Rong that Xiang Yu ruled the realm unjustly, giving good lands to his own generals and moving former kings to bad lands.

entries.zh: 願王假臣兵，請以南皮為扞蔽。」
entries.en: We beg Your Majesty to lend your servant troops, and I request to use Nanpi as a defensive screen."
entries.literal: Chen Yu asked to borrow troops, offering Nanpi as a defensive screen."

entries.zh: 田榮欲樹黨，乃遣兵從餘。
entries.en: Tian Rong wanted to build his own faction and sent troops to aid Chen Yu.
entries.literal: Tian Rong wanted to build his own faction and sent troops to aid Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 餘悉三縣兵，襲常山王耳。
entries.en: Chen Yu gathered all forces from his three counties and struck Zhang Er, King of Changshan.
entries.literal: Chen Yu gathered all forces from his three counties and struck Zhang Er, King of Changshan.

entries.zh: 耳敗走，曰：「漢王與我有故，而項王彊，立我，我欲之楚。」
entries.en: Defeated, Zhang Er fled and said, "The Han king and I have old ties, but King Xiang is strong and installed me as king, so I mean to go to Chu."
entries.literal: Defeated, Zhang Er fled and said, "The Han king and I have old ties, but King Xiang is strong and was the one who made me king; I intend to go to Chu."

entries.zh: 甘公曰：「漢王之入關，五星聚東井。
entries.en: "Gan Gong said that when the Han king entered the passes, the Five Planets gathered in Eastern Well.
entries.literal: Gan Gong said that when the Han king entered the passes, the Five Planets gathered in Eastern Well.

entries.zh: 東井者，秦分也。
entries.en: Eastern Well belonged to Qin's celestial division.
entries.literal: Eastern Well belonged to Qin's celestial division.

entries.zh: 先至必王。
entries.en: He who arrived first would surely become king.
entries.literal: He who arrived first would surely become king.

entries.zh: 楚雖彊，後必屬漢。」
entries.en: So although Chu was strong, it would ultimately submit to Han."
entries.literal: So although Chu was strong, it would ultimately submit to Han."

entries.zh: 耳走漢。
entries.en: Zhang Er therefore fled to Han.
entries.literal: Zhang Er therefore fled to Han.

entries.zh: 漢亦還定三秦，方圍章邯廢丘。
entries.en: Han had also turned back to pacify the Three Qins and was besieging Zhang Han at Feiqiu.
entries.literal: Han had also turned back to pacify the Three Qins and was besieging Zhang Han at Feiqiu.

entries.zh: 耳謁漢王，漢王厚遇之。
entries.en: Zhang Er met the Han king, who received him generously.
entries.literal: Zhang Er met the Han king, who received him generously.

entries.zh: 七年，高祖從平城過趙，趙王旦暮自上食，體甚卑，有子婿禮。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Gaozu passed through Zhao on his way from Pingcheng. The king of Zhao personally served his meals morning and evening, humbling himself like a son-in-law.
entries.literal: In year seven, when Gaozu passed through Zhao from Pingcheng, the Zhao king personally served meals from morning to night with extreme humility, like a son-in-law.

entries.zh: 高祖箕踞罵詈，甚慢之。
entries.en: Gaozu sat with legs spread, cursing and insulting him, and treated him with great contempt.
entries.literal: Gaozu sat with legs spread, cursing and insulting him, and treated him with great contempt.

entries.zh: 趙相貫高、趙午年六十餘，故耳客也，怒曰：「吾王孱王也！」
entries.en: Zhao's chancellor Guan Gao and Zhao Wu, both over sixty and former retainers of Zhang Er, grew angry and said, "Our king is a weakling!"
entries.literal: Zhao's chancellor Guan Gao and Zhao Wu, both over sixty and former followers of Zhang Er, grew angry and said, "Our king is a weakling!"

entries.zh: 說敖曰：「天下豪桀並起，能者先立，今王事皇帝甚恭，皇帝遇王無禮，請為王殺之。」
entries.en: They urged Zhang Ao, saying, "Heroes are rising everywhere, and the able establish themselves first. You serve the emperor with great respect, yet he treats you without courtesy — let us kill him for you."
entries.literal: They urged Zhang Ao, saying, "Heroes are rising everywhere, and the able establish themselves first. The king serves the emperor with great respect, yet the emperor treats the king without courtesy — let us kill him for the king."

entries.zh: 敖齧其指出血，曰：「君何言之誤！
entries.en: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and said, "How wrong you are to speak of this!
entries.literal: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and said, "How wrong you are to speak this way!

entries.zh: 且先王亡國，賴皇帝得復國，德流子孫，秋豪皆帝力也。
entries.en: My father lost his state, and only through the emperor did he recover it; his kindness extends to his descendants — even the smallest benefit comes from the emperor.
entries.literal: My father lost his state, and only through the emperor did he recover it; his kindness flows to his descendants — even the smallest benefit comes from imperial power.

entries.zh: 願君無復出口。」
entries.en: Please never speak of this again."
entries.literal: I beg you never to speak of this again."

entries.zh: 貫高等十餘人相謂曰：「
entries.en: "Guan Gao and more than ten others then discussed the matter among themselves.
entries.literal: Guan Gao and more than ten others then discussed the matter among themselves.

entries.zh: 四年夏，立耳為趙王。
entries.en: In the fourth year, in summer, Zhang Er was made King of Zhao.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, summer, Zhang Er was established as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 五年秋，耳薨，諡曰景王。
entries.en: In the fifth year, in autumn, Er died and was given the posthumous title King Jing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, autumn, Er died; he was posthumously titled King Jing.

entries.zh: 子敖嗣立為王，尚高祖長女魯元公主，為王后。
entries.en: His son Ao succeeded as king, married Gaozu's eldest daughter Princess Lu Yuan, and she became queen.
entries.literal: His son Ao succeeded and was established as king. He married Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Lu Yuan, who became queen.

entries.zh: 九年，貫高怨家知其謀，告之。
entries.en: In year nine, an enemy of Guan Gao learned of the plot and reported it.
entries.literal: In year nine, an enemy of Guan Gao learned of the plot and reported it.

entries.zh: 於是上逮捕趙王諸反者。
entries.en: The emperor then arrested the King of Zhao and those implicated in the plot.
entries.literal: The emperor then arrested the King of Zhao and those implicated in the plot.

entries.zh: 趙午等十餘人皆爭自剄，貫高獨怒罵曰：「誰令公等為之？
entries.en: Zhao Wu and more than ten others all vied to cut their own throats. Guan Gao alone cursed them in anger, saying, "Who told you gentlemen to do this?
entries.literal: Zhao Wu and more than ten others all struggled to cut their own throats, but Guan Gao alone cursed them angrily, saying, "Who told you to do this?

entries.zh: 今王實無謀，而并捕王；
entries.en: The king in truth had no plot, yet he is being arrested along with us;
entries.literal: The king in truth had no plot, yet he is being arrested along with us;

entries.zh: 公等死，誰當白王不反者？」
entries.en: if you all die, who will clear the king of the charge of rebellion?"
entries.literal: if you all die, who will clear the king of the charge of rebellion?"

entries.zh: 乃檻車與王詣長安。
entries.en: He and the king were taken in caged carts to Chang'an.
entries.literal: He and the king were taken in caged carts to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 高對獄曰：「獨吾屬為之，王不知也。」
entries.en: "In interrogation, Guan Gao said only his own group had acted and the king knew nothing."
entries.literal: In interrogation, Guan Gao said only his own group had acted and the king knew nothing.

entries.zh: 吏榜笞數千，刺爇，身無完者，終不復言。
entries.en: Officials beat him with thousands of strokes and burned him with irons; his body had no uninjured part, yet he never changed his statement.
entries.literal: Officials beat him with thousands of strokes and burned him with irons; his body had no uninjured part, yet he never changed his statement.

entries.zh: 呂后數言張王以魯元故，不宜有此。
entries.en: Empress Lu repeatedly said Zhang Ao, because of his tie to Princess Lu Yuan, should not be treated this way.
entries.literal: Empress Lu repeatedly said Zhang Ao, because of his tie to Princess Lu Yuan, should not be treated this way.

entries.zh: 上怒曰：「使長敖據天下，豈少乃女虖！」
entries.en: The emperor angrily replied, "If Zhang Ao held the realm, would your daughter be the only woman he took?"
entries.literal: The emperor angrily replied, "If Zhang Ao held the realm, would your daughter be the only one he took?"

entries.zh: 廷尉以貫高辭聞，上曰：「壯士！
entries.en: When the chief justice reported Guan Gao's testimony, the emperor said, "What a strong man!
entries.literal: When the chief justice reported Guan Gao's testimony, the emperor said, "A true strong man!

entries.zh: 誰知者，以私問之。」
entries.en: Whoever knows him, go and question him privately."
entries.literal: Whoever knows him, go question him privately."

entries.zh: 中大夫泄公曰：「臣素知之，此固趙國立名義不侵為然諾者也。」
entries.en: Grandee Xie Gong said, "I have long known him; he is exactly the sort of man in Zhao who values honor and will not break a sworn promise."
entries.literal: Grandee Xie Gong said, "I have long known him; he is exactly the sort of man in Zhao who establishes a reputation for righteousness and will not violate a sworn promise."

entries.zh: 上使泄公持節問之箯輿前。
entries.en: The emperor sent Xie Gong with tally-staff credentials to question Guan Gao before his prison litter.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Xie Gong with tally-staff credentials to question Guan Gao before his prison litter.

entries.zh: 卬視泄公，勞若如平生歡。
entries.en: Guan Gao raised his head, recognized Xie Gong, and greeted him as warmly as in earlier days.
entries.literal: Guan Gao raised his head, recognized Xie Gong, and greeted him as warmly as in earlier days.

entries.zh: 與語，問張王果有謀不。
entries.en: In conversation, Xie Gong asked whether Zhang Ao had truly plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: In conversation, Xie Gong asked whether Zhang Ao had truly plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 高曰：「人情豈不各愛其父母妻子哉？
entries.en: Guan Gao said, "Does not every man love his parents, wife, and children?
entries.literal: Guan Gao said, "Does not every man love his parents, wife, and children?

entries.zh: 今吾三族皆以論死，豈以王易吾親哉！
entries.en: Now my three clans are already condemned to death — how could I trade the king for my kin!
entries.literal: Now my three clans are already condemned to death — how could I trade the king for my kin!

entries.zh: 顧為王實不反，獨吾等為之。」
entries.en: In truth the king did not rebel; only we did this."
entries.literal: In truth the king did not rebel; only we did this."

entries.zh: 具道本根所以，王不知狀。
entries.en: He laid out the full roots and circumstances in detail, showing the king had no knowledge of it.
entries.literal: He laid out the full roots and circumstances in detail, showing the king had no knowledge of it.

entries.zh: 於是泄公具以報上，上乃赦趙王。
entries.en: Xie Gong reported all this fully to the emperor, and the emperor then pardoned the King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Xie Gong reported all this fully to the emperor, and the emperor then pardoned the King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 漢二年，東擊楚，使告趙，欲與俱。
entries.en: In Han year two, Han attacked Chu in the east and notified Zhao, seeking joint action.
entries.literal: In Han year two, Han attacked Chu in the east and notified Zhao, seeking joint action.

entries.zh: 餘曰：「漢殺張耳乃從。」
entries.en: Chen Yu said, "I will join you only if Han kills Zhang Er."
entries.literal: Chen Yu said, "I will follow only if Han kills Zhang Er."

entries.zh: 於是漢求人類耳者，斬其頭遺餘，餘乃遣兵助漢。
entries.en: The Han side then found a man who looked like Zhang Er, cut off his head, and sent it to Chen Yu. Only then did Chen Yu send troops to assist Han.
entries.literal: Han then found a man who resembled Zhang Er, beheaded him, and sent the head to Chen Yu, who then dispatched troops to help Han.

entries.zh: 漢敗於彭城西，餘亦聞耳詐死，即背漢。
entries.en: After Han's defeat west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu learned Zhang Er had only feigned death and therefore turned against Han.
entries.literal: After Han's defeat west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu learned Zhang Er had only feigned death and therefore turned against Han.

entries.zh: 漢遣耳與韓信擊破趙井陘，斬餘泜水上，追殺趙王歇襄國。
entries.en: Han sent Zhang Er and Han Xin against Zhao. They defeated Zhao at Jingxing, killed Chen Yu by the Zhi River, and pursued King Xie to Xiangguo, where they put him to death.
entries.literal: Han sent Zhang Er with Han Xin, who broke Zhao at Jingxing, beheaded Chen Yu at the Zhi River, and pursued and killed King Xie at Xiangguo.

entries.zh: 吾等非也。
entries.en: They said, The fault is ours.
entries.literal: They said, The fault is ours.

entries.zh: 吾王長者，不背德。
entries.en: Their king was an honorable elder who would not betray gratitude.
entries.literal: Their king was an honorable elder who would not betray gratitude.

entries.zh: 且吾等義不辱，今帝辱我王，故欲殺之，何乃汙王為？
entries.en: Moreover, we cannot bear this insult to our honor; the emperor has humiliated our king, so we wish to kill him — why should we involve the king and stain him?
entries.literal: Moreover, in honor we cannot bear insult; now the emperor has insulted our king, so we wish to kill him — why should we stain the king by involving him?

entries.zh: 事成歸王，事敗獨身坐耳。」
entries.en: If the plan succeeds, the credit goes to the king; if it fails, we alone will bear the punishment."
entries.literal: If the plan succeeds, the credit goes to the king; if it fails, we alone will bear punishment."

entries.zh: 八年，上從東垣過。
entries.en: In year eight, the emperor passed through Dongyuan.
entries.literal: In year eight, the emperor passed through Dongyuan.

entries.zh: 貫高等乃壁人柏人，要之置廁。
entries.en: Guan Gao's group secretly placed men at Bairen to strike him in a latrine.
entries.literal: Guan Gao's group secretly placed men at Bairen to strike him in a latrine.

entries.zh: 上過欲宿，心動，問曰：「縣名為何？」
entries.en: "The emperor considered lodging there, then felt uneasy and asked the county name."
entries.literal: The emperor considered lodging there, then felt uneasy and asked the county name.

entries.zh: 曰：「柏人。」
entries.en: "He was told it was Bairen."
entries.literal: He was told it was Bairen.

entries.zh: 「柏人者，迫於人！」
entries.en: He said, "Bairen — that sounds like being forced by men!"
entries.literal: He said, "Bairen — forced by men!"

entries.zh: 不宿去。
entries.en: So he did not stay and left.
entries.literal: So he did not stay and left.

entries.zh: 上賢高能自立然諾，使泄公赦之，告曰：「張王已出，上多足下，故赦足下。」
entries.en: The emperor admired Guan Gao for holding to his pledged word. He ordered Xie Gong to release him and tell him: "Zhang Wang has already been released; the emperor greatly values you, so you are pardoned."
entries.literal: The emperor admired Guan Gao for holding to his pledged word. He ordered Xie Gong to release him and tell him: Zhang Wang has already been released; the emperor greatly values you, so you are pardoned.

entries.zh: 高曰：「所以不死，白張王不反耳。
entries.en: Guan Gao said, "The reason I did not die was to clear the King of Zhao of rebellion.
entries.literal: Guan Gao said, "The reason I did not die was to clear Zhang Wang of rebellion.

entries.zh: 今王已出，吾責塞矣。
entries.en: Now that the king is out, my duty is fulfilled.
entries.literal: Now that the king is out, my duty is fulfilled.

entries.zh: 且人臣有篡弒之名，豈有面目復事上哉！」
entries.en: Moreover, a subject who bears the name of plotting regicide — how could he face serving the ruler again!"
entries.literal: Moreover, a subject who bears the name of plotting regicide — how could he have the face to serve the ruler again!"

entries.zh: 乃仰絕亢而死。
entries.en: He then threw back his head and died by cutting his throat.
entries.literal: He then threw back his head and died by cutting his throat.

entries.zh: 敖已出，尚魯元公主如故，封為宣平侯。
entries.en: After Zhang Ao was released, he remained married to Princess Luyuan as before and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping.
entries.literal: After Zhang Ao was released, he remained married to Princess Luyuan as before and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping.

entries.zh: 於是上賢張王諸客，皆以為諸侯相、郡守。
entries.en: The emperor then valued the retainers of the Zhao king and appointed them as chancellors of feudal states and commandery governors.
entries.literal: The emperor then valued the retainers of the Zhao king and appointed them as chancellors of feudal states and commandery governors.

entries.zh: 語在田叔傳。
entries.en: This account appears in the biography of Tian Shu.
entries.literal: This account appears in the biography of Tian Shu.

entries.zh: 及孝惠、高后、文、景時，張王客子孫皆為二千石。
entries.en: By the reigns of Emperor Hui, Empress Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, the descendants of King Zhang's retainers all held offices at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
entries.literal: By the reigns of Emperor Hui, Empress Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, descendants of the Zhao king's retainers were all serving at the two-thousand-shi rank.

entries.zh: 初，孝惠時，齊悼惠王獻城陽郡，尊魯元公主為太后。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Hui's reign, Prince Daohui of Qi presented Chengyang Commandery and honored Princess Lu Yuan as empress dowager.
entries.literal: At the beginning, during Emperor Hui's reign, Prince Daohui of Qi presented Chengyang Commandery and honored Princess Lu Yuan as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 高后元年，魯元太后薨。
entries.en: In the first year of Empress Gao's reign, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan died.
entries.literal: In the first year of Empress Gao, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan died.

entries.zh: 後六年，宣平侯敖復薨。
entries.en: Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao also died.
entries.literal: Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao then died.

entries.zh: 呂太后立敖子偃為魯王，以母為太后故也。
entries.en: Empress Lu made Ao's son Yan King of Lu because his mother had been empress dowager.
entries.literal: Empress Lu established Ao's son Yan as King of Lu because his mother had been empress dowager.

entries.zh: 又憐其年少孤弱，乃封敖前婦子二人：壽為樂昌侯，侈為信都侯。
entries.en: Pitying his youth and isolation, she also enfeoffed Ao's two sons by his former wife, making Shou Marquis of Lechang and Chi Marquis of Xindu.
entries.literal: Pitying his youth and orphanhood, she also enfeoffed Ao's two sons by his former wife: Shou as Marquis of Lechang and Chi as Marquis of Xindu.

entries.zh: 高后崩，大臣誅諸呂，廢魯王及二侯。
entries.en: After Empress Gao died, the ministers executed the Lü clan and deposed the King of Lu and the two marquises.
entries.literal: When Empress Gao died, the ministers executed the Lü clan and deposed the King of Lu and the two marquises.

entries.zh: 孝文即位，復封故魯王偃為南宮侯。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, he re-enfeoffed the former King of Lu, Yan, as Marquis of Nangong.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he again enfeoffed the former King of Lu, Yan, as Marquis of Nangong.

entries.zh: 薨，子生嗣。
entries.en: He died, and his son Sheng succeeded.
entries.literal: He died; his son Sheng succeeded.

entries.zh: 武帝時，生有罪免，國除。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu, Sheng was removed for a crime and the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wu's reign, Sheng was removed for crime, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 元光中，復封偃孫廣國為睢陵侯。
entries.en: During the Yuanguang era, Yan's grandson Guangguo was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiling.
entries.literal: During Yuanguang, Yan's grandson Guangguo was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiling.

entries.zh: 薨，子昌嗣。
entries.en: He died, and his son Chang succeeded.
entries.literal: He died; his son Chang succeeded.

entries.zh: 太初中，昌坐不敬免，國除。
entries.en: During the Taichu era, Chang lost the fief for an offense of disrespect.
entries.literal: During Taichu, Chang was removed for sitting guilty of irreverence, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 孝平元始二年，繼絕世，封敖玄孫慶忌為宣平侯，食千戶。
entries.en: In Yuanshi 2 of Emperor Ping, when broken noble lines were revived, Ao's great-great-grandson Qingji was made Marquis of Xuanping with a thousand-household estate.
entries.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era, continuing a severed line, Ao's great-great-grandson Qingji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 張耳、陳餘
entries.en: Zhang Er and Chen Yu.
entries.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 漢滅項籍，漢王立為皇帝，彭越為梁王。
entries.en: After Han destroyed Xiang Ji and the Han king became emperor, Peng Yue was made king of Liang.
entries.literal: After Han destroyed Xiang Ji and the Han king became emperor, Peng Yue was made king of Liang.

entries.zh: 橫懼誅，而與其徒屬五百餘人入海，居島中。
entries.en: Tian Heng feared he would be put to death, so he and more than five hundred followers put to sea and settled on an island.
entries.literal: Tian Heng feared execution, so he and more than five hundred followers put to sea and lived on an island.

entries.zh: 高帝聞之，以橫兄弟本定齊，齊人賢者多附焉，今在海中不收，後恐有亂，乃使使赦橫罪而召之。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard of this, he considered that Tian Heng and his brothers had originally pacified Qi, and that many worthy men of Qi had attached themselves to them. If Tian Heng remained at sea and was not brought in, Gaozu feared there would be disorder later; he therefore sent an envoy to pardon Heng's crimes and summon him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard this, he noted that Tian Heng and his brothers had originally stabilized Qi and that many worthy Qi people were attached to them. He feared future unrest if Tian Heng remained at sea, so he sent an envoy pardoning Tian Heng and summoning him.

entries.zh: 橫謝曰：「臣亨陛下之使酈食其，今聞其弟商為漢將而賢，臣恐懼，不敢奉詔，請為庶人，守海島中。」
entries.en: Tian Heng declined, saying, "I boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear his younger brother Shang is a valued Han general. I am afraid and dare not obey; I ask only to remain a commoner and stay on an island at sea."
entries.literal: Tian Heng declined, saying, "Your servant boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear that his younger brother Shang is a Han general and a man of talent. I am afraid and dare not obey the summons; I ask only to remain a commoner and stay on an island at sea."

entries.zh: 使還報，高帝乃詔衛尉酈商曰：「齊王橫即至，人馬從者敢動搖者致族夷！」
entries.en: When the envoy returned and reported, Gaozu ordered the Commandant of the Guards, Li Shang: "When King Tian Heng of Qi arrives, if any of his followers stir up trouble, exterminate their clans!"
entries.literal: When the envoy returned and reported, Gaozu issued an edict to the Commandant of the Guards, Li Shang: "When the king of Qi Tian Heng arrives, anyone among his followers who stirs up trouble is to be exterminated to the third degree of kinship!"

entries.zh: 乃復使使持節具告以詔意，曰：「橫來，大者王，小者乃侯耳；
entries.en: He then sent another envoy bearing credentials to explain the edict in full, saying, "If Tian Heng comes, at best he will be made a king, and at least a marquis;
entries.literal: He then sent another envoy with credentials to explain the imperial intent fully, saying, "If Tian Heng comes, at most he will be made a king, and at least a marquis;

entries.zh: 不來，且發兵加誅。」
entries.en: if he does not come, troops will be sent to destroy him."
entries.literal: if he does not come, troops will be sent to punish him."

entries.zh: 橫乃與其客二人乘傳詣雒陽。
entries.en: Tian Heng then rode in an official relay carriage with two retainers to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Tian Heng then rode in an official relay carriage with two retainers to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 漢王還定三秦，渡臨晉，豹以國屬焉，遂從擊楚於彭城。
entries.en: After the King of Han returned and secured the Three Qins, he crossed at Linjin. Wei Bao placed his state under Han and then joined the attack on Chu at Pengcheng.
entries.literal: After the Han king returned and secured the Three Qins, he crossed at Linjin; Wei Bao attached his state to Han and joined the campaign against Chu at Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 漢王敗，還至滎陽，豹請視親病，至國，則絕河津畔漢。
entries.en: When the King of Han was defeated and withdrew to Xingyang, Wei Bao requested leave to visit his sick parent. Once he reached his state, he cut off the river ferries and broke with Han.
entries.literal: When the Han king was defeated and withdrew to Xingyang, Wei Bao asked leave to visit an ailing relative. Once back in his state, he cut the ferry crossings on the river and broke with Han.

entries.zh: 漢王謂酈生曰：「緩頰往說之。」
entries.en: The Han king told Li Yiji, "Use soft persuasion and go win him over."
entries.literal: The Han king said to Li Yiji, "Go with gentle words and persuade him."

entries.zh: 酈生至，豹謝曰：「人生一世間，如白駒過隙。
entries.en: When Li Yiji arrived, Wei Bao excused himself, saying, "A human life is but a white colt flashing past a crevice.
entries.literal: When Li Yiji arrived, Wei Bao declined, saying, "Life in this world passes like a white colt through a crack.

entries.zh: 今漢王嫚侮人，罵詈諸侯群臣如奴耳，非有上下禮節，吾不忍復見也。」
entries.en: The king of Han treats people with contempt, cursing feudal lords and ministers like slaves. There is no proper etiquette between ruler and subject, and I cannot bear to see him again."
entries.literal: The Han king insults people, reviling lords and ministers like slaves; he has no proper hierarchy of superior and inferior—I cannot bear to see him again."

entries.zh: 漢王遣韓信擊豹，遂虜之，傳豹詣滎陽，以其地為河東、太原、上黨郡。
entries.en: The King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao. Han Xin captured him and conveyed him to Xingyang, while his territory was made into the commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang.
entries.literal: The Han king sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured him, and brought him to Xingyang; his lands were turned into Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang commanderies.

entries.zh: 漢王令豹守滎陽。
entries.en: The Han king ordered Wei Bao to guard Xingyang.
entries.literal: The Han king ordered Wei Bao to guard Xingyang.

entries.zh: 楚圍之急，周苛曰：「反國之王，難與共守。」
entries.en: As the Chu siege tightened, Zhou Ke said, "A king who has rebelled against his own realm is not someone we can hold the city with."
entries.literal: When the siege of Chu grew urgent, Zhou Ke said, "A king who turned against his state is hard to defend with."

entries.zh: 遂殺豹。
entries.en: He therefore had Wei Bao killed.
entries.literal: He therefore had Wei Bao killed.

entries.zh: 韓王信，故韓襄王孽孫也，長八尺五寸。
entries.en: Han Wang Xin was an illegitimate grandson in the line of King Xiang of Han, and stood eight chi five cun tall.
entries.literal: Han Wang Xin was an illegitimate grandson in the line of King Xiang of Han, and stood eight chi five cun tall.

entries.zh: 項梁立楚懷王，燕、齊、趙、魏皆已前王，唯韓無有後，故立韓公子橫陽城君為韓王，欲以撫定韓地。
entries.en: When Xiang Liang installed King Huai of Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had all already restored kings, but Han alone had no successor. Therefore the Han prince Lord Hengyang was established as king of Han, in order to soothe and settle Han territory.
entries.literal: When Xiang Liang set up King Huai of Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had already restored their kings, but Han had no heir, so a Han prince, Lord Hengyang, was made king of Han to pacify Han territory.

entries.zh: 項梁死定陶，成奔懷王。
entries.en: After Xiang Liang died at Dingtao, Lord Cheng fled to King Huai.
entries.literal: After Xiang Liang died at Dingtao, Lord Cheng fled to King Huai.

entries.zh: 沛公引兵擊陽城，使張良以韓司徒徇韓地，得信，以為韓將，將其兵從入武關。
entries.en: The Duke of Pei led troops against Yangcheng and sent Zhang Liang, Han's Minister of Education, to bring the Han territories over. Zhang Liang found Han Xin, made him a Han general, and had him lead his troops through Wuguan.
entries.literal: The Duke of Pei attacked Yangcheng and sent Zhang Liang, as Han's Minister of Education, to rally Han lands; he found Han Xin, made him a Han general, and had him lead his troops through Wuguan.

entries.zh: 至尸鄉廄置，橫謝使者曰：「人臣見天子，當洗沐。」
entries.en: At the posting station in Shixiang, Tian Heng told the envoy, "A subject who is to see the Son of Heaven should bathe and wash first."
entries.literal: At the posting station in Shixiang, Tian Heng told the envoy, "When a subject is to see the Son of Heaven, he should bathe and wash."

entries.zh: 止留。
entries.en: So he stayed there.
entries.literal: So he stayed there.

entries.zh: 謂其客曰：「橫始與漢王俱南面稱孤，今漢王為天子，而橫乃為亡虜，北面事之，其媿固已甚矣。
entries.en: He told his retainers, "Tian Heng and the Han king once both faced south as independent rulers. Now the Han king is emperor, while I am a fugitive who must face north and serve him—the humiliation is already more than I can bear.
entries.literal: He told his retainers, "Tian Heng and the Han king once both faced south as independent rulers; now the Han king is Son of Heaven, while I am a fugitive who must face north and serve him—the shame is already more than I can bear.

entries.zh: 又吾亨人之兄，與其弟併肩而事主，縱彼畏天子之詔，不敢動搖，我獨不媿於心乎？
entries.en: Moreover, I boiled Li Yiji, and now I would serve as minister alongside his younger brother. Even if he fears the emperor's edict and does not act, how could I not be ashamed at heart?
entries.literal: Moreover, I boiled Li Yiji, and now I would serve shoulder to shoulder with his younger brother as ministers. Even if he fears the Son of Heaven's edict and does not stir, how could I not be ashamed in my own heart?

entries.zh: 且陛下所以欲見我，不過欲壹見我面貌耳。
entries.en: Besides, the reason Your Majesty wishes to see me is only to look once upon my face.
entries.literal: Moreover, the reason Your Majesty wishes to see me is only to look once upon my face.

entries.zh: 陛下在雒陽，今斬吾頭，馳三十里間，形容尚未能敗，猶可知也。」
entries.en: Your Majesty is at Luoyang. Cut off my head now and send it thirty li—my features will not yet have decayed, and you can still recognize me."
entries.literal: Your Majesty is at Luoyang. If you cut off my head now and send it thirty li, my features will not yet have decayed—you can still recognize me."

entries.zh: 遂自剄，令客奉其頭，從使者馳奏之高帝。
entries.en: He then cut his own throat, ordering the retainers to carry his head and race with the envoy to report to Gaozu.
entries.literal: He then cut his own throat, ordering the retainers to carry his head and race with the envoy to report to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「嗟乎，有以！
entries.en: Gaozu sighed and said, "Ah! He had his reasons!
entries.literal: Gaozu sighed and said, "Ah! There is reason for this!

entries.zh: 起布衣，兄弟三人更王，豈非賢哉！」
entries.en: They rose from commoners, and three brothers in succession became kings—are they not worthy men?"
entries.literal: Starting as commoners, three brothers in succession became kings—is that not worthy?"

entries.zh: 為之流涕，而拜其二客為都尉，發卒二千，以王者禮葬橫。
entries.en: He wept, appointed the two retainers commandants, dispatched two thousand troops, and buried Tian Heng with rites due a king.
entries.literal: He wept, appointed the two retainers commandants, dispatched two thousand troops, and buried Tian Heng with rites due a king.

entries.zh: 項王聞之，大怒，乃北伐齊。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu heard this, he was enraged and marched north to attack Qi.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu heard this, he was enraged and marched north to attack Qi.

entries.zh: 榮發兵距之城陽。
entries.en: Tian Rong sent troops to resist him at Chengyang.
entries.literal: Tian Rong sent troops to resist him at Chengyang.

entries.zh: 榮兵敗，走平原，平原民殺榮。
entries.en: Tian Rong's army was defeated; he fled to Pingyuan, where local people killed him.
entries.literal: Tian Rong's army was defeated; he fled to Pingyuan, where local people killed him.

entries.zh: 項羽遂燒夷齊城郭，所過盡屠破。
entries.en: Xiang Yu then burned and leveled Qi's cities, massacring and destroying everything along his route.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu then burned and leveled Qi's cities, massacring and destroying everything along his route.

entries.zh: 齊人相聚畔之。
entries.en: The Qi people gathered and rebelled against him.
entries.literal: The Qi people gathered and rebelled against him.

entries.zh: 榮弟橫收齊散兵，得數萬人，反擊項羽於城陽。
entries.en: Tian Rong's brother Tian Heng gathered scattered Qi troops, raised tens of thousands, and counterattacked Xiang Yu at Chengyang.
entries.literal: Tian Rong's brother Tian Heng gathered scattered Qi troops, raised tens of thousands, and counterattacked Xiang Yu at Chengyang.

entries.zh: 而漢王帥諸侯敗楚，入彭城。
entries.en: At that same time, the Han king led the feudal armies to defeat Chu and entered Pengcheng.
entries.literal: At that same time, the Han king led the feudal armies to defeat Chu and entered Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 項羽聞之，乃釋齊而歸擊漢於彭城，因連與漢戰，相距滎陽。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu heard this, he left Qi and returned to attack Han at Pengcheng. Thereafter he and Han fought one engagement after another, facing each other at Xingyang.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu heard this, he abandoned the Qi campaign and returned to strike Han at Pengcheng, after which Han and Chu fought continuously around Xingyang.

entries.zh: 以故橫復收齊城邑，立榮子廣為王，而橫相之，政事無巨細皆斷於橫。
entries.en: For this reason Tian Heng again gathered in the cities and towns of Qi, established Tian Rong's son Tian Guang as king, and served as his chancellor. Every matter of government, large or small, was decided by Heng.
entries.literal: Tian Heng therefore recovered Qi cities, enthroned Tian Rong's son Tian Guang as king, and served as chancellor; all matters, great or small, were decided by Tian Heng.

entries.zh: 既葬，二客穿其冢旁，皆自剄從之。
entries.en: After the burial, the two retainers dug beside the grave and cut their own throats to follow him in death.
entries.literal: After the burial, the two retainers dug beside the grave and cut their own throats to follow him in death.

entries.zh: 高帝聞而大驚，以橫之客皆賢者，吾聞其餘尚五百人在海中，使使召至，聞橫死，亦皆自殺。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard of it, he was greatly shocked. Believing that Tian Heng's retainers were all worthy men, he sent envoys to summon the five hundred or so who still remained on the island; when they heard that Heng was dead, they too all killed themselves.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard this, he was astonished. He said Tian Heng's retainers were all worthy men, and when envoys summoned the remaining five hundred still at sea, they too committed suicide on hearing Tian Heng was dead.

entries.zh: 於是乃知田橫兄弟能得士也。
entries.en: Only then did he truly recognize how Tian Heng and his brothers won men's loyalty.
entries.literal: Only then did he truly recognize how Tian Heng and his brothers won men's loyalty.

entries.zh: 沛公為漢王，信從入漢中，乃說漢王曰：「項王王諸將，王獨居此，遷也。
entries.en: When the Duke of Pei became king of Han, Han Xin followed him into Hanzhong and advised him, saying, "Xiang Yu has made the generals kings but has left you alone here—this is banishment.
entries.literal: When the Duke of Pei became king of Han, Han Xin followed him into Hanzhong and advised him, saying, "Lord Xiang has made the generals kings, but has stationed you alone here—this is exile.

entries.zh: 士卒皆山東人，竦而望歸，及其蠭東鄉，可以爭天下。」
entries.en: Your troops are all men from east of the passes; they stand alert, yearning to go home. Once they swarm eastward, you can contend for the empire."
entries.literal: Your soldiers are all men from east of the mountains; they stand alert, longing to return home. Once they surge eastward, you can contend for the empire."

entries.zh: 漢王還定三秦，乃許王信，先拜為韓太尉，將兵略韓地。
entries.en: After the King of Han returned and settled the Three Qins, he agreed to make Han Xin king. He first appointed him grand commandant of Han and sent him to seize Han territory.
entries.literal: After the Han king returned and settled the Three Qins, he agreed to enfeoff Han Xin, first appointing him grand commandant of Han and sending him to seize Han territory.

entries.zh: 項籍之封諸王皆就國，韓王成以不從無功，不遣之國，更封為穰侯，後又殺之。
entries.en: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed the various kings, all of them went to their assigned states. Because King Cheng of Han had not followed Xiang Ji and had no merit, Xiang Ji did not allow him to go to his state, but instead changed his title to Marquis of Rang, and later killed him.
entries.literal: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed kings, all went to their assigned states. Because King Cheng of Han had not followed him and had no merit, Xiang Ji did not let him go to his state, demoted him to Marquis of Rang, and later killed him.

entries.zh: 聞漢遣信略韓地，乃令故籍游吳時令鄭昌為韓王距漢。
entries.en: Hearing that Han had sent Xin to seize Han territory, Xiang Ji ordered Zheng Chang, who had once served as his magistrate when he was in Wu, to become king of Han and resist Han.
entries.literal: Hearing Han had sent Xin to seize Han lands, Xiang Ji ordered Zheng Chang, who had once served under him in Wu, to become king of Han and resist Han.

entries.zh: 漢二年，信略定韓地十餘城。
entries.en: In Han year two, Xin captured more than ten Han cities.
entries.literal: In Han year two, Xin captured more than ten Han cities.

entries.zh: 漢王至河南，信急擊韓王昌，昌降漢。
entries.en: When the Han king reached Henan, Xin swiftly attacked King Chang of Han, and Chang surrendered.
entries.literal: When the Han king reached Henan, Xin swiftly attacked King Chang of Han, and Chang surrendered.

entries.zh: 乃立信為韓王，常將韓兵從。
entries.en: Xin was then made king of Han and usually led Han troops in campaign.
entries.literal: Xin was then made king of Han and usually led Han troops in campaign.

entries.zh: 漢王使信與周苛等守滎陽，楚拔之，信降楚。
entries.en: The Han king ordered Xin and Zhou Ke to guard Xingyang. Chu captured the city, and Xin surrendered to Chu.
entries.literal: The Han king ordered Xin and Zhou Ke to guard Xingyang. Chu captured the city, and Xin surrendered to Chu.

entries.zh: 已得亡歸漢，漢復以為韓王，竟從擊破項籍。
entries.en: Afterward he escaped and returned to Han. Han again made him king of Han, and in the end he followed the army in defeating Xiang Ji.
entries.literal: He later escaped and returned to Han. Han restored him as king of Han, and he followed through to the final defeat of Xiang Ji.

entries.zh: 五年春，與信剖符，王潁川。
entries.en: In the spring of year five, Gaozu divided the tally with Xin and granted him Yingchuan.
entries.literal: In the spring of year five, Gaozu divided the tally with Xin and granted him Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 齊人聞儋死，乃立故齊王建之弟田假為王，田角為相，田閒為將，以距諸侯。
entries.en: When the people of Qi heard that Tian Dan had died, they installed Tian Jia, the younger brother of the former King Jian of Qi, as king, made Tian Jiao chancellor and Tian Jian general, and used them to resist the other lords.
entries.literal: When Qi people heard Tian Dan had died, they enthroned Tian Jia, younger brother of former King Jian of Qi, with Tian Jiao as chancellor and Tian Jian as general, to resist the other lords.

entries.zh: 羽既存趙，降章邯，西滅秦，立諸侯王，乃徙齊王市更王膠東，治即墨。
entries.en: After Xiang Yu had preserved Zhao, accepted Zhang Han's surrender, gone west and destroyed Qin, and installed the kings among the lords, he moved King Shi of Qi and made him king of Jiaodong, with his seat at Jimo.
entries.literal: After Xiang Yu rescued Zhao, accepted Zhang Han's surrender, moved west to destroy Qin, and enfeoffed the lords, he transferred King Shi of Qi to Jiaodong to rule from Jimo.

entries.zh: 齊將田都從共救趙，因入關，故立都為齊王，治臨菑。
entries.en: The Qi general Tian Du had taken part in the joint relief of Zhao and then entered the passes, so Xiang Yu established Du as king of Qi, with his seat at Linzi.
entries.literal: Qi general Tian Du had followed the relief of Zhao and then entered the passes, so Xiang Yu set him up as king of Qi at Linzi.

entries.zh: 故齊王建孫田安，項羽方渡河救趙，安下濟北數城，引兵降項羽，羽立安為濟北王，治博陽。
entries.en: Tian An, grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, had captured several cities in Jibei while Xiang Yu was crossing the river to rescue Zhao, then led his troops in surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu established An as king of Jibei, with his seat at Boyang.
entries.literal: Tian An, grandson of former King Jian of Qi, had taken several Jibei cities while Xiang Yu was crossing the river to aid Zhao and then surrendered to him; Xiang Yu made him king of Jibei at Boyang.

entries.zh: 榮以負項梁，不肯助楚攻秦，故不得王。
entries.en: Because Tian Rong had failed Xiang Liang and refused to aid Chu against Qin, he received no kingship.
entries.literal: Because Tian Rong had failed Xiang Liang and refused to aid Chu against Qin, he received no kingship.

entries.zh: 趙將陳餘亦失職，不得王。
entries.en: Chen Yu, a general of Zhao, was likewise passed over for the rank he expected and was not made king.
entries.literal: Chen Yu, a general of Zhao, likewise failed to receive the position he felt due and was not made king.

entries.zh: 二人俱怨項羽。
entries.en: Both men resented Xiang Yu.
entries.literal: Both men resented Xiang Yu.

entries.zh: 定齊三年，聞漢將韓信引兵且東擊齊，齊使華毋傷、田解軍歷下以距漢。
entries.en: Three years after Qi had been settled, they heard that the Han general Han Xin was leading troops east to attack Qi. Qi therefore sent Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to encamp at Lixia and resist Han.
entries.literal: After Qi had been settled for three years, they heard Han general Han Xin was leading troops east to attack Qi, so Qi sent Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to garrison Lixia against Han.

entries.zh: 會漢使酈食其往說王廣及相橫，與連和。
entries.en: Meanwhile Han envoy Li Yiji went to persuade King Guang and Chancellor Tian Heng to make an alliance.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Han envoy Li Yiji went to persuade King Guang and Chancellor Tian Heng to make an alliance.

entries.zh: 橫然之，乃罷歷下守備，縱酒，且遣使與漢平。
entries.en: Tian Heng agreed, withdrew the defenses at Lixia, held drinking feasts, and prepared to send envoys for peace with Han.
entries.literal: Tian Heng agreed, withdrew the defenses at Lixia, held drinking feasts, and prepared to send envoys for peace with Han.

entries.zh: 韓信乃渡平原，襲破齊歷下軍，因入臨菑。
entries.en: Han Xin then crossed from Pingyuan, launched a surprise attack, smashed the Qi army at Lixia, and entered Linzi.
entries.literal: Han Xin then crossed from Pingyuan, launched a surprise attack, smashed the Qi army at Lixia, and entered Linzi.

entries.zh: 王廣、相橫以酈生為賣己而亨之。
entries.en: King Guang and Chancellor Tian Heng believed Li Yiji had sold them out and therefore boiled him alive.
entries.literal: King Guang and Chancellor Tian Heng believed Li Yiji had sold them out and therefore boiled him alive.

entries.zh: 廣東走高密，橫走博，守相田光走城陽，將軍田既軍於膠東。
entries.en: Guang fled east to Gaomi, Tian Heng fled to Bo, Chancellor Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji camped at Jiaodong.
entries.literal: Guang fled east to Gaomi, Tian Heng fled to Bo, Chancellor Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji camped at Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 楚使龍且救齊，齊王與合軍高密。
entries.en: Chu sent Long Ju to rescue Qi, and the Qi king joined forces with him at Gaomi.
entries.literal: Chu sent Long Ju to rescue Qi, and the Qi king joined forces with him at Gaomi.

entries.zh: 漢將韓信、曹參破殺龍且，虜齊王廣。
entries.en: Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated and killed Long Ju and captured King Guang of Qi.
entries.literal: Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated and killed Long Ju and captured King Guang of Qi.

entries.zh: 漢將灌嬰追得守相光，至博。
entries.en: Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured Chancellor Tian Guang at Bo.
entries.literal: Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured Chancellor Tian Guang at Bo.

entries.zh: 而橫聞王死，自立為王，還擊嬰，嬰敗橫軍於贏下。
entries.en: Hearing the king was dead, Tian Heng made himself king and counterattacked Guan Ying, but Guan Ying defeated Tian Heng below Ying.
entries.literal: Hearing the king was dead, Tian Heng made himself king and counterattacked Guan Ying, but Guan Ying defeated Tian Heng below Ying.

entries.zh: 橫亡走梁，歸彭越。
entries.en: Tian Heng fled to Liang and took refuge with Peng Yue.
entries.literal: Tian Heng fled to Liang and took refuge with Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 越時居梁地，中立，且為漢，且為楚。
entries.en: At that time Peng Yue held Liang territory in a middle position, at times aiding Han and at times aiding Chu.
entries.literal: At that time Peng Yue held Liang territory in a middle position, at times aiding Han and at times aiding Chu.

entries.zh: 韓信已殺龍且，因進兵破殺田既於膠東，灌嬰破殺齊將田吸於千乘，遂平齊地。
entries.en: After Han Xin had killed Long Ju, he advanced and defeated and killed Tian Ji in Jiaodong. Guan Ying also defeated and killed the Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng, and Qi territory was thereby pacified.
entries.literal: After Han Xin had killed Long Ju, he advanced, defeated and killed Tian Ji at Jiaodong; Guan Ying also defeated and killed Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng, and thus Qi territory was pacified.

entries.zh: 六年春，上以為信壯武，北近鞏、雒，南迫宛、葉，東有淮陽，皆天下勁兵處也，乃更以太原郡為韓國，徙信以備胡，都晉陽。
entries.en: In the spring of the sixth year, the emperor considered Xin strong and martial. Since to the north his territory lay near Gong and Luo, to the south it pressed upon Wan and Ye, and to the east it had Huaiyang, all places with powerful troops, the emperor instead made Taiyuan Commandery the Han kingdom, moved Xin there to guard against the Hu, and set his capital at Jinyang.
entries.literal: In spring of year six, the emperor judged Xin fierce and martial. Because the northern front bordered Gong and Luo, the south pressed against Wan and Ye, and the east touched Huaiyang, all strategic military zones, he reassigned Taiyuan as Han's kingdom, moved Xin there to guard against the Hu, and set his capital at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 信上書曰：「國被邊，匈奴數入，晉陽去塞遠，請治馬邑。」
entries.en: Han Xin memorialized, saying, "My state borders the frontier and the Xiongnu raid repeatedly. Jinyang is far from the border passes—I ask to administer from Mayi."
entries.literal: Han Xin memorialized, saying, "The state borders the frontier and the Xiongnu raid repeatedly; Jinyang is far from the passes—I ask to govern from Mayi."

entries.zh: 上許之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 秋，匈奴冒頓大入圍信，信數使使胡求和解。
entries.en: That autumn, Modu of the Xiongnu made a major incursion and besieged Xin, who repeatedly sent envoys to seek peace with the Hu.
entries.literal: That autumn, Modu of the Xiongnu made a major incursion and besieged Xin, who repeatedly sent envoys to seek peace with the Hu.

entries.zh: 漢發兵救之，疑信數間使，有二心。
entries.en: Han dispatched troops to rescue him, but suspected Xin's repeated secret contacts meant divided loyalties.
entries.literal: Han dispatched troops to rescue him, but suspected Xin's repeated secret contacts meant divided loyalties.

entries.zh: 上賜信書責讓之曰：「專死不勇，專生不任，寇攻馬邑，君王力不足以堅守乎？
entries.en: The emperor sent Xin a letter of reprimand, saying, "To cling to death alone is not courage; to cling to life alone is not responsibility. When the enemy attacked Mayi, was your strength insufficient to hold it?
entries.literal: The emperor sent Xin a letter of reprimand, saying, "To seek death alone is not courage; to seek life alone is not responsibility. When the enemy attacked Mayi, was the king's strength insufficient to hold it?

entries.zh: 安危存亡之地，此二者朕所以責於君王。」
entries.en: This is ground where safety and ruin, survival and extinction, are decided—these are the two points for which I hold you accountable."
entries.literal: This is ground where safety and ruin, survival and extinction, are decided—these are the two points for which I hold the king accountable."

entries.zh: 信得書，恐誅，因與匈奴約共攻漢，以馬邑降胡，擊太原。
entries.en: When Xin received the letter, he feared execution. He therefore made an agreement with the Xiongnu to attack Han together, surrendered Mayi to the Hu, and attacked Taiyuan.
entries.literal: After receiving the letter and fearing execution, Xin made terms with the Xiongnu to attack Han together, surrendered Mayi to the Hu, and struck Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 七年冬，上自往擊破信軍銅鞮，斬其將王喜。
entries.en: In winter of year seven, the emperor personally campaigned, defeated Xin's forces at Tongdi, and beheaded Xin's general Wang Xi.
entries.literal: In winter of year seven, the emperor personally campaigned, defeated Xin's forces at Tongdi, and beheaded Xin's general Wang Xi.

entries.zh: 信亡走匈奴。
entries.en: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 與其將白土人曼丘臣、王黃立趙苗裔趙利為王，復收信散兵，而與信及冒頓謀攻漢。
entries.en: Xin's generals Manqiu Chen of Baitu and Wang Huang established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao royal house, as king. They regrouped Xin's scattered troops and joined Xin and Modu in plotting an attack on Han.
entries.literal: His generals, Manqiu Chen of Baitu and Wang Huang, established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao royal house, as king, regrouped Xin's scattered troops, and joined Xin and Modu in plotting an attack on Han.

entries.zh: 匈奴使左右賢王將萬餘騎與王黃等屯廣武以南，至晉陽，與漢兵戰，漢兵大破之，追至于離石，復破之。
entries.en: The Xiongnu sent the Left and Right Wise Kings with more than ten thousand cavalry to encamp with Wang Huang and the others south of Guangwu. When they reached Jinyang and fought the Han troops, the Han troops routed them, pursued them to Lishi, and defeated them again.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu sent their Left and Right Wise Kings with more than ten thousand cavalry to join Wang Huang south of Guangwu. They reached Jinyang and fought Han forces, but Han routed them, pursued them to Lishi, and defeated them again.

entries.zh: 匈奴復聚兵樓煩西北。
entries.en: The Xiongnu then regrouped northwest of Loufan.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu then regrouped northwest of Loufan.

entries.zh: 漢令車騎擊匈奴，常敗走，漢乘勝追北。
entries.en: Han sent cavalry and chariots against them; the Xiongnu often feigned retreat, and Han pursued north in victory.
entries.literal: Han sent cavalry and chariots against them; the Xiongnu often feigned retreat, and Han pursued north in victory.

entries.zh: 聞冒頓居代谷，上居晉陽，使人視冒頓，還報曰「可擊」。
entries.en: Hearing that Modu was at Daigu, the emperor remained at Jinyang and sent scouts to observe him. They returned and reported, "He can be attacked."
entries.literal: Hearing that Modu was at Daigu, the emperor stayed at Jinyang and sent scouts to observe him. They returned and reported, "He can be attacked."

entries.zh: 上遂至平城，上白登。
entries.en: The emperor advanced to Pingcheng and camped at Baideng.
entries.literal: The emperor advanced to Pingcheng and camped at Baideng.

entries.zh: 匈奴騎圍上，上乃使人厚遺閼氏。
entries.en: Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him, and he sent rich gifts to Modu's consort.
entries.literal: Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him, and he sent rich gifts to Modu's consort.

entries.zh: 閼氏說冒頓曰：「今得漢地，猶不能居，且兩主不相厄。」
entries.en: The consort persuaded Modu, saying, "Even if we now gain Han territory, we still cannot hold it. Moreover, two rulers should not drive each other to extremes."
entries.literal: The consort persuaded Modu, saying, "Even if we now gain Han territory, we still cannot hold it. Moreover, two rulers should not harry each other to ruin."

entries.zh: 居七日，胡騎稍稍引去。
entries.en: After seven days, the Hu cavalry gradually withdrew.
entries.literal: After seven days, the Hu cavalry gradually withdrew.

entries.zh: 天霧，漢使人往來，胡不覺。
entries.en: Under heavy fog, Han couriers moved in and out without the Hu noticing.
entries.literal: Under heavy fog, Han couriers moved in and out without the Hu noticing.

entries.zh: 護軍中尉陳平言上曰：「胡者全兵，請令彊弩傅兩矢外鄉，徐行出圍。」
entries.en: Guard Commandant Chen Ping told the emperor, "The Hu army is still at full strength. Order the strong crossbowmen to fit two arrows each and face outward, and withdraw slowly from the encirclement."
entries.literal: Guard Commandant Chen Ping told the emperor, "The Hu force is intact. I ask that strong crossbows with paired arrows be posted facing outward, and that we withdraw slowly from the encirclement."

entries.zh: 入平城，漢救兵亦至。
entries.en: He then reentered Pingcheng, and Han relief forces also arrived.
entries.literal: He then reentered Pingcheng, and Han relief forces also arrived.

entries.zh: 胡騎遂解去，漢亦罷兵歸。
entries.en: The Hu cavalry finally lifted the siege and withdrew, and Han likewise ended the campaign and returned.
entries.literal: The Hu cavalry finally lifted the siege and withdrew, and Han likewise ended the campaign and returned.

entries.zh: 信為匈奴將兵往來擊邊，令王黃等說誤陳豨。
entries.en: As a Xiongnu commander, Xin kept raiding the border and had Wang Huang and others mislead Chen Xi into rebellion.
entries.literal: As a Xiongnu commander, Xin kept raiding the border and had Wang Huang and others mislead Chen Xi into rebellion.

entries.zh: 十一年春，信復與胡騎入居參合。
entries.en: In spring of year eleven, Xin again entered and occupied Shenhe with Hu cavalry.
entries.literal: In spring of year eleven, Xin again entered and occupied Shenhe with Hu cavalry.

entries.zh: 漢使柴將軍擊之，遺信書曰：「陛下寬仁，諸侯雖有叛亡，而後歸，輒復故位號，不誅也。
entries.en: Han sent General Chai to attack and sent Xin a letter, saying, "The emperor is generous and humane. Even feudal lords who rebel and flee, if they later return, are restored to their former ranks and titles and are not put to death.
entries.literal: Han sent General Chai to attack and sent Xin a letter, saying, "The emperor is generous and humane: even feudal lords who rebel and flee, if they later return, are restored to their former ranks and titles and are not executed.

entries.zh: 大王所知。
entries.en: You know this well, great king.
entries.literal: Your Majesty knows this well.

entries.zh: 今王以敗亡走胡，非有大罪，急自歸。」
entries.en: Now you have been defeated and fled to the Hu—this is not a grave crime. Return quickly."
entries.literal: Now you have been defeated and fled to the Hu—this is not a grave crime. Return quickly."

entries.zh: 信報曰：「陛下擢僕閭巷，南面稱孤，此僕之幸也。
