entries.literal: Though Your Majesty repeatedly lost east of the mountains, Xiao He always preserved Guanzhong intact awaiting Your Majesty—this is achievement for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 今雖無曹參等百數，何缺於漢？
entries.en: Had we lacked a hundred men like Cao Shen, would the dynasty have suffered?
entries.literal: Now though there were not a hundred men such as Cao Shen, what would Han lack?

entries.zh: 漢得之不必待以全。
entries.en: The house of Han would not have lacked for conquest even without them.
entries.literal: In winning the empire, Han did not need to wait for such men to make it complete.

entries.zh: 柰何欲以一旦之功而加萬世之功哉！
entries.en: How can you rank a day’s fight above a lifetime’s stewardship?
entries.literal: How then can you wish to place a single day’s achievement above achievement for ten thousand generations!

entries.zh: 蕭何當第一，曹參次之。」
entries.en: Xiao He must be first; Cao Shen second.”
entries.literal: Xiao He should be first; Cao Shen next.”

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Sovereign said, “Agreed.”
entries.literal: The Sovereign said, “Good.”

entries.zh: 於是乃令何第一，賜帶劍履上殿，入朝不趨。
entries.en: He ranked Xiao He first, allowed him to wear sword and shoes in the audience hall, and waived the rule that he must trot into court.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered He first, granting him the privilege of wearing a sword and shoes in the hall and entering court without hurrying.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾聞進賢受上賞，蕭何功雖高，待鄂君乃得明。」
entries.en: He added, “They say recommending talent wins the highest reward. Xiao He’s greatness needed Lord E’s voice to be recognized.”
entries.literal: The Sovereign said, “I have heard that he who recommends the worthy receives the highest reward; though Xiao He’s achievement is high, it was through the Lord of E that it became clear.”

entries.zh: 於是因鄂千秋故所食關內侯邑二千戶，封為安平侯。
entries.en: On the two-thousand-household Guannei estate E Qianqiu already held, he was now created Marquis of Anping.
entries.literal: Thereupon on the territory of two thousand households that E Qianqiu formerly held as Marquis Guannei, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping.

entries.zh: 是日，悉封何父母兄弟十餘人，皆食邑。
entries.en: That same day he granted fiefs to more than ten members of Xiao He's family, including his parents and brothers.
entries.literal: That day he enfeoffed more than ten members of He's family, including his parents and brothers, each with an estate.

entries.zh: 乃益封何二千戶，「以嘗繇咸陽時何送我獨贏錢二也」。
entries.en: He added two thousand households to Xiao He’s fief, “for the time when, bound for corvée at Xianyang, he alone gave me two hundred cash more than the others.”
entries.literal: He additionally enfeoffed He by two thousand households, “because when I once performed corvée at Xianyang, He alone sent me two hundred cash extra.”

entries.zh: 漢三年，與項羽相距京、索間，上數使使勞苦丞相。
entries.en: In the third Han year, locked with Xiang Yu between Jing and Suo, the Sovereign repeatedly sent messengers to console his weary chancellor.
entries.literal: In the third year of Han, [the King of Han] with Xiang Yu faced each other between Jing and Suo; the Sovereign repeatedly sent envoys to express sympathy for the toil of the chancellor.

entries.zh: 鮑生謂何曰：「今王暴衣露蓋，數勞苦君者，有疑君心。
entries.en: Bao Sheng warned Xiao He, “The King endures hardship in the field yet keeps sending messengers to inquire after you—he is testing your loyalty.
entries.literal: Bao Sheng said to He, “Now the King, exposing his person to wind and rain, repeatedly consoles your toil because he harbors doubts about you.

entries.zh: 為君計，莫若遣君子孫昆弟能勝兵者悉詣軍所，上益信君。」
entries.en: Send every able-bodied son, brother, and kinsman you have into his camp; only then will he truly trust you.”
entries.literal: For your sake I calculate: nothing would be better than to send your sons, grandsons, brothers, and cousins who can bear arms all to join the army in camp, so the Sovereign will trust you the more.”

entries.zh: 於是何從其計，漢王大說。
entries.en: Xiao He did so, and the King of Han was delighted.
entries.literal: Thereupon He followed his plan, and the King of Han was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 其秋，黥布反，上自將擊之，數使使問相國何為。
entries.en: That autumn Qing Bu rebelled; the Sovereign took the field against him and kept sending messengers to ask what Minister of State Xiao He was doing.
entries.literal: That autumn Qing Bu rebelled; the Sovereign personally led the army to strike him and repeatedly sent messengers to ask what the minister of state He was doing.

entries.zh: 曰：「為上在軍，拊循勉百姓，悉所有佐軍，如陳豨時。」
entries.en: The reply was, “Since the Sovereign is with the army, I am comforting and encouraging the people and devoting everything I have to support the campaign, just as I did during the affair of Chen Xi.”
entries.literal: [He] said, “Because the Sovereign is in the army, I console and encourage the common people and devote all I have to aid the army, as at the time of Chen Xi.”

entries.zh: 客又說何曰：「君滅族不久矣。
entries.en: Another adviser warned him, “You are courting extermination for your whole line.
entries.literal: A guest again said to He, “Your clan will soon be exterminated.

entries.zh: 夫君位為相國，功第一，不可復加。
entries.en: You are minister of state and already first in merit—there is nowhere higher to climb.
entries.literal: My lord, your position is minister of state and your achievement is first; nothing further can be added.

entries.zh: 然君初入關，本得百姓心，十餘年矣。
entries.en: Yet from the day you entered the passes you won the people’s hearts, and more than ten years have passed.
entries.literal: Yet when my lord first entered the Pass, you fundamentally won the hearts of the common people, and it has been more than ten years.

entries.zh: 皆附君，尚復孳孳得民和。
entries.en: They still look to you, and you keep burnishing your popularity.
entries.literal: All cling to you, and you still diligently win the harmony of the people.

entries.zh: 上所謂數問君，畏君傾動關中。
entries.en: Each time he asks after you, he is gauging whether you might sway Guanzhong against him.
entries.literal: What the Sovereign calls repeatedly asking after you is fearing that you will shake Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 今君胡不多買田地，賤貰貣以自汙？
entries.en: Why not buy up land and deal in disreputable loans, deliberately blackening your name?
entries.literal: Why does my lord not buy large amounts of land and make sordid purchases and loans to stain his own reputation?

entries.zh: 上心必安。」
entries.en: Only then will he feel secure.”
entries.literal: Then the Sovereign’s mind will be at ease.”

entries.zh: 於是何從其計，上乃大說。
entries.en: Xiao He followed the advice, and the Sovereign was greatly relieved.
entries.literal: Thereupon He followed his plan, and the Sovereign was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 曹參，沛人也。
entries.en: Cao Shen came from Pei.
entries.literal: Cao Shen was a man of Pei.

entries.zh: 秦時為獄掾，而蕭何為主吏，居縣為豪吏矣。
entries.en: Under the Qin he served as jail clerk while Xiao He was chief clerk; together they ranked as the county’s foremost officers.
entries.literal: Under Qin he was clerk of the jail, while Xiao He was chief clerk; in the county they were the leading clerks.

entries.zh: 高祖為沛公也，參以中涓從。
entries.en: When Liu Bang became Duke of Pei, Cao Shen joined him as an inner attendant.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Duke of Pei, Shen followed as palace attendant within.

entries.zh: 擊胡陵、方與，攻秦監公軍，大破之。
entries.en: He fought at Huling and Fangyu, routed the army of Qin’s local inspector, and broke it utterly.
entries.literal: He struck Huling and Fangyu, attacked the army of the Qin inspector, and smashed it.

entries.zh: 東下薛，擊泗水守軍薛郭西。
entries.en: He marched east to Xue and attacked the Sishui governor’s force west of the city wall.
entries.literal: He went east down to Xue, struck the army of the Sishui defender west of Xue’s outer wall.

entries.zh: 復攻胡陵，取之。
entries.en: He attacked Huling again and captured it.
entries.literal: Again he attacked Huling and took it.

entries.zh: 徙守方與。
entries.en: He was reassigned to hold Fangyu.
entries.literal: He was moved to guard Fangyu.

entries.zh: 方與反為魏，擊之。
entries.en: When Fangyu went over to Wei, he struck it back.
entries.literal: Fangyu turned to Wei; he attacked it.

entries.zh: 豐反為魏，攻之。
entries.en: When Feng declared for Wei, he attacked it.
entries.literal: Feng turned to Wei; he attacked it.

entries.zh: 賜爵七大夫。
entries.en: He was awarded the seventh rank of grandee.
entries.literal: He was granted the rank of seventh grandee.

entries.zh: 北擊司馬欣軍碭東，取狐父、祁善置。
entries.en: He drove north against Sima Xin’s host east of Dang, seizing Hufu and the Qishan courier post.
entries.literal: He struck north against Sima Xin’s army east of Dang, taking Hufu and the Qishan relay station.

entries.zh: 又攻下邑以西，至虞，擊秦將章邯車騎。
entries.en: He pushed west from Xiayi to Yu and engaged the chariotry and horse of Qin’s Zhang Han.
entries.literal: Again he attacked west of Xiayi to Yu, striking Qin general Zhang Han’s chariots and cavalry.

entries.zh: 攻轅戚及亢父，先登。
entries.en: At Yuanqi and Kangfu he led the first assault over the walls.
entries.literal: He attacked Yuanqi and Kangfu, being first to mount the wall.

entries.zh: 遷為五大夫。
entries.en: He was raised to fifth grandee.
entries.literal: He was promoted to fifth grandee.

entries.zh: 北救東阿，擊章邯軍，陷陳，追至濮陽。
entries.en: He relieved Dong’e in the north, shattered Zhang Han’s battle line, and chased him to Puyang.
entries.literal: He rescued Dong’e to the north, struck Zhang Han’s army, broke the formation, and pursued to Puyang.

entries.zh: 攻定陶，取臨濟。
entries.en: He took Dingtao and captured Linji.
entries.literal: He attacked Dingtao and took Linji.

entries.zh: 南救雍丘，擊李由軍，破之，殺李由，虜秦候一人。
entries.en: Marching south to Yongqiu, he crushed Li You's army, slew Li You, and captured a Qin scout.
entries.literal: He rescued Yongqiu to the south, struck Li You's army, destroyed it, killed Li You, and captured one Qin scout.

entries.zh: 章邯破殺項梁也，沛公與項羽引兵而東。
entries.en: After Zhang Han destroyed Xiang Liang, the Duke of Pei and Xiang Yu led their troops eastward.
entries.literal: When Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, the Duke of Pei with Xiang Yu led the army eastward.

entries.zh: 楚懷王以沛公為碭郡長，將碭郡兵。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu named the Duke of Pei governor of Dang and gave him command of its army.
entries.literal: King Huai of Chu appointed the Duke of Pei as governor of Dang commandery and put him in command of Dang’s troops.

entries.zh: 於是乃封參執帛，號曰建成君。
entries.en: Cao Shen was then raised to the Chu rank of Zhibo and styled Lord Jiancheng.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shen was appointed Zhibo, and he was styled Lord Jiancheng.

entries.zh: 遷為戚公，屬碭郡。
entries.en: He was promoted to lord of Qi township under Dang commandery.
entries.literal: He was promoted to lord of Qi, subordinate to Dang commandery.

entries.zh: 項羽至，以沛公為漢王。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu came up he named the Duke of Pei King of Han.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu arrived he made the Duke of Pei King of Han.

entries.zh: 漢王封參為建成侯。
entries.en: The King of Han enfeoffed Cao Shen as Marquis of Jiancheng.
entries.literal: The King of Han enfeoffed Shen as Marquis of Jiancheng.

entries.zh: 從至漢中，遷為將軍。
entries.en: He accompanied the court to Hanzhong and was promoted general.
entries.literal: He followed to Hanzhong and was promoted to general.

entries.zh: 從還定三秦，攻下辨、故道、雍、斄。
entries.en: On the campaign to reconquer the Three Qin he took Xiabian, Gudao, Yong, and Tai.
entries.literal: He followed in the return to settle the Three Qin, attacking Xiabian, Gudao, Yong, and Tai.

entries.zh: 擊章平軍於好畤南，破之，圍好畤，取壤鄉。
entries.en: South of Haozhi he broke Zhang Ping, besieged the town, and seized Xiang township.
entries.literal: He struck Zhang Ping’s army south of Haozhi, destroyed it, besieged Haozhi, and took Xiang township.

entries.zh: 擊三秦軍壤東及高櫟，破之。
entries.en: He smashed Three Qin forces east of Xiang and at Gaoli.
entries.literal: He struck the Three Qin armies east of Xiang and at Gaoli, destroying them.

entries.zh: 復圍章平，平出好畤走。
entries.en: He besieged Zhang Ping again until Zhang Ping broke out of Haozhi and fled.
entries.literal: Again he besieged Zhang Ping; Ping fled out of Haozhi.

entries.zh: 因擊趙賁、內史保軍，破之。
entries.en: He followed up by crushing the armies of Zhao Ben and Interior Secretary Bao.
entries.literal: Then he struck the armies of Zhao Ben and Interior Secretary Bao, destroying them.

entries.zh: 東取咸陽，更名曰新城。
entries.en: He seized Xianyang to the east and renamed it New City.
entries.literal: East he took Xianyang, renaming it New City.

entries.zh: 參將兵守景陵二十三日，三秦使章平等攻參，參出擊，大破之。
entries.en: Cao Shen held Jingling for twenty-three days; when Three Qin generals led by Zhang Ping attacked, he sallied and shattered them.
entries.literal: Shen led troops and guarded Jingling twenty-three days; the Three Qin sent Zhang Ping and others to attack Shen; Shen sallied forth and smashed them.

entries.zh: 賜食邑於寧秦。
entries.en: He received a food fief at Ningqin.
entries.literal: He was granted a fief at Ningqin.

entries.zh: 以將軍引兵圍章邯廢丘；
entries.en: As general he led the siege that penned Zhang Han in Feiqiu.
entries.literal: As general he led troops to besiege Zhang Han at Feiqiu;

entries.zh: 以中尉從漢王出臨晉關。
entries.en: as colonel of the guard he escorted the King of Han through Linjin Pass.
entries.literal: As colonel of the guard he followed the King of Han out through Linjin Pass.

entries.zh: 至河內，下脩武，度圍津，東擊龍且、項佗定陶，破之。
entries.en: In Henei he reduced Xiuwu, crossed the ford at Weijin, and eastward defeated Long Ju and Xiang Tuo at Dingtao.
entries.literal: Reaching Henei, he took Xiuwu, crossed Weijin ford, struck east at Long Ju and Xiang Tuo at Dingtao, and destroyed them.

entries.zh: 東取碭、蕭、彭城。
entries.en: He drove east to take Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng.
entries.literal: East he took Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 擊項籍軍，漢軍大敗走。
entries.en: There he collided with Xiang Yu’s host and the Han army was routed.
entries.literal: He struck Xiang Yu’s army; the Han army was badly defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 參以中尉圍取雍丘。
entries.en: As colonel of the guard Cao Shen besieged and took Yongqiu.
entries.literal: Shen as colonel of the guard besieged and took Yongqiu.

entries.zh: 王武反於外黃，程處反於燕，往擊，盡破之。
entries.en: Wang Wu rose at Waihuang and Cheng Chu at Yan; Cao Shen marched against them and crushed both revolts.
entries.literal: Wang Wu rebelled at Waihuang and Cheng Chu at Yan; he went and struck, destroying both.

entries.zh: 柱天侯反於衍氏，進破取衍氏。
entries.en: When the Pillar-of-Heaven marquis mutinied at Yanshi, Cao Shen advanced, broke him, and occupied the town.
entries.literal: The Pillar-of-Heaven marquis rebelled at Yanshi; he advanced, destroyed, and took Yanshi.

entries.zh: 擊羽嬰於昆陽，追至葉。
entries.en: He fought Yu Ying at Kunyang and chased him to Ye.
entries.literal: He struck Yu Ying at Kunyang and pursued to Ye.

entries.zh: 還攻武彊，因至滎陽。
entries.en: On the withdrawal he stormed Wuqiang and then fell back on Xingyang.
entries.literal: Turning back he attacked Wuqiang, then arrived at Xingyang.

entries.zh: 參自漢中為將軍中尉，從擊諸侯，及項王敗，還至滎陽。
entries.en: From Hanzhong onward Cao Shen held the ranks of general and colonel of the guard, campaigned against the lords, and when Xiang Yu fell he was back at Xingyang.
entries.literal: Shen from Hanzhong served as general and colonel of the guard, followed in striking the feudal lords, and when the King of Xiang was defeated, returned to Xingyang.

entries.zh: 參子窋為中大夫。
entries.en: His son Cao Zhu held the post of palace counselor.
entries.literal: Shen’s son Zhu was a palace counselor.

entries.zh: 惠帝怪相國不治事，以為「豈少朕與？」
entries.en: Emperor Hui wondered at the minister of state not governing affairs, thinking “Does he belittle Us?”
entries.literal: Emperor Hui wondered at the minister of state not governing affairs, thinking “Does he belittle Us?”

entries.zh: 乃謂窋曰：「女歸，試私從容問乃父曰：『高帝新棄群臣，帝富於春秋，君為相國，日飲，無所請事，何以憂天下？』
entries.en: He said to Cao Zhu, “When you go home, try privately and calmly asking your father: ‘The High Emperor has only just left his ministers, and the emperor is still young. You, as chancellor, drink every day and request no affairs of state; how does this show concern for the realm?
entries.literal: He therefore said to Zhu, “You return; try privately and at ease to ask your father, saying, ‘The High Emperor has newly left the ministers; the Emperor is rich in spring and autumn; you as minister of state daily drink, request nothing in the way of affairs—how do you worry for the empire?’

entries.zh: 然無言吾告女也。」
entries.en: Say nothing of my instructions.”
entries.literal: But do not say that I told you.”

entries.zh: 窋既洗沐歸，時間，自從其所諫參。
entries.en: After his ritual bath Cao Zhu waited for a private moment and spoke as the emperor had coached him.
entries.literal: Zhu having bathed and returned, at the appropriate time, from his own standpoint remonstrated with Shen.

entries.zh: 參怒而笞之二百，曰：「趣入侍，天下事非乃所當言也。」
entries.en: Cao Shen thrashed him two hundred strokes with the rod and barked, “Back to your post—state business is not yours to discuss.”
entries.literal: Shen in anger flogged him two hundred strokes, saying, “Hasten to enter and serve; affairs of the empire are not what you ought to speak of.”

entries.zh: 至朝時，帝讓參曰：「與窋胡治乎？
entries.en: At the next audience Emperor Hui reproached him: “Why did you beat Cao Zhu?
entries.literal: When court arrived, Emperor Hui reproached Shen, saying, “What dealing did you have with Zhu?

entries.zh: 乃者我使諫君也。」
entries.en: I sent him to reason with you.”
entries.literal: Recently I had him remonstrate with you.”

entries.zh: 參免冠謝曰：「陛下自察聖武孰與高皇帝？」
entries.en: Cao Shen removed his cap and asked, “How do Your Majesty's wisdom and martial ability compare with those of the High Emperor?”
entries.literal: Shen removed his cap and apologized, saying, “May Your Majesty examine yourself: in sagely martial prowess, how do you compare to the High Emperor?”

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕乃安敢望先帝！」
entries.en: “I dare not compare myself to him,” said the emperor.
entries.literal: The Sovereign said, “How would We dare look up to the Late Emperor!”

entries.zh: 參曰：「陛下觀參孰與蕭何賢？」
entries.en: “And how do I measure against Xiao He?” asked Cao Shen.
entries.literal: Shen said, “Your Majesty observe Shen: how does he compare to Xiao He in worth?”

entries.zh: 上曰：「君似不及也。」
entries.en: “You fall short,” the emperor admitted.
entries.literal: The Sovereign said, “You seem not to reach him.”

entries.zh: 參曰：「陛下言之是也。
entries.en: “Then we agree,” said Cao Shen.
entries.literal: Shen said, “What Your Majesty says is correct.

entries.zh: 且高皇帝與蕭何定天下，法令既明具，陛下垂拱，參等守職，遵而勿失，不亦可乎？」
entries.en: The Late Emperor and Xiao He set the laws in clear order. Your Majesty has only to fold your hands on the throne; we ministers need only hold the line without blunder—is that not enough?”
entries.literal: Moreover the High Emperor with Xiao He fixed the empire; laws and orders are already clear and complete; Your Majesty hangs down the sash; we such as Shen guard office, follow and do not lose—is this not also acceptable?”

entries.zh: 惠帝曰：「善。
entries.en: “Well said,” said Emperor Hui.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui said, “Good.

entries.zh: 君休矣！」
entries.en: You may leave off.”
entries.literal: Sir, rest yourself!”

entries.zh: 窋嗣侯，高后時至御史大夫。
entries.en: Cao Zhu inherited the title and under Empress Lü rose to imperial censor in chief.
entries.literal: Zhu succeeded to the marquisate; in Empress Gao’s time he reached imperial censor in chief.

entries.zh: 傳國至曾孫襄，武帝時為將軍，擊匈奴，薨。
entries.en: The line passed to great-grandson Xiang, who under Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu as a general and died.
entries.literal: The state passed to great-grandson Xiang, who under Emperor Wu was a general, struck the Xiongnu, and died.

entries.zh: 子宗嗣，有罪，完為城旦。
entries.en: His son Zong inherited but was convicted and sentenced to penal labor building walls.
entries.literal: His son Zong succeeded; for a crime he was spared mutilation and sentenced to penal labor as a wall-builder.

entries.zh: 至哀帝時，乃封參玄孫之孫本始為平陽侯，二千戶，王莽時薨。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ai, Benshi, a grandson of Cao Shen’s great-great-grandson, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang with two thousand households; he died in Wang Mang’s time.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Ai, Benshi, a grandson of Cao Shen’s great-great-grandson, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang with two thousand households; he died in Wang Mang’s time.

entries.zh: 子宏嗣，建武中先降河北，封平陽侯。
entries.en: His son Hong was among the first to submit in Hebei during the Jianwu era and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang.
entries.literal: His son Hong succeeded; in the Jianwu period he first surrendered north of the He and was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingyang.

entries.zh: 至今八侯。
entries.en: By the compilers’ time the house had produced eight marquises.
entries.literal: Down to the present eight marquises.

entries.zh: 漢王即皇帝位，韓信徙為楚王。
entries.en: When Liu Bang took the throne, Han Xin was moved to the kingship of Chu.
entries.literal: The King of Han assumed the imperial position; Han Xin was transferred to be King of Chu.

entries.zh: 參歸相印焉。
entries.en: Cao Shen handed back his chancellor’s seal.
entries.literal: Shen returned the chancellor’s seal.

entries.zh: 高祖以長子肥為齊王，而以參為相國。
entries.en: Gaozu made his eldest son Liu Fei king of Qi and named Cao Shen minister of state to him.
entries.literal: Gaozu appointed his eldest son Fei King of Qi, and made Shen minister of state.

entries.zh: 高祖六年，與諸侯剖符，賜參爵列侯，食邑平陽萬六百三十戶，世世勿絕。
entries.en: In Gaozu’s sixth year he split the tally with the lords and enfeoffed Cao Shen at Pingyang with 10,630 households in perpetuity.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Gaozu, splitting tallies with the feudal lords, he granted Shen the rank of ranked marquis with an estate at Pingyang of ten thousand six hundred thirty households, generation after generation not to be cut off.

entries.zh: 參以齊相國擊陳豨將張春，破之。
entries.en: As Qi’s minister of state Cao Shen defeated Chen Xi’s general Zhang Chun.
entries.literal: Shen as Qi minister of state struck Chen Xi’s general Zhang Chun and destroyed him.

entries.zh: 黥布反，參從悼惠王將車騎十二萬，與高祖會擊黥布軍，大破之。
entries.en: When Qing Bu rose, Cao Shen led a hundred twenty thousand chariots and horse for Prince Liu Fei (Daohui), joined Gaozu, and shattered Qing Bu’s army.
entries.literal: When Qing Bu rebelled, Shen followed Prince Dao Hui of Qi in commanding a hundred twenty thousand chariots and horse, joining Gaozu in striking Qing Bu’s army and smashing it greatly.

entries.zh: 南至蘄，還定竹邑、相、蕭、留。
entries.en: He drove south to Qi, then on the withdrawal secured Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.
entries.literal: South he reached Qi, returning to pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.

entries.zh: 漢二年，拜為假左丞相，入屯兵關中。
entries.en: In the second Han year he was named acting left chancellor and sent into Guanzhong to garrison troops.
entries.literal: In the second year of Han he was appointed acting left chancellor and entered to station troops in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 月餘，魏王豹反，以假丞相別與韓信東攻魏將孫速東張，大破之。
entries.en: A month later King Bao of Wei rebelled; Cao Shen, still acting chancellor, joined Han Xin in a separate column, struck Wei general Sun Su at Dongzhang, and shattered him.
entries.literal: After a month more the King of Wei Bao rebelled; as acting chancellor in a separate column with Han Xin he struck east against Wei general Sun Su at Dongzhang, smashing him.

entries.zh: 因攻安邑，得魏將王襄。
entries.en: He pressed on to Anyi and took Wei general Wang Xiang prisoner.
entries.literal: Then he attacked Anyi and captured Wei general Wang Xiang.

entries.zh: 擊魏王於曲陽，追至東垣，生獲魏王豹。
entries.en: At Quyang he engaged King Bao of Wei, chased him to Dongyuan, and took him alive.
entries.literal: He struck the King of Wei at Quyang, pursued to Dongyuan, and captured alive the King of Wei, Bao.

entries.zh: 取平陽，得豹母妻子，盡定魏地，凡五十二縣。
entries.en: He took Pingyang, captured Wei Bao's mother, wife, and children, and pacified all fifty-two counties of Wei.
entries.literal: He took Pingyang, captured Wei Bao's mother, wife, and children, and fully pacified the fifty-two counties of Wei.

entries.zh: 賜食邑平陽。
entries.en: The court awarded him a revenue fief at Pingyang.
entries.literal: He was granted a food fief at Pingyang.

entries.zh: 因從韓信擊趙相國夏說軍於鄔東，大破之，斬夏說。
entries.en: He then followed Han Xin, routed Zhao's chancellor Xia Yue east of Wu, and killed Xia Yue.
entries.literal: He then joined Han Xin in striking the army of Xia Yue, chancellor of Zhao, east of Wu, smashed it, and beheaded Xia Yue.

entries.zh: 韓信與故常山王張耳引兵下井陘，擊成安君陳餘，而令參還圍趙別將戚公於鄔城中。
entries.en: While Han Xin and Zhang Er drove through Jingxing against Chen Yu, Cao Shen was sent back to bottle up Zhao’s general Qi in Wu.
entries.literal: Han Xin with the former King of Changshan Zhang Er led troops down Jingxing to strike Lord Cheng’an Chen Yu, and ordered Shen in return to besiege Zhao’s detached general Lord Qi in Wu city.

entries.zh: 戚公出走，追斬之。
entries.en: When Qi broke out and ran, Cao Shen overtook him and cut him down.
entries.literal: Lord Qi fled out; [Shen] pursued and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 乃引兵詣漢王在所。
entries.en: He then marched to join the King of Han.
entries.literal: Then he led troops to where the King of Han was.

entries.zh: 韓信已破趙，為相國，東擊齊，參以左丞相屬焉。
entries.en: After Han Xin crushed Zhao he was named chancellor of state and turned east on Qi; Cao Shen served under him as left chancellor.
entries.literal: Han Xin having destroyed Zhao became chancellor of state and struck east at Qi; Shen was attached to him as left chancellor.

entries.zh: 攻破齊歷下軍，遂取臨淄。
entries.en: He shattered the Qi host at Lixia and captured the capital Linzi.
entries.literal: He broke and overcame Qi’s army at Lixia, then took Linzi.

entries.zh: 還定濟北郡，收著、漯陰、平原、鬲、盧。
entries.en: He secured Jibei on the way back, recovering Zhu, Luoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.
entries.literal: Returning he pacified Jibei commandery, taking Zhu, Luoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.

entries.zh: 已而從韓信擊龍且軍於上假密，大破之，斬龍且，虜亞將周蘭。
entries.en: He next followed Han Xin against Long Ju at Jiami, broke his army, slew Long Ju, and took Zhou Lan, his second-in-command, prisoner.
entries.literal: Subsequently he followed Han Xin in striking Long Ju's army at Jiami, smashed it, beheaded Long Ju, and captured deputy general Zhou Lan.

entries.zh: 定齊郡，凡得七十縣。
entries.en: He brought the whole of Qi under control—seventy counties.
entries.literal: He pacified the commanderies of Qi, in all obtaining seventy counties.

entries.zh: 得故齊王田廣相田光，其守相許章，及故將軍田既。
entries.en: He captured Tián Guāng, chancellor to Tián Guǎng, the former King of Qi; Xu Zhang, the acting chancellor; and Tian Ji, a former general.
entries.literal: He captured Tián Guāng, chancellor to Tián Guǎng, the former King of Qi; Xu Zhang, the acting chancellor; and the former general Tian Ji.

entries.zh: 韓信立為齊王，引兵東詣陳，與漢王共破項羽，而參留平齊未服者。
entries.en: After Han Xin was made King of Qi he marched east to Chen to help the King of Han destroy Xiang Yu, while Cao Shen stayed to mop up Qi’s holdouts.
entries.literal: Han Xin being established as King of Qi led troops east to Chen, with the King of Han together destroying Xiang Yu, while Shen remained to pacify those of Qi not yet submitted.

entries.zh: 孝惠元年，除諸侯相國法，更以參爲齊丞相。
entries.en: In Emperor Hui's first year, the office of minister of state in the vassal kingdoms was abolished, and Cao Shen was redesignated chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Emperor Hui, the office of minister of state in the vassal kingdoms was abolished, and Shen was redesignated chancellor of Qi.

entries.zh: 參之相齊，齊七十城。
entries.en: When Cao Shen governed Qi, the state had seventy cities.
entries.literal: When Can governed Qi, Qi had seventy cities.

entries.zh: 天下初定，悼惠王富於春秋，參盡召長老諸先生，問所以安集百姓。
entries.en: The empire had just been settled; King Dao Hui was still young. Cao Shen summoned all the elders and various masters and asked how to settle and gather the people.
entries.literal: The empire had just been settled; King Dao Hui was in the vigor of youth. Can summoned all the elders and various masters and asked how to settle and gather the people.

entries.zh: 而齊故諸儒以百數，言人人殊，參未知所定。
entries.en: Qi's established Confucian scholars numbered in the hundreds, and each offered different advice, leaving Cao Shen unsure what policy to adopt.
entries.literal: But the long-established Confucian scholars of Qi numbered in the hundreds; each man's words differed, and Shen did not know what to decide.

entries.zh: 聞膠西有蓋公，善治黃老言，使人厚幣請之。
entries.en: He heard that in Jiaoxi there was Master Gai, skilled in Huang-Lao teachings, and sent someone with generous gifts to invite him.
entries.literal: He heard that in Jiaoxi there was Master Gai, skilled in Huang-Lao teachings, and sent someone with generous gifts to invite him.

entries.zh: 既見蓋公，蓋公爲言治道貴清靜而民自定，推此類具言之。
entries.en: When Cao Shen met Master Gai, the scholar explained that government should prize purity and tranquility, allowing the people to settle themselves, and developed the principle in detail.
entries.literal: Once he met Master Gai, Master Gai explained that the art of government prized purity and tranquility, through which the people would settle themselves, and elaborated fully on this principle.

entries.zh: 參於是避正堂，舍蓋公焉。
entries.en: Cao Shen then yielded the main hall and lodged Master Gai there.
entries.literal: Can then yielded the main hall and lodged Master Gai there.

entries.zh: 其治要用黃老術，故相齊九年，齊國安集，大稱賢相。
entries.en: His governing essentials used Huang-Lao methods; therefore he served as chancellor of Qi for nine years, Qi was settled and gathered, and he was greatly praised as a worthy chancellor.
entries.literal: His governing essentials used Huang-Lao methods; therefore he was chancellor of Qi for nine years, Qi was settled and gathered, and he was greatly praised as a worthy chancellor.

entries.zh: 蕭何薨，參聞之，告舍人趣治行，「吾且入相。」
entries.en: When Xiao He died, Cao Shen heard of it and told his house attendants to hurry and prepare for the journey: "I am about to enter the chancellorship."
entries.literal: Xiao He died; when Can heard it, he told his house attendants to hurry and prepare for the journey: "I am about to enter the chancellorship."

entries.zh: 居無何，使者果召參。
entries.en: Before long, an envoy indeed summoned Cao Shen.
entries.literal: Before long, an envoy indeed summoned Can.

entries.zh: 參去，屬其後相曰：「以齊獄市爲寄，慎勿擾也。」
entries.en: When Cao Shen departed, he entrusted his successor, saying, "Take the prisons and markets of Qi as your charge; be careful not to disturb them."
entries.literal: When Can departed, he entrusted his successor, saying, "Take the prisons and markets of Qi as your charge; be careful not to disturb them."

entries.zh: 後相曰：「治無大於此者乎？」
entries.en: The successor said, "Is there nothing greater in governing than this?"
entries.literal: The successor said, "Is there nothing greater in governing than this?"

entries.zh: 參曰：「不然。
entries.en: Cao Shen said, "Not so.
entries.literal: Can said, "Not so.

entries.zh: 夫獄市者，所以并容也，今君擾之，姦人安所容乎？
entries.en: Prisons and markets must make room even for dubious people. If you meddle with them, where will such people go?
entries.literal: Prisons and markets are places that accommodate all sorts; if you now disturb them, where will wrongdoers find room?

entries.zh: 吾是以先之。」
entries.en: That is why I put this first."
entries.literal: That is why I put this first."

entries.zh: 張蒼，陽武人也，好書律曆。
entries.en: Zhang Cang was a native of Yangwu who devoted himself to books, law, and the calendar.
entries.literal: Zhang Cang was a man of Yangwu; he loved books, statutes, and calendrical astronomy.

entries.zh: 秦時為御史，主柱下方書。
entries.en: Under the Qin he served as imperial clerk, supervising the archive of documents beneath the pillar.
entries.literal: In Qin times he was an imperial clerk, in charge of the documents kept beneath the pillar.

entries.zh: 有罪，亡歸。
entries.en: He ran afoul of the law and fled home.
entries.literal: Having committed an offense, he fled and returned home.

entries.zh: 及沛公略地過陽武，蒼以客從攻南陽。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei was expanding his holdings and marched through Yangwu, Zhang Cang joined him as a retainer and took part in the campaign against Nanyang.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei seized territory and passed through Yangwu, Cang as a guest-retainer followed him to attack Nanyang.

entries.zh: 蒼當斬，解衣伏質，身長大，肥白如瓠，時王陵見而怪其美士，乃言沛公，赦勿斬。
entries.en: Zhang Cang was condemned to death. He bared his torso and stretched out on the block—tall and heavyset, his skin pale and smooth as a gourd. Wang Ling happened to see him, struck by what an impressive man he was, and interceded with the Lord of Pei, who spared his life.
entries.literal: Cang was sentenced to beheading; he stripped and lay on the execution block. His body was tall and large, fat and white as a gourd. At that time Wang Ling saw him, marveled at this fine gentleman, and spoke to the Lord of Pei, who pardoned him from beheading.

entries.zh: 遂西入武關，至咸陽。
entries.en: They then marched west through Wu Pass into Xianyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon they went west, entered Wu Pass, and reached Xianyang.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，入漢中，還定三秦。
entries.en: The Lord of Pei was made King of Han, withdrew into Hanzhong, and then fought his way back to subdue the Three Qin.
entries.literal: The Lord of Pei was established as King of Han; he entered Hanzhong and returned to pacify the Three Qin.

entries.zh: 陳餘擊走常山王張耳，耳歸漢。
entries.en: Chen Yu routed Zhang Er, the King of Changshan, who then came over to Han.
entries.literal: Chen Yu attacked and drove away the King of Changshan Zhang Er, and Er returned to Han.

entries.zh: 漢以蒼為常山守。
entries.en: The Han court named Zhang Cang governor of Changshan.
entries.literal: Han appointed Cang governor of Changshan.

entries.zh: 從韓信擊趙，蒼得陳餘。
entries.en: He followed Han Xin against Zhao and took Chen Yu prisoner.
entries.literal: Following Han Xin in attacking Zhao, Cang captured Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 趙地已平，漢王以蒼為代相，備邊冠。
entries.en: Once Zhao had been secured, the King of Han appointed Zhang Cang minister of Dai to hold the northern frontier.
entries.literal: When Zhao's territory was pacified, the King of Han made Cang minister of Dai, to prepare the border against incursions.

entries.zh: 已而徙為趙相，相趙王耳。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to serve as Zhao's chancellor under King Zhang Er.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to be minister of Zhao, serving King Er of Zhao.

entries.zh: 耳卒，相其子敖。
entries.en: When Zhang Er died, Zhang Cang became chancellor to his son Ao.
entries.literal: When Er died, he served his son Ao.

entries.zh: 復徙相代。
entries.en: He was moved once more to the chancellorship of Dai.
entries.literal: Again he was transferred to minister Dai.

entries.zh: 燕王臧荼反，蒼以代相從攻荼有功，封為北平侯，食邑千二百戶。
entries.en: When Zang Tu, king of Yan, rose in rebellion, Zhang Cang accompanied the campaign in his capacity as chancellor of Dai, distinguished himself, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Beiping with twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: The King of Yan Zang Tu rebelled; Cang, as minister of Dai, followed in attacking Tu, meriting service, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Beiping with a fief of 1,200 households.

entries.zh: 周昌者，沛人也。
entries.en: Zhou Chang was a native of Pei.
entries.literal: Zhou Chang was a man of Pei.

entries.zh: 其從兄苛，秦時皆為泗水卒史。
entries.en: His cousin Zhou Ke had served with him under the Qin as clerks of the corps for the Sishui commandery.
entries.literal: His cousin Ke—in Qin times both served as clerks of the corps for Sishui.

entries.zh: 及高祖起沛，擊破泗水守監，於是苛、昌以卒史從沛公，沛公以昌為職志，苛為客。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor rose at Pei and overthrew the Sishui governor and his inspector, the Zhou brothers followed the Lord of Pei in their old clerkships; the Lord of Pei named Zhou Chang duty officer and Zhou Ke a guest-retainer.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor rose in Pei, struck and defeated the Sishui governor and supervisor, thereupon Ke and Chang followed the Lord of Pei as clerks of the corps; the Lord of Pei made Chang duty officer and Ke a guest-retainer.

entries.zh: 從入關破秦。
entries.en: They accompanied him through the passes and helped bring down the Qin.
entries.literal: They followed him into the passes and broke Qin.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，以苛為御史大夫，昌為中尉。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei became King of Han, he appointed Zhou Ke imperial counsellor and Zhou Chang commandant of the guard.
entries.literal: The Lord of Pei was established as King of Han; he made Ke imperial counsellor and Chang commandant of the guard.

entries.zh: 昌為人強力，敢直言，自蕭、曹等皆卑下之。
entries.en: Zhou Chang was blunt and fearless; even Xiao He and Cao Shen treated him with deference.
entries.literal: Chang was by nature forceful and dared speak plainly; even Xiao, Cao, and the rest held themselves beneath him.

entries.zh: 昌嘗燕入奏事，高帝方擁戚姬，昌還走。
entries.en: Once, when Zhou Chang came in informally to report on business, he found the High Ancestor with Lady Qi in his arms and beat a hasty retreat.
entries.literal: Chang once at ease entered to report affairs; the High Ancestor was embracing Lady Qi, and Chang turned and ran.

entries.zh: 高帝逐得，騎昌項，上問曰：「我何如主也？」
entries.en: The High Ancestor caught up, threw an arm over his shoulders like a rider's grip, and asked, "What kind of sovereign do you take me for?"
entries.literal: The High Ancestor chased and caught him, rode Chang's neck, and asked, "What sort of ruler am I?"

entries.zh: 昌仰曰：「陛下即桀、紂之主也。」
entries.en: Zhou Chang looked him in the eye and said, "You are a sovereign in the mold of Jie or Zhou—the last kings of Xia and Shang."
entries.literal: Chang looked up and said, "Your Majesty is even a ruler like Jie or Zhou."

entries.zh: 於是上笑之，然尤憚昌。
entries.en: The emperor laughed—but from then on he was warier of Zhou Chang than ever.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor laughed at him, yet all the more feared Chang.

entries.zh: 及高帝欲廢太子，而立威姬子如意為太子，大臣固爭莫能得，上以留侯策止。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor wanted to set aside the heir apparent in favor of Lady Qi's son Ruyi, his senior ministers argued themselves hoarse to no avail, until he dropped the idea on the advice of the Marquis of Liu.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor wished to abolish the heir apparent and establish the son of Lady Qi, Ruyi, as heir apparent, the great ministers firmly remonstrated but could not prevail, until the emperor stopped it with the Marquis of Liu's stratagem.

entries.zh: 而昌庭爭之強，上問其說，昌為人吃，又盛怒，曰：「臣口不能言，然臣期期知其不可。
entries.en: Zhou Chang opposed him just as fiercely in open court. Asked to explain, he stammered with rage: "I—I cannot find the words, but I know in my bones this must not happen.
entries.literal: But Chang remonstrated forcefully in court; the emperor asked his reasoning. Chang stuttered, and moreover was in great anger, saying, "Your subject's mouth cannot speak, yet your subject qi-qi knows it cannot be done.

entries.zh: 陛下欲廢太子，臣期期不奉詔。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty insists on deposing the heir, I—I will not carry out the edict."
entries.literal: Your Majesty wishes to abolish the heir apparent; your subject qi-qi will not accept the edict."

entries.zh: 上欣然而笑，即罷。
entries.en: The emperor broke into a relieved laugh and let the matter drop.
entries.literal: The emperor laughed with pleasure and desisted.

entries.zh: 呂後側耳於東箱聽，見昌，為跪謝曰：「微君，太子幾廢。」
entries.en: Empress Lü had been listening from the eastern gallery. When she met Zhou Chang afterward, she knelt in gratitude and said, "Had it not been for you, the heir would have been lost."
entries.literal: Empress Lü listened with her ear at the eastern corridor; when she saw Chang, she knelt in thanks and said, "Were it not for you, the heir would nearly have been abolished."

entries.zh: 嘉為人廉直，門不受私謁。
entries.en: Shentu Jia was honest and blunt; he would not receive private callers at his gate.
entries.literal: Jia as a person was incorrupt and upright; his gate did not accept private visits.

entries.zh: 是時，太中大夫鄧通方愛幸，賞賜累巨萬。
entries.en: At that time Deng Tong, a grandee of the palace, stood high in the emperor's favor, and the gifts heaped on him ran into tens of thousands in cash.
entries.literal: At that time Grandee of the Palace Deng Tong was just then loved and favored; rewards and gifts accumulated to tens of thousands in gold.

entries.zh: 文帝常燕飲通家，其寵如是。
entries.en: Emperor Wen often dropped in informally to drink at Deng Tong's house; such was the extent of his favor.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen often at ease drank at Tong's house; his favor was thus.

entries.zh: 是時，嘉入朝而通居上旁，有怠慢之禮。
entries.en: Once, when Shentu Jia came to court, Deng Tong was lounging at the emperor's side with a slovenly disregard for protocol.
entries.literal: At that time, when Jia entered court, Tong sat beside the emperor and had negligent ritual demeanor.

entries.zh: 嘉奏事畢，因言曰：「陛下幸愛群臣則富貴之，至於朝廷之禮，不可以不肅！」
entries.en: When Shentu Jia had finished his report, he added, "If Your Majesty wishes to show love to your ministers, wealth and rank are the way to do it—but the dignity of the court must be kept inviolate."
entries.literal: When Jia finished presenting affairs, he thereupon said, "If Your Majesty in favor loves the assembled ministers, then enrich and ennoble them; as for the ritual of the court, it cannot but be solemn!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「君勿言，吾私之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Say no more; he is my private favorite."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "You, do not speak; I favor him privately."

entries.zh: 罷朝坐府中，嘉為檄召通詣丞相府，不來，且斬通。
entries.en: After court Shentu Jia returned to his compound and issued a written summons ordering Deng Tong to report to the chancellor's residence, warning that if he failed to appear he would be executed.
entries.literal: Court dismissed, sitting in the office, Jia drafted a summons calling Tong to come to the chancellor's office; if he did not come, he would behead Tong.

entries.zh: 通恐，入言上。
entries.en: Deng Tong was terrified and ran to the emperor.
entries.literal: Tong was afraid and went in to speak to the emperor.

entries.zh: 上曰：「汝第往，吾今使人召若。」
entries.en: The emperor told him, "Go as summoned; I will send for you in good time."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "You just go; I will now send someone to summon you."

entries.zh: 通至丞相府，免冠，徒跣，頓首謝嘉。
entries.en: Deng Tong presented himself at the chancellor's gate bareheaded and barefoot, kowtowing in apology to Shentu Jia.
entries.literal: When Tong reached the chancellor's office, he removed cap, went barefoot, and knocked his head in apology to Jia.

entries.zh: 嘉坐自如，弗為禮，責曰：「夫朝廷者，高皇帝之朝廷也，通小臣，戲殿上，大不敬，當斬。
entries.en: Shentu Jia remained seated and did not return the courtesy. "This court," he said, "is the court of the High Emperor. Deng Tong is a minor official who has made a mockery of the throne—a capital offense.
entries.literal: Jia sat at ease, did not perform ritual for him, and rebuked, saying, "As for the court, it is the High Emperor's court; Tong is a petty minister, playing on the hall—great disrespect; he should be beheaded.

entries.zh: 史今行斬之！」
entries.en: Officers, carry out the sentence and behead him!"
entries.literal: Scribe—now carry out beheading him!"

entries.zh: 通頓首，首盡出血，不解。
entries.en: Deng Tong kowtowed until his forehead bled, but Shentu Jia would not relent.
entries.literal: Tong knocked his head; his head was entirely bleeding out, and he was not released.

entries.zh: 上度丞相已困通，使使持節召通，而謝丞相：「此語弄臣，君釋之。」
entries.en: When the emperor judged that the chancellor had Deng Tong sufficiently frightened, he dispatched an envoy with imperial credentials to recall him and sent word to Shentu Jia: "He is my household fool; let him go."
entries.literal: The emperor estimated the chancellor had already cornered Tong; he sent an envoy bearing credentials to summon Tong, and apologized to the chancellor, "This is my jesting minister; you, release him."

entries.zh: 鄧通既至，為上泣曰：「丞相幾殺臣。」
entries.en: When Deng Tong reached the palace, he wept before the emperor and said, "The chancellor came within a hair of killing me."
entries.literal: When Deng Tong had arrived, he wept before the emperor, saying, "The chancellor nearly killed your subject."

entries.zh: 遷為計相，一月，更以列侯為主計四歲。
entries.en: He was promoted to counting minister; a month later he was reassigned, still as a full marquis, to serve four years as chief of the annual accounts.
entries.literal: He was promoted to counting minister; after one month, he was again made chief counter for four years as a full marquis.

entries.zh: 是時，蕭何為相國，而蒼乃自秦時為柱下御史，明習天下圖書計籍，又善用算律曆，故令蒼以列侯居相府，領主郡國上計者。
entries.en: Xiao He was chancellor at the time, and Zhang Cang—who had been a pillar-clerk recorder under the Qin—knew the empire's maps, archives, and tax rolls inside out and was adept at calculation, law, and the calendar. The court therefore had him, still a full marquis, take quarters in the chancellor's compound and supervise the officials who received the year-end reports from every commandery and kingdom.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao He was chancellor, and Cang had since Qin times been the pillar-clerk recorder; he was thoroughly versed in the empire's maps, documents, and registers, and moreover skilled at reckoning, statutes, and the calendar; therefore Cang was ordered, as a full marquis, to reside in the chancellor's office and oversee those who presented the annual accounts from the commanderies and kingdoms.

entries.zh: 黥布反，漢立皇子長為淮南王，而蒼相之。
entries.en: When Qing Bu rebelled, the Han enthroned the imperial prince Liu Chang as king of Huainan, with Zhang Cang as his chancellor.
entries.literal: When Qing Bu rebelled, Han established the imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Cang served him as minister.

entries.zh: 十四年，遷為御史大夫 〈(180 BCE)〉。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of his reign (180 BCE) he was raised to the rank of imperial counsellor.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to imperial counsellor (180 BCE).

entries.zh: 漢三年，楚圍漢王滎陽急，漢王出去，而使苛守滎陽城。
entries.en: In the third year of Han, Chu forces had Xingyang in a stranglehold; the King of Han slipped away but left Zhou Ke to hold the city.
entries.literal: In the third year of Han, Chu besieged the King of Han at Xingyang urgently; the King of Han went out but left Ke to hold Xingyang city.

entries.zh: 楚破滎陽城，欲令苛將，苛罵曰：「若趣降漢王！
entries.en: When Chu took Xingyang, they tried to make Zhou Ke switch sides. He shouted back at them, "Surrender to the King of Han at once!
entries.literal: When Chu broke Xingyang city, they wished to have Ke command for them; Ke cursed them, saying, "Hurry and surrender to the King of Han!

entries.zh: 不然，今為虜矣！」
entries.en: If you refuse, you will be prisoners before the day is out!"
entries.literal: If not, you will now become captives!"

entries.zh: 項羽怒，亨苛。
entries.en: Enraged, Xiang Yu had Zhou Ke executed in the cauldron.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu in anger boiled Ke alive.

entries.zh: 漢王於是拜昌為御史大夫。
entries.en: The King of Han then named Zhou Chang imperial counsellor.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King of Han appointed Chang imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 常從擊破項籍。
entries.en: He fought at the king's side until Xiang Yu was destroyed.
entries.literal: He constantly followed in striking and defeating Xiang Ji.

entries.zh: 六年，與蕭、曹等俱封，為汾陰侯。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed along with Xiao He, Cao Shen, and the rest, as marquis of Fenyin.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, together with Xiao, Cao, and others he was enfeoffed and made marquis of Fenyin.

entries.zh: 苛子成以父死事，封為高景侯。
entries.en: Zhou Ke's son Cheng was enfeoffed as marquis of Gaojing in recognition of his father's sacrifice.
entries.literal: Ke's son Cheng, because his father died in service, was enfeoffed as marquis of Gaojing.

entries.zh: 是歲，戚姬子如意為趙王，年十歲，高祖憂萬歲之後不全也。
entries.en: That same year Lady Qi's son Ruyi, only ten, was invested as king of Zhao, and the High Ancestor brooded over how to keep the boy safe after his own death.
entries.literal: That year Lady Qi's son Ruyi became King of Zhao, aged ten, and the High Ancestor worried that after his ten-thousand-year span [death] he would not be kept whole.

entries.zh: 趙堯為符璽御史，趙人方與公謂御史大夫周昌曰：「君之史趙堯年雖少，然奇士，君必異之，是且代君之位。」
entries.en: Zhao Yao served as clerk of tallies and seals. A Zhao native known as the lord of Fangyu said to Imperial Counsellor Zhou Chang, "That clerk of yours, Zhao Yao, is young, but he is no ordinary man. Mark my words—he will one day take your chair."
entries.literal: Zhao Yao was clerk of the tallies and seals; a man of Zhao, the lord of Fangyu, said to imperial counsellor Zhou Chang, "Your clerk Zhao Yao, though young, is an extraordinary gentleman; you must treat him as unusual; he will replace your position."

entries.zh: 昌笑曰：「堯年少，刀筆吏耳，何至是乎！」
entries.en: Zhou Chang laughed. "Zhao Yao is a youngster—a mere scribal clerk. How could he rise that high?"
entries.literal: Chang laughed and said, "Yao is young, a brush-and-knife clerk only; how could it reach this!"

entries.zh: 居頃之，堯侍高祖，高祖獨心不樂，悲歌，群臣不知上所以然。
entries.en: Not long afterward Zhao Yao was attending the High Ancestor, who sat alone in gloom, humming a mournful tune while his ministers wondered what troubled him.
entries.literal: After a short while, Yao attended the High Ancestor; the High Ancestor alone was unhappy in heart, sang sadly, and the assembled ministers did not know why the emperor was thus.

entries.zh: 堯進請問曰：「陛下所為不樂，非以趙王年少，而戚夫人與呂後有隙，備萬歲之後而趙王不能自全乎？」
entries.en: Zhao Yao stepped forward and said softly, "Your Majesty's sorrow—is it not because the king of Zhao is still a child, because Lady Qi and the empress are at odds, and because you fear for his life once you are gone?"
entries.literal: Yao advanced and asked, saying, "What Your Majesty does in being unhappy—is it not because the King of Zhao is young, and Lady Qi and Empress Lü have a rift, and you prepare for after your ten-thousand-year span that the King of Zhao cannot preserve himself?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「我私憂之，不知所出。」
entries.en: The High Ancestor replied, "It weighs on me privately, and I see no way through."
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, "I privately worry about it and do not know the way out."

entries.zh: 堯曰：「陛下獨為趙王置貴強相，及呂後、太子、群臣素所敬憚者乃可。」
entries.en: Zhao Yao said, "Then invest Zhao with a chancellor who is both weighty and formidable—someone the empress, the heir, and the whole court already fear and respect."
entries.literal: Yao said, "Your Majesty alone for the King of Zhao should appoint a noble and strong minister, and it must be one whom Empress Lü, the heir apparent, and the assembled ministers have always respected and feared."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「然。
entries.en: The High Ancestor said, "Exactly.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, "So.

entries.zh: 吾念之欲如是，而群臣誰可者？」
entries.en: I have been turning that very thought over in my mind—but whom among my ministers can I send?"
entries.literal: I have thought to wish it thus, but among the assembled ministers who is suitable?"

entries.zh: 堯曰：「御史大夫昌，其人堅忍伉直，自呂後、太子及大臣皆素嚴憚之。
entries.en: Zhao Yao answered, "Imperial Counsellor Zhou Chang is stubborn, plain-spoken, and unbending. The empress, the heir, and every senior minister already tread softly around him.
entries.literal: Yao said, "Imperial counsellor Chang—his person is firm, enduring, upright, and blunt; from Empress Lü and the heir apparent down to the great ministers, all have always strictly feared him.

entries.zh: 獨昌可。」
entries.en: He alone will do."
entries.literal: Only Chang is suitable."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「善。」
entries.en: The High Ancestor said, "Very well."
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, "Good."

entries.zh: 於是召昌謂曰：「吾固欲煩公，公強為我相趙。」
entries.en: He summoned Zhou Chang and said, "I hate to impose on you, but I need you to take the chancellorship of Zhao."
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned Chang and said, "I indeed wish to trouble you; you must force yourself to be minister of Zhao for me."

entries.zh: 昌泣曰：「臣初起從陛下，陛下獨奈何中道而棄之于諸侯乎？」
entries.en: Zhou Chang wept. "I have followed Your Majesty since the very beginning. How can you cast me off midway among the regional kings?"
entries.literal: Chang wept and said, "Your subject from the first rose following Your Majesty; how can Your Majesty alone midway abandon him among the feudal lords?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「吾極知其左遷，然吾私憂趙，念非公無可者。
entries.en: The High Ancestor said, "I know full well this is a step down for you. My heart is with Zhao, and no one but you will serve.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, "I extremely know it is a demotion, yet I privately worry for Zhao, and thinking, there is none suitable but you.

entries.zh: 公不得已強行！」
entries.en: You must go, however hard it is!"
entries.literal: You have no choice but to force yourself to go!"

entries.zh: 於是徙御史大夫昌為趙相。
entries.en: Imperial Counsellor Zhou Chang was therefore transferred to the chancellorship of Zhao.
entries.literal: Thereupon imperial counsellor Chang was transferred to be minister of Zhao.

entries.zh: 既行久之，高祖持御史大夫印弄之，曰：「誰可以為御史大夫者？」
entries.en: Some time after Zhou Chang had left, the High Ancestor turned the imperial counsellor's seal over in his hands and asked, "Who is fit to be imperial counsellor now?"
entries.literal: After he had gone a long time, the High Ancestor took the imperial counsellor's seal and toyed with it, saying, "Who can be imperial counsellor?"

entries.zh: 孰視堯曰：「無以易堯。」
entries.en: He fixed his gaze on Zhao Yao and said, "No one else will do."
entries.literal: He stared at Yao and said, "None can replace Yao."

entries.zh: 遂拜堯為御史大夫。
entries.en: Zhao Yao was appointed imperial counsellor on the spot.
entries.literal: Thereupon he appointed Yao imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 堯亦前有軍功食邑，及以御史大夫從擊陳豨有功，封為江邑侯。
entries.en: Zhao Yao already held a fief for earlier military service; as imperial counsellor he campaigned against Chen Xi with distinction and was enfeoffed as marquis of Jiangyi.
entries.literal: Yao also previously had military merit and a fief, and as imperial counsellor followed in attacking Chen Xi, meriting service, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Jiangyi.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，太后使使召趙王，其相昌令王稱疾不行。
entries.en: After the High Ancestor's death, the empress dowager sent for the king of Zhao. Chancellor Zhou Chang had the young king plead illness and refuse to travel.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor died, the empress dowager sent envoys to summon the King of Zhao; his minister Chang ordered the king to claim illness and not go.

entries.zh: 使者三反，昌曰：「高帝屬臣趙王，王年少，竊聞太后怨戚夫人，欲召趙王並誅之。
entries.en: The envoys came back three times. Zhou Chang replied, "The late emperor left the king of Zhao in my care. The boy is young, and word has reached me that the empress dowager bears a grudge against Lady Qi and means to summon the king of Zhao so she can destroy them together.
entries.literal: The envoys returned three times; Chang said, "The High Emperor entrusted the King of Zhao to your subject; the king is young; I privately hear the empress dowager resents Lady Qi and wishes to summon the King of Zhao together to execute them.

entries.zh: 臣不敢遣王，王且亦疾，不能奉詔。」
entries.en: I dare not send him on his way, and in any case he is unwell and cannot obey the summons."
entries.literal: Your subject dares not send the king; the king moreover is also ill and cannot obey the edict."

entries.zh: 太后怒，乃使使召趙相。
entries.en: Furious, the empress dowager sent for the chancellor of Zhao instead.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was angry and thereupon sent envoys to summon the minister of Zhao.

entries.zh: 相至，謁太后，太后罵昌曰：「爾不知我之怨戚氏乎？
entries.en: When he arrived at court and was admitted to her presence, she rounded on Zhou Chang: "Do you not know how I hate the Qi house?
entries.literal: When the minister arrived, he visited the empress dowager; the empress dowager cursed Chang, saying, "Do you not know my resentment toward the Qi clan?

entries.zh: 而不遣趙王！」
entries.en: Yet you still would not send me the king of Zhao!"
entries.literal: Yet you do not send the King of Zhao!"

entries.zh: 昌既被征，高後使使召趙王。
entries.en: Once Zhou Chang had been called away, Empress Gao sent again for the king of Zhao.
entries.literal: When Chang had already been summoned, Empress Gao sent envoys to summon the King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 王果來，至長安月餘，見鴆殺。
entries.en: The boy came. Within little more than a month of his arrival in Chang'an he was dead—poisoned.
entries.literal: The king indeed came; after reaching Chang'an, within a little more than a month he was poisoned to death.

entries.zh: 昌謝病不朝見，三歲而薨，諡曰悼侯。
entries.en: Zhou Chang pleaded illness and stayed away from court. He died three years later and was given the posthumous title Dao—the Lamented Marquis.
entries.literal: Chang pleaded illness and did not attend court audience; after three years he died, posthumous title marquis Dao.

entries.zh: 傳子至孫意，有罪，國除。
entries.en: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson Yi, who forfeited the fief for a crime.
entries.literal: It passed to the son down to the grandson Yi, who committed an offense, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 景帝復封昌孫左車為安陽侯，有罪，國除。
entries.en: Emperor Jing later restored the line, enfeoffing Zhou Chang's grandson Zuoche as marquis of Anyang, but that fief, too, was stripped after a conviction.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing again enfeoffed Chang's grandson Zuoche as marquis of Anyang, who committed an offense, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 初，趙堯既代周昌為御史大夫，高祖崩，事惠帝終世。
entries.en: Zhao Yao had succeeded Zhou Chang as imperial counsellor before the High Ancestor died, and he served out Emperor Hui's entire reign.
entries.literal: At first, when Zhao Yao had replaced Zhou Chang as imperial counsellor, the High Ancestor died, and he served Emperor Hui to the end of his reign.

entries.zh: 高後元年，怨堯前定趙王如意之畫，乃抵堯罪，以廣阿侯任敖為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Empress Gao's reign she remembered how Zhao Yao had engineered the plan to protect Prince Ruyi as king of Zhao, found a charge against him, and replaced him with Ren Ao, marquis of Guang'a, as imperial counsellor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Empress Gao, resenting Yao's earlier settling the plan for King of Zhao Ruyi, she struck Yao with a crime and made marquis of Guang'a Ren Ao imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 任敖，沛人也，少為獄吏。
entries.en: Ren Ao was a native of Pei who began his career as a prison clerk.
entries.literal: Ren Ao was a man of Pei; in youth he was a prison clerk.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗避吏，吏系呂後，遇之不謹。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor was hiding from the authorities, an officer detained Empress Lü and treated her roughly.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor once evaded officials; an official detained Empress Lü and treated her without proper care.

entries.zh: 任敖素善高祖，怒，擊傷主呂後吏。
entries.en: Ren Ao, who had long been friendly with the High Ancestor, flew into a rage and beat the officer who had detained Empress Lü.
entries.literal: Ren Ao had long been on good terms with the High Ancestor; in anger he struck and wounded the official who had detained Empress Lü.

entries.zh: 及高祖初起，敖以客從為御史，守豐二歲。
entries.en: When the uprising began, Ren Ao followed as a retainer, was made an imperial clerk, and held Feng for two years.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor first rose, Ao followed as a guest-retainer and became an imperial clerk, holding Feng for two years.

entries.zh: 高祖立為漢王，東擊項羽，遨遷為上黨守。
entries.en: After the High Ancestor became King of Han and marched east against Xiang Yu, Ren Ao was transferred to govern Shangdang.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor was established as King of Han and marched east to attack Xiang Yu, Ao was transferred to be governor of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 陳豨反，敖堅守，封為廣阿侯，食邑千八百戶。
entries.en: When Chen Xi rebelled, Ren Ao held his post steadfastly and was enfeoffed as marquis of Guang'a with eighteen hundred households.
entries.literal: When Chen Xi rebelled, Ao held firm and was enfeoffed as marquis of Guang'a with a fief of 1,800 households.

entries.zh: 高后時為御史大夫，三歲免。
entries.en: Under Empress Gao he served as imperial counsellor and was removed after three years.
entries.literal: In Empress Gao's time he served as imperial counsellor and was dismissed after three years.

entries.zh: 孝文元年薨，諡曰懿侯。
entries.en: He died in the first year of Emperor Wen's reign and was given the posthumous title Yi—the Gracious Marquis.
entries.literal: In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen he died; his posthumous title was marquis Yi.

entries.zh: 傳子至曾孫越人，坐為太常廟酒酸不敬，國除。
entries.en: The fief passed to his son and on to his great-grandson Yueren, who lost the marquisate for offering sour wine at the Grand Minister of Ceremonies' temple—a capital offense of disrespect.
entries.literal: The title passed to his son down to his great-grandson Yueren, who was charged because the wine for the Grand Minister of Ceremonies' temple was sour and disrespectful, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 漢興二十餘年，天下初定，公卿皆軍吏。
entries.en: More than twenty years had passed since the founding of Han; the realm was only beginning to settle, and most of the men at the summit of government were veterans who had risen from the ranks.
entries.literal: Han had risen more than twenty years; the empire was first settled; dukes and ministers were all military clerks.

entries.zh: 蒼為計相時，緒正律曆。
entries.en: While Zhang Cang held the office of counting minister, he set the statutes and calendar in order.
entries.literal: When Cang was counting minister, he ordered and corrected statutes and the calendar.

entries.zh: 以高祖十月始至霸上，故因秦時本十月為歲首，不革。
entries.en: The High Ancestor had first reached Bashang in the tenth month, so the Han kept the Qin practice of reckoning the new year from the tenth month and did not alter it.
entries.literal: Because the High Ancestor in the tenth month first reached Bashang, therefore following Qin times they fundamentally took the tenth month as year beginning, not changing it.

entries.zh: 推五德之運，以為漢當水德之時，上黑如故。
entries.en: He traced the cycle of the Five Phases and concluded that Han stood under the power of Water; court ritual therefore continued to favor black, as under the Qin.
entries.literal: He inferred the movement of the five powers; he thought Han was at the time of the water power, and upward black remained as before.

entries.zh: 吹律調樂，入之音聲，及以比定律令。
entries.en: He matched pitch-pipes to tune the court music, aligned the scales, and on that basis harmonized the statutes and regulations.
entries.literal: He blew pitch-pipes to adjust music, entered into sounds and tones, and thereby compared and fixed statutes and orders.

entries.zh: 若百工，天下作程品。
entries.en: For every craft under heaven he established standards and grades of workmanship.
entries.literal: As for the hundred crafts, the empire made models and grades.

entries.zh: 至於為丞相，卒就之。
entries.en: By the time he rose to chancellor, he had brought the whole program to completion.
entries.literal: As for becoming chancellor, in the end he completed it.

entries.zh: 故漢家言律曆者本張蒼。
entries.en: Henceforth, whenever the Han court spoke of law and the calendar, it traced the authority back to Zhang Cang.
entries.literal: Therefore those of Han who spoke of statutes and the calendar took Zhang Cang as root.

entries.zh: 蒼凡好書，無所不觀，無所不通，而尤邃律曆。
entries.en: Zhang Cang loved books in general—he read widely, missed little, and went deepest of all into law and calendrical science.
entries.literal: Cang in general loved books; there was nothing he did not read, nothing he did not penetrate, and especially he was deep in statutes and the calendar.

entries.zh: 申屠嘉，梁人也。
entries.en: Shentu Jia was a native of Liang.
entries.literal: Shentu Jia was a man of Liang.

entries.zh: 以材官蹶張從高帝擊項籍，遷為隊率。
entries.en: He served as a strong-arm crossbowman under the High Ancestor in the war against Xiang Yu and rose to platoon leader.
entries.literal: As a strong-arm crossbowman he followed the High Ancestor in attacking Xiang Ji and was promoted to platoon leader.

entries.zh: 從擊黥布，為都尉。
entries.en: He campaigned against Qing Bu and was named commandant.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Qing Bu and became commandant.

entries.zh: 孝惠時，為淮陽守。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui he was governor of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xiaohui's time, he was governor of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 孝文元年，舉故以二千石從高祖者，悉以為關內侯，食邑二十四人，而嘉食邑五百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, every former official at the two-thousand-dan level who had served the High Ancestor was ennobled as a noble within the passes; twenty-four were granted revenue from estates, among them Jia, with five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen, those formerly at two-thousand-dan rank who had followed the High Ancestor were all raised to nobles within the passes; twenty-four received fiefs, and Jia had a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 十六年，遷為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of that reign he was promoted to imperial counsellor.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 張蒼免相，文帝以皇后弟竇廣國賢有行，欲相之，曰：「恐天下以吾私廣國。」
entries.en: When Zhang Cang left the chancellorship, Emperor Wen wished to appoint the empress's brother Dou Guangguo—virtuous and well regarded—to the post, but said, "I am afraid the realm would think I am playing favorites for Guangguo."
entries.literal: Zhang Cang was dismissed from chancellor; Emperor Wen, because the empress's younger brother Dou Guangguo was worthy and had conduct, wished to make him chancellor, saying, "I fear the empire will think I favor Guangguo privately."

entries.zh: 久念不可，而高帝時大臣余見無可者，乃以御史大夫嘉為丞相，因故邑封為故安侯。
entries.en: After long reflection he gave the idea up, and among the surviving senior ministers who had served the founder he could find no one equal to the task. He therefore elevated Imperial Counsellor Shentu Jia to chancellor and, building on the old enfeoffment, created him marquis of Gu'an.
entries.literal: Long pondering, it could not be done; yet among the great ministers of the High Emperor's time who remained, he saw none suitable; thereupon he made imperial counsellor Jia chancellor, and on account of his former fief enfeoffed him as marquis of Gu'an.

entries.zh: 嘉為丞相五歲，文帝崩，孝景即位。
entries.en: Shentu Jia had been chancellor five years when Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne.
entries.literal: Jia was chancellor five years; Emperor Wen died, and Emperor Xiaojing ascended.

entries.zh: 二年，晁錯為內史，貴幸用事，諸法令多所請變更，議以適罰侵削諸侯，而丞相嘉自絀所言不用，疾錯。
entries.en: In the second year of the reign Chao Cuo held the post of inner scribe; favored and powerful, he pushed through wholesale revisions of the law and urged fines and legal pressure to whittle away the princes' domains. Chancellor Shentu Jia found his own counsel ignored and came to detest Chao Cuo.
entries.literal: In the second year, Chao Cuo was inner scribe, noble and favored and wielding power; on many statutes and orders he requested changes, deliberating to use fines and penalties to encroach and diminish the feudal lords, while Chancellor Jia himself was thwarted that his words were not used, and hated Cuo.

entries.zh: 錯為內史，門東出，不便，更穿一門，南出。
entries.en: As inner scribe, Chao Cuo's official gate opened inconveniently to the east, so he opened a second gate to the south.
entries.literal: Cuo as inner scribe had his gate exit east—it was inconvenient; he further bored a gate, exiting south.

entries.zh: 南出者，太上皇廟堧垣也。
entries.en: The southern opening cut through the sacred boundary wall of the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple.
entries.literal: What exited south was the Grand Supreme Emperor temple's shielding wall.

entries.zh: 嘉聞錯穿宗廟垣，為奏請誅錯。
entries.en: When Shentu Jia learned that Chao Cuo had breached a wall of the imperial temple precinct, he memorialized for Chao Cuo's death.
entries.literal: When Jia heard Cuo had bored through the ancestral temple wall, he made a memorial requesting execution of Cuo.

entries.zh: 客有語錯，錯恐，夜入宮上謁，自歸上。
entries.en: A client warned Chao Cuo, who in panic went to the palace that night, sought an audience, and placed himself at the emperor's mercy.
entries.literal: A guest informed Cuo; Cuo was afraid, entered the palace by night to present a visit, and submitted himself to the emperor.

entries.zh: 至朝，嘉請誅內史錯。
entries.en: At the next court session Shentu Jia demanded the execution of Inner Scribe Chao Cuo.
entries.literal: When court came, Jia requested execution of Inner Scribe Cuo.

entries.zh: 上曰：「錯所穿非真廟垣，乃外堧垣，故冗官居其中，且又我使為之，錯無罪。」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "Chao Cuo did not breach the inner temple wall but the outer precinct wall, where retired supernumerary officials were quartered—and I told him to do it. He is guilty of nothing."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "What Cuo bored through was not the true temple wall; it was the outer shielding wall, where former supernumerary officials dwelt within, and moreover I ordered him to do it; Cuo has no guilt."

entries.zh: 罷朝，嘉謂長史曰：「吾悔不先斬錯乃請之，為錯所賣！」
entries.en: After court Shentu Jia told his chief clerk, "I should have cut Chao Cuo's throat before I ever brought the matter to the throne—he has made a fool of me."
entries.literal: Court dismissed, Jia said to the chief clerk, "I regret not first beheading Cuo and then requesting it—I have been sold by Cuo!"

entries.zh: 至舍，因嘔血而死。
entries.en: He reached home, vomited blood, and died.
entries.literal: When he reached his lodging, thereupon he vomited blood and died.

entries.zh: 諡曰節侯。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Jie—the Steadfast Marquis.
entries.literal: Posthumous title was marquis Jie.

entries.zh: 傳子至孫臾，有罪，國除。
entries.en: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson Yu, who lost the fief for a crime.
entries.literal: It passed to the son down to the grandson Yu, who committed an offense, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 蒼為丞相十餘年，魯人公孫臣上書，陳終始五德傳，言「漢土德時，其符黃龍見，當改正朔，易服色」。
entries.en: Zhang Cang had been chancellor for more than ten years when Gongsun Chen of Lu submitted a memorial on the cycle of the Five Phases, saying, "When Han enters the era of Earth, the omen will be the appearance of a yellow dragon; the calendar and court colors must be changed."
entries.literal: Cang had been chancellor more than ten years when Gongsun Chen of Lu submitted a memorial presenting the transmission of the beginning and end of the five powers, saying, "When Han is in the time of the earth power, its omen is the appearance of the yellow dragon; the new year and court colors should be changed."

entries.zh: 事下蒼，蒼以為非是，罷之。
entries.en: The memorial was referred to Zhang Cang, who rejected it and had the proposal set aside.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to Cang; Cang thought it was not correct and dismissed it.

entries.zh: 其後黃龍見成紀，於是文帝召公孫臣以為博士，草立土德時曆制度，更元年。
entries.en: Later, when a yellow dragon was sighted at Chengji, Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an erudite, and had him draft the calendar and institutions for the Earth era and proclaim a new inaugural year.
entries.literal: Afterward a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji; thereupon Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen and made him an erudite, drafting the calendar and institutions of the earth-power era and changing the inaugural year.

entries.zh: 蒼由此自絀，謝病稱老。
entries.en: Zhang Cang took this as a personal rebuff, pleaded illness, and asked to retire on grounds of age.
entries.literal: From this Cang demoted himself, pleaded illness, and claimed old age.

entries.zh: 蒼任人為中候，大為奸利，上以為讓，蒼遂病免。
entries.en: An official Zhang Cang had appointed as zhong hou turned corrupt and profited greatly; when the emperor reproached him, Zhang Cang pleaded illness and resigned.
entries.literal: A man Cang had appointed as zhong hou engaged in great corruption for profit; the emperor reproached him for it, and Cang thereupon pleaded illness and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 孝景五年薨，諡曰文侯。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's reign and was given the posthumous title Wen—the Cultured Marquis.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaojing he died; his posthumous title was marquis Wen.

entries.zh: 傳子至孫類，有罪，國除。
entries.en: The fief passed to his son and then to his grandson Lei, who forfeited the marquisate for a crime.
entries.literal: The title passed to his son down to the grandson Lei, who committed an offense, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 初任敖免，平陽侯曹窋代敖為御史大夫。
entries.en: When Ren Ao was removed from office, Cao Zhu, marquis of Pingyang, succeeded him as imperial counsellor.
entries.literal: At first when Ren Ao was dismissed, marquis of Pingyang Cao Zhu replaced Ao as imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 高後崩，與大臣共誅諸呂。
entries.en: After Empress Gao's death he joined the senior ministers in wiping out the Lü clan.
entries.literal: When Empress Gao died, together with the great ministers he jointly executed the various Lüs.

entries.zh: 後坐事免，以淮南相張蒼為御史大夫。
entries.en: He was later dismissed for an offense, and Zhang Cang, chancellor of Huainan, was named imperial counsellor in his place.
entries.literal: Later, having been charged with an offense, he was dismissed; Huainan minister Zhang Cang was made imperial counsellor.

entries.zh: 蒼與絳侯等尊立代王為孝文皇帝，四年，代灌嬰為丞相。
entries.en: Zhang Cang joined the Marquis of Jiang and the others in raising the King of Dai to the throne as Emperor Wen; in the fourth year of his reign, Cang succeeded Guan Ying as chancellor.
entries.literal: Zhang Cang and the Marquis of Jiang and the others honored and installed the King of Dai as Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year, Cang replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.

entries.zh: 自嘉死後，開封侯陶青、桃侯劉舍及武帝時柏至侯許昌、平棘侯薛澤、武強侯莊青翟、商陵侯趙周，皆以列侯繼踵，娖娖廉謹，為丞相備員而已，無所能發明功名著於世者。
entries.en: After Shentu Jia's death came Tao Qing of Kaifeng and Liu She of Tao, and under Emperor Wu, Xu Chang of Bozhi, Xue Ze of Pingji, Zhuang Qingdi of Wuqiang, and Zhao Zhou of Shangling—each a full marquis who stepped into the chancellorship in turn. They were honest, cautious placeholders, none of whom left a mark on the age.
entries.literal: From after Jia's death, Marquis of Kaifeng Tao Qing, Marquis of Tao Liu She, and in Emperor Wu's time Marquis of Bozhi Xu Chang, Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze, Marquis of Wuqiang Zhuang Qingdi, Marquis of Shangling Zhao Zhou—all followed one another as full marquises, cautious and careful, incorrupt and prudent, serving as chancellor reserve personnel only, none able to develop and clarify merit and fame manifest in the world.

entries.zh: 萬石君石奮，其父趙人也。
entries.en: The Lord of Wan, Shi Fen, traced his father’s line to the state of Zhao.
entries.literal: The Lord of Wan, Shi Fen, was a man of Zhao by his father’s origin.

entries.zh: 趙亡，徙溫。
entries.en: When Zhao was destroyed, the family relocated to Wen.
entries.literal: When Zhao fell, they moved to Wen.

entries.zh: 高祖東擊項籍，過河內，時奮年十五，為小吏，侍高祖。
entries.en: While the Supreme Ancestor was campaigning east against Xiang Yu and passed through Henei, Fen—then fifteen—held a minor clerkship and waited upon him.
entries.literal: When the Supreme Ancestor marched east to attack Xiang Yu and passed through Henei, Fen was fifteen, a petty clerk, and attended the Supreme Ancestor.

entries.zh: 高祖與語，愛其恭敬，問曰：「若何有？」
entries.en: The Supreme Ancestor found him respectful in conversation and asked, "What dependents do you have?"
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor spoke with him, loved his deference and respect, and asked, “What do you have?”

entries.zh: 對曰；
entries.en: Fen answered:
entries.literal: He replied:

entries.zh: 「有母，不幸失明。
entries.en: “My mother has gone blind, I am sorry to say.
entries.literal: “I have a mother who, unhappily, has lost her sight.

entries.zh: 家貧。
entries.en: We are poor.
entries.literal: The family is poor.

entries.zh: 有姊，能鼓瑟。」
entries.en: My elder sister plays the se zither well.”
entries.literal: I have an elder sister who can play the se.”

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「若能從我乎？」
entries.en: The Supreme Ancestor said, “If you can, will you follow me?”
entries.literal: The Supreme Ancestor said, “If you can, will you follow me?”

entries.zh: 曰：「願盡力。」
entries.en: “I will serve you with all I have,” he said.
entries.literal: He said, “I wish to exert my utmost strength.”

entries.zh: 於是高祖召其姊為美人，以奮為中涓，受書謁。
entries.en: The emperor then took Fen’s sister into the harem as a Meiren beauty and made Fen a zhongjuan usher to handle petitions and callers.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Supreme Ancestor summoned his sister to be a Meiren and appointed Fen as palace usher (zhongjuan) to receive petitions and calling cards.

entries.zh: 徙其家長安中戚里，以姊為美人故也。
entries.en: Their household was settled in Qili ward in Chang’an on account of her appointment.
entries.literal: He moved the family to Qili in Chang’an because of the sister’s rank as Meiren.

entries.zh: 張敺字叔，高祖功臣安丘侯說少子也。
entries.en: Zhang Ou—styled Shu—was the youngest son of Zhang Shuo, the Anqiu marquis who had served the dynastic founder.
entries.literal: Zhang Ou, courtesy name Shu, was the youngest son of Marquis of Anqiu Shuo, a meritorious minister of the Supreme Ancestor.

entries.zh: 敺孝文時以治刑名侍太子，然其人長者。
entries.en: Under Wen he tutored the heir in legalist “forms and names,” though his manner remained that of a gentleman.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wen’s time Ou, by studying penal names, attended the Heir Apparent, yet the man was one of mature years.

entries.zh: 景帝時尊重，常為九卿。
entries.en: Jing treated him with respect and kept him among the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jing’s time he was honored and often one of the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 至武帝元朔中，代韓安國為御史大夫。
entries.en: In Wu’s Yuanshuo years he succeeded Han Anguo as Imperial Clerk.
entries.literal: Down to Emperor Wu’s Yuanshuo era he replaced Han Anguo as Imperial Clerk.

entries.zh: 敺為吏，未嘗言按人，剸以誠長者處官。
entries.en: He never boasted of cracking cases; he ran his bureau as a patient elder.
entries.literal: As a clerk he never spoke of pressing people; he governed purely as a man of mature years in office.

entries.zh: 官屬以為長者，亦不敢大欺。
entries.en: Staff who saw him as a soft touch found they could not easily fool him.
entries.literal: His subordinates thought him a man of mature years and also did not greatly deceive him.

entries.zh: 上具獄事，有可卻，卻之；
entries.en: Edicts from the throne that could be softened, he softened;
entries.literal: When the emperor sent down prison cases, if they could be set aside he set them aside;

entries.zh: 不可者，不得已，為涕泣，面而封之。
entries.en: when the law left no room, he wept before the emperor, then sealed the dossier anyway.
entries.literal: if they could not, then unavoidably, weeping, he faced the emperor and sealed them.

entries.zh: 其愛人如此。
entries.en: Such was his reluctance to harm others.
entries.literal: His loving of people was like this.

entries.zh: 奮積功勞，孝文時官至太中大夫。
entries.en: By steady service under Emperor Wen he reached the rank of Grand Counselor of the Palace.
entries.literal: Fen accumulated merit through service; under Emperor Wen he rose to Grand Counselor of the Palace.

entries.zh: 無文學，恭謹，舉無與比。
entries.en: He was no scholar, yet in courtesy and care no one was his match.
entries.literal: He had no literary learning, but was respectful and cautious; none could be compared with him in that.

entries.zh: 東陽侯張相如為太子太傅，免。
entries.en: When Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru was dismissed from the post of Grand Tutor to the heir apparent,
entries.literal: Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru was Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 選可為傅者，皆推奮太子太傅。
entries.en: the court unanimously nominated Fen for Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In choosing who could serve as tutor, all recommended Fen as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 及孝景即位，以奮為九卿。
entries.en: Emperor Jing raised him to one of the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he made Fen one of the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 迫近，憚之，徙奮為諸侯相。
entries.en: Finding him too near and formidable, they moved him to a chancellorship among the feudal states.
