entries.literal: Fen said, "So long as the realm is fortunate enough to be at peace and without incident, I, Fen, have been able to be kin to the throne; what I love are music, dogs, horses, fields, and houses; what I cherish are singers, actors, and clever craftsmen—I am not like Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu, who day and night gather the bold spirits and stalwarts of the realm to debate with them, who slander in the belly and revile in the heart, who look up to mark the sky and look down to trace the earth, who squint between the two palaces, hoping the realm will meet with change so they may win great merit.

entries.zh: 臣乃不如魏其等所為。」
entries.en: I am not in their league."
entries.literal: I am indeed not equal to what Marquis of Weiqi and the others do."

entries.zh: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？」
entries.en: The emperor asked his ministers, "Who speaks truth?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked the court ministers, "Which of the two is right?"

entries.zh: 御史大夫韓安國曰：「魏其言灌夫父死事，身荷戟馳不測之吳軍，身被數十創，名冠三軍，此天下壯士，非有大惡，爭杯酒，不足引它過以誅也。
entries.en: Han Anguo said, "Dou Ying is right that Guan Fu's father died in battle while the son, halberd in hand, charged the Wu lines and took dozens of wounds—a hero of the empire. Without a graver crime than a wine quarrel, he should not die for it.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief Han Anguo said, "As Marquis of Weiqi says, Guan Fu's father died in service; he himself shouldered a halberd and galloped into the immeasurable Wu army, his body suffering dozens of wounds; his fame crowned the three armies—he is a stalwart of the realm. Unless he has committed some great evil, to wring another fault from a quarrel over cups of wine is not enough ground for execution.

entries.zh: 魏其言是。
entries.en: Marquis Dou speaks the truth.
entries.literal: What Marquis of Weiqi says is correct.

entries.zh: 丞相亦言灌夫通姦猾，侵細民，家累巨萬，橫恣穎川，□轢宗室，侵犯骨肉，此所謂『支大於干，脛大於股，不折必披』。
entries.en: The chancellor is also right: Guan Fu consorts with villains, preys on the weak, has piled up a fortune, tyrannizes Yingchuan, rides roughshod over the imperial clan, and wrongs his own blood—what the proverb calls a limb thicker than the trunk, a calf thicker than the thigh: something must snap.
entries.literal: The chancellor also says that Guan Fu associates with crafty scoundrels, bullies the common people, his household wealth piles to vast sums, he runs riot in Yingchuan, tramples the imperial house, and violates flesh-and-blood kin—this is what is called "when the branch is greater than the trunk, when the shin is greater than the thigh, if it does not break it will split."

entries.zh: 丞相信亦是。
entries.en: The chancellor speaks truth as well.
entries.literal: What the chancellor says is also correct.

entries.zh: 唯明主裁之。」
entries.en: Only Your Majesty can judge."
entries.literal: Let the enlightened ruler decide."

entries.zh: 主爵都尉汲黯是魏其。
entries.en: Ji An, chief commandant of the nobility, backed Dou Ying.
entries.literal: Chief Commandant of the Nobility Ji An sided with Marquis of Weiqi.

entries.zh: 內史鄭當時是魏其，後不堅。
entries.en: Palace secretary Zheng Dangshi began on Dou Ying's side, then wavered.
entries.literal: Palace Secretary Zheng Dangshi sided with Marquis of Weiqi, but later did not hold firm.

entries.zh: 餘皆莫敢對。
entries.en: The others held their tongues.
entries.literal: The rest all dared not answer.

entries.zh: 上怒內史曰：「公平生數言魏其、武安長短，今日廷論，局趣效轅下駒，吾並斬若屬矣！」
entries.en: The emperor turned on Zheng Dangshi: "You have spent years weighing Dou Ying against Tian Fen; today at court you freeze like a colt between the traces—I could behead you all!"
entries.literal: The emperor grew angry at the palace secretary and said, "You, sir, have all your life often spoken of the strengths and weaknesses of Marquis of Weiqi and Marquis of Wu'an; today at court debate you are cramped and act like a colt under the shafts—I will behead the lot of you!"

entries.zh: 即罷起入，上食太后。
entries.en: He cut the session short, rose, and withdrew to dine with his mother.
entries.literal: Immediately he stopped, rose, and entered; he took his meal with the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后亦已使人候司，具以語太后。
entries.en: She had already posted spies; they told her everything.
entries.literal: The empress dowager had already sent someone to watch and report; they fully told the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后怒，不食，曰：「我在也，而人皆藉吾弟，令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！
entries.en: She refused her meal in fury: "I am still alive, yet they walk on my brother; when I am gone, will they cut him to pieces?
entries.literal: The empress dowager was angry, would not eat, and said, "While I am still alive, they all trample my younger brother; after I reach a hundred years, will they carve him up like fish meat!

entries.zh: 且帝寧能為石人邪！
entries.en: And is the emperor a block of stone, deaf to his own mother?
entries.literal: Moreover can the emperor really be a stone man!

entries.zh: 此特帝在，即錄錄，設百歲後，是屬寧有可信者乎？」
entries.en: Only while you sit on the throne do they cringe; once you are gone, would you trust a single one of them?"
entries.literal: This is only while the emperor is alive that they are submissive and timid; suppose after a hundred years—can any of this lot be trusted?"

entries.zh: 上謝曰：「俱外家，故廷辨之。
entries.en: The emperor apologized: "Both sides are my in-laws—that is why I aired the dispute in open court.
entries.literal: The emperor apologized and said, "They are both maternal kin, therefore I debated them at court.

entries.zh: 不然，此一獄吏所決耳。」
entries.en: Otherwise a county jailer could have settled it."
entries.literal: If not for that, this would be something a single jail clerk could decide."

entries.zh: 是時，郎中令石建為上分別言兩人。
entries.en: Supervisor of the household Shi Jian then gave the emperor a private briefing on each man.
entries.literal: At that time the supervisor of the household Shi Jian separately explained the two men to the emperor.

entries.zh: 於是上使御史簿責嬰所言灌夫頗不讎，劾繫都司空。
entries.en: The emperor had the censor cross-examine Dou Ying: his claims about Guan Fu did not check out; he was impeached and jailed under the metropolitan superintendent.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered the censor to register and call Ying to account for what he had said about Guan Fu, which largely did not match; he impeached him and bound him in the metropolitan superintendent's custody.

entries.zh: 孝景時，嬰嘗受遺詔，曰「事有不便，以便宜論上」。
entries.en: Emperor Jing had once given Dou Ying a sealed rescript: "If state business goes awry, memorialize as you see fit."
entries.literal: Under Emperor Jing, Ying had once received a testamentary edict saying, "If affairs are inconvenient, you may memorialize at your discretion on what is advantageous."

entries.zh: 及系，灌夫罪至族，事日急，諸公莫敢復明言於上。
entries.en: By then Guan Fu faced extermination of his clan; the case raced toward verdict, and no minister dared speak for Dou Ying at court.
entries.literal: By the time he was bound, Guan Fu's crime reached to clan extermination; the affair grew urgent daily, and no grandee dared speak plainly again to the emperor.

entries.zh: 嬰乃使昆弟子上書言之，幸得召見。
entries.en: Dou Ying smuggled a memorial out through a nephew, hoping for a summons.
entries.literal: Ying then had a nephew submit a memorial on it, hoping to obtain an audience.

entries.zh: 書奏，案尚書，大行無遺詔。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, the imperial secretariat searched its records but found no such testamentary edict from the late emperor.
entries.literal: When the memorial was presented, they examined the secretariat records and found no such testamentary edict from the late emperor.

entries.zh: 詔書獨臧嬰家，嬰家丞封。
entries.en: The only copy of the alleged edict had lain in Dou Ying's house under his steward's seal.
entries.literal: The edict text alone was stored in Ying's house; Ying's household steward had sealed it.

entries.zh: 乃劾嬰矯先帝詔害，罪當棄市。
entries.en: He was charged with forging a dead emperor's edict—a capital offense.
entries.literal: Thereupon they impeached Ying for forging the late emperor's edict to do harm; the crime merited execution in the market.

entries.zh: 五年十月，悉論灌夫支屬。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year the entire Guan clan was condemned.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year, they sentenced all branches of Guan Fu's kin.

entries.zh: 嬰良久乃聞有劾，即陽病痱，不食慾死。
entries.en: Dou Ying learned of the impeachment late; he feigned a stroke, refused food, and prepared to die.
entries.literal: Only after a long time did Ying hear of the impeachment; then he feigned apoplexy, would not eat, and wished to die.

entries.zh: 或聞上無意殺嬰，復食，治病，議定不死矣。
entries.en: Word spread that the emperor would spare him; he took food again, nursed his health, and his friends thought he was safe.
entries.literal: Some heard that the emperor had no intention of killing Ying; he ate again, treated his illness, and they reckoned he would surely not die.

entries.zh: 乃有飛語為惡言聞上，故以十二月晦論棄市渭城。
entries.en: Then anonymous slander reached the throne; on the last day of the twelfth month he was ordered executed at Weicheng market.
entries.literal: Then flying rumors of evil words reached the emperor; therefore on the last day of the twelfth month he was sentenced to execution in the market at Weicheng.

entries.zh: 春，蚡疾，一身盡痛，若有擊者，呼服謝罪。
entries.en: That spring Tian Fen fell ill, racked with pains as from blows, screaming confessions and pleas for mercy.
entries.literal: In spring Fen fell ill; his whole body ached as if struck; he cried out that he submitted and begged pardon.

entries.zh: 上使視鬼者瞻之，曰：「魏其侯與灌夫共守，笞欲殺之。」
entries.en: The emperor sent a spirit-medium, who reported, "Marquis Dou and Guan Fu stand over him, flogging him to death."
entries.literal: The emperor had one who could see ghosts examine him; he said, "Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu together guard him, beating him with sticks and wishing to kill him."

entries.zh: 竟死。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: In the end he died.

entries.zh: 子恬嗣，元朔中有罪免。
entries.en: His son Tian inherited the title but lost it to a crime in Yuanshuo.
entries.literal: His son Tian succeeded; during Yuanshuo he committed a crime and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 後淮南王安謀反，覺。
entries.en: Later Liu An, king of Huainan, rebelled; the plot was exposed.
entries.literal: Later the King of Huainan, Liu An, plotted rebellion; it was discovered.

entries.zh: 始安入朝時，蚡為太尉，迎安霸上，謂安曰：「上未有太子，大王最賢，高祖孫，即宮車晏駕，非大王立，尚誰立哉？」
entries.en: On Liu An's first visit to court, Tian Fen—then grand commandant—met him at Bashang and said, "The throne has no heir; you are Gaozu's ablest grandson; when the emperor dies, if anyone mounts the throne but you, who should it be?"
entries.literal: When An first entered court for an audience, Fen was grand commandant; he welcomed An at Bashang and said to An, "The emperor has not yet established an heir apparent; you, great king, are the worthiest, a grandson of Gaozu; when the imperial carriage is delayed in setting out, if not you, great king, who is established, who else could be?"

entries.zh: 淮南王大喜，厚遺金錢財物。
entries.en: The king of Huainan was delighted and showered him with gold and treasure.
entries.literal: The King of Huainan was greatly pleased and richly presented gold, cash, and goods.

entries.zh: 上自嬰、夫事時不直蚡，特為太后故。
entries.en: Throughout the Dou–Guan affair the emperor had judged Tian Fen in the wrong but indulged him for his mother's sake.
entries.literal: From the time of the affair of Ying and Fu the emperor had not thought Fen in the right, but only for the empress dowager's sake.

entries.zh: 及聞淮南事，上曰：「使武安侯在者，族矣。」
entries.en: When the Huainan case broke, the emperor said, "If Tian Fen still lived, I would exterminate his whole line."
entries.literal: When he heard of the Huainan affair, the emperor said, "If Marquis of Wu'an were still alive, he would have been exterminated to the clan."

entries.zh: 梁王以至親故，得自置相、二千石，出入遊戲，僭於天子。
entries.en: As the emperor's brother, the king of Liang could name his own chancellor and two-thousand-picul officials; his comings and goings aped the imperial style.
entries.literal: Because the King of Liang was close kin, he was permitted to appoint his own chancellor and officials at two thousand piculs; in going out and coming in for sport he exceeded the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子聞之，心不善。
entries.en: The emperor heard of it and took offense.
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of it, his heart was not pleased.

entries.zh: 太后知帝弗善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。
entries.en: The empress dowager knew her son disapproved; she snubbed Liang's messengers and demanded an accounting of the king's behavior.
entries.literal: The empress dowager knew the emperor did not approve; she then grew angry at Liang's envoys, would not receive them, and investigated and called the king to account for his conduct.

entries.zh: 安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，而太后曾不省也？
entries.en: Han Anguo, speaking for Liang, wept before the grand princess: "The king is a dutiful son and a loyal vassal—why will the empress dowager not see it?
entries.literal: Anguo, as Liang's envoy, saw the grand princess and wept, saying, "How is it that the King of Liang, as a son, is filial, as a minister is loyal, yet the empress dowager never examines this?

entries.zh: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反，自關以東皆合從而西向，唯梁最親，為限難。
entries.en: When the seven kingdoms rose east of the passes and turned their spears westward, only Liang—closest of kin—bore the brunt.
entries.literal: The other day when Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao, and the seven states rebelled, from the passes east all joined in a vertical alliance and faced west; only Liang was closest kin and formed the hard barrier.

entries.zh: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，壹言泣數行而下，跪送臣等六人將兵擊卻吳、楚、吳、楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁之力也。
entries.en: With the realm in chaos he thought only of you and the emperor; tears streamed at a single word; he knelt and sent six of us with an army that pinned Wu and Chu so they never marched west—that broke the rebellion.
entries.literal: The King of Liang thought of the empress dowager and the emperor amid them while the marquises were in turmoil; with one word his tears fell in several streams; he knelt and sent us six men with troops to strike back Wu and Chu; for this reason Wu and Chu did not dare go west, and in the end were broken and destroyed—the strength was Liang's.

entries.zh: 今太后以小苛禮責望梁王。
entries.en: Now you fault him for petty breaches of etiquette.
entries.literal: Now the empress dowager blames and expects the King of Liang over petty matters of ritual.

entries.zh: 梁王父兄皆帝王，而所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜，即以□鄙小縣，驅馳國中，欲誇諸侯，令天下知太后、帝愛之也。
entries.en: Raised among emperors, he thinks in large scale: he speaks of imperial escort and cordons because his equipage was all your gift; even on a tour of a minor county he parades the kingdom so all may see how you and the emperor cherish him.
entries.literal: The King of Liang's father and elder brothers were all emperors, and what he has seen is great; therefore when he goes out he speaks of clearing the way, when he enters he speaks of precautions; chariots and banners were all gifts from the emperor—even in this petty commandery he gallops through the state, wishing to boast to the marquises and let the realm know the empress dowager and the emperor love him.

entries.zh: 今梁使來，輒案責之，梁王恐，日夜滋泣思慕，不知所為。
entries.en: Yet every Liang messenger is hauled in for interrogation; the king lives in terror, weeping day and night, unsure what to do.
entries.literal: Now whenever Liang's envoys come, you always investigate and call them to account; the King of Liang is afraid, day and night weeps and longs in thought, and does not know what to do.

entries.zh: 何梁王之忠孝而太后不恤也？」
entries.en: How can he be so loyal and filial while you withhold your mercy?"
entries.literal: How can the King of Liang be loyal and filial while the empress dowager shows no pity?"

entries.zh: 長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為帝言之。」
entries.en: The grand princess repeated every word; the empress dowager beamed and said, "Tell the emperor."
entries.literal: The grand princess reported everything to the empress dowager; the empress dowager was pleased and said, "Speak of it to the emperor."

entries.zh: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」
entries.en: She did; the emperor's anger melted. He doffed his cap and apologized to his mother: "We brothers failed each other and caused you grief."
entries.literal: When she spoke of it, the emperor's heart was then relieved; he removed his cap and apologized to the empress dowager, saying, "Brothers could not instruct each other, and so caused the empress dowager worry."

entries.zh: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。
entries.en: He received every Liang envoy and rewarded them generously.
entries.literal: He received all Liang's envoys and richly rewarded them.

entries.zh: 其後，梁王益親歡。
entries.en: Afterward the bond between throne and king of Liang grew warm again.
entries.literal: After that, the King of Liang grew ever closer in affection.

entries.zh: 太后、長公主更賜安國直千餘金。
entries.en: The empress dowager and the grand princess together gave Han Anguo over a thousand cash-weight in gold.
entries.literal: The empress dowager and the grand princess additionally bestowed on Anguo more than a thousand in cash weight of gold.

entries.zh: 由此顯，結於漢。
entries.en: He rose in fame and was tied to the court at Chang'an.
entries.literal: From this he became eminent and formed ties with Han.

entries.zh: 公孫詭、羊勝說王求為帝太子及益地事，恐漢大臣不聽，乃陰使人刺漢用事謀臣。
entries.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng urged the king to seek the crown princeship and more land; fearing refusal from Chang'an, they hired killers for Han's leading advisers.
entries.literal: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng persuaded the king to seek to become heir apparent to the emperor and to increase his territory; fearing Han ministers would not consent, they secretly sent men to assassinate influential Han strategists.

entries.zh: 及殺故吳相爰盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計劃，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。
entries.en: After they murdered Yuan Ang, the former chancellor of Wu, Emperor Jing learned of the plot and sent men to seize Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng alive.
entries.literal: When they had killed the former chancellor of Wu, Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing eventually learned of Gui and Sheng's plots; he then sent agents to arrest Gui and Sheng, demanding they be taken.

entries.zh: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。
entries.en: Ten separate Han delegations searched Liang from chancellor to constable for over a month without success.
entries.literal: Han envoys came in ten parties to Liang; from the chancellor down the whole state searched greatly for more than a month without finding them.

entries.zh: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。
entries.en: Han Anguo learned the two men were hidden in the palace. He entered in tears: "When the lord is dishonored, his servant should die.
entries.literal: Anguo heard that Gui and Sheng were hidden at the king's place; he then entered, saw the king, and wept, saying, "When the ruler is shamed, the minister should die.

entries.zh: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。
entries.en: You have no loyal ministers—that is why matters have come to this pass.
entries.literal: The great king has no good ministers; therefore it has come to this confusion.

entries.zh: 今勝、詭不得，請辭賜死。」
entries.en: If those two are not produced, grant me death."
entries.literal: Now that Sheng and Gui cannot be obtained, I beg leave to accept a gift of death."

entries.zh: 王曰：「何至此？」
entries.en: The king said, "How can it be so grave?"
entries.literal: The king said, "How has it reached this?"

entries.zh: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高帝及皇帝與臨江王親？」
entries.en: Han Anguo wept freely: "Tell me—which bond is tighter: the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, or the emperor and the prince of Linjiang?"
entries.literal: Anguo's tears fell in several streams as he said, "Great king, you yourself measure against the emperor—which is closer, the Grand Supreme Emperor to Gaozu, or the emperor to the Prince of Linjiang?"

entries.zh: 王曰：「弗如也。」
entries.en: The king said, "I am not as close to the emperor as those pairs were."
entries.literal: The king said, "It does not compare."

entries.zh: 安國曰：「夫太上皇、臨江親父子間，然高帝曰『提三尺取天下者朕也』，故太上終不得制事，居於櫟陽。
entries.en: Han Anguo said: "Gaozu and his father, the emperor and the prince of Linjiang—each was a tight father-son pair—yet Gaozu declared, The sword that won the realm is mine, and the old emperor finished his life powerless at Liyang.
entries.literal: Anguo said, "Between the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, and between the Prince of Linjiang and the emperor—these were close father-and-son bonds—yet Gaozu said, 'He who took the realm with a three-foot sword is I,' so in the end the Grand Supreme could not control affairs and dwelt at Liyang.

entries.zh: 臨江，適長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；
entries.en: The prince of Linjiang was the legitimate eldest son; one slip of the tongue cost him his kingdom;
entries.literal: Linjiang, as the eldest heir apparent of the proper line, because of one word's fault was deposed as king of Linjiang;

entries.zh: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。
entries.en: on a charge about palace walls he ended his life in the metropolitan commandant's yamen.
entries.literal: because of the affair of the palace walls, in the end he killed himself in the commandant of the capital's office.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why was it so?

entries.zh: 治天下終不用私亂公。
entries.en: Because the empire is never ruled by private affection over public law.
entries.literal: In ruling the realm one never uses private feeling to disorder the public good.

entries.zh: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知不為虎？
entries.en: The proverb runs: Even a loving father may prove a tiger;
entries.literal: The saying goes, "Though there is a loving father, how do you know he is not a tiger?

entries.zh: 雖有親兄，安知不為狼？』
entries.en: even a loving brother may prove a wolf."
entries.literal: Though there is a loving elder brother, how do you know he is not a wolf?"

entries.zh: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。
entries.en: You are only a feudal king; venal advisers have led you to break the throne's edicts and warp the code.
entries.literal: Now you, great king, are listed among the marquises; seduced by wicked ministers' empty talk, you violate the sovereign's prohibitions and bend the clear law.

entries.zh: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王。
entries.en: The emperor stays his hand only for his mother's sake.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven, for the empress dowager's sake, cannot bear to apply the law to you, great king.

entries.zh: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。
entries.en: She weeps day and night for you to mend your ways; you refuse to wake.
entries.literal: The empress dowager weeps day and night, hoping you, great king, will reform yourself; you, great king, never wake to it.

entries.zh: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」
entries.en: When her carriage at last climbs the western slope, whom will you cling to?"
entries.literal: Suppose the empress dowager's carriage should be delayed in setting out—whom will you, great king, cling to then?"

entries.zh: 語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出之。」
entries.en: Before he finished, the king was sobbing; he thanked Han Anguo and said, "I will hand them over."
entries.literal: Before the words were finished, the king's tears fell in several streams; he apologized to Anguo, saying, "I will now release them."

entries.zh: 即日詭、勝自殺。
entries.en: That day Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide.
entries.literal: That same day Gui and Sheng killed themselves.

entries.zh: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國力也。
entries.en: The Han envoy reported back; the Liang crisis dissolved—through Han Anguo's doing.
entries.literal: The Han envoy returned and reported; the Liang affair was all released—it was Anguo's strength.

entries.zh: 景帝、太后益重安國。
entries.en: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager prized him the more.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager valued Anguo all the more.

entries.zh: 上怒恢不出擊單于輜重也，恢曰：「始約為入馬邑城，兵與單于接，而臣擊其輜重，可得利。
entries.en: The emperor raged that Wang Hui had not attacked the baggage train. Wang Hui said, "The plan was for the shanyu to enter Mayi while the main army pinned him; I was to fall on his wagons.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry that Hui had not gone out to strike the shanyu's baggage train; Hui said, "The original agreement was that he would enter Mayi city, troops would engage the shanyu, and your servant would strike his baggage train—gain could be had.

entries.zh: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，祗取辱。
entries.en: He never came; my thirty thousand could not have beaten his host—I would only have shamed the throne.
entries.literal: Now the shanyu did not arrive but returned; your servant with thirty thousand men could not match the enemy—he would only fetch disgrace.

entries.zh: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。」
entries.en: I knew retreat meant death, but I saved your thirty thousand men."
entries.literal: Your servant knew that returning meant execution, yet he preserved Your Majesty's thirty thousand men intact."

entries.zh: 於是下恢廷尉，廷尉當恢逗橈，當斬。
entries.en: He sent Wang Hui to the commandant of justice, who convicted him of cowardice in the face of the enemy—a capital crime.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent Hui down to the commandant of justice; the commandant of justice judged Hui for dilatory and weak conduct, meriting execution.

entries.zh: 恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而硃恢，是為匈奴報仇也。」
entries.en: Wang Hui bribed Chancellor Tian Fen with a thousand catties of gold; Tian Fen dared not plead to the emperor but told the empress dowager, "Wang Hui began the Mayi plot; to execute him now is to do the Xiongnu a favor."
entries.literal: Hui carried a thousand in gold weight to Chancellor Fen; Fen did not dare speak to the emperor, but spoke to the empress dowager, saying, "Wang Hui was first to propose the Mayi affair; now that it has failed and they would execute Hui, this is to avenge the Xiongnu."

entries.zh: 上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。
entries.en: At court with his mother, the emperor heard her repeat Tian Fen's plea.
entries.literal: The emperor attended court with the empress dowager; the empress dowager told the emperor Fen's words.

entries.zh: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言，為此。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Wang Hui started Mayi; I mobilized hundreds of thousands on his word.
entries.literal: The emperor said, "The one who first proposed the Mayi affair was Hui; therefore I raised several hundred thousand troops of the realm and followed his word in doing this.

entries.zh: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊，猶頗可得，以尉士大夫心。
entries.en: Even if we missed the shanyu, Wang Hui could still have bloodied the baggage train and heartened the army.
entries.literal: Moreover even if the shanyu could not be got, what Hui's command struck could still have been largely got—it would have consoled the hearts of gentlemen.

entries.zh: 今不誅恢，無以謝天下。」
entries.en: If I spare him, I owe the empire an apology."
entries.literal: Now if we do not execute Hui, there is no way to apologize to the realm."

entries.zh: 於是恢聞，乃自殺。
entries.en: Wang Hui killed himself when he heard.
entries.literal: Thereupon when Hui heard, he killed himself.

entries.zh: 安國為人多大略，知足以當世取舍，而出於忠厚。
entries.en: Han Anguo was broad in strategic vision, wise enough to judge the age's choices, yet fundamentally loyal and honest.
entries.literal: Anguo was by nature broad in strategic grasp, his wisdom sufficient for the choices of the age, yet he came from loyalty and honesty.

entries.zh: 貪耆財利，然所推舉皆廉士賢於己者。
entries.en: He was greedy for wealth, yet everyone he recommended was an upright man more worthy than himself.
entries.literal: He was greedy for wealth and profit, yet those he recommended were all upright men more worthy than himself.

entries.zh: 於梁舉壺遂、臧固，至它，皆天下名士，士亦以此稱慕之，唯天子以為國器。
entries.en: In Liang he recommended Hu Sui and Zang Gu; elsewhere too his picks were famous men of the realm; scholars admired him for it, and the emperor alone treated him as a pillar of state.
entries.literal: In Liang he recommended Hu Sui and Zang Gu; everywhere else, all were famous men of the realm; men therefore admired him for this; only the Son of Heaven regarded him as state treasure.

entries.zh: 安國為御史大夫五年，丞相蚡薨。
entries.en: Han Anguo served five years as censor-in-chief; then Chancellor Tian Fen died.
entries.literal: Anguo served as censor-in-chief five years; Chancellor Fen died.

entries.zh: 安國行丞相事，引墮車，蹇。
entries.en: Han Anguo acted as chancellor; he fell from a carriage while attending to his duties and went lame.
entries.literal: Anguo performed chancellor's duties; leading a carriage, he fell from the vehicle and was lame.

entries.zh: 上欲用安國為丞相，使使視，蹇甚，乃更以平棘侯薛澤為丞相。
entries.en: The emperor meant to make Han Anguo chancellor and sent an envoy to look him over; his limp was too severe, so he appointed Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze instead.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Anguo chancellor and sent an envoy to observe him; his lameness was severe; he then changed to appoint Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze as chancellor.

entries.zh: 安國病免，數月，瘉，復為中尉。
entries.en: Han Anguo resigned on grounds of illness; months later, recovered, he was reappointed metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: Anguo was dismissed on grounds of illness; after several months he recovered and was again made metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 歲餘，徙為衛尉。
entries.en: A year later he was transferred to chamberlain for the guard.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to be chamberlain for the guard.

entries.zh: 而將軍衛青等擊匈奴，破龍城。
entries.en: Meanwhile General Wei Qing and others struck the Xiongnu and took Dragon City.
entries.literal: Meanwhile General Wei Qing and others attacked the Xiongnu and broke Dragon City.

entries.zh: 明年，匈奴大入邊。
entries.en: The next year the Xiongnu raided the frontier in force.
entries.literal: The next year the Xiongnu raided the border in force.

entries.zh: 語在青傳。
entries.en: The full account is in the biography of Wei Qing.
entries.literal: The account is in Qing's biography.

entries.zh: 安國為材官將軍，屯漁陽，捕生口虜，言匈奴遠去。
entries.en: Han Anguo, as specialist general at Yuyang, took prisoners who swore the Xiongnu had withdrawn deep into the steppe.
entries.literal: Anguo was general of specialist troops, encamped at Yuyang, captured living prisoners from the barbarians, who said the Xiongnu had gone far away.

entries.zh: 即上言方佃作時，請且罷屯。
entries.en: He memorialized that spring planting needed labor and asked to stand the garrison down.
entries.literal: He immediately memorialized that it was the season of field work and requested for the nonce to disband the encampment.

entries.zh: 罷屯月餘，匈奴大入上谷、漁陽。
entries.en: A month after he sent the troops home, the Xiongnu smashed into Shanggu and Yuyang.
entries.literal: A month after the encampment was disbanded, the Xiongnu raided in force into Shanggu and Yuyang.

entries.zh: 安國壁乃有七百餘人，出與戰，安國傷，入壁。
entries.en: Han Anguo had only seven hundred men in his fort; he sortied, was wounded, and crawled back inside.
entries.literal: Anguo's rampart then had only more than seven hundred men; he went out to fight; Anguo was wounded and entered the rampart.

entries.zh: 匈奴虜略千餘人及畜產去。
entries.en: The raiders took over a thousand captives and beasts and rode away.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu carried off more than a thousand people and livestock and left.

entries.zh: 上怒，使使責讓安國。
entries.en: The emperor sent messengers to blister Han Anguo.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and sent envoys to rebuke Anguo.

entries.zh: 徙益東，屯右北平。
entries.en: He was shifted east to garrison Youbeiping.
entries.literal: He was transferred farther east to encamp at Youbeiping.

entries.zh: 是時，虜言當入東方。
entries.en: Intelligence said the next strike would fall on the eastern sector.
entries.literal: At that time the barbarians said they were about to enter the east.

entries.zh: 壺遂與太史遷等定漢律歷，官至詹事，其人深中篤行君子。
entries.en: Hu Sui worked with Sima Qian and others on the Han calendar and code, rose to chamberlain for the heir apparent, and was remembered as a grave, steady gentleman.
entries.literal: Hu Sui, together with Grand Scribe Sima Qian and others, fixed the Han statutes and calendar; he rose to office as chamberlain for the heir apparent; the man was a gentleman of deep moderation and steadfast conduct.

entries.zh: 上方倚欲以為相，會其病卒。
entries.en: The emperor meant to make him chancellor; he died of illness first.
entries.literal: The emperor was leaning on him and wished to make him chancellor, but he fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 卷五十二 竇田灌韓傳第二十二
entries.en: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han (Part 22).
entries.literal: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han, number twenty-two.

entries.zh: 對既畢，天子以仲舒為江都相，事易王。
entries.en: When the answers were done, the emperor named Dong Zhongshu chancellor to the king of Jiangdu.
entries.literal: When the replies were finished, the Son of Heaven made Zhongshu minister of Jiangdu, serving King Yi.

entries.zh: 易王，帝兄，素驕，好勇。
entries.en: King Yi was the emperor's elder brother—proud by nature and fond of brawling.
entries.literal: King Yi was the emperor's elder brother; by nature arrogant, he loved bravery.

entries.zh: 仲舒以禮誼匡正，王敬重焉。
entries.en: Dong Zhongshu set him right with ritual and duty, and the king treated him with deep respect.
entries.literal: Zhongshu with ritual and righteousness corrected him; the king respected and honored him.

entries.zh: 久之，王問仲舒曰：「粵王勾踐與大夫洩庸、種、蠡謀伐吳，遂滅之。
entries.en: One day the king asked, "Goujian of Yue and his ministers Xie Yong, Wen Zhong, and Fan Li destroyed Wu by counsel.
entries.literal: After a long time the king asked Zhongshu, saying: "The Yue king Goujian, with his great officers Xie Yong, Zhong, and Li, plotted to attack Wu and thereby destroyed it.

entries.zh: 孔子稱殷有三仁，寡人亦以為粵有三仁。
entries.en: Confucius called Shang's three men humane; I say Yue had three as well.
entries.literal: Confucius praised Yin as having three benevolent men—I, too, think Yue had three benevolent men.

entries.zh: 桓公決疑於管仲，寡人決疑於君。」
entries.en: Duke Huan trusted Guan Zhong with every doubt; I would trust you the same."
entries.literal: Duke Huan resolved doubts with Guan Zhong; I resolve doubts with you."

entries.zh: 仲舒對曰：「臣愚不足以奉大對。
entries.en: Dong Zhongshu answered, "I am too dull for so weighty a question.
entries.literal: Zhongshu replied, saying: "Your servant is foolish and not sufficient to undertake the great reply.

entries.zh: 聞昔者魯君問柳下惠：『吾欲伐齊，何如？』
entries.en: I recall the lord of Lu asking Liuxia Hui whether he should attack Qi.
entries.literal: I have heard that formerly the lord of Lu asked Liuxia Hui: 'I desire to attack Qi—how about it?

entries.zh: 柳下惠曰：『不可。』
entries.en: Liuxia Hui said no.
entries.literal: Liuxia Hui said: 'It cannot.

entries.zh: 歸而有憂色，曰：『吾聞伐國不問仁人，此言何為至於我哉！』
entries.en: At home he darkened with shame: "Humane men are never consulted on invasion—why were those words put to me?"
entries.literal: Returning home he had a worried look and said: 'I have heard that attacking a state is not asked of a benevolent man—why did these words reach me!

entries.zh: 徒見問耳，且猶羞之，況設詐以伐吳乎？
entries.en: He had only been asked, yet blushed—how much more men who used fraud to crush Wu!
entries.literal: He was only asked, and still was ashamed—how much more if one set deceit to attack Wu!

entries.zh: 由此言之，粵本無一仁。
entries.en: By that measure Yue never had a single true man of humaneness.
entries.literal: From this speaking, Yue fundamentally did not have one benevolent man.

entries.zh: 夫仁人者，正其誼不謀其利，明其道不計其功。
entries.en: The humane man sets duty straight and ignores profit, clarifies the Way and scorns mere success.
entries.literal: As for the benevolent man, he corrects his righteousness and does not scheme for profit, clarifies his Way and does not reckon achievement.

entries.zh: 是以仲尼之門，五尺之童羞稱五伯，為其先詐力而後仁誼也。
entries.en: Even a child at Confucius' gate is ashamed to praise the Five Hegemons—they put fraud and force ahead of kindness and right.
entries.literal: Therefore at the gate of Zhongni, boys of five chi's height are ashamed to name the Five Hegemons, because they put deceit and force first and benevolence and righteousness after.

entries.zh: 苟為詐而已，故不足稱於大君子之門也。
entries.en: Pure cunning wins no place among great men.
entries.literal: If it is only deceit, therefore it is not worth naming at the gate of the great gentleman.

entries.zh: 五伯比於他諸侯為賢，其比三王，猶武夫之與美玉也。」
entries.en: The hegemons surpassed other lords, yet beside the Three Kings they look like a brawler beside polished jade."
entries.literal: The Five Hegemons, compared to other marquises, were worthy; compared to the Three Kings, they are like a rough warrior compared to fine jade."

entries.zh: 王曰：「善。」
entries.en: The king said, "Well spoken."
entries.literal: The king said: "Good."

entries.zh: 贊曰：劉向稱：「董仲舒有王佐之材，雖伊、呂亡以加，管、晏之屬，伯者之佐，殆不及也。」
entries.en: The encomium says: Liu Xiang wrote, "Dong Zhongshu had the talent to assist a true king. Even Yi Yin and Lü Wang could add nothing to him; Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, ministers to hegemons, likely fell short."
entries.literal: The encomium says: Liu Xiang declared, "Dong Zhongshu had the talent of an assistant to a true king. Even Yi Yin and Lü Wang could add nothing to him; Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, assistants to hegemons, likely did not equal him."

entries.zh: 至向子歆以為：「伊、呂乃聖人之耦，王者不得則不興。
entries.en: But Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin held: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang were companions fit for sages; without men like them, a true king could not rise.
entries.literal: But Xiang's son Xin held: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang were companions to sages; if a true king did not obtain them, he could not rise.

entries.zh: 故顏淵死，孔子曰『噫！
entries.en: When Yan Hui died, Confucius cried, "Alas!
entries.literal: Therefore when Yan Hui died, Confucius said 'Ah!

entries.zh: 天喪余。』
entries.en: Heaven is killing me."
entries.literal: Heaven has bereft me."

entries.zh: 唯此一人為能當之，自宰我、子贛、子游、子夏不與焉。
entries.en: Only Hui could stand beside them—not Zaiwo, Zigong, Ziyou, or Zixia.
entries.literal: Only this one man could match them—Ziwo, Zigong, Ziyou, and Zixia were not among them.

entries.zh: 仲舒遭漢承秦滅學之後，《六經》離析，下帷發憤，潛心大業，令後學者有所統壹，為群儒首。
entries.en: Dong lived when Qin had shattered learning; he drew the curtain, burned with purpose, and gave later scholars a single thread to follow—chief among the Confucians.
entries.literal: Zhongshu met Han after Qin's destruction of learning; the Six Classics were split apart; he let down the curtain, roused his mind, and sank his heart in the great enterprise, causing later scholars to have something by which to unify—first among the throng of scholars.

entries.zh: 然考其師友淵源所漸，猶未及乎游、夏，而曰管、晏弗及，伊、呂不加，過矣。」
entries.en: Yet weighed against the lineage that produced Ziyou and Zixia, to call Guan and Yan his inferiors and rank him with Yi and Lü is going too far."
entries.literal: Yet examining the gradualness of the depth of his teachers and friends, he still had not reached Ziyou and Zixia, yet to say Guan and Yan did not reach him, Yi and Lü did not surpass him—excessive."

entries.zh: 至向曾孫龔，篤論君子也，以歆之言為然。
entries.en: Liu Xiang's great-grandson Liu Gong, a fair critic, sided with Liu Xin.
entries.literal: Reaching Xiang's great-grandson Gong, a man who firmly judged gentlemen, he held Xin's words to be correct.

entries.zh: 卷五十六 董仲舒傳第二十六
entries.en: Book 56: The Biography of Dong Zhongshu, the Twenty-Sixth
entries.literal: Volume 56: Biography of Dong Zhongshu, No. 26

entries.zh: 司馬相如字長卿，蜀郡成都人也。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru, whose courtesy name was Zhangqing, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
entries.literal: Sima Xiangru, style name Zhangqing, was a man of Chengdu in the commandery of Shu.

entries.zh: 少時好讀書，學擊劍，名犬子。
entries.en: As a boy he loved books, trained in swordsmanship, and bore the childhood name Quanzi (“Pup”).
entries.literal: In his youth he loved to read books, studied swordsmanship, and his childhood name was Quanzi.

entries.zh: 相如既學，慕藺相如之為人也，更名相如。
entries.en: Once his schooling was done, he so admired the conduct of Lin Xiangru that he adopted the name Xiangru for himself.
entries.literal: After Xiangru had completed his studies, he admired the conduct of Lin Xiangru and changed his name to Xiangru.

entries.zh: 以訾為郎，事孝景帝，為武騎常侍，非其好也。
entries.en: He bought his way into appointment as a gentleman-attendant, served Emperor Jing as a regular palace cavalry guard, and found the post uncongenial.
entries.literal: By wealth qualification he became a gentleman-attendant and served Emperor Xiaojing as a regular mounted guard, which was not what he loved.

entries.zh: 會景帝不好辭賦，是時梁孝王來朝，從遊說之士齊人鄒陽、淮陰枚乘、吳嚴忌夫子之徒，相如見而說之，因病免，客遊梁，得與諸侯游士居，數歲，乃著《子虛之賦》。
entries.en: Emperor Jing had little taste for fu rhapsody. Just then King Xiao of Liang was at court with a retinue of persuader-scholars—Zou Yang of Qi, Mei Sheng of Huaiyin, Master Yan Ji of Wu, and others. Sima Xiangru took to their company, pleaded illness, left his post, and went to Liang as a client. For several years he lived among the itinerant literati at the feudal courts, and there he wrote his “Sir Vacuity.”
entries.literal: It happened that Emperor Jing did not favor rhapsodies; at that time King Xiao of Liang came to court, accompanied by persuader-retainers such as Zou Yang of Qi, Mei Sheng of Huaiyin, Master Yan Ji of Wu, and their sort. Xiangru saw them and was delighted with them; on grounds of illness he resigned his office, traveled as a guest to Liang, was able to dwell with the wandering scholars of the feudal lords, and after several years then composed the “Rhapsody on Sir Vacuity.”

entries.zh: 會梁孝王薨，相如歸，而家貧無以自業。
entries.en: When King Xiao of Liang died, Xiangru went home, only to find his household too poor to make a living.
entries.literal: When King Xiao of Liang died, Xiangru returned home, but his family was poor and he had no means to support himself.

entries.zh: 素與臨邛令王吉相善，吉曰：「長卿久宦游，不遂而困，來過我。」
entries.en: He was old friends with Wang Ji, magistrate of Linqiang. Wang Ji said, “Zhangqing, you have been in service and on the road for years without getting anywhere. Come stay with me.”
entries.literal: He had always been on good terms with the magistrate of Linqiang, Wang Ji. Ji said, “Zhangqing has long been an official and wandered abroad; he has not succeeded and is in straits; come visit me.”

entries.zh: 於是相如往捨都亭，臨邛令繆為恭敬，日往朝相如。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru moved into the county relay inn. The magistrate feigned elaborate respect and called on him every morning.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xiangru went and lodged at the capital relay lodge. The magistrate of Linqiang pretended great deference and daily went to pay court to Xiangru.

entries.zh: 相如初尚見之，後稱病，使從者謝吉，吉愈益謹肅。
entries.en: At first he received Wang Ji, then pleaded illness and sent retainers to turn him away—whereupon the magistrate grew only more punctilious and deferential.
entries.literal: At first Xiangru still received him; afterward he claimed illness and had his followers decline Ji; Ji became all the more careful and solemn.

entries.zh: 居久之，蜀人楊得意為狗監，侍上。
entries.en: Some time later a fellow townsman, Yang Deyi, served as imperial kennel-master at court.
entries.literal: After dwelling a long time, a Shu man Yang Deyi was dog-keeper and attended the emperor.

entries.zh: 上讀《子虛賦》而善之，曰：「朕獨不得與此人同時哉！」
entries.en: The emperor read the “Sir Vacuity” and exclaimed, “Why could I not have lived in the same era as the man who wrote this?”
entries.literal: The emperor read the “Sir Vacuity Rhapsody” and praised it, saying, “How is it that I alone cannot be of the same age as this person!”

entries.zh: 得意曰：「臣邑人司馬相如自言為此賦。」
entries.en: Yang Deyi replied, “My countryman Sima Xiangru claims authorship of that piece.”
entries.literal: Deyi said, “My townsman Sima Xiangru himself says he composed this rhapsody.”

entries.zh: 上驚，乃召問相如。
entries.en: Startled, the emperor summoned Sima Xiangru for an audience.
entries.literal: The emperor was startled and then summoned and questioned Xiangru.

entries.zh: 相如曰：「有是。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru said, “It is so.
entries.literal: Xiangru said, “It is so.

entries.zh: 然此乃諸侯之事，未足觀，請為天子遊獵之賦。」
entries.en: But that piece,” he went on, “only treats the hunts of the feudal lords—it is hardly fit for your majesty. Allow me to offer a fu on the Son of Heaven’s hunt.”
entries.literal: Yet this is the affair of feudal lords; it is not enough to view; I request to compose a rhapsody on the Son of Heaven’s hunting.”

entries.zh: 上令尚書給筆札，相如以「子虛」，虛言也，為楚稱；
entries.en: The emperor ordered brushes and bamboo slips from the Secretariat. Sima Xiangru explained that “Sir Vacuity” stood for empty boasting on Chu’s behalf;
entries.literal: The emperor ordered the Secretary to supply brush and slips; Xiangru took “Sir Vacuity” as vacuous words, speaking for Chu;

entries.zh: 「烏有先生」者，烏有此事也，為齊難；
entries.en: that “Mr. Nonexistence” meant “there is no such thing,” voicing Qi’s counter;
entries.literal: “Mr. Nonexistence” is that this affair does not exist, speaking for Qi’s rebuttal;

entries.zh: 「亡是公」者，亡是人也，欲明天子之義。
entries.en: and that “Lord No-such-person” signified no such man at all—figures meant to expound the Son of Heaven’s true standard.
entries.literal: “Lord No-such-person” is that this person does not exist, intending to clarify the righteousness of the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 故虛借此三人為辭，以推天子諸侯之苑囿。
entries.en: He used these three allegorical speakers to unfold the hunting grounds of emperor and kings alike.
entries.literal: Therefore he vacuously borrowed these three persons as wording, in order to extend the parks and preserves of Son of Heaven and feudal lords.

entries.zh: 其卒章歸之於節儉，因以風諫。
entries.en: The closing movement turns to restraint and frugality, turning the whole piece into a veiled admonition.
entries.literal: Its final chapter returns to moderation and thrift, thereby using indirect remonstrance.

entries.zh: 奏之天子，天子大說。
entries.en: He presented it to the throne, and the emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: He presented it to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The text runs as follows:
entries.literal: Its wording says:

entries.zh: 賦奏，天子以為郎。
entries.en: When the fu was laid before the throne, the emperor appointed Sima Xiangru a gentleman-attendant at court.
entries.literal: When the rhapsody was presented, the Son of Heaven made him a gentleman-attendant (lang).

entries.zh: 亡是公言上林廣大，山谷水泉萬物，及子虛言雲夢所有甚眾，侈靡多過其實，且非義理所止，故刪取其要，歸正道而論之。
entries.en: Lord No-such-person’s description of Shanglin and Sir Vacuity’s catalogue of Cloud Dream swell beyond fact and stray from moral purpose; the historian has therefore trimmed them to essentials and set the discourse back on the proper path.
entries.literal: Lord No-such-person’s speech on Shanglin’s vastness, mountains valleys water springs myriad things, and Sir Vacuity’s speech on Cloud Dream’s possessing very much, extravagant dissolute much exceeding the reality, and moreover not what righteousness and principle rest in—therefore delete and take their essentials, return to the correct Way and discuss them.

entries.zh: 「於是酒中樂酣，天子芒然而思，似若有亡，曰：『嗟乎，此大奢侈！
entries.en: Deep in wine and music the emperor’s mood turns grave, as if something had been lost, and he murmurs, “This is too much—far too much.
entries.literal: “Thereupon in the midst of wine music warm, the Son of Heaven dimly ponders, as if having something lost, saying, “Alas, this is great extravagance!

entries.zh: 朕以覽聽餘閒，無事棄日，順天道以殺伐，時休息於此，恐後世靡麗，遂往而不返，非所以為繼嗣創業垂統也。』
entries.en: I used my free hours to hunt in accord with the seasons, never dreaming that posterity might ape this splendor, drift into excess, and never find their way back—that is no foundation for an heir or a dynasty.”
entries.literal: I by surveying listening spare leisure, without affairs abandon days, follow heaven’s way thereby to kill and attack, at times rest here, fear later generations dissolute beautiful, follow gone and not return, this is not the means by which to bequeath heir establish enterprise hang continuity.”

entries.zh: 於是乎乃解酒罷獵，而命有司曰：『地可墾闢，悉為農郊，以贍氓隸，隤牆填塹，使山澤之民得至焉。
entries.en: He ended the revel and ordered his ministers to open every acre that could be plowed, throw down the park walls and fill the ditches, and let hill folk and marsh dwellers come in to farm.
entries.literal: Thereupon then unbind wine cease hunt, and ordered the responsible officials, saying, “Land that can be opened for tillage, all make agricultural outskirts, thereby to enrich commoners and slaves; tear down walls fill moats, enable mountain marsh people to reach there.

entries.zh: 實陂池而勿禁，虛官館而勿仞。
entries.en: Let the people fish the ponds without ban and lodge in the empty guesthouses.
entries.literal: Fill slope pools yet do not forbid, empty official lodges yet do not occupy.

entries.zh: 發倉廩以救貧窮，補不足，恤鰥寡，存孤獨。
entries.en: Release grain for the hungry, aid the short of supplies, comfort widows and widowers, and shelter the orphaned and alone.
entries.literal: Open granaries thereby to save the poor and destitute, replenish insufficiency, pity widowers and widows, preserve orphans and alone.

entries.zh: 出德號，省刑罰，改制度，易服色，革正朔，與天下為始。』」
entries.en: Proclaim amnesty, lighten penalties, reform the calendar, change court dress—give the empire a new beginning.”’”
entries.literal: Issue virtuous edicts, reduce punishments, change institutions, alter dress colors, reform first month of year, with all under heaven make a beginning.”’”

entries.zh: 「於是乎背秋涉冬，天子校獵。
entries.en: “Thereupon turning back autumn crossing winter, the Son of Heaven conducts the grand hunt.
entries.literal: “Thereupon turning back autumn crossing winter, the Son of Heaven conducts the grand hunt.

entries.zh: 乘鏤象，六玉□，拖蜺旌，靡雲旗，前皮軒，後道游；
entries.en: He mounts an ivory-inlaid chariot drawn by six gleaming bays—one ornament name is missing—rainbow pennons and cloud standards streaming, a leather-screened vanguard and escort chariots to the rear.
entries.literal: Ride engraved elephant, six jade [lacuna], trail rainbow banners, spread cloud flags, in front leather screen wagon, behind dao-you;

entries.zh: 孫叔奉轡，衛公參乘，扈從橫行，出乎四校之中。
entries.en: Sun Shu takes the reins, the Duke of Wei rides escort, and the host breaks from the four-field cordon in full array.
entries.literal: Sun Shu holds reins, Duke of Wei acts side-rider, retinue follows moving crosswise, emerge within the four camps.

entries.zh: 鼓嚴簿，縱獵者，江河為□，泰山為櫓，車騎雷起，殷天動地，先後陸離，離散別追，淫淫裔裔，緣陵流澤，雲布雨施。
entries.en: The roll call ends, the beaters open, and the hunt spills across a front measured in rivers and mountains—chariots thunder, earth shakes, squadrons wheel like clouds bursting into rain.
entries.literal: Drum strict roster, release hunters; Yangtze and Yellow River serve as [lacuna], Mount Tai as shield; chariots and riders thunder rise, shake heaven move earth, first last scattered separate, separate scatter pursue apart, flowing long moving like waves, follow hills flow marshes, cloud spread rain cast.

entries.zh: 生貔豹，搏豺狼，手熊羆，足野羊。
entries.en: Men brought down leopards, wrestled wolves and bears, and ran down wild goats with their bare feet.
entries.literal: They brought down leopards, struck jackals and wolves, seized bears with their hands, and trampled wild goats underfoot.

entries.zh: 蒙鶡蘇，褲白虎，被斑文，跨野馬，陵三□之危，下磧歷之坻，逕峻赴險，越壑厲水。
entries.en: They wear plumed hoods and tiger-skin chaps, ride bareback, and charge slopes and gravel beds that would stop an ordinary horse.
entries.literal: Wear pheasant feather, trousers white tiger, covered spotted pattern, straddle wild horse, ascend three [lacuna] danger, descend gravel stony islet, pass steep rush danger, leap gully ford water.

entries.zh: 推蜚廉，弄解□，格蝦蛤，鋌猛氏，□要□，射封豕。
entries.en: They spear wind-spirits, gore fabulous beasts, and bring down giant boars—several monster names are defective.
entries.literal: Push feilian, play jie [lacuna], strike xia ge, stab Mengshi, [lacuna] yao [lacuna], shoot great boar.

entries.zh: 箭不苟害，解□陷腦；
entries.en: No arrow flies without purpose; each strike splits skull or spine.
entries.literal: Arrows do not carelessly harm, split [lacuna] pierce brain;

entries.zh: 弓不虛發，應聲而倒。」
entries.en: No bowstring hums without answer; game drops at the report.”
entries.literal: Bow does not loose empty, respond to sound and fall.”

entries.zh: 「且夫齊、楚之事又烏足道乎！
entries.en: “As for Qi and Chu—what is there even worth saying!
entries.literal: “Moreover the affairs of Qi and Chu—how are they worth speaking of!

entries.zh: 君未睹夫巨麗也，獨不聞天子之上林乎？
entries.en: You have never seen true magnificence. Surely you have heard of the Son of Heaven’s Shanglin preserve?
entries.literal: You, sir, have not beheld the great magnificence; have you alone not heard of the Son of Heaven’s Shanglin Park?

entries.zh: 左蒼梧，右西極，丹水更其南，紫淵徑其北。
entries.en: It runs toward Cangwu in the east and toward the western wastes; the Vermilion River washes its southern flank and the Purple Pool its northern.
entries.literal: Zangwu to the left, the western extreme to the right; the Vermilion River runs past its south, the Purple Abyss crosses its north.

entries.zh: 終始霸、產，出入涇、渭，□、鎬、潦、□，紆余委蛇，經營其內。
entries.en: The Ba and Chan rivers thread through it from end to end; the Jing and Wei pour in and out, joined by the Feng, Hao, Lao, and other streams—several river names are damaged in the text—that wind and coil across the park.
entries.literal: Beginning and ending with Ba and Chan, entering and exiting Jing and Wei, [lacuna], Hao, Lao, [lacuna], winding long, coiling within it.

entries.zh: 蕩蕩乎八川分流，相背異態，東西南北，馳騖往來，出乎椒丘之闕，行乎州淤之浦，逕乎桂林之中，過乎泱莽之野，汩乎混流，順阿而下，赴隘□之口，觸穹石，激堆□，沸乎暴怒，洶湧彭湃，滭弗宓汩，逼側泌瀄，橫流逆折，轉騰潎洌，滂濞沆溉，穹隆雲橈，宛水單膠□，逾波趨乂，蒞蒞下瀨，批巖沖擁，奔揚滯沛，臨坻注壑，□霣隊，沈沈隱隱，砰磅訇□蓋，□淈□，□鼎沸，馳波跳沫，汩□漂疾，悠遠長懷。
entries.en: Eight great rivers split and surge through the park, each with its own temper: they burst from defiles, braid across sandbars, thread the cassia groves, flood the open moors, then boil together, drop through narrows—one place name is lost—hammer boulders and shoals, rear in white rage, crash and cross-cut until the whole basin seethes like a cauldron. The passage piles on binomes for roaring water; many graphs are missing or corrupt in the received Hanshu.
entries.literal: Vastly the eight streams divide flow, turn backs with different forms, east west south north, gallop and rush back and forth, emerge from Pepper Hill’s gap, move on islet shallows, pass through Cassia Forest’s midst, cross the boundless wilds, boil in mingled currents, follow the bend downward, hasten to the narrow [lacuna] mouth, strike vaulting rocks, smash heaped [lacuna], bubble in violent rage, surge and swell, boil and seethe, press close and rush, cross flow reverse twist, turn and leap sparkling, pound and flood, arch high cloud-curved, wind water glue [lacuna], cross waves hasten currents, arrive arrive descend rapids, strike cliffs dash banks, run and splash dam-full, overlook islets pour into gullies, [lacuna] fall in ranks, deep deep hidden hidden, pound crash thunder [lacuna], [lacuna] welling, [lacuna] cauldron-boil, galloping waves leaping foam, swift [lacuna] drifting fast, far far long longing.

entries.zh: 寂□無聲，肆乎永歸。
entries.en: Then all at once the torrent subsides into a deep hush, and the waters glide home to rest. (One character is missing.)
entries.literal: Silent [lacuna] without sound, freely then forever return.

entries.zh: 然後灝□潢漾，安翔徐□，□乎□，東注大湖，衍溢陂池。
entries.en: Spreading wide, the currents ease and slide eastward into the great lake, spilling over into every marsh and pond along the way.
entries.literal: Then [lacuna] vast and flowing, peacefully soaring slowly [lacuna], [lacuna] then [lacuna], eastward pour into the great lake, overflow and fill slope pools.

entries.zh: 於是蛟龍赤螭，□恆□瞢漸離，□禺禺□鰨，健鰭掉尾，振鱗奮翼，潛處乎深巖。
entries.en: Horned dragons and lesser river dragons thrash their fins and fan their scales in the depths—several fish names are defective in the manuscript.
entries.literal: Thereupon horned dragons and red chi, [lacuna] gradually leave, [lacuna] fish [lacuna] sole, strong fins wag tails, shake scales spread wings, hide in deep crags.

entries.zh: 魚鱉歡聲，萬物眾伙。
entries.en: Fish and turtles sport on the surface; countless creatures flourish in the flood.
entries.literal: Fish and turtles sound joy; the myriad things are many in kind.

entries.zh: 明月珠子，的皪江靡，蜀石黃□，水玉磊砢，磷磷爛爛，采色澔汗，叢積乎其中。
entries.en: Lustrous pearls line the banks; Shu jade, yellow crystal, and heaped “water jade” flash so many hues that the riverbed seems paved with gems.
entries.literal: Bright moon pearls, sparkling along the river’s edge, Shu stones yellow [lacuna], water jade piled high, gleaming bright, colors vast and brilliant, cluster-accumulated within them.

entries.zh: 工□鷫鵠鴇，鴽鵝屬玉，交精旋目，煩鶩庸渠，箴疵□盧，群浮乎其上。
entries.en: Wildfowl of every description—swans, bustards, teals, and rarer species partly lost in the text—raft in dense flocks on the water.
entries.literal: Craft [lacuna] siskin swan bustard, ru goose jade duck, cross-eyed turning-eye, vexed duck canal duck, zhen ci [lacuna] ruddy, flock float upon its surface.

entries.zh: 浮淫氾濫，隨風澹淡，與波搖蕩，奄薄水□，唼喋菁藻，咀嚼鞭藕。」
entries.en: They drift with the breeze, bob on the chop, dabble in the shallows, and peck at algae and lotus root.”
entries.literal: Floating dissolute overflow, following wind light ripple, sway with the waves, cover near water [lacuna], peck and chatter on green algae, chew lotus root.”

entries.zh: 「道盡塗殫，回車而還。
entries.en: “Way exhausted path ended, turn chariot and return.
entries.literal: “Way exhausted path ended, turn chariot and return.

entries.zh: 消□乎襄羊，降集乎北□，率乎直指，□乎反鄉，蹶石關，歷封巒，過□鵲，望露寒，下堂□，息宜春，西馳宣曲，濯□牛首，登龍台，掩細柳，觀士大夫之勤略，鈞獵者之所得獲。
entries.en: The procession drifts through the park’s gates and lodges—Shimen, Fengluan, and the rest, many names partly lost—while the emperor reviews what his men have taken.
entries.literal: Wandering far in roaming [lacuna], descend gather in north [lacuna], lead straight to, [lacuna] return home, pass Stone Gate, pass Fengluan, pass [lacuna] magpie, gaze Dew-cold, descend Hall [lacuna], rest Yichun, west gallop Xuanqu, wash [lacuna] Ox-head, ascend Dragon Terrace, cover Willow, observe officers and gentlemen’s diligent strategy, weigh hunters’ catches.

entries.zh: 徒車之所□轢，騎之所蹂若，人之所蹈藉，與其窮極倦，□驚憚讋伏，不被創刃而死者，它它藉藉，填坑滿谷，掩平彌澤。」
entries.en: Beasts crushed under wheel and hoof, stunned without a blade’s touch, lie heaped until gorges and flats are carpeted with carcasses.”
entries.literal: Where foot chariots have [lacuna] crushed, where riders have trampled, where men have trod, together with their exhausted frightened [lacuna] alarm submit crouch, not receiving blade wounds yet dead, other other piled piled, fill gullies full valleys, cover level fill marshes.”

entries.zh: 卷五十七上 司馬相如傳 第二十七 上
entries.en: Volume 57a: Biography of Sima Xiangru, chapter twenty-seven, first part.
entries.literal: Volume 57a, Biography of Sima Xiangru, Twenty-Seven, Upper.

entries.zh: 相如還報。
entries.en: Xiangru returned and made his report.
entries.literal: Xiangru returned and reported.

entries.zh: 唐蒙已略通夜郎，因通西南夷道，發巴、蜀、廣漢卒，作者數萬人。
entries.en: Tang Meng had already pushed through to Yelang and was extending the southwest road, drafting tens of thousands of laborers from Ba, Shu, and Guanghan.
entries.literal: Tang Meng had already opened communications with Yelang, and on that account opened the road to the southwestern barbarians, mobilizing workers from Ba, Shu, and Guanghan, several tens of thousands of laborers.

entries.zh: 治道二歲，道不成，士卒多物故，費以億萬計。
entries.en: Work dragged on for two years without finishing the route. Casualties mounted among the troops, and costs ran into the hundreds of millions.
entries.literal: For two years they worked on the road; the road was not completed; many soldiers died of hardship; the expense was reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

entries.zh: 蜀民及漢用事者多言其不便。
entries.en: Shu locals and influential men at court repeatedly argued that the project was a waste.
entries.literal: The people of Shu and Han officials in power often said it was not advantageous.

entries.zh: 是時邛、莋之君長聞南夷與漢通，得賞賜多，多欲願為內臣妾，請吏，比南夷。
entries.en: The chiefs of Qiong and Zuo learned that the southern tribes had submitted to Han and been showered with gifts; most of them now wanted to enter the register as tributaries, asked for imperial magistrates, and sought the same status as the southern peoples.
entries.literal: At this time the lords of Qiong and Zuo heard that the southern barbarians had opened relations with Han and received rich rewards; many wished to become inner subjects and concubines-in-submission, requested officials, and asked to be treated like the southern barbarians.

entries.zh: 上問相如，相如曰：「邛、莋、冉、駹者近蜀，道易通，異時嘗通為郡縣矣，至漢興而罷。
entries.en: The emperor asked Xiangru for his view. He replied: "The tribes of Qiong, Zuo, Ran, and Mang border Shu; their routes are easy to open. They were once organized as commanderies in earlier dynasties and only lapsed when the Han arose.
entries.literal: The emperor questioned Xiangru, and Xiangru said: "Qiong, Zuo, Ran, and Mang lie near Shu; the road is easy to open; in former times they were once connected as commanderies and counties, but at the rise of Han that was discontinued.

entries.zh: 今誠復通，為置縣，愈於南夷。」
entries.en: If we reopen ties and place magistrates among them, we will gain more for less trouble than we have had in the far south."
entries.literal: Now if we truly reopen communications, establish counties for them, it will be better than dealing with the southern barbarians."

entries.zh: 上以為然，乃拜相如為中郎將，建節往使。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and appointed Xiangru General of the Household, sending him as an envoy bearing imperial credentials.
entries.literal: The emperor deemed it right, and therefore appointed Xiangru commandant of palace attendants, bearing the imperial insignia to go as envoy.

entries.zh: 副使者王然於、壺充國、呂越人，馳四乘之傳，因巴、蜀吏幣物以賂西南夷。
entries.en: His deputies Wang Ranyu, Hu Chongguo, and Lü Yueren raced ahead on four-horse relay carriages, while local officials from Ba and Shu carried gifts to win over the southwestern tribes.
entries.literal: Associate envoys Wang Ranyu, Hu Chongguo, and Lü Yueren galloped post relays of four horses, and by means of Ba and Shu officials presented goods to bribe the southwestern barbarians.

entries.zh: 至蜀，太守以下郊迎，縣令負弩矢先驅，蜀人以為寵。
entries.en: At their arrival in Shu the governor led his staff in a suburban welcome; the county magistrate marched ahead shouldering bow and bolts. The Shu people took it as a mark of singular favor.
entries.literal: When they reached Shu, the governor and all below came out to the suburbs to welcome them; the county magistrate bore crossbows and arrows as vanguard; the people of Shu considered it an honor.

entries.zh: 於是卓王孫、臨邛諸公皆因門下獻牛、酒以交歡。
entries.en: Zhuo Wangsun and the leading families of Linqiong then sent cattle and wine through Xiangru's attendants to join the celebration.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhuo Wangsun and the gentlemen of Linqiong all by way of his retainers presented oxen and wine to cultivate good relations.

entries.zh: 卓王孫喟然而歎，自以得使女尚司馬長卿晚，乃厚分與其女財，與男等。
entries.en: Zhuo Wangsun sighed that he had waited too long to gain Sima Changqing as a son-in-law; he now settled a lavish marriage portion on his daughter, equal to what he gave his sons.
entries.literal: Zhuo Wangsun sighed with regret, thinking himself late in obtaining a son-in-law like Sima Changqing for his daughter, and therefore divided his daughter's share of wealth generously, equal to that of his sons.

entries.zh: 相如使略定西南夷，邛、莋、冉、駹、斯榆之君皆請為臣妾，除邊關，邊關益斥，西至沫、若水，南至牂牁為徼，通靈山道，橋孫水，以通邛、莋。
entries.en: On mission Xiangru brought the southwest under control: the rulers of Qiong, Zuo, Ran, Mang, and Siyu all asked to submit as tributaries. Frontier barriers came down and the line of outposts stretched west to the Mo and Ruoshui rivers and south to Zangke as the outer perimeter. Roads pierced Mount Ling, bridges spanned the Sun River, and traffic linked Qiong and Zuo.
entries.literal: Xiangru as envoy broadly pacified the southwestern barbarians; the lords of Qiong, Zuo, Ran, Mang, and Siyu all requested to become subjects and concubines-in-submission; border passes were removed; the border passes were further extended west to Mo and Ruoshui, south to Zangke as the outer cordon; the Ling Mountain road was opened, a bridge thrown across the Sun River, to communicate with Qiong and Zuo.

entries.zh: 還報，天子大說。
entries.en: When he reported back, the emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: He returned and reported; the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 相如使時，蜀長老多言通西南夷之不為用，大臣亦以為然。
entries.en: While Xiangru was away, Shu notables kept saying that the southwest road served no purpose, and senior ministers at court agreed.
entries.literal: When Xiangru had been on mission, Shu elders often said opening communications with the southwestern barbarians was useless; great ministers also thought it so.

entries.zh: 相如欲諫，業已建之，不敢，乃著書，借蜀父老為辭，而己詰難之，以風天子，且因宣其使指，令百姓皆知天子意。
entries.en: He wanted to argue the case but dared not, having himself sponsored the scheme. Instead he drafted a dialogue, putting the objections in the mouths of Shu elders and answering them in his own voice, both to sway the throne and to spell out what his mission had meant so that every household would grasp the emperor's purpose.
entries.literal: Xiangru wished to remonstrate, but since he had already initiated the project, he did not dare; he therefore composed a book, borrowing the words of Shu elders as his text, while he himself posed the hard questions, in order to influence the Son of Heaven, and also thereby proclaim the intent of his mission, so that the hundred surnames would all know the emperor's mind.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The piece begins:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 相如口吃而善著書。
entries.en: Xiangru stammered yet excelled at literary composition.
entries.literal: Xiangru stammered but was good at writing books.

entries.zh: 常有消渴病。
entries.en: He suffered chronically from diabetes.
entries.literal: He often had the wasting-thirst illness.

entries.zh: 與卓氏婚，饒於財。
entries.en: His marriage to the Zhuo family left him wealthy.
entries.literal: He married into the Zhuo clan and was rich in wealth.

entries.zh: 故其仕宦，未嘗肯與公卿國家之事，常稱疾閒居，不慕官爵。
entries.en: Hence he seldom took part in high policy, often pleaded illness, lived quietly at home, and showed no ambition for office or title.
entries.literal: Therefore in his official career he was never willing to join in the affairs of the dukes and ministers of state; he often pleaded illness and dwelt at leisure, not coveting rank or salary.

entries.zh: 嘗從上至長楊獵。
entries.en: He once accompanied the emperor on a hunt at the Changyang park.
entries.literal: He once accompanied the emperor to hunt at Changyang.

entries.zh: 是時天子方好自擊熊豕，馳逐野獸，相如因上疏諫。
entries.en: The emperor had taken to killing bears and boars with his own hands and racing after game; Xiangru therefore presented a written remonstrance.
entries.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven was fond of personally striking bears and boars, galloping in pursuit of wild beasts; Xiangru therefore submitted a memorial remonstrating.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: It read:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 陛下患使者有司之若彼，悼不肖愚民之如此，故遣信使，曉諭百姓以發卒之事，因數之以不忠死亡之罪，讓三老孝弟以不教誨之過。
entries.en: The throne deplores officials who behaved as they did and pities ignorant folk who reacted so rashly. Hence a reliable envoy has been sent to explain why levies were ordered, to spell out how disloyalty leads to death, and to call village elders to account for failing to teach their people.
entries.literal: Your Majesty grieves that envoys and officials were like that, mourns that unworthy foolish commoners were thus, and therefore sends a trusted envoy to enlighten the hundred surnames concerning the matter of raising troops, and thereby enumerates to them the crime of disloyalty leading to death, and reproaches the village elders for the fault of not teaching and instructing.

entries.zh: 方今田時，重煩百姓，已親見近縣，恐遠所溪谷山澤之民不遍聞，檄到，亟下縣道，鹹諭陛下意，毋忽！
entries.en: It is planting season, and the court regrets the burden on the people. Envoys have already toured the nearer counties, but those in remote valleys and hills may not have heard. When this edict reaches you, relay it at once along every county and post road so that every household understands the emperor's purpose. Do not treat it lightly.
entries.literal: Now it is plowing season; we heavily trouble the hundred surnames; already we have personally visited the nearby counties; we fear those in distant streams, valleys, mountains, and marshes have not all heard; when the proclamation arrives, urgently transmit it down to counties and circuits, thoroughly make known the emperor's intent; do not neglect it!

entries.zh: 臣聞物有同類而殊能者，故力稱烏獲，捷言慶忌，勇其賁、育。
entries.en: Your servant has heard that creatures of one kind may differ in gifts: hence men praise Wuhuo for strength, Qingji for speed, Ben and Yu for valor.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that among things there are those of the same kind yet different capabilities; therefore in strength they cite Wuhuo, in swiftness they speak of Qingji, in courage they name Ben and Yu.

entries.zh: 臣之愚，竊以為人誠有之，獸亦宜然。
entries.en: In my ignorance I believe that if this is true of men, it is true of beasts as well.
entries.literal: Your servant's foolish opinion privately holds that if it is so with men, it should also be so with beasts.

entries.zh: 今陛下好陵阻險，射猛獸，卒然遇逸材之獸，駭不存之地，犯屬車之清塵，輿不及還轅，人不暇施巧，雖有烏獲、逢蒙之技不能用，枯木朽株盡為難矣。
entries.en: Yet Your Majesty loves to climb dangerous ground and shoot savage game. Should some powerful beast bolt from cover in a spot where the chariot cannot save you, the dust of your escort would be thrown into peril: the carriage could not wheel about in time, guards could not react in time—even Wuhuo's strength or Peng Meng's archery would be useless, and every dead trunk becomes a weapon against you.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty delights in scaling steep peril and shooting fierce beasts; suddenly you may meet a beast of outstanding mettle, startled in a place where you cannot survive, disturbing the clear dust of the accompanying chariots; the carriage has no time to turn the hubs, men have no time to apply their skills; though you had the arts of Wuhuo and Peng Meng they could not be used; withered trees and rotted stumps all become hazards.

entries.zh: 是胡越起於轂下，而羌夷接軫也，豈不殆哉！
entries.en: It would be like barbarians springing up beneath the royal axle—could anything be more deadly?
entries.literal: This is Hu and Yue rising under the wheel-hubs, and Qiang and Yi meeting the axle-trees—is it not perilous!

entries.zh: 雖萬全而無患，然本非天子之所宜近也。
entries.en: Even if no disaster came, such sport is unworthy of the Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Though utterly safe without calamity, yet fundamentally it is not what the Son of Heaven should draw near.

entries.zh: 相如為郎數歲，會唐蒙使略通夜郎、僰中，發巴、蜀吏卒，千人，郡又多為發轉漕萬餘人，用軍興法誅其渠率。
entries.en: Xiangru had served as a gentleman attendant for several years when Tang Meng was dispatched to push the frontier toward Yelang and the Bozhong region. Tang called up a thousand officers and troops from Ba and Shu, and the commanderies raised more than ten thousand additional laborers for transport and supply. Invoking the statutes used in wartime mobilization, he put their leaders to death.
entries.literal: Xiangru had been a gentleman attendant for several years when, as it happened, Tang Meng was sent to open communications with Yelang and Bozhong; he mobilized officers and soldiers of Ba and Shu, a thousand men, and the commanderies further raised for him over ten thousand men for transport and supply; he used the laws governing military emergencies to execute their ringleaders.

entries.zh: 巴、蜀民大驚恐。
entries.en: The people of Ba and Shu were thrown into panic.
entries.literal: The people of Ba and Shu were greatly alarmed and terrified.

entries.zh: 上聞之，乃遣相如責唐蒙等，因諭告巴、蜀民以非上意。
entries.en: When the emperor learned of the unrest, he sent Xiangru to reprimand Tang Meng and his associates and to make clear to the people of Ba and Shu that none of this had been the sovereign's will.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he then sent Xiangru to rebuke Tang Meng and the others, and thereby instructed and informed the people of Ba and Shu that this was not the emperor's intention.

entries.zh: 檄曰：
entries.en: The proclamation read:
entries.literal: The proclamation said:

entries.zh: 上善之。
entries.en: The emperor approved the memorial.
entries.literal: The emperor deemed it good.

entries.zh: 還過宜春宮，相如奏賦以哀二世行失。
entries.en: On the way back the imperial train passed Yichun Palace, where Xiangru offered a rhapsody mourning the Second Emperor's moral failure.
entries.literal: On the return journey passing Yichun Palace, Xiangru submitted a fu to lament the faults in conduct of the Second Emperor.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The piece begins:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 漢興七十有八載，德茂存乎六世，威武紛雲，港恩汪濊，群生霑濡，洋溢乎方外。
entries.en: Seventy-eight years have passed since the Han rose; through six sovereigns virtue has deepened, military glory towers like clouds, and imperial kindness spreads wide until every living thing shares in it and the influence reaches beyond the borders.
entries.literal: The Han has risen seventy-eight years; virtue flourishes through six reigns; martial awesomeness piles like clouds; imperial favor spreads vast and deep; the myriad creatures are soaked and drenched; it overflows beyond the regions.

entries.zh: 於是乃命使西征，隨流而攘，風之所被，罔不披靡。
entries.en: He therefore sent armies west along the rivers; wherever their influence reached, resistance collapsed.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered envoys to march west, following the currents and pushing outward; where the wind blew, none did not bend low.

entries.zh: 因朝冉從□，定莋存邛，略斯榆，舉苞蒲，結軌還轅，東鄉將報，至於蜀都。
entries.en: Ran came to court, Mang followed in train, Zuo was secured, Qiong preserved, Siyu overrun, Bao and Pu brought to heel; the expedition wheeled its chariots homeward, turned east toward the capital for its report, and halted at Chengdu.
entries.literal: Thereby he received court from Ran, followed Mang, stabilized Zuo, preserved Qiong, overran Siyu, raised Bao and Pu, hitched the traces and turned the hubs, faced east about to report, and arrived at the Shu capital.

entries.zh: 於是天子沛然改容，曰：「俞乎，朕其試哉！」
entries.en: The emperor's face cleared; he said, "Very well—I will make the attempt!"
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven buoyantly changed countenance, saying: "Yes indeed, I will try it!"

entries.zh: 乃遷思回慮，總公卿之議，詢封禪之事，詩大澤之博，廣符瑞之富。
entries.en: He gathered his wits, polled his high ministers on the feng and shan, praised the breadth of the great marsh, and rehearsed the wealth of recent omens.
entries.literal: Thereupon shifting thought, turning consideration, gathering the deliberations of dukes and ministers, inquiring into feng and shan affairs, extolling the vastness of the great marsh, broadening the richness of tallies and omens.

entries.zh: 遂作頌曰：
entries.en: He then composed this hymn:
entries.literal: Thereupon he made a eulogy, saying:

entries.zh: 相如既病免，家居茂陵。
entries.en: When illness forced Xiangru to retire, he lived quietly at Maoling.
entries.literal: When Xiangru had been dismissed on illness, he dwelt at home in Maoling.

entries.zh: 天子曰：「司馬相如病甚，可往從悉取其書，若後之矣。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Sima Xiangru is dying; send someone to collect whatever manuscripts he has before it is too late."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said: "Sima Xiangru is gravely ill; someone may go and take all his writings from him, lest they come too late."

entries.zh: 使所忠往，而相如已死，家無遺書。
entries.en: Suo Zhong was dispatched, but Xiangru had already died and his house held no books.
entries.literal: He sent Suo Zhong; but Xiangru had already died, and his household had no writings left.

entries.zh: 問其妻，對曰：「長卿未嘗有書也。
entries.en: When they asked his wife, she said: "Changqing never kept books of his own.
entries.literal: Questioning his wife, she replied: "Changqing never had books.

entries.zh: 時時著書，人又取去。
entries.en: Whenever he wrote something, someone carried the draft away.
entries.literal: From time to time he wrote books, and people again took them away.

entries.zh: 長卿未死時，為一卷書，曰有使來求書，奏之。」
entries.en: Before he died he left one scroll with the note, 'If an envoy comes for my writings, present this memorial.'"
entries.literal: Before Changqing died, he made one scroll of writing, saying, 'If an envoy comes seeking writings, present this memorial.'"

entries.zh: 其遺札書言封禪事，所忠奏焉，天子異之。
entries.en: That final manuscript discussed the feng and shan sacrifices. Suo Zhong laid it before the throne, and the emperor received it with wonder.
entries.literal: The farewell note he left discussed the feng and shan sacrifices; Suo Zhong presented it, and the Son of Heaven marveled at it.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: It reads:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 耆老大夫搢紳先生之徒二十有七人，儼然造焉。
entries.en: Twenty-seven elders, officials, and gentry in full dress presented themselves with grave formality.
entries.literal: Twenty-seven men—elders, grandees, girdle-and-ribbon gentlemen—solemnly came forward.

entries.zh: 辭畢，進曰：「蓋聞天子之於夷狄也，其義羈縻勿絕而已。
entries.en: When formal greetings were finished, they stepped forward: "We have always understood that the Son of Heaven's policy toward barbarians is to keep them on a loose tether without cutting them off.
entries.literal: When the courtesies were complete, they advanced and said: "We have heard that the Son of Heaven's treatment of the Yi and Di is, in principle, to hold them on loose reins without severing ties.

entries.zh: 今罷三郡之士，通夜郎之塗，三年於茲，而功不竟。
entries.en: Yet you have drafted three commanderies, opened the road to Yelang, and three years on the work is still unfinished.
entries.literal: Now you have mobilized the levies of three commanderies and opened the road to Yelang; for three years until now, yet the work is not completed.

entries.zh: 士卒勞倦，萬民不贍；
entries.en: The troops are exhausted and the people can barely feed themselves;
entries.literal: Soldiers are weary; the myriad people lack sufficiency;

entries.zh: 今又接之以西夷，百姓力屈，恐不能卒業，此亦使者之累也，竊為左右患之。
entries.en: now you would link them with the tribes of the west. The people's strength is exhausted, and we fear the work cannot be completed. This would also become a liability for you as envoy, and we privately fear for you.
entries.literal: now you further join them to the western barbarians; the strength of the hundred surnames is bent; we fear they cannot finish the undertaking; this is also the fault of the envoys; we privately worry for those on your left and right.

entries.zh: 且夫邛、莋、西僰之與中國並也，歷年茲多，不可記已。
entries.en: Besides, Qiong, Zuo, and the western Bo have stood beside China for ages beyond counting.
entries.literal: Moreover Qiong, Zuo, and the western Bo have existed alongside the Central States for many years; the years are so many they cannot be recorded.

entries.zh: 仁者不以德來，強者不以力並，意者殆不可乎！
entries.en: The humane ruler does not win them by kindness alone; the strong state does not swallow them by force alone—and we suspect neither course will really work!
entries.literal: The humane [ruler] does not bring them in by virtue alone; the strong [state] does not annex them by force alone—in our opinion perhaps it cannot be done!

entries.zh: 今割齊民以附夷狄，弊所恃以事無用，鄙人固陋，不識所謂。」
entries.en: To strip our settled farmers for the sake of barbarians, to waste what we depend on to serve a useless venture—we are plain folk, perhaps, but we cannot see the sense of it."
entries.literal: Now you carve out orderly commoners to attach to the Yi and Di, exhaust what you rely on to serve the useless; we petty men are indeed rustic and do not understand what is meant."

entries.zh: 且夫賢君之踐位也，豈特委瑣握齪，拘文牽俗，循誦習傳，當世取說云爾哉！
entries.en: And when a true king takes the throne, does he mean to stay petty and cramped, shackled by precedent and slave to gossip, merely repeating old formulas to win easy applause?
