entries.literal: Moreover, when a worthy lord mounts the throne, how could it be only petty, cramped, bound by precedent and tied by custom, reciting transmitted learning, pleasing the age—that is all?

entries.zh: 必將崇論□議，創業垂統，為萬世規。
entries.en: No—he must voice great policies and bold counsel, found institutions that will last, and lay down models for endless generations.
entries.literal: He must elevate discourse and broaden counsel, found enterprises and hand down a continuing line, setting a pattern for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 故馳騖乎兼容並包，而勤思乎參天貳地。
entries.en: He therefore rides forth on a course broad enough to embrace all under heaven and sets his sights as high as the sky and as deep as the earth.
entries.literal: Therefore he gallops in inclusive breadth, and diligently thinks of matching heaven and doubling earth.

entries.zh: 且《詩》不雲乎：『普天之下，莫非王土；
entries.en: Does not the Odes say, "Under the whole sky every scrap of soil belongs to the king;
entries.literal: Moreover does not the Classic of Songs say: "Under the whole heaven, none is not the king's land;

entries.zh: 率土之濱，莫非王臣。』
entries.en: along every shore of the realm every man is the king's subject."
entries.literal: along the banks of the land, none is not the king's subject."

entries.zh: 是以六合之內，八方之外，浸淫衍溢，懷生之物有不浸潤於澤者，賢君恥之。
entries.en: Within the six directions and beyond the eight outer regions, if any creature fails to feel the royal bounty, a worthy ruler counts it his shame.
entries.literal: Therefore within the six coordinates, beyond the eight directions, soaking and overflowing, if any living creature does not receive the moisture of favor, the worthy lord is ashamed of it.

entries.zh: 今封疆之內，冠帶之倫，鹹獲嘉祉，靡有闕遺矣。
entries.en: Inside the frontiers every belted official already shares in the blessing; none is left out.
entries.literal: Now within the sealed frontiers, among the capped-and-girded classes, all have received fine blessing; none is left lacking.

entries.zh: 而夷狄殊俗之國，遼絕異黨之域，舟車不通，人跡罕至，政教未加，流風猶微，內之則犯義侵禮於邊境，外之則邪行橫作，放殺其上，君臣易位，尊卑失序，父兄不辜，幼孤為奴虜，係累號泣。
entries.en: Yet beyond lie tribes of strange dress and alien speech, lands cut off by distance where neither cart nor boat can pass and few travelers go, places never touched by law or rite. Leave them outside and they raid the frontier; fold them in and murder and revolt multiply—subjects kill their lords, high and low are reversed, the innocent are cut down, children are dragged off as slaves, roped together and sobbing.
entries.literal: But the countries of the Yi and Di with alien customs, regions of remote separation and different clans, where boats and carts do not reach and human tracks are seldom seen, to which government and instruction have not yet been extended and drifting influence is still slight—if brought within, they violate duty and encroach on ritual at the borders; if left without, wicked deeds run rampant, they slay their superiors, lord and minister exchange places, noble and base lose order, fathers and elder brothers suffer unjust death, infants and orphans become slaves and captives, tied and led off, wailing and weeping.

entries.zh: 內鄉而怨，曰：『蓋聞中國有至仁焉，德洋恩普，物磨不得其所，今獨曷為遺己！』
entries.en: They turn their faces toward China and cry, "We hear that the Middle Kingdom is ruled by perfect humanity, that virtue floods every corner until nothing lacks its place—why then are we alone cast off!"
entries.literal: Inwardly they incline and resent, saying: "We have heard that in the Central States there is utmost benevolence; virtue spreads wide and favor is universal; no creature fails to find its place—why alone are we left out!"

entries.zh: 舉踵思慕，若枯旱之望雨，□夫為之垂涕，況乎上聖，又烏能已？
entries.en: They strain on tiptoe toward us like parched fields waiting for rain; the plowman weeps for them—how could the sage on high hold back?
entries.literal: They stand on tiptoe and long for it, like drought looking for rain; [even] the husbandman sheds tears for them—how much more the supreme sage—how could he stop?

entries.zh: 故北出師以討強胡，南馳使以誚勁越。
entries.en: That is why armies went north against the Xiongnu and envoys raced south to rebuke the Yue.
entries.literal: Therefore he marched troops north to chastise the mighty Hu, galloped envoys south to reprove the fierce Yue.

entries.zh: 四面風德，二方之君鱗集仰流，願得受號者以億計。
entries.en: On every side peoples incline toward our virtue; chiefs of two quarters swarm upstream like spawning fish, and those begging for investiture are counted by the hundred thousand.
entries.literal: On four sides they turn to virtue; the lords of two regions swarm like fish swimming upstream, those wishing to receive titles numbering in the hundreds of millions.

entries.zh: 故乃關沫、若，徼牂牁，鏤靈山，梁孫原，創道德之塗，垂仁義之統，將博恩廣施，遠撫長駕，使疏逖不閉，昒爽暗昧得耀乎光明，以偃甲兵於此，而息討伐於彼。
entries.en: Hence the passes on the Mo and Ruo were shut, Zangke was ringed with outposts, Mount Ling was cut through, the Sun River bridged, opening a highway of moral sway and stretching the net of benevolence and duty—intending to spread grace far and wide, to bind the distant in peace, to leave no far corner closed, to bring twilight peoples into the light, to stack weapons here and end campaigns there.
entries.literal: Therefore he closed Mo and Ruo, cordoned Zangke, carved Ling Mountain, bridged the Sun plain, opened the path of virtue and humanity, hung the cord of benevolence and right, intending broadly to extend favor and widely to soothe and long to drive, so that the remote are not shut off, the dim and dark may shine in the bright light, thereby to lay down arms here and cease punitive expeditions there.

entries.zh: 遐邇一體，中外禔福，不亦康乎？
entries.en: Near and far become one fabric, inner and outer alike secure—is that not the true peace?
entries.literal: Far and near are one body, within and without share blessing—is it not peaceable?

entries.zh: 夫拯民於沈溺，奉至尊之休德，反衰世之陵夷，繼周氏之絕業，天子之急務也。
entries.en: Snatching people from the flood, displaying the sovereign's perfect virtue, reversing the rot of a declining age, and taking up the broken work of the Zhou—these are the throne's pressing duties.
entries.literal: To rescue the people from drowning, to uphold the supreme one's splendid virtue, to reverse the decline of a fading age, to continue the broken enterprise of the house of Zhou—these are the Son of Heaven's urgent tasks.

entries.zh: 百姓雖勞，又惡可以已哉？
entries.en: Even if the people grow tired, how can such work simply stop?
entries.literal: Though the hundred surnames are weary, how can it be stopped?

entries.zh: 且夫清道而後行，中路而馳，猶時有銜橛之變。
entries.en: Even when the avenue is cleared and you gallop down the highway, accidents of rein and bit still happen.
entries.literal: Moreover, when the road is cleared and then you proceed, galloping on the middle road, still sometimes there are bit-and-bridge accidents.

entries.zh: 況乎涉豐草，騁丘虛，前有利獸之樂，而內無存變之意，其為害也不亦難矣！
entries.en: How much worse to plunge through tall grass and race over open wastes, with the thrill of the kill ahead and no guard against ambush—the danger then is beyond reckoning!
entries.literal: How much more when you ford deep grass, gallop over barren hills, with the lure of fierce beasts ahead and no thought of lurking danger within—is not the harm then hard to foresee!

entries.zh: 夫輕萬乘之重不以為安，樂出萬有一危之塗以為娛，臣竊為陛下不取。
entries.en: To treat the safety of the imperial equipage lightly and seek pleasure on a road where ruin needs only one chance in ten thousand—your servant respectfully urges that Your Majesty should not choose this.
entries.literal: To slight the weight of the ten thousand chariots and not deem it security, to delight in going out on a path where danger exists once in ten thousand and take it as amusement—your servant privately holds that Your Majesty should not approve.

entries.zh: 蓋明者遠見於未萌，而知者避危於無形，禍固多藏於隱微而發於人之所忽者也。
entries.en: The clear-sighted foresee trouble before it appears; the wise step aside before danger takes shape—most disasters nest in what is small and silent until they burst forth where no one was watching.
entries.literal: The enlightened see far before sprouting, the wise avoid danger before it takes form; calamity indeed often hides in the hidden and subtle and breaks out where men neglect it.

entries.zh: 故鄙諺曰：「家累千金，坐不垂堂。」
entries.en: Thus a rustic proverb says, "When a household has amassed a thousand in gold, one does not sit beneath the eaves of the hall."
entries.literal: Therefore a rustic proverb says: "When the household has piled up a thousand in gold, one does not sit beneath the overhanging eaves of the hall."

entries.zh: 此言雖小，可以諭大。
entries.en: Small as the adage is, it speaks to a great truth.
entries.literal: Though this saying is small, by it one may illustrate what is great.

entries.zh: 臣願陛下留意幸察。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to weigh these words with care.
entries.literal: Your servant begs Your Majesty to take note and deign to examine.

entries.zh: 相如拜為孝文園令。
entries.en: Xiangru received appointment as steward of Emperor Wen's mausoleum park.
entries.literal: Xiangru was appointed director of the park of Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 上既美子虛之事，相如見上好仙，因曰：「上林之事未足美也，尚有靡者。
entries.en: The sovereign had already praised his "Sir Fantasy" rhapsody. Seeing how fond the emperor was of immortals, Xiangru said: "What I wrote of the Upper Grove is not the limit of splendor; something grander remains.
entries.literal: The emperor already admired the affair of Sir Fantasy; Xiangru saw the emperor loved immortals, and therefore said: "The affair of the Upper Forest is not enough to be admired; there is yet something more splendid.

entries.zh: 臣嘗為《大人賦》，未就，請具而奏之。」
entries.en: I have drafted a "Rhapsody for the Great Man" but never finished it; allow me to polish it and lay it before you."
entries.literal: Your servant once composed a "Rhapsody for the Great Man," unfinished; I beg to complete it and present it."

entries.zh: 相如以為列仙之儒居山澤間，形容甚□，此非帝王之仙意也，乃遂奏《大人賦》。
entries.en: He thought the common picture of immortals—emaciated recluses in hills and swamps—beneath an emperor's dignity, and so he offered the "Rhapsody for the Great Man" instead.
entries.literal: Xiangru considered that the sort who rank as immortals dwell among mountains and marshes with forms very [wretched]; this was not the immortal intent proper to an emperor; thereupon he presented the "Rhapsody for the Great Man."

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: It opens:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 相如既奏《大人賦》，天子大說，飄飄有陵雲氣游天地之間意。
entries.en: After Xiangru recited the "Rhapsody for the Great Man," the emperor was transported; he felt light enough to ride the wind between heaven and earth.
entries.literal: When Xiangru had presented the "Rhapsody for the Great Man," the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased, buoyantly as if he had the intent of cloud-riding spirit roaming between heaven and earth.

entries.zh: 於是大司馬進曰：「陛下仁育群生，義征不譓，諸夏樂貢，百蠻執贄，德牟往初，功無與二，休烈液洽，符瑞眾變，斯應紹至，不特創見。
entries.en: The commander-in-chief then stepped forward: "Your Majesty nurtures all life with humanity and chastises the stubborn with justice. The Hua states gladly bring tribute; barbarian chiefs arrive with gifts. Your virtue outshines antiquity; your deeds have no peer. Glory spreads abroad; omens arrive in endless variety—this is no first-time wonder but heaven's steady answer.
entries.literal: Thereupon the grand marshal of state advanced and said: "Your Majesty humanely nurtures the myriad creatures, righteously punishes the disobedient; the various Xia delight in tribute, the hundred Man grasp their gifts; virtue exceeds the beginnings of old, achievement has no second; splendid merit spreads in fusion; tallies and omens crowd in change; such responses come in succession, not merely first creation.

entries.zh: 意者太山、梁父設壇場望幸，蓋號以況榮，上帝垂恩儲祉，，將以慶成，陛下嗛讓而弗發也。
entries.en: Mount Tai and Mount Liangfu have long stood ready with their altars, waiting for your chariot so their names may share your glory. High God heaps favor upon you to mark the work fulfilled—yet you modestly hold back and will not begin.
entries.literal: I suppose Mount Tai and Liangfu have set altar platforms hoping for your fortunate visit, intending titles to match the glory; High God hangs down favor and stores blessing, intending thereby to celebrate completion; Your Majesty humbly yields and does not initiate.

entries.zh: 挈三神之歡，缺王道之儀，群臣恧焉。
entries.en: To deny the Three Powers their joy and leave the kingly sacrifice incomplete shames every minister at court.
entries.literal: To withhold the joy of the three spirits, to lack the rites of the kingly way—the various ministers are ashamed.

entries.zh: 或謂且天為質□，示珍符固不可辭；
entries.en: Some argue that heaven itself is bond, that the rare talismans it sends cannot decently be refused;
entries.literal: Some say moreover heaven is pledge [obscure], showing precious tallies indeed cannot be refused;

entries.zh: 若然辭之，是泰山靡記而梁父罔幾也。
entries.en: To refuse them would leave Tai Shan without its inscription and Liangfu without its hope of the rite.
entries.literal: If so and you refuse them, then Mount Tai has no record and Liangfu has no expectation.

entries.zh: 亦各並時而榮，鹹濟厥世而屈，說者尚何稱於後，而雲七十二君哉？
entries.en: The seventy-two ancient kings each rose in his season, served his age, then bowed out—what would later ages praise in them if you break the chain now?
entries.literal: Also each in its time flourished, all aided their age then bent—what would speakers still praise in later times, saying seventy-two lords?

entries.zh: 夫修德以錫符，奉符以行事，不為進越也。
entries.en: To earn heaven's tallies by virtue and to act once they are granted is not presumption—it is the way of the sage.
entries.literal: For cultivating virtue to grant tallies, receiving tallies to conduct affairs—is not advancing beyond.

entries.zh: 故聖王弗替，而修禮地祇，謁款天神，勒功中岳，以章至尊，舒盛德，發號榮，受厚福，以浸黎民。
entries.en: That is why sage kings never set the rite aside: they perfected worship of earth, made humble approach to heaven, carved their achievement on the sacred peak, displayed the supremacy of the throne, unfolded deep virtue, proclaimed a noble style, drew down rich blessing, and let it flood the common people.
entries.literal: Therefore the sage kings did not abandon it, but cultivated ritual to the earth spirits, sincerely approached the heavenly spirits, inscribed merit on the central marchmount, thereby to manifest the supreme, unfold flourishing virtue, issue glorious titles, receive thick blessing, thereby to soak the black-haired people.

entries.zh: 皇皇哉斯事，天下之壯觀，王者之卒業，不可貶也。
entries.en: This is the supreme spectacle of the empire and the capstone of kingship; it must not be slighted.
entries.literal: Bright bright is this affair—the realm's grand sight, the king's concluding work—it cannot be belittled.

entries.zh: 願陛下全之。
entries.en: We beg you to bring it to fulfillment.
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to complete it.

entries.zh: 而後因雜縉紳先生之略術，使獲曜日月之末光絕炎，以展采錯事。
entries.en: Then let your scholars catch a reflected gleam of your glory and set their talents to the task.
entries.literal: Afterward thereby mixing the rough arts of girdle-and-ribbon gentlemen, causing them to obtain to glisten in the last rays and dying gleam of sun and moon, thereby to unfold their colors and arrange affairs.

entries.zh: 猶兼正列其義，祓飾厥文，作《春秋》一藝。
entries.en: Let them align the doctrine, polish the prose, and add a chapter worthy of the Spring and Autumn.
entries.literal: Still together correcting and arraying their meanings, cleansing and adorning their texts, making the single art of the Spring and Autumn.

entries.zh: 將襲舊六為七，攄之無窮，俾萬世得激清流，揚微波，蜚英聲，騰茂實。
entries.en: The canon will swell from six classics to seven, its influence endless, so that ages to come may ride its clear stream, catch its ripples, and carry its fame and solid achievement abroad.
entries.literal: Will inherit the old six as seven, spreading them without end, causing ten thousand generations to be stirred by clear current, raise slight wave, fly splendid sound, leap luxuriant substance.

entries.zh: 前聖之所以永保鴻名而常為稱首者用此。
entries.en: Earlier sages kept their great names forever at the head of the record by doing exactly this.
entries.literal: Former sages thereby forever preserved vast name and constantly were called chief—by using this.

entries.zh: 宜命掌故悉奏其儀而覽焉。」
entries.en: Order the archivists to set down the full ritual program for your review."
entries.literal: It is fitting to order the archivist fully to memorialize their rites and inspect them."

entries.zh: 披藝觀之，天人之際已交，上下相發允答。
entries.en: Open the classics and see: heaven and man already meet; high and low answer each other in truth.
entries.literal: Spreading the arts and viewing them, the juncture of heaven and man has already intersected, above and below mutually issuing true response.

entries.zh: 聖王之事，兢兢翼翼。
entries.en: The sage-king's business is done with trembling care.
entries.literal: The affairs of the sage king, cautious cautious, careful careful.

entries.zh: 故曰於興必慮衰，安必思危。
entries.en: Hence the saying: in advance remember retreat; in peace remember peril.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: in rising one must consider decline, in security one must think of danger.

entries.zh: 是以湯、武至尊嚴，不失肅祗，舜在假典，顧省厥遺：此之謂也。
entries.en: Tang and Wu held the highest rank yet never dropped their awe; Shun, while dwelling in the great canons, still reviewed his faults. This is the sense of it.
entries.literal: Therefore Tang and Wu, though supremely honored, did not lose reverent awe; Shun, dwelling in the great canons, looked back and examined his oversights: this is what is meant.

entries.zh: 相如既卒五歲，上始祭后土。
entries.en: Five years after Xiangru's death the emperor first offered sacrifice to Hou Tu.
entries.literal: Xiangru having died, five years later the emperor first sacrificed to Hou Tu.

entries.zh: 八年而遂禮中岳，封於太山，至梁甫，禪肅然。
entries.en: Eight years after Xiangru's death he worshiped the central peak, performed the feng on Mount Tai, went on to Liangfu, and the shan at Suyan.
entries.literal: In eight years then he performed rite at the central marchmount, feng on Mount Tai, reaching Liangfu, shan at Suyan.

entries.zh: 司馬相如（下）
entries.en: Sima Xiangru (Part Two).
entries.literal: Sima Xiangru (Part Two).

entries.zh: 武帝初即位，招賢良文學士，是時，弘年六十，以賢良徵為博士。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Wu's reign the court called for worthy men and literary scholars; Hong was sixty and was recommended as worthy and good and summoned to be a court erudite.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu had just ascended the throne, he summoned worthy and good men of literary learning; at that time Hong was sixty sui and, as a worthy and good man, was summoned to serve as an erudite.

entries.zh: 使匈奴，還報，不合意，上怒，以為不能，弘乃移病免歸。
entries.en: Sent on a mission to the Xiongnu, he reported back in terms the emperor disliked. Enraged, the sovereign judged him useless; Hong pleaded illness, gave up his office, and went home.
entries.literal: He was sent to the Xiongnu; on his return he reported, but it did not accord with the emperor's wishes. The emperor was angry, deemed him incompetent, and Hong thereupon feigned illness, resigned, and returned home.

entries.zh: 時對者百餘人，太常奏弘第居下。
entries.en: More than a hundred men had submitted answers; the Chamberlain for Ceremonials ranked Hong last.
entries.literal: At that time those answering numbered more than a hundred; the Chamberlain for Ceremonials memorialized that Hong's ranking was at the bottom.

entries.zh: 策奏，天子擢弘對為第一。
entries.en: When the papers went up, the emperor placed Hong's first.
entries.literal: When the policy essays were presented, the Son of Heaven raised Hong's answer to first place.

entries.zh: 召見，容貌甚麗，拜為博士，待詔金馬門。
entries.en: Called into audience, he cut a striking figure; the court named him erudite and kept him on call at the Golden Horse Gate.
entries.literal: He was summoned for audience; his appearance was very handsome; he was appointed erudite and awaited edicts at the Golden Horse Gate.

entries.zh: 時漢方事匈奴，式上書，願輸家財半助邊。
entries.en: While Han was fighting the Xiongnu, Bu Shi offered to send half his estate to the frontier.
entries.literal: At that time Han was just engaged with the Xiongnu; Shi submitted a memorial, wishing to convey half his household wealth to aid the border.

entries.zh: 上使使問式：「欲為官乎？」
entries.en: The court sent men to ask Bu Shi: "Do you want an appointment?"
entries.literal: The emperor sent envoys to ask Shi, "Do you wish to hold office?"

entries.zh: 式曰：「自小牧羊，不習仕宦，不願也。」
entries.en: Bu Shi replied: "I have herded sheep since I was a boy; I know nothing of government—I do not want a post."
entries.literal: Shi said, "From youth I have herded sheep; I am not practiced in serving as an official; I do not wish it."

entries.zh: 使者曰：「家豈有冤，欲言事乎？」
entries.en: The envoy pressed: "Is there a wrong you wish to redress?"
entries.literal: The envoy said, "Does your household perhaps have a grievance; do you wish to speak of some affair?"

entries.zh: 式曰：「臣生與人亡所爭，邑人貧者貸之，不善者教之，所居，人皆從式，式何故見冤！」
entries.en: Bu Shi said: "I have quarreled with no man; I lend to the poor in my village and teach the unruly; my neighbors follow my lead—what grievance could I have?"
entries.literal: Shi said, "Your servant from birth has contended with no one; to those in the town who are poor he lends; to those who are not good he teaches; where he dwells, people all follow Shi—why should Shi be seen as having a grievance!"

entries.zh: 使者曰：「苟，子何欲？」
entries.en: The envoy said, "Very well—what is it you want?"
entries.literal: The envoy said, "If it is so, what do you desire?"

entries.zh: 式曰：「天子誅匈奴，愚以為賢者宜死節，有財者宜輸之，如此而匈奴可滅也。」
entries.en: Bu Shi answered: "The Son of Heaven is chastising the Xiongnu; the worthy should be ready to die for the cause, the rich should open their granaries—only so can the nomads be crushed."
entries.literal: Shi said, "The Son of Heaven is punishing the Xiongnu; your foolish servant thinks the worthy ought to die for principle, those with wealth ought to convey it—thus the Xiongnu can be extinguished."

entries.zh: 使者以聞。
entries.en: The envoys carried his words to the throne.
entries.literal: The envoy reported it on hearing.

entries.zh: 上以語丞相弘。
entries.en: The emperor mentioned it to Chancellor Hong.
entries.literal: The emperor told Chancellor Hong.

entries.zh: 弘曰：「此非人情。
entries.en: Hong said, "That is not how ordinary men behave.
entries.literal: Hong said, "This is not human feeling.

entries.zh: 不軌之臣不可以為化而亂法，願陛下勿許。」
entries.en: A restless subject must not be held up as an example or he will wreck your statutes; I beg you to decline his offer."
entries.literal: A minister who does not follow the track cannot be used to transform and will disorder the law; I beg Your Majesty not to grant it."

entries.zh: 上不報，數歲乃罷式。
entries.en: The emperor made no answer; only years later did he let Bu Shi go.
entries.literal: The emperor did not reply; only after several years did he send Shi away.

entries.zh: 式歸，復田牧。
entries.en: Bu Shi went home to his flocks and fields.
entries.literal: Shi returned and again farmed and herded.

entries.zh: 元朔中，代薛澤為丞相。
entries.en: During Yuanshuo he succeeded Xue Ze as chancellor.
entries.literal: In the Yuanshuo period he replaced Xue Ze as chancellor.

entries.zh: 先是，漢常以列侯為丞相，唯弘無爵，上於是下詔曰：「朕嘉先聖之道，開廣門路，宣招四方之士，蓋古者任賢而序位，量能以授官，勞大者厥祿厚，德盛者獲爵尊，故武功以顯重，而文德以行褒。
entries.en: Before Hong, every Han chancellor had held a marquisate; Hong alone had none. The emperor therefore proclaimed: "I honor the teaching of the ancient sages, throw wide the doors, and call talent from every quarter. Antiquity appointed the worthy by rank and matched office to ability—great toil won rich pay, towering virtue a high title—so martial deeds were exalted and civil grace rewarded.
entries.literal: Before this, Han had constantly used marquises as chancellors; only Hong had no noble rank; thereupon the emperor issued an edict, saying, "I admire the Way of the former sages, open wide the gates and roads, proclaim and summon gentlemen from the four quarters. In antiquity they appointed the worthy and ordered ranks, measured capacity and conferred office; great labor received thick stipends, abundant virtue obtained honored nobility; therefore military merit was displayed as weighty, and civil virtue was practiced and rewarded.

entries.zh: 其以高成之平津鄉戶六百五十封丞相弘為平津侯。」
entries.en: I enfeoff Chancellor Hong as Marquis of Pingjin with six hundred fifty households at Pingjin township in Gaocheng."
entries.literal: Let Pingjin village in Gaocheng, six hundred fifty households, be enfeoffed to Chancellor Hong as Marquis of Pingjin."

entries.zh: 其後以為故事，至丞相封，自弘始也。
entries.en: Thereafter the grant of a marquisate with the seal of chancellor became precedent, and it began with Hong.
entries.literal: Afterward it was taken as precedent; as for enfeoffment at the chancellorship, it began with Hong.

entries.zh: 元光五年，復征賢良文學，菑川國復推上弘。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Yuanguang the court once more summoned worthy men and literary scholars, and the state of Zichuan again put Hong forward.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanguang, worthy and literary men were again summoned, and the kingdom of Zichuan again advanced Hong.

entries.zh: 弘謝曰：「前已嘗西，用不能罷，願更選。」
entries.en: Hong demurred: "I have already been summoned west once and was let go for incompetence; please select someone else."
entries.literal: Hong declined, saying, "I have already once been summoned west; because of inability I was dismissed; I ask that another be chosen."

entries.zh: 國人固推弘，弘至太常。
entries.en: The men of the state insisted on nominating him, and he was sent on to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
entries.literal: The people of the state firmly advanced Hong, and Hong arrived at the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 上策詔諸儒：
entries.en: The emperor set a policy examination and called the scholars to answer.
entries.literal: The emperor issued a policy question and summoned the various Confucians:

entries.zh: 制曰：蓋聞上古至治，畫衣冠，異章服，而民不犯；
entries.en: The edict read: They say that under the perfect rule of remote antiquity, distinguishing caps and robes and regulating insignia sufficed to keep the people from crime;
entries.literal: The edict said: I have heard that in high antiquity, at the height of good order, they drew caps and garments and differentiated insignia and dress, yet the people did not offend;

entries.zh: 陰陽和，五穀登，六畜蕃，甘露降，風雨時，嘉禾興，朱草生，山不童，澤不涸；
entries.en: yin and yang were balanced, the five grains stood high in the stack, livestock throve, sweet dew descended, wind and rain kept their seasons, auspicious grain appeared, red cinnabar grass sprouted, hills kept their timber, and marshes did not parch;
entries.literal: Yin and yang were in harmony; the five grains ripened; the six kinds of livestock multiplied; sweet dew fell; wind and rain came at the proper times; exceptional grain sprouted; cinnabar grass grew; mountains were not denuded; marshes did not dry up;

entries.zh: 麟鳳在郊藪，龜龍游於沼，河洛出圖書；
entries.en: unicorns and phoenixes haunted the outskirts, turtles and dragons disported in the pools, and chart and text emerged from the Yellow River and the Luo;
entries.literal: unicorns and phoenixes were in the suburban marshes; turtles and dragons swam in the ponds; the Yellow River and Luo River produced charts and books;

entries.zh: 父不喪子，兄不哭弟；
entries.en: fathers did not mourn sons, and elder brothers did not weep for younger brothers;
entries.literal: fathers did not mourn sons; elder brothers did not weep for younger brothers;

entries.zh: 北發渠搜，南撫交阯，舟車所至，人跡所及，跂行喙息，咸得其宜。
entries.en: Their sway ran north to Qusou and south to Jiaozhi; wherever wheel and keel could go and foot could follow, every creature that walks or flies found its proper place.
entries.literal: North they reached Qusou; south they soothed Jiaozhi; wherever boats and carts went, wherever human tracks reached, all who walk on legs and breathe with beaks alike obtained what was fitting for them.

entries.zh: 朕甚嘉之，今何道而臻乎此？
entries.en: I greatly rejoice in such an age—by what path may we reach it today?
entries.literal: I greatly admire this; by what way may one arrive at this?

entries.zh: 子大夫修先聖之術，明君臣之義，講論洽聞，有聲乎當世，敢問子大夫：天人之道，何所本始？
entries.en: You, gentlemen, have mastered the teachings of the ancient sages, understand the duty of lord and minister, and are learned and heard in counsel—your names resound in our time. Tell me, gentlemen: where do Heaven and the human realm first take their origin?
entries.literal: You great officers cultivate the arts of the former sages, clarify the righteousness of ruler and minister, discourse broadly and hear much, and have reputation in the present age. I venture to ask you great officers: in the Way of Heaven and man, where does it begin and take its root?

entries.zh: 吉凶之效，安所期焉？
entries.en: Where may we look for the signs of blessing and calamity?
entries.literal: Where are the effects of auspiciousness and inauspiciousness to be expected?

entries.zh: 禹、湯水旱，厥咎何由？
entries.en: When Yu and Tang suffered flood and drought, what fault brought it on?
entries.literal: In the floods and droughts of Yu and Tang, from what did their blame arise?

entries.zh: 仁、義、禮、知四者之宜，當安設施？
entries.en: How should benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and wisdom be ordered and put into practice?
entries.literal: As to the appropriateness of the four—benevolence, righteousness, rites, and wisdom—how ought they to be instituted and applied?

entries.zh: 屬統垂業，物鬼變化，天命之符，廢興何如？
entries.en: As the succession is maintained and the work passed down, as things and spirits shift and Heaven's mandate shows itself—how are flourishing and decay to be read?
entries.literal: In continuing the line and handing down the enterprise, in the transformations of things and spirits, in the tokens of Heaven's mandate—how do decline and rise compare?

entries.zh: 天文、地理、人事之紀，子大夫習焉。
entries.en: You are versed in the patterns of sky and earth and the affairs of men.
entries.literal: As to the norms of astronomy, geography, and human affairs—you great officers are versed in them.

entries.zh: 其悉意正議，詳具其對，著之於篇，朕將親覽焉，靡有所隱。
entries.en: Set forth your views with care, spell out your replies in full on the scroll, and lay them before me; I shall read them myself and expect nothing held back.
entries.literal: Give your minds fully to upright discussion; set forth your answers in detail in your essays; I will personally peruse them—do not conceal anything.

entries.zh: 弘復上疏曰：「陛下有先聖之位而無先聖之名，有先聖之名而無先聖之吏，是以勢同而治異。
entries.en: Hong again memorialized: "You hold the throne of the ancient paragons but not yet their renown; you bear their reputation yet lack their ministers—so your position matches theirs, but your governance does not.
entries.literal: Hong again submitted a memorial, saying, "Your Majesty occupies the position of the former sages yet lacks the name of the former sages; Your Majesty has the name of the former sages yet lacks the officers of the former sages; therefore the circumstances are alike but the governance differs.

entries.zh: 先世之吏正，故其民篤；
entries.en: When ancient officials were upright, the people grew steadfast;
entries.literal: The officers of former ages were correct; therefore their people were honest.

entries.zh: 今世之吏邪，故其民薄。
entries.en: when today's clerks go crooked, the people turn shallow.
entries.literal: The officers of the present age are deviant; therefore their people are thin.

entries.zh: 政弊而不行，令倦而不聽。
entries.en: Policy grows corrupt and stalls; decrees tire the ear and go unheeded.
entries.literal: Government is flawed and does not proceed; orders are weary and are not heeded.

entries.zh: 夫使邪吏行弊政，用倦令治薄民，民不可得而化，此治之所以異也。
entries.en: Send twisted men to execute a broken policy and weary commands to govern a jaded populace, and you will never win or change them—that is why your rule falls short.
entries.literal: Now to employ deviant officers to carry out flawed government, to use weary orders to govern thin people—the people cannot be obtained and transformed; this is why the ordering is different.

entries.zh: 臣聞周公旦治天下，期年而變，三年而化，五年而定。
entries.en: I have heard that the Duke of Zhou took the realm in hand: within a single cycle things began to shift, in three years they were transformed, in five they stood firm.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when the Duke of Zhou ordered the realm, in one full year there was change, in three years there was transformation, in five years there was stabilization.

entries.zh: 唯陛下之所志。」
entries.en: All hangs on what Your Majesty resolves to do."
entries.literal: It depends only on what Your Majesty sets his mind upon."

entries.zh: 書奏，天子以冊書答曰：「問：弘稱周公之治，弘之材能自視孰與周公賢？」
entries.en: The memorial reached the throne; the emperor replied in his own hand: "You praise the Duke of Zhou's rule—do you count your own gifts the equal of his?"
entries.literal: When the document was submitted, the Son of Heaven answered with a written edict, saying, "I ask: Hong praised the government of the Duke of Zhou—as to Hong's talents and abilities, comparing himself in his own view, how does he compare with the worthiness of the Duke of Zhou?"

entries.zh: 弘對曰：「愚臣淺薄，安敢比材於周公！
entries.en: Hong answered: "I am shallow and coarse—how dare I measure myself against the Duke of Zhou!
entries.literal: Hong replied, saying, "Your foolish servant is shallow and thin; how dare he compare his talents with the Duke of Zhou!

entries.zh: 雖然，愚心曉然見治道之可以然也。
entries.en: Yet this dull heart clearly sees that such order is possible.
entries.literal: Even so, your foolish servant's mind is plainly enlightened and sees that the way of good order can be thus.

entries.zh: 夫虎豹馬牛，禽獸之不可制者也，及其教馴服習之，至可牽持駕服，唯人之從。
entries.en: Tiger, leopard, horse, and ox are brutes that defy control—yet train and gentle them long enough, and they will take halter and rein and obey the driver.
entries.literal: Tigers, leopards, horses, and oxen are creatures that cannot be controlled; yet when they are taught, tamed, accustomed, and practiced, in the end they can be led and harnessed and driven, and follow only what humans intend.

entries.zh: 臣聞揉曲木者不累日，銷金石者不累月，夫人之於利害好惡，豈比禽獸木石之類哉？
entries.en: They say the joiner straightens warped timber in days, not seasons, and the founder melts bronze or iron in months, not years—are men, with their loves and hates of profit and loss, no quicker to teach than wood and stone or fur and feather?
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the artisan who bends crooked wood does not use up many days; he who melts metal and stone does not use up many months—as for people's relation to benefit, harm, liking, and hating, how can they be compared to the categories of birds, beasts, trees, and stones?

entries.zh: 期年而變，臣弘尚竊遲之。」
entries.en: A single cycle for the first change—your servant would still call that slow."
entries.literal: In one full year there is change—your servant Hong still privately deems that slow."

entries.zh: 上異其言。
entries.en: The emperor was struck by his reply.
entries.literal: The emperor marveled at his words.

entries.zh: 後淮南、衡山謀反，治黨與方急，弘病甚，自以為無功而封侯，居宰相位，宜佐明主填撫國家，使人由臣子之道。
entries.en: When Huainan and Hengshan rose, the dragnet for their partisans tightened; Hong lay gravely ill, convinced that he—a man without battlefield merit who had still been made marquis and chancellor—should be steadying the realm and teaching subjects their duty to ruler and father.
entries.literal: Later when Huainan and Hengshan plotted rebellion, the investigation of accomplices was just urgent; Hong was very ill and himself thought that without merit he had been enfeoffed as marquis and occupied the chancellor's position—he ought to assist an enlightened ruler in pacifying the state and causing people to follow the way of minister and son.

entries.zh: 今諸侯有畔逆之計，此大臣奉職不稱也。
entries.en: Now the kings plot treason on the frontier; that means ministers like me have failed their charge.
entries.literal: Now the feudal lords have plans of rebellion on the borders—this is great ministers not fulfilling their posts.

entries.zh: 恐病死無以塞責，乃上書曰：「臣聞天下通道五，所以行之者三。
entries.en: Afraid he might die before answering for it, he memorialized: "I have heard the world knows five constant relationships, yet only three virtues carry them out.
entries.literal: Fearing that if he died of illness he would have no means to answer for his responsibility, he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that the thoroughfares of the realm are five, and those by which they are practiced are three.

entries.zh: 君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友之交，五者天下之通道也；
entries.en: Between lord and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friend—these five bonds are the highways of human life;
entries.literal: The interactions of ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend—these five are the thoroughfares of the realm;

entries.zh: 仁、知、勇三者，所以行之也。
entries.en: benevolence, wisdom, and courage are what put them into practice.
entries.literal: benevolence, wisdom, and courage—these three are that by which they are practiced.

entries.zh: 故曰『好問近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇，知此三者，知所以自治；
entries.en: The classic says, 'Love of inquiry nears wisdom, earnest effort nears benevolence, conscience of shame nears courage; know these three and you know how to govern yourself;
entries.literal: Therefore it is said, 'Loving to ask is close to wisdom, vigorous practice is close to benevolence, knowing shame is close to courage; knowing these three, one knows thereby how to order oneself;

entries.zh: 知所以自治，然後知所以治人。』
entries.en: know yourself and you will know how to govern others.'
entries.literal: knowing thereby how to order oneself, then one knows thereby how to order others.'

entries.zh: 未有不能自治而能治人者也。
entries.en: No one who cannot rule himself can rule another.
entries.literal: There has never been one who could not order himself yet could order others.

entries.zh: 陛下躬孝弟，監三王，建周道，兼文武，招徠四方之士，任賢序位，量能授官，將以厲百姓勸賢材也。
entries.en: Your Majesty embodies filial piety and brotherly love, takes the Three Kings as mirror, revives Zhou's institutions, blends wen and wu, draws talent from every quarter, ranks the worthy by merit, fits office to ability—all to stir the people and lift the able.
entries.literal: Your Majesty personally practices filiality and fraternal duty, mirrors the Three Kings, establishes the way of Zhou, combines civil and martial, summons and attracts gentlemen from the four quarters, appoints the worthy and orders ranks, measures capacity and confers office, intending thereby to encourage the hundred surnames and urge on worthy talent.

entries.zh: 今臣愚駑，無汗馬之勞，陛下過意擢臣弘卒伍之中，封為列侯，致位三公。
entries.en: Yet I am a dull blade with no campaign sweat; you plucked me from the ranks, made me a full marquis, and set me among the Three Excellences.
entries.literal: Now your servant is foolish and dull; he has no sweat-and-horse toil; Your Majesty passingly raised your servant Hong from the ranks of soldiers and commoners, enfeoffed him as a full marquis, and brought him to the place of the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 臣弘行能不足以稱，加有負薪之疾，恐先狗馬填溝壑，終無以報德塞責。
entries.en: My deeds do not match my titles, and I bear the 'wood-carrier's' sickness—likely I shall die in harness like a dog or horse and never repay your kindness.
entries.literal: Your servant Hong's conduct and ability are not sufficient to match it; moreover he has the ailment of carrying firewood—he fears he will first fill the ditches and gullies like a dog or horse and in the end will have no means to repay virtue and answer for his responsibility.

entries.zh: 願歸侯，乞骸骨，避賢者路。」
entries.en: I beg leave to surrender my fief, retire my bones, and clear the path for better men."
entries.literal: I beg to return the marquisate, request my bones, and yield the road to the worthy."

entries.zh: 上報曰：「古者賞有功，褒有德，守成上文，遭遇右武，未有易此者也。
entries.en: The throne answered: "Antiquity rewarded merit, praised virtue; peaceful times exalted letters, peril exalted arms—nothing has changed that rule.
entries.literal: The emperor replied, saying, "In antiquity they rewarded those with merit, praised those with virtue; guarding accomplishment honored culture, meeting crisis honored martial prowess—none has altered this.

entries.zh: 朕夙夜庶幾，獲承至尊，懼不能寧，惟所與共為治者，君宜知之。
entries.en: I took the throne trembling day and night; you are among those I trust to bring peace—surely you know my mind.
entries.literal: I, morning and night hoping, have received the supreme position; I fear I cannot bring tranquility; as to those with whom I share in ordering—sir, you ought to know it.

entries.zh: 蓋君子善善及後世，若茲行，常在朕躬。
entries.en: A gentleman's goodness ripples to later ages; such conduct begins with myself.
entries.literal: As a rule the gentleman who does good extends to later generations; such conduct is always in my person.

entries.zh: 君不幸罹霜露之疾，何恙不已，乃上書歸侯，乞骸骨，是章朕之不德也。
entries.en: You are ill with nothing worse than wind and chill—why not heal? To resign your fief now would advertise my lack of grace.
entries.literal: Sir, unhappily suffering the ailments of frost and dew—what illness is not cured? Yet you submit a memorial returning the marquisate and requesting bones—this displays my lack of virtue.

entries.zh: 今事少閒，君其存精神，止念慮，輔助醫藥以自恃。」
entries.en: Affairs are light for the moment—gather your strength, quiet your cares, and let medicine do its work."
entries.literal: Now affairs are somewhat slack; sir, preserve your spirit, stop anxious thoughts, and rely on physicians and medicine to sustain yourself."

entries.zh: 因賜告牛、酒、雜帛。
entries.en: He granted sick leave with gifts of cattle, wine, and silks.
entries.literal: Thereupon he granted leave, bestowing oxen, wine, and assorted silks.

entries.zh: 居數月，有瘳，視事。
entries.en: A few months later he mended and returned to duty.
entries.literal: After several months he had recovered and attended to affairs.

entries.zh: 元始中，修功臣後，下詔曰：「漢興以來，股肱在位，身行儉約，輕財重義，未有若公孫弘者也。
entries.en: In Yuanshi the court ennobled the descendants of great servants and proclaimed: "Since Han began, no minister on the dais has matched Hong for thrift in his person and zeal for right over riches.
entries.literal: In the Yuanshi period, when they repaired the posterity of meritorious ministers, an edict was issued, saying, "Since the rise of Han, those who have been arms and thighs in office, personally practicing frugality, esteeming righteousness over wealth—none has been like Gongsun Hong.

entries.zh: 位在宰相封侯，而為布被脫粟之飯，奉祿以給故人賓客，無有所餘，可謂減於制度，而率下篤俗者也，與內富厚而外為詭服以釣虛譽者殊科。
entries.en: Chancellor and marquis though he was, he ate millet under a homespun cover and spent every coin on friends—below the sumptuary norm, yet he pulled custom upward; that is not the same breed as men who hoard gold yet dress like beggars for a hollow name.
entries.literal: His position was chancellor and enfeoffed as marquis, yet he used a cloth quilt and coarse unpolished rice for food, and his salary and stipends were given to old friends and guests with nothing left over—this may be called reduction below the regulations, yet leading subordinates to strengthen custom; it is a different category from those who inwardly amass wealth while outwardly wear deceptive dress to fish for empty reputation.

entries.zh: 夫表德章義，所以率世厲俗，聖王之制也。
entries.en: To make virtue visible and righteousness plain is how sage kings regulate the age and steel the folk.
entries.literal: Now to display virtue and make clear righteousness is the means by which to lead the age and encourage custom—it is the regulation of sage kings.

entries.zh: 其賜弘後子孫之次見為適者，爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。」
entries.en: Bestow marquis-within-the-passes rank and three hundred households on the senior legitimate heir among Hong's descendants."
entries.literal: Let those among Hong's posterity and grandchildren who are next in line as heirs be granted rank as marquis within the passes, with three hundred households for their fief."

entries.zh: 會呂嘉反，式上書曰：「臣聞主愧臣死。
entries.en: When Lü Jia rose in the south, Bu Shi wrote: "They say when the sovereign is shamed his servants must die.
entries.literal: When Lü Jia rebelled, Shi submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that when the ruler is ashamed the minister dies.

entries.zh: 群臣宜盡死節，其駑下者宜出財以佐軍，如是則強國不犯之道也。
entries.en: Every minister should be ready to lay down his life; the least of us should open our purses for the host—only thus does a great power go unchallenged.
entries.literal: The host of ministers ought all to die for principle; those who are inferior and dull ought to produce wealth to aid the army—if so, that is the way by which a strong state is not violated.

entries.zh: 臣願與子男及臨菑習弩博昌習船者請行死之，以盡臣節。」
entries.en: Let me take my sons and the crossbowmen of Linzi and boatmen of Bochang and march to the death—so I may pay my debt of honor."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes together with his sons and men and those of Linzi skilled at crossbows and of Bochang skilled at boats to request to go and die in action, thereby fully fulfilling your servant's ministerial principle."

entries.zh: 上賢之，下詔曰：「朕聞報德以德，報怨以直。
entries.en: The emperor praised him and proclaimed: "Kindness is answered with kindness, injury with plain dealing.
entries.literal: The emperor deemed him worthy and issued an edict, saying, "I have heard that virtue is repaid with virtue, grievance with straight dealing.

entries.zh: 今天下不幸有事，郡縣諸侯未有奮繇直道者也。
entries.en: The realm is in trouble, yet no county or kingdom has stepped forward as duty demands.
entries.literal: Now the realm unhappily has affairs; among commanderies, counties, and feudal lords there are none who have roused corvée along the straight way.

entries.zh: 齊相雅行躬耕，隨牧畜番，輒分昆弟，更造，不為利惑。
entries.en: The minister of Qi tills his own soil; whenever his herds multiply he shares with his kin, helps them rebuild when they fail, and never lets greed cloud him.
entries.literal: The minister of Qi by custom practices plowing with his own hands; as his herds and flocks multiply he shares with his brothers and helps them rebuild; he is not deluded by profit.

entries.zh: 日者北邊有興，上書助官。
entries.en: When the north flared up, he was first to offer funds to the state.
entries.literal: Formerly when there was a rising on the northern border, he submitted a memorial to aid the government.

entries.zh: 往年西河歲惡，率齊人入粟。
entries.en: In a lean year west of the river he drove his neighbors to ship grain.
entries.literal: In former years Hexi had a bad harvest; he led the men of Qi to bring in grain.

entries.zh: 今又首奮，雖未戰，可謂義形於內矣。
entries.en: Now he leads again though swords are not yet drawn—his good faith shows from within.
entries.literal: Now again he is first to rouse; although there has not yet been battle, it may be called righteousness formed within.

entries.zh: 其賜式爵關內侯，黃金四十斤，田十頃，佈告天下，使明知之。」
entries.en: I grant him marquis-within-the-passes rank, forty jin of gold, ten qing of land, and publish the edict so all may know."
entries.literal: Let him be granted rank as marquis within the passes, forty jin of gold, ten qing of fields, and proclaimed to all under Heaven, causing them clearly to know it."

entries.zh: 既成，將用事，拜寬為御史大夫，從東封泰山，還登明堂。
entries.en: When all was ready he named Kuan imperial counselor; Kuan escorted him east to Tai, then back to the Bright Hall.
entries.literal: When it was complete and the time came to perform the rites, he appointed Kuan imperial counselor; Kuan followed east to perform feng on Mount Tai, then returned and ascended the Bright Hall.

entries.zh: 寬上壽曰：「臣聞三代改制，屬象相因。
entries.en: At the Bright Hall Kuan raised his cup: "The Three Houses refashioned rites and handed their emblems down in turn.
entries.literal: Kuan offered a toast, saying, "Your servant has heard that the Three Dynasties revised institutions and linked their symbolic systems in succession.

entries.zh: 間者聖統廢絕，陛下發憤，合指天地，祖立明堂辟雍，宗祀泰一，六律五聲，幽贊聖意，神樂四合，各有方象，以丞嘉祀，為萬世則，天下幸甚。
entries.en: That line fell silent until you took it up: you paired earth with sky, raised the Bright Hall and the Biyong academy, honored the Grand Unity, and let pitch and mode voice a music the spirits answer—rites that will model all later ages and bless the world.
entries.literal: For a time the sacred line was broken; Your Majesty roused yourself, matched finger to Heaven and earth, founded as ancestor the Bright Hall and the royal academy, performed lineage sacrifice to the Grand Unity, so that the six pitchpipes and five tones secretly assist the sage intent, divine music joins from the four quarters, each with its emblem, to second the splendid offerings and be a model for ten thousand generations—great fortune for the realm.

entries.zh: 將建大元本瑞，登告岱宗，發祉闓門，以候景至。
entries.en: You will plant the Grand Beginning omen, mount Tai to report, fling wide the gate of blessing, and wait for the sign.
entries.literal: You will establish the Grand Beginning's root token, ascend to announce to the Lord of Dai, open the gate of blessing, and await the arrival of the portent.

entries.zh: 癸亥宗祀，日宣重光；
entries.en: On the guihai day of the lineage rite the sun shows double radiance;
entries.literal: On guihai the lineage sacrifice; the sun proclaims doubled light;

entries.zh: 上元甲子，肅邕永享。
entries.en: In the founding jiazi of the new cycle, solemn peace is pledged without end.
entries.literal: In the upper-origin jiazi year, solemn harmony endures forever.

entries.zh: 光輝充塞，天文粲然，見象日昭，報降符應。
entries.en: Heaven's patterns blaze; each omen grows plainer; the matching signs fall in reply.
entries.literal: Radiance fills the void; the patterns of Heaven shine clear; the images appear daily brighter, and answering tokens descend.

entries.zh: 臣寬奉觴再拜，上千萬歲壽。」
entries.en: Your servant raises the cup twice and bows, wishing Your Majesty ten thousand years of life."
entries.literal: Your servant Kuan raises the goblet twice and bows, offering Your Majesty a toast of ten thousand years."

entries.zh: 制曰：「敬舉君之觴。」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "I accept your toast with respect."
entries.literal: The edict said, "Respectfully I accept my lord's toast."

entries.zh: 及議欲放古巡狩封禪之事，諸儒對者五十餘人，未能有所定。
entries.en: Debate on restoring the ancient progress and the Tai-shan rites drew answers from fifty-odd scholars and still no decision.
entries.literal: When they deliberated on reviving in antiquity's manner the royal tour and the feng and shan sacrifices, more than fifty Confucians submitted answers yet could settle nothing.

entries.zh: 先是，司馬相如病死，有遺書，頌功德，言符瑞，足以封泰山。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru had left a posthumous memorial praising the reign and its omens as warranting the Tai-shan ceremony.
entries.literal: Earlier Sima Xiangru had died of illness, leaving a testament that praised merit and virtue, spoke of auspicious tokens, and argued that feng on Mount Tai was warranted.

entries.zh: 上奇其書，以問寬，寬對曰：「陛下躬發聖德，統楫群元，宗祀天地，薦禮百神，精神所鄉，徵兆必報，天地並應，符瑞昭明。
entries.en: The emperor showed him Xiangru's text; Kuan answered: "Your virtue steers the people, your sacrifices reach Heaven, earth, and the gods—where mind and rite meet, omens reply in plain sight.
entries.literal: The emperor marveled at the document and asked Kuan; Kuan replied, saying, "Your Majesty has personally unfolded sacred virtue, steers the myriad subjects, performs lineage sacrifice to Heaven and earth, and presents offerings to the hundred spirits; where your spirit turns, signs answer; Heaven and earth respond together, and auspicious tokens shine clear.

entries.zh: 其封泰山，禪梁父，昭姓考瑞，帝王之盛節也。
entries.en: The feng on Tai and the shan at Liangfu, proclaiming your line and reading the portents, are the crown acts of true kings.
entries.literal: To perform feng on Tai and shan at Liangfu, clarifying the royal surname and examining tokens, is the supreme observance of emperors and kings.

entries.zh: 然享薦之義，不著於經，以為封禪告成，合祛於天地神祇，祗戒精專以接神明。
entries.en: The classics do not spell every detail of the offerings; still, feng and shan close the great enterprise, join your report to Heaven and earth, and call for the purest reverence toward the gods.
entries.literal: Yet the meaning of offering and presenting is not spelled out in the classics; I hold that the feng and shan announce the work's completion, unite the purifying rite with the spirits and gods of Heaven and earth, and demand reverent vigil and single-minded purity to meet the spirits.

entries.zh: 總百官之職，各稱事宜而為之節文。
entries.en: Each ministry must fit its part to the season and supply the proper liturgical text.
entries.literal: Gather the functions of the hundred offices, let each match what is timely, and frame the ritual wording for them.

entries.zh: 唯聖主所由，制定其當，非君臣之所能列。
entries.en: Only the Son of Heaven can set the mean and fix the forms—no roster of ministers can substitute for that.
entries.literal: Only the course the sage ruler takes, fixing what is fitting, is not something lord and minister can lay out in a list.

entries.zh: 令將舉大事，優遊數年，使群臣得人自盡，終莫能成。
entries.en: Dawdle for years while every adviser pushes a private scheme, and the great rite will never be done.
entries.literal: If you are about to undertake a great affair yet linger at ease for years, letting each minister exhaust his own notion, in the end nothing will be finished.

entries.zh: 唯天子建中和之極，兼總條貫，金聲而玉振之，以順成天慶，垂萬世之基。」
entries.en: Only the throne can strike the perfect chord, draw every strand together, and "sound the bell of metal and the chime of jade"—finishing Heaven's celebration and founding an age that will last."
entries.literal: Only the Son of Heaven establishes the apex of central harmony, gathers every thread, sets them ringing like metal and concluding like jade, thereby completing Heaven's blessing and laying the foundation for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 上然之，乃自製儀，采儒術以文焉。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, wrote much of the ritual himself, and draped it in Confucian phrase.
entries.literal: The emperor approved; thereupon he personally drafted the liturgy, borrowing Confucian learning to give it polish.

entries.zh: 元鼎中，征式代石慶為御史大夫。
entries.en: In Yuanding the court called Bu Shi to replace Shi Qing as imperial counselor.
entries.literal: In the Yuanding period he summoned Shi to replace Shi Qing as imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 式既在位，言郡國不便鹽鐵而船有算，可罷。
entries.en: Once in office he urged repeal of the salt-and-iron monopoly and the boat levy, which he said hurt the commanderies.
entries.literal: When Shi was already in office, he said that commanderies and kingdoms found the salt and iron monopolies inconvenient and that there was a tax on boats—they could be abolished.

entries.zh: 上由是不說式。
entries.en: The emperor took offense and cooled toward him.
entries.literal: The emperor thereby was not pleased with Shi.

entries.zh: 明年當封禪，式又不習文章，貶秩為太子太傅，以兒寬代之。
entries.en: The next year, with the Feng and Shan rites at hand, Bu Shi could not draft the liturgies; he was demoted to tutor to the heir apparent while Er Kuan took his chair.
entries.literal: The next year, when it was time to enfeoff Mount Tai and offer the subjugated sacrifice, Shi was again not practiced in literary composition; his rank was reduced to grand tutor to the heir apparent, and Er Kuan replaced him.

entries.zh: 式以壽終。
entries.en: Bu Shi died in his bed, full of years.
entries.literal: Shi ended his life by old age.

entries.zh: 汲黯曰：「弘位在三公，奉祿甚多，然為布被，此詐也。」
entries.en: Ji An said, "Hong sits among the Three Excellencies on a fat stipend yet sleeps under a homespun quilt—that is a pose."
entries.literal: Ji An said, "Hong's position is among the Three Dukes; his salary and stipends are very many, yet he uses a cloth quilt—this is deceit."

entries.zh: 上問弘，弘謝曰：「有之。
entries.en: The emperor questioned Hong, who confessed: "It is true.
entries.literal: The emperor asked Hong; Hong apologized, saying, "It is so.

entries.zh: 夫九卿與臣善者無過黯，然今日庭詰弘，誠中弘之病。
entries.en: Of the nine ministers none is closer to me than Ji An, yet he rebuked me in open court—and he put his finger on my fault.
entries.literal: Among the nine ministers none who are on good terms with your servant surpasses Ji An, yet today in court he confronted Hong—it truly hit Hong's ailment.

entries.zh: 夫以三公為布被，誠飾詐欲以釣名。
entries.en: For a grand chancellor to affect a patchwork cover is plainly a trick to angle for a reputation.
entries.literal: Now for one of the Three Dukes to use a cloth quilt is truly adornment and deceit intending to fish for a name.

entries.zh: 且臣聞管仲相齊，有三歸，侈擬於君，桓公以霸，亦上僭於君。
entries.en: I recall Guan Zhong as minister of Qi kept three household establishments and lived almost like his lord; Duke Huan still made him the engine of hegemony—yet that was presumption toward the throne.
entries.literal: Moreover your servant has heard that when Guan Zhong served as minister to Qi, he had three returns, his extravagance rivaling the ruler's; Duke Huan thereby became hegemon—this was also upward transgression against the ruler.

entries.zh: 晏嬰相景公，食不重肉，妾不衣絲，齊國亦治，亦下比於民。
entries.en: Yan Ying served Duke Jing on a single meat dish and would not dress his concubines in silk, yet Qi was well governed—he pressed himself down to the people's level.
entries.literal: Yan Ying served Duke Jing of Qi; he did not have double portions of meat at meals, his concubines did not wear silk, yet the state of Qi was also well ordered—this was also downward comparison with the people.

entries.zh: 今臣弘位為御史大夫，為布被，自九卿以下至於小吏無差，誠如黯言。
entries.en: I am imperial counselor yet share a peasant's bedding with every clerk from the nine ministers down—Ji An had the right of it.
entries.literal: Now your servant Hong's position is imperial counselor; using a cloth quilt, from the nine ministers down to petty clerks there is no distinction—it is truly as Ji An said.

entries.zh: 且無黯，陛下安聞此言？」
entries.en: Moreover, without Ji An, how would Your Majesty ever have heard this?"
entries.literal: Moreover, were it not for Ji An, how would Your Majesty have heard these words?"

entries.zh: 上以為有讓，愈益賢之。
entries.en: The emperor read his reply as modesty and esteemed him the more.
entries.literal: The emperor deemed him deferential and all the more deemed him worthy.

entries.zh: 為內史數年，遷御史大夫。
entries.en: After some years as metropolitan superintendent he rose to imperial counselor.
entries.literal: Having been Metropolitan Superintendent for several years, he was promoted to imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 時又東置蒼海，北築朔方之郡。
entries.en: At the same time the court opened the Canghai commandery in the east and walled Shuofang in the north.
entries.literal: At that time they also established Canghai to the east and built the commandery of Shuofang to the north.

entries.zh: 弘數諫，以為罷弊中國以奉無用之地，願罷之。
entries.en: Hong remonstrated again and again that these schemes beggared the heartland to hold empty borderlands and should be dropped.
entries.literal: Hong repeatedly remonstrated, holding that to exhaust and ruin the central states in order to serve useless lands—he wished to abolish them.

entries.zh: 於是上乃使硃買臣等難弘置朔方之便。
entries.en: The emperor set Zhu Maichen and others to debate him on the worth of Shuofang.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor then sent Zhu Maichen and others to challenge Hong on the convenience of establishing Shuofang.

entries.zh: 發十策，弘不得一。
entries.en: They put ten questions; Hong could not best a single one.
entries.literal: They raised ten points; Hong could not answer one.

entries.zh: 弘乃謝曰：「山東鄙人，不知其便若是，願罷西南夷、蒼海，專奉朔方。」
entries.en: Hong conceded: "I am a bumpkin from east of the passes; I did not see how useful Shuofang could be—let the southwest and Canghai go, and pour our strength into Shuofang alone."
entries.literal: Hong thereupon apologized, saying, "I am a rustic from east of the mountains and did not know its convenience was like this; I wish to abolish the southwestern Yi and Canghai and devote our efforts solely to Shuofang."

entries.zh: 上乃許之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon granted it.

entries.zh: 初，梁相褚大通《五經》，為博士，時寬為弟子。
entries.en: Long before, Liang minister Chu Da, a Five-Classics scholar and court erudite, had numbered Kuan among his students.
entries.literal: Earlier the minister of Liang, Chu Da, was broadly versed in the Five Classics and served as erudite; at that time Kuan was his disciple.

entries.zh: 及御史大夫缺，征褚大，大自以為得御史大夫。
entries.en: When the censor's chair fell empty, the court called for Chu Da, who assumed the job was his.
entries.literal: When the post of imperial counselor was vacant, they summoned Chu Da; Da himself thought he would obtain the post of imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 至洛陽，聞兒寬為之，褚大笑。
entries.en: At Luoyang he learned Er Kuan held the post—and laughed aloud.
entries.literal: When he reached Luoyang he heard that Er Kuan held it, and Chu burst out laughing.

entries.zh: 及至，與寬議封禪於上前，大不能及，退而服曰：「上誠知人。」
entries.en: When Chu Da reached court and debated the Feng and Shan sacrifices with Kuan before the emperor, he could not match him. Afterward he conceded, "The sovereign truly knows men."
entries.literal: When he arrived and with Kuan debated feng and shan before the emperor, he could not match him; withdrawing he submitted, saying, "The sovereign truly knows men."

entries.zh: 寬為御史大夫，以稱意任職，故久無有所匡諫於上，官屬易之。
entries.en: Kuan pleased the emperor so well that he rarely criticized policy; his staff despised him for it.
entries.literal: Kuan as imperial counselor, because he pleased the emperor in office, for long remonstrated on nothing to the emperor; his subordinates looked down on him.

entries.zh: 居位九歲，以官卒。
entries.en: Nine years he held the censorate, then died in harness.
entries.literal: He occupied the post nine years and died in office.

entries.zh: 贊曰：公孫弘、卜式、兒寬皆以鴻漸之翼困於燕爵，遠跡羊豕之間，非遇其時，焉能致此位乎？
entries.en: The historian sighs: Hong, Bu Shi, and Er Kuan were swans mistaken for hens, men of worth herding pigs and sheep—without a ruler who sought them, how would they ever have risen?
entries.literal: The appraising comment says: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Er Kuan all had the great swan's pinions yet were trapped among barnyard sparrows, their tracks far among sheep and pigs—had they not met their season, how could they have reached these positions?

entries.zh: 是時，漢興六十餘載，海內艾安，府庫充實，而四夷未賓，制度多闕。
entries.en: By then Han had stood sixty years at peace, the vaults were full, but the border tribes still stood outside the rites and many statutes waited to be written.
entries.literal: At that time, more than sixty years after Han's rise, within the seas were at peace, granaries and treasuries were full, yet the four barbarians had not submitted and institutions were still largely lacking.

entries.zh: 上方欲用文武，求之如弗及，始以蒲輪迎枚生，見主父而歎息。
entries.en: The sovereign meant to wield both wen and wu and hunted talent as if starved for it—he fetched Mei Sheng with the rush-wheeled cart and caught his breath at the sight of Zhufu Yan.
entries.literal: The emperor above wished to employ both civil and martial means and sought men as if he could not catch up; he first welcomed Master Mei with the rush-wheeled carriage and sighed on seeing Zhufu.

entries.zh: 群士慕向，異人並出。
entries.en: Scholars flocked to the capital; strange gifts turned up in pairs.
entries.literal: The host of gentlemen yearned toward him; unusual men appeared together.

entries.zh: 卜式拔於芻牧，弘羊擢於栗豎，衛青奮於奴僕，日磾出於降虜，斯亦曩時版築飯牛之朋已。
entries.en: Bu Shi rose from the pasture, Sang Hongyang from the granary urchin, Wei Qing from slavery, Jin Midi from the ranks of captives—kin to the wall-builders and ox-herders of legend.
entries.literal: Bu Shi was pulled up from fodder and herding, Sang Hongyang was promoted from a boy who husked grain, Wei Qing roused himself from slave status, Jin Midi came forth from surrendered captives—these too are companions of the men who built walls and fed oxen in older days.

entries.zh: 漢之得人，於茲為盛，儒雅則公孫弘、董仲舒、兒寬，篤行則石建、石慶，質直則汲黯、卜式，推賢則韓安國、鄭當時，定令則趙禹、張湯，文章則司馬遷、相如，滑稽則東方朔、枚皋，應對則嚴助、硃買臣，歷數則唐都、洛下閎，協律則李延年，運籌則桑弘羊，奉使則張騫、蘇武，將率則衛青、霍去病，受遺則霍光、金日磾，其餘不可勝紀。
entries.en: Never did the dynasty gather talent so thickly: Hong, Dong, and Kuan for classical breadth; the Shi brothers for steadfast service; Ji An and Bu Shi for blunt loyalty; Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi for lifting others; Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang for codifying law; Sima Qian and Xiangru for voice; jesters Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao; debaters Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen; calendar-makers Tang Du and Luoxia Hong; the harmonist Li Yan'nian; the reckoner Sang Hongyang; envoys Zhang Qian and Su Wu; blades Wei Qing and Huo Qubing; regents Huo Guang and Jin Midi—and a cloud of names besides.
entries.literal: Thus Han obtained men; at this time it was most flourishing: in Confucian elegance then Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, Er Kuan; in steadfast conduct then Shi Jian, Shi Qing; in plain straightforwardness then Ji An, Bu Shi; in advancing the worthy then Han Anguo, Zheng Dangshi; in fixing statutes then Zhao Yu, Zhang Tang; in literary composition then Sima Qian, Xiangru; in jest then Dongfang Shuo, Mei Gao; in repartee then Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen; in calendrical reckoning then Tang Du, Luoxia Hong; in harmonizing pitch then Li Yan'nian; in planning transport then Sang Hongyang; as envoys then Zhang Qian, Su Wu; as generals then Wei Qing, Huo Qubing; as testamentary appointees then Huo Guang, Jin Midi—the rest cannot be fully recorded.

entries.zh: 是以興造功業，制度遺文，後世莫及。
entries.en: Hence the works they raised and the laws they left posterity have scarcely been equaled since.
entries.literal: Therefore they raised achievements and enterprises, and the institutions and writings they bequeathed later ages could not match.

entries.zh: 孝宣承統，纂修洪業，亦講論六藝，招選茂異，而蕭望之、梁丘賀、夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖，尹更始以儒術進，劉向，王褒以文章顯，將相則張安世、趙充國、魏相、丙吉、於定國、杜延年，治民則黃霸、王成、龔遂、鄭弘、召信臣、韓延壽、尹翁歸、趙廣漢、嚴延年、張敞之屬，皆有功跡見述於世。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too expounded the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction for their writing; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; and among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All left achievements celebrated in their age.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too discussed the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men: Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction through literary composition; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All had achievements recounted in their age.

entries.zh: 參其名臣，亦其次也。
entries.en: Against that roster of great servants, the three men treated here belong in the second rank.
entries.literal: If one compares them to those famous ministers, they likewise are of the next rank.

entries.zh: 公孫弘
entries.en: Gongsun Hong.
entries.literal: Gongsun Hong (the subject of this biography).

entries.zh: 武安侯為丞相，徵湯為史，薦補侍御史。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Wu'an became chancellor, he called Tang up as a clerk on his staff and had him promoted to attendant censor.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Wu'an became chancellor, he summoned Tang as a clerk and recommended him to fill a vacancy as attendant censor.

entries.zh: 治陳皇后巫蠱獄，深竟黨與，上以為能，遷太史大夫。
entries.en: He prosecuted the witchcraft case involving Empress Chen, tracking every accomplice to the end. The emperor judged him competent and raised him to grand clerk of records.
entries.literal: In handling the case of witchcraft against Empress Chen, he pursued the clique to the utmost; the emperor thought him capable and promoted him to grand clerk.

entries.zh: 與趙禹共定諸律令，務在深文，拘守職之吏。
entries.en: He and Zhao Yu rewrote the statutes and regulations, aiming for severe, tight legal language that would keep petty officials from shirking their responsibilities.
entries.literal: Together with Zhao Yu he fixed the various statutes and ordinances, striving for harsh wording and restraining clerks who guarded their duties.

entries.zh: 已而禹至少府，湯為廷尉，兩人交歡，兄事禹。
entries.en: Zhao Yu later rose to chamberlain for the palace revenues while Tang became commandant of justice. The two remained on excellent terms, and Tang deferred to Yu as he would to an older brother.
entries.literal: Afterward Yu reached the chamberlain for the palace revenues; Tang became commandant of justice. The two were on warm terms, and Tang treated Yu as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 禹志在奉公孤立，而湯舞知以御人。
entries.en: Zhao Yu set his heart on impartial public service and stood aloof from intrigue; Tang, by contrast, traded on his wits to manipulate those around him.
entries.literal: Yu's intent was to uphold public duty in isolation, while Tang wielded cleverness to control others.

entries.zh: 始為小吏，干沒，與長安富賈田甲、魚翁叔之屬交私。
entries.en: In his early days as a low clerk he skimmed funds and kept company with wealthy Chang'an traders like Tian Jia and Yu Wengshu.
entries.literal: When he first was a petty clerk, he embezzled and associated privately with Chang'an rich merchants such as Tian Jia and Yu Wengshu.

entries.zh: 及列九卿，收接天下名士大夫，己內心雖不合，然陽浮道與之。
entries.en: Once he sat among the nine ministers, he cultivated ties with eminent scholars from every quarter. Inwardly he often disagreed with them, yet he publicly affected the rhetoric of classical learning.
entries.literal: When he reached the nine ministers, he received the famous gentlemen of the empire; though inwardly he did not agree with them, he outwardly floated the Way with them.

entries.zh: 會渾邪等降，漢大興兵伐匈奴，山東水旱，貧民流徙，皆卬給縣官，縣官空虛。
entries.en: When Hunye and his followers submitted, the Han mobilized on a vast scale against the Xiongnu; floods and drought struck the eastern heartland; refugees streamed from their homes and looked to the state for relief until the public granaries stood bare.
entries.literal: It happened that Hunye and others surrendered; Han greatly raised troops to attack the Xiongnu; east of the mountains there were flood and drought; poor people wandered and migrated—all looked up to the government for supplies, and the government treasuries were empty.

entries.zh: 湯承上指，請造白金及五銖錢，籠天下鹽鐵，排富商大賈，出告緡令，鋤豪強並兼之家，舞文巧詆以輔法。
entries.en: Reading the emperor's wishes, Tang proposed minting the white-metal currency and the five-zhu coin, bringing the empire's salt and iron under state monopoly, squeezing the great merchant houses, promulgating the "report-your-neighbor's-wealth" statute, and breaking up powerful clans that engrossed land and labor—all the while bending the statutes to give the policy a legal veneer.
entries.literal: Tang received the ruler's intent, requested to mint white metal and five-zhu cash, monopolize salt and iron over the empire, displace great rich merchants, issued the denunciation ordinance, rooted out powerful families who swallowed others' holdings, and twisted text and craftily slandered to assist the law.

entries.zh: 湯每朝奏事，語國家用，日旰，天子忘食。
entries.en: Whenever Tang spoke at audience on fiscal policy, he went on until the sun stood low in the west, and the Son of Heaven forgot his meal.
entries.literal: Tang each time at court submitted affairs, discoursing on state use, until the sun was late; the Son of Heaven forgot food.

entries.zh: 丞相取充位，天子事皆決湯。
entries.en: The chancellor was a figurehead; every important decision passed through Tang.
entries.literal: The chancellor held a filling seat; the Son of Heaven's affairs were all decided by Tang.

entries.zh: 百姓不安其生，騷動，縣官所興未獲其利，奸吏並侵漁，於是痛繩以罪。
entries.en: Common folk could not live in peace; unrest spread. State ventures brought little gain while corrupt clerks fed on the people, so Tang cracked down with harsh punishments.
entries.literal: The hundred surnames were not secure in their lives, stirred and restless; what the government raised did not obtain its profit, and wicked clerks together encroached and preyed—thereupon he painfully bound them with guilt.

entries.zh: 自公卿以下至於庶人咸指湯。
entries.en: From the highest ministers to the meanest commoner, everyone blamed Tang.
entries.literal: From the dukes and ministers down to the common people, all pointed at Tang.

entries.zh: 湯嘗病，上自至捨視，其隆貴如此。
entries.en: When Tang fell ill, the emperor visited his house in person—such was the height of his favor.
entries.literal: Tang once was ill; the ruler in person came to his lodging to look—his exalted honor was thus.

entries.zh: 昭帝即位，大將軍霍光秉政，以安世篤行，光親重之。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhao came to the throne, Grand General Huo Guang held power. Because Zhang Anshi was known for upright conduct, Huo Guang personally valued him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhao succeeded, Grand General Huo Guang held the government; because Anshi was of steadfast conduct, Guang personally esteemed him.

entries.zh: 會左將軍上官桀父子及御史大夫桑弘羊皆與燕王、蓋主謀反誅，光以朝無舊臣，白用安世為右將軍光祿勳，以自副焉。
entries.en: When Left General Shangguan Jie and his son, together with Grand Minister of Finance Sang Hongyang, were executed for plotting with the King of Yan and the Princess of Gai, Huo Guang—finding the court bereft of senior ministers—recommended Anshi as general of the right and superintendent of the masters of writing to serve as his deputy.
entries.literal: It happened that Left General Shangguan Jie, father and son, and Grand Minister of Finance Sang Hongyang all plotted rebellion with the King of Yan and the Princess of Gai and were executed; Guang, because the court had no old ministers, reported and appointed Anshi as General of the Right and superintendent of the masters of writing, to serve as his deputy.

entries.zh: 久之，天子下詔曰：「右將軍光祿勳安世輔政宿衛，肅敬不怠，十有三年，咸以康寧。
entries.en: After some time the emperor issued an edict: "General of the Right and superintendent of the masters of writing Anshi has assisted in government and guarded the palace with reverent diligence for thirteen years, and the realm has remained at peace.
entries.literal: After a long time, the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying, "General of the Right and superintendent of the masters of writing Anshi has assisted in government and guarded the palace, reverent and diligent without slackening, for thirteen years, and all have thereby been at peace.

entries.zh: 夫親親任賢，唐、虞之道也，其封安世為富平侯。」
entries.en: To cherish kin and employ the worthy is the Way of Tang and Yu. Let Anshi be enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuping."
entries.literal: To cherish kin and employ the worthy is the Way of Tang and Yu; let Anshi be enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuping."

entries.zh: 明年，昭帝崩，未葬，大將軍光白太后，徙安世為車騎將軍，與共徵立昌邑王。
entries.en: The next year Emperor Zhao died. Before the funeral, Huo Guang reported to the empress dowager, transferred Anshi to general of chariots and cavalry, and together they summoned and enthroned the King of Changyi.
entries.literal: The next year Emperor Zhao died; before burial, Grand General Guang reported to the empress dowager and transferred Anshi to be general of chariots and cavalry, and together they summoned and enthroned the King of Changyi.

entries.zh: 王行淫亂，光復與安世謀，廢王、尊立宣帝。
entries.en: When the new king proved dissolute, Huo Guang again plotted with Anshi, deposed him, and enthroned Emperor Xuan in his place.
entries.literal: The king behaved licentiously and disorderly; Guang again plotted with Anshi, deposed the king, and honored and enthroned Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 帝初即位，褒賞大臣，下詔曰：「夫褒有德，賞有功，古今之通義也。
entries.en: Soon after his accession the emperor rewarded his leading ministers with an edict: "To praise the virtuous and reward the meritorious is the universal principle of ancient and modern times.
entries.literal: When the emperor had just succeeded, he rewarded and honored great ministers and issued an edict saying, "To praise the virtuous and reward the meritorious is the universal principle of ancient and modern times.

entries.zh: 車騎將軍光祿勳富平侯安世，宿衛忠正，宣德明恩，勤勞國家，守職秉義，以安宗廟，其益封萬六百戶，功次大將軍光。」
entries.en: General of chariots and cavalry, superintendent of the masters of writing, and Marquis of Fuping Anshi has guarded the palace with loyal rectitude, spread virtue abroad, toiled for the state, and upheld righteousness to secure the ancestral temple. Increase his fief by ten thousand six hundred households; his merit ranks next to Grand General Huo Guang."
entries.literal: General of chariots and cavalry, superintendent of the masters of writing, and Marquis of Fuping Anshi has guarded the palace with loyal rectitude, spread virtue and made grace clear, toiled for the state, kept his post and upheld righteousness, and thereby secured the ancestral temple. Let his fief be increased by ten thousand six hundred households; his merit ranks next to Grand General Guang."

entries.zh: 安世子千秋、延壽、彭祖，皆中郎將侍中。
entries.en: Anshi's sons Zhang Qianqiu, Zhang Yanshou, and Pengzu were all made generals of the household gentlemen and attendants of the interior.
entries.literal: Anshi's sons Qianqiu, Yanshou, and Pengzu were all generals of the household gentlemen and attendants of the interior.

entries.zh: 大將軍光薨後數月，御史大夫魏相上封事曰：「聖王褒有德以懷萬方，顯有功以勸百寮，是以朝廷尊榮，天下鄉風。
entries.en: Several months after Huo Guang died, Grand Minister of Works Wei Xiang submitted a sealed memorial: "The sage king praises the virtuous to win over the myriad regions and displays the meritorious to encourage the hundred officials, so that the court is honored and the realm takes its lead.
entries.literal: Several months after Grand General Guang died, Grand Minister of Works Wei Xiang submitted a sealed memorial saying, "The sage king praises the virtuous to embrace the myriad regions and displays the meritorious to encourage the hundred officials; thereby the court is honored and the realm takes its lead.

entries.zh: 國家承祖宗之業，制諸侯之重，新失大將軍，宜宣章盛德以示天下，顯明功臣以填籓國。
entries.en: The state inherits the ancestral enterprise and holds the feudal lords in check. Having just lost the grand general, it is fitting to proclaim great virtue to the realm and elevate meritorious ministers to fill the frontier marches.
entries.literal: The state inherits the enterprise of the ancestors and controls the weight of the feudal lords; having newly lost the grand general, it is fitting to proclaim and display great virtue to show the realm and make clear meritorious ministers to fill the frontier states.

entries.zh: 毋空大位，以塞爭權，所以安社稷絕未萌也。
entries.en: Great offices must not be left vacant, lest rivalries for power arise; that is how the altars of state are secured and trouble nipped in the bud.
entries.literal: Do not leave great offices empty and thereby block struggles for power—this is how to secure the altars of soil and grain and cut off what has not yet sprouted.

entries.zh: 車騎將軍安世事孝武皇帝三十餘年，忠信謹厚，勤勞政事，夙夜不怠，與大將軍定策，天下受其福，國家重臣也，宜尊其位，以為大將軍，毋令領光祿勳事，使專精神，憂念天下，思惟得失。
entries.en: General of chariots and cavalry Anshi served Emperor Wu for more than thirty years with loyal, careful service, toiling day and night in government. With the grand general he settled the succession, and the realm benefited. He is a pillar of the state and should be raised to grand general, relieved of the superintendent of the masters of writing, so that he may devote himself wholly to the realm and weigh its gains and losses.
entries.literal: General of chariots and cavalry Anshi served Emperor Xiaowu for more than thirty years, loyal, trustworthy, careful, and sincere, diligent in government affairs, early and late without slackening; with the grand general he settled the succession, and the realm received its blessing.
