He is a weighty minister of the state and should have his rank exalted to grand general, and should not be made to continue leading the affairs of superintendent of the masters of writing, so that he may devote his spirit, worry over the realm, and reflect on gains and losses.

entries.zh: 安世子延壽重厚，可以為光祿勳，領宿衛臣。」
entries.en: Anshi's son Zhang Yanshou is grave and sincere and may serve as superintendent of the masters of writing, leading the palace guard ministers."
entries.literal: Anshi's son Yanshou is grave and sincere and may serve as superintendent of the masters of writing, leading the palace guard ministers."

entries.zh: 上亦欲用之。
entries.en: The emperor was inclined to follow this plan.
entries.literal: The emperor also wished to employ him thus.

entries.zh: 安世聞指，懼不敢當。
entries.en: When Anshi heard what was intended, he was afraid and did not dare accept.
entries.literal: Anshi heard the drift of it, was afraid, and did not dare accept.

entries.zh: 請聞求見，免冠頓首曰：「老臣耳妄聞，言之為先事，不言情不達，誠自量不足以居大位，繼大將軍後，唯天子財哀，以全老臣之命。」
entries.en: He asked leave to see the emperor, removed his cap, and kowtowed, saying, "This old minister has only overheard rumors. I must speak before events overtake us; if I stay silent my meaning will not be understood. I truly know myself unfit for so great a post after the grand general. May Your Majesty alone show mercy and spare this old minister's life."
entries.literal: He requested permission to seek an audience, removed his cap, and knocked his head on the ground, saying, "This old minister has only rashly heard rumors. To speak is to anticipate events; if I do not speak, feeling cannot be conveyed. I truly measure myself and find I am not sufficient to occupy the great post and succeed after the grand general. May the Son of Heaven alone show mercy and preserve this old minister's life."

entries.zh: 上笑曰：「君言泰謙。
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, "You are far too modest.
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Your words are excessively modest.

entries.zh: 君而不可，尚誰可者！」
entries.en: If you are not fit, then who could be!"
entries.literal: If you are not fit, then who could be!"

entries.zh: 安世深辭弗能得。
entries.en: Anshi declined with all his strength but could not prevail.
entries.literal: Anshi declined deeply but could not succeed.

entries.zh: 後數日，竟拜為大司馬車騎將軍，領尚書事。
entries.en: A few days later he was appointed grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry with charge over the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Several days later, he was at last appointed grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry, directing the affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 數月，罷車騎將軍屯兵，更為衛將軍，兩宮衛尉，城門、北軍兵屬焉。
entries.en: A few months later his field command was abolished and he was made general of the guard, with the two palace guard commandants, the gate guards, and the northern army all placed under him.
entries.literal: Several months later, the garrison troops of the general of chariots and cavalry were abolished; he was changed to general of the guard, and the two palace guard commandants, the gate guards, and the northern army all came under his authority.

entries.zh: 始，長史硃買臣素怨湯，語在其傳。
entries.en: Chief Clerk Zhu Maichen had nursed a grudge against Tang for years—the story is told in his own chapter.
entries.literal: At first Chief Clerk Zhu Maichen had long resented Tang—the words are in his biography.

entries.zh: 王朝，齊人，以術至右內史。
entries.en: Wang Chao of Qi had risen to right metropolitan superintendent through his technical expertise.
entries.literal: Wang Chao, a man of Qi, by arts reached right metropolitan superintendent.

entries.zh: 邊通學短長，剛暴人也。
entries.en: Bian Tong was a specialist in the "short and long" school of persuasion—abrasive, violent-tempered.
entries.literal: Bian Tong studied short and long; he was a violent fierce man.

entries.zh: 官至濟南相。
entries.en: He had served as chancellor of the kingdom of Jinan.
entries.literal: Official rank reached Jinan chancellor.

entries.zh: 故皆居湯右，已而失官，守長史，詘體於湯。
entries.en: All three had once outranked Tang; later they were stripped of their posts and ended up as chief clerks under him, forced to humble themselves.
entries.literal: Therefore all had been to Tang's right; afterward they lost office, guarded as chief clerks, and bent their bodies before Tang.

entries.zh: 湯數行丞相事，知此三長史素貴，常陵折之。
entries.en: Whenever Tang acted for the chancellor, he knew how exalted these three had been and took every chance to humiliate them.
entries.literal: Tang repeatedly acted chancellor affairs, knew these three chief clerks had been noble, and always humiliated and broke them.

entries.zh: 故三長史合謀曰：「始湯約與君謝，已而賣君；
entries.en: The three chief clerks put their heads together. "At first Zhang Tang pledged to apologize with you," they said, "then he betrayed you;
entries.literal: Therefore the three chief clerks conspired and said, "At first Tang agreed with you, sir, to apologize together, afterward selling you;

entries.zh: 今欲劾君以宗廟事，此欲代君耳。
entries.en: now he means to impeach you over the desecration of the imperial tombs because he wants your seat;
entries.literal: Now he wishes to impeach you, sir, on the ancestral temple affair—this is because he wishes to replace you, sir.

entries.zh: 吾知湯陰事。」
entries.en: and we know the dirty secrets he is hiding."
entries.literal: We know Tang's secret affairs."

entries.zh: 使吏捕案湯左田信等，曰湯且欲為請奏，信輒先知之，居物致富，與湯分之。
entries.en: They had agents seize Tang's confederate Tian Xin, charging that whenever Tang was about to memorialize a ruling, Xin learned of it in advance, cornered goods, grew rich, and split the profits with Tang.
entries.literal: He had clerks arrest and investigate Tang's confidant Tian Xin and others, saying Tang was about to memorialize for approval, Xin always knew beforehand, hoarded goods and grew rich, and divided with Tang.

entries.zh: 及它奸事。
entries.en: They added further counts of misconduct.
entries.literal: And other wicked affairs.

entries.zh: 事辭頗聞。
entries.en: Word of the accusations began to reach the throne.
entries.literal: The affair's words were somewhat heard.

entries.zh: 上問湯曰：「吾所為，賈人輒知，益居其物，是類有以吾謀告之者。」
entries.en: The emperor asked Tang, "Whatever policy I mean to adopt, the merchants seem to know it in advance and stockpile accordingly. Someone must be leaking my deliberations."
entries.literal: The ruler asked Tang, saying, "What I do, merchants always know and increase hoarding their goods—is there someone of this kind who tells them my plans?"

entries.zh: 湯不謝，又陽驚曰：「固宜有。」
entries.en: Tang offered no denial and again feigned surprise: "No doubt there is."
entries.literal: Tang did not apologize, and again feigned surprise and said, "Indeed there ought to be."

entries.zh: 減宜亦奏謁居事。
entries.en: Jian Xuan weighed in with his own memorial on the Yéju business.
entries.literal: Jian Xuan also memorialized the Yéju affair.

entries.zh: 上以湯懷詐面欺，使使八輩簿責湯。
entries.en: Convinced that Tang had lied to his face, the emperor dispatched eight successive envoys to cross-examine him from the written record.
entries.literal: The ruler thought Tang harbored deceit and had deceived him to his face, and sent envoys in eight rounds to register-blame Tang.

entries.zh: 湯具自道無此，不服。
entries.en: Tang insisted he was innocent and refused to confess.
entries.literal: Tang fully himself said there was not this and did not submit.

entries.zh: 於是上使趙禹責湯。
entries.en: The emperor then sent Zhao Yu to confront him.
entries.literal: Thereupon the ruler sent Zhao Yu to blame Tang.

entries.zh: 禹至，讓湯曰：「君何不知分也！
entries.en: When Zhao Yu arrived, he rebuked Tang. "Have you no sense of proportion?
entries.literal: When Yu arrived, he reproached Tang, saying, "Sir, how do you not know your lot!

entries.zh: 君所治，夷滅者幾何人矣！
entries.en: Think how many families you have destroyed in the cases you have tried!
entries.literal: What you have handled—how many people have been exterminated and extinguished!

entries.zh: 今人言君皆有狀，天子重致君獄，欲令君自為計，何多以對為？」
entries.en: Every charge against you now carries weight. His Majesty is moving to commit you to prison so you may settle your own affairs—why prolong the interrogation with endless denials?"
entries.literal: Now men who speak of you all have substance; the Son of Heaven gravely sends you to prison, wishing to make you, sir, devise your own course—why multiply answers?"

entries.zh: 湯乃為書謝曰：「湯無尺寸之功，起刀筆吏，陛下幸致位三公，無以塞責。
entries.en: Tang then drafted a memorial of apology: "I began as a mere scribal clerk and owe my rise to the three highest offices entirely to Your Majesty's favor—yet I have failed in my responsibility.
entries.literal: Tang thereupon made a document apologizing, saying, "Tang has not an inch of merit; he rose from knife-and-brush clerk; Your Majesty graciously raised him to the three dukes—there is no way to answer for his duty.

entries.zh: 然謀陷湯者，三長史也。」
entries.en: Those who schemed to bring me down are the three chief clerks of the chancellor's office."
entries.literal: Yet those who plotted to trap Tang are the three chief clerks."

entries.zh: 遂自殺。
entries.en: He then took his own life.
entries.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.

entries.zh: 湯死，家產直不過五百金，皆所得奉賜，無它贏。
entries.en: At his death his estate amounted to no more than five hundred catties of gold, every ounce of it from official salary and imperial gifts—nothing ill-gotten.
entries.literal: When Tang died, his household property was worth no more than five hundred catties of gold, all from salaries and gifts received, no other surplus.

entries.zh: 昆弟諸子欲厚葬湯，湯母曰：「湯為天子大臣，被惡言而死，何厚葬為！」
entries.en: His brothers and sons wanted an elaborate funeral. His mother said, "He was a chief minister of the throne and died under a cloud of slander—what good would pomp do?"
entries.literal: Brothers and various sons wished to bury Tang richly; Tang's mother said, "Tang was a great minister of the Son of Heaven; he died bearing evil words—what is rich burial for!"

entries.zh: 載以牛車，有棺而無槨。
entries.en: He was taken to the grave on an ox cart, in a plain inner coffin with no outer shell.
entries.literal: They carried him on an ox cart, having a coffin but no outer coffin.

entries.zh: 上聞之，曰：「非此母不生此子。」
entries.en: When the emperor heard, he remarked, "Only such a mother could have raised such a son."
entries.literal: The ruler heard it and said, "Were it not for this mother, such a son would not have been born."

entries.zh: 乃盡按誅三長史。
entries.en: He then had all three chief clerks arrested, tried, and executed.
entries.literal: Thereupon he fully investigated and executed the three chief clerks.

entries.zh: 丞相青翟自殺。
entries.en: Chancellor Zhuang Qingzhai committed suicide.
entries.literal: Chancellor Qingzhai killed himself.

entries.zh: 出田信。
entries.en: Tian Xin was cleared and released.
entries.literal: Released Tian Xin.

entries.zh: 上惜湯，復稍進其子安世。
entries.en: The emperor still regretted Tang's fate and began again to advance his son Zhang Anshi.
entries.literal: The ruler pitied Tang and again gradually promoted his son Anshi.

entries.zh: 鴻嘉中，上欲遵武帝故事，與近臣游宴，放以公主子開敏得幸。
entries.en: During the Hongjia era Emperor Cheng wished to revive Emperor Wu's habit of informal outings and banquets with his inner circle. Zhang Fang, as the princess's son—quick-witted and polished—won exceptional favor.
entries.literal: In the Hongjia years, the ruler wished to follow Emperor Wu's precedents and with near ministers roam and feast; Fang by being the princess's son open and clever obtained favor.

entries.zh: 放取皇后弟平恩侯許嘉女，上為放供張，賜甲第，充以乘輿服飾，號為天子取婦，皇后嫁女。
entries.en: Zhang Fang married the daughter of Xu Jia, the Marquis of Ping'en and younger brother of the empress. The emperor staged the wedding himself, granted a mansion of the first rank, and filled it with wardrobe and ornaments from the imperial workshops, so that courtiers quipped it was as if the Son of Heaven had taken a bride and the empress had given her daughter away.
entries.literal: Fang took the daughter of the empress's younger brother Marquis of Ping'en Xu Jia; the ruler for Fang supplied furnishings, granted a first-ranked mansion, filled it with imperial carriage robes and ornaments, calling it the Son of Heaven taking a wife and the empress marrying a daughter.

entries.zh: 大官私官並供其第，兩宮使者冠蓋不絕，賞賜以千萬數。
entries.en: The palace stewards of both households provisioned the estate without stint; couriers from the two palaces arrived in an unbroken stream of carriages; gifts ran into the tens of millions of cash.
entries.literal: Great Steward and Private Steward together supplied his mansion; two palaces' envoys caps and covers unbroken; gifts and grants in the tens of millions.

entries.zh: 放為侍中、中郎將，監平樂屯兵，置莫府，儀比將軍。
entries.en: Zhang Fang held concurrent rank as palace attendant and general of the household gentlemen, commanded the encamped troops at Pingyue, maintained a full staff, and enjoyed ceremonial honors equal to a field general.
entries.literal: Fang was palace attendant and general of the household gentlemen, supervised the Pingyue garrison, set up headquarters, ceremony comparable to a general.

entries.zh: 與上臥起，寵愛殊絕，常從為微行出遊，北至甘泉，南至長楊、五莋，鬥雞走馬長安中，積數年。
entries.en: He attended the emperor waking and sleeping and stood alone in favor. He was the constant companion on disguised excursions—north to Ganquan, south to the hunting parks of Changyang and Wuzuo, cockfighting and racing horses through the streets of Chang'an—for years on end.
entries.literal: With the ruler he slept and rose; favor and love were uniquely extreme; he always followed on incognito outings, north to Ganquan, south to Changyang and Wuzuo, cockfighting and horse racing in Chang'an—accumulated several years.

entries.zh: 是時，上方鄉文學，湯決大獄，欲傅古義，乃請博士弟子治《尚書》、《春秋》，補廷尉史，平亭疑法。
entries.en: The emperor was then turning toward Confucian scholarship. When Tang tried major cases he liked to cloak his rulings in classical precedent, so he asked the court academicians to assign disciples trained in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn to serve as clerks in his office and help iron out disputed interpretations of the law.
entries.literal: At this time the emperor was inclining toward literary learning; Tang decided great cases and wished to attach ancient meanings, and therefore requested students of the erudits versed in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn to supplement as clerks of the commandant of justice and settle doubtful points of law.

entries.zh: 奏讞疑，必奏先為上分別其原，上所是，受而著讞法廷尉挈令，揚主之明。
entries.en: Whenever he submitted a doubtful case for decision, he first laid out the legal reasoning on both sides for the throne. Whatever the emperor endorsed, he incorporated into the commandant's codified precedents, giving full credit to the sovereign's discernment.
entries.literal: When memorializing doubtful judgments, he always first memorialized to distinguish the origins for the ruler; what the ruler approved, he received and set down as precedent in the commandant's binding rules, displaying the ruler's brilliance.

entries.zh: 奏事即譴，湯摧謝，鄉上意所便，必引正監掾史賢者，曰：「固為臣議，如上責臣，臣弗用，愚抵此。」
entries.en: If the emperor faulted a memorial as soon as it was presented, Tang at once withdrew it with an apology and bent to the sovereign's wishes. He would then name some worthy among his supervisors or clerks and say, "These men urged that course on me; when Your Majesty censures me, it is because I was too dull to follow their advice."
entries.literal: When on submitting a matter he was immediately rebuked, Tang yielded and apologized, inclining toward what suited the ruler's mind, and always cited the upright supervisor and clerk worthies, saying, "They certainly deliberated for your servant; as your Majesty blames your servant, your servant failed to adopt it—stupidity brought me to this."

entries.zh: 罪常釋。
entries.en: The blame thus rarely stuck to him.
entries.literal: The fault was always released.

entries.zh: 間即奏事，上善之，曰：「臣非知為此奏，乃監、掾、史某所為。」
entries.en: When a proposal won praise, he would say, "I cannot claim credit for that memorial—it was drafted by such-and-such a supervisor or clerk."
entries.literal: Sometimes when he submitted a matter and the ruler praised it, he said, "Your servant did not know to make this memorial—it was done by supervisor and clerk so-and-so."

entries.zh: 其欲薦吏，揚人之善、解人之過如此。
entries.en: That was how he promoted subordinates: he broadcast their merits and glossed over their lapses.
entries.literal: In wishing to recommend clerks, he thus praised people's good points and excused people's faults.

entries.zh: 所治即上意所欲罪，予監吏深刻者；
entries.en: If the emperor wanted a man ruined, Tang handed the file to a clerk known for pitiless severity.
entries.literal: In what he handled, if it was what the ruler's mind wished to condemn, he gave it to a supervisor clerk who was harsh and deep;

entries.zh: 即上意所欲釋，予監吏輕平者。
entries.en: If the emperor wished someone spared, he assigned the case to a clerk with a reputation for leniency and even-handedness.
entries.literal: If it was what the ruler's mind wished to release, he gave it to a supervisor clerk who was lenient and even.

entries.zh: 所治即豪，必舞文巧詆；
entries.en: Against powerful families he would twist the statute book and frame charges with malicious ingenuity.
entries.literal: In what he handled, if it was a powerful house, he always twisted the text and craftily slandered;

entries.zh: 即下戶羸弱，時口言「雖文致法，上裁察。」
entries.en: Against humble, defenseless commoners he would sometimes remark aloud, "The letter of the law may condemn him, but let His Majesty weigh the matter."
entries.literal: If it was a low household, weak and feeble, he sometimes orally said, "Although the text reaches the law, let the ruler examine and decide."

entries.zh: 於是往往釋湯所言。
entries.en: Time and again the court accepted Tang's wording and let the accused go.
entries.literal: Thereupon often what Tang said was released.

entries.zh: 湯至於大吏，內行修，交通賓客飲食，於故人子弟為吏及貧昆弟，調護之尤厚，其造請諸公，不避寒暑。
entries.en: Though he had risen to high office, he kept up scrupulous private conduct, entertained a wide circle, and looked after the sons of old friends who held petty posts and his own indigent kinsmen with exceptional generosity. He called on the great ministers in person, whatever the season.
entries.literal: Tang, reaching great clerk, cultivated inner conduct, associated with guests for drink and food, and toward old friends' sons who were clerks and poor brothers, regulated and protected them especially thickly; in visiting the great lords he did not avoid cold or heat.

entries.zh: 是以湯雖文深意忌不專平，然得此聲譽。
entries.en: So despite legal harshness and a jealous temperament—far from even-handed—he enjoyed a reputation for benevolence.
entries.literal: Therefore, although Tang's legal wording was harsh and his mind jealous and he was not solely even-handed, yet he obtained this reputation.

entries.zh: 而深刻吏多為爪牙用者，依於文學之士。
entries.en: The ruthless clerks who served as his enforcers likewise wrapped themselves in the language of the classics.
entries.literal: And the many harsh deep clerks who were used as claws and fangs relied on men of literary learning.

entries.zh: 丞相弘數稱其美。
entries.en: Chancellor Gongsun Hong often spoke of him in glowing terms.
entries.literal: Chancellor Gongsun Hong repeatedly praised his excellence.

entries.zh: 及治淮南、衡山、江都反獄，皆窮根本。
entries.en: In the treason trials of Huainan, Hengshan, and Jiangdu he pursued every lead to the bottom.
entries.literal: When he handled the rebellion cases of Huainan, Hengshan, and Jiangdu, all were exhausted to the root.

entries.zh: 嚴助、伍被，上欲釋之，湯爭曰：「伍被本造反謀，而助親幸出入禁闥，腹心之臣，乃交私諸侯如此，弗誅，後不可治。」
entries.en: The emperor wanted to pardon Yan Zhu and Wu Bei. Tang objected: "Wu Bei helped lay the plot from the beginning, and Yan Zhu enjoyed intimate access to the inner apartments—he was a minister of the ruler's inmost counsels—yet he secretly conspired with the kings. If they are not put to death, the law will never again command respect."
entries.literal: Yan Zhu and Wu Bei—the ruler wished to release them; Tang contended, saying, "Wu Bei at root plotted rebellion, and Zhu, personally favored, going in and out of the inner palace, a heart-and-belly minister, yet privately associated with the feudal lords like this—if not executed, later cannot be governed."

entries.zh: 上可論之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his argument and condemned them.
entries.literal: The ruler approved the judgment.

entries.zh: 其治獄所巧排大臣自以為功，多此類。
entries.en: His habit of outmaneuvering senior ministers and claiming the credit in such trials was typical of his style.
entries.literal: In handling cases, the clever way he displaced great ministers, taking credit for himself, was mostly of this kind.

entries.zh: 繇是益尊任，遷御史大夫。
entries.en: He was therefore trusted more heavily and promoted to imperial counselor.
entries.literal: From this he was increasingly honored and employed, and promoted to imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 匈奴求和親，群臣議前，博士狄山曰：「和親便。」
entries.en: The Xiongnu sued for a marriage alliance. At the council before the throne, Academician Di Shan said, "An alliance by marriage is the prudent course."
entries.literal: The Xiongnu sought peace and kinship; the various ministers deliberated before the court; Erudite Di Shan said, "Peace and kinship is convenient."

entries.zh: 上問其便，山曰：「兵，凶器，未易數動。
entries.en: The emperor asked why. Shan replied, "Arms are unlucky instruments; they should not be lightly wielded again and again.
entries.literal: The ruler asked wherein lay the convenience; Shan said, "Weapons are ill-omened tools; it is not easy to move them repeatedly.

entries.zh: 高帝欲伐匈奴，大困平城，乃遂結和親。
entries.en: Gaozu tried to strike the Xiongnu and was trapped in desperate straits at Pingcheng; after that he settled for peace through intermarriage.
entries.literal: The High Emperor wished to attack the Xiongnu, was greatly distressed at Pingcheng, and thereupon concluded peace and kinship.

entries.zh: 孝惠、高后時，天下安樂，及文帝欲事匈奴，北邊蕭然苦兵。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui and Empress Lü the realm knew quiet prosperity. When Emperor Wen turned against the Xiongnu, the northern frontier knew nothing but the miseries of war.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, the empire was peaceful and happy; when Emperor Wen wished to serve the Xiongnu, the northern border was desolate and bitter with soldiers.

entries.zh: 孝景時，吳、楚七國反，景帝往來東宮間，天下寒心數月。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in revolt; the emperor shuttled between the two palace complexes while the whole country held its breath for months on end.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaojing, Wu and Chu and the seven states rebelled; Emperor Jing went back and forth between the eastern palaces; the empire was cold in heart for months.

entries.zh: 吳、楚已破，竟景帝不言兵，天下富實。
entries.en: After Wu and Chu were crushed, Jing never again spoke of major campaigns, and the realm grew wealthy and secure.
entries.literal: Wu and Chu already broken, to the end of Emperor Jing he did not speak of soldiers; the empire was rich and solid.

entries.zh: 今自陛下興兵擊匈奴，中國以空虛，邊大困貧。
entries.en: Since Your Majesty took the field against the Xiongnu, the interior has been drained and the frontier left exhausted and destitute.
entries.literal: Now from Your Majesty raising troops to strike the Xiongnu, the central states thereby are empty; the border is greatly distressed and poor.

entries.zh: 由是觀之，不如和親。」
entries.en: Judged by that record, an alliance is still the better policy."
entries.literal: From this viewing it, it is not as good as peace and kinship."

entries.zh: 上問湯，湯曰：「此愚儒無知。」
entries.en: The emperor turned to Tang, who said, "That is the talk of a pedantic scholar who understands nothing."
entries.literal: The ruler asked Tang; Tang said, "This is a foolish Ru who knows nothing."

entries.zh: 狄山曰：「臣固愚忠，若御史大夫湯，乃詐忠。
entries.en: Di Shan retorted, "I may be a simple loyalist, but Imperial Counselor Zhang Tang is loyal only in pretense.
entries.literal: Di Shan said, "Your servant is indeed foolishly loyal; as for Imperial Counselor Tang, he is feignedly loyal.

entries.zh: 湯之治淮南、江都，以深文痛詆諸侯，別疏骨肉，使籓臣不自安，臣固知湯之詐忠。」
entries.en: In the Huainan and Jiangdu trials he stretched the law to vilify the kings, pitting kin against kin until no prince felt safe at his post. That is the loyalty I call false."
entries.literal: Tang's handling of Huainan and Jiangdu, with deep text painfully slandering the feudal lords, separating and estranging bone and flesh, caused border ministers not to be secure in themselves—your servant indeed knows Tang's feigned loyalty."

entries.zh: 於是上作色曰：「吾使生居一郡，能無使虜入盜乎？」
entries.en: The emperor's face darkened. "I give you one commandery," he said. "Could you keep the raiders out?"
entries.literal: Thereupon the ruler changed color and said, "I send you, sir, to dwell in one commandery—can you prevent the barbarians from entering and stealing?"

entries.zh: 山曰：「不能。」
entries.en: "No," said Shan.
entries.literal: Shan said, "I cannot."

entries.zh: 曰：「居一縣？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "What about one county?"
entries.literal: The ruler said, "Dwell in one county?"

entries.zh: 曰：「不能。」
entries.en: Shan said, "I could not."
entries.literal: Shan said, "I cannot."

entries.zh: 復曰：「居一鄣間？」
entries.en: Again the emperor said, "Very well—one fortified barrier sector along the wall?"
entries.literal: Again the ruler said, "Dwell within one barrier interval?"

entries.zh: 山自度辯窮且下吏，曰：「能。」
entries.en: Shan saw he had argued himself into a corner and would soon be handed over to the law; he answered, "I could."
entries.literal: Shan himself reckoned his argument exhausted and about to go down to clerks, and said, "I can."

entries.zh: 乃譴山乘鄣。
entries.en: The emperor promptly sent him to hold a signal tower on the frontier.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent Shan to ride the barrier.

entries.zh: 至月餘，匈奴斬山頭而去。
entries.en: A little over a month later the Xiongnu rode up and took his head.
entries.literal: After more than a month, the Xiongnu cut off Shan's head and left.

entries.zh: 是後群臣震讋。
entries.en: After that the ministers were all shaken with fear.
entries.literal: After this the various ministers were shaken and fearful.

entries.zh: 河東人李文，故嘗與湯有隙，已而為御史中丞，薦數從中文事有可以傷湯者，不能為地。
entries.en: Li Wen of Hedong had long been Tang's enemy. When Wen became vice director of the imperial secretariat, he combed the palace files for anything that might incriminate Tang and showed him no quarter.
entries.literal: Li Wen of Hedong had formerly had a rift with Tang; afterward he became vice director of the secretariat and repeatedly from central documents had matters that could injure Tang; he could not make room.

entries.zh: 湯有所愛史魯謁居，知湯弗平，使人上飛變告文奸事，事下湯，湯治論殺文，而湯心知謁居為之。
entries.en: Tang kept a favorite clerk, Lu Yéju, who saw how Tang brooded on the grudge. Yéju arranged for a sealed denunciation accusing Wen of misconduct; when the case landed in Tang's hands, he tried Wen and had him executed, all the while knowing Yéju was the author of the charge.
entries.literal: Tang had a favored clerk Lu Yéju; knowing Tang was not reconciled, he had someone submit a flying denunciation reporting Wen's wicked affairs; the matter went down to Tang; Tang handled it and judged and killed Wen, while Tang inwardly knew Yéju had done it.

entries.zh: 上問：「變事從跡安起？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Who is behind this anonymous accusation?"
entries.literal: The ruler asked, "Whence arose the traces of the denunciation affair?"

entries.zh: 湯陽驚曰：「此殆文故人怨之。」
entries.en: Tang put on a show of surprise. "Probably one of Wen's old acquaintances with a grudge against him," he said.
entries.literal: Tang feigned surprise and said, "This is probably an old friend of Wen who resents him."

entries.zh: 謁居病臥閭里主人，湯自往視病，為謁居摩足，趙國以冶鑄為業，王數訟鐵官事，湯常排趙王。
entries.en: When Yéju fell ill and lodged with a neighbor, Tang visited him in person and massaged his feet. The kingdom of Zhao lived by its foundries; its king repeatedly sued the monopoly officials, and Tang as a rule ruled against the king.
entries.literal: Yéju was ill and lay at his ward host's; Tang in person went to look at the illness and for Yéju rubbed feet; Zhao state took smelting founding as occupation; the king repeatedly sued iron office affairs; Tang often displaced the King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 趙王求湯陰事。
entries.en: The King of Zhao set out to dig up dirt on Tang.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao sought Tang's secret affairs.

entries.zh: 謁居嘗案趙王，趙王怨之，並上書告：「湯大臣也，史謁居有病，湯至為摩足，疑與為大奸。」
entries.en: Yéju had once prosecuted the king, who nursed a grudge. The king now sent up a joint memorial: "Zhang Tang is a chief minister; when his clerk Yéju fell ill, Tang actually massaged the man's feet—clear evidence of some monstrous conspiracy between them."
entries.literal: Yéju had once investigated the King of Zhao; the king resented him, and together submitted a memorial reporting, "Tang is a great minister; clerk Yéju was ill, yet Tang went so far as to rub his feet—suspicion is that together they commit great wickedness."

entries.zh: 事下廷尉。
entries.en: The case was referred to the commandant of justice.
entries.literal: The matter went down to the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 謁居病死，事連其弟，弟繫導官。
entries.en: Yéju died before trial, but the investigation ensnared his younger brother, who was locked up in the guide office prison.
entries.literal: Yéju died of illness; the affair connected his younger brother; the younger brother was imprisoned at the guide office.

entries.zh: 湯亦治它囚導官，見謁居弟，欲陰為之，而陽不省。
entries.en: Tang happened to be interrogating other inmates there. When he saw Yéju's brother, he meant to help him quietly while pretending not to notice him.
entries.literal: Tang also handled other prisoners at the guide office; seeing Yéju's younger brother, he wished secretly to favor him, but outwardly feigned not to recognize.

entries.zh: 謁居弟不知而怨湯，使人上書，告湯與謁居謀，共變李文。
entries.en: The brother did not understand and blamed Tang; he had someone memorialize that Tang and Yéju had conspired to frame Li Wen.
entries.literal: Yéju's younger brother did not know and resented Tang, and had someone submit a memorial reporting that Tang and Yéju plotted together and jointly submitted a sealed denunciation against Li Wen.

entries.zh: 事下減宣。
entries.en: The case was assigned to Jian Xuan.
entries.literal: The matter went down to Jian Xuan.

entries.zh: 宣嘗與湯有隙，及得此事，窮竟其事，未奏也。
entries.en: Xuan had old scores with Tang; he seized the chance to investigate to the limit, though he had not yet reported his findings.
entries.literal: Xuan had once had a rift with Tang; when he obtained this affair, he pursued it to the utmost; he had not yet memorialized.

entries.zh: 會人有盜發孝文園瘞錢，丞相青翟朝，與湯約俱謝，至前，湯念獨丞相以四時行園，當謝，湯無與也，不謝。
entries.en: Then robbers broke into the burial mound in Emperor Wen's mausoleum park and stole the consecrated coins. At court Chancellor Zhuang Qingzhai agreed with Tang that they would both apologize. When they came before the throne, Tang reflected that only the chancellor made the seasonal rounds of the shrines and therefore bore responsibility; he himself had nothing to do with it, so he offered no apology.
entries.literal: It happened that someone dug up and stole the buried cash of Emperor Xiaowen's park; Chancellor Qingzhai at court, with Tang agreed together to apologize; arriving before the ruler, Tang thought only the chancellor by the four seasons went to the park and ought to apologize; Tang had no part in it and did not apologize.

entries.zh: 丞相謝，上使御史案其事。
entries.en: The chancellor apologized alone, and the emperor ordered the censorate to look into the matter.
entries.literal: The chancellor apologized; the ruler ordered the censor to investigate the affair.

entries.zh: 湯欲致其文丞相見知，丞相患之。
entries.en: Tang meant to shape the documentary evidence so as to implicate the chancellor in prior knowledge; the chancellor grew alarmed.
entries.literal: Tang wished to bring his documents so the chancellor would be shown to know; the chancellor worried.

entries.zh: 三長史皆害湯，欲陷之。
entries.en: The three chief clerks of the chancellor's office hated Tang and conspired to destroy him.
entries.literal: The three chief clerks all harmed Tang and wished to trap him.

entries.zh: 時，霍光子禹為右將軍，上亦以禹為大司馬，罷其右將軍屯兵，以虛尊加之，而實奪其眾。
entries.en: At that time Huo Guang's son Huo Yu held the post of general of the right while also bearing the title of grand marshal. The emperor stripped him of his field command, leaving the grand marshal's title a hollow honor while removing his real military following.
entries.literal: At this time Huo Guang's son Yu was general of the right; the ruler also made Yu grand marshal, abolished his right general garrison troops, applied empty honor to him, and in reality stripped his hosts.

entries.zh: 後歲餘，禹謀反，夷宗族，安世素小心畏忌，已內憂矣。
entries.en: A little over a year later Huo Yu rose in rebellion and his entire clan was wiped out. Anshi, who had always been cautious and easily alarmed, was already anxious at heart.
entries.literal: After more than a year, Yu plotted rebellion; the clan was exterminated; Anshi had always been careful and fearful—already he was inwardly worried.

entries.zh: 其女孫敬為霍氏外屬婦，當相坐，安世瘦懼，形於顏色，上怪而憐之，以問左右，乃赦敬，以尉其意。
entries.en: His granddaughter Zhang Jing had married into a Huo-affiliated family and stood liable to collective punishment. Anshi grew haggard with dread, and it showed on his face. The emperor noticed, took pity, asked his attendants for the story, and pardoned Jing to set his mind at ease.
entries.literal: His granddaughter Jing was wife of a collateral of the Huo clan and ought to suffer connected guilt; Anshi was emaciated with fear, showing in face color; the ruler wondered and pitied him, asked those at his side, and thereupon pardoned Jing, in order to comfort his mind.

entries.zh: 安世浸恐。
entries.en: His fear only deepened.
entries.literal: Anshi gradually was more fearful.

entries.zh: 職典樞機，以謹慎周密自著，外內無間。
entries.en: He held the levers of confidential policy, winning a reputation for meticulous care. Not a whisper of what passed in the inner palace reached the outer court through him, nor vice versa.
entries.literal: He held office governing the pivot machinery, and by careful cautious thoroughness made himself known; outside and inside there was no gap.

entries.zh: 每定大政，已決，輒移病出；
entries.en: Whenever a major decision had been taken, he would plead illness and withdraw;
entries.literal: Each time a great policy was settled, already decided, he always shifted illness and went out;

entries.zh: 聞有詔令，乃驚，使吏之丞相府問焉。
entries.en: and if he then heard that an edict had been issued, he would start in alarm and dispatch a clerk to the chancellor's office to learn what it said.
entries.literal: hearing there was an edict order, then was startled, and sent a clerk to the chancellor's office to ask.

entries.zh: 自朝廷大臣莫知其與議也。
entries.en: Even senior ministers at court had no idea that he had been in on the discussion.
entries.literal: From the court great ministers none knew his participation in deliberation.

entries.zh: 安世自見父子尊顯，懷不自安，為子延壽求出補吏，上以為北地太守。
entries.en: Seeing how exalted he and his son had become, Anshi grew uneasy. He asked that his son Yanshou be given a provincial post, and the emperor appointed Yanshou governor of Beidi.
entries.literal: Anshi himself seeing father and son honored and prominent, harbored unease in himself, and for his son Yanshou sought to go out and fill a clerk post; the ruler made him governor of Beidi.

entries.zh: 歲餘，上閔安世年老，復徵延壽為左曹、太僕。
entries.en: A year later, pitying Anshi's age, the emperor recalled Yanshou to court as left aide in the secretariat and chamberlain for the imperial stud.
entries.literal: After more than a year, the ruler pitied Anshi's old age and again summoned Yanshou as left aide and chamberlain for the imperial stud.

entries.zh: 初，安世兄賀幸於衛太子，太子敗，賓客皆誅，安世為賀上書，得下蠶室。
entries.en: At first Anshi's elder brother Zhang He had been favored by Crown Prince Liu Ju of Wei. When the prince fell, all his clients were executed; Anshi memorialized on He's behalf and won reduction of the sentence to the silkworm chambers.
entries.literal: At first, Anshi's elder brother He was favored by the Heir Apparent of Wei; when the heir fell, all his clients were executed; Anshi submitted a memorial for He and obtained reduction to the silkworm chambers.

entries.zh: 後為掖庭令，而宣帝以皇曾孫收養掖庭。
entries.en: He later became director of the palace consorts quarters, where the future Emperor Xuan was reared as imperial great-grandson.
entries.literal: Later he became director of the palace consorts, and Emperor Xuan, as imperial great-grandson, was reared in the palace consorts quarters.

entries.zh: 賀內傷太子無辜，而曾孫孤幼，所以視養拊循，恩甚密焉。
entries.en: He grieved that the crown prince had been innocent while the great-grandson was orphaned and young, and so he watched over, reared, and comforted the boy with the closest affection.
entries.literal: He inwardly grieved that the crown prince was innocent, while the great-grandson was orphaned and young; therefore he watched over, reared, and comforted him, and their kindness was very close.

entries.zh: 及曾孫壯大，賀教書，令受《詩》，為取許妃，以家財聘之。
entries.en: When the boy grew up, He taught him letters, had him study the Odes, secured Lady Xu as his bride, and betrothed her with his own family wealth.
entries.literal: When the great-grandson grew up, He taught him letters, had him study the Odes, took Lady Xu for him, and betrothed her with his family wealth.

entries.zh: 曾孫數有徵怪，語在《宣紀》。
entries.en: The great-grandson several times experienced strange omens; the account is in the Annals of Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: The great-grandson several times had strange omens; the account is in "Annals of Emperor Xuan."

entries.zh: 賀聞知，為安世道之，稱其材美。
entries.en: When He heard of these omens, he told Anshi and praised the boy's talents.
entries.literal: He heard and knew of it, and for Anshi recounted it, praising his talent and excellence.

entries.zh: 安世輒絕止，以為少主在上，不宜稱述曾孫。
entries.en: Anshi always cut him short, holding that with the reigning young emperor above, it was improper to speak openly of the great-grandson.
entries.literal: Anshi always cut him off and stopped him, holding that with the young lord above, it was not fitting to speak of and recount the great-grandson.

entries.zh: 及宣帝即位，而賀已死。
entries.en: By the time Emperor Xuan came to the throne, He had already died.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, He was already dead.

entries.zh: 上謂安世曰：「掖廷令平生稱我，將軍止之，是也。」
entries.en: The emperor said to Anshi, "The director of the palace consorts quarters praised me all his life, and you stopped him—that was right."
entries.literal: The emperor said to Anshi, "The director of the palace consorts quarters praised me all his life; the general stopped him—that was right."

entries.zh: 上追思賀恩，欲封其塚為恩德侯，置家塚二百家。
entries.en: The emperor recalled He's kindness and wished to enfeoff his tomb as Marquis of Endeavor and Virtue with two hundred households to guard the family grave.
entries.literal: The emperor recalled He's kindness and wished to enfeoff his tomb as Marquis of Endeavor and Virtue and establish two hundred households to guard the family tomb.

entries.zh: 賀有一子蚤死，無子，子安世小男彭祖。
entries.en: He had one son who died young without issue, so he adopted Anshi's youngest son Pengzu.
entries.literal: He had one son who died young without issue; he adopted Anshi's youngest son Pengzu.

entries.zh: 彭祖又小與上同席研書，指欲封之，先賜爵關內侯。
entries.en: Pengzu had also studied at the same mat with the emperor in youth; the emperor meant to enfeoff him and first granted him the rank of marquis within the passes.
entries.literal: Pengzu had also been young and studied at the same mat with the emperor; the emperor indicated he wished to enfeoff him and first granted him the rank of marquis within the passes.

entries.zh: 故安世深辭賀封，又求損守塚戶數，稍減至三十戶。
entries.en: Anshi therefore declined the enfeoffment for He and asked to reduce the tomb-guard households, eventually cutting them to thirty.
entries.literal: Therefore Anshi deeply declined the enfeoffment for He and also requested to reduce the number of tomb-guard households, gradually cutting them to thirty households.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾自為掖廷令，非為將軍也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I do this for the director of the palace consorts quarters himself, not for you, General."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "I do this for the director of the palace consorts quarters myself, not for the general."

entries.zh: 安世乃止，不敢復言。
entries.en: Anshi then desisted and did not dare speak again.
entries.literal: Anshi then stopped and did not dare speak again.

entries.zh: 遂下詔曰：「其為故掖廷令張賀置守塚三十家。」
entries.en: An edict followed: "Let thirty households be established to guard the tomb of the former director of the palace consorts quarters, Zhang He."
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued saying, "Let thirty households be established to guard the tomb of the former director of the palace consorts quarters, Zhang He."

entries.zh: 上自處置其裡，居塚西鬥雞翁捨南，上少時所嘗游處也。
entries.en: The emperor himself arranged the ward south of the cockfighting elder's lodge west of the tomb—the place where he had wandered in youth.
entries.literal: The emperor himself arranged its ward; it lay south of the cockfighting elder's lodge west of the tomb—the place where the emperor in youth had once wandered.

entries.zh: 明年，復下詔曰：「朕微眇時，故掖廷令張賀輔道朕躬，修文學經術，恩惠卓異，厥功茂焉。
entries.en: The next year another edict declared: "When I was still insignificant, the former director of the palace consorts quarters Zhang He guided me, cultivated my literary and classical learning, and showed outstanding grace; his merit was abundant.
entries.literal: The next year another edict was issued: "When I was slight and insignificant, the former director of the palace consorts quarters Zhang He assisted and guided my person, cultivated literary learning and classical arts, and his grace was outstanding and extraordinary; his merit was abundant.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：『無言不仇，無德不報。』
entries.en: The Odes says, 'No words go without response; no virtue goes unrequited.'
entries.literal: The Odes says, 'No words go without response; no virtue goes unrequited.'

entries.zh: 其封賀弟子侍中關內侯彭祖為陽都侯，賜賀謚曰陽都哀侯。」
entries.en: Let Pengzu, He's adopted son, who is a palace attendant and marquis within the passes, be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangdu, and let He receive the posthumous title Marquis Ai of Yangdu."
entries.literal: Let He's adopted son, attendant of the interior and marquis within the passes Pengzu, be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangdu, and let He be granted the posthumous title Marquis Ai of Yangdu."

entries.zh: 時，賀有孤孫霸，年七歲，拜為散騎、中郎將，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。
entries.en: At that time He had an orphaned grandson, Ba, only seven years old, who was appointed attendant cavalier and general of the household gentlemen, granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and given a fief of three hundred households.
entries.literal: At that time He had an orphaned grandson Ba, seven years old, who was appointed attendant cavalier and general of the household gentlemen, granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and given a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 安世以父子封侯，在位大盛，乃辭祿。
entries.en: With father and son both enfeoffed and his power at its height, Anshi declined further salary.
entries.literal: Anshi, because father and son were enfeoffed as marquises and his office was at its greatest height, then declined salary.

entries.zh: 詔都內別臧張氏無名錢以百萬數。
entries.en: An edict ordered the imperial treasury to set aside millions in unmarked cash for the Zhang family.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the imperial treasury to set aside Zhang family unmarked cash in the millions.

entries.zh: 安世尊為公侯，食邑萬戶，然身衣弋綈，夫人自紡績，家童七百人，皆有手技作事，內治產業，累織纖微，是以能殖其貨，富於大將軍光。
entries.en: Though ennobled at the highest rank with a fief of ten thousand households, he dressed in plain black silk and his wife spun the household's cloth herself. Seven hundred retainers were each put to skilled manual labor. He micromanaged the family estates, pinching every cash, until his private wealth outstripped even Grand General Huo Guang's.
entries.literal: Anshi was honored as duke or marquis, with fief of ten thousand households, yet personally he wore coarse black silk; his wife herself spun and wove; household youths seven hundred persons all had handicraft work; inwardly he managed industry, accumulating stitch by stitch fine detail—thereby he was able to increase his goods, richer than Grand General Guang.

entries.zh: 天子甚尊憚大將軍，然內親安世，心密於光焉。
entries.en: The emperor treated Huo Guang with awe and kept him at a distance, but he was genuinely intimate with Anshi in a way he never was with Guang.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven greatly honored and feared the grand general, yet inwardly was close to Anshi, his heart more secret than toward Guang.

entries.zh: 元康四年春，安世病，上疏歸侯，乞骸骨。
entries.en: In spring of the fourth year of Yuankang, Anshi fell ill, submitted a memorial returning his marquisate, and begged to retire.
entries.literal: In spring of the fourth year of Yuankang, Anshi fell ill, submitted a memorial returning his marquisate, and begged to retire with his old bones.

entries.zh: 天子報曰：「將軍年老被病，朕甚閔之。
entries.en: The emperor replied, "General, you are old and ill; I am deeply concerned.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven replied, "The general is old and afflicted with illness; I greatly pity him.

entries.zh: 雖不能視事，折衝萬里，君先帝大臣，明於治亂，朕所不及，得數問焉，何感而上書歸衛將軍富平侯印？
entries.en: Though you cannot attend to affairs, you still repel enemies a myriad li away. You are a minister of the former emperor, clear-sighted in order and chaos beyond my reach; I may still consult you—why feel moved to return the seal of general of the guard and Marquis of Fuping?
entries.literal: Although you cannot attend to affairs, you repel enemies a myriad li away. You are a minister of the former emperor, clear about order and chaos, beyond what I can match; I may question you several times—why feel moved to submit a memorial returning the seal of General of the Guard and Marquis of Fuping?

entries.zh: 薄朕忘故，非所望也！
entries.en: You slight me as forgetting old ties—that is not what I wish!
entries.literal: You slight me as forgetting old ties; that is not what I hope for!

entries.zh: 願將軍強餐食，近醫藥，專精神，以輔天年。」
entries.en: Eat well, keep to your medicines, devote your spirit, and thereby prolong your allotted years."
entries.literal: I wish the general to force himself to eat, keep close to medicine, devote his spirit, and thereby assist his allotted years."

entries.zh: 安世復強起視事，至秋薨。
entries.en: Anshi forced himself to resume office, but by autumn he died.
entries.literal: Anshi again forced himself to rise and attend to affairs, and by autumn he died.

entries.zh: 天子贈印綬，送以輕車介士，謚曰敬侯。
entries.en: The emperor presented seals and ribbons, sent light carriages and armored soldiers as escort, and granted the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven presented seals and ribbons, sent light carriages and armored soldiers as escort, and granted the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

entries.zh: 賜塋杜東，將作穿復土，起塚祠堂。
entries.en: He was granted a grave mound east of Du; the director of palace construction raised the tomb and ancestral shrine.
entries.literal: He was granted a grave mound east of Du; the director of palace construction dug and returned the earth and raised tomb and ancestral shrine.

entries.zh: 子延壽嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhang Yanshou succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Yanshou succeeded.

entries.zh: 延壽已歷位九卿，既嗣侯，國在陳留，別邑在魏郡，租入歲千餘萬。
entries.en: Yanshou had already served among the nine chief ministers. Once he succeeded as marquis, his state lay in Chenliu with a separate estate in Wei commandery yielding more than ten million in annual rent.
entries.literal: Yanshou had already passed through the nine chief ministers; once he succeeded as marquis, his state was in Chenliu and a separate estate in Wei commandery, with annual rent income of more than ten million.

entries.zh: 延壽自以身無功德，何以能久堪先人大國，數上書讓減戶邑，又因弟陽都侯彭祖口陳至誠，天子以為有讓，乃徙封平原，並一國，戶口如故，而租稅減半。
entries.en: Yanshou felt himself without merit and wondered how he could long hold his forebear's great fief. He repeatedly memorialized to yield and reduce his households, and through his younger brother Marquis of Yangdu Pengzu spoke his utmost sincerity. The emperor took this as genuine yielding and transferred the enfeoffment to Pingyuan, merging the two states into one with the same households but half the rent and tax.
entries.literal: Yanshou himself felt he had no merit or virtue and wondered how he could long bear his forebear's great state; he repeatedly submitted memorials declining and requesting reduction of households in the fief, and also through his younger brother Marquis of Yangdu Pengzu spoke his utmost sincerity by mouth. The Son of Heaven held that he had shown yielding and therefore transferred the enfeoffment to Pingyuan, merging the two states into one; households remained as before, but rent and tax were halved.

entries.zh: 薨，謚曰愛侯。
entries.en: He died and was granted the posthumous title Marquis Ai.
entries.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Ai.

entries.zh: 子勃嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhang Bo succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Bo succeeded.

entries.zh: 為散騎、諫大夫。
entries.en: He served as attendant cavalier and grand adviser.
entries.literal: He served as attendant cavalier and grand adviser.

entries.zh: 元帝初即位，詔列侯舉茂材，勃舉太官獻丞陳湯。
entries.en: Soon after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, an edict ordered the ranked marquises to recommend men of outstanding talent. Zhang Bo recommended Chen Tang, assistant director of the imperial kitchen.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan had just succeeded, an edict ordered the ranked marquises to recommend outstanding talent; Bo recommended Chen Tang, assistant director of the imperial kitchen.

entries.zh: 湯有罪，勃坐削戶二百，會薨，故賜謚曰繆侯。
entries.en: When Tang was found guilty, Bo was implicated and lost two hundred households from his fief. He happened to die at the time and was therefore granted the posthumous title Marquis Miu.
entries.literal: Tang had guilt; Bo was implicated and had two hundred households cut from his fief; it happened that he died, and therefore he was granted the posthumous title Marquis Miu.

entries.zh: 後湯立功西域，世以勃為知人。
entries.en: Later Chen Tang won merit in the Western Regions, and the age judged that Bo had known how to recognize talent.
entries.literal: Later Tang established merit in the Western Regions, and the age held that Bo had known men.

entries.zh: 子臨嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhang Lin succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Lin succeeded.

entries.zh: 初，安世長子千秋與霍光子禹俱為中郎將，將兵隨度遼將軍范明友擊烏桓。
entries.en: Long before, Anshi's eldest son Zhang Qianqiu and Huo Guang's son Huo Yu had both been generals of the household gentlemen when they campaigned under the Trans-Liao general Fan Mingyou against the Wuhuan.
entries.literal: At first, Anshi's eldest son Qianqiu and Huo Guang's son Yu together were generals of the household gentlemen, leading troops following the Trans-Liao general Fan Mingyou to strike the Wuhuan.

entries.zh: 還，謁大將軍光，問千秋戰鬥方略，山川形勢，千秋口對兵事，畫地成圖，無所忘失。
entries.en: On their return they called on Huo Guang, who questioned Qianqiu about tactics and terrain. Qianqiu answered from memory, sketching the campaign map in the dust without a single error.
entries.literal: Returning, they visited Grand General Guang; Guang asked Qianqiu battle methods and plans, mountains and rivers configuration; Qianqiu orally replied on military affairs, drew on the ground and made a map, nothing forgotten or lost.

entries.zh: 光復問禹，禹不能記，曰：「皆有文書。」
entries.en: When he put the same questions to Huo Yu, Yu could not recall a thing and said, "It is all on file somewhere."
entries.literal: Guang again asked Yu; Yu could not remember, saying, "All have documents."

entries.zh: 光由是賢千秋，以禹為不材，歎曰：「霍氏世衰，張氏興矣！」
entries.en: From that day Huo Guang respected Qianqiu and wrote Yu off as worthless, sighing, "The house of Huo is fading; the house of Zhang is on the rise!"
entries.literal: Guang from this deemed Qianqiu worthy and Yu not talented, sighed, saying, "The Huo clan generation declines; the Zhang clan rises!"

entries.zh: 及禹誅滅，而安世子孫相繼，自宣、元以來為侍中、中常侍、諸曹散騎、列校尉者凡十餘人。
entries.en: After the Huo clan was extirpated, Zhang Anshi's descendants held one high post after another. From the reigns of Xuandi and Yuandi onward, more than ten of them served as palace attendants, regular attendants, mounted escorts in the various bureaus, or colonels of the guard.
entries.literal: When Yu was exterminated and destroyed, yet Anshi's sons and grandsons succeeded one another, from Emperors Xuan and Yuan onward as palace attendants, regular palace attendants, various bureau mounted escorts, and colonels—more than ten persons in all.

entries.zh: 功臣之世，唯有金氏、張氏，親近寵貴，比於外戚。
entries.en: Of all the families ennobled for merit, only the Jins and the Zhangs remained so close to the throne—almost like imperial in-laws.
entries.literal: Among meritorious minister generations, only the Jin clan and Zhang clan were intimate, favored, and honored, comparable to affines by marriage.

entries.zh: 張湯本居杜陵，安世武、昭、宣世輒隨陵，凡三徙，復還杜陵。
entries.en: Zhang Tang originally lived at Duling. During the reigns of Emperor Wu, Emperor Zhao, and Emperor Xuan, Anshi followed each new imperial mausoleum settlement—three relocations in all—before returning to Duling.
entries.literal: Zhang Tang originally dwelt at Duling; Anshi in the Wu, Zhao, and Xuan generations always followed the mausoleum sites; in all three moves, again returned to Duling.

entries.zh: 贊曰：馮商稱張湯之先與留侯同祖，而司馬遷不言，故闕焉。
entries.en: The historian's comment: Feng Shang claimed that Zhang Tang's line shared an ancestor with the Marquis of Liu, but Sima Qian does not say so, and we leave the point aside.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Feng Shang claimed Zhang Tang's ancestors shared the same ancestor as the Marquis of Liu, but Sima Qian does not speak of it—therefore it is omitted.

entries.zh: 漢興以來，侯者百數，保國持寵，未有若富平者也。
entries.en: Since the founding of Han, hundreds of families have received marquisates, yet none has held its fortune and imperial favor as steadily as Fuping.
entries.literal: Since Han rose, those enfeoffed as marquis have been in the hundreds; to preserve the state and maintain favor, none has been like Fuping.

entries.zh: 湯雖酷烈，及身蒙咎，其推賢揚善，固宜有後。
entries.en: Zhang Tang was a cruel judge and came to a bad end himself, yet in promoting able men and speaking well of others he earned the posterity he deserved.
entries.literal: Although Tang was cruel and fierce, reaching himself covered with blame, his pushing the worthy and displaying the good—solidly he ought to have posterity.

entries.zh: 安世履道，滿而不溢。
entries.en: Zhang Anshi walked the middle path—his cup was full, yet he never let it spill.
entries.literal: Anshi trod the Way, full yet not overflowing.

entries.zh: 賀之陰德，亦有助云。
entries.en: The quiet kindness Zhang He once showed the future Emperor Xuan also played its part in the family's lasting good fortune.
entries.literal: The hidden virtue of He also had its part.

entries.zh: 張湯，杜陵人也。
entries.en: Zhang Tang came from Duling.
entries.literal: Zhang Tang was a man of Duling.

entries.zh: 父為長安丞，出，湯為兒守舍。
entries.en: His father served as assistant magistrate of Chang'an. Whenever the father left on business, the boy Tang stayed behind to watch the house.
entries.literal: His father was assistant magistrate of Chang'an; when he went out, Tang as a child guarded the house.

entries.zh: 還，鼠盜肉，父怨，笞湯。
entries.en: When he came home, he found a rat had stolen the meat. Angry, he beat Tang with a stick.
entries.literal: Returning, a rat had stolen meat; the father was resentful and flogged Tang.

entries.zh: 湯掘熏得鼠及余肉，劾鼠掠治，傳爰書，訊鞫論報，並取鼠與肉，具獄磔堂下。
entries.en: Tang excavated the burrow, smoked the rat out, recovered the leftover meat, then drew up a formal accusation against the creature. He subjected it to interrogation under torture, filed the written record of the inquest, examined it, passed sentence, and reported the outcome. He produced the rat and the meat as evidence, closed the entire case, and had the convict torn apart alive in the courtyard.
entries.literal: Tang dug and smoked out the rat and the remaining meat, impeached the rat, tortured and examined it, transmitted the indictment, interrogated and judged and reported, and together took the rat and meat, completed the case, and dismembered them below the hall.

entries.zh: 父見之，視文辭如老獄吏，大驚，遂使書獄。
entries.en: When his father read the document, the wording read like that of a veteran prison clerk. He was astonished and thereafter set the boy to drafting legal briefs.
entries.literal: The father saw it, looked at the phrasing as that of an old jail clerk, was greatly startled, and thereupon had him write cases.

entries.zh: 見國家承武帝奢侈師旅之後，數為大將軍光言：「年歲比不登，流民未盡還，宜修孝文明政，示以儉約寬和，順天心，說民意，年歲宜應。」
entries.en: Seeing the empire still reeling from Emperor Wu's wars and waste, he urged Huo Guang more than once: "Harvests have failed year after year and refugees have not all come home. We should revive the restrained, humane government of Emperor Wen, teach frugality and mercy, and align policy with Heaven and the common people—then the seasons will answer in kind."
entries.literal: Seeing the state inheriting after Emperor Wu's extravagance and armies, several times he spoke to Grand General Guang: "Years in succession are not good harvests; wandering people have not all returned—it is fitting to cultivate Emperor Wen's enlightened government, show them frugal agreement lenient and harmonious, comply with Heaven's mind, please the people's intent—years and harvests should respond."

entries.zh: 光納其言，舉賢良，議罷酒榷、鹽、鐵，皆自延年發之。
entries.en: Guang took his advice: the summons of worthy men, the debates on ending the wine monopoly and the salt and iron monopolies—all began with Yannian.
entries.literal: Guang accepted his words, raised the worthy and good, deliberated abolishing wine monopoly, salt, and iron—all sprang from Yannian's initiating.

entries.zh: 吏民上書言便宜，有異，輒下延年平處復奏。
entries.en: Whenever officials or commoners submitted policy suggestions that sparked controversy, the drafts went to Yannian for adjudication and a follow-up memorial.
entries.literal: Officials and people memorializing on conveniences, having differences, always sent down to Yannian to level-handle and memorialize again.

entries.zh: 言可官試者，至為縣令，或丞相、御史除用，滿歲以狀聞，或抵其罪法，常與兩府及廷尉分章。
entries.en: If a proposal merited a trial appointment, the man might be made county magistrate, or the chancellor and imperial counselor would assign him a post; after a full year his performance was reported, or he was charged if he had failed—Yannian routinely split this paperwork with the two chief ministries and the commandant of justice.
entries.literal: Those whose words could be officially tried, reached to being county magistrates, or chancellor and imperial counselor dismissed and employed; full year they reported the condition, or matched their crime to law—he constantly divided memorials with the two offices and the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 哀帝崩，王莽秉政，諸前議立廟尊號者皆免，徙合浦。
entries.en: After Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang took charge, everyone who had backed the temple and title controversy was removed from office and banished to Hepu.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang held government; those who formerly had deliberated establishing temples and honoring titles were all dismissed and moved to Hepu.

entries.zh: 業以前罷黜，故見闊略，憂恐，發病死。
entries.en: Because Du Ye had already been disgraced earlier, Mang let him off lightly; still, Ye lived in such dread that he sickened and died.
entries.literal: Ye because formerly had been dismissed and demoted, therefore was treated with lenient omission; worried and afraid, he fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 業成帝初尚帝妹穎邑公主，主無子，薨，業家上書求還京師與主合葬，不許，而賜謚曰荒侯，傳子至孫絕。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Cheng's reign Du Ye had married Princess Yingyi, the emperor's sister. She died without issue, and his family petitioned to bring his remains to the capital for burial beside hers. The court refused but bestowed the posthumous epithet Dissolute Marquis. The marquisate passed to his son and then his grandson before the line failed.
entries.literal: Ye at Emperor Cheng beginning had married the emperor younger sister Princess Yingyi; the princess had no sons; when she died, Ye family submitted a memorial requesting to return to the capital region and be jointly buried with the princess—not permitted; yet he was granted posthumous title Marquis Dissolute, transmitted son to grandson and cut off.

entries.zh: 初，杜周武帝時徙茂陵，至延年徙杜陵雲。
entries.en: Du Zhou's household had been relocated to Maoling under Emperor Wu; by Du Yannian's generation the family had settled at Duling—or so the note runs.
entries.literal: At first Du Zhou in Emperor Wu time moved to Maoling; reaching Yannian he moved to Duling—it is said.

entries.zh: 昭帝末，寢疾，征天下名醫，延年典領方藥。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Zhao's reign he fell ill. Famous physicians were summoned from across the realm, and Du Yannian was placed in charge of prescriptions.
entries.literal: Near the end of Emperor Zhao's reign he fell ill; famous physicians were summoned from across the realm, and Yannian was put in charge of prescriptions.

entries.zh: 帝崩，昌邑王即位，廢，大將軍光、車騎將軍張安世與大臣議所立。
entries.en: The emperor died. The king of Changyi was enthroned and then deposed. Grand General Huo Guang and Cavalry General Zhang Anshi deliberated with the great ministers on whom to enthrone.
entries.literal: The emperor died; the King of Changyi ascended the throne and was deposed; Grand General Guang and Cavalry General Zhang Anshi deliberated with the great ministers on whom to enthrone.

entries.zh: 時，宣帝養於掖廷，號皇曾孫，與延年中子佗相愛善，延年知曾孫德美，勸光、安世立焉。
entries.en: At that time Emperor Xuan was being raised in the rear court under the title Imperial Great-Grandson. He and Yannian's middle son Tuo were on close terms. Knowing the great-grandson's virtue, Yannian urged Guang and Anshi to enthrone him.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was being raised in the rear court, styled Imperial Great-Grandson; he and Yannian's middle son Tuo were fond of each other. Yannian knew the great-grandson's virtue and excellence and urged Guang and Anshi to enthrone him.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，褒賞大臣，延年以定策安宗廟，益戶二千三百，與始封所食邑凡四千三百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne he rewarded the great ministers. For helping settle the succession policy and secure the ancestral temples, Yannian received an additional 2,300 households, bringing his total fief to 4,300 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne he rewarded the great ministers; Yannian, for settling the succession policy and securing the ancestral temples, received an additional 2,300 households, bringing his total fief to 4,300 households.

entries.zh: 詔有司論定策功：大司馬大將軍光功德過太尉絳侯周勃；
entries.en: An edict ordered the relevant offices to assess merits in settling the succession: Grand Marshal Grand General Huo Guang's merit surpassed that of Marquis of Jiang, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo;
entries.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to assess merits in settling the succession: Grand Marshal Grand General Guang's merit surpassed Marquis of Jiang, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo;

entries.zh: 車騎將軍安世、丞相楊敞功比丞相陳平；
entries.en: Cavalry General Zhang Anshi and Chancellor Yang Chang were ranked with Chancellor Chen Ping;
entries.literal: Cavalry General Anshi and Chancellor Yang Chang were ranked with Chancellor Chen Ping;

entries.zh: 前將軍韓增、御史大夫蔡誼功比穎陰侯灌嬰；
entries.en: Former General Han Zeng and Imperial Counselor Cai Yi were ranked with Marquis of Yingyin Guan Ying;
entries.literal: Former General Han Zeng and Imperial Counselor Cai Yi were ranked with Marquis of Yingyin Guan Ying;

entries.zh: 太僕杜延年功比硃虛侯劉章；
entries.en: Grand Coachman Du Yannian was ranked with Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang;
entries.literal: Grand Coachman Du Yannian was ranked with Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang;

entries.zh: 後將軍趙充國、大司農田延年、少府史樂成功比典客劉揭，皆封侯益土。
entries.en: Rear General Zhao Chongguo, Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian, and Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Shi Yuecheng were ranked with Director of Guests Liu Jie. All were enfeoffed as marquises and granted additional fiefs.
entries.literal: Rear General Zhao Chongguo, Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian, and Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Shi Yuecheng were ranked with Director of Guests Liu Jie—all were enfeoffed as marquises and granted additional fiefs.

entries.zh: 霍光薨後，子禹與宗族謀反，誅。
entries.en: After Huo Guang's death his son Huo Yu conspired with the clan and paid with his life.
entries.literal: After Huo Guang died, his son Yu with the clan plotted rebellion and was executed.

entries.zh: 上以延年霍氏舊人，欲退之，而丞相魏相奏延年素貴用事，官職多奸。
entries.en: The emperor, seeing Yannian as an old Huo partisan, meant to ease him out, but Chancellor Wei Xiang memorialized that Yannian had long abused high office and his conduct was riddled with corruption.
entries.literal: The ruler because Yannian was Huo clan's old man wished to retire him, but Chancellor Wei Xiang memorialized that Yannian had long been noble and in power, his offices many wicked.

entries.zh: 遣吏考案，但得苑馬多死，官奴婢乏衣食，延年坐免官，削戶二千。
entries.en: An inquiry turned up only neglected park horses and underfed government slaves—thin grounds—but Yannian was stripped of office and docked two thousand households of his fief.
entries.literal: He sent clerks to investigate; they only obtained that park horses many died, official slave girls lacked clothes and food; Yannian sat guilty and was dismissed from office, households cut two thousand.

entries.zh: 後數月，復召拜為北地太守。
entries.en: A few months later he was recalled and named governor of Beidi.
entries.literal: After several months, again summoned and appointed governor of Beidi.

entries.zh: 延年以故九卿外為邊吏，治郡不進，上以璽書讓延年。
entries.en: A former nine minister banished to a frontier post, he administered the commandery listlessly until the emperor sent a sealed edict rebuking him.
entries.literal: Yannian because formerly nine ministers went out to be border clerk, governed the commandery without advancing; the ruler by sealed edict reproached Yannian.

entries.zh: 延年乃選用良吏，捕擊豪強，郡中清靜。
entries.en: Stung, he recruited able subordinates, smashed the local magnates, and brought order to the region.
entries.literal: Yannian thereupon selected and employed good clerks, struck and captured the powerful and strong; within the commandery it was clear and quiet.

entries.zh: 居歲餘，上使謁者賜延年璽書，黃金二千斤，徙為西河太守，治甚有名。
entries.en: After a year the court sent a herald with a commendatory edict and two thousand catties of gold, transferring him to Xihe, where his administration won wide praise.
entries.literal: Dwelling more than a year, the ruler sent a herald to grant Yannian a sealed edict, yellow gold two thousand jin, transferred him to be governor of Xihe; his governance had great reputation.

entries.zh: 五鳳中，征入為御史大夫。
entries.en: During the Wufeng era (57–54 BCE) he was summoned to serve as imperial counselor.
entries.literal: In the Wufeng years, summoned in as imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 延年居父官府，不敢當舊位，坐臥皆易其處。
entries.en: He moved into his father's official mansion but refused to use the old reception rooms, changing every hall and chamber where Du Zhou had sat.
entries.literal: Yannian dwelt in his father's official residence, did not dare occupy the old seat; sitting and lying he all changed their places.

entries.zh: 是時，四夷和，海內平，延年視事三歲，以老病乞骸骨，天子優之，使光祿大夫持節賜延年黃金百斤、酒，加致醫藥，延年遂稱病篤。
entries.en: The frontiers were quiet and the realm at peace. After three years in office, Yannian cited age and illness and asked to retire. The emperor treated him generously, sending a Grandee of Palace Splendor with an imperial staff, one hundred catties of gold, wine, and medicine. Yannian then reported that his condition had become critical.
entries.literal: At this time the four quarters were at peace and the realm was tranquil. After Yannian had served for three years, age and illness led him to request retirement. The Son of Heaven treated him generously, sending a Grandee of Palace Splendor with the imperial staff to grant him one hundred jin of gold and wine, together with medicines. Yannian then declared that his illness had become grave.

entries.zh: 賜安車駟馬，罷就第。
entries.en: He was awarded a comfortable carriage team and permission to withdraw to his private residence.
entries.literal: He was granted a secure carriage and four horses, dismissed to go to his mansion.

entries.zh: 後數月薨，謚曰敬侯，子緩嗣。
entries.en: He died a few months later with the posthumous epithet "Respectful Marquis"; his son Du Huan succeeded him.
entries.literal: After several months he died; posthumous title was Marquis Jing; his son Huan inherited.

entries.zh: 緩少為郎，本始中以校尉從蒲類將軍擊匈奴，還為諫大夫，遷上谷都尉，雁門太守。
entries.en: Du Huan began as a gentleman-attendant. In the Benshi era (73–70 BCE) he campaigned against the Xiongnu as a colonel under the Pulei general, then served as remonstrance grandee, commandant of Shanggu, and governor of Yanmen.
entries.literal: Huan in youth was a gentleman; in Benshi he as colonel followed the Pulei general to strike the Xiongnu; returning he became remonstrance grandee, transferred to be commandant of Shanggu, governor of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 父延年薨，征視喪事，拜為太常，治諸陵縣，每冬月封具獄日，常去酒省食，官屬稱其有恩。
entries.en: When Yannian died he was called to the capital to direct the obsequies and was appointed Grand Master of ceremonies in charge of the imperial tomb districts. Each winter, on the day capital cases were closed for the year, he abstained from wine and took spare meals; his staff praised his compassion.
entries.literal: When father Yannian died, he was summoned to oversee funeral affairs, appointed Grand Master of ceremonies, governed the various mausoleum counties; each winter month when sealing and completing prison days, he always removed wine and reduced food; official subordinates praised him as having kindness.

entries.zh: 元帝初即位，谷貴民流，永光中西羌反，緩輒上書入錢、谷以助用，前後數百萬。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Yuan's reign grain prices soared and refugees filled the roads. When the western Qiang rose in Yongguang, Huan repeatedly donated cash and grain to the treasury—several million over the years.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan first took the throne, grain was expensive and people wandered; in Yongguang the western Qiang rebelled; Huan repeatedly memorialized entering cash and grain to assist use—front and rear several million.

entries.zh: 其春，丞相方進薨，業上書言：「方進本與長深結厚，更相稱薦，長陷大惡，獨得不坐，苟慾障塞前過，不為陛下廣持平例，又無恐懼之心，反因時信其邪辟，報睚眥怨。
entries.en: That spring Chancellor Zhai Fangjin died. Du Ye submitted a memorial saying, "Fangjin had been deeply bound in friendship with Chang and repeatedly recommended each other. Chang fell into great wickedness yet alone escaped punishment. Fangjin wished to cover his former faults, did not extend evenhanded standards for Your Majesty, and lacked fear; instead he seized the moment to trust Chang's perverse ways and repay a grudge for a trifle.
entries.literal: That spring Chancellor Fangjin died. Ye submitted a memorial saying, "Fangjin had been deeply bound in friendship with Chang and repeatedly recommended each other. Chang fell into great wickedness yet alone escaped punishment. Fangjin wished to cover his former faults, did not extend evenhanded standards for Your Majesty, and lacked fear; instead he seized the moment to trust Chang's perverse ways and repay a grudge for a trifle.

entries.zh: 故事，大逆朋友坐免官，無歸故郡者，今坐長者歸故郡，已深一等；
entries.en: Under precedent, friends implicated in great treason were punished by removal from office; they were not sent back to their native commanderies. Now those punished because of Chang have been returned to their home commanderies, which is already one degree harsher;
entries.literal: By precedent, friends implicated in great treason were punished by dismissal from office, with none sent back to their native commandery. Now those implicated through Chang were sent to their native commanderies—already one degree too severe;

entries.zh: 紅陽侯立坐子受長貨賂故就國耳，非大逆也，而方進復奏立黨友後將軍朱博、巨鹿太守孫宏、故少府陳咸，皆免官，歸咸故郡。
entries.en: Wang Li, marquis of Hongyang, was punished because his son accepted Chang's bribes and therefore went to his fief—this was not great treason. Yet Fangjin again memorialized against Li's partisan associates: Rear General Zhu Bo, Administrator of Julu Sun Hong, and former Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Chen Xian. All were dismissed, and Chen Xian was sent to his native commandery.
entries.literal: Marquis of Hongyang Li was punished because his son accepted Chang's bribes and therefore went to his fief—this was not great treason. Yet Fangjin again memorialized against Li's partisan associates: Rear General Zhu Bo, Administrator of Julu Sun Hong, and former Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Chen Xian—all were dismissed and Chen Xian was sent to his native commandery.

entries.zh: 刑罰無平，在方進之筆端，眾庶莫不疑惑，皆言孫宏不與紅陽侯相愛。
entries.en: Punishment lacked fairness—it lay at the tip of Fangjin's brush. The common people were all puzzled and said Sun Hong was not on friendly terms with the marquis of Hongyang.
entries.literal: Punishment lacked fairness—it lay at the tip of Fangjin's brush. The common people were all puzzled and said Sun Hong was not on friendly terms with Marquis of Hongyang.

entries.zh: 宏前為中丞時，方進為御史大夫，舉掾隆可侍御史，宏奏隆前奉使欺謾，不宜執法近侍，方進以此怨宏。
entries.en: When Sun Hong was Censor-in-Chief and Fangjin imperial counselor, Fangjin recommended his clerk Long as an attendant censor. Hong objected in a memorial that Long had deceived the court on an earlier mission and was unfit for a law-enforcement post near the emperor. Fangjin never forgave him.
entries.literal: When Sun Hong had earlier served as Censor-in-Chief, Fangjin was imperial counselor and recommended his clerk Long for appointment as an attendant censor. Hong memorialized that Long had previously deceived the court while on a mission and was unfit to enforce the law in close attendance; Fangjin resented Hong for this.

entries.zh: 又方進為京兆尹時，陳咸為少府，在九卿高弟，陛下所自知也。
entries.en: Moreover, when Fangjin was metropolitan governor, Chen Xian served as Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, occupying one of the highest places among the Nine Ministers; Your Majesty knows this personally.
entries.literal: Again, when Fangjin was metropolitan governor, Chen Xian was chamberlain for the palace revenues, among the highest of the nine ministers—Your Majesty knows this yourself.

entries.zh: 方進素與司直師丹相善，臨御史大夫缺，使丹奏咸為奸利，請案驗，卒不能有所得，而方進果自得御史大夫。
entries.en: Fangjin had long been friendly with the supervisor Shi Dan. When the office of Imperial Counselor became vacant, he had Dan submit a memorial accusing Chen Xian of illicit profiteering and requesting an investigation. In the end nothing could be found, while Fangjin himself did indeed obtain the office.
entries.literal: Fangjin had long been on good terms with Supervisor Shi Dan. When the post of imperial counselor fell vacant, he had Dan memorialize that Chen Xian sought illicit profit and requested investigation. In the end nothing was found, yet Fangjin indeed obtained the post of imperial counselor himself.

entries.zh: 為丞相，即時詆欺，奏免咸，復因紅陽侯事歸咸故郡。
entries.en: As chancellor he immediately slandered and memorialized to dismiss Xian, and again through the marquis of Hongyang affair sent Xian back to his native commandery.
entries.literal: As chancellor he immediately slandered and memorialized to dismiss Xian, and again through the Marquis of Hongyang affair sent Xian back to his native commandery.

entries.zh: 眾人皆言國家假方進權太甚。
entries.en: Everyone said the state had lent Fangjin too much power.
entries.literal: Everyone said the state had lent Fangjin too much power.

entries.zh: 案師丹行能無異，及光祿勳許商被病殘人，皆但以附從方進，嘗獲尊官。
entries.en: Consider Shi Dan: there was nothing exceptional in his conduct or ability. Xu Shang, Superintendent of the Imperial Household, suffered from a disabling illness. Both obtained high office only by attaching themselves to Fangjin.
entries.literal: Consider Shi Dan: his conduct and ability were unremarkable, while Xu Shang, Superintendent of the Imperial Household, suffered from a disabling illness. Both gained exalted offices only by attaching themselves to Fangjin.

entries.zh: 丹前親薦邑子丞相史能使巫下神，為國求福，幾獲大利。
entries.en: Dan had earlier personally recommended a fellow townsman, a clerk in the chancellor's office, claiming that he could use shamans to bring down spirits and seek blessings for the state, almost securing great advantage thereby.
entries.literal: Dan had earlier personally recommended a native son, a chancellor clerk who could make shamans descend spirits and seek blessings for the state, nearly obtaining great profit.

entries.zh: 幸賴陛下至明，遣使者毛莫如先考驗，卒得其奸，皆坐死。
entries.en: Fortunately, through Your Majesty's utmost discernment, the envoy Mao Moru was first sent to examine the matter. In the end their fraud was uncovered, and all were condemned to death.
entries.literal: Fortunately, relying on Your Majesty's supreme clarity, an envoy Mao Moru was sent to investigate first; in the end their fraud was exposed and all were punished by death.

entries.zh: 假令丹知而白之，此誣罔罪也；
entries.en: If Dan had known and reported it, this would be the crime of false accusation;
entries.literal: If Dan had known and reported it, this would be the crime of false accusation;

entries.zh: 不知而白之，是背經術惑左道也：二者皆在大辟，重於朱博、孫宏、陳咸所坐。
entries.en: if he did not know and nevertheless reported it, then he abandoned classical learning and misled the court with heterodox arts. Either offense deserves capital punishment and is graver than the charges for which Zhu Bo, Sun Hong, and Chen Xian were punished.
entries.literal: if he had not known and yet reported it, this would be turning against classical learning and deluding with heterodox ways: both are capital offenses, heavier than what Zhu Bo, Sun Hong, and Chen Xian were punished for.

entries.zh: 方進終不舉白，專作威福，阿黨所厚，排擠英俊，托公報私，橫厲無所畏忌，欲以熏轑天下。
entries.en: Yet Fangjin never reported the matter. He monopolized power and patronage, protected those close to his faction, drove out men of talent, used public office to repay private resentment, and acted violently without fear or restraint, intending to overawe the whole realm.
entries.literal: Fangjin to the end never reported it. He monopolized authority and favor, favored his faction, squeezed out the talented, used public office to settle private scores, and rampaged without fear or restraint, wishing to steamroll the realm.

entries.zh: 天下莫不望風而靡，自尚書近臣皆結舌杜口，骨肉親屬莫不股慄。
entries.en: Everyone under Heaven bent before his influence. Even the close attendants among the Masters of Writing tied their tongues and shut their mouths; his own kin and relatives all trembled in fear.
entries.literal: No one under Heaven failed to bow before the wind. Even close attendants among the Masters of Writing bit their tongues and sealed their mouths; kinsmen near and far all trembled in their limbs.

entries.zh: 威權泰盛而不忠信，非所以安國家也。
entries.en: Authority so excessive without loyalty and good faith is not the way to secure the state.
entries.literal: Authority so excessive without loyalty and good faith is not the way to secure the state.

entries.zh: 今聞方進卒病死，不以尉示天下，反覆賞賜厚葬，唯陛下深思往事，以戒來今。」
entries.en: Now I hear that Fangjin suddenly died of illness, yet he was not exposed as a warning to reassure the realm; instead, repeated rewards and a lavish burial were granted. May Your Majesty think deeply on past events and use them to admonish the future."
entries.literal: Now I hear Fangjin died suddenly of illness, yet he was not displayed to reassure the realm; instead rewards and a lavish burial were repeatedly granted. May Your Majesty deeply ponder past events to warn the future."
