entries.zh: 會成帝崩，哀帝即位，業復上書言：「王氏世權日久，朝無骨鯁之臣，宗室諸侯微弱，與系囚無異，自佐史以上至於大吏皆權臣之黨。
entries.en: It happened that Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai took the throne. Du Ye again submitted a memorial saying, "The Wang clan has held power for generations. The court has no blunt-spoken ministers. Imperial clansmen and feudal lords are weak, no different from bound prisoners. From clerks upward to great officials, all are partisans of the power-holders.
entries.literal: It happened that Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai took the throne. Ye again submitted a memorial saying, "The Wang clan has held power for generations. The court has no blunt-spoken ministers. Imperial clansmen and feudal lords are weak, no different from bound prisoners. From clerks upward to great officials, all are partisans of the power-holders.

entries.zh: 曲陽侯根前為三公輔政，知趙昭儀殺皇子，不輒白奏，反與趙氏比周，恣意妄行，譖訴故許後，被加以非罪，誅破諸許族，敗元帝外家。
entries.en: Wang Gen, marquis of Quyang, had served among the Three Excellencies and helped direct the government. He knew that Consort Zhao Hede had killed the imperial sons but failed to report it. Instead he colluded with the Zhao clan, acted without restraint, slandered the deposed Empress Xu, had her falsely condemned, destroyed the Xu clan, and ruined Emperor Yuan's maternal family.
entries.literal: Marquis of Quyang Wang Gen had earlier assisted the government as one of the Three Excellencies. He knew that Consort Zhao Hede had killed the imperial sons but did not immediately report it; instead he allied himself with the Zhao clan, acted willfully and recklessly, slandered the deposed Empress Xu, imposed false charges on her, destroyed the Xu clan, and ruined Emperor Yuan's maternal family.

entries.zh: 內嫉妒同產兄姊紅陽侯立及淳于氏，皆老被放棄。
entries.en: Within his own family he resented his elder brother Wang Li, marquis of Hongyang, and his elder sister Lady Chunyu, abandoning both in their old age.
entries.literal: Within the family he resented his full elder brother Wang Li, marquis of Hongyang, and his elder sister Lady Chunyu; both were cast aside in old age.

entries.zh: 新喋血京師，威權可畏。
entries.en: Fresh blood was shed in the capital; authority inspired dread.
entries.literal: Fresh blood was shed in the capital; authority inspired dread.

entries.zh: 高陽侯薛宣有不養母之名，安昌侯張禹奸人之雄，惑亂朝廷，使先帝負謗於海內，尤不可不慎。
entries.en: Xue Xuan, marquis of Gaoyang, bore the name of one who did not support his mother; Zhang Yu, marquis of Anchang, was a chief among wicked men, confusing and disordering the court and causing the late emperor to bear slander within the seas—this above all must not be treated lightly.
entries.literal: Marquis of Gaoyang Xue Xuan bore the name of one who did not support his mother; Marquis of Anchang Zhang Yu was a chief among wicked men, confusing and disordering the court and causing the late emperor to bear slander within the seas—this above all must not be treated lightly.

entries.zh: 陛下初即位，謙讓未皇，孤獨特立，莫可據杖，權臣易世，意若探湯。
entries.en: Your Majesty has only just taken the throne; modest deference has left no time for other concerns, and you stand alone without support to rely on. Powerful ministers change with the times, and their intentions are as dangerous to test as boiling water.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has just taken the throne, humility not yet fully displayed, standing alone without support to lean on. Power-holders change with the age, and the mind is as if touching boiling water.

entries.zh: 宜蚤以義割恩，安百姓心。
entries.en: You should early cut favor by righteousness and settle the hearts of the common people.
entries.literal: You should early cut favor by righteousness and settle the hearts of the common people.

entries.zh: 竊見朱博忠信勇猛，材略不世出，誠國家雄俊之寶臣也，宜征博置左右，以填天下。
entries.en: I have privately observed that Zhu Bo is loyal, trustworthy, brave, and forceful, with talent and strategy rarely seen in any age. He is truly a heroic and precious minister of the state. He should be summoned and placed at Your Majesty's side to steady the realm.
entries.literal: I have observed that Zhu Bo is loyal, trustworthy, brave, and fierce, with talent and strategy unmatched in the age—truly a treasured minister of heroic excellence for the state. He should be summoned and placed at Your side to fill the realm.

entries.zh: 此人在朝，則陛下可高枕而臥矣。
entries.en: With this man at court, Your Majesty may sleep with head on high pillow.
entries.literal: With this man at court, Your Majesty may sleep with head on high pillow.

entries.zh: 昔諸呂欲危劉氏，賴有高祖遺臣周勃、陳平尚存，不者，幾為奸臣笑。」
entries.en: In the past, when the Lü clan sought to endanger the Liu house, survival depended on the continued presence of the High Emperor's old ministers, Zhou Bo and Chen Ping. Without them, the dynasty would almost have become a laughingstock for treacherous ministers."
entries.literal: Formerly the Lü clan wished to endanger the Liu house; it relied on surviving founding ministers of the High Emperor, Zhou Bo and Chen Ping—otherwise it would nearly have been laughed at by wicked ministers."

entries.zh: 欽為人深博有謀。
entries.en: Du Qin was deep, learned, and full of stratagem.
entries.literal: Qin as a man was deep, learned, and full of stratagem.

entries.zh: 自上為太子時，以好色聞，及即位，皇太后詔采良家女。
entries.en: From the time he was crown prince he was known for love of women. When he took the throne the empress dowager ordered the selection of maidens from reputable families.
entries.literal: From the time he was crown prince he was known for love of women; when he took the throne the empress dowager ordered the selection of maidens from reputable families.

entries.zh: 欽因是說大將軍鳳曰：「禮壹娶九女，所以極陽數，廣嗣重祖也；
entries.en: Qin used the occasion to persuade Grand General Wang Feng, saying, "Ritual prescribes one marriage to nine wives, to fulfill the yang number, extend the lineage, and honor ancestors;
entries.literal: Qin used the occasion to persuade Grand General Feng, saying, "Ritual prescribes one marriage to nine wives, to fulfill the yang number, extend the lineage, and honor ancestors;

entries.zh: 必鄉舉求窈窕，不問華色，所以助德理內也；
entries.en: one must seek graceful maidens through local recommendation, not asking about beauty or color, thereby to aid virtue and order the inner quarters;
entries.literal: one must seek graceful maidens through local recommendation, not asking about beauty or color, thereby to aid virtue and order the inner quarters;

entries.zh: 娣侄雖缺不復補，所以養壽塞爭也。
entries.en: though junior wives or nieces-in-law may be lacking, none are added to fill the gap, thereby to preserve longevity and stop strife.
entries.literal: though junior wives or nieces-in-law may be lacking, none are added to fill the gap, thereby to preserve longevity and stop strife.

entries.zh: 故后妃有貞淑之行，則胤嗣有賢聖之君；
entries.en: Hence if the empress and consorts have chaste and virtuous conduct, the heirs will have wise and sage rulers;
entries.literal: Hence if the empress and consorts have chaste and virtuous conduct, the heirs will have wise and sage rulers;

entries.zh: 制度有威儀之節，則人君有壽考之福。
entries.en: if the institutions have dignified ceremonial propriety, the sovereign will have the blessing of long life.
entries.literal: if the institutions have dignified ceremonial propriety, the sovereign will have the blessing of long life.

entries.zh: 廢而不由，則女德不厭；
entries.en: If such standards are abandoned and not followed, feminine virtue will not be satisfied;
entries.literal: If such standards are abandoned and not followed, feminine virtue will not be satisfied;

entries.zh: 女德不厭，則壽命不究於高年。
entries.en: if feminine virtue is not satisfied, life will not run its full course to advanced years.
entries.literal: if feminine virtue is not satisfied, life will not run its full course to advanced years.

entries.zh: 《書》云：『或四三年』，言失欲之生害也。
entries.en: The Documents says, 'Some reigns lasted only three or four years,' speaking of the harm born of indulging desire.
entries.literal: The Documents says, 'Some reigns lasted only three or four years,' speaking of the harm born of indulging desire.

entries.zh: 男子五十，好色未衰；
entries.en: At fifty a man has not yet lost desire;
entries.literal: At fifty a man has not yet lost desire;

entries.zh: 婦人四十，容貌改前。
entries.en: at forty a woman's appearance has changed from what it was.
entries.literal: at forty a woman's appearance has changed from what it was.

entries.zh: 以改前之容侍於未衰之年，而不以禮為制，則其原不可救而後徠異態；
entries.en: If she serves in years when desire has not yet waned but her appearance has changed from before, and no ritual system regulates the matter, then the root of the problem cannot be remedied and strange consequences will follow;
entries.literal: To serve with a changed countenance in years when desire has not yet waned, without regulating it by ritual—its source cannot be remedied and strange forms follow after;

entries.zh: 後徠異態，則正後自疑而支庶有間適之心。
entries.en: when strange forms follow after, the principal consort grows suspicious and collateral branches harbor thoughts of seizing advantage.
entries.literal: when strange forms follow after, the principal consort grows suspicious and collateral branches harbor thoughts of seizing advantage.

entries.zh: 是以晉獻被納讒之謗，申生蒙無罪之辜。
entries.en: Thus Duke Xian of Jin suffered slander from accepted calumny, and Shensheng bore guilt though innocent.
entries.literal: Thus Duke Xian of Jin suffered slander from accepted calumny, and Shensheng bore guilt though innocent.

entries.zh: 今聖主富於春秋，未有適嗣，方鄉術入學，未親后妃之議。
entries.en: Now the sage ruler is still in the fullness of youth, has no heir apparent, is only beginning to turn toward study, and has not yet personally considered the question of empress and consorts.
entries.literal: Now the sage ruler is still young, has no heir apparent, is just beginning his scholarly training, and has not yet attended to discussion of empress and consorts.

entries.zh: 將軍輔政，宜因始初之隆，建九女之制，詳擇有行義之家，求淑女之質，毋必有色聲音技能，為萬世大法。
entries.en: As regent, General, you should take advantage of this auspicious beginning to establish the system of nine consorts. Select carefully from families known for conduct and righteousness, seeking the substance of virtuous women rather than mere beauty, voice, or accomplishments, and make this the great model for all later ages.
entries.literal: General, as regent, should take advantage of this early flourishing and establish the system of nine wives, carefully selecting from families of moral conduct and seeking the quality of virtuous maidens—not necessarily color, voice, or skill—as the great law for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 夫少，戒之在色，《小卞》之作，可為寒心。
entries.en: For youth the chief warning lies in lust; the composition "Xiao Bian" should make the heart tremble.
entries.literal: For youth the chief warning lies in lust; the composition "Xiao Bian" should make the heart tremble.

entries.zh: 唯將軍常以為憂。」
entries.en: Only the general should constantly make this a concern."
entries.literal: Only the general should constantly make this a concern."

entries.zh: 後有日蝕、地震之變，詔舉賢良方正能直言士，合陽侯梁放舉欽。
entries.en: Later, after solar eclipses and earthquakes, the throne called for outspoken men of integrity. Liang Fang, the marquis of Heyang, nominated Du Qin.
entries.literal: Afterward there were solar eclipse and earthquake changes; an edict ordered raising the worthy and upright who could speak directly; Marquis of Heyang Liang Fang raised Qin.

entries.zh: 欽上對曰：「陛下畏天命，悼變異，延見公卿，舉直言之士，將以求天心，跡得失也。
entries.en: Du Qin answered the rescript: "Your Majesty stands in awe of Heaven, mourns these omens, has opened the court to ministers, and summoned blunt speakers because you wish to read the mind of Heaven and learn where government has erred.
entries.literal: Qin submitted reply, saying, "Your Majesty fears Heaven's command, grieves at changes and prodigies, extends audience to dukes and ministers, raises straight-speaking knights—you will thereby seek Heaven's mind and trace gain and loss.

entries.zh: 臣欽愚戇，經術淺薄，不足以奉大對。
entries.en: Your servant Du Qin is dull-witted and poorly versed in the classics—hardly fit to answer so weighty an examination.
entries.literal: Your servant Qin is foolish and blunt; his classical learning is shallow and thin—not enough to undertake this great reply.

entries.zh: 臣聞日蝕、地震，陽微陰盛也。
entries.en: I have read that eclipses and earthquakes betoken feeble yang and rampant yin.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that solar eclipse and earthquake mean yang is slight and yin is abundant.

entries.zh: 臣者，君之陰也；
entries.en: Ministers are the yin counterpart to their sovereign;
entries.literal: The minister is the ruler's yin;

entries.zh: 子者，父之陰也；
entries.en: sons are the yin of their fathers;
entries.literal: the son is the father's yin;

entries.zh: 妻者，夫之陰也；
entries.en: wives are the yin of their husbands;
entries.literal: the wife is the husband's yin;

entries.zh: 夷狄者，中國之陰也。
entries.en: and the barbarians are the yin of the Central States.
entries.literal: the barbarians are the Central States' yin.

entries.zh: 《春秋》日蝕三十六，地震五，或夷狄侵中國，或政權在臣下，或婦乘夫，或臣子背君父，事雖不同，其類一也。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn records thirty-six eclipses and five earthquakes: some coincided with barbarian invasions, some with ministerial dictatorship, some with wives dominating husbands, some with subjects betraying their lords—different events, one pattern.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn records thirty-six solar eclipses and five earthquakes—sometimes barbarians invaded the Central States, sometimes government power lay under ministers, sometimes wives rode atop husbands, sometimes sons and ministers betrayed lord and father; though the affairs differed, the category was one.

entries.zh: 臣竊觀人事以考變異，則本朝大臣無不自安之人，外戚親屬無乖刺之心，關東諸侯無強大之國，三垂蠻夷無逆理之節；
entries.en: When I weigh human affairs against these omens, I find no minister at court nursing sedition, no imperial in-laws nursing grudges, no eastern kingdom strong enough to challenge the throne, no frontier tribe openly defying the moral order;
entries.literal: Your servant privately views human affairs to examine prodigies—then this court's great ministers have none who are not self-secure; affinal kin have no perverse-thorn hearts; east of the Pass the feudal lords have no mighty great states; on the three frontiers the barbarians have no contrary-to-pattern conduct;

entries.zh: 殆為後宮。
entries.en: the source must lie in the harem.
entries.literal: probably it is the rear palace.

entries.zh: 何以言之？
entries.en: Why do I say so?
entries.literal: How do I say it?

entries.zh: 日以戊申蝕。
entries.en: The eclipse fell on the day wushen.
entries.literal: The sun was eclipsed on wushen day.

entries.zh: 時加未。
entries.en: The hour was wei.
entries.literal: The hour added was wei.

entries.zh: 戊未，土也。
entries.en: Both wu and wei belong to the element earth.
entries.literal: Wu and wei are earth.

entries.zh: 土者，中宮之部也。
entries.en: Earth governs the central palace—the empress's domain.
entries.literal: Earth is the department of the central palace.

entries.zh: 其夜地震未央宮殿中，此必適妾將有爭寵相害而為患者，唯陛下深戒之。
entries.en: That very night the earth shook inside Weiyang Palace. The omen points to rival concubines contending for your favor and doing one another harm. I beg Your Majesty to take it to heart.
entries.literal: That night the earth shook within Weiyang Palace—this must mean secondary consorts will contend for favor and harm one another and become a scourge; only may Your Majesty deeply guard against it.

entries.zh: 變感以類相應，人事失於下，變象見於上。
entries.en: Heaven answers human misconduct in kind: error below, portent above.
entries.literal: Prodigies respond by category to one another; human affairs miss below, prodigy images appear above.

entries.zh: 能應之以德，則異咎消亡；
entries.en: Meet them with true virtue and the ill omens will fade;
entries.literal: If able to respond to them with virtue, then strange blame is extinguished;

entries.zh: 不能應之以善，則禍敗至。
entries.en: fail to reform, and ruin follows.
entries.literal: if not able to respond to them with goodness, then disaster and defeat arrive.

entries.zh: 高宗遭雊雉之戒，飭己正事，享百年之壽，殷道復興，要在所以應之。
entries.en: Gaozong of Shang heeded the warning of the crowing pheasant, corrected himself and set affairs right, enjoyed a lifespan of a hundred years, and restored the Shang way. Everything turns on how a ruler responds to such a warning.
entries.literal: Gaozong received the pheasant's crowing warning, corrected himself and set affairs right, enjoyed a hundred years' life, Yin's way again rose—the crux lies in how one responds.

entries.zh: 應之非誠不立，非信不行。
entries.en: Such a response must be sincere to endure and trustworthy to succeed.
entries.literal: To respond, without sincerity it does not stand; without trust it does not proceed.

entries.zh: 宋景公，小國之諸侯耳，有不忍移禍之誠，出人君之言三，熒惑為之退捨。
entries.en: Duke Jing of Song was lord of a minor state, yet his unwillingness to shift calamity onto his subjects was so genuine that he thrice spoke as a true sovereign should—and Mars changed its course for him.
entries.literal: Duke Jing of Song, a small state's feudal lord, had the sincerity of not shifting disaster; he uttered the lord's words three times, and the Sparkling Deluder for him withdrew and halted.

entries.zh: 以陛下聖明，內推至誠，深思天變，何應而不感？
entries.en: Your Majesty is wise enough to search your heart, ponder these signs in utmost good faith, and move Heaven itself.
entries.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely clarity, inwardly pushing utmost sincerity, deeply pondering Heaven's changes—what response would not be moved?

entries.zh: 何搖而不動？
entries.en: What stubborn ill could then resist you?
entries.literal: What shaking would not be stirred?

entries.zh: 孔子曰：『仁遠乎哉！』
entries.en: Confucius asked, "Is humanity really so far away?"
entries.literal: Confucius said, "Is benevolence far away?"

entries.zh: 唯陛下正後妾，抑女寵，防奢泰，去佚游，躬節儉，親萬事，數御安車，由輦道，親二宮之饔膳，致晨昏之定省。
entries.en: Set the harem in proper order, curb excessive favoritism, shun luxury and idle excursions, practice frugality, and attend personally to government. Ride often by the palace carriageways to oversee the meals in both senior palaces and perform the morning and evening courtesies owed to your elders.
entries.literal: May Your Majesty set the ranks of empress and consorts in order, restrain favoritism toward women, guard against extravagance, abandon idle excursions, personally practice frugality, attend to the myriad affairs, frequently ride the quiet carriage along the imperial carriageway, personally inspect the meals in the two palaces, and perform the morning and evening inquiries after your elders' health.

entries.zh: 如此，即堯、舜不足與比隆，咎異何足消滅？
entries.en: Do this, and you will surpass even Yao and Shun—what omen could stand against you?
entries.literal: If thus, then Yao and Shun are not enough to compare in loftiness—how could strange blame suffice to be extinguished?

entries.zh: 如不留聽於庶事，不論材而授位，殫天下之財以奉淫侈，匱萬姓之力以從耳目，近諂諛之人而遠公方，信讒賊之臣以誅忠良，賢俊失在巖穴，大臣怨於不以，雖無變異、社稷之憂也。
entries.en: But if you ignore the business of government, hand posts to unfit men, squander the treasury on debauchery, grind the people down to amuse your senses, flatterers at your elbow while honest men stand far off, believe slander and kill the loyal until talent hides in the hills and great ministers nurse resentment—then even without eclipses or tremors, the altars of state are already in peril.
entries.literal: If you do not retain listening in the myriad affairs, do not discuss talent and grant office, exhaust the empire's wealth to serve dissolute extravagance, drain the myriad surnames' strength to follow ears and eyes, draw near to fawning sycophants and distance the public and upright, trust slanderous wicked ministers to execute the loyal and good, so that worthy and outstanding are lost in cliff caves and great ministers resent not being used—although there are no prodigies, there is worry for altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 天下至大，萬事至眾，祖業至重，誠不可以佚豫為，不可以奢泰持也。
entries.en: The realm is vast, its business endless, and the patrimony you hold is heavy beyond measure: you cannot rule by self-indulgence or maintain it through excess.
entries.literal: The empire is greatest, the myriad affairs most numerous, the ancestral enterprise weightiest—truly one cannot act with idle ease, cannot hold with extravagance and excess.

entries.zh: 唯陛下忍無益之欲，以全眾庶之命。
entries.en: I beg you to renounce pleasures that profit nothing and so preserve the lives of your people.
entries.literal: Only may Your Majesty endure and set aside profitless desires, thereby to preserve the multitude of commoners' lives.

entries.zh: 臣欽愚戇，言不足采。」
entries.en: Your foolish servant has said more than his deserts; whether any of it merits heed is for Your Majesty alone to judge."
entries.literal: Your servant Qin is foolish and blunt; his words are not worth gathering."

entries.zh: 鳳白之太后，太后以為故事無有。
entries.en: When Feng laid the memorial before the empress dowager, she replied that no precedent existed for what he proposed.
entries.literal: Feng reported it to the empress dowager; the empress dowager thought by precedent there was none.

entries.zh: 欽復重言：「《詩》云：『殷監不遠，在夏後氏之世』。
entries.en: Qin pressed his case again, quoting the Book of Odes: "Yin's mirror is not far off—it lies in the house of Xia.
entries.literal: Qin again emphasized, saying, "The Songs says, 'Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the house of the Xia royal house.

entries.zh: 刺戒者至迫近，而省聽者常怠忽，可不慎哉！
entries.en: The warning voices are close at hand, yet rulers grow deaf to them—can we afford to be careless?
entries.literal: Those who prick and warn are extremely close, yet those who listen are always negligent—can one not be cautious!

entries.zh: 前言九女，略陳其禍福，甚可悼懼，竊恐將軍不深留意。
entries.en: My earlier memorial on the nine imperial concubines sketched their blessings and curses in frightening detail; I fear Your Lordship has not weighed it seriously enough.
entries.literal: The former words on nine daughters, briefly displaying their disaster and fortune, were very worthy of grief and fear; I privately fear the general does not deeply attend.

entries.zh: 后妃之制，夭壽治亂存亡之端也。
entries.en: The institution of empress and harem is where the fate of dynasties turns—whether rulers die young or live long, whether the realm thrives or falls.
entries.literal: The system of empress and consorts is the tip of early death, long life, order, chaos, survival, and destruction.

entries.zh: 跡三代之季世，覽宗、宣之饗國，察近屬之符驗，禍敗曷常不由女德？
entries.en: Trace the last generations of the Three Dynasties, consider how long Gaozong of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou enjoyed their realms, and examine the signs confirmed among more recent kin: when did disaster and ruin not turn on the conduct of women?
entries.literal: Trace the final generations of the Three Dynasties, consider Gaozong and King Xuan's long possession of their realms, and examine the signs confirmed among more recent kin: when did disaster and ruin not arise from the conduct of women?

entries.zh: 是以佩玉晏鳴，《關雎》歎之，知好色之伐性短年，離制度之生無厭，天下將蒙化，陵夷而成俗也。
entries.en: Thus the jade pendants sounded late, and the "Guanju" lamented it. Indulgence in beauty wastes a ruler's vitality and shortens his life; once established limits are abandoned, desire becomes insatiable, and the realm follows the palace until decadence hardens into custom.
entries.literal: Thus the jade pendants sounded late, and the "Guanju" lamented it. It understood that indulgence in beauty injures one's nature and shortens life, while departure from established limits breeds insatiable desire; the realm will absorb that influence until decline becomes custom.

entries.zh: 故詠淑女，幾以配上，忠孝之篤，仁厚之作也。
entries.en: That is why the ode celebrates a virtuous maiden fit to be matched with the ruler: it was composed from profound loyalty, filial devotion, and humane concern.
entries.literal: Thus it sang of a virtuous maiden, hoping to match her with the ruler. This arose from the deepest loyalty and filial devotion, and from humane concern.

entries.zh: 夫君親壽尊，國家治安，誠臣子至願，所當勉之也。
entries.en: Long life and high honor for ruler and father, peace for state and family—that is every loyal subject's prayer and his proper goal.
entries.literal: Now if lord and parent live long and honored, state and family are peaceful and secure—this is truly what ministers and sons most desire, what they ought to strive for.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：『正其本，萬物理。』
entries.en: As the Classic of Changes puts it, "Set the root straight and the myriad things fall into order."
entries.literal: The Changes says, "Correct its root, and the myriad things obtain their pattern."

entries.zh: 凡事論有疑未可立行者，求之往古則典刑無，考之來今則吉凶同，卒搖易之則民心惑，若是者誠難施也。
entries.en: Whenever policy is uncertain, looking backward yields no clear precedent and looking around shows only mixed results; flip-flopping further confuses the people—such measures are nearly impossible to enforce.
entries.literal: Whenever in deliberating affairs there is doubt and what cannot be established and carried out, seeking it in the past ancient then models and punishments are not; examining it in coming present then good and ill are the same; finally shaking and changing it then the people's hearts are doubtful—such as this is truly hard to apply.

entries.zh: 今九女之制，合於往古，無害於今，不逆於民心，至易行也，行之至有福也，將軍輔政而不蚤定，非天下之所望也。
entries.en: The ancient rule limiting the harem to nine secondary consorts fits antiquity, injures nothing today, and offends no popular sentiment; it could be enacted tomorrow to the empire's great good. Yet you govern as regent and still delay—this is not what the realm expects of you.
entries.literal: Now the nine-daughters system matches the past ancient, harms not the present, does not oppose the people's heart, is extremely easy to carry out; carrying it out reaches greatest blessing; the general assists government yet does not early fix it—not what the empire hopes for.

entries.zh: 唯將軍信臣子之願，念《關雎》之思，逮委政之隆，及始初清明，為漢家建無窮之基，誠難以忽，不可以遴。」
entries.en: I beg you to heed a loyal subject, recall the lesson of "Guanju," seize this moment of paramount authority while your judgment is still lucid, and lay an unshakable foundation for Han. The matter is too grave to shrug off or postpone."
entries.literal: Only may the general trust your servant-son's wish, think on Guanju's thought, seize the height of delegated government's vigor, and while the beginning is still clear and bright, for the Han house establish inexhaustible foundation—truly hard to neglect, cannot be put aside."

entries.zh: 鳳不能自立法度，循故事而已。
entries.en: Wang Feng lacked the courage to innovate; he hid behind precedent.
entries.literal: Feng could not himself establish law degrees; he followed precedent only.

entries.zh: 會皇太后女弟司馬君力與欽兄子私通，事上聞，欽慚懼，乞骸骨去。
entries.en: Then it came out that the empress dowager's younger sister Sima Junli had carried on an affair with Qin's nephew. Qin, mortified and terrified, resigned his post.
entries.literal: It happened that the empress dowager's younger sister Sima Junli had private intercourse with Qin's elder brother's son; the affair ascended to hearing; Qin was ashamed and afraid, begged bones and departed.

entries.zh: 征詣大將軍莫府，國家政謀，鳳常與欽慮之。
entries.en: He was then summoned to Grand General Wang Feng's headquarters, where Feng habitually discussed state strategy with him.
entries.literal: Summoned to the grand general's headquarters—state policy and stratagem—Feng constantly deliberated them with Qin.

entries.zh: 數稱達名士王駿、韋安世、王延世等，救解馮野王、王尊、胡常之罪過，及繼功臣絕世，填撫四夷，當世善政，多出於欽者。
entries.en: He repeatedly praised worthy men such as Wang Jun, Wei Anshi, and Wang Yanshi to high office, cleared Feng Yewang, Wang Zun, and Hu Chang of unjust charges, restored titles to meritorious families whose lines had failed, and soothed the frontier tribes—most of the era's sound policies owed something to Du Qin.
entries.literal: Repeatedly he praised and advanced noted gentlemen Wang Jun, Wei Anshi, Wang Yanshi, and others, rescued and explained the faults of Feng Yewang, Wang Zun, and Hu Chang, and as to continuing meritorious ministers' cut-off lines, filling and soothing the four barbarians—good government of the age mostly came from Qin.

entries.zh: 見鳳專政泰重，戒之曰：「昔周公身有至聖之德，屬有叔父之親，而成王有獨見之明，無信讒之聽，然管、蔡流言而周公懼。
entries.en: Seeing Wang Feng's grip on power grow oppressive, Du Qin warned him: "The Duke of Zhou was the paragon of sagehood and the king's uncle, and King Cheng was a discerning sovereign who refused slander—yet the rumor spread by Guan and Cai still struck terror into the duke.
entries.literal: Seeing Feng monopolized government too heavily, he warned him, saying, "Formerly the Duke of Zhou personally had utmost sage virtue, in kinship had uncle relation, yet King Cheng had alone-seeing clarity, had no listening to slander—still Guan and Cai spread drifting words and the Duke of Zhou feared.

entries.zh: 穰侯，昭王之舅也，權重於秦，威震鄰敵，有旦莫偃伏之愛，心不介然有間，然范雎起徒步，由異國，無雅信，開一朝之說，而穰侯就封。
entries.en: Marquis Rang, uncle to King Zhao of Qin, dominated that state and awed its neighbors; he shared the king's pillow and board without a shadow between them—yet Fan Ju, a stranger on foot, won a single hearing and sent Rang packing to his domain.
entries.literal: Marquis Rang was King Zhao of Qin maternal uncle; his weight of power was in Qin, his awesomeness shook neighboring enemies; he had morning-and-evening couch-bending love, his mind was not stuck with a gap—yet Fan Ju rose from walking the roads, came from a different state, had no long-standing trust, opened one morning persuasion, and Marquis Rang went to his fief.

entries.zh: 及近者武安侯之見退，三事之跡，相去各數百歲，若合符節，甚不可不察。
entries.en: Add the recent fall of the Marquis of Wu'an: three lessons centuries apart that fit together like matching tallies. They demand your deepest reflection.
entries.literal: As to the near case of the Marquis of Wu an being dismissed—the three affairs traces, separated by several hundred years each, match tally and seal—very much cannot fail to be examined.

entries.zh: 願將軍由周公之謙懼，損穰侯之威，放武安之欲，毋使范雎之徒得間其說。」
entries.en: I urge you to keep the Duke of Zhou's humility, shed Marquis Rang's arrogance, and curb the appetites that ruined the Marquis of Wu'an—lest another Fan Ju find a crack through which to speak."
entries.literal: I wish the general would take the Duke of Zhou humble fear, diminish Marquis Rang awesomeness, release the Marquis of Wu an desires, and not let a Fan Ju class obtain a gap for his persuasion."

entries.zh: 頃之，復日蝕，京兆尹王章上封事求見，果言鳳專權蔽主之過，宜廢勿用，以應天變。
entries.en: Soon another eclipse darkened the sun. Wang Zhang, governor of the capital, sealed a memorial and begged an audience, denouncing Wang Feng for monopolizing power and blinding the throne. He urged that Feng be removed to answer Heaven.
entries.literal: Before long, again solar eclipse; Metropolitan Governor Wang Zhang submitted a sealed memorial requesting audience, and indeed spoke of Feng monopolizing power and covering the ruler fault—it was fitting to dismiss and not use him, to respond to Heaven change.

entries.zh: 於是天子感悟，召見章，與議，欲退鳳。
entries.en: The emperor was stirred, received Wang Zhang in audience, and began to consider dismissing Feng.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven was moved and awakened, summoned and saw Wang Zhang, and with him deliberated, wishing to retire Feng.

entries.zh: 鳳甚憂懼，欽令鳳上疏謝罪，乞骸骨，文指甚哀。
entries.en: Feng was terrified. Du Qin had him memorialize an abject apology and offer to resign—the wording was heart-rending.
entries.literal: Feng was greatly worried and afraid; Qin ordered Feng to submit a memorial apologizing for guilt, begging bones; the text intent was very piteous.

entries.zh: 太后涕泣為不食。
entries.en: The empress dowager wept and refused her meals for his sake.
entries.literal: The empress dowager wept tears and for him did not eat.

entries.zh: 上少而親倚鳳，亦不忍廢，復起鳳就位。
entries.en: The emperor, who had leaned on Feng since boyhood, could not bear to cast him off and restored him to power.
entries.literal: The ruler from youth had been intimate with and relied on Feng, also could not bear to dismiss him, again raised Feng to take his position.

entries.zh: 鳳心慚，稱病篤，欲遂退。
entries.en: Chastened, Feng pleaded grave illness and tried to withdraw.
entries.literal: Feng heart was ashamed; he claimed illness was grave, wishing thereupon to retire.

entries.zh: 欽復說之曰：「將軍深悼輔政十年，變異不已，故乞骸骨，歸咎於身，刻己自責，至誠動眾，愚知莫不感傷。
entries.en: Du Qin urged him again: "Your memorial blames yourself for ten years of ill omens under your regency and asks to retire—such self-reproach moves every heart, high or low.
entries.literal: Qin again persuaded him, saying, "The general deeply grieves that in ten years of assisting government prodigies have not ceased—therefore begging bones, returning blame to the self, carving the self and blaming the self—utmost sincerity moves the multitude; foolish and wise none are not moved and wounded.

entries.zh: 雖然，是無屬之臣，執進退之分，絜其去就之節者耳，非主上所以待將軍，非將軍所以報主上也。
entries.en: Yet that is only the language of a disposable clerk who minds his own exit—hardly what a loyal minister owes his sovereign, or a sovereign owes the pillar of his state.
entries.literal: Although it is so, this is the conduct of a minister without attachment, who holds the division of advance and retreat and marks the knot of going and staying—no more. It is not what the ruler uses to treat the general, nor what the general uses to repay the ruler.

entries.zh: 昔周公雖老，猶在京師，明不離成周，示不忘王室也。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou stayed in the capital in old age to show he never abandoned the royal city or the king.
entries.literal: Formerly although the Duke of Zhou was old, he still was in the capital region, making clear he did not leave Cheng Zhou, showing he did not forget the royal house.

entries.zh: 仲山父異姓之臣，無親於宣，就封於齊，猶歎息永懷，宿夜徘徊，不忍遠去，況將軍之於主上，主上之與將軍哉！
entries.en: Zhong Shanfu, no kin to King Xuan, still lingered in sorrow when posted to Qi—how much more should you, bound to the emperor by blood and office?
entries.literal: Zhong Shanfu was a minister of different surname, without closeness to Xuan, yet when he went to his fief in Qi still sighed long thoughts, lodged night wandering, could not bear to go far—how much more the general toward the lord above, the lord above toward the general!

entries.zh: 夫欲天下治安變異之意，莫有將軍，主上照然知之，故攀援不遣，《書》稱『公毋困我！』
entries.en: No one cares more than you for the realm's peace or for ending these portents, and the emperor knows it. That is why he holds on to you and refuses to let you go. In the Documents, King Cheng pleads, "Duke, do not leave me in distress!"
entries.literal: No one desires the realm's peace and an end to the portents more than you, General. The ruler knows this clearly, and so he clings to you and will not let you depart. The Documents says, "Duke, do not leave me in distress!"

entries.zh: 唯將軍不為四國流言自疑於成王，以固至忠。」
entries.en: Do not let rumors like those spread by the four rebel states give your King Cheng reason to doubt you. Make your perfect loyalty unmistakable."
entries.literal: Only do not let the rumors of the four states cause King Cheng to suspect you, General; thereby make your utmost loyalty secure."

entries.zh: 鳳復起視事。
entries.en: Wang Feng returned to duty.
entries.literal: Feng again rose and attended to affairs.

entries.zh: 上令尚書劾奏京兆尹章，章死詔獄。
entries.en: The emperor then ordered the Masters of Writing to impeach Wang Zhang, who died in the imperial prison.
entries.literal: The ruler ordered the Masters of Writing to impeach and memorialize Metropolitan Governor Wang Zhang; Wang Zhang died in imperial-order prison.

entries.zh: 語在《元后傳》。
entries.en: The full story is told in the biography of Empress Yuan.
entries.literal: The words are in the biography of Empress Yuan.

entries.zh: 章既死，眾庶冤之，以譏朝廷。
entries.en: The people believed Wang Zhang had been wronged, and the court became a laughingstock.
entries.literal: When Wang Zhang had died, the multitude of commoners thought him wronged, thereby to ridicule the court.

entries.zh: 欽欲救其過，復說鳳曰：「京兆尹章所坐事密，吏民見章素好言事，以為不坐官職，疑其以日蝕見對有所言也。
entries.en: Du Qin, hoping to repair the damage, again urged Feng: "The charge against Metropolitan Governor Wang Zhang was never made public. The capital supposes that because he always spoke boldly on policy, he lost his life not for corruption but for what he said about the eclipse.
entries.literal: Qin wished to repair the fault, and again urged Feng, saying, "The charge against Metropolitan Governor Wang Zhang was kept secret; officials and people saw that Wang Zhang had always loved to speak on affairs, and thought he was not guilty of an offense against his office—they suspected that in his reply at the policy examination after the solar eclipse he had said something.

entries.zh: 假令章內有所犯，雖陷正法，事不暴揚，自京師不曉，況於遠方。
entries.en: Even if he were guilty of some private crime, a quiet execution would have left the capital guessing, to say nothing of the provinces.
entries.literal: Suppose Wang Zhang inwardly had something he violated; although sunk in correct law, the affair was not violently displayed—from the capital they did not understand, how much more the distant regions.

entries.zh: 恐天下不知章實有罪，而以為坐言事也。
entries.en: I fear the realm will conclude he was executed for honest counsel, not for proven guilt.
entries.literal: I fear the empire does not know Wang Zhang in fact had guilt, and thinks he sat guilty for speaking on affairs.

entries.zh: 如是，塞爭引之原，損寬明之德。
entries.en: That would choke off frank advice and tarnish your reputation for fairness.
entries.literal: If thus, then it blocks the spring of contention and citation, injures the virtue of breadth and clarity.

entries.zh: 欽愚以為宜因章事舉直言極諫，並見郎從官展盡其章，加於往前，以明示四方，使天下咸知主上聖明，不以言罪下也。
entries.en: I suggest you use this case to invite the harshest criticism: let every gentleman-attendant and staff officer air his views more freely than before, so the whole empire will see that the sage Son of Heaven does not punish men for speaking out.
entries.literal: Qin foolishly thinks it is fitting to take Wang Zhang affair to raise straight speech and utmost remonstrance, together see gentlemen-attendants and follower officials unfold their memorials to the full, add beyond what went before, thereby to make clear to the four quarters, cause the empire all to know the ruler is sagely clear and does not by words blame subordinates.

entries.zh: 若此，則流言消釋，疑惑著明。」
entries.en: Then rumor will die away and suspicion will clear."
entries.literal: If thus, then drifting words dissolve and melt, doubt and confusion are made clear."

entries.zh: 鳳白行其策。
entries.en: Feng adopted the plan and put it into effect.
entries.literal: Feng reported and carried out his plan.

entries.zh: 欽之補過將美，皆此類也。
entries.en: Du Qin's habit of covering others' missteps while advancing what was right ran in this vein.
entries.literal: Qin mending fault and advancing beauty were all of this kind.

entries.zh: 杜周，南陽杜衍人也。
entries.en: Du Zhou came from Duyang in Nanyang commandery.
entries.literal: Du Zhou was a man of Duyang in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 義縱為南陽太守，以周為爪牙，薦之張湯，為廷尉史。
entries.en: When Yi Zong served as governor of Nanyang, he used Du Zhou as his enforcer and recommended him to Zhang Tang, who took him on as a clerk in the office of the commandant of justice.
entries.literal: Yi Zong was governor of Nanyang; he took Zhou as claw and fang, recommended him to Zhang Tang, and he became a clerk of the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 使案邊失亡，所論殺甚多。
entries.en: He was dispatched to investigate frontier casualties and desertions; the death sentences he procured ran very high.
entries.literal: He was sent to investigate border losses and desertions; those he sentenced and killed were very many.

entries.zh: 奏事中意，任用，與減宣更為中丞者十餘歲。
entries.en: His reports consistently matched the emperor's wishes, and for more than ten years he and Jian Xuan alternated as Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: His memorials accorded with the emperor's wishes, so he was employed and alternated with Jian Xuan as Censor-in-Chief for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 騫身所至者，大宛、大月氏、大夏、康居，而傳聞其旁大國五六，具為天子言其地形所有，語皆在《西域傳》。
entries.en: In person he had reached Dayuan, the Greater Yuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju, and by report knew five or six other great kingdoms nearby; he laid all of this—lands and resources—before the emperor, as recorded in the Western Regions treatise.
entries.literal: As for places Qian himself reached, there were Dayuan, the Greater Yuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju, and by hearsay five or six great states beside them; he fully reported to the Son of Heaven their terrain and what they possessed; the words are all in the "Treatise on the Western Regions."

entries.zh: 騫曰：「臣在大夏時，見邛竹杖、蜀布，問：『安得此？』
entries.en: Zhang Qian said, "In Daxia I saw bamboo canes from Qiong and cloth from Shu and asked, 'How did these come here?'
entries.literal: Qian said, "When your servant was in Daxia, I saw Qiong bamboo staffs and Shu cloth and asked, 'How did these come here?'

entries.zh: 大夏國人曰：『吾賈人往市之身毒國。
entries.en: They answered, 'Our traders brought them back from Shendu (India).
entries.literal: The people of Daxia said, 'Our merchants went to buy them in the Shendu state.

entries.zh: 身毒國在大夏東南可數千里。
entries.en: Shendu lies some thousands of li southeast of Daxia.
entries.literal: The Shendu state is in Daxia's southeast, perhaps several thousand li.

entries.zh: 其俗土著，與大夏同，而卑濕暑熱。
entries.en: The people are settled like those of Daxia, but the land is low, humid, and sweltering.
entries.literal: Its customs are sedentary, the same as Daxia's, but low-lying, damp, and hot in summer.

entries.zh: 其民乘象以戰。
entries.en: They fight from the backs of elephants.
entries.literal: Its people mount elephants to fight.

entries.zh: 其國臨大水焉。』
entries.en: Their country fronts on a great river.'
entries.literal: Its state borders a great water.'

entries.zh: 以騫度之，大夏去漢萬二千里，居西南。
entries.en: By Zhang Qian's estimate Daxia stood twelve thousand li from the capital, to the southwest.
entries.literal: By Qian's reckoning, Daxia is twelve thousand li from Han and lies in the southwest.

entries.zh: 今身毒又居大夏東南數千里，有蜀物，此其去蜀不遠矣。
entries.en: Shendu lies thousands of li beyond Daxia to the southeast yet already has Shu goods—so it cannot be far from Shu itself.
entries.literal: Now Shendu again lies several thousand li southeast of Daxia and has Shu goods; this means it is not far from Shu.

entries.zh: 今使大夏，從羌中，險，羌人惡之；
entries.en: The route to Daxia through Qiang territory is dangerous, and the Qiang resent intruders;
entries.literal: Now to send envoys to Daxia through the Qiang region is perilous, and the Qiang detest it;

entries.zh: 少北，則為匈奴所得；
entries.en: veer slightly north and the Xiongnu take you;
entries.literal: a little to the north, then one is taken by the Xiongnu;

entries.zh: 從蜀，宜徑，又無寇。」
entries.en: from Shu the way should be straighter and free of marauders."
entries.literal: from Shu it should be a direct route and moreover without raiders."

entries.zh: 天子既聞大宛及大夏、安息之屬皆大國，多奇物，土著，頗與中國同俗，而兵弱，貴漢財物；
entries.en: The emperor had learned that Dayuan, Daxia, Parthia, and their neighbors were large, settled kingdoms rich in curiosities, with customs not unlike China's, weak armies, and a hunger for Han wealth;
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven having heard that Dayuan and Daxia, Anxi, and the like were all great states, with many strange goods, sedentary populations, customs rather like China's, yet weak in arms and valuing Han goods;

entries.zh: 其北則大月氏、康居之屬，兵強，可以賂遺設利朝也。
entries.en: north of them lay the Greater Yuezhi and Kangju—hard fighters who might nonetheless be courted with bribes and profit.
entries.literal: to their north were the Greater Yuezhi, Kangju, and the like, strong in arms, who could be drawn by gifts and profit to court audience.

entries.zh: 誠得而以義屬之，則廣地萬里，重九譯，致殊俗，威德遍於四海。
entries.en: If they could be bound in good faith to the throne, Han might stretch ten thousand li, speak through chains of interpreters to distant peoples, and spread its majesty to the ends of the earth.
entries.literal: If truly obtained and by righteousness made subject, then lands would extend ten thousand li, repeated ninefold interpretation would reach strange customs, and awe-inspiring virtue would spread over the four seas.

entries.zh: 天子欣欣以騫言為然。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and accepted Zhang Qian's counsel.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven gladly deemed Qian's words correct.

entries.zh: 乃令因蜀犍為發間使，四道並出：出駹，出莋，出徙、邛，出僰，皆各行一二千里。
entries.en: He ordered secret missions from Shu and Jianwei along four routes—through Mang, Zuo, Xi and Qiong, and Bo—each probing one or two thousand li.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered that from Shu and Jianwei secret envoys be dispatched, four routes going out together: out by Mang, out by Zuo, out by Xi and Qiong, out by Bo, each going one or two thousand li.

entries.zh: 其北方閉氐、莋，南方閉巂、昆明。
entries.en: The Di and Zuo blocked the northern parties; the Xi and Kunming barred the southern ones.
entries.literal: On the northern side they were blocked by the Di and Zuo; on the southern side blocked by Xi and Kunming.

entries.zh: 昆明之屬無君長，善寇盜，輒殺略漢使，終莫得通。
entries.en: The Kunming peoples had no chiefs, lived by raiding, killed and plundered Han envoys, and no road was ever opened through them.
entries.literal: The Kunming sort had no rulers or chiefs, were good at raiding and plundering, repeatedly killed and robbed Han envoys, and in the end passage could not be obtained.

entries.zh: 然聞其西可千餘里，有乘象國，名滇越，而蜀賈間出物者或至焉，於是漢以求大夏道始通滇國。
entries.en: Word had it that a thousand li west lay an elephant-riding realm called Dianyue, where Shu merchants sometimes appeared; in pursuit of a road to Daxia, Han thus opened relations with Dian for the first time.
entries.literal: Yet it was heard that west of them perhaps over a thousand li there was an elephant-riding state named Dianyue, and Shu merchants who occasionally went out with goods sometimes reached there; thereupon Han, in seeking the road to Daxia, first opened communication with the Dian state.

entries.zh: 初，漢欲通西南夷，費多，罷之。
entries.en: Earlier attempts to reach the southwestern tribes had been dropped as too costly.
entries.literal: At first, Han wished to open communication with the southwestern Yi, but the expense was great and it abandoned this.

entries.zh: 及騫言可以通大夏，及復事西南夷。
entries.en: Zhang Qian's report that Daxia could be reached from the southwest revived the whole frontier policy.
entries.literal: When Qian said one could reach Daxia, then again they took up affairs with the southwestern Yi.

entries.zh: 是時，上方數巡狩海上，乃悉從外國客，大都多人則過之，散財帛賞賜，厚具饒給之，以覽視漢富厚焉。
entries.en: The emperor was touring the coast; he brought foreign guests in his train, detouring through populous cities, showering them with silk and cash and lavish rations so they could see how rich Han was.
entries.literal: At this time the sovereign was repeatedly hunting and inspecting along the sea; thereupon he entirely took along foreign guests; where a great metropolis had many people he passed through it, scattering silks and coins as rewards, richly preparing abundant supplies for them, in order to let them survey and see Han's wealth and thickness.

entries.zh: 大角氐，出奇戲諸怪物，多聚觀者，行賞賜，酒池肉林，令外國客遍觀名各倉庫府臧之積，欲以見漢廣大，傾駭之。
entries.en: He staged bullfights, exotic spectacles, and freak shows before crowds, heaped rewards on guests, spread the proverbial pools of wine and forests of meat, and marched them through every state granary and treasury—anything to stagger them with Han's scale.
entries.literal: Great horned wrestlers, displaying strange plays and various monsters, many gathered watchers; he carried out rewards and gifts; pools of wine and forests of meat; he ordered foreign guests everywhere to view the accumulations in each named granary, treasury, and storehouse, wishing thereby to show Han's vastness and overturn and awe them.

entries.zh: 及加其眩者之工，而角氐奇戲歲增變，其益興，自此始。
entries.en: Conjurers grew more skilled, the arena shows multiplied and changed year by year, and the fashion for such display dates from this period.
entries.literal: And increasing the illusionists' craft, while horned-wrestler strange plays yearly increased and changed, their further flourishing began from this.

entries.zh: 而外國使更來更去。
entries.en: Foreign embassies began passing in and out in a steady stream.
entries.literal: And foreign envoys came and went in alternation.

entries.zh: 大宛以西皆自恃遠，尚驕恣，未可詘以禮羈縻而使也。
entries.en: States west of Ferghana trusted their remoteness, stayed arrogant, and could not yet be managed with courtesy alone.
entries.literal: West of Dayuan all relied on distance, still were arrogant and self-willed, and could not be bent by ritual halter-and-bridle and sent as envoys.

entries.zh: 李廣利，女弟李夫人有寵於上，產昌邑哀王。
entries.en: Li Guangli's sister, the favored Lady Li, had borne Prince Ai of Changyi.
entries.literal: Li Guangli—his younger sister Lady Li had favor with the sovereign and bore King Ai of Changyi.

entries.zh: 太初元年，以廣利為貳師將軍，發屬國六千騎及郡國惡少年數萬人以往，期至貳師城取善馬，故號「貳師將軍」。
entries.en: In the first year of Taichu (104 BCE) he was named Ershi general and given six thousand tribal horse and tens of thousands of adventurers from the commanderies—his brief was to seize the bloodstock at Ershi, whence the title "General of Ershi."
entries.literal: In the first year of Taichu, Guangli was made Ershi general; they raised six thousand cavalry from dependent states and several tens of thousands of rowdy youths from commanderies and kingdoms to go, the term being to reach Ershi city and take fine horses; therefore he was titled "Ershi general."

entries.zh: 故浩侯王恢使道軍。
entries.en: The former Marquis of Hao, Wang Hui, served as route guide for the expedition.
entries.literal: Former Marquis of Hao Wang Hui was sent to guide the army.

entries.zh: 既西過鹽水，當道小國各堅城守，不肯給食，攻之不能下。
entries.en: West of the salt desert every petty state barred its gates, refused provisions, and could not be stormed.
entries.literal: Having gone west and crossed the salt water, each small state athwart the road firmly guarded its walls, was unwilling to supply food, and when attacked could not be taken.

entries.zh: 下者得食，不下者數日則去。
entries.en: Cities that yielded fed them; those that held out were abandoned after a few days.
entries.literal: Those taken supplied food; those not taken, after several days, then departed.

entries.zh: 比至郁成，士財有數千，皆饑罷。
entries.en: By Yucheng only a few thousand starving, spent men remained.
entries.literal: By the time they reached Yucheng, soldiers were only several thousand in number, all hungry and exhausted.

entries.zh: 攻郁成城，郁成距之，所殺傷甚眾。
entries.en: They assaulted Yucheng; the garrison held, and Han losses were heavy.
entries.literal: They attacked Yucheng city; Yucheng resisted them, and those killed and wounded were very many.

entries.zh: 貳師將軍與左右計：「至郁成尚不能舉，況至其王都乎？」
entries.en: General Ershi told his officers, "If we cannot crack Yucheng, what hope have we of the capital?"
entries.literal: The Ershi general consulted his staff: "Reaching Yucheng we still cannot take it—how much more their royal capital?"

entries.zh: 引而還。
entries.en: He ordered a retreat.
entries.literal: He led them and returned.

entries.zh: 往來二歲，至敦煌，士不過什一二。
entries.en: Two years out and back brought them to Dunhuang with barely one man in ten.
entries.literal: Coming and going two years, reaching Dunhuang, soldiers were not more than one or two in ten.

entries.zh: 使使上書言：「道遠，多乏食，且士卒不患戰而患饑。
entries.en: He memorialized: "The march is long, rations fail, and the men dread hunger more than combat.
entries.literal: He sent envoys to submit a memorial saying, "The road is long, food is often lacking, and moreover the soldiers do not fear battle but fear hunger.

entries.zh: 人少，不足以拔宛。
entries.en: We are too few to take Ferghana.
entries.literal: The men are few, insufficient to uproot Dayuan.

entries.zh: 願且罷兵，益發而復往。」
entries.en: Pray let us stand down, raise fresh troops, and try again."
entries.literal: We beg for the moment to halt troops, increase levies, and go again."

entries.zh: 天子聞之，大怒，使使遮玉門關，曰：「軍有敢入，斬之。」
entries.en: The emperor raged and posted guards at the Jade Gate, saying, "If any in the army dares enter, behead him."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven heard this and was greatly angry; he sent envoys to block Jade Gate pass, saying, "If any in the army dares enter, behead him."

entries.zh: 貳師恐，因留屯敦煌。
entries.en: Ershi dared not advance and camped at Dunhuang.
entries.literal: Ershi was afraid and thereupon remained garrisoned at Dunhuang.

entries.zh: 漢使往既多，其少從率進孰於天子，言大宛有善馬在貳師城，匿不肯示漢使。
entries.en: So many missions had returned that junior attendants routinely reported to the throne what they had seen: Ferghana kept its best bloodstock at Ershi and refused to show Han's envoys.
entries.literal: Han envoys having gone in great number, their junior attendants mostly reported their firsthand knowledge to the Son of Heaven, saying Dayuan had fine horses at Ershi city, hid them, and were unwilling to show Han envoys.

entries.zh: 天子既好宛馬，聞之甘心，使壯士車令等待千金及金馬以請宛王貳師城善馬。
entries.en: The emperor, already horse-mad, sent Che Ling with a fortune in gold and a golden horse to buy the Ershi studs from the king of Ferghana.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven already loved Ferghana horses; hearing this he was willing at heart, and sent the stalwart Che Ling and others bearing a thousand in gold weight and a golden horse to request of the king of Dayuan the fine horses at Ershi city.

entries.zh: 宛國饒漢物，相與謀曰：「漢去我遠，而鹽水中數有敗，出其北有胡寇，出其南乏水草，又且往往而絕邑，乏食者多。
entries.en: Ferghana was awash in Han luxuries. Its nobles reasoned: "The capital lies far beyond the salt desert, where caravans founder; north lie the nomads, south little water or grass, and long stretches without towns—most parties starve.
entries.literal: The state of Dayuan was abundant in Han goods; they plotted together, saying, "Han is far from us, and in the salt water there are frequent disasters; going out northward there are Hu raiders, going out southward there is lack of water and grass, and moreover there are often cut-off settlements; many lack food.

entries.zh: 漢使數百人為輩來，常乏食，死者過半，是安能致大軍乎？
entries.en: Han missions arrive in hundreds, usually half dead of hunger—how could they field a real army?
entries.literal: Han envoys come in parties of several hundred men and always lack food; the dead exceed half—how in this case can they bring a great army?

entries.zh: 且貳師馬，宛寶馬也。」
entries.en: Besides, the Ershi horses are our kingdom's treasure."
entries.literal: Moreover the Ershi horses are Dayuan's treasure horses."

entries.zh: 遂不肯予漢使。
entries.en: They refused the sale.
entries.literal: Thereupon they were unwilling to give them to Han envoys.

entries.zh: 漢使怒，妄言，椎金馬而去。
entries.en: The Han envoy lost his temper, hurled abuse, shattered the golden horse, and stalked off.
entries.literal: The Han envoy was angry, spoke wildly, smashed the golden horse, and departed.

entries.zh: 宛中貴人怒曰：「漢使至輕我！」
entries.en: Ferghana's grandees cried, "This envoy has insulted us beyond bearing!"
entries.literal: Dayuan's great men were angry and said, "The Han envoy has grossly slighted us!"

entries.zh: 遣漢使去，令其東邊郁成王遮攻，殺漢使，取其財物。
entries.en: They sent the party on its way, then had Yucheng king on the eastern march ambush it, kill the envoys, and seize the treasure.
entries.literal: They sent the Han envoy away, ordered the king of Yucheng on their eastern border to intercept and attack, killed the Han envoy, and took his goods.

entries.zh: 天子大怒。
entries.en: The emperor was furious.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly angry.

entries.zh: 諸嘗使宛姚定漢等言：「宛兵弱，誠以漢兵不過三千人，強弩射之，即破宛矣。」
entries.en: Veterans of Ferghana such as Yao Dinghan assured the court: "Their army is feeble—three thousand Han crossbowmen would shatter them."
entries.literal: Those who had formerly been envoys to Dayuan, Yao Dinghan and others, said, "Dayuan's troops are weak; truly if Han troops do not exceed three thousand men, with strong crossbows shooting them, then Dayuan will be broken at once."

entries.zh: 天子以嘗使浞野侯攻樓蘭，以七百騎先至，虜其王，以定漢等言為然，而欲侯寵姬李氏，乃以李廣利為將軍，伐宛。
entries.en: The emperor remembered how Zhuoye marquis had taken Loulan with seven hundred horsemen, believed the optimists, and wanting a fief for his favorite Lady Li's kin, named Li Guangli general and sent him against Ferghana.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven because Zhuoye marquis had once attacked Loulan, with seven hundred cavalry arriving first and capturing its king, deemed Yao Dinghan and others' words correct, and wishing to enfeoff the favored concubine Li clan, thereupon made Li Guangli general and attacked Dayuan.

entries.zh: 張騫，漢中人也，建元中為郎。
entries.en: Zhang Qian came from Hanzhong and held a courtier's post in the Jianyuan years.
entries.literal: Zhang Qian was a man of Hanzhong; during the Jianyuan era he served as a gentleman-at-court.

entries.zh: 時，匈奴降者言匈奴破月氏王，以其頭為飲器，月氏遁而怨匈奴，無與共擊之。
entries.en: Defectors from the Xiongnu reported that the nomads had crushed the Yuezhi king and turned his skull into a cup; the Yuezhi had withdrawn in bitterness, with no ally willing to help them strike back.
entries.literal: At that time, defectors from the Xiongnu said the Xiongnu had defeated the king of the Yuezhi and made his skull into a drinking vessel; the Yuezhi had fled and resented the Xiongnu, but had no one to join them in striking the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 漢方欲事滅胡，聞此言，欲通使，道必更匈奴中，乃募能使者。
entries.en: The court was bent on breaking the northern tribes; on hearing this, it wanted to open contact with the Yuezhi, yet any road there ran through Xiongnu territory, so it called for a man willing to make the journey.
entries.literal: Han was at that time intent on destroying the Hu; hearing these words, it wished to send envoys, but the route had necessarily to pass through the Xiongnu, so it recruited one who could go.

entries.zh: 騫以郎應募，使月氏，與堂邑氏奴甘父俱出隴西。
entries.en: Zhang Qian, a courtier, volunteered for the mission to the Yuezhi and set out from Longxi with his guide Ganfu, a Tangyi household slave.
entries.literal: Qian, as a gentleman-at-court, answered the recruitment and was sent to the Yuezhi, together with the Tangyi clan's slave Ganfu, both departing from Longxi.

entries.zh: 徑匈奴，匈奴得之，傳詣單于。
entries.en: They cut across Xiongnu lands, were taken prisoner, and were escorted to the chanyu.
entries.literal: They went straight through the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu seized them and conveyed them to the chanyu.

entries.zh: 單于曰：「月氏在吾北，漢何以得往使？
entries.en: The chanyu asked, "The Yuezhi lie north of me—how does Han imagine it can send envoys past us?
entries.literal: The chanyu said, "The Yuezhi are to my north; how can Han go and send envoys there?

entries.zh: 吾欲使越，漢肯聽我乎？」
entries.en: If I wanted an embassy to cross Han territory into Yue, would your court allow it?"
entries.literal: If I wished to send envoys to Yue, would Han listen to me?"

entries.zh: 留騫十餘歲，予妻，有子，然騫持漢節不失。
entries.en: Qian was held over ten years, given a wife and a child, but he never let go of his Han staff of office.
entries.literal: He detained Qian for more than ten years, gave him a wife, and he had a son, yet Qian held fast to the Han credentials and did not lose them.

entries.zh: 騫以校尉從大將軍擊匈奴，知水草處，軍得以不乏，乃封騫為博望侯。
entries.en: As a colonel under the grand general he guided the army to water and pasture so the troops did not lack; for this he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bowang.
entries.literal: Qian as colonel followed the grand general in striking the Xiongnu; he knew the places of water and grass, so the army was able not to lack supplies, and thereupon Qian was enfeoffed as marquis of Bowang.

entries.zh: 是歲，元朔六年也。
entries.en: This was the sixth year of Yuanshuo (123 BCE).
entries.literal: That year was the sixth year of Yuanshuo.

entries.zh: 後二年，騫為衛尉，與李廣俱出右北平擊匈奴。
entries.en: Two years later, as commandant of the guards, he joined Li Guang in a sortie from Youbeiping against the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: After two years, Qian was commandant of the guards and together with Li Guang both went out of Youbeiping to strike the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 匈奴圍李將軍，軍失亡多，而騫後期當斬，贖為庶人。
entries.en: The Xiongnu encircled Li Guang's command with heavy losses; Zhang Qian arrived late, faced capital sentence, ransomed his rank away, and was reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu surrounded General Li; the army lost and fled many, while Qian was late to the rendezvous and deserved execution; he ransomed himself and became a commoner.

entries.zh: 是歲，驃騎將軍破匈奴西邊，殺數萬人，至祁連山。
entries.en: That same year the flying-charge general shattered the western Xiongnu, killing tens of thousands and pushing to the Qilian range.
entries.literal: That year the flying-charge general broke the Xiongnu western border, killed several tens of thousands, and reached the Qilian Mountains.

entries.zh: 其秋，渾邪王率眾降漢，而金城、河西並南山至鹽澤，空無匈奴。
entries.en: That autumn Hunye king came over with his people, and from Jincheng and the Hexi corridor south to the salt lakes the steppe lay empty of nomads.
entries.literal: That autumn the king of Hunye led his masses to surrender to Han, and from Jincheng and Hexi along the southern mountains to the Salt Marsh it was empty of Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 匈奴時有候者到，而希矣。
entries.en: Occasional Xiongnu scouts still appeared, but they were few.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu at times had scouts arrive, but they were rare.

entries.zh: 後二年，漢擊走單于於幕北。
entries.en: Two years later Han drove the chanyu beyond the northern desert.
entries.literal: After two years, Han struck and drove the chanyu north of the desert curtain.

entries.zh: 初，貳師後行，天子使使告烏孫大發兵擊宛。
entries.en: During Ershi's second march the emperor sent word to Wusun to mobilize heavily against Ferghana.
entries.literal: At first, when Ershi marched later, the Son of Heaven sent envoys to inform Wusun to raise a great army and strike Dayuan.

entries.zh: 烏孫發二千騎往，持兩端，不肯前。
entries.en: Wusun sent two thousand horse but sat on the fence and would not close with the enemy.
entries.literal: Wusun raised two thousand cavalry to go, held both ends, and was unwilling to advance.

entries.zh: 貳師將軍之東，諸所過小國聞宛破，皆使其子弟從入貢獻，見天子，因為質焉。
entries.en: On Ershi's return march every petty state along the road, hearing Ferghana had fallen, sent princes in his train to court with tribute and stayed as hostages.
entries.literal: When the Ershi general went east, the various small states he passed heard Dayuan was broken and all sent their sons and younger brothers to follow in and present tribute, see the Son of Heaven, and thereby become hostages.

entries.zh: 軍還，入玉門者萬餘人，馬千餘匹。
entries.en: More than ten thousand men and a thousand horses crossed back through the Jade Gate.
entries.literal: The army returned; those who entered Jade Gate were over ten thousand men, horses over a thousand head.

entries.zh: 後行，非乏食，戰死不甚多，而將吏貪，不愛卒，侵牟之，以此物故者眾。
entries.en: The second expedition did not starve and lost few in battle, yet greedy officers preyed on the ranks, and most deaths came from that abuse.
entries.literal: On the later march it was not lack of food; battle deaths were not very many, but generals and officers were greedy, did not cherish the soldiers, and encroached on them; for this reason casualties from such causes were many.

entries.zh: 天子為萬里征伐，不錄其過，乃下詔曰：「匈奴為害久矣，今雖徙幕北，與旁國謀共要絕大月氏使，遮殺中郎將江、故雁門守攘。
entries.en: For a march of ten thousand li the emperor overlooked their faults and proclaimed: "The Xiongnu have long plagued the border; though driven north of the desert, they still league with neighbors to ambush Greater Yuezhi embassies and have cut down Palace Gentleman Jiang and former Yanmen warden Rang.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven because of the ten-thousand-li campaign and conquest did not record their faults; thereupon he issued an edict saying, "The Xiongnu have been a harm long; now although they have moved north of the desert curtain, they plot with neighboring states jointly to intercept and cut off Greater Yuezhi envoys, intercepting and killing palace gentleman Jiang and former Yanmen guardian Rang.

entries.zh: 危須以西及大宛皆合約殺期門車令、中郎將朝及身毒國使，隔東西道。
entries.en: From Yanxu west to Ferghana they conspired to murder Expectant Gates Che Ling, Palace Gentleman Chao, and the Indian envoy, severing the road between east and west.
entries.literal: West of Yanxu and including Dayuan all jointly in covenant killed Expectant Gates Che Ling, palace gentleman Chao, and the Shendu-state envoy, cutting off east-west roads.

entries.zh: 貳師將軍廣利征討厥罪，伐勝大宛。
entries.en: General Ershi Li Guangli marched to punish those crimes and conquered Ferghana.
entries.literal: Ershi general Guangli campaigned and punished their crimes, attacked and overcame Dayuan.

entries.zh: 賴天之靈，從溯河山，涉流沙，通西海，山雪不積，士大夫徑度，獲王首虜，珍怪之物畢陳於闕。
entries.en: By heaven's favor they traced rivers, crossed the Gobi, reached the western sea, marched snow-free heights, took enemy kings captive, and heaped rare tribute before the palace.
entries.literal: Relying on heaven's numinous power, following upstream rivers and mountains, crossing shifting sands, opening to the western sea, mountain snow not accumulating, gentlemen officers went straight across, captured kings' heads and captives, and strange precious things were all displayed at the palace gate.

entries.zh: 其封廣利為海西侯，食邑八千戶。」
entries.en: Let Li Guangli be enfeoffed as Marquis of Haixi with eight thousand households."
entries.literal: Let Guangli be enfeoffed marquis of Haixi, with a fief of eight thousand households."

entries.zh: 又封斬郁成王者趙弟為新畤侯；
entries.en: Zhao Di, who had executed the king of Yucheng, was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinzhai;
entries.literal: Moreover he enfeoffed Zhao Di, who had beheaded the king of Yucheng, as marquis of Xinzhai;

entries.zh: 軍正趙始成功最多，為光祿大夫；
entries.en: Army Rectifier Zhao Shicheng, who had piled up the greatest merit, became grand counsellor of the palace;
entries.literal: the army rectifier Zhao Shicheng had the most merit and was made grand counsellor of the palace;

entries.zh: 上官桀敢深入，為少府；
entries.en: Shangguan Jie, commended for pressing deep into enemy country, was named privy treasurer;
entries.literal: Shangguan Jie dared to go deep in and was made privy treasurer;

entries.zh: 李哆有計謀，為上黨太守。
entries.en: Li Duo, valued for his counsel, was appointed governor of Shangdang.
entries.literal: Li Duo had stratagems and was made governor of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 軍官吏為九卿者三人，諸侯相、郡守、二千石百餘人，千石以下千餘人。
entries.en: Three officers rose to the nine senior ministries; more than a hundred became chancellors of nobles, commandery governors, or two-thousand-dan officials; over a thousand received ranks of a thousand dan or less.
entries.literal: Of army officers and clerks, three became one of the nine ministers; over a hundred became marquisate chancellors, commandery governors, or holders of two-thousand-dan rank; over a thousand were at one-thousand-dan rank and below.

entries.zh: 奮行者官過其望，以適過行者皆黜其勞。
entries.en: The eager were promoted beyond their dreams; those who had gone in disgrace saw their service struck from the rolls.
entries.literal: Those who strove to march had offices exceeding their hopes; those who marched with faults through banishment all had their merit dismissed.

entries.zh: 士卒賜直四萬錢。
entries.en: Common soldiers each received a bounty equivalent to forty thousand cash.
entries.literal: Soldiers were granted cash worth forty thousand cash.

entries.zh: 伐宛再反，凡四歲而得罷焉。
entries.en: The two Ferghana expeditions ran four years in all before the armies could stand down.
entries.literal: The attack on Dayuan went back and forth twice; in all four years and then it was able to be halted.

entries.zh: 留歲餘，還，並南山，欲從羌中歸，復為匈奴所得。
entries.en: After more than a year he turned homeward along the southern ranges, hoping to slip through Qiang country, only to be seized again by the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: He stayed over a year, then returned, keeping south of the mountains, intending to return through the Qiang region, and again was taken by the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 留歲餘，單于死，國內亂，騫與胡妻及堂邑父俱亡歸漢。
entries.en: Another year passed; the chanyu died and the realm fell into strife, and Zhang Qian fled to Han with his Xiongnu wife and Ganfu.
entries.literal: He was detained over a year; the chanyu died and the state was in turmoil within; Qian together with his Hu wife and Tangyi Fu all fled and returned to Han.

entries.zh: 拜騫太中大夫，堂邑父為奉使君。
entries.en: The emperor appointed Zhang Qian grand counsellor of the palace and ennobled Ganfu as Lord Fengshi for his part in the embassy.
entries.literal: Qian was appointed grand counsellor of the palace; Tangyi Fu was made Fengshi lord.

entries.zh: 天子數問騫大夏之屬。
entries.en: The emperor often pressed Zhang Qian for news of Daxia and the western states.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven repeatedly asked Qian about Daxia and the like.

entries.zh: 騫既失侯，因曰：「臣居匈奴中，聞烏孫王號昆莫。
entries.en: Stripped of his fief, Zhang Qian said, "Among the Xiongnu I heard that the Wusun ruler bears the title Kunmo.
entries.literal: Qian having lost his marquisate, thereupon said, "When your servant dwelt among the Xiongnu, I heard the Wusun king is titled Kunmo.

entries.zh: 昆莫父難兜靡本與大月氏俱在祁連、敦煌間，小國也。
entries.en: Kunmo's father Nandoumi had ruled a small people between the Qilian range and Dunhuang alongside the Greater Yuezhi.
entries.literal: Kunmo's father Nandoumi originally together with the Greater Yuezhi were between Qilian and Dunhuang, a small state.

entries.zh: 大月氏攻殺難兜靡，奪其地，人民亡走匈奴。
entries.en: The Greater Yuezhi slew Nandoumi, seized his territory, and his followers fled to the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: The Greater Yuezhi attacked and killed Nandoumi, seized his land, and the people fled in disorder to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 子昆莫新生，傅父布就翕侯抱亡置草中，為求食，還，見狼乳之，又烏銜肉翔其旁，以為神，遂持歸匈奴，單于愛養之。
entries.en: The infant Kunmo was carried off by his nurse-father Bu-jiu the Xihou, hidden in the grass while food was sought; returning, the man found a wolf nursing the child and crows dropping meat nearby. Convinced the boy was spirit-touched, he brought him to the chanyu, who reared him with favor.
entries.literal: The son Kunmo was newly born; the foster father Bu-jiu Xihou took him in flight, placed him in the grass, went to seek food, returned, saw a wolf suckling him, and moreover a crow holding meat circling beside him; deeming him divine, he then carried him back to the Xiongnu, and the chanyu cherished and raised him.

entries.zh: 及壯，以其父民眾與昆莫，使將兵，數有功。
entries.en: When the boy came of age, the chanyu restored his father's tribesmen to him, gave him a command, and he won repeated distinction.
entries.literal: When he was grown, the chanyu gave him his father's people and masses, ordered him to lead troops, and several times he had merit.

entries.zh: 時，月氏已為匈奴所破，西擊塞王。
entries.en: By then the Xiongnu had shattered the Yuezhi, who marched west against the Sai king.
entries.literal: At that time the Yuezhi had already been broken by the Xiongnu and went west to strike the Sai king.

entries.zh: 塞王南走遠徙，月氏居其地。
entries.en: The Sai king withdrew far to the south, and the Yuezhi took his ground.
entries.literal: The Sai king fled south and removed far; the Yuezhi dwelt in his land.

entries.zh: 昆莫既健，自請單于報父怨，遂西攻破大月氏。
entries.en: Once Kunmo grew strong he begged leave to avenge his father; marching west, he crushed the Greater Yuezhi.
entries.literal: Kunmo having become strong, himself requested of the chanyu to repay his father's grudge, and thereupon went west and broke the Greater Yuezhi.

entries.zh: 大月氏復西走，徒大夏地。
entries.en: The Yuezhi fled farther west and settled on Daxia's soil.
entries.literal: The Greater Yuezhi again fled west and moved to Daxia's territory.

entries.zh: 昆莫略其眾，因留居，兵稍強，會單于死，不肯復朝事匈奴。
entries.en: Kunmo absorbed their warriors, stayed put, and grew in strength; when the chanyu died he refused ever again to acknowledge Xiongnu overlordship.
entries.literal: Kunmo plundered their masses, thereupon stayed and dwelt, arms gradually grew strong, it happened the chanyu died, and he was unwilling again to attend court and serve the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 匈奴遣兵擊之，不勝，益以為神而遠之。
entries.en: Xiongnu attacks failed; they came to regard him as uncanny and gave him a wide berth.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu sent troops to strike him, did not prevail, and increasingly deemed him divine and kept distant from him.

entries.zh: 今單于新困於漢，而昆莫地空。
entries.en: The chanyu is newly worsted by Han, and Kunmo's old pasture lands lie open.
entries.literal: Now the chanyu has newly been distressed by Han, while Kunmo's land is empty.

entries.zh: 蠻夷戀故地，又貪漢物，誠以此時厚賂烏孫，招以東居故地，漢遣公主為夫人，結昆弟，其勢宜聽，則是斷匈奴右臂也。
entries.en: Frontier peoples cling to ancestral ground yet hunger for Han goods; rich gifts now could draw the Wusun back east to their old pastures, a Han princess sealing a brotherly pact—they would surely listen, and you would sever the Xiongnu's right arm.
entries.literal: The barbarian Yi cling to old lands and moreover covet Han goods; if truly at this time one richly bribes Wusun, summons them to dwell east in the old lands, Han sends a princess as consort, binds brotherhood, by the situation they ought to listen—then this is cutting off the Xiongnu's right arm.

entries.zh: 既連烏孫，自其西大夏之屬皆可招來而為外臣。」
entries.en: Once Wusun is bound to us, Daxia and the states beyond can be summoned as outer vassals."
entries.literal: Having already linked Wusun, from west of them Daxia and the like can all be summoned and come to be outer subjects."

entries.zh: 天子以為然，拜騫為中郎將，將三百人，馬各二匹，牛、羊以萬數，齎金幣帛直數千巨萬，多持節副使，道可便遣之旁國。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, named Zhang Qian general of the household with three hundred followers, two mounts each, vast herds of stock, and treasure worth tens of millions in cash and silk, with many credentialled deputies who could be sent on to neighboring courts as the route allowed.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven deemed it right, appointed Qian general of the gentlemen of the household, leading three hundred men, each with two horses, cattle and sheep in tens of thousands, carrying gold, coins, and silks worth several thousand times ten thousand, many holding credentials as deputy envoys, on the road being able as convenient to dispatch them to neighboring states.

entries.zh: 騫既至烏孫，致賜諭指，未能得其決。
entries.en: Zhang Qian reached Wusun with gifts and the emperor's message but could not secure a firm answer.
entries.literal: Qian having reached Wusun, conveyed gifts and explained intent, was not able to obtain their decision.

entries.zh: 語在《西域傳》。
entries.en: The details are given in the Western Regions treatise.
entries.literal: The words are in the "Treatise on the Western Regions."

entries.zh: 騫即分遣副使使大宛、康居、月氏、大夏。
entries.en: He at once sent deputies on to Dayuan, Kangju, the Yuezhi, and Daxia.
entries.literal: Qian thereupon separately dispatched deputy envoys to go to Dayuan, Kangju, the Yuezhi, and Daxia.

entries.zh: 烏孫發道譯送騫，與烏孫使數十人，馬數十匹。
entries.en: The Wusun furnished guides to escort him home with dozens of their envoys and mounts.
entries.literal: Wusun issued guides and interpreters to escort Qian, together with several tens of Wusun envoys and several tens of horses.

entries.zh: 報謝，因令窺漢，知其廣大。
entries.en: They came to offer thanks, and the court had them tour the realm until they understood how vast Han was.
entries.literal: They returned thanks; thereupon Han had them observe Han and know its vastness.

entries.zh: 初，天子發書《易》，曰「神馬當從西北來」。
entries.en: The emperor had once consulted the Changes and read the omen: "A spirit horse will come from the northwest."
entries.literal: At first, the Son of Heaven opened the document Changes, and it said, "The divine horse shall come from the northwest."

entries.zh: 得烏孫馬好，名曰：「天馬」。
entries.en: The fine Wusun mounts were dubbed "heavenly horses."
entries.literal: Obtaining Wusun horses that were fine, they named them "heavenly horses."

entries.zh: 及得宛汗血馬，益壯，更名烏孫馬曰「西極馬」，宛馬曰「天馬」云。
entries.en: When the blood-sweating Ferghana horses arrived—still hardier—the Wusun stock was renamed "horses of the western pole" and the Ferghana animals alone kept the title "heavenly horses."
entries.literal: When they obtained Ferghana blood-sweating horses, still more robust, they changed the name of Wusun horses to "western-pole horses" and Ferghana horses to "heavenly horses," it is said.

entries.zh: 而漢始築令居以西，初置酒泉郡，以通西北國。
entries.en: Han began building the wall west of Lingju and founded Jiuquan commandery to hold the road open to the northwest.
entries.literal: And Han for the first time built west of Lingju, first established Jiuquan commandery, in order to open communication with the northwestern states.

entries.zh: 因發使抵安息、奄蔡、犛靬、條支、身毒國。
entries.en: Thereupon the court sent missions to Parthia, Yancai, Lijian, Characene on the Persian Gulf, and Shendu (India).
entries.literal: Thereupon envoys were dispatched reaching Anxi, Yancai, Lijian, Tiaozhi, and Shendu.

entries.zh: 而天子好宛馬，使者相望於道，一輩大者數百，少者百餘人，所齎操，大放博望侯時。
entries.en: The emperor's passion for Ferghana horses filled the highways with embassies—some missions ran to hundreds of men, none to fewer than a hundred—with baggage trains dwarfing Zhang Qian's first expedition.
entries.literal: And the Son of Heaven loved Ferghana horses; envoys thronged the roads; a large party numbered several hundred, a small one still over a hundred; the goods and equipage they carried in train far exceeded what had been sent in the Marquis of Bowang's day.

entries.zh: 其後益習而衰少焉。
entries.en: Later, as the routes grew familiar, the traffic thinned.
entries.literal: After that they increasingly became practiced and declined and diminished.

entries.zh: 漢率一歲中使者多者十餘，少者五六輩，遠者八九歲，近者數歲而反。
entries.en: In a typical year Han sent ten or more missions, or as few as five or six; the long journeys took eight or nine years, shorter ones several years, before men returned.
entries.literal: Han as a rule in one year had envoys in the many case over ten, in the few case five or six parties; those far took eight or nine years, those near several years and returned.

entries.zh: 自騫開外國道以尊貴，其吏士爭上書言外國奇怪利害，求使。
entries.en: After Zhang Qian's opening of the western routes brought him rank and favor, officials and troops vied to memorialize about exotic lands, gains, and risks—all begging for an embassy.
entries.literal: From the time Qian opened the road to foreign states and became honored, his clerks and soldiers vied in submitting memorials speaking of foreign states' strangenesses, wonders, profits, and harms, seeking to be sent as envoys.

entries.zh: 天子為其絕遠，非人所樂，聽其言，予節，募吏民無問所從來，為具備人眾遣之，以廣其道。
entries.en: The emperor knew the journey was grim and uninviting, yet he heard them out, issued staffs of office, and recruited clerks and commoners of any origin, fitting out full parties to widen the traffic in every direction.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven because it was utterly distant, not what men delight in, listened to their words, gave them credentials, recruited clerks and commoners without asking whence they came, for them fully prepared men and masses and dispatched them, in order to broaden the road.

entries.zh: 來還不能無侵盜幣物，及使失指，天子為其習之，輒復按致重罪，以激怒令贖，復求使。
entries.en: Returning missions could not help embezzling part of the imperial gifts, or bungling their instructions; the emperor, used to the pattern, would indict them on grave charges, let them buy their way out, and watch them volunteer for another posting.
entries.literal: Coming back they could not but sometimes encroach on and steal goods and silks, and as for envoys missing the intent, the Son of Heaven because they were practiced in this, repeatedly again investigated and brought heavy crimes, in order to provoke anger and order ransom, again seeking to be envoys.

entries.zh: 使端無窮，而輕犯法。
entries.en: Excuses for new embassies multiplied, and men flouted the statutes with little fear.
entries.literal: The pretexts for missions were endless, while they lightly violated the law.

entries.zh: 其吏卒亦輒復盛推外國所有，言大者予節，言小者為副，故妄言無行之徒皆爭相效。
